What this document is
The repository reference for the standardized artifact-display process. It contains the complete function, the ViewModel state it relies on, the two call-site shapes, and the verified facts behind every decision.
No code has been applied to the tree. Wiring (replacing the three inline blocks) is the next session's first action, done one change at a time with a build/certify between steps.
Why this is safe (and why we chose it)
The fragile part of the earlier design was a worker thread blocking on a main-thread dialog � the classic ANR risk, and exactly the kind of mechanism this codebase has had to revert before.
Protecting selection by state removes that mechanism entirely. Simpler to reason about, impossible to deadlock, and it matches the user�s intent: �don�t trash my list because I zoomed in for a look.�
Secondary bugs the standard process also fixes
Interface #1 routes bug: builds GeoJSON from the unfiltered routesRaw while the filtered list is computed and discarded.
Interface #2: declares the checked-ID variables inside the thread and never uses them � no selection filtering.
onSetState divergence: ConvoyMapViewer clears checkedIds when leaving SELECTED (659�662); ConvoyScreen does not (1164�1167). Align convoy to match planning during wiring.
State | What renders | On viewport change | Selection
ALL | Everything in the box | Follows the box (new in / out as box moves) | n/a
OFF | Nothing | hide<Type>() | n/a
SELECTED | Selected items that are in the box | Selected set unchanged; viewport just narrows what is drawable | Protected � only user/panel changes it
object SpatialDisplayManager {
    const val DS_OFF = 0; const val DS_ON = 1; const val DS_SELECTED = 2
 
    private data class TypeBinding(
        val displayState: () -> Int,
        val checkedIds:   () -> Set<String>?,
        val idField: String,
        val query: (Double,Double,Double,Double,Int) -> List<Map<String,String?>>,
        val build: (List<Map<String,String?>>) -> String,
        val jsUpdate: String, val jsShow: String, val jsHide: String,
        val minZoom: Int
    )
 
    private fun bindingFor(type: String): TypeBinding? = when (type) {
        "Trails" -> TypeBinding(
            { ConvoyConfig.trailDisplayState }, { ConvoyConfig.trailChecked }, "trail_id",
            { s,w,n,e,l -> SpatialDbManager.queryTrailsByViewport(s,w,n,e,l) },
            { SpatialDbManager.buildTrailGeoJson(it) },
            "updateTrails","showTrails","hideTrails", 8)
        "Tracks" -> TypeBinding(
            { ConvoyConfig.trackDisplayState }, { ConvoyConfig.trackChecked }, "track_id",
            { s,w,n,e,l -> SpatialDbManager.queryTracksByViewport(s,w,n,e,l) },
            { SpatialDbManager.buildTrackGeoJson(it) },
            "updateTracks","showTracks","hideTracks", 0)
        "Waypoints" -> TypeBinding(
            { ConvoyConfig.waypointDisplayState }, { ConvoyConfig.waypointChecked }, "waypoint_id",
            { s,w,n,e,l -> SpatialDbManager.queryWaypointsByViewport(s,w,n,e,l) },
            { SpatialDbManager.buildWaypointGeoJson(it) },
            "updateWaypoints","showWaypoints","hideWaypoints", 0)
        "Routes" -> TypeBinding(
            { ConvoyConfig.routeDisplayState }, { ConvoyConfig.routeChecked }, "route_id",
            { s,w,n,e,l -> SpatialDbManager.queryRoutesByViewport(s,w,n,e,l) },
            { SpatialDbManager.buildRouteGeoJson(it) },
            "updateRoutes","showRoutes","hideRoutes", 0)
        else -> null
    }
fun processArtifact(
        type: String,
        south: Double, west: Double, north: Double, east: Double,
        zoom: Int, webView: WebView?, context: Context
    ) {
        val b = bindingFor(type) ?: return
        val wv = webView ?: return
        val state = b.displayState()
        val main = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())
 
        // OFF � hide and stop. (Both convoy paths never hid; explicit hide
        // makes OFF actually clear the map. hide*() verified present in HTML.)
        if (state == DS_OFF) { main.post { wv.evaluateJavascript(b.jsHide+"()",null) }; return }
 
        // Below the type's min zoom (trails z<8): nothing to show.
        if (zoom < b.minZoom) { main.post { wv.evaluateJavascript(b.jsHide+"()",null) }; return }
 
        SpatialDbManager.init(context)
        val limit = if (type == "Tracks") { if (zoom >= 12) 200 else 50 }
                    else { if (zoom < 14) 500 else 2000 }
 
        val raw = b.query(south, west, north, east, limit)
 
        // SELECTED � draw only protected (checked) items in view.
        // ON � draw everything in view.
        val checked = b.checkedIds()
        val items = if (state == DS_SELECTED && checked != null)
            raw.filter { it[b.idField] in checked } else raw
 
        val json = b.build(items)
 
        // THE FIX: update THEN show. Both convoy interfaces omitted show().
        main.post {
            wv.evaluateJavascript(b.jsUpdate+"("+json+")", null)
            wv.evaluateJavascript(b.jsShow+"()", null)
        }
    }
 
    fun processViewport(
        south: Double, west: Double, north: Double, east: Double,
        zoom: Int, webView: WebView?, context: Context
    ) {
        for (t in listOf("Trails","Tracks","Waypoints","Routes"))
            processArtifact(t, south, west, north, east, zoom, webView, context)
    }
}
On the protected-selection model and requery
Phase 1 requeries the viewport each change and filters to the checked set. Because the checked set (ConvoyConfig.*Checked) is untouched by viewport changes, selection is automatically protected � zoom/pan can only change which selected items are in view, never the set itself. No retained list is required to achieve the protection; the ID set already provides it.
This is the simplest implementation of �protected until SELECTED changes� and carries no threading risk.
fun onViewportChanged(north: Double, south: Double,
                      east: Double, west: Double, zoom: Double) {
    lastViewportSouth = south; lastViewportWest = west
    lastViewportNorth = north; lastViewportEast = east
    val wv = webViewRef.value          // ConvoyMapViewer: its own webViewRef
    Thread {
        SpatialDisplayManager.processViewport(
            south, west, north, east, zoom.toInt(), wv, context)
    }.start()
}

=== cfg_from_json.docx ===
CONVOY TRACKER
Creating a Binary .cfg File from JSON Source
Technical Reference  |  March 19, 2026  |  Feature Branch: convoy-event-ride

1.  Overview
This document defines the complete process for constructing a Meshtastic binary .cfg file programmatically from your JSON configuration source � specifically master_config.json and ride-specific overrides � without requiring a connected radio.
Two production paths exist. Both are documented here.


Path B is the focus of this document. It enables ride organisers to generate a distributable .cfg file for any ride without touching a radio at all � channel name, PSK, and all base config fields come from WorkingConfig alone.

2.  What the Binary .cfg File Actually Is
A Meshtastic .cfg file is a serialised DeviceProfile protobuf binary. It is not JSON, not a zip archive, and not a proprietary format. It is a standard Protocol Buffers binary encoding of a single DeviceProfile message defined in clientonly.proto.

DeviceProfile Structure
clientonly.proto � DeviceProfile definition

LocalConfig Structure
localonly.proto � LocalConfig definition

The channel_url field encodes all active channels as a base64-encoded ChannelSet protobuf. This is the same URL format used in Meshtastic QR codes. It carries both channel settings (name, PSK) and the LoRa modem preset together in one string.

3.  JSON Source to Protobuf Field Mapping
Your master_config.json contains human-readable values for all radio config groups. The table below maps each JSON section and key to the target DeviceProfile protobuf field.


4.  Build Process � Step by Step
The following steps describe how to build a DeviceProfile binary from WorkingConfig inside the Convoy Android app. WorkingConfig is already populated by the rules engine before this function is called.

Step 1 � Parse master_config.json into WorkingConfig
The rules engine already does this. By the time binary creation begins, WorkingConfig holds all fields for all groups. No additional parsing is required here.

Step 2 � Build Config.LoRaConfig protobuf

Step 3 � Build Config.DeviceConfig protobuf

Step 4 � Build Config.PositionConfig protobuf

Step 5 � Assemble LocalConfig from all groups

Step 6 � Build the ChannelSet and encode as channel_url
The channel_url field encodes channels AND the LoRa preset together. The Meshtastic Android codebase already has a utility to produce this URL from a ChannelSet protobuf � it is the same encoding used for QR codes.

Step 7 � Build and serialise the DeviceProfile

Step 8 � Save the binary file

Before distributing, round-trip verify the binary by parsing it back and checking a few key fields:

5.  Using master.cfg as the Base for Display and Module Fields
Display (4 fields) and Module (17 fields) are ride-invariant. They do not change between rides. The correct source for these is the pre-loaded master.cfg DeviceProfile binary that is already bundled in app assets.



6.  Distribution: Email the Binary to Riders
Once the ride binary is saved, it is attached to the ride record and distributed via Android email intent. The recipient flow requires zero manual configuration steps � the rider opens the attachment in the Convoy app and the radio is written automatically.


Recipient Import Flow
The recipient opens the .cfg attachment in the Convoy app. The app is registered as a file handler for .cfg files (via intent-filter in AndroidManifest.xml). The import flow is identical to the master.cfg apply flow:

message DeviceProfile {
optional string      long_name     = 1;   // node display name
optional string      short_name    = 2;   // callsign (4 chars)
optional string      channel_url   = 3;   // base64 ChannelSet protobuf
optional LocalConfig config        = 4;   // all radio config groups
optional ModuleConfig module_config = 5;  // all module config groups
}
message LocalConfig {
Config.DeviceConfig   device   = 1;   // 9 fields
Config.PositionConfig position = 2;   // 12 fields
Config.PowerConfig    power    = 3;
Config.NetworkConfig  network  = 4;
Config.DisplayConfig  display  = 5;   // 4 fields
Config.LoRaConfig     lora     = 6;   // 18 fields
Config.BluetoothConfig bluetooth = 7;
Config.SecurityConfig security = 8;
}

Session Summary
Day 15 focused on completing the radio write engine, expanding the config data model to all 47 fields, and resolving the rules engine architecture. The session uncovered fundamental issues with the partial-write approach and established a new architecture based on Meshtastic's native import/export mechanism.

Completed This Session

Data Model Expansion � 47 Fields
WorkingConfig, ConvoyMasterConfig, and the rules engine were expanded from a partial subset to all 47 radio configuration fields across 6 groups:


Rules Engine � WorkingConfig Builder
The WorkingConfig builder in ConvoyApplyRadioScreen was rewritten to implement the rules engine for all 47 fields:
If field is CHECKED in apply list: use master config value
If field is UNCHECKED in apply list: use current radio value (from localConfig/channels)
Channel Name and Encryption Key: always from master config or ride file � locked, never from radio
In RIDE mode: Channel Name and PSK come from the ride file, all other fields follow the apply list

Apply List � 4 New Channel Fields
The ChannelField enum was expanded with 4 new fields. Only CHANNEL_NAME and ENCRYPTION_KEY remain locked:
CHANNEL_ID � channel index (0 = primary)
UPLINK_ENABLED � MQTT uplink for this channel
DOWNLINK_ENABLED � MQTT downlink for this channel
MODULE_SETTINGS � per-channel module configuration
Assets updated and committed: convoy_apply_list.json now contains all 6 channel fields.

Master Config Capture Screen
ConvoyMasterCaptureScreen updated to read all 47 fields from the radio at capture time, including device, LoRa, channel, position, and display config. Module fields default to zero/false pending a separate module config read API.

Archive � Long Name and PSK Captured
The archive process now correctly captures:
Long name from ourNodeInfo.user.long_name
Primary channel name from channelSet.settings
AES-256 PSK as base64 from channelSet.settings
All LoRa values including TX enabled

CAPTURE MASTER CONFIG � capture only, does not navigate to apply list on completion

Write Sequence � Corrected Navigation
The write screen navigation was corrected to: LoRa -> Channel -> Device -> Position -> Verify. The prior sequence had LoRa navigating directly to Verify, skipping Channel and Device.

Auto-Reconnect � BT Toggle
reconnectDevice() in UIViewModel was updated to toggle Android Bluetooth adapter off/on rather than calling setDeviceAddress(n). The 10-second countdown is shown on reboot screens. If radio does not reconnect after countdown, the BT toggle fires automatically.

Radio Write Architecture � Revised Design
During testing, the 4-screen individual setConfig() write approach proved unreliable. The following architecture was defined for implementation in the next session.

Key Insight: Use Meshtastic DeviceProfile
Meshtastic's native import/export mechanism uses a DeviceProfile binary protobuf that contains all 47 config fields in one atomic structure. Writing via Import Configuration writes all fields in one call, triggers one reboot, and uses Meshtastic's own reconnect mechanism. This replaces the 4-screen setConfig() approach entirely.

Function 1 � Master Config to Radio
Read current radio state using Meshtastic Export Configuration � creates DeviceProfile binary
Save binary to archive: convoy_backups/<nodeId>/<datetime>_<channelName>.cfg
Apply master config to radio � for each CHECKED field in apply list: write that field to radio using setConfig()
For UNCHECKED fields: leave radio's existing value untouched
After all writes: use Export Configuration to capture final state
Save final image as master.cfg binary � the canonical master binary
Output: master.cfg binary + master_config.json + archive backup

Function 2 � Apply Ride Info to Radio
Archive current radio state using Export Configuration � save as <nodeId>_<datetime>_<channelName>.cfg
Import master.cfg binary to radio via Meshtastic Import Configuration � sets all master fields atomically, one reboot
Apply ride-specific overrides using setConfig() � Channel Name and Encryption Key mandatory, plus any ride-specific fields from rules engine
Export complete final config � attach to ride record as .cfg binary
Distribute ride .cfg via email
Recipients: import .cfg email attachment directly into app � no manual configuration. App saves archive copy automatically.

Function 3 � Archive Restore
List available .cfg archives for this radio ID sorted by date
User selects archive
Import selected .cfg binary via Import Configuration � one call, all 47 fields, one reboot
Verify radio state after reconnect

Post-Import Corrections via setConfig()
After the bulk import, the rules engine identifies which fields need individual correction via setConfig() � these are the fields where the apply list says to use the radio's original value rather than the master config value. The JSON config and apply list tools do this identification. No work performed today is lost � the WorkingConfig, rules engine, and apply list remain as the control layer.

Ride Distribution Model
The first person to set up a ride does the full configuration work. The resulting ride .cfg file contains the complete radio configuration � LoRa, channel, device, position, display, module. Anyone receiving the ride .cfg via email simply imports it. Zero manual configuration for riders.

Ride Config Transfer � Design Specification

SEND � Organizer Emails Ride Config
From the Create Ride or Ride List screen, organizer taps SHARE RIDE. App exports the ride definition as a .json file and opens the Android share sheet. Organizer selects email client. Ride JSON is sent as an attachment.

RECEIVE � Rider Imports Ride Config
Rider receives email, taps attachment. Android opens Convoy app via file handler registration. App parses ride JSON, saves to local rides DB, ride appears in Apply Radio RIDE tab. Rider selects ride and applies to radio.

Ride JSON File Format



Research Item � Single Binary Import with Channel + PSK

Current Architecture
Stage 1: InstallProfileUseCase installs DeviceProfile binary � writes 38 radio config fields. channel_url field in DeviceProfile is ignored by InstallProfileUseCase. Stage 2: setChannels() wrapped in beginEditSettings/commitEditSettings transaction writes channel name + PSK + module_settings. Two transactions, two reboots.

Key Finding
When a user exports their radio config and imports it on another device via the standard Meshtastic import flow, channels ARE applied correctly including PSK � in a single import with one reboot. The standard import path must be processing channel_url differently than InstallProfileUseCase.



Convoy File Transfer Method � Architecture Reference

Overview
Convoy uses a custom file format (.convoy) with mime type application/x-convoy-ride for all data exchange between devices. Files are sent as email attachments and automatically processed when received. The format is extensible � any new data type adds a new convoyDocType value without infrastructure changes.

File Format
Every .convoy file is a JSON document with a mandatory convoyDocType field that identifies the document type and routes it to the correct handler.

Send Flow
Organizer opens Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email from convoy menu. Selects ride from list (sorted future first, searchable by organizer name). Taps SEND � Android share sheet opens with .convoy file attached. Organizer selects email client and sends.

Receive Flow
Rider receives email, taps .convoy attachment. Android routes directly to Convoy app (no chooser dialog) via registered intent filter. MainActivity copies file to convoy_import/ directory. On next app open: ConvoyViewModel.scanImportDirectory() processes the file, saves ride to local DB, deletes from import queue. When rider opens convoy menu: 3-second splash shows imported ride names.

Implementation Files

The .convoy File Format � Technical Specification

File Format Overview
Files use the .convoy extension with MIME type application/x-convoy-ride. Content is UTF-8 JSON with a required convoyDocType field that identifies the document type and routes it to the correct handler. The format is extensible � new document types are added by defining a new convoyDocType value and handler case.

convoyDocType Registry

convoy_ride JSON Fields

Import Flow
1. Organizer taps Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email in convoy submenu. 2. Selects ride from list (search by organizer name, future dates first). 3. Taps SEND � share sheet opens with .convoy attachment. 4. Recipient receives email, taps attachment. 5. Android opens Convoy app via intent filter. 6. handleConvoyRideImport() copies file to convoy_import/. 7. On next app open: scanImportDirectory() processes file, saves ride to DB, deletes file. 8. When convoy menu opens: 3-second splash shows NEW RIDE IMPORTED: <name>. 9. Ride appears in Apply Radio RIDE tab.

Second Device Install � APK via Email
To install Convoy Tracker on a device without ADB access: email app-google-debug.apk as attachment. On receiving device: enable Settings > Security > Install from unknown sources. Open email, tap APK attachment, install. Then test full ride transfer flow.

Convoy File Exchange Format � Technical Reference

Format Specification
All convoy data files use the .convoy extension with mime type application/x-convoy-ride. The file contains a JSON object with a required convoyDocType field that identifies the content type and routes it to the correct handler on import.

=== convoy_platform_spec.docx ===
CONVOY TRACKER
Platform Business & Product Specification
Version 1.0  |  March 2026  |  Confidential
Mission: Make every group ride safe, coordinated, and connected � from casual weekend trips to professional off-grid expeditions. No cellular required in the field.

1. THE PROBLEM
Group rides � off-road, overland, convoy, search and rescue � have a coordination problem. Riders get separated. Someone drops off and nobody knows for 20 minutes. The group stops, splits, or someone gets hurt waiting. Cellular doesn't work in the field. Radios require manual setup that most riders can't do. There is no purpose-built platform that handles the full lifecycle of a group ride � from registration to radio config to real-time tracking to post-ride route archive.

No cellular in the field � standard mapping and communication apps fail
Manual radio setup � too complex for casual riders, error-prone for everyone
No live convoy map � riders don't know who is ahead, behind, or missing
No ride registration system � orgs manage signups in spreadsheets and email
No post-ride record � route data is lost when the session ends

2. THE SOLUTION
Convoy Tracker is a two-part platform: a mobile field app that runs on Meshtastic mesh radio hardware, and a web platform that manages ride registration, radio configuration, and post-ride route delivery. Together they handle every phase of a group ride � before, during, and after.

The field app works with no cellular. The web platform handles everything before and after the ride. Riders never touch a radio config file manually.

The Flywheel
Riders subscribe to access organized rides
Demand for Convoy-listed rides grows in their community
Clubs and orgs see members asking for Convoy � they join to keep them
More rides listed, more riders subscribe
Corporate operators see clubs running professional operations � they want white label
Platform revenue funds offline map development and hardware at scale
Crowdsourced ride ratings and route data create a defensible data moat

3. MARKET ENTRY STRATEGY � WIDEST FUNNEL FIRST
Stage 1 � Connected Riders (Launch)
Target casual and infrequent riders in areas with cellular coverage. Lowest barrier to entry. No offline map infrastructure required. Proves the business model with zero infrastructure risk.

Weekend recreational riders � parks, rural day trips, accessible trails
Rides in areas with partial or full cellular coverage
App works with live tile streaming � Gaia GPS or onX for map layer
Day pass riders � no hardware, phone GPS only, pickup rides
Monthly subscribers � full org ride access, hardware on annual plan

Stage 2 � Semi-Connected Riders
Suburban to rural transitions with patchy coverage. Meshtastic hardware fills the gaps where cellular drops. Gaia/onX integration for pre-cached map tiles.

Riders who venture beyond reliable cellular � gravel roads, remote parks
Meshtastic hardware becomes essential � mesh fills coverage gaps
Org rides in semi-remote areas � canyons, desert edges, mountain approaches
Ride card includes Gaia/onX region link for pre-ride tile caching

Stage 3 � True Off-Grid (Full Platform)
Zero cellular, zero internet in the field. Native offline tile download from ride card. Full Meshtastic mesh convoy coordination. Enterprise and professional clients.

Desert, backcountry, remote trails � zero infrastructure
Native offline tile download built into Convoy � no third-party map app required
Ride card defines bounding box � one tap downloads exactly the right tiles
Corporate clients � SAR, military, professional tour operators
At this stage Gaia/onX become the competitor, not the partner

4. PRICING MODEL
Access Tiers

Pricing Logic
Day pass ($40) � pickup rides only, phone GPS, no org rides, no hardware
Two day passes = $80 = more than annual membership
Natural conversion path � rider pays twice, switches to annual
Individual monthly ($5) � full access, all org rides, named rider, config per ride
Annual plan includes pre-configured Meshtastic device � device cost recovered in subscription
Club/Org � publish rides, manage registrations, receive post-ride KML
Members see org rides, day pass riders do not � exclusivity drives subscriptions
Corporate/White Label � full platform on their domain, their branding, SLA
Org provides web interface location and branding � Convoy provides infrastructure

Hardware Strategy
Annual individual membership includes a pre-configured Meshtastic device. Device arrives ready to ride � channel, GPS settings, call sign pre-loaded. Zero setup friction.

Device cost (~$30 at scale) absorbed into annual fee � recovered by month 7-8
Pre-configured to the rider's account � long name, default channel settings
Rider mounts device and opens app � nothing else required
Corporate tier � bulk device orders at cost, pre-flashed under client branding
Dealer program � Convoy certified dealers sell pre-configured devices, earn referral on activations

5. RIDE LIFECYCLE
Step 1 � Ride Creation (Organizer)
Organizer logs into Convoy web portal
Creates ride card: Location, Date/Time, Hosted By, Ride Name, Description
System generates: Channel name (color + 8-digit random e.g. BLUE-47382910), AES256 PSK, Ride ID
Organizer defines map bounding box for tile download region
Organizer optionally uploads planned route KML � shown to registered riders before the ride
Ride published � visible to all monthly/annual subscribers

Step 2 � Rider Registration
Rider browses published rides, selects and registers
Enters: Cart callsign (e.g. HOTEL-10), emergency contact, vehicle description
System generates personalized config: long name, shared channel, shared PSK, GPS interval
Rider receives email with config file and ride details
System saves rider's current radio config � will be restored after ride

Step 3 � Pre-Ride Config Push
Rider opens email, taps config file
Config file launches Meshtastic app or Convoy app via deep link or file handler
Pushes to radio via BLE: long name, channel name, PSK, position broadcast interval, GPS mode
Rider confirmed ready � green status in organizer dashboard
Rider opens Convoy app � downloads ride tile region with one tap
Planned route KML visible on map before departure

Step 4 � The Ride
All registered riders visible on convoy map � color coded, named, ordered
LEAD and TAIL identified automatically by position
SIGNAL_DROP and LOST alerts fire when a rider goes out of range
Each rider's tablet GPS records a personal KML track to my_tracks/
Lead track polyline shows convoy spread in real time
No cellular required � full mesh radio operation

Step 5 � Post-Ride
Rider taps END � KML file saved to device, uploaded to platform when cellular returns
Platform aggregates all rider KML tracks into a combined ride record
Organizer receives: combined route KML, per-rider tracks, ride stats
KML embeds as Google Earth overlay on org website � permanent ride record and marketing asset
Rider's original radio config restored � one tap from post-ride email
Ride card archived � searchable, shareable, attracts future registrations

6. PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE
Components

7. PHASED BUILD PLAN
Phase 1 � Core Platform (Current)
Goal: Prove the model. Connected riders, cellular areas, Gaia/onX for maps. Ship fast, validate demand, generate revenue to fund Phase 2.


Phase 2 � White Label + Dealer Program

Phase 3 � Native Offline Maps

8. COMPETITIVE POSITION
No existing product covers the full ride lifecycle. Competitors own pieces of the problem but not the whole.


Convoy Tracker is the only product that covers all four dimensions. The combination of live convoy map + automated radio config + ride registration + off-grid operation is the moat.

9. DEFENSIBILITY
Network effect � more riders = more org rides listed = more riders subscribe
Crowdsourced data � ride ratings, route conditions, hazard reports build a dataset competitors cannot replicate
Hardware lock-in � pre-configured devices tied to Convoy accounts create switching cost
Org dependency � once an org's member base is on Convoy, leaving means losing member coordination tools
Post-ride KML archive � orgs accumulate years of ride history on the platform
Config backup/restore � riders trust Convoy with their radio config, high switching friction

10. IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS
Complete Convoy Android app V1 � field test with live hardware (Days 8-9)
Define ride card data model � fields, config generation spec, email template
Select backend stack � API, database, email service, file storage for KML
Build ride creation and registration flow � web portal Phase 1
Define config file format � Meshtastic BLE deep link or import file spec
Pilot with one org � real ride, real riders, end-to-end flow validation
Instrument everything � conversion from day pass to subscription, org signup rate
 | Day Pass | Individual | Club / Org
Price | $40 / day | $5/mo or Annual | TBD

=== convoy_process_flows.docx ===
CONVOY TRACKER
Radio Configuration Process Flows
Day 17 Startup Reference � March 19, 2026



Architecture Overview
The radio configuration system uses three project assets distributed in the APK and three distinct functions for radio setup and ride management.

Three Project Assets (app/src/main/assets/)

Key Rules
master.cfg does 90% of the work atomically via InstallProfileUseCase
setConfig() used only for delta corrections after import
short_name is always stripped from master.cfg before import � riders keep their own names
Channel Name and Encryption Key are always mandatory overrides in ride config
Every write is preceded by a binary archive of current radio state
ReconnectWait screen gates entry to Verify � user confirms connection before verify runs
Verify screen compares all 47 WorkingConfig fields against radio read-back



PREREQUISITE � Master Config Capture (One-Time Setup)
Performed once by developer. Results in three project assets committed to repo and distributed in APK.


CRITICAL � Binary File Pull Method
Never use 'cat' to pull binary files. Use adb pull with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1:
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 adb pull /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/com.geeksville.mesh.google.debug/cache/master.cfg "C:/Users/kixaz/Meshtastic-Android/app/src/main/assets/master.cfg"

Apply List Maintenance (Independent of Capture)


=== convoy_product_roadmap.docx ===


CONVOY TRACKER
Product Roadmap
kixazz25/Meshtastic-Android  |  March 2026

This is the governing document for the project.
Every coding decision must be measured against the current version deliverable.
Features not in the current version are deferred � no exceptions.



Mission
Build an off-grid group ride coordination app running on Meshtastic mesh radio hardware. No cellular, no internet required in the field. Riders can see each other on a map, know who is ahead and behind, and be alerted when someone drops out of range � all from a tablet or phone mounted in their vehicle.


Core Design Principle
One expert creates the ride. Every rider just shows up.

The app is built around a single operational model:
One person configures the radios � everyone connects
One person creates the event and map package � everyone imports the invite
One person masters the map delivery � everyone receives
One person�s recorded routes become the history for the whole group

No rider is required to understand mesh networking, tile packages, or radio configuration. The complexity is invisible. The expertise is baked in before anyone shows up.

Market
Any group of people moving through terrain where cell service is unreliable or nonexistent, and someone needs to know where everyone is:
Motorcycle group rides and convoys
Off-road and overlanding � 4x4, ATV, UTV
Mountain biking and off-road cycling
Hiking groups and trail teams
Hunters � split groups covering different terrain
Car show caravans and road rallies
Search and rescue volunteer teams
Any event requiring group coordination in dead zones

Business Model
Free to ride. $5 to lead.

Hardware: $50 Meshtastic device per rider � no lock-in, any vendor
App: Free download � riders pay nothing
Event creation: $5 per event � organizer only, one-time per ride
No subscription, no data plan, no monthly fees

The organizer is the expert and the beneficiary of the professional toolset. $5 is the price of having infrastructure that just works � the same way a club pays for a radio repeater or a trail fee.










Version 1 � Manual Setup Group Ride Tracker
Target
A technically configured group ride where the operator sets up all radios manually. The app tracks all riders on a map, shows each rider their own status, and alerts when someone drops off. Works without internet in the field.
Must Have Features
Live map with all convoy vehicles as labeled markers
My Cart identification by paired radio node ID
HUD strip � GROUP / MY CART / NODE detail modes
Group Track � START/STOP, LEAD ONLY / ALL CARTS modes
Off-track alert � 150ft threshold, callsign turns red
KML track recording with ride name, saved to device
Vehicle status � ACTIVE / SIGNAL DROP / LOST / OFF TRACK
Convoy order � auto-determined by position and heading
Map tile buttons � SAT / HYB / RD
Zoom slider � controls display zoom level
Map Delivery
WebView/Leaflet. Online tiles or pre-cached before field use. Zoom slider governs display level. No in-app download capability in V1.
Current Status
Complete. APK built and distributed. Tagged v1.0 on GitHub. Testers receiving install package.


Version 2 � Self-Service Setup + Event/Ride Creation
Target
A non-technical rider can join a convoy group without operator assistance. Organizer creates a complete ride package � channel config, radio settings, and map tiles � distributed as a single invite. Riders receive everything they need before the ride.
Four Functions
F1 � Create Event/Ride: Config generation, map area selection, tile package creation
F2 � Transfer Event/Ride Configuration: Email and multi-method distribution of complete ride package
F3 � Update Radio for Event/Ride: Apply event config directly to paired radio (V3 scope)
F4 � Restore Previous Radio Configuration: Backup and restore pre-event radio settings
Map Area Selector � F1
F1 includes a map interface for defining the ride area and generating the tile package:
Organizer draws bounding box on map to define ride area
Zoom depth slider � reused from V1, recontextualized as download depth control
Live file size estimate updates as area and zoom depth change
App packages tiles for the defined area at the selected depth
Tile package bundled with event config for F2 distribution

Map Package Distribution
The ride invite is a complete ride kit � channel settings, radio config, and map tiles in one package. Distribution methods in priority order:


V2 Research Track � ATAK Map Architecture
Parallel to the four build functions, V2 includes a formal research deliverable on ATAK/iTAK offline map architecture:
How ATAK manages offline tile packages and map sources on Android
How iTAK implements the same on iPad and iPhone
How both handle area-of-interest selection for download
Comparison to current WebView/Leaflet tile delivery model
Assessment of migration path � what changes, what stays, what the V1 retrofit requires


iOS Platform Track
V2 opens the iOS/iPad platform track. Feature parity with Android at each version. Source repo: meshtastic/Meshtastic-Apple (Swift/SwiftUI). Build via cloud Mac service (MacStadium or MacInCloud) � no Mac hardware required. Code translation Android Kotlin to Swift handled collaboratively.


Version 3 � ATAK-Modeled Map Integration
Target
Full offline map integration modeled on the ATAK/iTAK architecture. Defines and selects offline map sources. Manages tile provider selection and offline package delivery. Must run identically on Android and iPad.
Scope
Tile provider selection and management � multiple sources, runtime switching
Offline tile package management � download, store, serve
Area-of-interest download � used in F1 Event/Ride creation for pre-ride map packaging
Map source architecture � retrofit scope for V1 WebView/Leaflet determined during V2 F1 development
Reference Model
ATAK (Android) and iTAK (iOS/iPad) � battle-tested off-grid mapping used in serious field operations. Both run on their respective platforms, both support offline tile packages, KML/KMZ overlays, and area-of-interest download. Used as architectural and UX design pattern only.
Cross-Platform Constraint
React Native and Flutter explicitly excluded. Core app is fully off-grid � no JS runtime dependencies in the field. WebView/Leaflet or a library with first-class support on both Android and iOS required.


Version 4 � KML Track History Overlay
Target
All rides recorded in V1 displayed as toggleable overlays on the live map. Riders can see where they have been and compare past routes. Works across any map source selected in V3.
Scope
KML tracks saved with ride name at recording time
Ride history library � stored on device, browsable by name and date
Single master toggle � Show Past Rides on/off � displays all saved tracks as overlay
Works across all map sources � not tied to a specific tile provider






Where We Are � March 2026

Architecture complete
All radios configured
Mesh working
Map tiles delivering via WebView/Leaflet
My Cart identified by node ID
APK built, tagged v1.0 on GitHub
Installation and User Guide written
Testers receiving install package
Version 2 � Starting
Phase 2 design document complete

iOS platform track established
ATAK research track defined
F1 map area selector approach to be confirmed during development


PRODUCT VISION
TAGLINE:  Enjoy your ride. You�re safe, not lost, and not worried at every fork in the road.
NOTE:  The organizer does not need to understand the technology. Event creation is a simple workflow: name the ride, draw the area, set the date, pay $5, send. The infrastructure handles everything else automatically.
VERSION ROADMAP
V1 | Manual Setup Group Ride Tracker
A technically configured group ride where the operator sets up all radios manually.
V2 | Self-Service Setup + Event/Ride Creation
Non-technical rider can join without operator assistance. Organizer creates event with map package included.
V3 | ATAK-Modeled Map Integration
Full offline map system. Tile provider selection, area download management. Feeds V1 retrofit and V2 ride creation.
V4 | KML Track History Overlay
All recorded rides as toggleable overlays on live map. Single master toggle across all map sources.
VERSION DETAILS
NOTE:  The F1 map area selector is a standalone component. The tile delivery method selected here becomes the model for V3 to standardize and for V1 to follow in its retrofit.
Method | Description
Bundled with invite | Organizer pre-packages tiles during event creation. Riders receive complete map with the ride invite. Preferred method � zero scrambling at staging.
Bluetooth transfer | Organizer transfers tile package device-to-device at staging. No internet required. Complete off-grid delivery.
Local file import | Tile package copied via USB cable or shared drive before leaving home. File manager import on device.
On-demand download | Rider opens F1 map area selector at staging, draws area, sets zoom depth, downloads on available connection. Last resort � same tool, same slider, any connection.
CONSTRAINT:  All map source and tile management solutions selected in V2 and V3 must support both Android and iPad. No platform-exclusive mapping libraries. Must run cross-platform.
NOTE:  ATAK and iTAK are referenced as design pattern models only. No TAK server integration, no TAK communication protocols, no TAK ecosystem dependency.
MAP USAGE BY VERSION
Version | Map Method | Detail
V1 | Online / Pre-cached | WebView/Leaflet tile delivery. Requires internet connection or tiles pre-cached before field use. Zoom slider controls display level. No in-app download capability.
V2 | In-app area download | F1 Event/Ride creation includes map area selector � organizer draws bounding box, sets zoom depth via slider, app packages tiles. Tile package bundled with ride invite and distributed with event config. Riders receive complete map before departure. Field download also supported for last-minute use.
V3 | ATAK-modeled map system | Full offline map integration modeled on ATAK/iTAK architecture. Tile provider selection, map source management, offline package management. Must run on both Android and iPad � no platform-exclusive libraries. Retrofit scope for V1 tile source determined during V2 F1 development. ATAK/iTAK used as design pattern only � no TAK server, no TAK protocol integration.
V4 | KML track history overlay | KML tracks recorded in V1 saved with ride names. Displayed as overlay on any map source selected in V3. Single master toggle � Show Past Rides on/off. Works across all map sources.
CURRENT STATUS
RULE:  This document is the source of truth for what gets built and when. If it is not in the current version, it does not get built yet.

=== convoy_radio_write_process.docx ===
CONVOY TRACKER
Radio Write Process � Design Document
Branch: feature/convoy-event-ride  |  Author: Fred Kix
Three processes � one write engine � five screens
OVERVIEW
The radio write process applies a complete convoy configuration to a Meshtastic radio via Bluetooth. Three distinct processes use the same screen-by-screen write engine. Each screen handles one config group, executes the write, and monitors for reboot before advancing to the next screen. A final verify screen reads back all values and confirms the write was successful.

THREE WRITE PROCESSES
Process 1 � Apply Master Config
Applies the master_config.json to the radio. Used to standardize a radio to the base convoy configuration.
Config source: master_config.json
Channel name + PSK: from master_config.json
Checklist rules applied: fields in apply list are written, others kept from radio
Long name: from master config, editable before write

Process 2 � Apply Ride Config
Applies a ride-specific configuration. Channel name and PSK come from the selected ride file.
Config source: master_config.json + ride file override
Channel name + PSK: from selected ride file
Checklist rules applied: same as Process 1
Long name: from working config, editable before write

Process 3 � Restore from Archive
Restores a radio to a previously archived configuration. No rules engine � exact restore.
Config source: selected archive file from convoy_backups/
All values restored exactly � no overrides
No channel/PSK override � original radio state completely restored
Used for: post-ride restore, error recovery


WRITE PROCESS FLOW � All Three Processes

Phase 0 � Pre-Write (ConvoyApplyRadioScreen)

=== convoy_ride_creation_spec_v1.docx ===
CONVOY TRACKER
Ride Creation & Registration Specification
Version 1.0  |  March 9, 2026
1. RIDE CARD � DATA MODEL
The ride card is the central object of the platform. Created by an organizer before the ride. Published to registered members. Drives config generation, registration, and post-ride delivery.


2. RIDER REGISTRATION � DATA MODEL

3. RADIO CONFIG GENERATION
Each ride generates a unique radio configuration. Config is personalized per rider � shared channel credentials plus individual long name.


4. CONFIG FILE FORMAT
The config file is delivered via email as an attachment. Opening the file triggers the Meshtastic app or Convoy app to push settings to the connected radio via BLE.

Research required: Does Meshtastic Android support a config import file format or URL scheme? Options: (A) meshtastic:// URL deep link, (B) .meshtastic config file handler, (C) Convoy app reads file and pushes via Meshtastic BLE API directly.

Candidate approaches:
meshtastic:// URL scheme � deep link opens Meshtastic app with pre-filled config
.convoy config file � Convoy app registered as file handler, reads JSON, pushes via BLE
QR code in email � rider scans with Meshtastic app to import channel config

5. RIDER ONBOARDING FLOW
Field | Type / Format | Notes
Ride ID | UUID � auto-generated | Unique per ride, used in config generation
Ride Name | String � free text | e.g. 'Desert Run March 2026'
Location | String + GPS coords | City/region + lat/lon bounding box
Date | Date � YYYY-MM-DD | Ride date
Start Time | Time � HH:MM local | Staging time
Hosted By | String � org name | Organizing club or individual
Description | Text � free form | Route notes, requirements, meetup details
Channel Name | Auto-generated | Color + 8-digit random e.g. BLUE-47382910
PSK | AES256 � auto-generated | Unique per ride, never reused
Map Bounding Box | 4x GPS coords | NE/SW corners for tile download region
Planned Route KML | File upload � optional | Pre-ride route overlay for riders
Max Riders | Integer � optional | Cap on registration
Access Level | Day Pass / Member / Invite | Controls who can register
Status | Draft / Published / Closed / Archived | Ride lifecycle state
Field | Type / Format | Notes
Registration ID | UUID � auto-generated | Unique per rider per ride
Ride ID | UUID � foreign key | Links to ride card
Full Name | String | Rider legal name
Email | String � validated | Config delivery address
Cart Callsign | String � e.g. HOTEL-10 | Assigned by organizer or self-selected
Emergency Contact | String � name + phone | Required field
Vehicle Description | String � make/model/color | For field identification
Radio Long Name | = Cart Callsign | Pushed to radio on config apply
Subscription Tier | Day Pass / Monthly / Annual | Access control
Pre-Ride Config | JSON � saved radio config | Backup before ride config push
Ride Config | JSON � generated per ride | Channel, PSK, GPS settings
Status | Registered / Configured / Ready / Completed | Readiness tracking
Config Field | Value / Source | Notes
Long Name | = Cart Callsign (e.g. HOTEL-10) | Unique per rider
Short Name | First 4 chars of callsign | e.g. HOTE
Channel Name | Auto-generated: COLOR-######## | e.g. BLUE-47382910, shared per ride
PSK | AES256 � auto-generated per ride | Same key for all riders on this ride
Position Broadcast | 30 seconds | Standard convoy interval
GPS Update Interval | 30 seconds | Standard convoy interval
Smart Position | OFF | Fixed interval, no adaptive
GPS Mode | ENABLED | Always on during ride
Role | TRACKER | Standard convoy role
Node Broadcast | 90 seconds | Telemetry interval
Step | Action | System
1 | Organizer creates ride card � fills fields, system generates channel/PSK | Web portal
2 | Organizer publishes ride � visible to registered members | Web portal
3 | Rider browses ride listing, taps Register | Web portal / app
4 | Rider enters callsign, emergency contact, vehicle description | Web portal / app
5 | System saves current radio config as backup | Backend API
6 | System generates personalized config file for this rider and ride | Backend API
7 | Rider receives email � config file attachment + ride details + restore link | Email service
8 | Rider opens email, taps config file � radio updated automatically | Meshtastic / Convoy app
9 | Rider status updates to READY � visible in organizer dashboard | Backend API
10 | Post-ride � rider taps restore link in email � radio returns to pre-ride config | Email / app

=== convoy_user_guide_v1.docx ===
CONVOY TRACKER
User Guide
Off-Grid Mesh Network Convoy Coordination
Version 1.0  |  March 2026
Developed by: Fred Kix



OVERVIEW
Convoy Tracker is an off-grid mesh network application for real-time GPS position sharing and convoy coordination. It runs on Android tablets and communicates via Meshtastic radio hardware � no cell service or internet required during convoy operations.

The app shows all convoy vehicles on a live map, tracks the route being driven, alerts you when a vehicle goes off-route, and records GPS tracks for post-ride review.

NOTE: Convoy Tracker requires Meshtastic-compatible radio hardware and a paired Android device. Map tiles require an internet connection or cached tiles.

HARDWARE SETUP
Compatible Radios
Convoy Tracker works with any Meshtastic-compatible radio. Recommended:
SenseCAP T1000-E � compact, long battery, reliable GPS
LILYGO T-Beam v2 � high power, good range

Radio Configuration
All radios in the convoy must be configured identically:


TIP: Use the Meshtastic app or Web Client to configure radios before a convoy. All devices must use the same channel name and PSK key or they will not communicate.

FIRST LAUNCH
Install Convoy Tracker APK on your Android tablet.
Open the app � the CONVOY splash screen appears for 3 seconds.
The map loads automatically. No internet is required for the mesh network � only for map tiles.
Open the side navigation menu and tap Radio Configuration to pair your Meshtastic radio via Bluetooth.
Once the radio is paired and connected, your convoy vehicles will appear on the map.

TIP: Connect your radio before the ride. The app will automatically identify your cart based on the radio's node ID.

MAIN SCREEN
The main screen has three areas: the map, the HUD strip at the bottom, and the REC button in the top-left corner.

The Map
Each convoy vehicle appears as a colored circle with its callsign above it.
Your own vehicle (My Cart) appears as a larger circle.
The route trail is a colored line showing where the convoy has traveled.
Tap any vehicle marker to zoom to it and see its details.

Map Tile Buttons
SAT � Satellite imagery
HYB � Hybrid (satellite + roads)
RD � Road map (default)

TIP: Connect your iPhone as a hotspot for map tiles during a convoy if cell service is limited.

THE HUD (Heads-Up Display)
The HUD strip at the bottom of the screen has three modes. Tap the mode buttons to switch between them.

GROUP Mode
Shows the overall convoy status at a glance:
UNITS � total number of vehicles in the convoy
ACTIVE � vehicles heard recently
LOST � vehicles that have gone silent
LEAD � callsign of the lead vehicle (green)
TAIL � callsign of the tail vehicle (orange)
SPAN � distance in miles from lead to tail

MY CART Mode
Shows your own vehicle's stats:
SPD � current speed in mph
HDG � heading in degrees
BAT � battery percentage
ALT � altitude in meters
AHEAD / BEHIND � distance to nearest vehicles
TO LEAD / TO TAIL � distance to front and back of convoy

NODE Detail Mode
Tap any vehicle marker on the map to see its detail HUD showing status, speed, battery, SNR, position in convoy, heading, altitude, and last seen time.

Collapsed Mode
Tap the collapse button to minimize the HUD to a small pill showing unit count and lost count. Tap the pill to expand again.

GROUP TRACK
The group track feature draws a route trail on the map as the convoy moves. The trail shows where the convoy has been and helps vehicles find the route.

Starting the Track
In the GROUP HUD, tap START TRACK.
Any previous trail is cleared and a fresh trail begins.
Move the lead vehicle � a black line will grow behind it on the map.

Track Modes
LEAD ONLY (default) � only the lead vehicle's path is recorded. Recommended for most convoys.
ALL CARTS � every vehicle's path is recorded. Useful for seeing individual vehicle routes.

Stopping the Track
Tap STOP TRACK to stop accumulating new trail segments. The existing trail stays on the map.

TIP: Start the track at the ride start point � not in the staging area. This keeps the route trail clean and relevant.

OFF-TRACK ALERT
When a vehicle strays more than 150 feet from the established route trail, its callsign label on the map turns red. The label returns to normal when the vehicle returns to within 150 feet of the route.

NOTE: Off-track alerts only work when START TRACK has been pressed and route trail segments exist. There is no alert before the track is started.

KML TRACK RECORDING
KML recording saves your GPS track to a file that can be imported into Google Earth, Google Maps, or other mapping tools.

Recording a Track
Tap the REC button in the top-left corner of the map.
Enter a name for the track and tap START.
The REC button turns red while recording.
Tap the red button to access PAUSE, RESUME, or STOP & SAVE options.
The KML file is saved to Documents/my_tracks/ on your device.

Using Your KML File
Open your device file manager and navigate to Documents/my_tracks/.
The file is named [trackname]_[date]_[time].kml.
Transfer to a computer and open with Google Earth to view your route.

TIP: KML recording uses the tablet's GPS � not the Meshtastic radio. For best accuracy, ensure location permissions are granted and GPS is enabled on the tablet.

CONVOY ORDER & ROLES
The app automatically determines convoy order based on vehicle positions relative to the direction of travel. No manual configuration is required.

LEAD � the frontmost vehicle. Its path defines the convoy route trail.
TAIL � the rearmost vehicle. When tail passes a route segment, it resets to black.
All other vehicles � ordered by position between lead and tail.

NOTE: Convoy order is computed automatically each tick. With only 2 vehicles, lead and tail are the same two carts and the order may flip depending on heading calculation.

VEHICLE STATUS INDICATORS

FIELD TIPS
Disable network connectivity on all devices during convoy operations for privacy and battery life.
Mount the tablet where it is visible to the driver with minimal glare.
Charge all radios fully before a convoy � T1000-E batteries last 8-12 hours of active tracking.
If a vehicle's marker is not updating, check the radio is powered on and within mesh range of another node.
The app works best with 3 or more vehicles � lead/tail determination is most accurate with more nodes.
Use START TRACK at the official ride start, not in the staging area.
Tap any vehicle to see its battery level � low battery carts may drop out during long rides.

=== ADDENDUM_esri_tile_store_and_forward_2026-06-01.md ===
# ADDENDUM — Esri tile store-and-forward via AWS (idea captured 2026-06-01)

Append to the NEXT_SESSION_HANDOFF. This is an AWS-related architecture idea, also tied to the existing V3 Map Manager cloud-tile-sync work.

## The idea
Esri (ArcGIS) offers a FREE API tier of ~2 million tiles/month — enough headroom to TEST a new tile-download method at no cost.

The real design question (not just "download faster"): **should GroupTrack pull tiles from Esri ONCE, store them on AWS, and then store-and-forward to devices FROM AWS** — so the first user who pulls a given area populates the AWS tile cache, and every subsequent user/device for that same area reads from AWS instead of hitting Esri again. A caching-proxy / first-pull-populates-the-cloud model for TILES.

## Why it fits
- It's the SAME shape as the artifact first-occurrence model ("first arrival populates the shared store; others read the cached copy") — just applied to map tiles instead of trails/tracks/waypoints/routes.
- **Quota protection:** the Esri free tier (2M tiles/mo) burns fast if every device independently pulls tiles for the same popular areas (e.g. the St George / southern Utah corridor everyone rides). Pull-once-serve-many from AWS minimizes redundant Esri pulls and keeps usage under the free cap.
- **Ties into existing roadmap:** V3 Map Manager Phase C already specifies "AWS tile cloud sync per org," PROTECTED/PURGEABLE tile states, a 2GB cap, and auto-download on ride enrollment. This Esri store-and-forward is the upstream source side of that same tile-cloud system — worth designing them together.

## Open questions for when this is worked
- Esri free-tier license terms: confirm caching/re-serving tiles on AWS is permitted under the free API license (some tile providers prohibit re-hosting — check before building the cache). This is the gating legal/ToS question.
- Tile storage format on AWS: individual tiles vs packaged (.mbtiles) blobs; how devices request a region.
- Cache key + freshness: how AWS decides it already has an area (tile x/y/z coords) and whether/when tiles expire.
- Relationship to the existing osmdroid tile cache and the tile-storage media-scan fix (tiles should live OUT of media-scanned storage — see STATE_OF_PLAY follow-ups).

## Status
IDEA / to-investigate. Not started. Belongs in the AWS-session scope (store-and-forward is an AWS feature) and overlaps V3 Map Manager Phase C.


=== ADDENDUM_large_gpx_split_2026-06-01.md ===
# ADDENDUM — Large GPX (>32MB) handling: split approach (captured 2026-06-01)

Refines the existing OPEN item in v25_master_checklist Section C: "Large GPX >32MB: regex → string-loop (catastrophic backtracking)."

## The crash
GPX files over ~32MB crash the import process. These large files are not single huge recordings — they are **50+ separate GPX downloads concatenated into one file**. (onX-style markup exports bundling many tracks.)

## TWO fix approaches (not mutually exclusive)
1. **Parser fix (already noted in Section C):** the parser uses a regex that catastrophically backtracks on huge input. Switch regex → string-loop so the parser survives a big file as-is. Makes import robust to whatever size comes in.
2. **Split-before-import (Fred's framing, 2026-06-01):** since the big file is really N concatenated GPX downloads, SPLIT the oversized GPX into multiple ~50-track pieces BEFORE import, and process each piece. Sidesteps the size limit entirely by feeding the importer bite-sized chunks.

## Why split is appealing given the new dedup/recap work
- Each piece gets its own import pass + its own RECAP (the breakdown we just built) — more observable.
- The session-scoped in-memory dedup lookup already handles duplicates ACROSS batches correctly (begin/end session spans the pieces, or each piece checks against what's already in the DB), so splitting does NOT break dedup — same-geometry tracks across pieces still collapse / alias correctly.
- Keeps each import batch small = less memory pressure, less crash surface.

## To decide when worked
- Parser fix vs split vs both. Split alone may be enough to dodge the crash; parser fix makes it bulletproof regardless of input. Likely do split first (simpler, directly addresses the concatenated-download reality), keep parser-fix as the robustness backstop.
- Split mechanics: detect track boundaries in the GPX XML, emit chunks of ~50 tracks each, feed each to the existing import path.
- Where the split runs: pre-import step (scan the file, if >threshold or >N tracks, split into temp pieces, import each).

## Status
OPEN — refinement of the Section C >32MB item. Not started. Belongs with GPX Import Expansion work.

=== Convoy_EntryRestore_Design_2026-06-16.md ===
# Convoy Entry/Restore Design Map (before Stage 5 patching)
**2026-06-16 · base commit `fe8a0849a` (Stages 1-3 done: planning on shared fn)**

---

## THE PROBLEM (why convoy entry is broken)
Convoy on entry does GPS `setView` (ConvoyScreen onPageFinished ~656-660) → that move fires onViewportChanged → writes `lastViewport*` = the GPS-centered frame. So:
1. **lastViewport gets GPS-polluted on entry** (the stale-value trap Fred flagged). Anything reading it before a user pan gets a GPS point, not the work frame.
2. **Convoy has NO frame restore** — unlike planning (which does `fitBounds(pmSeed.bbox)` @693), convoy always lands on GPS, never the saved frame.
3. Convoy's JSON saves **no bbox** anyway (Stage 4 deferred it), so there's nothing to restore yet.

## FRED'S KEY INSIGHT (the fix direction)
**Seed `lastViewport*` from the JSON bbox on entry/restore — BEFORE any draw fires.** Then lastViewport is a real frame from the moment of restore, not GPS-polluted. This makes lastViewport trustworthy, which in turn makes saving `BBox(lastViewport*)` safe. The seed + the restore are the same fix.

---

## CONVOY PERSISTENCE MODEL (settled, from memory)
- **SESSION-ONLY.** Cold launch (fresh app start) → GPS fresh (no restore). In-session map-switch back → restore saved frame.
- Mechanism: cold launch DELETES convoy_panel.json (deleteMap on splash — NOT on base, must add). So:
  - **Cold launch:** convoy_panel.json absent/empty → no bbox → GPS setView (current behavior). Correct.
  - **In-session re-entry:** convoy_panel.json has bbox (saved during the session) → restore frame + seed lastViewport. Correct.
- So the SAME onPageFinished logic works for both: "if cmSeed.bbox != null → restore + seed; else → GPS." The deleteMap-on-cold-launch is what makes bbox absent on cold launch. **deleteMap is the gate between the two behaviors.**

## THE TWO WEBVIEW PATHS (the drift to unify)
Convoy has TWO WebView setups, each with its own onViewportChanged:
- **(A) REUSE path** — ConvoyScreen ~533 `val existing = viewModel.persistentWebView` → onVC@~569 → calls `processViewport` ✅ (already on shared fn, 573 fixed). Used on LATER entries (persistent WebView exists).
- **(B) CREATE path** — ConvoyScreen ~606 `WebView(ctx).apply{}` → onVC@~735 → INLINE draw ~730-815 (the old copy). Used on FIRST entry (no persistent WebView yet); stored to persistentWebView @~882.
- onPageFinished @626 is in the CREATE path (the WebView being built).

**Unify:** delete the inline draw (730-815); make path B's onViewportChanged call `processViewport` JSON-fed like path A. Then both paths draw identically through the shared fn.

---

## THE DESIGN — convoy entry/restore, step by step

### On entry (onPageFinished, both paths should behave the same):
```
1. Page loads (map HTML ready, JS draw fns exist).
2. Read cmSeed = readMap("convoy")   [already done @186 at composable top]
3. IF cmSeed.bbox != null  (in-session re-entry — saved frame exists):
     a. SEED lastViewport* = cmSeed.bbox.south/west/north/east   ← Fred's seed, BEFORE draw
     b. fitBounds(cmSeed.bbox)                                     ← restore the frame visually
     c. drawPersistedState("convoy", webView, context)            ← deterministic artifact restore
   ELSE  (cold launch — convoy_panel.json was deleted on splash):
     a. GPS setView (current behavior @656-660)                   ← fresh GPS
     b. (the GPS move fires onViewportChanged → draws via processViewport;
         lastViewport gets the GPS frame, which is correct for a fresh start)
```

### Why seed lastViewport in the restore branch (3a):
- The fitBounds(cmSeed.bbox) will eventually fire onViewportChanged and update lastViewport — BUT there's a window before that where lastViewport is stale/0.0. Seeding it explicitly (3a) closes that window: lastViewport is correct immediately, so any save firing before the fitBounds-moveend gets the right frame.
- Also, drawPersistedState (3c) uses the JSON bbox directly (not lastViewport), so the artifact restore is correct regardless. The seed is belt-and-suspenders for OTHER lastViewport readers (the save, route-snap queries @542).

### On save (saveConvoyState):
- After the seed design, `BBox(lastViewportSouth, ...)` is SAFE to save — lastViewport is seeded-from-JSON on restore and updated-by-pan during use, never GPS-polluted (because cold launch has no bbox → no restore → GPS is correct there; re-entry seeds the real frame).
- So Stage 4's bbox save folds back in here, AFTER the seed is in place.

### deleteMap (cold-launch clear) — the session-only gate:
- Add `MapStateStore.deleteMap("convoy")` at app splash/cold-launch (NOT on map entry — only true cold start).
- Effect: cold launch → convoy_panel.json gone → cmSeed.bbox null → GPS branch. In-session → file present → restore branch.
- ⚠️ deleteMap doesn't exist in MapStateStore yet — add `fun deleteMap(mapKey) { fileFor(mapKey).delete() }`.
- ⚠️ Must fire on COLD LAUNCH only, not every convoy entry (else re-entry wouldn't restore). Splash/Application onCreate, gated to once-per-process.

---

## STAGE 5 BUILD ORDER (small tested steps)
1. **Clobber fix** (Stage 4a — rowsFor from CheckedIds, no bbox yet). Build, JSON-pull test: all types persist on panel switch. [SAFE, isolated]
2. **Unify WebView paths:** delete inline draw 730-815; path B onVC calls processViewport JSON-fed. Build, test: convoy draws same on first entry and re-entry (no more order-dependent divergence).
3. **Entry restore + lastViewport seed:** onPageFinished → if cmSeed.bbox: seed lastViewport + fitBounds + drawPersistedState; else GPS. Build, test: re-entry restores frame+artifacts.
4. **Save bbox:** now safe — saveConvoyState saves BBox(lastViewport*). Build, JSON-pull test: bbox is real (matches work frame, not GPS point).
5. **deleteMap on cold launch:** add deleteMap + splash call. Test: cold launch → GPS; in-session re-entry → restore.
6. Commit convoy unified.

## OPEN QUESTIONS for Stage 5
- **Q-A:** Where exactly is the cold-launch hook? (Splash screen / Application.onCreate / a once-per-process flag.) Need to find convoy's app-entry point.
- **Q-B:** Does the GPS setView @656 also fire when restoring (we want it SKIPPED when bbox exists)? The if/else in onPageFinished handles it — confirm the GPS block is in the else.
- **Q-C:** The two onViewportChanged (569 + 735) — after unifying, is there ONE WebView or genuinely two instances? If persistentWebView is reused, only one survives; confirm we're not maintaining two.
- **Q-D:** route-snap queries @542-543 read lastViewport directly — the seed helps them too, but verify they're correct post-seed (separate from persistence but same variable).

# GroupTrack — EOD Handoff — 2026-07-11

## Focus of the day
V2.6a **Route+ persistence** — making an in-progress route survive navigation, recomposition, and process death, then recover cleanly on return.

## Where things landed (honest status)
Route+ persistence is **in progress — not committed, not shipped.** The SAVE side is verified working; the RESTORE side is mid-fix, and the current on-device build is broken (details below). A cleaner recovery design was reached this session and is the plan going forward.

## What is verified working (SAVE side)
- **Per-point draft save** — confirmed on device: a test draft captured 33 clean, correctly-snapped vertices (all lineId / segmentIndex / snapped fields correct).
- **WIP-save** — re-pull returns byte-identical geometry with fresh timestamps.
- **routeState now writes** to the panel JSON (the field wired into the map snapshot).
- **Auto-naming** — new routes auto-name to "Auto Saved In Progress" with no start-time dialog.
- **Discard "Delete in-progress"** — calls delete and clears state (works; earlier "didn't delete" was the "Roll back" button, which keeps the draft by design).

## Current build state (broken — do not ship)
- Phase-2 build compiled green (29m45s) and is installed on the sacrificial test device.
- **On device it is broken:** route-add mode is stuck armed at launch, so every map tap/pan/search drops a route point (map unusable), the add-on/off toggle appears dead, and a phantom first point lands at launch.
- **Cause:** the phase-2 approach seeded the armed flag from the persisted state and guarded the map's follow behavior — this combination leaves the flag stuck on. This approach is being replaced (see plan).

## The plan going forward (converged this session)
**Recovery-file dialog, triggered on map open.**

- **Trigger:** any time the map opens and a recovery-file route exists, recovery fires. (Map open = event; recovery file present = condition; recovery flow = action. No seeded flag, no nav-path conditions.)
- **Flow:** dialog — "Recovery file found — press OK to recover your route" — then on OK, *after the map draw completes*: load the recovery route, arm route-add, and position the map on the route's first vertex (center at zoom 15). The user then has the save/discard controls and must resolve.
- **Why it's clean:** the state JSON is rewritten on every draw, so it self-corrects — there is no stale state to manage. Resolving (complete or discard) is itself the write that clears the state. Resolution is the clearing; no separate flag logic needed.
- **Shared components:** the dialog, the load-after-draw-complete resume, and the position-on-first-vertex logic are built as common code that BOTH the convoy map and the planner map call — extracted from the existing planner resume logic, not duplicated.

## Before the next patch — two validations
1. **Blast radius** of the GPS-center-on-launch call — confirm via logcat it fires only on map load/return, not on pan or record.
2. **State-writes-on-draw** — confirm the map-state write (which carries routeState) actually fires on route on/off/resolve, not only on viewport change.

## Undo when the fix goes in
Back out the phase-2 armed-flag seed and the three follow-guards (the stuck-armed cause). Keep the routeState-write wiring and the auto-naming.

## Still open / lower priority
- In-progress picker didn't list a populated draft (an empty one showed) — inspect the list query.
- Broader V2.6 scope unchanged (loadQueue boot-loop hardening, clear-area/delete-area, the three regressions, etc.).

## Next-session pickup
1. Run the two validations (logcat blast-radius; state-write-on-draw).
2. Extract the planner resume into a shared recovery helper.
3. Wire the recovery-file check + dialog + resume into both maps' page-finished path.
4. Build, install on the test device, verify recovery on map-open.

# GroupTrack — EOD Handoff — 2026-07-12

## Focus of the day
Continued V2.6a **Route+ persistence / convoy bbox-restore** — but the day became a **direction change**: rolled back three days of uncommitted convoy viewport work, froze the convoy map, and moved Route+ to **planner-only**.

## Headline (read this first)
**The convoy map is FROZEN. Route+ is planner-only going forward.** Three days of convoy viewport/restore work was rolled back (it was never committed). Nothing shipped today; this was a rollback-and-replan session. The build is green on the rolled-back baseline + kept planner Route+.

## What happened today (honest narrative)
1. Chased a convoy reopen bug ("map opens in a new location / exit-vs-reopen frame not identical"). Two theories were pursued and **both were wrong** (fitBounds-recompute; artifact-dismiss clobber).
2. The **real root cause** was found in the JS: `convoy_map.html:163` — `setView()` calls `reportViewport()`, so **every programmatic map move re-saves itself**. Restore re-saves; the Kotlin-side guard could never catch a save that originates in JS. (z18 was the maxNativeZoom clamp ceiling caught in the loop.)
3. On the reverted, known-good 07-11 baseline, the **bbox-padding cumulative zoom-out** (trail shrinks / map area grows every reopen) **still reproduces** — proving it is a **pre-existing** convoy flaw, present before any of the three days' work.
4. Decision: **stop patching a system with no documentation or coherent mental model.** Freeze convoy. Roll back. Keep Route+ on the planner where it works.

## What was rolled back / kept
- **Rolled back** (`git checkout -- convoy_map.html ConvoyScreen.kt`): all convoy viewport/zoom work — viewport-save patch, zoom-persistence + isRestoring guard, the artifact-dismiss one-liner, the z12 diagnostic. All of it was **uncommitted**, so rollback was clean; last commit is 825f7babd (07-11, docs-only).
- **Kept** (still uncommitted, working planner Route+ + shared deps): `ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt` (planner — routeState-in-save, onNewRoute auto-name, onUndo per-point save), `MapStateStore.kt` (RouteState field; also an inert zoom field left over — harmless), `RouteDraftStore.kt`.
- **Build:** `assembleGoogleRelease` — **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**. Reverted convoy + kept planner compile clean against the shared MapStateStore signature.

## Still verified working (SAVE side — unchanged from 07-11)
Per-point draft save (33 clean snapped vertices), WIP-save (byte-identical re-pull), routeState writes to panel JSON, auto-name "Auto Saved In Progress", Discard "Delete in-progress".

## The plan going forward — PLANNER ONLY
Recovery is **simpler** now: Route+ is planner-only, so any auto-recovery JSON can only come from the planner — no cross-map source ambiguity, single writer/reader.

**Recovery model = 3-way resolution forced at launch-detection.** When an auto-recovery JSON exists at launch: dialog "auto-recovery route detected" → user must resolve one of three ways:
1. **Save as in-progress** (keep as WIP)
2. **Save as completed** (graduate to a permanent route — real name required)
3. **Discard** (delete the auto-recovery JSON)

This is the same resolution set the earlier exit-gates model used; only the trigger point differs (launch vs exit). Confirm exit-gates vs dialog-on-load as the chosen model at next session start — they were alternatives and this revives dialog-on-load.

## Next-session checklist (all planner unless noted)
1. **Remove Route+ from the convoy artifact panel** — the only convoy touch, and it is a *removal* of an entry point (not editing convoy's restore/save logic). Respects the freeze.
2. **Planner: New Route drops the name prompt** — creates the auto-recovery JSON instead (no start dialog).
3. **Planner: Save-in-progress renames** the auto-recovery JSON to the user's chosen name.
4. **Planner: check auto-recovery JSON existence on load.**
5. **Planner: if found → dialog → 3-way resolution** (in-progress / completed / discard).
6. **Fix the padding issue on the planner** — same cumulative bbox-padding-on-restore drift. ⚠ **SHARED-FUNCTION CHECK FIRST:** trace whether the padding/restore path is shared with convoy. If separable → fix planner's copy. If truly shared → the fix also touches convoy (would fix convoy's drift as a side effect) → needs explicit sign-off before proceeding, since convoy is frozen. Fix direction: don't re-pad an already-padded saved bbox; silent-setView if the planner JS self-saves like convoy's.
7. **Fix the draw yes/no toggle on the planner** — point-registration guard: a tap becomes a route vertex ONLY when draw is ON. Launch = draw OFF (taps pan); user explicitly arms; only then do taps register. Draw-mode = explicit `DrawMode {OFF, ON}` enum, program-set OFF at load, never persisted, one source of truth driving switch + guard + JS bridge. **This exists only in Route+ → planner-only, no convoy/shared risk.**

## Known pre-existing convoy bug (documented, NOT fixing — frozen)
Convoy reopen = **cumulative zoom-out**: restore reads saved bbox → pads it → saves the padded bbox → next reopen pads that → frame grows each cycle. Reproduces on the 07-11 baseline (pre-existing). Left as-is. Real fix if convoy is ever revived: silent setView (no reportViewport) for restore + don't re-pad an already-padded bbox. **Prerequisite for ANY convoy change = document the layered process (Kotlin ↔ JS bridge ↔ Leaflet ↔ self-saving setView ↔ shared MapStateStore) first.**

## Doc-process status
- **Release notes (HTML asset):** NOT updated with Route+ (still unshipped). Only the date stamp carried forward as superset — no new user-facing work shipped today.
- **Manual (HTML asset):** Route+ persistence section stays **unapplied** (unshipped). The staged manual-updates doc corrected: recovery is **planner-only**, not "both maps."
- **Living master:** updated (this session) to reflect freeze + planner-only pivot + rollback.

## Still open / backlog (unchanged)
In-progress picker not listing a populated draft; loadQueue boot-loop immunity; saveQueue atomic-write hardening; clear-area/delete-area; the three no-radio regressions; lead-cart re-engineer; git push blocked by 3 large .db in history; Esri tile-cost strategy; V2.6 release delayed ~4 weeks.
