COMPLETED — 2026-07-31 · Trails display, canvas renderer, tap fixes
Graduated out of the Living Master. Six files, 249 insertions. Thirteen builds.
Two bugs closed that had been misattributed for months, one diagnosed to a
specific July commit, and a route-mode design settled that is smaller than what it replaces.
⭐⭐ 1 — TRAILS: the six-month "not fixable because of volume" bug
SpatialDbManager.queryTrailsByViewport used LIMIT with no
ORDER BY. SQLite therefore returned whichever rows it reached first — rowid order,
i.e. OSM import insertion order, which carries no spatial meaning.
At z8 roughly 89,536 Utah trails matched the bbox and 500 drew. Any viewport change returned a
DIFFERENT arbitrary 500. Nothing was ever misplaced — the membership churned.
What identified it — both from behaviour, neither from code
"Seems to load bands by longitude." A Geofabrik extract walks its own spatial index, so
insertion order carries a rough geographic sweep. The first 500 by rowid is a STRIPE, not a scatter.
"Adding Arizona places the trails below the tracks." Utah imported first and holds the low
rowids, so every Arizona trail sorted after every Utah trail. Import order made visible.
⭐ Volume was never the variable. smoothFactor is a per-polyline screen-space tolerance and
behaves identically at 500 artifacts or 89,000. The story that this was unfixable because of trail
count made a prediction — that doubling coverage would worsen it — and that prediction failed.
⭐ And the tap test is what redirected the whole hunt. Taps fired on trails where they were
DRAWN, proving Leaflet placed them exactly where the data said. The data was never wrong; there was
just an arbitrary subset of it.
The fix
ORDER BY (CASE WHEN name IS NULL OR name = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
         ((max_lat-min_lat)*(max_lat-min_lat)+(max_lon-min_lon)*(max_lon-min_lon)) DESC
Named first — OSM carries no carto_code, so name is the only quality
signal. Then largest bbox extent (squared diagonal, no sqrt needed for ordering, both columns already
indexed). Plus minZoom 11 and a 10,000 row cap as a safety valve, not the mechanism.
⚠ Why tracks were never affected: a few hundred exist, so their cap never binds. That is also why
it appeared to "resolve at z12" — that is simply where viewport trail density drops under the cap.
No z12 threshold exists in the code.
⭐⭐ 2 — CANVAS RENDERER: tolerance had never worked
renderer: L.svg({ tolerance: 44 })
tolerance is an option of L.Canvas. L.SVG ignores it. Under SVG,
hit-testing is done natively by the browser against the &lt;path&gt; element — so the
effective tap target was the stroke width, 3 pixels. On both maps, since at least 07-08.
Device evidence: ~40 taps at z18, 3 hits, 0 trails.
⛔ Note this was suspected of the OPPOSITE — that a 44px halo was swallowing taps at OSM density.
It was doing nothing at all. And commit ef00baca8 had raised it from 18 to 44 believing
it worked.
Fix: both maps to L.canvas. ⭐ Tracks pinned to L.svg()
per-layer so polylineDecorator keeps the per-path geometry its arrows need — Leaflet
takes a renderer per layer, not only per map.
⚠ Canvas also removes the one-DOM-element-per-path cost that ANR'd the WebView at 120,000 trails.
The z11 gate and 10,000 cap are worth revisiting now that constraint is gone — separately, with
its own test.
⭐ 3 — CONVOY LONG-PRESS WAYPOINTS
Seven long-presses produced ZERO console output while taps logged cleanly. convoy_map.html
uses map.on('contextmenu'), and Leaflet 1.9 removed its own tap handler — it relies
on the browser firing a native contextmenu. ConvoyScreen.kt:938 installs a
setOnTouchListener on the WebView (the planner has none), which intercepts before
View.onTouchEvent — and onTouchEvent is what starts the long-press timer.
Fix: detect the long-press in that listener — 500 ms timer, 20 px move slop — and call
longPressAt(x,y), which converts a container point to a latlng and calls the EXISTING
bridge. pendingWaypoint and the dialog were complete all along; only the gesture never
arrived.
⚠ Timer state is held in remembered arrays, not MutableState — the
listener lives in update = { } which re-runs on every recomposition, and state mutated
from a touch event would reinstall the listener mid-gesture.
⭐ Canvas later restored native contextmenu as well, so onMapLongPress now fires
twice per press from two paths. Harmless (second write wins) but the timer is now redundant.
⭐ 4 — addPointMode DEFAULTED TRUE
var addPointMode by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
    // Tap:Route(on)/Artifact(off) — consumed by onMapTap next build
"Next build" never came. The flag shipped defaulted ON, so every planner track tap was
suppressed — device-confirmed as PLANNER SUPPRESSED by addPointMode with no route
ever drawn. Convoy has no such guard, which is why the two maps behaved differently.
The only assignment is :1256 — addPointMode = armed — so the value still
comes from arming; it just no longer STARTS armed. The guard itself is correct and stays.
⭐ Fixing it also restored planner long-press, since :553 reads the same flag.
⚠ IN THE COMMIT, TO REMOVE BEFORE RELEASE
smoothFactor: 0 on trails, both maps. Device-disproven as a fix for the splay.
Left in deliberately — small, isolated, reversible in seconds, and separating it at the end of a long
session was judged the greater risk.
Three WAYPOINT-TRACE log lines in ConvoyScreen.kt. One fires
every 5 seconds (the convoy screen recomposes on a timer) and would spam production logs.
Retained by decision until the spatial-labels work is done, since that will need the same tracing.

⚠ METHOD NOTE — thirteen builds, and why
Seven hypotheses were tested and eliminated on trails alone before the cause was found; four more
on convoy taps. Every one was a plausible mechanism, and every one was disproven on device.
⭐ What actually solved both bugs was reasoning about BEHAVIOUR, not code — the longitude
banding, the Arizona ordering, the tap test, and "planner has popups and convoy doesn't, which is
backwards". Each was decisive and none came from reading source.
⚠ The structural cost driver is patchy instrumentation. Tap handlers log, bridges mostly do
not, state writes never do. Every hunt begins by spending a build to see anything at all. A
one-time tracing pass across tap → bridge → state → composition, kept permanently, would repay itself
immediately.
⭐ Fred, at the end: "our errors were at 30,000 feet and we were dealing in the details."
State the rule in English first and check the code against it — not the reverse. Both real fixes came
from that direction.

Convoy Download Queues Panel Width FixCOMPLETED TASK · 2026-07-22 · shipped in Rel 2.6c
The problem
On the Convoy map the DOWNLOAD QUEUES panel rendered broken: the CLEAR DONE button wrapped to ONE LETTER PER LINE down a vertical column, and queued entries fragmented with digits scattered down the right edge. The same panel on the Planning map rendered correctly. Downloads themselves were unaffected — progress, tile counts and controls all worked; this was purely visual.
Discovered while recapturing manual screenshots for 2.6c: the Convoy queues capture was unusable as documentation.
Root cause
The two panels are separate hand-mirrored copies, not a shared component. grep -rn "DOWNLOAD QUEUES" returned two independent render sites, and Convoy's carries the comment "Real download-queue monitor (matches planning &quot;DOWNLOAD QUEUES&quot;)" — a duplicate that had drifted from its model.
Both wrap the same inner DownloadQueuePanel composable at identical font sizes. Only the outer Surface modifier differed:
// Convoy  (ConvoyScreen.kt ~1453) - BROKEN
modifier = Modifier
    .align(Alignment.TopEnd)
    .statusBarsPadding()
    .padding(top = 32.dp, end = 8.dp)
    .width(260.dp)
// Planning (ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt ~814) - CORRECT
modifier = Modifier
    .align(Alignment.Center)
    .padding(16.dp)
    .fillMaxWidth(0.90f)
On the test device (800px wide) a fixed 260dp is roughly ONE THIRD of Planning's 90%-of-screen width. Identical content forced into a third of the space wraps per-character — hence the vertical "CLEAR DONE".
The fix
Bring Convoy's modifier chain in line with Planning's. .statusBarsPadding() and .padding(top=32,end=8) were dropped — they existed only to tuck the panel under the top-right QUEUES button, which is irrelevant once centered.
Decisions + rejected alternatives
Centered vs wider-but-still-top-right. Considered keeping TopEnd and merely widening to ~360dp / fillMaxWidth(0.55f) (less map obstruction). REJECTED — Fred asked for parity with Planning, and parity also means the manual screenshot matches across both maps.
⭐ Substituting the Planning screenshot for the Convoy one in the manual. Proposed as a shortcut while the bug was still live. REJECTED: it would depict a screen that does not exist in the app, and would specifically HIDE the bug (a cropped Planning panel lays out correctly). Failure mode: a tester sees mangled text, checks the manual, sees a clean panel, concludes their install is broken → false bug report.
Interim honesty. Before the fix was authorized, the BROKEN capture was embedded with a "Known issue (V2.6c)" note directing users to the Planning panel for a clearer view. Once the fix shipped, the image was replaced and the note deleted.
Freeze question. ConvoyScreen.kt is the FROZEN file. Proceeded because the change is a Compose layout attribute in a self-contained panel — nothing near the WebView, JS bridge, Leaflet, self-saving setView, or MapStateStore (the layered process the freeze protects). Verified by grep that Convoy's panel is a separate copy, so Planning could not regress.
Implementation
Patch script patch_convoy_queues_width_2026-07-22.py, per standing conventions: uniquely-dated, written to /c/Users/kixaz/Downloads/, dry-run by default (--apply to write), count==1 anchor guard with clean abort, idempotent marker guard, CRLF detection and preservation, timestamped .bak. The anchor was validated against the exact source text before delivery.
Dry-run: 1 anchor match, CRLF detected. Applied clean. assembleGoogleRelease BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 11m 03s — no imports needed (Alignment.Center, padding, fillMaxWidth all already used in the file).
Verification
Installed to Droid 2 and reopened Convoy → QUEUES. Confirmed: panel centered at 90% width; CLEAR DONE reads horizontally; HOLD / CANCEL ALL / CLEAR DONE in a proper row; queued entries intact with tile counts aligned; layout matches Planning. Recaptured and embedded in the 2.6c manual, replacing the broken interim image.
Lessons
Hand-mirrored duplicates drift. A comment saying "matches planning" documented an intention, not a guarantee. Where two screens must look alike, share the component or expect divergence.
Grep before assuming a component is shared. Had these been one component, changing the width would have regressed Planning; two greps established independence before any edit.
The freeze is about a layer, not a file. Compose layout attributes in ConvoyScreen.kt are safely changeable; the map/JS/Leaflet/state-store tangle is not.
Ship the honest picture. Documenting a known issue accurately beat depicting a screen that doesn't exist — and the note cost nothing to remove once fixed.

Download Maps by Corridor &mdash; design, build, proof, cutoverCOMPLETED TASK &middot; Phase 2 &middot; 2026-07-24 &middot; patches F, G1&ndash;G4, H (+ I failed, J) &middot; proven on device
The full record for the corridor feature, from the measurement that motivated it through the cutover that retired the bbox path for tracks. The Living Master entry is gone &mdash; this is the record. Read this before touching corridor derivation, ConvoyCorridorWorker, or the artifact panel's SAVE MAPS controls. Prerequisite reading: COMPLETED_TASK_download_queue_schema_and_panel_2026-07-24.html (the queue had to carry job type and priority before corridor entries could exist).
The headline
PROVEN ON DEVICE Tester track "bar 10" &mdash; the ~100-mile figure-7 that started this whole investigation:
ModelTiles queued (3 sources)Notes
bbox (old)1,000,000+~95% empty desert; Fred: "8 hours to download an area that will not be ridden"
corridor (new)65,000 + 21,000 + 21,000 &asymp; 107,000half-mile buffer, same geography
&asymp;90% reduction. Built, queued and downloaded end to end on the planning map. G1&ndash;G4 all compiled first try (14m03s).
&#9888; Three caveats that must travel with this number.
Bar 10 is the BEST CASE. It is the longest, thinnest track available, so it shows corridor at its most favourable. A compact track's bbox is already close to its corridor and the gain there will be modest. When quoting this to testers, say so &mdash; the headline comes from the worst-shaped track.
This is BEFORE the z-cap. If TOPO+ really tops out at z15, a meaningful slice of its 21,000 is requests that will 404. That saving compounds on top of this one and must be measured separately &mdash; two variables, two measurements.
The 894,507 planning baseline was not the comparable number. 894,507 was sizeTiles (the SAT-sizing figure); the real bbox total queued across all sources was higher, over a million. The two were never the same quantity.
The 65K/21K/21K split is per source and uneven because of layer counts, not different geometry &mdash; same corridor, SAT carrying 3 layers where the others carry fewer.
Why bbox was the wrong model
Measured 07-23. Bar 10 is a single path ~100 miles long with a ~10-mile spread at the top &mdash; "like a figure 7". It alone accounted for 22% of all tiles in a 10-track import (894,507 sizeTiles &rarr; 18 cells per source). Its bounding rectangle is ~100&times;10 miles while the ridden corridor is ~half a mile wide.
&#9888; Segmentation was never the bug. Every split in the 07-23 trace satisfied ceil(sizeTiles/50000) exactly. Four theories died on inspection before the real finding landed. The MODEL was wrong, not the math &mdash; which is why no amount of tuning the splitter would ever have helped.
&#11088; THE RULE
Anything TRACK-based or ROUTE-based submits a CORRIDOR download. User-DRAWN area downloads keep the BBOX. The user drew a rectangle &rarr; the rectangle is the request. The user picked a track or route &rarr; they want the line and its immediate surroundings, not the rectangle enclosing it.
Architecture &mdash; the decisions that shaped it
&#11088;&#11088;&#11088; downloadType SELECTS THE WORKER
Fred: "so the downloadType would specify the worker. great design when we get to the delete function." launchWorker dispatches on type and enqueues a different Worker class &mdash; dispatch at the boundary, not a branch inside shared logic (patch F).
DownloadTypeWorker
AREAConvoyDownloadWorker
CORRIDORConvoyCorridorWorker (new)
MAP_SOURCE_REFRESHConvoyDownloadWorker (refresh branch)
DELETE_AREA_TILESConvoyDeleteWorker (when written)
&#11088; Why declaring the 4th enum value early paid off. Delete removes tiles rather than fetching &mdash; opposite direction, different completion semantics, no network. A shared-worker model would need a flag threaded through a download worker plus branches inside it. With type-selected workers it is simply a third worker that never touches the network, and nothing existing changes. It also makes priority 0 coherent: deletes run first because they free storage.
&#9940; CORRIDOR IS NOT FITTED INTO THE AREA MACHINERY
Claude drifted there twice &mdash; first a downloadType parameter threaded through submitDownload, then "add a branch to ConvoyDownloadWorker" &mdash; and Fred overruled both: "why are we fitting this into the area download box. it is its own code? does not exist?" and "convoy download worker would be replaced by a corridor version?" None of the corridor path existed; it is all new code ALONGSIDE the area path. ConvoyDownloadWorker was not touched.
&#11088; Only TWO shared artifacts were affected
QueueEntry gains geomHash: String = "" so an entry can name its track &mdash; written only by the corridor process, read only by the corridor worker, therefore inert to everything else. Existing readers use opt* defaults and ignore unknown keys; the four existing construction sites needed no edits.
launchWorker picks the Worker class by type.
That is the whole footprint. Buffer width needs no field &mdash; it is a constant (the half-mile getTrackBbox already uses).
&#11088; What the entry carries &mdash; Option B
&#9940; Run-boxes were RULED OUT. Fred: "cannot use boxes, the startup time for new area requests is long 5-10 seconds added to every new bbox request. not workable." 30 run-boxes = 3&ndash;5 minutes of pure startup overhead before a tile moves &mdash; worse than the problem being solved.
&#9940; Option A (serialize the tile list into the entry) was REJECTED &mdash; a 60K-tile list is megabytes per entry in download_queue.json, the one file with no recovery path on a release build.
&#11088; Option B shipped: the entry stores a geometry reference &mdash; geomHash + downloadType=CORRIDOR (+ bbox for display/progress). The worker re-derives the tile list at run time. Startup cost is paid once per corridor entry, not per box.
Persistence concern is mitigated by hasTile(): the mbtiles store is the source of truth for what is already down, so a corridor entry re-derives its list on resume and simply skips what landed. The tile list never needs persisting.
&#9888; Accepted duplication &mdash; deliberate, and it has a cost
ConvoyCorridorWorker duplicates progress (updateProgress), completion (markComplete), notifications, and the downloadTiles call. Different tile derivation, same plumbing. Cost: a change to any of that plumbing now lands in two places. Traded deliberately for the clean split &mdash; but see the open refresh-completion issue below, which is exactly this cost coming due.
Derivation &mdash; the model
The standard GIS name is buffering a linestring, but for tile downloading no polygon is needed: walk the line's points and, for each, emit the tiles within the buffer radius at each zoom, deduped into a SET. Overlaps and self-intersections (the figure-7 doubles back on itself) collapse automatically. No join geometry, no self-intersection cases.
Buffer width = the same half-mile the bbox path already used &mdash; getTrackBbox pads 0.00724&deg; lat and 0.00724/cos(midLat) lon (SpatialDbManager:1915). Keeping the same value made the PoC directly comparable to the old baseline.
&#9888; WKT coordinate order is lon lat &mdash; SpatialDbManager:1763 flips with parts[1], parts[0]. Getting this backwards puts the geometry in the wrong hemisphere.
Geometry shapes: tracks are MULTILINESTRING or LINESTRING; routes are plain LINESTRING. Parse model copied from wktToGeoJsonCoords (SpatialDbManager:340-361), which handles both &mdash; strip prefix/suffix, and for MULTI split on "),(" then trim parens. It returns a JSON string so it was not directly reusable; a sibling returning POINTS was written instead.
&#11088; MULTILINESTRING matters: disjoint segments are walked separately and buffered independently. That is precisely the case where the bbox spans the empty gap between segments and the corridor does not.
&#11088; The corridor worker filters PRE-FETCH
The open question from 07-23 &mdash; does hasTile() skip the request or only the write? &mdash; resolved: MBTilesStore.hasTile is at MBTilesStore.kt:136; ConvoyDownloadWorker:61 filters and sizes totalTiles off the filtered list (:65), so the refresh branch genuinely skips requests, while the main path (:111-117) has no filter at all and downloads everything.
So the corridor worker copies the :61 pattern. Without it a resumed corridor would re-request every tile from Esri and only then find it already had them &mdash; full network cost paid twice, real money on per-tile pricing. It also makes totalTiles honest: remaining work, not the whole corridor.
What shipped &mdash; patch by patch
PatchWhat it did
FlaunchWorker dispatches on downloadType &mdash; the boundary that makes everything else possible
G1corridor derivation &mdash; geometry &rarr; points (SpatialDbManager), points+buffer &rarr; tile SET (ConvoyTileCalculator)
G2enqueueCorridor &mdash; build + enqueue, geomHash on the entry, one entry per source
G3ConvoyCorridorWorker &mdash; derives from geometry, filters pre-fetch against hasTile, downloads per layer with foreground progress
G4wiring &mdash; orange SAVE MAPS CORR button beside the green area button on BOTH maps, pendingCorridorHash carrying the hash to onProceed, cleared on proceed AND cancel
HCUTOVER &mdash; area button deleted from the artifact panel; track import swapped bbox &rarr; corridor
Iconvoy confirm centring &mdash; FAILED TO COMPILE, see below
Jconvoy confirm centring, done correctly &mdash; Box wrapper
The shared ConvoyDownloadConfirm prompt (source selection + replace-tiles Y/N) is used unchanged by both paths. That is user intent &mdash; identical regardless of geometry &mdash; so each caller passes its own onProceed lambda in rather than the prompt branching on a mode flag.
The cutover (patch H) &mdash; two decisions worth keeping
1. The area button was DELETED, not flagged off
The side-by-side existed to produce the comparison, and it has. Leaving a disabled path behind is exactly how gridCells and downloadMapsForTrackHash both survived their own replacements and later masqueraded as live code &mdash; two dead functions this project has already had to chase down.
The onDownloadMaps parameter stays on the composable &mdash; the two screens still pass it and removing it would touch call sites for no benefit &mdash; but nothing renders it, so the area path is unreachable from the artifact panel. Deleting the parameter is a separate cleanup if it ever matters.
2. The import swap was a LOOP, not a substitution
The old call was one submitDownload covering all slots. Corridor is one entry per source, so the import loops the slots. Everything needed was already in hand at ConvoyTrackOps:586 &mdash; gh (computed one line earlier), downloadMapSlots, replaceExisting. getTrackBbox is no longer called there.
&#9888; Ten tracks &times; three sources = 30 queue rows, not 10. That is the same shape the area path already produced (submitDownload looped slots internally), so the panel needed no change &mdash; but the row COUNT is per track per source, and testers will see it.
&#9888; enqueueCorridor DERIVES the corridor to get its tile count, so a large import does that work per track per source on the IO thread. Already an IO thread at that call site, so no new threading &mdash; but a 10-track import will spend real time in derivation before the first tile moves. If that reads as a hang to a tester, it isn't; it is the cost Option B deliberately pays once per entry instead of 5&ndash;10s per run-box.
Untouched: area downloads from the map (draw-a-box) work exactly as before. The cutover changed only the artifact panel and the importer.
&#9940; Patch I &mdash; a wrong diagnosis worth recording
The bug: the shared ConvoyDownloadConfirm popup renders mid-panel on CONVOY and overflows the bottom &mdash; its buttons unreachable unless the device is rotated to landscape. Planning shows the same dialog centred and fully accessible.
The diagnosis (wrong): one missing modifier.
convoy    ConvoyScreen.kt:2014        modifier = Modifier.padding(16.dp)
planning  ConvoyMapViewerScreen:1569  modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.Center).padding(16.dp)
It looked like the same drift pattern as the 07-22 queues-panel width bug &mdash; two hand-mirrored call sites where one lost a modifier the other kept. Patch I simply added .align(Alignment.Center) to convoy's chain.
It did not compile: 'fun Modifier.align' cannot be called in this context with an implicit receiver.
The real cause: Modifier.align() is a BoxScope extension &mdash; it only exists inside a Box. Planning's dialog sits in a Box; convoy's sits in a Column (ConvoyScreen ~1495). The missing modifier was never drift between mirrored call sites; it was a consequence of different containers.
&#11088; THE LESSON: the symptom matched a known bug, the cause did not. Pattern-matching to a bug this project has already seen is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis &mdash; and here the previous bug's shape actively misled, because the fix that worked last time was scope-illegal this time.
Patch J &mdash; bring a Box rather than borrow scope
Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize(), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) {
    ConvoyDownloadConfirm( ... )
}
contentAlignment centres the child without needing the scope extension, so it works regardless of what encloses it. fillMaxSize makes the Box the whole viewport, so "centre" means centre of the screen &mdash; which is what stops a tall dialog running off the bottom. The dialog's own modifier = Modifier.padding(16.dp) was left alone; only its placement was ever wrong.
Anchor design note: patch J's anchor spans the whole call &mdash; open paren through the closing brace of the enclosing if &mdash; so the wrapper's braces cannot land in the wrong place. That is the one way this class of fix fails twice.
&#9888; Convoy freeze &mdash; why this was allowed. ConvoyScreen.kt is frozen, but the freeze protects a LAYER, not the file: the Kotlin&harr;JS&harr;Leaflet&harr;self-saving-setView&harr;shared-MapStateStore tangle. This is a Compose layout wrapper around an overlay dialog &mdash; nothing near the WebView, the JS bridge, or map state. Same reasoning as the 07-22 queues width fix, which shipped clean.
Rollout &mdash; as executed
DONE Corridor button added alongside the area button on both maps (G4), so the same track could be run both ways on real geography with nothing regressing for testers.
DONE Compared &mdash; bar 10, ~107,000 vs 1,000,000+.
DONE Removed the area button from the artifact panel (H).
DONE Replaced the bbox derivation in track import (H).
PENDING Install H+J build on Droid 1 and Droid 2; confirm the ETA renders once two corridor jobs start and finish on a stamped build.
Deliberately NOT done (deferred, by design):
No splitting. One entry per track per source. Measure first; decide on segmenting corridors after real numbers exist.
Route corridors &mdash; the routes table has min/max lat/lon and geometry is fetchable by id (SpatialDbManager:1755), but there is no getRouteBbox and no download-by-route path at all today. The route corridor is a NEW capability with nothing legacy to preserve &mdash; build it right the first time, no migration risk.
Delete-area tiles &mdash; the enum value exists, the worker does not.
&#9888; ROLLBACK NOTE: a corridor entry read by an older build parses fine (defaulted reads) but that build's worker would download its BBOX. Only matters if a rollback ships &mdash; but it would be silent, and it would be the exact behaviour this task removed.
Open items this task leaves behind
These are live in the Living Master; recorded here so the corridor context travels with them.
OPEN Refresh does not log as a completed job (found 07-24). Bears directly on the corridor ETA &mdash; see the Living Master entry. The accepted per-worker duplication means completion is called separately by each worker, so this class of miss can exist independently in ConvoyCorridorWorker.
OPEN Per-source z-level download limits &mdash; maxZoomForSource() is a stub returning DOWNLOAD_ZOOM and ignoring its argument, so everything pulls to z18 including sources capped at 15. corridorTiles inherits the same gap &mdash; it has no source awareness either, so fixing the stub alone will NOT fix corridor; the source must be passed in.
METHOD The xref docs index declarations. onDownloadMaps is a lambda parameter and appears in none of them &mdash; same class as the earlier @JavascriptInterface miss. xref for candidates, grep for call sites.
Durable lessons
When the math is right and the answer is still wrong, check the MODEL. Segmentation was provably correct at every split; the rectangle was the wrong shape for a line. Four theories died before anyone questioned the geometry.
Dispatch at the boundary, not inside shared logic. Type-selects-worker meant corridor cost two shared-artifact changes and touched ConvoyDownloadWorker not at all &mdash; and delete-area now costs nothing existing.
Delete the replaced path in the same commit. This codebase has already been misled twice by dead functions that outlived their replacements.
A matching symptom is not a matching cause. Patch I failed because the previous bug's fix was scope-illegal in the new container.
Measure one variable at a time. The corridor number and the z-cap number must not be taken together, or neither is attributable.

OSM Trail Import — C1 ACQUIRE + C2 REDUCE
  Completed 2026-07-28 · commit 3fd526517 ·
  branch feature/convoy-event-ride · release 2.6e ·
  11 files changed, 2,912 insertions
Permanent per-task record. Full design and fix detail retained so the feature can be
reviewed or changed later without reconstructing the reasoning.
What the feature does
The user downloads a Geofabrik state extract in their browser. The app detects it,
adopts it, reduces it to a small local database, and stages it for import. GroupTrack
never obtains, hosts, or distributes OSM-derived data — which is what keeps ODbL
share-alike off Fred entirely rather than merely mitigated.
Working directory
/sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/osm/&lt;slug&gt;/
    ledger.json                       created C1, renamed away at C4
    &lt;slug&gt;-latest-free.gpkg.zip       RECOVERY POINT 1
    &lt;slug&gt;.gpkg                       transient, exists only inside C2
    ready_for_import.db               RECOVERY POINT 2
Architecture rules (durable)
RuleStatement
R1Stage is DERIVED FROM DISK, never stored. No status field anywhere.
R2Only the zip and the skinny are recovery points. The .gpkg never is.
R3Existence means COMPLETE — .part + atomic rename.
R5Derivation happens at MOMENTS: panel open, job done, return from background.
R7On ACQUIRE entry, sweep debris only. Never blind-delete the directory.
R1's unplanned payoff. Because stage derives from disk, the panel can be
destroyed and recreated and lands in exactly the same place. That rule was written for
crash recovery — it is what makes C3's area-selection handoff possible with no state
flag at all: row 3 closes the panel, the map's bbox submission relaunches it, and
nothing needs preserving across the gap.
C1 ACQUIRE
MediaStore query, not a filesystem scan — browser-agnostic and
    location-independent. findCandidates() queries
    MediaStore.Downloads.
adoptCandidate() copies via ContentResolver.openInputStream
    → .part → atomic rename. Not renameTo —
    content:// plus cross-volume.
probeDownloads() returns a sealed AcquireProbe:
    NotFound / BadFile / Found / Several.
    Deliberately no StillDownloading — Android browsers are indistinguishable
    from "not done yet".
FIELD FIX — dated filenames. Geofabrik serves the same product under two
spellings: utah-latest-free.gpkg.zip and
arizona-260728-free.gpkg.zip. The probe demanded "latest" and reported
"extract not found" for a 610 MB file sitting in Downloads. Now accepts either.
Slug derivation strips the trailing -latest or a trailing 6–8 digit
date. Not "text before the first hyphen" — that would reduce
north-carolina-260728 to north, and nobody would notice until a
two-word state.
C2 REDUCE
The catalog — what gets extracted is data, not code
assets/osm_layers.json declares each layer's source table, target table,
columns, and optional filter. Fred: "a json to control items placed in skinny import
file … so we edit json rather than recompile code."
An asset alone would not have delivered that — assets are baked into the
APK, so editing one still means a rebuild. The catalog is therefore read from an
on-disk override at
/sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/config/osm_layers.json if present, falling back
to the asset. Public directory on purpose: run-as is blocked on release
builds, so app-private storage is not reachable by adb push.
A broken override falls back and logs rather than bricking the feature.
The failure mode of a hand-edited config is a typo, and a typo should cost you your
customization — not the import.
Shipped state: trails, places, natural enabled;
pois present but disabled. Flipping one boolean and pushing an override is how
you find out whether 48k POIs help or clutter — without a rebuild and without another
610 MB unzip.
The decoder
Ported from osm_gpkg_subset_v2_2026-07-27.py, itself written because v1
would have lied: it emitted WKT as "lon lat, lon lat" at fixed
precision while the app writes comma-with-no-space and shortest-round-trip
Double.toString(). Every feature would have reported as new.
THE SIGNED-BYTE TRAP. Python's blob[3] is unsigned 0–255;
Kotlin's Byte is signed. A direct transcription of
(blob[3] &gt;&gt; 1) &amp; 0x07 sign-extends and returns the wrong envelope
size — which starts the WKB read at the wrong offset and yields plausible garbage
coordinates, not an exception. Every byte read masks 0xFF first.
⚠ Correction made during the work: the GPKG flags byte uses only bits 0–5,
so it never exceeds 0x3F and cannot sign-extend on valid input. The mask
there is defensive. The mask that is genuinely load-bearing is in
geomHash, where SHA-256 digest bytes are uniformly distributed and roughly
half exceed 0x80.
One thing got simpler in Kotlin. The Python contorted itself to imitate
Double.toString() and carried a warning about exponent notation near the prime
meridian. In Kotlin we are the authority — whatever Double.toString()
emits is by definition what the app emits. The edge case does not get handled; it stops
existing.
Point layers run first — the decoder self-test
After the GPKG header a point is two doubles: almost nothing to get wrong in the body.
So a bad envelope offset shows up against a town you recognise in seconds, rather than
silently poisoning 89,536 linestrings where it is invisible. Any point outside the layer's
own declared extent aborts the run before trails are written.
Validated on the PC first: Phoenix decoded 0.05 km from its known
position, 1,581 of 1,581 Arizona places inside the declared extent.
Progress model
Fred: "a simple counter per type, what % of that type has processed, check box when
type is completed" and "time is preferred just relative to each type being
transferred."
No blended bar, no whole-job ETA. Unzip moves BYTES; passes move ROWS; per-row cost differs
by orders of magnitude between a 1,581-row places pass and a 134,242-row trails pass. Each
type owns its denominator, and the rate window never crosses a type boundary
— carrying a rate across one is exactly how the shipped download ETA came out ~50× long.
⚠ Two bugs found by using it, and their real causes
1. PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF returns a row. SQLite reports back
the mode it settled on, making the statement a QUERY — and Android's execSQL
rejects anything returning data. The Python does the identical thing legally, because
sqlite3.execute does not care. The transcription was faithful; the
assumption that both APIs tolerate the same statement was not.
2. Progress rows never ticked — and the throttle was NOT the cause.
My first diagnosis blamed the 30-second publish interval. Fred's observation — "unzip
logged progress, only trails did not" — ruled that out, since a throttle would hit
both equally.
Real cause: WorkManager DISCARDS progress Data on a terminal state.
getProgress() is empty once a worker finishes, so the worker's final forced
publish is real but unreadable. Earlier layers escaped because a LATER pass
published while still RUNNING and carried their completed state along. Nothing follows
trails. Fixed in the panel: a SUCCEEDED state means every layer completed, by definition.
The 30-second tick was a contributing error — sized against my estimate of 8–20 minutes per
pass when reality was 40 seconds end to end.
⭐ The storage move
The working directory was originally in getExternalFilesDir(). On a release
build that is unreachable by anything: run-as blocked by
signing, adb blocked by Android 11+, no file manager can browse
Android/data.
Two consequences: an extract could not be inspected without writing an export feature to
work around a directory choice; and a user who downloaded the wrong state had no way to
delete a 610 MB file from inside the app or outside it — the only exit being Settings →
Clear Storage, which also silently revokes All Files Access, breaking the
feature they were escaping from.
Moved to Documents/GroupTrack/osm/ with one-shot migration on first path
resolution. The planning state file already lived in Documents/GroupTrack/state
for exactly this reason — the decision was on record and had not been applied here.
⚠ Files now survive uninstall and are not cleared by Clear Storage. Right for a 610 MB
extract, but it makes CANCEL the only cleanup path.
CANCEL — every stage needs a way out
Fred, on being unable to remove a wrong download: "that is not really handy because
we cannot get rid of it now."
CLEANUP existed but was armed only at IMPORT, so at EXTRACT it was greyed out — the one
control that would have helped was disabled precisely when needed.
The general lesson, worth more than the button: the pipeline was designed as a
forward path, and the only reverse gear was parked at the end of it.
CANCEL sits at the bottom of the panel rather than beside EXTRACT — bottom placement
removes the misfire risk instead of mitigating it, and needs no
RowSpec or StageRow change. It also closed a gap neither of us had
named: there was no way to stop a running extract. The worker already
checked isStopped; nothing called cancelUniqueWork.
⭐ Verification — the evidence C2 is correct
Device-built skinny compared against one built by the validated Python:
device rows whose geom_hash exists in the reference: 89,448 of 89,536 (99.902%)
shared osm_id, disagreeing hash: 58
  GEOMETRY CHANGED : 58     real OSM edits between the two extracts
  FORMAT DIFFERS   :  0     would have been a port bug
Several of the 58 have identical point counts but different coordinates — exactly
what a mapper nudging a trail looks like. Had the WKT contract diverged, all 89,536 would
have mismatched, not 58. This proves the envelope offset AND the WKT contract byte for byte,
which is what makes geom_hash dedup trustworthy.
Measured performance
MetricValue
C2 on device, end to end~40 s (unzip 14 s, trails 23 s, natural 1.2 s)
Utah skinny108 MB · 89,536 trails · 3,674 places · 4,048 natural
Arizonazip 610 MB → gpkg 1,214 MB (2.09×) · 134,242 trails
Free-space gateuncompressed + 25%; Utah needed 788 MB
My device estimate was wrong by ~20× (predicted 8–20 min, actual 40 s) —
and that error is what sized the progress tick, which is why nothing rendered.
Per-state variance is large: Utah 89,536 vs Arizona 134,242, 50% apart
between neighbouring states. Size gates and ETAs must be derived per state, never scaled
from one sample.
Decisions and rejected alternatives
DecisionRejected alternative, and why
User downloads via browser; app detectsIn-app download — GroupTrack would touch Geofabrik traffic; licensing cleaner this way, and the browser handles resume/background
Overlay panel inside MVS, no RouteA nav route — would have forced a core-module edit and two-ConvoyNavigation ambiguity
Skinny is ready_for_import.db for every statePer-state filename — only one state is ever in flight, and the old name said "osm_trails" while the file also holds places and natural
carto_code BLANKA synthetic code — OSM has no carto classification; blank renders cyan "Unspecified" and touches none of the three hand-synchronised colour files
osm_id → source_unique_id—
Table name resolved from gpkg_contentsHardcoding — Geofabrik's GPKG drops the _1 suffix its shapefile spec documents; a wrong name gives a silent empty table
MULTILINESTRING stops at a degenerate partSkip-and-continue (what the Python does) — without the part's length there is no way to resynchronise, and continuing would decode from a wrong offset
⛔ Lesson: verify identity before diagnosing behaviour
Hours were lost to adb commands pointed at
com.geeksville.mesh — the Kotlin package. The installed application id
is com.grouptrack.android, renamed for Play. Source package and application id
are independent.
Every dead end traced to that one error: empty ls, an rm -rf that
deleted nothing, a false "Arizona is gone" reading, and three invented theories (Android 11
restrictions, secondary volume, MediaStore ghosts).
pm list packages | grep -i geeksville returns nothing and would have ended it in
the first minute.
When several unrelated commands all return "not found", suspect the path, not the
platform.

OSM Trail Import &mdash; C3 IMPORT + C4 CLEANUP

Baseline entering the day: 3fd526517 (C1+C2).
What shipped
The four-row OSM panel is complete end to end. A user downloads a Geofabrik
state extract in their browser, the app adopts and reduces it (C1+C2, shipped
07-28), then imports it into the production spatial database &mdash; whole
state or an area drawn on the map &mdash; and cleans up, archiving the run
record and deleting the working files.
The first real import landed, and both balance assertions held.
Typefoundinsertedaliaseddroppedbalanced
trails89,53689,52709&#10003;
points7,7227,679&mdash;43&#10003;
Places 3,674 + natural 4,048 = 7,722. Import wall time approximately three
minutes on Droid&nbsp;2.
&#11088;&#11088; dropped = 9 exactly reproduces the 07-27 laptop
measurement (&ldquo;Utah 9 hash matches out of 89,554&rdquo;). The on-device
dedup arrived at the same answer as the offline reference, which confirms the WKT
contract and geom_hash identity end to end on real data &mdash; not
by inspection, by agreement between two independent implementations.
aliased = 0 is also correct: the 2,021 name-matches were pruned on
the laptop before staging.
C3a + C3c &mdash; the worker
One worker does trails AND points in a single dedup session and writes
one ledger record. Fred: &ldquo;one import so we do not have to parse code to
import separately.&rdquo;
Trails route through SpatialDbManager.insertTrail
(INSERT / DROP / ALIAS). Points go to a new reference_points table
created by the import (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS &mdash; a new empty
table needs no migration and no schema_version bump), with
UNIQUE(geom_hash).
Points must NOT go in waypoints. Those are user-authored:
editable, deletable, listed, V3-shared. 3,674 OSM localities would bury the
user&rsquo;s own waypoints and make &ldquo;remove all OSM data&rdquo;
impossible.
beginDedupSession() is mandatory &mdash;
resolveByGeom and sourceUidSeen read in-memory HashMaps.
Skip it and every trail looks new: 89,536 duplicates with nothing reporting an
error.
Counters: found &middot; inserted &middot; aliased &middot; dropped &middot;
geometryChanged &middot; errors &middot; points_*. Fred: &ldquo;processed
should equal added, rejected, and dupes identified&rdquo; &rarr; tally
assertion with balanced: true/false recorded per type.
Re-import inserts a second trail; it does not update geometry.
updateExistingFeature never touches geometry, bbox or
geom_hash &mdash; its own comment says so. The stronger reason is
not the count: routes snap by lineId, so replacing geometry would
silently orphan every saved route touching that trail.
C3b &mdash; scope selection and the area round trip
As built, where it differs from the pre-build spec
The specification called for map_area and
selected_area in the ledger. As implemented,
pending_import carries scope plus a single
bbox, and row 3 uses a Row3Choice enum
(FULL / AREA). Whole state derives its bbox from
OsmImportStage.trailExtent().
The panel&rsquo;s rule is one line, and it held: on every derive, if a pending
bbox is present &rarr; launch. Checking on derive rather than on
open is what prevents Row3Choice resetting on reopen and
wiping a bbox the user had already drawn. That was a real bug, caught before it
shipped.
Whole state is not a separate code path
The extent comes from the trails themselves, so every trail overlaps it by
definition and a full-extent area import returns exactly what
SELECT * would. Testing whole state IS testing area.
Confirmed: 89,536 overlapping on the full extent, matching
extract.kept exactly.
The area cycle
Row 3 &rarr; SELECTED AREA &rarr; IMPORT writes pending_import
with a null bbox and closes the panel.
ConvoyMapViewerScreen sees the close, positions the planning map
on the state extent, ticks Import OSM and opens the draw panel.
The drawn bbox arrives at onAreaSelected, is written to the
ledger, the draw panel closes and the OSM panel reopens.
The derive effect finds the bbox and raises the confirm.
The draw completing IS the submit &mdash; there is no separate OSM
execute button. Verified: 25,400 trails in the drawn box against 89,536 whole
state.
&#11088;&#11088; The handoff mechanism already existed.
TrailImporter has writePendingArea /
readPendingArea / clearPendingArea. The OSM handoff is
the second instance of a shipped mechanism, not a new invention. Found via
the navigation xref. The recurring lesson of this project, again: the file
already knows.
No flag in the map screen
Both panels are flags in one screen, so no navigation is involved. A
persistent mode flag was rejected because of the routeMode leak
&mdash; two back paths, one gated. R1 (stage derived from disk) means nothing
needs preserving across the gap. osmAwaitingSlug is derived from
disk and guards against a stray draw filling the wrong record.
No AreaDrawPurpose
ConvoyDownloadPanel already carries intent in checkbox state
(Download Tiles / Import Trails / Remove Tiles). An Import OSM row was
added; the checkboxes ARE the routing.
OSM never becomes a QueueEntry. It shares the drawer, never the queue. An
import measured in ROWS would poison the tiles-per-minute yardstick exactly as
deletes would. OSM never touches onExecuteDownload and cannot reach
the queue.
Area filters WHICH rows go, never geometry. Overlap, not containment; a
boundary trail comes over WHOLE. Clipping would change the WKT &rarr; change
geom_hash &rarr; break dedup against a later whole-state
import.
C3c &mdash; wiring, and the progress display
The C3b gate became the launch: a confirm dialog naming the count and the
four coordinates, then OsmImportWorker.enqueue. Both scopes reach
one launch point.
Visibility is derived from WorkManager, never stored. Leaving the panel
and returning re-attaches to a running import. A local showProgress
flag would have been the routeMode failure again.
Live counts from progress; final counts from disk. WorkManager
discards progress Data on a terminal state, so
getProgress() is empty once the worker finishes. The completion
recap reads imports[], which appendImport writes before
the worker returns.
Fix &mdash; the confirm re-raised every few seconds.
pending_import deliberately outlives a run; that is what makes
a failed or cancelled import reprocess unattended, and
appendImport clears it only on success. So the derive effect kept
finding the bbox and raising the dialog again. No damage &mdash;
enqueueUniqueWork(KEEP) made every repeat a no-op &mdash; but
unusable.
Fix: ask WorkManager whether work is already ENQUEUED/RUNNING before
prompting.
Rejected: clearing the record on accept. That breaks unattended
reprocess by design &mdash; a crash between enqueue and completion would leave
nothing to resume from.
Fix &mdash; the completion dialog cycled forever. OK cleared the dialog
string and bumped refreshTick, which restarted the observer, which
re-read the permanent imports[] and raised it again. The
importFinal == null guard could not help: OK is what makes it null.
Fix: latch on the record&rsquo;s own at timestamp. A
nullable dialog string can never answer &ldquo;have I shown this?&rdquo;
My error &mdash; the progress overlay showed nothing for the entire run. I
read every Int in progress.keyValueMap. The worker
publishes one JSON string under osm_extract_progress, in the
shape C2 had already established, and it was in the log the whole time. Guessing
key names generically instead of reading the payload was the wrong
instinct.
C4 &mdash; cleanup
Enumerate and size the working files.
Archive the ledger by RENAME &mdash;
osm/&lt;slug&gt;/ledger.json &rarr;
osm/history/&lt;slug&gt;_&lt;date&gt;T&lt;time&gt;.json, via
OsmImportLedger.archiveLedger().
OsmImportStage.discardState() sweeps the zip, gpkg and skinny,
then the directory.
&#11088;&#11088; Order is load-bearing: rename BEFORE the sweep.
discardState deletes ledger.json along with the data
files, so a rename afterwards would have nothing to rename.
history/ sits OUTSIDE osm/&lt;slug&gt;/ and the sweep
cannot reach it. That is why rename beats copy: the record is safe before
anything destructive runs, and a copy leaves a window where both exist and the
wrong one is deleted.
If the rename fails the sweep does not run. Losing the run record to
keep a cleanup on schedule is the wrong trade; the files can go on a later
pass.
Measured on the first real cleanup: 3 files, 422&nbsp;MB removed
(utah-latest-free.gpkg.zip 314&nbsp;MB,
ready_for_import.db 108&nbsp;MB, ledger.json), record
kept as utah_2026-07-29T135649.json.
Decisions taken on the day
No cleanup screen. Row 4 is a process that executes. Fred: &ldquo;it
has to be selected to run after imports. button goes green after
imports.&rdquo;
Row 4 arms off imports[] being non-empty &mdash; derived,
not a flag, so it survives navigation and reflects what actually happened.
Acknowledging the recap closes the panel. Correct rather than merely
convenient: cleanup removed the working directory, so
statesInFlight() is empty and the panel would derive back to row 1
anyway.
Cleanup does not auto-roll after import &mdash; it waits to be
selected.
&#11088; REVERSAL &mdash; no multi-area from one download. Fred 07-29:
&ldquo;no multi areas from one download. areas are downloaded to support a
ride and we are killing downloads after import process.&rdquo; Rationale:
&ldquo;3 minute download vs cascading complexity for imports.&rdquo;
This reverses the 07-28 decision that kept the extract alive so a second area
could be drawn from it. The trade was weighed and taken: carrying extract
lifetime across imports means a driver that reasons about which areas share a
download, and cleanup that has to know whether anyone still needs the file. That
complexity compounds; the download does not. The state machine collapses back to
acquire &rarr; extract &rarr; import &rarr; cleanup, once through, nothing
surviving between runs.
Consequence: the reprocess-driver cost model moves from per
state to per import. The &ldquo;group by state, replay all area records
from one download&rdquo; idea assumed the extract persisted.
Optional-retain seam is marked in the code (Fred: &ldquo;if we have
any issue we can make removing the downloaded file optional&rdquo;). Keeping
the ZIP alone (~330&nbsp;MB) makes a re-import a 40-second re-extract instead of
a 3-minute download &mdash; the middle option if the trade ever looks wrong in
the field.
Dry-run mode &mdash; proposed and rejected
I pushed for a dry-run before the first write, on the grounds that it would
give the full INSERT/ALIAS/DROP distribution across all 89,536 rows and test the
balance assertion before any row existed.
Fred killed it with the decisive objection: a dry run cannot see the
case that matters &mdash; &ldquo;an issue in a trail in this run that was
simulated as added but is duped within db.&rdquo;
resolveByGeom and sourceUidSeen read in-memory
HashMaps filled by beginDedupSession(). A dry run reproduces a stale
session faithfully and reports &ldquo;added&rdquo; for a row that will collide on
the real write. It simulates the decision, not the database&rsquo;s response
to it.
The real run catches exactly that, immediately, via
UNIQUE(geom_hash) and the balance assertion. And recovery is cheap:
all imported trail rows carry source_id='osm', so a bad import is a
laptop DELETE ... WHERE source_id='osm' on a sacrificial device.
Points differ &mdash; they carry no source_id;
reference_points is OSM-only by construction, so that is a
full-table delete.
Do not re-propose dry-run mode.
What did ship instead, because no undo exists in-app: a confirm dialog naming
the trail count and the four coordinates.
Documentation produced

&rarr; G &mdash; Work with Artifacts went from 5 screens to 8, with
18 captures embedded at 720px WebP q60 (all under the 115&nbsp;KB ceiling;
manual 3.62 &rarr; 4.53&nbsp;MB). Screens: the four steps &middot; Step 1
Download &middot; Step 2 Extract &middot; Step 3 Import &middot; Step 4 Cleanup
&middot; What OpenStreetMap adds &middot; CANCEL &middot; Where the files are
kept.
The Work with Artifacts recapture is done &mdash; three buttons now
visible, closing the caption/image mismatch that was flagged do-not-ship.
Two statements in the old text were false and were corrected:
&ldquo;steps 3 and 4 are not active in this build&rdquo;, and &ldquo;you can come
back and draw another area from the same download&rdquo;.
Fred&rsquo;s framing paragraph opens the section, before the step list:
&ldquo;This is a four-step process, and GroupTrack keeps track of your
progress. Any time you leave &mdash; for any reason &mdash; you can come back,
select IMPORT OSM DATA again, and you will be brought to the next step in your
process.&rdquo; This is the user-facing statement of R1, and it is what stops
people restarting from step 1 and re-downloading 330&nbsp;MB they already
have.
Section title stays Import OSM Data &mdash; Fred: &ldquo;it is a
button name just like import trails data.&rdquo; I renamed it to prose and

Still open in that section: the adoption moment (the panel

Five coordinate orderings coexist in this feature. Ledger

Appendix &mdash; the specification as it stood, moved verbatim
These sections were the working specification in GroupTrack_Living_Master before the build. They are moved here unedited rather than summarised, so the design reasoning survives in full and nothing depends on my account of it. Where the build diverged, the body of this document says so.
# 🔴 C3b — THE NEXT BUILD (full specification)
Everything below was settled in conversation 07-28 and is not re-litigated.
This section exists so C3b can be written without re-deriving any of it.
## The handoff mechanism — why JSON and not Compose state
Row 3 offers **WHOLE STATE** or **SELECT AREA**. Area requires the planning map,
which means the OSM panel must go away and come back.
**Fred's design (07-28):** row 3 simply *closes the panel*. The map's bbox
submission *relaunches* it. There is **no flag in MVS**, no `AreaDrawPurpose`
enum, and no navigation change.
&gt; ⭐ **Why this works:** R1 — stage is derived from disk, never stored. The panel
&gt; can be destroyed and recreated and lands in exactly the same place. That rule
&gt; was written for crash recovery; this is an unplanned payoff.
&gt; ⚠ **Why a flag was rejected:** the `routeMode` leak. There were two back paths
&gt; and only one was gated — the on-screen BACK bypassed the `BackHandler`
&gt; entirely. A `osmAwaitingBbox` flag in MVS has the identical shape, and every
&gt; exit path would have to clear it. Closing the panel means there is nothing to
&gt; leak.
## The ledger record — uniform, both scopes
```json
"pending_import": {
  "scope": "state",
  "chosen_at": "2026-07-28T22:41:09",
  "map_area":      { "s": 36.99, "w": -114.05, "n": 42.00, "e": -109.04 },
  "selected_area": { "s": 36.99, "w": -114.05, "n": 42.00, "e": -109.04 }
}
```
- **`map_area`** — ALWAYS the state extent. Positions the planning map. 5% margin
  so the box occupies ~95% of the view.
- **`selected_area`** — what actually gets imported.
| scope | map_area | selected_area |
|---|---|---|
| state | state extent | state extent (identical, written immediately) |
| area | state extent | `null` until the draw fills it |
**THE PANEL'S RULE IS ONE LINE: on open, if `selected_area` is present, launch.**
Both paths converge there. The map never has to ask where to open — the answer
is in the record regardless of scope. The importer never has to know which
scope it is.
&gt; ⭐ **Whole state is not a separate code path.** The extent is derived from the
&gt; trails themselves, so every trail overlaps it *by definition*. A full-extent
&gt; area import returns exactly the rows a `SELECT *` would — identically, not
&gt; approximately. One function, exercised two ways. **Testing whole state IS
&gt; testing area.**
&gt; ⚠ **This bends R1 knowingly.** R1 said the ledger never decides what runs next.
&gt; "User chose area and hasn't drawn yet" is not derivable from any disk artifact,
&gt; so it genuinely must be stored. The STAGE stays IMPORT throughout — this is a
&gt; sub-state inside it, not a competing stage.
## The area cycle, step by step
```
1. Row 3 tapped
   -&gt; dialog: WHOLE STATE / SELECT AREA / cancel
2a. WHOLE STATE
   -&gt; extent = OsmImportStage.skinnyExtent(ctx, slug)
        SELECT MIN(min_lat), MIN(min_lon), MAX(max_lat), MAX(max_lon)
        FROM osm_trails            (sub-second over 89,536 rows)
   -&gt; setPendingImport(scope="state", map_area=extent, selected_area=extent)
   -&gt; OsmImportWorker.enqueue()
   -&gt; panel STAYS OPEN, progress rows appear under row 3
2b. SELECT AREA
   -&gt; setPendingImport(scope="area", map_area=extent, selected_area=null)
   -&gt; showOsmPanel = false                 (panel closes; MVS is underneath)
   -&gt; open the download panel with "Import OSM" CHECKED
   -&gt; map framed to map_area with 5% margin
3. User draws + submits
   -&gt; ConvoyMapViewerScreen bbox handler sees osmChecked
   -&gt; slug from OsmImportStage.statesInFlight().firstOrNull()
   -&gt; OsmImportLedger.setPendingBbox(ctx, slug, s, w, n, e)
   -&gt; showOsmPanel = true                  (panel relaunches)
4. Panel opens, sees selected_area present
   -&gt; OsmImportWorker.enqueue()            (KEEP makes a double-enqueue a no-op)
   -&gt; progress rows under row 3
5. Import completes
   -&gt; appendImport() writes the record AND removes pending_import
   -&gt; row 3 ticks, row 4 arms
```
&gt; ⚠ **Clearing must be airtight.** The trigger is "selected_area present" and the
&gt; panel re-derives on every refresh. A pending record that outlives its import
&gt; re-enqueues on every panel open. `appendImport` removes it; `enqueueUniqueWork`
&gt; with `KEEP` makes a duplicate enqueue harmless in the meantime — but the
&gt; removal is the actual fix, not the KEEP.
&gt; ⚠ **Row 3 must SHOW the pending state.** `WAITING FOR AREA — draw one, or
&gt; cancel`, with a visible cancel. An invisible mode is precisely the `routeMode`
&gt; failure. If the user picks area, gets distracted, and returns tomorrow, the
&gt; panel must explain itself.
## The panel's own checkbox row (ConvoyDownloadPanel.kt)
The panel already carries intent in checkbox state — **this is why
`AreaDrawPurpose` is unnecessary**:
```
Download Tiles    blue    tilesChecked
Import Trails     green   trailsChecked
Remove Tiles      red     removeTilesChecked
Import OSM        orange  osmChecked          &lt;- NEW ROW
```
`Draw Area` is enabled when any is checked (`ConvoyDownloadPanel.kt` ~:243).
The caller dispatches on whichever ones are. **The checkboxes are the routing.**
New row needs:
- `osmChecked: Boolean` + `onOsmCheckedChange` — same shape as the other three
- added to the `enabled =` condition on Draw Area
- ⚠ **`osmAvailable: Boolean`** — disabled when no skinny exists. Same mechanism
  the V2.6 stub rows already use.
- bbox display line mirroring `"Trails: $trailSourceCount sources found"`:
  **`"OSM: 8,412 trails in area"`** — indexed count off `ix_osm_trails_bbox`,
  instant, appears the moment the box is drawn.
&gt; ⭐ **The count IS the confirmation.** The user sees exactly what they are
&gt; committing to before submitting, so a confirm dialog adds nothing. (Whole-state
&gt; is the exception — see Open Questions.)
&gt; ⚠ **Checkboxes are not mutually exclusive.** Tiles + OSM both checked = one
&gt; draw does both. Arguably a feature. But dispatch must handle combinations, and
&gt; **OSM must never become a `QueueEntry`** — see the yardstick warning below.
## ⛔ OSM MUST NOT ENTER THE DOWNLOAD QUEUE
Share the **drawer**. Never the queue.
`DownloadQueueManager.submitDownload` is not involved. The yardstick averages
tiles-per-minute; deletes were excluded from it precisely because a different
unit poisons `avgMinutesPer100` and every later download estimate collapses
toward zero. **An OSM import measured in ROWS does exactly the same thing.**
Same UI, separate pipeline.
## Tally assertion (add in C3b — 3 lines)
Fred: *"processed should equal added, rejected, and dupes identified."*
```kotlin
val tallied = inserted + aliased + dropped + geomChanged + errors
if (tallied != found) Log.e(TAG, "TALLY MISMATCH: found=$found accounted=$tallied")
```
Same for points: `pointsFound == pointsInserted + pointsMoved + pointsDropped`.
&gt; ⚠ Reading the C3a loop back, every path *appears* to increment exactly one
&gt; counter — but "appears complete" is how the `deleteOriginal` assumption went
&gt; wrong this morning. The assertion turns a silent accounting hole into a log
&gt; line on the first run.
Record the result: **`"balanced": true/false` per type in the import record**, so
the audit is in the file rather than a logcat buffer that is gone by morning.
## Per-layer point counters (amend in C3b)
Points are currently one bucket. If `natural` silently stops importing, the
total still looks plausible. Split by layer — `places_found`, `natural_found` —
generated from the catalog, so enabling `pois` adds its keys automatically.
## Row 4 summary
Row 4 detail reads the state's own `imports[]`:
```
CLEANUP    3 imports · 12,847 added · 402 aliased · 1,633 dupes · 58 changed
```
&gt; ⚠ **Sum WITHIN one state's ledger only.** Do NOT sum across history files —
&gt; see the History section.
---
# 🔴 C4 CLEANUP — settled, not written
## The ledger is RENAMED, not copied
```
osm/utah/ledger.json  -&gt;  osm/history/utah_2026-07-28_224109.json
```
- **Rename replaces the delete.** `finalizeAndDelete` currently removes the
  ledger; now the rename IS the removal. If the rename fails, the ledger stays
  put — cleanup cannot destroy the record even by accident, because deletion is
  not a separate step that could succeed on its own.
- **Nothing is serialized twice**, so the archived record is byte-identical to
  what the import wrote.
- ⚠ **`history/` sits OUTSIDE `osm/&lt;slug&gt;/`** — CANCEL and cleanup both remove
  `osm/&lt;slug&gt;/` wholesale and would take the history with it. (This is also why
  `discardState` is deliberately non-recursive.)
- ⚠ **Never pruned.** A few KB each. Chosen, not overlooked.
## ⭐ C4 NO LONGER AUTO-ROLLS AFTER IMPORT
**This reverses an earlier decision and the reason matters.** C3→C4 auto-roll was
settled when whole-state was the only scope. With area scope it is wrong:
import Moab, cleanup fires, skinny deleted — a second area costs a 630 MB
re-download, defeating the entire point of area scope.
**Cleanup is explicit.** Row 4 arms after import; the user decides when they are
done with the state. Whole-state import may *suggest* it.
## History is per-run, never aggregated
Fred 07-28: *"the history is just that, results of one run at one moment in
time."*
- **History = what a run did.** One file, one run, read on its own.
  **No cross-run arithmetic anywhere.**
- **The database = what exists now.** "How many OSM trails do I have" is
  `COUNT(*) FROM trail_properties WHERE source_id='osm'` — asked of the DB,
  never derived from history.
&gt; ⚠ Summing runs produces a number that *looks* like inventory and is not. A
&gt; re-imported area contributes inserts and dupes that add up to nothing
&gt; meaningful. Better no total than a misleading one.
A history browser (list by state + timestamp, open one run, show its counters
and whether they balanced) is a later, cheap feature — the filenames already
carry both filter keys.
---
# 🔨 C3b — GATED BUILD (applied 07-29, not yet verified on device)
`patch_c3b_row3_scope_2026-07-29.py` — 7 anchors, dry run clean, applied.
Backups `.bak_20260729_100043`.
## What it does
- **Row 3 launch line carries two values** — FULL STATE / SELECTED AREA, checkbox
  glyphs, rendered in the `rows.forEach` loop rather than inside `StageRow`
  (StageRow is shared by all four rows; only row 3 has a choice).
- **IMPORT is disabled until one is selected** — `enabled = !busy &amp;&amp; skinnyExists &amp;&amp;
  importScope != null`. Fred 07-29: *"one must be selected for import button to function."*
- **FULL STATE derives the extent and writes `pending_import`; SELECTED AREA writes a
  null bbox.** Both go through `setPendingImport`, one channel.
- **Then it STOPS at a CANCEL-only recap** showing scope + the four bbox values
  individually + the overlap count. Nothing calls `OsmImportWorker.enqueue`.
## ⭐ Why the gate is where it is
It stands exactly where `enqueue()` will go, so **C3c is a swap, not a rewrite** —
which is the point Fred made on 07-29: *"it keeps us out of the weeds of rewriting a
section because of behaviour issues."* C3b's job ends at *correct `pending_import` on
disk at the right moment*; C3c's begins by consuming it.
## ⭐ The recap READS BACK from disk
It does not print what it meant to write — it re-reads via `pendingBbox`. A transposed
pair shows up in the S/W/N/E lines instead of being masked. Four values labelled
individually, never a joined string: `36.99,-114.05,42.00,-109.04` hides what
`S 36.99 / W -114.05` makes obvious.
## ✅ PASS CRITERION — exact, from the 07-28 ledger
Utah `extract.kept = 89536`. **A FULL STATE recap MUST show `Trails overlapping: 89536`.**
Every trail overlaps its own extent by definition. Any other number means the extent
query or the coordinate order is wrong.
## ⚠ CANCEL does NOT clear the pending record
Deliberate. The record stays on disk so the panel can be reopened to confirm the rule
re-derives off the same values, and so the JSON can be read between runs.
## Findings that drove the build
- ⛔ **`subset_meta` has NO extent.** Seven keys only: `source_file`, `classes`,
  `feature_count`, `built_at`, `wkt_format`, `hash_algo`, `attribution`. So
  `OsmImportLedger:222` (*"whole state writes its bbox straight from subset_meta"*)
  describes an intention that was never built. **Extent now derived by
  `OsmImportStage.trailExtent()`** — `SELECT MIN(min_lat), MAX(max_lat), MIN(min_lon),
  MAX(max_lon) FROM osm_trails`, covered by `ix_osm_trails_bbox`. ⭐ More correct than a
  stored value anyway: the extent comes from the trails themselves, which is *why* whole
  state is not a special case.
- **No 5% margin on `selected_area`.** The margin was specced for positioning the map;
  the import filter wants the true extent. Padding a box that already contains
  everything only widens it.
- ⚠ **`scope` at `OsmImportPanel.kt:95` is `rememberCoroutineScope()`.** The import
  choice is named `importScope` so it cannot shadow it.
- **`LaunchedEffect(refreshTick)` is the derive moment** (R5). The launch rule belongs
  there. Panel re-entry re-composes it, so the relaunch-after-draw path needs no new
  machinery.
- **Only `clickable` was missing from imports** — `padding`, `sp`, `Dispatchers`,
  `launch`, `withContext` were already present, so the panel already does
  `scope.launch { withContext(Dispatchers.IO) }` in the style the patch uses.
- **Nothing touches the skinny.** Both new helpers open `OPEN_READONLY`; C4 is still a
  stub. The skinny is stable across every test cycle, so **no restore is needed between
  runs** — `setPendingImport` overwrites the record wholesale rather than accumulating.
## ⚠ Uncertain until the build lands
`material3` vs `material` for the recap `AlertDialog`/`TextButton`, and whether the
two-value line inherits a readable colour on the panel background. Both are
compile-or-eyeball fixes, not design problems.
---
## 🔨 PART 2 — the area-draw round trip (applied 07-29, build pending)
`patch_c3b_area_draw_2026-07-29.py` — 7 anchors, dry run clean, applied.
Backups `.bak_20260729_114606`.
⭐ **BOTH PANELS ARE FLAGS IN ONE SCREEN.** `showOsmPanel` (MVS:149) and
`showDownloadPanel` (MVS:225). `OsmImportPanel` is called at **MVS:962** — it is
not a route. So the whole round trip is state changes in `ConvoyMapViewerScreen`:
no navigation, no `ConvoyRoutes` entry, no `AreaDrawPurpose`. Fred 07-29:
*"if you close the import process as this is launched you will be on the planning
map, just need to refresh the position."*
**The trip:**
1. Row 3 SELECTED AREA writes `pending_import` with a null bbox, closes the panel.
2. `LaunchedEffect(showOsmPanel)` sees the close, reads DISK (R1 — nothing is
   passed), and if a record is awaiting a draw: positions the map on the state
   extent + 5% and opens the download panel with IMPORT OSM ticked.
3. User draws. `onAreaSelected` sets `downloadBbox` as it always has.
4. `LaunchedEffect(downloadBbox, …)` writes `setPendingBbox`, closes the download
   panel, reopens the OSM panel — where row 3 finds a bbox and GATES.
- ⭐ **THE DRAW COMPLETING IS THE SUBMIT.** No OSM execute button. Fred 07-29:
  *"relaunch import and close area selection when the area is processed."*
- ⚠ **`onAreaSelected` is a `@JavascriptInterface`** (MVS:480) with no slug and no
  coroutine scope — disk I/O there would run on the JS thread. It keeps doing only
  what it does today; the reaction happens in composable scope.
- ⛔ **OSM never touches `onExecuteDownload`**, so it cannot reach the download
  queue. An import measured in ROWS would poison the tiles-per-minute yardstick.
- ⛔ **THE 5% PAD WAS REMOVED — see the FIX 6 section below.** I claimed it
  "sidestepped" FIX 6 because `fitBounds` pads nothing. **Wrong** — the drift comes
  from padded values being SAVED, not from the fit function. Fred 07-29: *"if we
  remove your 5% of use fit we have no issues."* The OSM path now passes the raw
  extent.
- ⚠ **Padding is PER AXIS** — `(n-s)*0.05` and `(e-w)*0.05` separately. One figure
  would skew tall or wide states. Utah is nearly square so it would have hidden.
- ⚠ **`osmAwaitingSlug` is the guard** that stops a stray area draw from filling
  someone else's record.
## ⭐⭐ THE XREF FINDING THAT DE-RISKED THIS — the handoff already exists
Fred 07-29: *"i would use the navigation xref doc to identify the import trails
function and then the functions where used to trace what is called."* That found:
**`TrailImporter.kt` already has `writePendingArea`:645 / `readPendingArea`:668 /
`clearPendingArea`:680**, consumed by `ConvoyTrailSourceScreen:75/:83`. The
download panel writes a pending area to JSON, navigates, and the target screen
reads it back — **exactly what `OsmImportLedger.setPendingBbox` / `pendingBbox` /
`clearPendingImport` does.** MVS:1737 is the working template.
⭐ **The OSM handoff is the SECOND INSTANCE of a shipped mechanism, not a new
one.** Built from first principles it would have worked and nobody would have
known there was a pattern to match.
⚠ **FIVE coordinate orderings are now in play. Named arguments at every call
site, never positional:**
| Thing | Order |
|---|---|
| `OsmImportLedger` pending record | `s, w, n, e` |
| `OsmImportStage.trailExtent()` | `[s, w, n, e]` |
| `ImportScope.Area(...)` constructor | `south, west, north, east` |
| `ImportScope.asLedgerString()` | `west,south,east,north` |
| `DownloadBbox(...)` | `north, south, east, west` |
| `TrailImporter.writePendingArea(...)` | `north, south, east, west` |
| `fitBounds([S,N],[W,E])` | S,N then W,E |
## ⛔ THE WASTED BUILD — 17 minutes, and the lesson is the same one
The first C3b build failed on `Redeclaration: ImportScope`. **A sealed interface
of that name already existed at `OsmImportStage.kt:28`** — and its doc comment
already made the CODE RULE 1 argument my enum restated (*"sealed rather than
`Bbox? = null`, deliberately: with `Bbox? = null` every call site is ambiguous
between 'the user chose whole state' and 'the caller forgot to set it'"*).
⚠ **I had been shown a fragment of that very declaration and did not read it.**
The `asLedgerString()` comment at `:37` was in the fragment; I read it as a stray
note about ledger format instead of asking what it was attached to. Fixed by
renaming the panel's type to `Row3Choice` (UI state, not the domain type).
⭐ **Same lesson twice in one day, from opposite directions: THE FILE ALREADY
KNOWS.** The xref read found a shipped pattern; the skipped read cost a build.

COMPLETED TASK — Planner tap handling: popups, waypoints, snap radius2026-07-30 · commits e84117e83 + follow-up · one root cause, two contributors
One doc per completed task; title = task title. Full design and fix
detail, so the feature can be reviewed or changed later without losing context.
Summary
Three reported defects on the planning map — popups unreliable on trails, no popup at
all on tracks, waypoints impossible to drop while route mode was on — turned out to have
one root cause and two unrelated contributors. The root cause had been present for
as long as the file existed and had never been visible.
Commits: e84117e83 plus the follow-up carrying items 4 and 5.
⭐⭐ ROOT CAUSE — a script block that killed itself at parse time
grouptrack_map.html opened with a &lt;script&gt; block at
:9-72 whose first statement was:
map.on('click', function(e) { ... Android.onProximityTap ... });
map is not created until :731. The block threw
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'on') at
parse time and died entirely, taking two things with it:
Android.onProximityTap was never registered. Short taps never
reached Kotlin — which is why onProximityTap had never logged anything.
showProximityPopup was never defined. It is the only definition
in the codebase; ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:578 calls it by name through
evaluateJavascript. Even a successful proximity query had nothing to render
into.
The block also held __legacy_proximity_unused, dead by its own comment,
whose unbalanced tail produced a second error — Uncaught SyntaxError at the
closing tag.
⚠ NONE OF IT WAS EVER VISIBLE. The planner had no WebChromeClient, so every
console message went nowhere. Confirmed pre-existing against HEAD~1 — not a regression
from any 2026-07-30 change.
How it was found — the method, not the luck
Four theories were worked and discarded before the evidence arrived, each plausible
and each wrong:
Route mode stuck true — killed by the log: routeMode=false at tap
time.
Popups bound conditionally at draw time — real defect, fixed, but not the
cause.
Missing stopPropagation — real, and the 547 ms double-fire proved
it, but downstream.
Stale bridge capture on the detail panel — still open, unrelated.
⭐ What broke the deadlock was adding a WebChromeClient — eight lines that
turned on instrumentation already written and dark. `ARTIFACTTAP` had been logging
in convoy since long before; the planner's console had simply never been connected.
THE LESSON: before theorising about behaviour you cannot see, check whether
the channel that would show it is connected. An unread log is worse than no log — it
looks like evidence of absence.
The two contributors
A. Popups bound conditionally at draw time
The planner bound popups only when route mode was off, at draw time
(:249 trails, :401 waypoints, :440 routes). But
setRouteMode's suppression works by stashing and unbinding on entry
and rebinding on exit — it assumes popups are always bound. A layer drawn during route
mode had nothing to stash, so the restore found _savedPopupContent == null
and it stayed popup-less permanently. Convoy binds unconditionally
(:468/:617/:657), which is why the two maps differed
here.
Fix: bind unconditionally; suppression stays with setRouteMode.
B. Missing stopPropagation, and the correction it needed
The log was decisive: trail taps fired twice per gesture, 547 ms apart; track
taps fired once. The only difference was L.DomEvent.stopPropagation(e)
in the track handler. Without it, the layer click opens the popup and propagates to
map.on('click'), whose own popup (autoClose,
closeOnClick) closes it again — "same trail, some popup, some don't".
⛔ MY ERROR, CAUGHT BY FRED BEFORE IT SHIPPED: I added stopPropagation
unconditionally. Route planning works by tapping ON trails, and swallowing the event at
the layer means the vertex never gets placed. Item 3b added the early return the track
handlers always had — if (window.__routeMode) return; BEFORE stopping
propagation. The pattern was in front of me twice and I did not carry it across.
The waypoint block — a mitigation that became the bug
onMapLongPress carried if (addPointMode) return. Fred's
history: it was added because popups were not responding, so long presses were
repeated attempts at a popup that dropped waypoints instead. The mitigation treated the
symptom of the root cause above.
Fred's rule, now implemented: long press always registers a waypoint, in every
state. ⚠ Order mattered — restoring it before the popup fix would have restored the
original frustration, so both went in the same build.
Snap radius — a unit mismatch, not a tuning problem
Popups hit-test in pixels (L.svg({tolerance: 44})); snap used a
fixed 30 metres. They only agree near z17:
zoom44 px on the groundsnap was
z1821 m30 m
z1685 m30 m
z14340 m30 m
⭐ That is why a tap could pop a trail's name and still free-place the vertex —
both behaviours were correct, measuring different things. Radius is now derived from the
zoom that was already crossing the bridge on onViewportChanged and
being discarded, clamped 15–150 m. VERIFIED z14–z18.
Still open from this investigation
The :813 duplicate proximity scan — a pure-JS copy still runs
alongside the restored Kotlin path, so two popups race per tap. Fred accepted this for
now. A third, dead copy sits at :74-123 inside a src-bearing
script tag whose inline content the browser ignores.
addPointMode stuck true with route mode off — the two-flag problem.
Artifact detail panel — bridge fires with a good id, panel never renders, both
maps.
Convoy — drawTrack/clearMarkers timing, and dead
route-mode scaffolding.
