DETAIL PANEL PATTERN (same composable, 4 type configs)
  Badge + display_name + aliases + type-specific properties + actions
  Alias source tags: agency (trail import), user (manual), aws (V2.6 standardization)
  Star = preferred. One per artifact. LOCAL ONLY (is_preferred not sent to AWS).
  Min 1 alias always. Agency/AWS undeletable. User deletable unless only one.
DELETE RULES
  TRAIL: no delete (agency data, batch remove by source only)
  TRACK: warn if route.source_track_id references it
  WAYPOINT: BLOCK if route.trailhead_id references it
  ROUTE: BLOCK if route_properties.ride_id not null
  All deletes cascade: properties + aliases + survey(track) + queue entries + data_log
§6 Waypoint Creation — Long Press + Proximity + Alias
UI SCAFFOLDING NEXT
WAYPOINT CREATION FLOW
  1. SELECT TYPE
    TRAILHEADFUEL
    GATEHAZARD
    SCENICWATER
    CAMPPARKING
    RALLYOTHER
  2. PROXIMITY CHECK (100m)
    📍 Gate 4 — 85m away
    ★ Gate 4 user
      ADD ALIAS
      SET PREFERRED
  CREATE NEW WAYPOINT
  3. NAME + SHARE
    NO
    SHARE
WAYPOINT CREATION LIFECYCLE (Owner: WaypointManager)
  Long-press → type select → proximity check via proximity_config (100m default)
  IF NEARBY: show existing + aliases → (A) add alias, (B) set preferred, (C) create new
  IF (A): AliasManager adds alias. No new spatial. Done.
  IF (C) or NO NEARBY: name → insert waypoints (spatial, POINT WKT) → insert waypoint_properties → AliasManager first alias → AuditLogger data_log → share? → QueueManager upload_queue
DATABASE WRITES
  grouptrack_spatial.db: INSERT INTO waypoints (waypoint_id, name, type, geometry, created_at, updated_at)
  grouptrack_data.db: INSERT INTO waypoint_properties, artifact_aliases, data_log
  geometry = SpatialDbManager.pointWkt(lat, lng)
PROXIMITY CONFIG (soft-coded, adjustable)
  waypoint: 100m | trail: 80% overlap | track: 70% overlap | route: 85% overlap
§7 Track Save Flow
UI SCAFFOLDING NEXT
TRACK SAVE — NAME + SHARE + SURVEY
  SAVE TRACK
  GPS recording complete. 12.4 mi, 2h 15m.
    SKIPSAVE
  SHARE
    NOYES
  RATE THIS RIDE
  12345
  RIDE AGAIN?
    NOYES
  DONE
TRACK CREATION LIFECYCLE (Owner: TrackManager)
  GPS stops or file imported → name prompt → Save/Skip
  Save GPX/KML to my_tracks/ → insert tracks (bbox = bboxWkt from points)
  Insert track_properties (distance, duration, speed, elevation)
  AliasManager: first alias (preferred, source='user')
  Share Y/N → if Y: shared=1, upload_queue entry
  Survey → insert track_surveys (enjoyment 1-5, ride again Y/N)
  AuditLogger: data_log entry
  TileRequestTrigger: tile_queue HIGH priority
V2.6 POST-UPLOAD
  AWS returns area track aliases → user picks standard or keeps own
  Three options: ACCEPT STANDARD | KEEP MINE REMOVE AWS | KEEP MINE KEEP AWS
  Internet-gated startup check. JSON inbox: Documents/GroupTrack/data/alias_review/

  Table: trail_sources (extension db). Vetted/approved catalog.

  Area selector is transient — not saved.

    One composable · four configs
    What changes by artifact type
    The frame is identical; the function list and full-data fields swap per type. Delete rules are enforced against real reference columns verified in the schema.
        TRAIL
        trail_properties
          Functions: Rename · Fit&nbsp;to&nbsp;display · Show&nbsp;aliases · Delete (blocked — agency)
          Data: class · carto code · motorized · surface · steward · county · distance · agency
        TRACK
        track_properties + track_surveys
          Functions: Rename · Fit · Aliases · Convert&nbsp;to&nbsp;route · Survey · Delete*
          Data: distance · duration · max/avg speed · elevation · points · survey
        WAYPOINT
        waypoint_properties
          Functions: Rename · Fit · Aliases · Edit · Delete**
          Data: elevation · description · source format · source file
        ROUTE
        route_properties
          Functions: Rename · Fit · Aliases · Set&nbsp;trailhead · Delete***
          Data: distance · method · trailhead · elevation · description
        Delete guards (checked against verified reference columns): Trail — never deletable (agency-owned, agency_id/data_source set). Track* — warn if a route's source_track_id references it. Waypoint** — block if a route's trailhead_id references it. Route*** — block if route_properties.ride_id is not null.
        Delete cascade (when allowed): remove the row's *_properties, its artifact_aliases, any track_surveys, queue entries, and write a data_log entry (before/after state).
    Alias accordion
    Preferred name, sources, and what's deletable
        Preferred (★) = the alias shown as the artifact's display name on the map. Exactly one per artifact, local only. There's no DB constraint enforcing this — when the user stars an alias, the code clears the other is_preferred flags for that artifact in the same transaction.
        Source chips read from artifact_aliases.source: agency and aws aliases are undeletable; user aliases are deletable — unless it's the only alias left (minimum one).
        Records are dated (created_at / creation_date) and shown newest context first. Adding an alias is blocked from creating a duplicate name by UNIQUE(artifact_type, artifact_id, alias).
        Write path: add-alias calls SpatialDbManager.addAlias(type, id, name, geomHash, creationDate) via ConvoyArtifactOps.addAlias(...). (AliasManager.kt is an empty stub — do not wire to it.)

GroupTrack — Decision Log (APPEND-ONLY detail record)
Full, uncompressed detail of decisions, specs, and diagnoses. Companion to the Living Checklist (which is the navigable index; this is the deep record it points into).
APPEND-ONLY RULE — read before editing. This file exists to stop detail decay. Each session ADDS a new dated block at the top. No prior block is ever edited, shortened, or deleted. The Living Checklist compresses freely because the full detail lives here, undamaged. When carried forward to a new dated filename, prior blocks are copied verbatim and the new block is prepended. Recommit keeps the latest (cumulative) file. Pruning duplicates/superseded files is the human task; this file is never pruned of its history.
2026-06-06 · Convoy-map snap-2 PROVEN; planning-map next; line-ending trap; build/package corrections
SNAP-2 ON CONVOY MAP — DONE &amp; PROVEN ON DEVICE. The route now traces along trail/track geometry instead of drawing straight chords between taps. Proven three ways: (1) logcat &mdash; tracedLen grows far faster than vertex count as consecutive same-line snapped points fill in trail geometry (run A: snapped 2&rarr;13, tracedLen 80&rarr;1285; run B: snapped 5&rarr;6 jumped tracedLen 709&rarr;2802 = a long trail slice; the pts= arrays contain intermediate trail vertices that are NOT taps); (2) on-screen, confirmed by Fred; (3) reproduced via undo/repost.
Root cause confirmed (branch A from the 06-05 diagnosis). Snap COMPUTES and STORES correctly &mdash; draft JSON vertices carry snapped:true, real lineId, lineType, segmentIndex, interpolation t. buildSegments() (RouteManager.kt:218) genuinely traces: walks consecutive vertex pairs, sameLine = a.snapped &amp;&amp; b.snapped &amp;&amp; same lineId (226), pulls lineGeom(a.lineId) and calls sliceLine (193) using pos = segmentIndex + t (187) to emit intermediate trail points. Its ONLY caller was buildWktAndBbox (246, save-completed). The live/resume/rollback DRAW paths all bypassed it, building the line from raw routeVertices() as [lat,lon] chords. That single missing transformation &mdash; never tracing the snapped geometry into what gets drawn &mdash; was the whole bug, exactly as hardened on 06-05.
The fix. The draw now runs the stored vertices through buildSegments against the viewport geometry, then draws the traced polyline. Patched block: addVertex(v); val pts = withContext(IO){ SpatialDbManager.init(context); queryTrailsByViewport + queryTracksByViewport; build byId(trail_id/track_id &rarr; geometry); RouteManager.buildSegments{ lineId &rarr; byId[lineId]?.let{ parseWktLine } }.joinToString swapping to [lat,lon] }; drawBuildLine(pts). CRITICAL: buildSegments returns [lon,lat] (WKT order); drawBuildLine wants [lat,lon] &mdash; emit [it[1],it[0]].
TWO onMapTap handlers &mdash; the key finding. ConvoyScreen.kt has two: site 544 in the if(existing != null) persistent-WebView branch, and site 694 in the else/factory branch. Fresh map sessions run the FACTORY (694) handler. Patching 544 alone compiled, installed, and changed nothing visible &mdash; trail taps were running 694 (unpatched), which is why the tracedLen log never appeared at first and looked (wrongly) like the patched block was throwing. It was NOT throwing; it simply wasn't the handler executing. Patching 694 made it work. This is the recurring "fixed one of two handlers" trap (cf. 06-04 free-place vs snap branches). Patches: patch_v25_trailtrace_site1_544_v6.py (544), patch_v25_trailtrace_site2_694_v1.py (694, 36-space indent). A diagnostic-log patch patch_v25_trailtrace_tracedlog_v1.py added tracedLen (544, ~555) and S2 tracedLen (694, ~716).
Behavior notes (not bugs). (a) Snap catch-rate depends on ZOOM &mdash; radius is hardcoded 30.0 m REAL-WORLD; zoomed out (~&frac14; mile) almost nothing lands within 30 m of a line, zoomed in it catches reliably. This explained an apparent "snap stopped working" that was just zoom level. (b) Trace draws ONLY between two CONSECUTIVE snapped vertices on the SAME line; isolated or cross-line snapped points draw straight to their neighbors, by design.
LINE-ENDING TRAP (cost ~6 patch iterations &mdash; record so it never costs that again). ConvoyScreen.kt has MIXED line endings. file reports CRLF (the majority), but individual lines (e.g. 544's draw line) end \r\n while others are \n. cat -A, grep -U, and xxd piped through sed ALL LIE &mdash; sed normalizes the terminator, so a CRLF line shows as $ / 0a. The ONLY reliable check is a raw Python byte read: python3 -c "d=open(PATH,'rb').read(); i=d.find(b'&lt;anchor&gt;'); print(repr(d[i-260:i+115]))". Patches must write OLD/NEW with the file's real \r\n. The identical raw draw line appears at BOTH 544 and 694, so single-line anchors match 2&times; &mdash; disambiguate by folding in unique context above (the freeVertex/addVertex lines) or by the differing indent (544 = 32 spaces, 694 = 36). No BOM (first bytes = pac of package).

The com/geeksville/mesh/ source paths are a Meshtastic-fork PATH ARTIFACT; the app identity is com.grouptrack.android. adb pull needs MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 on the REMOTE path only (not the local dest, which breaks it) &mdash; simplest is cd ~/Downloads then pull to ..

2026-06-05 · Route lifecycle settled, work sequence, cleanups, AAB fix, tester recovery

Route lifecycle — SETTLED MODEL (full detail; Item 1 to build)
A route is EITHER an in-progress draft (JSON file) OR a completed spatial-DB row — never both. The JSON is interim storage holding the SAME data the completed-save consumes (the vertex chain), so a route can be picked up, redisplayed, and editing continued. Graduation writes the DB row and deletes the JSON.
R1 Either/or — draft-file XOR DB-row. Graduation: write row + delete draft.
R2 Identity — in-progress identity = the typed NAME (set at New). Route id is assigned ONLY at graduation to the spatial DB, under DB dedup rules. No route id exists while a route is a draft. Draft world = name; DB world = id. (This replaced an earlier "currentDraftId" framing — the in-progress key is the name, not a generated id.)
R3 Save exits — EVERY save (completed or in-progress) EXITS route mode. To continue editing an in-progress route: Save In Progress → then RE-SELECT it from the In-Progress list. There is NO mid-session "save &amp; continue" and NO in-place state promotion. Save closes; select reopens. (This simplification was made deliberately this session to remove the messy mid-session promotion path.)
R4 State fixed at launch — the entry row is the launch fork: New ⇒ NEW for the whole session; Select In-Progress ⇒ RESUMED for the whole session (carrying the name). The adaptive Save/Discard screens read this fixed state; it does not change mid-session.
R5 Writes minimal — the ONLY writes are: create-draft, overwrite-draft, insertRoute(+delete-draft on graduate), delete-draft. Roll-back, discard-new, and cancel NEVER write.
R6 Both maps — identical on ConvoyScreen (convoy map, LF) and ConvoyMapViewerScreen (planning map, CRLF), driving the shared RouteManager singleton; toolbar ConvoyRouteToolbar CRLF. cat -A before every patch (endings flip across commits, esp. after git restore).
R7 Vertices not wkt — the draft stores the FULL vertex chain (lat, lon, lineId, lineType, segmentIndex, t, snapped); wkt/bbox are DERIVED at graduation by replaying buildWktAndBbox, so a resumed draft graduates through the IDENTICAL completed-save path. Vertices-not-wkt preserves true editing on resume.
Adaptive Save / Discard (full screen behavior)
Placement: Save and Discard live on the COLLAPSED title bar (one-tap access, no real-estate cost) AND in the expanded panel. Each is ONE entry point that opens an adaptive SCREEN; the choices presented are driven by the fixed launch state.
Adaptive SAVE — NEW route: [Save completed (needs ≥2 pts; LIVE — buildWktAndBbox→insertRoute→clear→exit→redraw)] · [Save in-progress → writeDraft (new JSON keyed by name), then EXIT (SOON)] · [Cancel → back to building, no write].
Adaptive SAVE — RESUMED draft: [Graduate = completed-save path → DB row, THEN deleteDraft, exit (SOON)] · [Save with changes → overwriteDraft (same name), exit (SOON)] · [Cancel].
Adaptive DISCARD — NEW route: [Discard &amp; exit → clearRoute+clearBuildLine+exit, NO write (LIVE)] · [Keep building]. (Open: direct vs confirm prompt.)
Adaptive DISCARD — RESUMED draft: [Roll back to last save → reload the unchanged draft file (drop in-memory edits), NO write — implemented as re-running openDraft (SOON)] · [Delete in-progress → deleteDraft, the ONLY discard path that writes (SOON)] · [Keep building].
Add ↔ Method coupling (CONFIRMED, asymmetric)
Add is the DEFAULT selection, GREEN/on, on entering BOTH New and In-Progress (taps place points). Add is ASYMMETRIC: it turns OFF/RED ONLY when Draw or Suggest is selected — there is NO manual turn-off. The ONLY manual action is tapping Add to turn it back ON, reclaiming design control FROM Draw/Suggest. Add = "design-control-is-here" indicator (GREEN = point-placement has control; RED = Draw/Suggest has control; tap Add = take control back). This refines the earlier "self-toggle" framing — Add is not a free toggle; off is automatic, on is manual.
Draft store functions to be written (LAST — after UI hardens)
RouteManager stays a PURE singleton (no Context/file I/O). The draft store is a NEW Context-holding component, working name RouteDraftStore.kt.
writeDraft(name, vertices, method) · overwriteDraft(name, vertices, method) · listDrafts() → [{name, updatedAt, pointCount}] · openDraft(name) → {vertices, method} (used by BOTH resume AND roll-back — same op) · deleteDraft(name) (graduate cleanup + discard-delete).
Storage: dedicated subfolder /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/route_drafts/&lt;name&gt;.json (sanitized name = filename; user-visible; survives reinstall; isolated from the spatial DB and map-state files). Atomic write: write &lt;name&gt;.json.tmp then rename over target — a draft is never half-written.
JSON shape: { schemaVersion, name, createdAt, updatedAt, method, vertices:[{lat,lon,lineId,lineType,segmentIndex,t,snapped}…] } — no id, no wkt, no bbox.
Why JSON files not DB: a draft is interim, standalone, document-shaped, and is EITHER a file OR a DB row (R1) — putting the interim form in the DB blurs that line and risks tangling with the dedup/geom_hash machinery (which is for completed rows). JSON costs no schema migration. (Would only flip to DB if drafts ever needed to sync to AWS or be cross-queried — they don't; they're purely local interim state until graduation.)
Build sequence for Item 1 (UI-first, functions last)
Patch 1 (UI-first): routeState (NEW|RESUMED + name) · adaptive Save/Discard SCREENS · Save/Discard on collapsed bar · EMULATED Select-In-Progress (hardcoded draft list + hardcoded vertex chain). All store calls STUBBED (log only). Files: ConvoyRouteToolbar (CRLF) + ConvoyScreen (LF) + ConvoyMapViewerScreen (CRLF). Walk the ✓-stub test rows on BOTH maps. Proves navigation + adaptive branching with ZERO file I/O.
Patch 2: real RouteDraftStore (write/overwrite/list/open/delete, atomic temp+rename). Swap stubs for real calls. Verify round-trip via logcat (write → list → open → vertices match).
Patch 3: wire graduate-delete + Discard-delete + roll-back-reload to the real store. Full end-to-end, both maps.
Why test with no functions: stub each store call to log + show a confirmation. The navigation and adaptive RULES are pure UI state branching, fully walkable with stubs. The emulated In-Progress selector (hardcoded list + chain) is the centerpiece — it lets resume → RESUMED-state Save/Discard choices be proven before any JSON is written. ✓-stub rows = provable now; ◐-needs-fn rows (real persistence) re-walked after Patch 2/3.
Open decisions
(a) DECIDED 2026-06-05 — Duplicate-name policy: DEMAND a unique name for manually-created routes, unique across BOTH the draft JSON world AND the routes DB. On save, if the name collides with an existing DRAFT (JSON) OR an existing ROUTE in the routes DB, REJECT and re-prompt — showing the OLD name pre-filled so the user can modify it. No overwrite, no silent disambiguation. Why both worlds: a draft graduates via insertRoute into the shared tracks/routes table — if its name already matches a completed route, graduation would create a name-dupe ON THE ROUTE-TABLE INSERT. Checking uniqueness against the DB AT THE PROMPT (not just against drafts) prevents that collision before it can reach insert. So a draft accepted as uniquely-named can always graduate cleanly. Consistent with R2 (name = identity → must be globally unique among routes/drafts). Function: isNameTaken(name) → bool checks BOTH sources — listDrafts() (JSON) AND a routes-DB name query. The New/rename dialog loops until a unique name is given or the user cancels. Safety re-check: also re-verify uniqueness AT GRADUATION (a name free when the draft was created could in principle be taken before it graduates — unlikely single-user, but re-prompt before insert if so). Primary enforcement = prompt; belt-and-suspenders = graduate-time re-check.
(b) Discard-on-NEW: acts directly vs. confirm prompt. STILL OPEN.
(c) In-Progress picker over-limit threshold, if any. STILL OPEN (likely moot — few drafts).
snap-2 (Item 2) — status &amp; diagnosis (carried, full)
snap-2 trail-snapping does NOT work on device — dropping points produces STRAIGHT LINES. The route-save FRAMEWORK works (create → name → save to spatial DB → redraw). The snap() call is wired into onMapTap and compiles but was never proven; observed behavior is straight lines.
Root cause #1 (found + fixed, in 204405fc7): ConvoyScreen had TWO onMapTap handlers — persistent-WebView branch snapped, but the FACTORY/loadUrl branch was free-place only (Handler.post{addVertex(freeVertex)}). Fresh WebView runs the factory branch → straight lines. Fixed (factory body → snap coroutine).
Root cause #2 (found, not fixed — chase FIRST): after the factory fix, still straight at radius 30 AND 80. SnapDiag showed radius read correctly (80.0), trails=138/tracks=10 returned, first tap snapped to a TRACK, every subsequent snapResult=null; a returned trail's geometry was at lat 37.25 while taps were at 37.48 → queryTrailsByViewport may be returning WRONG-AREA trails. Confirm queryTrailsByViewport returns right-area trails for the tapped viewport before anything else.
Root cause #3 / the real remaining gap: the LIVE redraw in onMapTap/onUndo feeds RAW routeVertices() to drawBuildLine (straight chords). buildSegments() — which slices trail geometry between same-line snapped vertices so the line FOLLOWS the trail — is ONLY called at Save (buildWktAndBbox), NEVER during live build. So even correctly-snapped points draw straight chords live.
The fix (Item 2 direction): a shared per-screen helper redrawRouteTraced(): query → byId(lineId→geometry) → RouteManager.buildSegments{lineId→parseWktLine} → emit Leaflet [lat,lon] (buildSegments returns [lon,lat], MUST swap) → drawBuildLine. Wire into all 5 redraw sites: ConvoyScreen onMapTap persistent (~530) + factory (~688) + onUndo (~1416); ConvoyMapViewerScreen onMapTap (~488) + onUndo (~898). Write the helper, wire ONE site (factory onMapTap) FIRST to prove, then roll to the other 4. CAUTION: helper must be placed AFTER webViewRef is declared (a v1 attempt failed at ~234, before webViewRef → "Unresolved reference webViewRef"). Save path's lineGeom pattern to mirror (ConvoyScreen ~1428): byId from trail_id ?: track_id → buildWktAndBbox{lineId→byId[lineId]?.let{parseWktLine(it)}}.
RouteManager surface (line refs, drift-prone — impact only): snap (138, trail-first/track-fallback) · snapToVertex (169) · freeVertex (172) · addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices (180-184) · parseWktLine (42) · buildSegments (218) · buildWktAndBbox (246) · insertRoute (647) · queryTrailsByViewport/queryTracksByViewport (265/342, keys "geometry","trail_id"/"track_id").
Tester DB — "dupes" investigation (resolved) + NULL-name cleanup
Confirmed NOT a bug: pulled tester spatial DB (114MB) and grouped trails by name. On every repeated name, copies == distinct_geom (Grass Valley ATV 3/3, Connector 42/42, Daybreak Pkwy 111/111, UofU Pathways 4583/4583, Not Named 620/620, etc.). These are UNIQUE geometries sharing a name — multi-segment trails — correctly kept by UNIQUE(geom_hash). Dedup is working. Do NOT merge/delete these (would destroy valid data). Verified Grass Valley ATV ×3 = three distinct geom_hashes.
Real item — NULL trail names → cleanup task: some unnamed trails land as SQL NULL instead of the 'Not Named' fallback (two "no-name" forms coexist: 'Not Named' ~620 rows + raw NULL). Fix 1 (DB, one-time, PC copy): UPDATE trails SET name='Not Named' WHERE name IS NULL; (count first). Fix 2 (import, root cause): coalesce missing/empty name → 'Not Named' at insert so no NULL ever enters (aligns trails with tracks). Folds into Item 3 (My Tracks display refactor).
Section field for same-name multi-segment items (NEW cleanup item — Fred surfaced 2026-06-05)
The geom_hash already does its job (dedup + identity) — that is NOT the issue. The ACTUAL problem is the recurring human question "why does this trail appear multiple times?" FIX: add a separate section field on the row. On import, when multiple rows share a name but have DIFFERENT hashes (genuinely distinct segments), assign section 1, 2, 3… to those rows. A name with a single row gets NO section (displays plain — no "section 1" on a one-piece trail). The hash is the DETECTOR (confirms the rows are distinct); the section is STRUCTURED DATA, not text baked into the name.
Why a separate field, NOT a number in the name string: the segments always appear back-to-back, so a number jammed into the display name ("Cedar Pass 2") is noise. As a field: (1) the stored name stays clean ("Cedar Pass") so search / group-by-name still work naturally; (2) section is a real value you can FILTER on, sort by, count — not a string to parse back out; (3) singletons simply have no section, so no ugly "Section 1" on a one-piece trail. Display shows section as a quiet SECONDARY element (e.g. "Cedar Pass · 2" or a sub-label), available for filter/display logic.
Trigger: on import, for a name with N rows and N distinct geom_hashes, set section = 1..N on those rows; single-row names leave section null/0.
Scope (like NULLs, import-only): only arises on IMPORTS. In-app created routes/tracks get a deliberate unique name at creation (R2 — typed name is identity), so they never hit this. The section assignment belongs on the import path; display reads the field.
Relationship to the two other naming items (keep distinct): (1) NULL → 'Not Named' (fallback for nameless); (2) same-name multi-segment rows are VALID, do not merge (copies==distinct_geom — confirmed); (3) THIS — add a structured section field (1..N) to same-name distinct-hash rows so the user sees numbered sections and stops asking why a trail "repeats".
Open for the design pass (decide then): display format for the extras ("· 2" vs a sub-label vs a column); numbering/ordering basis (import order, spatial/connected order, arbitrary-but-stable); whether section also feeds a "show all sections of this trail" filter. (Assign-at-import is DECIDED — see below — so it's no longer open.) Folds into Item 3 (My Tracks display refactor).
CHOSEN MECHANISM (2026-06-05): an end-of-import SQL pass that (a) fixes NULLs: UPDATE … SET name='Not Named' WHERE name IS NULL, and (b) populates the separate section field for same-name multi-distinct-hash groups. Numbering: first occurrence is IMPLIED (blank/null section — displays as just "Cedar Pass"); additional occurrences get 2, 3, … N to mark their uniqueness on the map. So only the EXTRAS carry a visible number; the first looks normal. Writes to section, NOT name — keeps name clean and searchable.
RESOLVE AT IMPORT, NOT AT READ (decided 2026-06-05): the name/section is read in TOO MANY display/filter places to control the numbering at read time. So the section is computed ONCE at import and written to the field; every read site just shows the stored field as-is — no read-side numbering logic duplicated across sites. (Same "rules in one place" principle as the DB-model validation: resolve at the boundary, trust the field downstream.) This settles the assign-at-import vs compute-at-display question → assign at import.
Must be re-import-STABLE: a later import must not renumber existing rows or double-number (no "2 2"); base numbering on a stable key (geom_hash order or createdAt), only number rows lacking a section, or recompute deterministically so the same row always gets the same section. Nail this in the design pass.
⚠️ SEQUENCING DEPENDENCY (critical — decided 2026-06-05): the section-numbering pass MUST run AFTER the import's add is COMPLETELY finished — you cannot identify unique occurrences until ALL occurrences of a name are in the table. Numbering mid-import sees an incomplete set for a name and numbers wrong. So the cleanup pass sits BEHIND the finished add (post-insert), not woven into the per-row insert. Order within the pass: (1) NULL fix FIRST — there are 1,644 nulls; convert them to 'Not Named' before numbering (otherwise NULLs group oddly / behave inconsistently in the partition). (2) THEN section numbering — group by name, find names with multiple distinct hashes, leave the first IMPLIED (blank), number additional occurrences 2..N; each added number identifies that track as a UNIQUE occurrence of that name. (Design note: after the NULL fix, the 1,644 'Not Named' rows become one big same-name group — decide whether 'Not Named' is excluded from sectioning or sectioned like any other name.)
Therefore the import must be UPDATED: add the post-add cleanup pass to the import process (behind the completed add). This is a change to the import flow, not just a one-time DB script — the same pass runs end-of-import every time so new imports stay clean. (A one-time SQL on the current DB also fixes the existing 1,644 nulls + existing same-name groups.)
geom_hash size (reference fact)
geom_hash = SHA-256 over the raw WKT = 256 bits / 32 bytes. Stored as TEXT hex digest = 64 characters per row (base64 would be ~44). At ~49K trails ≈ 3 MB of hash text — trivial. Collision probability effectively zero at this scale; safe identity key. (Per-type UNIQUE(geom_hash) is what makes the multi-segment trails coexist as distinct rows.)
Trail display over-limit guidance (fix; Item 3 / §D)
When the viewport trail count exceeds the display cap (200), the SEL/Edit button shows "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce" (disabled until count drops). State-driven label swap off the existing viewport count; no new query. Replaces silent truncation. Relates to the artifact-list 200-cap / paging item. Open: disabled-vs-tappable, and whether 200 is the right trail threshold.
⚠️ DB lifecycle on schema change — release artifact, NOT install-path logic (Fred refined 2026-06-05)
CORRECT MODEL: removing the existing DB is a deliberate RELEASE artifact, tied to a SCHEMA CHANGE — not something the install or update process does. Rationale: the automatic rebuild already covers the normal case (if data does not exist, the app rebuilds it — existing behavior). So normal install/update needs NO special DB handling. You only add a deliberate DB-removal step, gated to schema-change releases: that release clears the old DB so the automatic "no data → rebuild" lands on the NEW schema.
The inversion: do NOT burden the install/update path with detect-and-check-pre-existing-DB logic (an earlier framing this session). The automatic rebuild-if-absent already handles the normal case. Control belongs at the RELEASE, which actually KNOWS whether it changed the schema — the install path doesn't and shouldn't.
How it works: (1) normal release, no schema change → do nothing; existing DB is used; if absent, auto-rebuild. (2) schema-change release → the release carries the DB-removal artifact → old DB removed → auto-rebuild produces the new schema. Removal only ever fires on a schema-change release.
Second option — build/load/unload hook: this same release-time point gives a place to LOAD / TRANSFORM / UNLOAD data when required, instead of plain remove. So the artifact is a release-time DB-lifecycle hook: DEFAULT = remove (let auto-rebuild happen); OPTIONAL = load/transform/unload for a schema change that must PRESERVE user data across the migration.
CONTROL SURFACE — "save and reload data" checkbox (Fred 2026-06-05): a single checkbox on the schema-change release artifact gives FULL control of the DB upgrade path: unchecked → remove DB → auto-rebuild fresh new-schema DB (data discarded — for re-derivable data); checked → save existing data → rebuild on new schema → reload data into it (data preserved across migration). One switch covers both upgrade strategies, chosen per release at the point where the release knows what its schema change requires. Net upgrade matrix: normal release → nothing fires; schema-change + unchecked → remove + auto-rebuild; schema-change + checked → save→rebuild→reload.
HOME = the release JSON (app artifacts): the control lives in the release JSON as part of the app artifacts — two fields: db_name_to_delete (which DB the schema-change release removes) and a reinstall_data flag/checkbox (the save-and-reload control). The release carries the intent; the app reads it at the schema-change boundary.
⚠️ SHAPE DELIBERATELY DEFERRED — do NOT specify the reload mechanism now: we do NOT need any code or shape for the data save/reload yet. When it's actually needed it could be "rename existing DB and repopulate with logic" OR "a simple table unload and load" — but we do not give it that shape until we HAVE to use it. The release JSON reserves the control point (which DB, whether to preserve); the HOW is decided at the moment a real migration defines its requirements. (Same principle as the rest of the method: don't build/specify a mechanism before a concrete need defines it — specifying the reload shape now would be guessing at requirements we don't have.)
Why this is better than per-install detection: (a) no new logic in the hot install/update path; (b) decision sits where the knowledge is (the release knows the schema changed); (c) leverages the existing auto-rebuild instead of duplicating it; (d) the same hook scales to data-preserving migrations via the load/unload option.
Background that prompted this (tonight): tester uninstalled 2.4 → installed 2.5 (new install, schema changed 2.4→2.5). Spatial/data DBs can SURVIVE uninstall in shared storage (/sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/); a surviving OLD-schema DB would break 2.5. It worked tonight only because the uninstall happened to clear the DBs (verified via ls). The release-artifact model makes this deterministic: a schema-change release removes the old DB regardless of how uninstall behaved. (By design the user DB is MEANT to survive uninstall — §M — so the removal must be deliberate and schema-gated, never a blanket install-time wipe that would destroy user data on a same-schema reinstall.)
CAUTION (ties to §M data-survival + Standing Rule 1): removal must be gated strictly to schema-change releases. A blanket "remove DB on install" would destroy user data (waypoints/routes/tracks that are designed to persist across reinstall) on an ordinary same-schema reinstall. The gate is the whole point.
AAB versionCode collision — RESOLVED (full mechanism, so never re-derived)
Mechanism: app/build.gradle.kts computes versionCode = project.findProperty("android.injected.version.code") ?: System.getenv("VERSION_CODE") ?: (gitVersionProvider.get().toInt() + vcOffset), where vcOffset = VERSION_CODE_OFFSET = 29314197. A plain rebuild regenerates the same number from git commit count → collides with an already-uploaded bundle.
Error: Play rejected with "Version code 29320588 has already been used." App bundle explorer ceiling was 29320588 (the failed attempt itself, now Inactive); active was 29320569.
Fix (one-time, no file edit): the build honors -Pandroid.injected.version.code=NNNNN FIRST. Built ./gradlew bundleGoogleRelease -x uploadCrashlyticsMappingFileGoogleRelease -Pandroid.injected.version.code=29320600. BUILD SUCCESSFUL 40m47s (first build). Verified baked in: unzip -p …aab base/manifest/AndroidManifest.xml | grep -a versionCode → 29320600. Uploaded to Internal testing, rolled out. (Play Console "Next" button needed full-screen to be visible.)
Durable fix (optional, NOT done): bump VERSION_CODE_OFFSET so future plain builds clear the ceiling automatically.
versionName note: "2.7.14" is the user-facing versionName; the big number is versionCode. They are different — only versionCode must monotonically increase for Play.
Tester device clean-install recovery (lesson)
Tester (serial TC5010926B071521) uninstalled 2.4 to install 2.5. Schema changed 2.4→2.5; a clean install doesn't run migration, so old-schema DBs would break 2.5. Verified via ls that grouptrack_spatial.db and grouptrack_data.db were already GONE (uninstall removed them) — only empty 0-byte -journal orphans + data/trail_areas/ + maps/ remained. So 2.5 builds fresh v3 DBs; preserved tiles/areas intact.
adb fought hard: shell rm/ls hung repeatedly; recovery = taskkill //F //IM adb.exe → adb start-server → adb devices → re-authorize on device (unlock screen for the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt). appops grant fails before install ("No UID" = package not installed yet — install must precede permission grant).
KEY LESSON: the GroupTrack maps/ folder had ~200,000 tiles. Fresh install + large tile cache = the Files app spins and first launch ANRs while the OS/app enumerates the tile count — that is the device WORKING, not failing. Force-fighting (adb resets, reboots mid-scan) restarts the clock. Fred let the device SETTLE ~2 hours undisturbed → everything worked. Always: patient first launch on big tile caches.
Always confirm adb devices serial before any command (Droid 2 = 24039703201775 often unauthorized on the bench; don't cross wires).

⭐⭐ THE GOVERNING SPECIFICATION — settled 07-31, do not re-derive
ConceptMeansRule
Persistencestate RECREATION — position, zoom, artifact display states,
checked rowsBoth maps write on every screen refresh. Restores the map as you left it.
Route modeACTIVELY PLOTTING POINTS RIGHT NOW
⭐ FALSE ON EVERY MAP ENTRY, BOTH MAPS. Armed ONLY by user action — Route+, Draw, or a
recovery Continue. Never by persistence.
Draft filea route was not finishedDrives a message and the resolver.
Never arms anything.
THE TAP RULE, entire: route mode OFF → tap opens artifacts. Route mode ON → tap places a
route point, nothing else consumes it.
⭐⭐ THEREFORE POPUPS NEVER NEED SUPPRESSING. If the tap does not reach the artifact layer,
no popup can open. Every unbind / stash / restore / bind-gate in the codebase solves a problem that
correct tap routing makes impossible.
⚠ Route mode is an ACTIVITY, not restorable state. A file on disk means a route is
unfinished; route mode means points are being placed now. Conflating those two is the whole mess.

Two arm it: opening Route+ · selecting Draw.
⚠ Also add observability on the route button in the route panel — with six transitions and
no visible state, "did that discard actually turn it off?" is currently unanswerable.
🔴 STEP 3 — UNNAMED-DRAFT RESOLVER
Two draft types, two meanings:
DraftMeansResponse
Nameduser deliberately saved as in-progressSoft reminder —
"you have unfinished routes"
Unnamednever saved, no normal end of job — abnormal⚠ Resolution
prompt: Save (name it) or Discard
⭐ THE KEY DESIGN DECISION — file operations only
Fred: "we can even write a separate section of code for that instance that just renames or
deletes the json without touching the route state."
The resolver renames or deletes a FILE. It does not open Route+, arm route mode, load geometry
or draw a build line. That removes the whole reconciliation problem — entry sets route mode off,
the prompt resolves the file, route mode stays off.
⚠ And it likely makes :1472 deletable — the recovery arming exists to RESUME a
draft, and if resolution does not resume, nothing needs it. Confirm with the step-1 toast first.
The logic
unnamed draft exists?
  no        → return
  &lt;2 points → delete silently, LOG IT, return
  ≥2 points → prompt: Save (name it) / Discard
              → rename or delete the file
              → return
⭐ The &lt;2-point silent discard matters: a draft with one point or none carries nothing
worth recovering, and prompting for it is noise. ⚠ But log it — it is the only trace that a
crash occurred, and losing it hides how often that happens.
Called from TWO places
Planner entry and Route+ launch. One resolver, two callers. ⭐ Route+ cannot start
with the slot occupied because the resolver has already cleared it — the unnamed slot is
single-occupancy.
⚠ Named drafts do NOT block Route+. They are parked, not in the way.
⚠ "Save" here means keep the file and give it a name — not "resume and save properly". So
it needs the route-name dialog, not a plain confirm. Label the button to match.
🔴 STEP 4 — TAP BEHAVIOUR PER MODE, PER PANEL
This is where the 07-03 regression lives. Do not start it before steps 1–3, or a wrong tap
is indistinguishable from a stale state.
ModeTap does
Drawplaces a route point — nothing else consumes it
Artifacttracks → ARTIFACT DETAIL PANEL (not a popup); trails → popup
⭐ The detail panel chain is already proven: ARTIFACTTAP →
onTrackTap → pendingDetailType/pendingDetailId → gate →
ArtifactDetailPanel. __detailPanelEnabled is already true on
both maps. Convoy was showing the panel correctly on 07-31.
⚠ The planner is untested since the addPointMode fix. The popup seen afterwards
was probably the proximity scan — which is step 5's problem. Steps 4 and 5 are entangled: a
proximity popup racing the detail panel looks exactly like the panel not working.
⚠⚠ THE HARD REQUIREMENT — visible + snappable + non-interactive
During a route draw you must SEE trails, SNAP to them, and NOT TAP them. Three concerns the code
currently collapses into one flag.
⛔ Hiding layers is not a workaround — snap is fed from queryTrailsByViewport,
and with trails hidden there is no snap and no guidance. Tracks were removed from snap on 07-30
(snapTrailsOnly — a track is one geometry, so snapping pulled the whole thing).
⚠ And the SVG approach will not work. sub._path.style.pointerEvents — the line
commit 43ab77e16 deleted — is an SVG DOM property, and both maps moved to L.canvas on
07-31. Canvas paths are not DOM elements. The canvas mechanism is:
lyr.eachLayer(function(sub) { sub.options.interactive = !on; });
⚠ VERIFY THIS FIRST — it is the one unknown between the spec and the patch. Stateless,
survives layer rebuilds, and replaces the stash/restore block entirely.
⚠ Trails have no onTrailTap bridge on either map — they can only ever produce a
popup. That is a gap, not a bug.
⛔ Route drawing is BLOCKED as of 07-31. Before canvas the tap was SHARED (popup AND vertex
— messy but usable); now the artifact consumes it and no vertex lands. ⚠ Canvas did not break the
suppression — it removed the accident that was masking it. Reverting canvas is the wrong trade:
it would restore a broken mechanism to a merely tolerable failure mode while giving back the trail
hit-rate fix (3 hits in 40 taps at z18).
🔴 STEP 5 — HIDDEN ARTIFACTS CONTRIBUTE NOTHING
Fred: "hide keeps them from being placed on the map, not just invisible" — a hidden type
must not participate in taps, proximity, snap or selection. Visibility IS the selection.
Observed defect
Trails OFF, tap a track on the planner, get a list of TRAIL names.
Cause: hideTrails() does map.removeLayer(trailLayer) and sets
trailsVisible = false — it does NOT null the variable. The proximity scan at
grouptrack_map.html:831 calls checkLayer(trailLayer, …), which skips only
on null. A detached-but-populated layer is still fully walkable.
⚠ It also explains "occasionally the detail panel instead" — the scan is a MAP-level click handler
racing the layer's own handler.
⚠ And behaviour depends on HOW you turned it off: clearTrails() nulls the variable,
hideTrails() does not.
The fix
⛔ Do NOT null on hide — the retained variable is a CACHE. loadTrails rebuilds
from a fresh GeoJSON payload, so nulling means a full query and rebuild per toggle. At 10,000 trails
that is a visible cost.
function checkLayer(layer, visible, typeName, color) {
  if (!layer || !visible) return;
Four call sites, both maps. Correct regardless of which path turned the type off.
⚠ There is also a DUPLICATE proximity scan — a pure-JS copy at :813 running
alongside the restored Kotlin path, so two popups race per tap. Knowingly accepted on 07-30. A third,
dead copy sits at :74-123 inside a src-bearing script tag whose inline
content the browser ignores.
🔴 STEP 6 — SNAP VERIFICATION
Verify route points snap to trails only, and — under step 5's rule — visible trails
only.
⚠ RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) is fed from
queryTrailsByViewport / queryTracksByViewport — database queries, not
layers. Those know nothing about display state, so a vertex can probably snap to a HIDDEN trail.
Not verified — ConvoyScreen.kt:596 builds the byId map from both
queries with no visibility filter that I saw, but I only read part of it.

⚠ NAMING COLLISION — know this before reading the code
routeState means TWO UNRELATED THINGS in ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:
local var (:701) = the ROUTES ARTIFACT display state (DS_OFF/ON/SELECTED)
MapSnapshot.routeState = the route SESSION record (open/status/draftName)
Same name, same file, different concepts. This caused genuine confusion in discussion. Worth
renaming during the cleanup pass.
⚠ Similarly: ConvoyScreen.kt is convoy; ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt is
the planner. Both start with "Convoy" and neither says "planner".
⭐ METHOD — what actually worked, and what did not
07-31 cost thirteen builds. Seven hypotheses were eliminated on trails alone, four more on
convoy taps. Every one was a plausible mechanism and every one was disproven on device.
⭐ What solved both real bugs was reasoning about BEHAVIOUR, not code — "bands by
longitude", "adding Arizona puts trails below the tracks", the tap test, and "planner has popups and
convoy doesn't, which is backwards". Each was decisive; none came from reading source.
Fred: "our errors were at 30,000 feet and we were dealing in the details." ⭐
State the rule in English first, then check the code against it. Not the reverse.
⚠ The structural cost driver is patchy instrumentation. Tap handlers log, bridges mostly do
not, state writes never do — so every hunt begins by spending a build to see anything. Today's
patch is that lesson applied. Fred: "the absence of the toast is the absence of a change
request."
⚠ Blast radius: where_used_raw.txt and function_universe_raw.txt

uses it. field_crossref_raw.txt is the strongest of the four ([R]/[W] markers, bridge
caller analysis, code warnings). For anything JS-side, grep the assets.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING OF THE DAY — read this before touching either map
grouptrack_map.html opened with a script block whose first
statement was map.on('click', ...) — but map is not created
until 720 lines later. It threw at parse time and killed the whole block. Two
things died with it:
Android.onProximityTap was never registered — short taps never
reached Kotlin at all.
showProximityPopup was never defined. It is the only definition
in the codebase and ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:578 calls it by name, so even
a successful query had nothing to render into.
⚠ Invisible for as long as it has existed — the planner had no
WebChromeClient, so its console output went nowhere. Confirmed
pre-existing against HEAD~1.
⭐ Everything we changed downstream first — bind guards, stopPropagation,
stash/restore, route mode — sat below a handler that was never registered. That is
the lesson: instrument before theorising, and a console bridge is instrumentation.
⭐ Two flags for one concept — still unresolved
Kotlin addPointMode and JS window.__routeMode mean the
same thing and nothing keeps them in sync. Proven divergent 07-30:
TrackTap: PLANNER bridge id=8f8c39b1… addPointMode=true
TrackTap: PLANNER SUPPRESSED by addPointMode
— while every ARTIFACTTAP line in the same session read routeMode=false.
Route mode was off. The Kotlin flag was on. Every track tap died at that guard.
⚠ Fred's framing, and it is the right one: route mode is the wrong predicate.
It means "Route+ is open". What actually needs guarding is "the next tap places a
vertex". The fix is one flag, one setter, both sides updated from the same call
— and the narrow name, not the screen-state name.
⛔ Note item 3b's fall-through guard currently keys off __routeMode. If
the predicate changes, that has to change with it or it drifts again.
Convoy — different disease from the planner
⛔ Convoy does NOT have the parse-order defect. Its map is created
at :298 inside the first block, and clearMarkers (:184)
and drawTrack (:275) are defined in that same block. It parses
cleanly.
Its errors are timing: ConvoyScreen.kt:296 and :397
call evaluateJavascript("clearMarkers()") and drawTrack(...)
against a page that is not ready — they fired one second before the planner opened,
which is convoy being torn down.
⭐ Convoy already has a working console bridge — ConvoyJS at
ConvoyScreen.kt:777, twelve console.log calls including four
ARTIFACTTAP and a ROUTEMODE trace. Diagnosable with no build.
⚠ Convoy also carries dead route-mode scaffolding from when route add was
removed — var routeMode at :204, __routeMode guards,
setRouteMode with stash/unbind. On a map that cannot build routes those can
only do harm: if anything ever calls setRouteMode(true), every popup is
unbound with no path back. Fred's read: convoy is adopting planner values it never sets.

⚠ Process lessons — both cost real time today
1. Build on verified work, not on an empty queue. Items 1 and 2 were validated
an hour before we built. We held them to bundle item 3, which was still diagnostic —
and item 3 introduced a defect (3b) that forced a second build anyway. Worse: items 1
and 2 could have been tested and certified in that window. Bundling does not just
delay verification, it entangles it — if one item misbehaves the others are implicated
until proven otherwise.
2. Never bundle diagnostics with fixes. Settled work and exploratory work have
different risk. Item 3 was instrumentation written because we did not understand
the tap layers; putting it in the same build as two verified fixes let the unknown
break the known.
3. Check source timestamps against the APK before testing. Twice today we
tested a binary that predated the change — once losing a whole tap session. Twenty
seconds of ls -la against forty minutes of rebuild.
Environment notes worth keeping
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 fixes the REMOTE adb path and breaks the LOCAL
one. When both appear in one command the local side needs Windows form. adb
exec-out with a shell redirect avoids the conflict — the safer idiom for reading
device files.
Per-file newline detection is not optional. Today: OsmExtractWorker.kt
LF, OsmImportPanel.kt CRLF, grouptrack_map.html LF,
convoy_map.html CRLF — in the same patch run.
⚠ A literal &lt;/script&gt; inside a JS comment terminates the script
element. Item 4 v2 caught this in my own replacement text. Patch scripts that emit
HTML should refuse to insert script tags.

⭐ TILE STORAGE — unified process (ITEM A Pass 1 + ITEM B Pass 2) DESIGNNEXT
Design converged 07-06. This is the full design, written in.
The unified process (one spine, many origins, many destinations)
ORIGIN → NORMALIZE → EXPAND → CHOP → FETCH → [RETURN POINT] → WRITE → DESTINATION, pluggable at both ends.
  ORIGIN → (bbox, source-set) — the only place origins differ.
  NORMALIZE → (bbox, [sources]) — origins collapse to one canonical request; downstream is origin-blind.
  EXPAND → layers — each source → its layers via the source def (SAT → base + 2 overlays). "One SAT request → 3 destinations" happens here.
  CHOP → queue items — bbox → bounded cells; (layer, cell) = one queue item.
  FETCH → tiles — the ONE place the "miracle" varies: HTML per-tile, or batch export+unbundle, chosen per-layer by whether it has a batch process.
  RETURN POINT → uniform (type, z, x, y, bytes) stream — both transports emit this.
  WRITE → destination — the write contract resolves type → its .mbtiles and inserts.
Two fan points: fan-in at front (many origins → one canonical request); fan-out at back (one request → EXPAND layers → CHOP cells → many tiles → many DBs). Three extension points: add an origin = step 1 only; add a transport = step 5 miracle only; add a destination (new layer/type) = free.
MBTiles-only hard cutover (the decision)
Dual-path loose+MBTiles DROPPED — no state-file mode switch, no read/write fork, no Step-0 state-resolver. The ~5 map-invested testers re-download once. Storage format changes; HTML fetch survives. This supersedes the earlier "Steps 0 state-resolver → 1 write-fork → 2 read-fork → 3 batch-fetch" plan and the dual-path coexistence. GPX/track DBs stay separate. Worst case to design for: a tester at 80–90 GB of tiles (loose-file model = millions of files = the bloat/brick/slow-delete root cause).
Two-pass build
  Pass 1 — move current transport to spatial-DB storage. HTML fetch unchanged; only the WRITE changes (loose files → MBTiles). Covers all origins + all readers. MapView unchanged. = the V2.6 tile work + the "simplify" goal.
  Pass 2 — add a batch transport capability. New FETCH miracle built ALONGSIDE, gated off (layer.batch?.process), Esri first, provider-agnostic. Never touches Pass 1's storage — just a new way to feed the same write. Build-alongside-and-gate.
Write contract + the two "miracles"
Intercept at the RETURN POINT; everything above it is untouched. Two producers emit (type,z,x,y,bytes) into ONE shared write contract (MBTilesStore.insertTile + TileCodec + type→file resolve + y-flip):
  Miracle #1 (Pass 1): per-tile HTML write, redirected &lt;cache_dir&gt;/z/x/y.png → &lt;cache_dir&gt;.mbtiles.
  Miracle #2 (Pass 2): batch .tpkx → unbundle → same stream → same DBs.
The contract is producer-blind — that's why Pass 2 reuses Pass 1's write. Open: single insertTile vs transaction-batched insertTiles (faster for batch bulk); Miracle #2 streaming per-bundle vs collect-whole-package.
Schema — one MBTiles per TYPE (resolved 4 ways)
One MBTiles file per TYPE (= cache_dir = old directory name). No type column; base/overlay declared in each file's metadata; compositing at the Leaflet layer, not in storage. Confirmed by: (1) the render stacks separate per-type layers (we're not rewriting MapView); (2) the MBTiles spec mandates one tileset per file; (3) Esri best practice = base+reference separation; (4) Esri delivers per-service.
Canonical: tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row, tile_data) + metadata(name, value) + MANDATORY CREATE UNIQUE INDEX tile_index ON tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row). WebP yes; NEVER JPEG for overlays (kills alpha). FLAT vs NORMALIZED per type. PMTiles REJECTED (immutable — GroupTrack patches incrementally). TMS y-flip to settle.
DB naming = old directory names: cache_dir = type = old folder = convoy://tiles/&lt;type&gt;/… URL segment = .mbtiles filename. Migration: cache_dir folder → cache_dir.mbtiles. ⚠ TOPO+ has a + — verify it round-trips through the convoy:// URL + path open. Droid 2 has 5 type folders today: SAT, SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT, SAT_LABELS_PLACES, TOPO, TOPO+.
All download origins through the SAME area submission (audit + blast radius)
The unified process only holds if every origin funnels through the one area submission. Test per origin: does it end at the area submission with (bbox, sources), or bypass it (a second engine)?
  AREA — user-drawn bbox + selectable sources = the canonical engine.
  TRACK — bbox derived by padding the track's lat/long extents ½ mile + preference-sourced set → routes through area submission.
  ROUTE — "dupes track": same adapter shape (pad route extents → resolve sources from preference → area). Confirm it shares track's path.
  IMPORTED ARTIFACTS — an imported task WRITES A NEW ARTIFACT; the download panel has a "yes" import-maps toggle; if yes → the FIT PROCESS requests a map download for this track, right after track creation. So it is NOT a separate engine — it triggers a track-style download via the fit process → converges through track.
Prove the list exhaustive with a grep — enumerate every caller of the queue submission + every path reaching ConvoyTileDownloader/ConvoyDownloadWorker; classify each as canonical / adapter / rogue-bypass. May be unnamed origins — from code, not memory. Build a blast-radius process inventory (every process touching tile download/write + what it does) from the xref docs + code so a change doesn't underestimate what it breaks.
Source-set policy per origin: area = selectable; track/route = preference-default; artifacts = via track (likely track's preference).
Front-end standardization — WHY (inherit the large-bbox splitting)
Make each non-area origin a pure origin adapter — produce (bbox, source-set) and submit through the same area submission.
Primary reason: inherit the area process's large-bbox splitting. The area submission already chops a big bbox into bounded queue items (gridCells/tileBoundsLatLon) — real, tested. Track/route/artifacts on their own paths duplicate or lack it. Routing their bbox through the same submission → they inherit splitting for free. Triple duty: (i) splits big areas today; (ii) splits track/route/artifact downloads once standardized; (iii) sizes batch export jobs in Pass 2 (one split item = one Esri job under the 100k cap).
Other reasons: origins gain source control (fixed → selectable); convergence happens before the return point by construction → Pass 1's write-redirect is provably one seam. Confirm: does the area submission cleanly take (bbox, sources), or is it entangled with the drawing UI? If entangled, extract a pure (bbox, sources) → submit core first.
The ONE undefined region — the "miracle-happens" process (destination end)
Everything upstream is defined. The only open design work is the RETURN POINT → WRITE internals of MBTilesStore. It may already be a black box — before designing from scratch, find the existing tile-landing component and verify its internals against memory; reuse if it matches, design only the delta.
  (1) How many databases — dynamic: one MBTiles per type; count = however many distinct types across active sources (5 today). Open: who computes the DB set + when (up front from source defs vs lazy)? Rules-engine candidate.
  (2) How they're created — lifecycle: lazy create-if-absent on first insertTile, or provision up front? Creation writes canonical tiles + metadata + the mandatory tile_index, with metadata (name, base/overlay, format, bounds) at creation.
  (3) How overlays are linked — the base↔overlay relationship does NOT live in the tile DBs (each standalone, just tiles). It lives in the source definition (layers[] with role + render_order); MapView reads it at render to stack the right overlay DBs; each DB's metadata self-declares base-vs-overlay. Open: confirm nothing else needs the link (coverage? delete cascade?). Rules-engine candidate.
Pass 2 — batch transport (Esri) full design
  Core: the unit of variation is the provider's PROCESS, not just a key. Invoke the provider's own download+unbundle; one handler per provider protocol, reused across all its sources; the source def names the process + supplies parameters. One EsriExportTilesProcess serves all Esri sources.
  Schema: per-layer batch block — { "process":"esri_export_tiles", "export_endpoint":"&lt;MapServer&gt;/exportTiles", "package_format":"tpkx", "requires_key":true, "api_key_param":"token", "max_tiles_per_job":100000 }. process = dispatch key. No block → HTML per-tile.
  Request (async): POST exportTiles?f=json&amp;tilePackage=true&amp;exportBy=levelId&amp;levels={min-max}&amp;areaOfInterest={AOI wkid 4326}&amp;token={key} → jobId → poll /jobs/{jobId} until esriJobSucceeded → GET result → .tpkx.
  CompactV2 unpack (spec fully known): .tpkx = ZIP → root.json + iteminfo + thumbnail + tile/ of .bundle files. Each .bundle = 128×128 tile block: 64-byte header at offset 0 (LE) → tile index at byte 64 = 128×128 array of 8-byte records. TileIndexOffset = 64 + 8*(128*(row%128) + (col%128)). Each record: offset = bits 0–39, size = bits 40–63 → seek + read size bytes = raw tile. Absolute (row,col) = bundle base (from .bundle filename e.g. R0000C0000) + in-bundle row/col. Skip size-0. Port from Esri raster-tiles-compactcache (Vundler.py) / @syncpoint/compact-cache-bundle; GDAL 3.8+ ESRIC driver = cross-check oracle. .vtpk shares the same bundle format (vector pbf) → a future vector handler reuses the walk.
  SAT reassembly: exportTiles is per-service → 3 SAT services = 3 separate .tpkx, same unpack loop, only the destination DB differs (SAT / SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES). Separate, not combined.
  API key: reuse api_keys.json + getApiKey; inject ?token=&lt;key&gt;; never in source JSON, never logged; decrypt at call-time. Uses Fred's Esri Location Platform account (needs a token — the public tile endpoint doesn't).
  De-risk first: curl the exportTiles POST→poll→download flow against a real endpoint from Git Bash BEFORE any Kotlin. Confirm exportTiles is enabled on the public arcgisonline.com services.
Tile action plan (ordered Step 0 → 6)
  Step 0: verify the area download submission is the black box; origin audit + blast-radius inventory; scope the DB rules engine; pin down the fit process; standardize each non-area origin onto the area submission with a source preference (default = today's behavior).
  Step 0.5: resolve the miracle-happens design (find the existing black box + verify; settle DB-set enumeration, creation lifecycle, overlay linkage).
  Step 1 (Pass 1): read code bodies — ConvoyTileDownloader, ConvoyDownloadWorker, ConvoyDownloadQueue; both shouldInterceptRequest (CS 720-748, MVS 578+); overlay JS in convoy_map.html / grouptrack_map.html; show-downloaded/show-queued + MVS:658; how the codebase opens SQLite (SpatialDbManager) + the DB rules engine.
  Step 2 (Pass 1): scope-lock grep TILE_DIR/tilePath/File(...tiles → zero File(TILE_DIR,...) survivors.
  Step 3 (Pass 1): write MBTilesStore + TileCodec.toWebp, reusing the rules engine + SpatialDbManager. Settle y-flip, WebP content-type, schema variant, insertTile vs txn insertTiles, TOPO+ +.

⭐ ROUTE-STATE PERSISTENCE &amp; TEARDOWN (this morning's issue) OPEN
Root cause located 07-06 via fresh xref (recommit docs; navigation_xref regenerated 07-06 11:32). Fix design not yet locked — one source-check remains.
Problem (observed)
The route nav box disappears; states don't change as they should. Route-planning state is not reliably persisted across navigation, nor reliably torn down on exit. Two repro triggers (with a route open): (a) open/touch another item; (b) close the artifacts panel. Two failure modes: (1) route disappears from the map entirely; (2) route stays drawn but goes dead/inert (geometry visible, controls gone/unresponsive).
Root cause (located from xref)
Route mode is held in var routeMode by remember { mutableStateOf(false) } — ephemeral Compose state — at TWO independent copies: ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:129 and ConvoyScreen.kt:197. Both drive ONE shared window.__routeMode in convoy_map.html. Teardown = ~8 scattered hardcoded calls per screen of setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(); (ConvoyMapViewerScreen 955/1044/1075/1112, arm-on 996/1020, resume 1154; ConvoyScreen 1608/1684/1716/1743, arm-on 1648/1671, resume 1775). No single teardown funnel.
This one fact explains both failure modes: touching another item / closing the panel recomposes or orphans the remember boolean → Kotlin routeMode resets/desyncs but JS gets NO matching setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(). Disappear = a path fired clearBuildLine / a redraw overlaid it. Stays-but-dead = Kotlin routeMode went false so controls detach, but JS still shows the line.
Intent — Fred's 3 requirements
  Persist route-planning state in the MAP JSON so nav away + back restores it (survives recomposition/nav, which remember does not).
  States unique per map — Planning (grouptrack_map.html) vs Convoy (convoy_map.html) must not collide on the shared JS flag; the two booleans need per-map identity.
  Every exit ends it — save, discard, navigate away, back, mode-switch, backgrounding, item-tap, panel-close — via ONE teardown funnel every exit routes through (replacing the ~8 scattered teardowns).
Key principle: persist unless/until closed by an exit method — persist across nav, never past an exit.
Touchpoints + remaining source-check before locking
Touchpoints: setRouteMode (JS, convoy_map.html) toggled from both screens; window.__routeMode gate if(window.__routeMode)return; at convoy_map.html:495 (BUG A popup suppression — must stay mode-scoped); RouteManager holds build logic (snap/addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices, buildWktAndBbox, insertRoute); JS build fns drawBuildLine/clearBuildLine/updateRoutes/showRoutes; onTrackTap at ConvoyMapViewerScreen:515, ConvoyScreen:645 &amp; 895.
Before locking: the xref indexes definitions + bridge calls, not full handler bodies. Read the actual .kt for the artifact-panel-close (onDismiss/onClose) handler + the onTrackTap bodies and CONFIRM they lack a setRouteMode(false) teardown call (the diagnosis predicts they do). Then design = persist route state to the map JSON (per-map keyed) + single teardown funnel every exit routes through. Lock only after the two-handler read confirms.

V2.7 — iPad / CROSS-PLATFORM (post-V2.6 target)
Standing awareness — not an active task. iPad IS the post-V2.6 target (this overturns the old V3.0 "no iPad support" line). Reasoning arc reconciled 07-04. The evolution below is written in so it's never lost.
The reconciled strategy (07-04) STRATEGY
  Key collapse: Convoy is a fork of Meshtastic's messaging (Android = a fork of Meshtastic-Android, Kotlin). The native-vs-PWA-vs-WKWebView arc was all answering "how do we get BLE on iOS?" — a question that dissolves once convoy is seen as a fork of the mesh app. So iPad = a fork of Meshtastic-Apple (Swift/SwiftUI + BLE + protobuf; GPL v3; App-Store-approved; universal). Mac + Xcode = the prerequisite. Flag: Meshtastic-Apple ships native TAK/CoT — reconcile vs the roadmap's "TAK as pattern only."
  Config write is offloaded: the planning side CREATES a Meshtastic restore FILE (pure file creation, no BLE in GroupTrack's code); Meshtastic's own "restore config" applies it. Confirm the backup/restore format + Apple acceptance at build time.
  Presentation ~90% shared because it's already web (Leaflet in a WebView). SwiftUI rejected for presentation — it doesn't port to a browser + gives zero reuse of the Android web layer. iPad presentation = the existing web layer in a WKWebView behind a native Swift shell; PC = the same web (planning half) in a browser; Android = the same web unchanged. Swift's only job = the native shell (mesh source + WebView host + JS↔native bridge, the WKScriptMessageHandler analog of Android's JavascriptInterface).
  Real cost driver = the bridge/I/O surface. What renders inside the WebView ports cleanly; every point where the web reaches out to the device (file I/O, GPS, radio/mesh, camera, share, persistence, offline-tile reads, native dialogs) is a bridge call re-implemented per platform, many with no browser equivalent (why PC is planning-only). Next action: enumerate that surface from the Android code (every JavascriptInterface method + evaluateJavascript/postMessage crossing) — = the true iPad build cost AND which functions can/can't go to PC.
  Three surfaces split on connectivity: PC = planning-only web app (routes/waypoints/library + config-file generation; no mesh/radio; online); Android + iPad = off-grid native convoy execution (BLE/radio/live mesh — convoy cannot be web). The A/B decision touches only the mobile mesh source; PC proceeds independently.
  Two candidate iPad-execution patterns (open): (A) BRIDGE — convoy is its own native iOS app consuming mesh over a local loopback port from the separate Meshtastic app (less code; adds a runtime dependency + iOS-lifecycle fragility — the neighbor app must stay foregrounded, a real mark against A for an off-grid safety app); (B) FORK — import Meshtastic's BLE/mesh and extend, exactly as on Android (more work; no runtime dependency; Android-sameness). Not decided; off-grid reliability leans B.
  Target end-state: a messaging/logic SERVICE LAYER + logic-free presentation panels (panels call the service for everything). Serving all three platforms = the logic rewritten ONCE into one platform-independent implementation, not three copies. Current code isn't built this way (logic woven into the Android fork) → a one-time extraction = the same effort as the bridge-surface inventory seen from the other end.
  KMP is the natural target: logic is already Kotlin; KMP migration is incremental (share networking/data/domain first; expect/actual IS the "configured API resolves per platform" idea). KMP produces a shared logic module a Swift UI/shell consumes (it does NOT fork Meshtastic-Apple — that's Swift). Readiness gauge: (1) mechanical — KMP plugin preflight + Qodana; (2) architectural — a logic-entanglement inventory vs where_used/function_universe xref (the real effort predictor).
Sequencing (firm) + next-session deliverables STRATEGY
  Ship V2.6 on Windows (cleanup + map-download rewrite).
  Set up the Mac Air and build/run known-good V2.6 on it FIRST — prove the environment with a known-good artifact before piling on KMP.
  Then KMP plugin preflight + the entanglement inventory vs xref.
  Then incremental KMP extraction (share domain/logic first).
  Then iPad.
Rule: do NOT introduce KMP onto an unproven Mac — one unknown at a time (else a break is ambiguous between KMP and Mac setup). Building V2.6 on Mac is the first rung needed anyway (same env for preflight + eventual Xcode).
Deliverable 1 — Mac environment build-out: inventory required tools + install-and-confirm one at a time (Git + Terminal/zsh — macOS is real Unix, the Git-Bash/CRLF-heredoc pain may relax; Android Studio + SDK + Gradle + JDK/JavaVM; Python; keystore access — grouptrack-release-key.jks is in iCloud; clone + build V2.6; THEN the KMP plugin; MySQL — purpose TBD; Xcode + Apple Developer enrollment — later rung, iPad only). Deliverable 2 — consolidated cross-domain tooling/stack inventory (PC/local dev, Data/MySQL, AWS/V3.0 backend, Google Play, runtimes) — assemble + confirm from the actual environment + docs, not memory. Feeds the shared-layer language decision.
iPad open items
  iPad mesh source: A (bridge/port-listener) vs B (fork Meshtastic-Apple).
  Service layer: local-on-device vs network vs both.
  Shared-layer language/runtime (Kotlin/KMP leading, since logic is already Kotlin).

iPad EVOLUTION — how the thinking got here (the 4 prior positions) HISTORY
The iPad plan evolved four times before 07-04 reconciled it. Kept so the ground isn't re-walked:
  (1) Roadmap V9 (Mar 25): native-port via external dev.

⭐ TILE STORAGE — unified process (ITEM A Pass 1 + ITEM B Pass 2) DESIGNNEXT
Design converged 07-06. This is the full design, written in.
The unified process (one spine, many origins, many destinations)
ORIGIN → NORMALIZE → EXPAND → CHOP → FETCH → [RETURN POINT] → WRITE → DESTINATION, pluggable at both ends.
  ORIGIN → (bbox, source-set) — the only place origins differ.
  NORMALIZE → (bbox, [sources]) — origins collapse to one canonical request; downstream is origin-blind.
  EXPAND → layers — each source → its layers via the source def (SAT → base + 2 overlays). "One SAT request → 3 destinations" happens here.
  CHOP → queue items — bbox → bounded cells; (layer, cell) = one queue item.
  FETCH → tiles — the ONE place the "miracle" varies: HTML per-tile, or batch export+unbundle, chosen per-layer by whether it has a batch process.
  RETURN POINT → uniform (type, z, x, y, bytes) stream — both transports emit this.
  WRITE → destination — the write contract resolves type → its .mbtiles and inserts.
Two fan points: fan-in at front (many origins → one canonical request); fan-out at back (one request → EXPAND layers → CHOP cells → many tiles → many DBs). Three extension points: add an origin = step 1 only; add a transport = step 5 miracle only; add a destination (new layer/type) = free.
MBTiles-only hard cutover (the decision)
Dual-path loose+MBTiles DROPPED — no state-file mode switch, no read/write fork, no Step-0 state-resolver. The ~5 map-invested testers re-download once. Storage format changes; HTML fetch survives. This supersedes the earlier "Steps 0 state-resolver → 1 write-fork → 2 read-fork → 3 batch-fetch" plan and the dual-path coexistence. GPX/track DBs stay separate. Worst case to design for: a tester at 80–90 GB of tiles (loose-file model = millions of files = the bloat/brick/slow-delete root cause).
Two-pass build
  Pass 1 — move current transport to spatial-DB storage. HTML fetch unchanged; only the WRITE changes (loose files → MBTiles). Covers all origins + all readers. MapView unchanged. = the V2.6 tile work + the "simplify" goal.
  Pass 2 — add a batch transport capability. New FETCH miracle built ALONGSIDE, gated off (layer.batch?.process), Esri first, provider-agnostic. Never touches Pass 1's storage — just a new way to feed the same write. Build-alongside-and-gate.
Write contract + the two "miracles"
Intercept at the RETURN POINT; everything above it is untouched. Two producers emit (type,z,x,y,bytes) into ONE shared write contract (MBTilesStore.insertTile + TileCodec + type→file resolve + y-flip):
  Miracle #1 (Pass 1): per-tile HTML write, redirected &lt;cache_dir&gt;/z/x/y.png → &lt;cache_dir&gt;.mbtiles.
  Miracle #2 (Pass 2): batch .tpkx → unbundle → same stream → same DBs.
The contract is producer-blind — that's why Pass 2 reuses Pass 1's write. Open: single insertTile vs transaction-batched insertTiles (faster for batch bulk); Miracle #2 streaming per-bundle vs collect-whole-package.
Schema — one MBTiles per TYPE (resolved 4 ways)
One MBTiles file per TYPE (= cache_dir = old directory name). No type column; base/overlay declared in each file's metadata; compositing at the Leaflet layer, not in storage. Confirmed by: (1) the render stacks separate per-type layers (we're not rewriting MapView); (2) the MBTiles spec mandates one tileset per file; (3) Esri best practice = base+reference separation; (4) Esri delivers per-service.
Canonical: tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row, tile_data) + metadata(name, value) + MANDATORY CREATE UNIQUE INDEX tile_index ON tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row). WebP yes; NEVER JPEG for overlays (kills alpha). FLAT vs NORMALIZED per type. PMTiles REJECTED (immutable — GroupTrack patches incrementally). TMS y-flip to settle.
DB naming = old directory names: cache_dir = type = old folder = convoy://tiles/&lt;type&gt;/… URL segment = .mbtiles filename. Migration: cache_dir folder → cache_dir.mbtiles. ⚠ TOPO+ has a + — verify it round-trips through the convoy:// URL + path open. Droid 2 has 5 type folders today: SAT, SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT, SAT_LABELS_PLACES, TOPO, TOPO+.
All download origins through the SAME area submission (audit + blast radius)
The unified process only holds if every origin funnels through the one area submission. Test per origin: does it end at the area submission with (bbox, sources), or bypass it (a second engine)?
  AREA — user-drawn bbox + selectable sources = the canonical engine.
  TRACK — bbox derived by padding the track's lat/long extents ½ mile + preference-sourced set → routes through area submission.
  ROUTE — "dupes track": same adapter shape (pad route extents → resolve sources from preference → area). Confirm it shares track's path.
  IMPORTED ARTIFACTS — an imported task WRITES A NEW ARTIFACT; the download panel has a "yes" import-maps toggle; if yes → the FIT PROCESS requests a map download for this track, right after track creation. So it is NOT a separate engine — it triggers a track-style download via the fit process → converges through track.
Prove the list exhaustive with a grep — enumerate every caller of the queue submission + every path reaching ConvoyTileDownloader/ConvoyDownloadWorker; classify each as canonical / adapter / rogue-bypass. May be unnamed origins — from code, not memory. Build a blast-radius process inventory (every process touching tile download/write + what it does) from the xref docs + code so a change doesn't underestimate what it breaks.
Source-set policy per origin: area = selectable; track/route = preference-default; artifacts = via track (likely track's preference).
Front-end standardization — WHY (inherit the large-bbox splitting)
Make each non-area origin a pure origin adapter — produce (bbox, source-set) and submit through the same area submission.
Primary reason: inherit the area process's large-bbox splitting. The area submission already chops a big bbox into bounded queue items (gridCells/tileBoundsLatLon) — real, tested. Track/route/artifacts on their own paths duplicate or lack it. Routing their bbox through the same submission → they inherit splitting for free. Triple duty: (i) splits big areas today; (ii) splits track/route/artifact downloads once standardized; (iii) sizes batch export jobs in Pass 2 (one split item = one Esri job under the 100k cap).
Other reasons: origins gain source control (fixed → selectable); convergence happens before the return point by construction → Pass 1's write-redirect is provably one seam. Confirm: does the area submission cleanly take (bbox, sources), or is it entangled with the drawing UI? If entangled, extract a pure (bbox, sources) → submit core first.
The ONE undefined region — the "miracle-happens" process (destination end)
Everything upstream is defined. The only open design work is the RETURN POINT → WRITE internals of MBTilesStore. It may already be a black box — before designing from scratch, find the existing tile-landing component and verify its internals against memory; reuse if it matches, design only the delta.
  (1) How many databases — dynamic: one MBTiles per type; count = however many distinct types across active sources (5 today). Open: who computes the DB set + when (up front from source defs vs lazy)? Rules-engine candidate.
  (2) How they're created — lifecycle: lazy create-if-absent on first insertTile, or provision up front? Creation writes canonical tiles + metadata + the mandatory tile_index, with metadata (name, base/overlay, format, bounds) at creation.
  (3) How overlays are linked — the base↔overlay relationship does NOT live in the tile DBs (each standalone, just tiles). It lives in the source definition (layers[] with role + render_order); MapView reads it at render to stack the right overlay DBs; each DB's metadata self-declares base-vs-overlay. Open: confirm nothing else needs the link (coverage? delete cascade?). Rules-engine candidate.
Pass 2 — batch transport (Esri) full design
  Core: the unit of variation is the provider's PROCESS, not just a key. Invoke the provider's own download+unbundle; one handler per provider protocol, reused across all its sources; the source def names the process + supplies parameters. One EsriExportTilesProcess serves all Esri sources.
  Schema: per-layer batch block — { "process":"esri_export_tiles", "export_endpoint":"&lt;MapServer&gt;/exportTiles", "package_format":"tpkx", "requires_key":true, "api_key_param":"token", "max_tiles_per_job":100000 }. process = dispatch key. No block → HTML per-tile.
  Request (async): POST exportTiles?f=json&amp;tilePackage=true&amp;exportBy=levelId&amp;levels={min-max}&amp;areaOfInterest={AOI wkid 4326}&amp;token={key} → jobId → poll /jobs/{jobId} until esriJobSucceeded → GET result → .tpkx.
  CompactV2 unpack (spec fully known): .tpkx = ZIP → root.json + iteminfo + thumbnail + tile/ of .bundle files. Each .bundle = 128×128 tile block: 64-byte header at offset 0 (LE) → tile index at byte 64 = 128×128 array of 8-byte records. TileIndexOffset = 64 + 8*(128*(row%128) + (col%128)). Each record: offset = bits 0–39, size = bits 40–63 → seek + read size bytes = raw tile. Absolute (row,col) = bundle base (from .bundle filename e.g. R0000C0000) + in-bundle row/col. Skip size-0. Port from Esri raster-tiles-compactcache (Vundler.py) / @syncpoint/compact-cache-bundle; GDAL 3.8+ ESRIC driver = cross-check oracle. .vtpk shares the same bundle format (vector pbf) → a future vector handler reuses the walk.
  SAT reassembly: exportTiles is per-service → 3 SAT services = 3 separate .tpkx, same unpack loop, only the destination DB differs (SAT / SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES). Separate, not combined.
  API key: reuse api_keys.json + getApiKey; inject ?token=&lt;key&gt;; never in source JSON, never logged; decrypt at call-time. Uses Fred's Esri Location Platform account (needs a token — the public tile endpoint doesn't).
  De-risk first: curl the exportTiles POST→poll→download flow against a real endpoint from Git Bash BEFORE any Kotlin. Confirm exportTiles is enabled on the public arcgisonline.com services.
Tile action plan (ordered Step 0 → 6)
  Step 0: verify the area download submission is the black box; origin audit + blast-radius inventory; scope the DB rules engine; pin down the fit process; standardize each non-area origin onto the area submission with a source preference (default = today's behavior).
  Step 0.5: resolve the miracle-happens design (find the existing black box + verify; settle DB-set enumeration, creation lifecycle, overlay linkage).
  Step 1 (Pass 1): read code bodies — ConvoyTileDownloader, ConvoyDownloadWorker, ConvoyDownloadQueue; both shouldInterceptRequest (CS 720-748, MVS 578+); overlay JS in convoy_map.html / grouptrack_map.html; show-downloaded/show-queued + MVS:658; how the codebase opens SQLite (SpatialDbManager) + the DB rules engine.

  Step 3 (Pass 1): write MBTilesStore + TileCodec.toWebp, reusing the rules engine + SpatialDbManager. Settle y-flip, WebP content-type, schema variant, insertTile vs txn insertTiles, TOPO+ +.
