Design converged 07-06. This is the full design, written in.
The unified process (one spine, many origins, many destinations)
ORIGIN → NORMALIZE → EXPAND → CHOP → FETCH → [RETURN POINT] → WRITE → DESTINATION, pluggable at both ends.
  ORIGIN → (bbox, source-set) — the only place origins differ.
  NORMALIZE → (bbox, [sources]) — origins collapse to one canonical request; downstream is origin-blind.
  EXPAND → layers — each source → its layers via the source def (SAT → base + 2 overlays). "One SAT request → 3 destinations" happens here.
  CHOP → queue items — bbox → bounded cells; (layer, cell) = one queue item.
  FETCH → tiles — the ONE place the "miracle" varies: HTML per-tile, or batch export+unbundle, chosen per-layer by whether it has a batch process.
  RETURN POINT → uniform (type, z, x, y, bytes) stream — both transports emit this.
  WRITE → destination — the write contract resolves type → its .mbtiles and inserts.
Two fan points: fan-in at front (many origins → one canonical request); fan-out at back (one request → EXPAND layers → CHOP cells → many tiles → many DBs). Three extension points: add an origin = step 1 only; add a transport = step 5 miracle only; add a destination (new layer/type) = free.
MBTiles-only hard cutover (the decision)
Dual-path loose+MBTiles DROPPED — no state-file mode switch, no read/write fork, no Step-0 state-resolver. The ~5 map-invested testers re-download once. Storage format changes; HTML fetch survives. This supersedes the earlier "Steps 0 state-resolver → 1 write-fork → 2 read-fork → 3 batch-fetch" plan and the dual-path coexistence. GPX/track DBs stay separate. Worst case to design for: a tester at 80–90 GB of tiles (loose-file model = millions of files = the bloat/brick/slow-delete root cause).
Two-pass build
  Pass 1 — move current transport to spatial-DB storage. HTML fetch unchanged; only the WRITE changes (loose files → MBTiles). Covers all origins + all readers. MapView unchanged. = the V2.6 tile work + the "simplify" goal.
  Pass 2 — add a batch transport capability. New FETCH miracle built ALONGSIDE, gated off (layer.batch?.process), Esri first, provider-agnostic. Never touches Pass 1's storage — just a new way to feed the same write. Build-alongside-and-gate.
Write contract + the two "miracles"
Intercept at the RETURN POINT; everything above it is untouched. Two producers emit (type,z,x,y,bytes) into ONE shared write contract (MBTilesStore.insertTile + TileCodec + type→file resolve + y-flip):
  Miracle #1 (Pass 1): per-tile HTML write, redirected &lt;cache_dir&gt;/z/x/y.png → &lt;cache_dir&gt;.mbtiles.
  Miracle #2 (Pass 2): batch .tpkx → unbundle → same stream → same DBs.
The contract is producer-blind — that's why Pass 2 reuses Pass 1's write. Open: single insertTile vs transaction-batched insertTiles (faster for batch bulk); Miracle #2 streaming per-bundle vs collect-whole-package.
Schema — one MBTiles per TYPE (resolved 4 ways)
One MBTiles file per TYPE (= cache_dir = old directory name). No type column; base/overlay declared in each file's metadata; compositing at the Leaflet layer, not in storage. Confirmed by: (1) the render stacks separate per-type layers (we're not rewriting MapView); (2) the MBTiles spec mandates one tileset per file; (3) Esri best practice = base+reference separation; (4) Esri delivers per-service.
Canonical: tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row, tile_data) + metadata(name, value) + MANDATORY CREATE UNIQUE INDEX tile_index ON tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row). WebP yes; NEVER JPEG for overlays (kills alpha). FLAT vs NORMALIZED per type. PMTiles REJECTED (immutable — GroupTrack patches incrementally). TMS y-flip to settle.
DB naming = old directory names: cache_dir = type = old folder = convoy://tiles/&lt;type&gt;/… URL segment = .mbtiles filename. Migration: cache_dir folder → cache_dir.mbtiles. ⚠ TOPO+ has a + — verify it round-trips through the convoy:// URL + path open. Droid 2 has 5 type folders today: SAT, SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT, SAT_LABELS_PLACES, TOPO, TOPO+.
All download origins through the SAME area submission (audit + blast radius)
The unified process only holds if every origin funnels through the one area submission. Test per origin: does it end at the area submission with (bbox, sources), or bypass it (a second engine)?
  AREA — user-drawn bbox + selectable sources = the canonical engine.
  TRACK — bbox derived by padding the track's lat/long extents ½ mile + preference-sourced set → routes through area submission.
  ROUTE — "dupes track": same adapter shape (pad route extents → resolve sources from preference → area). Confirm it shares track's path.
  IMPORTED ARTIFACTS — an imported task WRITES A NEW ARTIFACT; the download panel has a "yes" import-maps toggle; if yes → the FIT PROCESS requests a map download for this track, right after track creation. So it is NOT a separate engine — it triggers a track-style download via the fit process → converges through track.
Prove the list exhaustive with a grep — enumerate every caller of the queue submission + every path reaching ConvoyTileDownloader/ConvoyDownloadWorker; classify each as canonical / adapter / rogue-bypass. May be unnamed origins — from code, not memory. Build a blast-radius process inventory (every process touching tile download/write + what it does) from the xref docs + code so a change doesn't underestimate what it breaks.
Source-set policy per origin: area = selectable; track/route = preference-default; artifacts = via track (likely track's preference).
Front-end standardization — WHY (inherit the large-bbox splitting)
Make each non-area origin a pure origin adapter — produce (bbox, source-set) and submit through the same area submission.
Primary reason: inherit the area process's large-bbox splitting. The area submission already chops a big bbox into bounded queue items (gridCells/tileBoundsLatLon) — real, tested. Track/route/artifacts on their own paths duplicate or lack it. Routing their bbox through the same submission → they inherit splitting for free. Triple duty: (i) splits big areas today; (ii) splits track/route/artifact downloads once standardized; (iii) sizes batch export jobs in Pass 2 (one split item = one Esri job under the 100k cap).
Other reasons: origins gain source control (fixed → selectable); convergence happens before the return point by construction → Pass 1's write-redirect is provably one seam. Confirm: does the area submission cleanly take (bbox, sources), or is it entangled with the drawing UI? If entangled, extract a pure (bbox, sources) → submit core first.
The ONE undefined region — the "miracle-happens" process (destination end)
Everything upstream is defined. The only open design work is the RETURN POINT → WRITE internals of MBTilesStore. It may already be a black box — before designing from scratch, find the existing tile-landing component and verify its internals against memory; reuse if it matches, design only the delta.
  (1) How many databases — dynamic: one MBTiles per type; count = however many distinct types across active sources (5 today). Open: who computes the DB set + when (up front from source defs vs lazy)? Rules-engine candidate.
  (2) How they're created — lifecycle: lazy create-if-absent on first insertTile, or provision up front? Creation writes canonical tiles + metadata + the mandatory tile_index, with metadata (name, base/overlay, format, bounds) at creation.
  (3) How overlays are linked — the base↔overlay relationship does NOT live in the tile DBs (each standalone, just tiles). It lives in the source definition (layers[] with role + render_order); MapView reads it at render to stack the right overlay DBs; each DB's metadata self-declares base-vs-overlay. Open: confirm nothing else needs the link (coverage? delete cascade?). Rules-engine candidate.
Pass 2 — batch transport (Esri) full design
  Core: the unit of variation is the provider's PROCESS, not just a key. Invoke the provider's own download+unbundle; one handler per provider protocol, reused across all its sources; the source def names the process + supplies parameters. One EsriExportTilesProcess serves all Esri sources.
  Schema: per-layer batch block — { "process":"esri_export_tiles", "export_endpoint":"&lt;MapServer&gt;/exportTiles", "package_format":"tpkx", "requires_key":true, "api_key_param":"token", "max_tiles_per_job":100000 }. process = dispatch key. No block → HTML per-tile.
  Request (async): POST exportTiles?f=json&amp;tilePackage=true&amp;exportBy=levelId&amp;levels={min-max}&amp;areaOfInterest={AOI wkid 4326}&amp;token={key} → jobId → poll /jobs/{jobId} until esriJobSucceeded → GET result → .tpkx.
  CompactV2 unpack (spec fully known): .tpkx = ZIP → root.json + iteminfo + thumbnail + tile/ of .bundle files. Each .bundle = 128×128 tile block: 64-byte header at offset 0 (LE) → tile index at byte 64 = 128×128 array of 8-byte records. TileIndexOffset = 64 + 8*(128*(row%128) + (col%128)). Each record: offset = bits 0–39, size = bits 40–63 → seek + read size bytes = raw tile. Absolute (row,col) = bundle base (from .bundle filename e.g. R0000C0000) + in-bundle row/col. Skip size-0. Port from Esri raster-tiles-compactcache (Vundler.py) / @syncpoint/compact-cache-bundle; GDAL 3.8+ ESRIC driver = cross-check oracle. .vtpk shares the same bundle format (vector pbf) → a future vector handler reuses the walk.
  SAT reassembly: exportTiles is per-service → 3 SAT services = 3 separate .tpkx, same unpack loop, only the destination DB differs (SAT / SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES). Separate, not combined.
  API key: reuse api_keys.json + getApiKey; inject ?token=&lt;key&gt;; never in source JSON, never logged; decrypt at call-time. Uses Fred's Esri Location Platform account (needs a token — the public tile endpoint doesn't).
  De-risk first: curl the exportTiles POST→poll→download flow against a real endpoint from Git Bash BEFORE any Kotlin. Confirm exportTiles is enabled on the public arcgisonline.com services.
Tile action plan (ordered Step 0 → 6)
  Step 0: verify the area download submission is the black box; origin audit + blast-radius inventory; scope the DB rules engine; pin down the fit process; standardize each non-area origin onto the area submission with a source preference (default = today's behavior).
  Step 0.5: resolve the miracle-happens design (find the existing black box + verify; settle DB-set enumeration, creation lifecycle, overlay linkage).
  Step 1 (Pass 1): read code bodies — ConvoyTileDownloader, ConvoyDownloadWorker, ConvoyDownloadQueue; both shouldInterceptRequest (CS 720-748, MVS 578+); overlay JS in convoy_map.html / grouptrack_map.html; show-downloaded/show-queued + MVS:658; how the codebase opens SQLite (SpatialDbManager) + the DB rules engine.
  Step 2 (Pass 1): scope-lock grep TILE_DIR/tilePath/File(...tiles → zero File(TILE_DIR,...) survivors.
  Step 3 (Pass 1): write MBTilesStore + TileCodec.toWebp, reusing the rules engine + SpatialDbManager. Settle y-flip, WebP content-type, schema variant, insertTile vs txn insertTiles, TOPO+ +.
  Step 4 (Pass 1): swap the return-point write to insertTile; route every tile-reference site through MBTilesStore; retire loose-file cleanup. Verify on Droid 1 (pull .mbtiles → SQLite → rows + index; render composite + coverage). Ship Pass 1.
  Step 5 (Pass 2): curl-de-risk the Esri flow from Git Bash before Kotlin.
  Step 6 (Pass 2): add the batch block; write EsriExportTilesProcess (port Vundler/compact-cache-bundle); reuse getApiKey; wire the layer.batch?.process dispatch gate closed; verify batch rows == HTML-path rows on Droid 1, then open the gate per-source.
On-device facts + Esri auth status
  Tiles at /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/maps (loose today). Droid 1 du -sh = 6.4 GB. ConvoyConfig.TILE_DIR = /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/maps/tiles/. MapSourceManager separates online (getOnlineUrl) vs offline (getLocalUrl) → online maps unaffected.
  ⚠ WebView/JS not fully observable → verify empirically on-device. grouptrack_map.html (Planning) does NOT route console.log to logcat → use a visible on-screen element.
  Delete benchmarks (07-05): loose maps delete slow across ALL paths (Termux, app deleteRecursively, privileged adb rm -rf on 6.4GB). Bottleneck = file count not privilege. X-plore ~6GB/hr. ⇒ MBTiles (one-file delete) is the only surgical+fast+in-app tester answer.

⭐ ROUTE-STATE PERSISTENCE &amp; TEARDOWN (this morning's issue) OPEN
Root cause located 07-06 via fresh xref (recommit docs; navigation_xref regenerated 07-06 11:32). Fix design not yet locked — one source-check remains.
Problem (observed)
The route nav box disappears; states don't change as they should. Route-planning state is not reliably persisted across navigation, nor reliably torn down on exit. Two repro triggers (with a route open): (a) open/touch another item; (b) close the artifacts panel. Two failure modes: (1) route disappears from the map entirely; (2) route stays drawn but goes dead/inert (geometry visible, controls gone/unresponsive).
Root cause (located from xref)
Route mode is held in var routeMode by remember { mutableStateOf(false) } — ephemeral Compose state — at TWO independent copies: ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:129 and ConvoyScreen.kt:197. Both drive ONE shared window.__routeMode in convoy_map.html. Teardown = ~8 scattered hardcoded calls per screen of setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(); (ConvoyMapViewerScreen 955/1044/1075/1112, arm-on 996/1020, resume 1154; ConvoyScreen 1608/1684/1716/1743, arm-on 1648/1671, resume 1775). No single teardown funnel.
This one fact explains both failure modes: touching another item / closing the panel recomposes or orphans the remember boolean → Kotlin routeMode resets/desyncs but JS gets NO matching setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(). Disappear = a path fired clearBuildLine / a redraw overlaid it. Stays-but-dead = Kotlin routeMode went false so controls detach, but JS still shows the line.
Intent — Fred's 3 requirements
  Persist route-planning state in the MAP JSON so nav away + back restores it (survives recomposition/nav, which remember does not).
  States unique per map — Planning (grouptrack_map.html) vs Convoy (convoy_map.html) must not collide on the shared JS flag; the two booleans need per-map identity.
  Every exit ends it — save, discard, navigate away, back, mode-switch, backgrounding, item-tap, panel-close — via ONE teardown funnel every exit routes through (replacing the ~8 scattered teardowns).
Key principle: persist unless/until closed by an exit method — persist across nav, never past an exit.
Touchpoints + remaining source-check before locking
Touchpoints: setRouteMode (JS, convoy_map.html) toggled from both screens; window.__routeMode gate if(window.__routeMode)return; at convoy_map.html:495 (BUG A popup suppression — must stay mode-scoped); RouteManager holds build logic (snap/addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices, buildWktAndBbox, insertRoute); JS build fns drawBuildLine/clearBuildLine/updateRoutes/showRoutes; onTrackTap at ConvoyMapViewerScreen:515, ConvoyScreen:645 &amp; 895.
07-08 FIX SPEC (Fred, hard rule): while Route+ is active the route screen persists through ANY other selection (?, hamburger, search, item, panel — anything); the only exit is an explicit close, which prompts save-or-discard. This subsumes the persistence issue — state can never be implicitly abandoned, so it can't be orphaned. Same prompt on BOTH exits (planning-exit + convoy-return). Next-session pickup.
Before locking: the xref indexes definitions + bridge calls, not full handler bodies. Read the actual .kt for the artifact-panel-close (onDismiss/onClose) handler + the onTrackTap bodies and CONFIRM they lack a setRouteMode(false) teardown call (the diagnosis predicts they do). Then design = persist route state to the map JSON (per-map keyed) + single teardown funnel every exit routes through. Lock only after the two-handler read confirms.
LEAD TRACK / TICK / MY-CART REWRITE (ITEM C — needs radio, LAST) SETTLED, NOT STARTED
Spec: GroupTrack_LeadCart_TrackRevision_DemolitionRebuild_2026-06-18.md (authority: LeadTrackReplacement_Spec.docx May 31). Problem: lead broadcasts position over radio; code reconstructs path + fills gaps with projection → phantom carts on rebroadcast (worst on switchbacks); three parallel track-drawing flows compete.
Demolition (part 1)
Find via fresh xref + dual-language grep + 2-cart field capture, then remove: the 3 parallel LIVE-track flows leadTrackSegments/gpsTrailSegments/routeTrailSegments + trackLeadOnly (~ConvoyScreen 345-350); live drawTrack(...); the lead-lock engine in ConvoyEngine (evaluateLeadLock, tick()→compute()→assignLeadTail(), lockedLeadNodeId, _leadLockedFlag — retire tick-oscillation: two tick entries/cycle ~170ms apart); all projection/proxy substitution (phantom source); per-node live segment-coloring. Do NOT touch: displayed/imported DB tracks (loadTracks/trackLayer), node markers, route lines, route-builder snap-2.
Rebuild (part 2) + rates + new reqs
(1) track ONLY the lead cart from broadcasts; (2) snap-2 100-yd radius onto known trail geometry; (3) every other cart = present-position marker only, NOT tracked (kills phantom at root); (4) each cart records own GPS and as it overtakes the lead's positions REPLACES the lead's path on its own map with own GPS. Net = one continuous trail improving in accuracy toward the rear.
Rates (supersede spec): lead broadcast ~4s (spec 5s); self-record 2s change-gated (spec 1s). Don't fake smoothness with projection. New reqs: remove "track all carts" toggle; lead cart picked from a list unless only 1 displayed (auto-lead); reassignable in cart HUD; lead segment (new pushTrackToMap, 0 refs = single draw/update entry) gets configurable color + weight. Open: overtake overwrite unconditional vs snap-gated (coarse lead data argues snap-gated) — confirm vs May-31 spec. Related: two concurrent ConvoyViewModel instances; cart-identity bug (startGroupTrack stores "!phone").
Recorder items (needs radio, ITEM C cluster) OPEN
  2s change-gated sampling (supersedes 1s) — tick 2s; write a GPX point ONLY if moved beyond a threshold (a few meters / snap-2 min — not any-delta, else stationary jitter writes noise). Why not 1s: no snap coverage like onX; onX ~3s. Pairs with Doppler max-speed. ConvoyGpsService interval. Helps only NEW tracks.
  Capture + store max speed during recording, write on save (Doppler each update, track max live). Recorded not derived → glitch gone.
  Android-GPS recording bug (Android-only fails; radio-create certified 06-30). ConvoyGpsService.kt (CRLF): startLocationUpdates (~251-277 prime suspect), onGpsUpdate (~288). Instrument first. + recorder truncation (no &lt;/trk&gt; on interrupt — record-stop must finalize the file).
Other V2.6 backlog (no-radio) OPEN
  ⚠ MAPS checkbox ignored when track already exists — fires only in the INSERT branch; move the maps call out of AddOutcome.INSERT -&gt; and gate on the checkbox for any non-error outcome.
  ⚠ CLEAR-AREA / DELETE-AREA for downloads — NEVER WIRED (add to 2.6). The per-area tile clear was deliberately left unwritten during the area-download build because the MBTiles cutover was pending (didn't want to write it against loose-file storage about to be replaced). Now that Pass 1 shipped, it's a real gap: no clean way to clear a specific area's tiles before re-downloading (replace flow), and no surgical clear for testing. Scope = bbox-surgical delete of tiles within the drawn area from the relevant .mbtiles (tied to the "replace" toggle in ConvoyDownloadConfirm), NOT whole-source drop. MUST respect the handle-hygiene hardening (close/reopen the cached SQLite handle cleanly — don't corrupt the DB / trigger the FUSE wedge). [scope to confirm: bbox-surgical vs whole-source]
  ⚠ UNEVEN QUEUE SEGMENT SIZES waste the concurrency (perf, new 07-09). SAT submits as TWO jobs — one ~60,000 tiles (starts at z18), one ~11,000 — wildly unequal. With MAX_CONCURRENT=2 the 11K finishes fast, then that slot idles / picks up TOPO while the 60K monster runs ~alone → parallelism collapses toward 1× for the long tail. Partly explains the 80 min, AND why raising MAX_CONCURRENT may not help much: an indivisible 60K job hogs one slot the whole download; more slots can't subdivide it. SEGMENTATION METHOD (Fred, 07-09 FINAL). Divide the area bbox into EQUAL AREAS sized so NO area exceeds 50,000 SAT tiles. SAT is the sizing driver (densest source — goes to z18); size the grid to keep SAT ≤50K/cell and every other source (shallower zoom, fewer tiles) is automatically well under 50K in the same cell. So: estimate SAT tiles for the bbox → divide into ceil(SAT_total / 50000) equal areas → ONE uniform grid, computed against SAT only, applied to ALL sources. The grid is UNIFORM (plain equal-area cells); applied to each source's tiles it yields even batches per segment. LOAD BALANCING = process segments sharing the SAME ZOOM VALUES FROM THE SAME SOURCE SEQUENTIALLY (queue homogeneous work → comparable batches → even flow); evenness is a PROCESSING-ORDER property (group like-with-like), not per-source count juggling. ⚠ LOAD-BALANCE PRINCIPLE (the why): each segment MUST be a COMPLETE VERTICAL SLICE OF THE ZOOM STACK (z-min..z-max) for its geographic cell — NOT segmented by zoom. Segmenting by zoom recreates the imbalance (z18-only = the 45K heavy monster; z10-16 = trivial). Full-stack-per-cell gives every segment the SAME SHAPE of work (its share of heavy z18 + light upper layers), so equal-area segments do equal work and finish together in parallel slots — that comparability IS the load balancing. Unit = a vertical column (full zoom) over a horizontal cell, sized so SAT full-stack ≤50K. NOTE the heavy part is z18: tiles there carry more DATA (imagery), so processing accelerates as it climbs past z18 — data-per-tile drives speed, not tile count; splitting the cell halves the heavy-z18 load per slot. Only SAT needs estimating (worst case); others ride the same grid under the ceiling. Slight overlap (~tile-width) prevents seam gaps; hasTile dedupes. Prerequisite for higher MAX_CONCURRENT to pay off; likely a bigger lever than raising it.
  ⚠ SAT OVERLAY DISPLAYING ON TOPO / TOPO+ (new 07-09). The SAT overlay tiles (labels / transportation — likely SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES) are rendering on top of the TOPO and TOPO+ base maps where they should not appear. Layer-compositing bug: the overlay isn't cleared/swapped when the active base map changes (SAT→TOPO), or overlays render regardless of the active base. Confirmed: ALWAYS ON, BOTH overlays (labels SAT_LABELS_PLACES + transportation SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT) — not intermittent, not download-dependent. "Always on, both" ⇒ overlays are unconditionally added and NOT gated on the active base; the fix is a "show these overlays only when base == SAT" condition in the Leaflet layer-stack logic (map HTML) / how MapSourceManager associates overlays with a base — not a swap-timing race. Add to 2.6.
  Tile download SPEED-UP (2.6b, 07-09) — concurrency + zoom-cap + 429 backoff. Parallelized the sequential tile-fetch loop in ConvoyTileDownloader.downloadTiles (fetch 8 concurrently via TILE_FETCH_CONCURRENCY, insert serially — single cached SQLite handle unsafe for concurrent writes). Removed the stale per-source download zoom cap in ConvoyTileCalculator.maxZoomForSource (TOPO+/TRAIL→17 was for the old hand-drawn source; now full range; JSON max_zoom retained as a display clamp). Added 429/503 backoff in fetchTileBytes (retry SAME tile, exponential, honors Retry-After; 404 fast-null) so concurrency can't silently drop tiles under throttling. Reason: current download speed is an adoption obstacle. Built + applied 07-09; testing on Droid 1. 125K-tile test (SAT+TOPO+TOPO+) = 80 min, ~100% success, ZERO 429s, 2 transient 502s [⭐ RECONCILED RESULT: 2 queues vs 3 queues, cause = segment balance. The 80-min run (2 queues) was balanced ONLY BY COINCIDENCE — the big SAT segment happened to have ~equal tiles to ALL other jobs combined, so a 2-slot split fell ~50/50 by luck. With 3 QUEUES that broke: the 3rd slot subdivided the "everything else" half, small jobs drained at ~45 min, and the big SAT job ran ALONE for the tail → ~113 min (92% at 104 min). So current balance is ACCIDENTAL/FRAGILE (holds only because big-segment ≈ sum-of-rest at 2 slots); changing concurrency/area/tile-mix breaks it. EVEN SEGMENTATION replaces luck with guarantee — equal ≤50K-SAT segments hold balance regardless of slot count or area shape. Keep concurrency modest (~2); segmentation is the fix. OPEN EXPERIMENT (post-segmentation): once segments are balanced, run the same area at MAX_CONCURRENT=2 then =3 to isolate concurrency (today's =3 was confounded by imbalance). If 3≈2 → resource-SATURATED, keep 2, SKIP the tuning rig; if 3&lt;2 → spare capacity, build the rig and tune up. Segmentation first (removes the confound), then this clean test. Fred's hypothesis — test as a GRID: the two multiplying levers are queues(MAX_CONCURRENT) × async(TILE_FETCH_CONCURRENCY); at the SAME total (e.g. 24), FEWER queues × MORE async each may WIN — 2×12 could beat 3×8 — because same request rate but parallelism concentrated as async-within-fewer-jobs avoids stranding, feeds the critical path directly, and wastes fewer slots on early-draining small jobs. Test {2,3 queues}×{8,12 async}, measure time + collisions. Rig should make BOTH knobs tunable.] (dropped — 502 not yet in retry set).
  TILE-DOWNLOAD TUNING RIG (planned, next session) — manual tuning, NOT auto-throttle. Decided against an adaptive feedback controller (overkill). Four pieces: (1) add 502 to the retryable set in fetchTileBytes (currently 429/503 only — the 2 dropped tiles were 502 transient server strain); (2) make MAX_CONCURRENT (job-level, ConvoyDownloadQueue) read from JSON so it's tunable without a rebuild — but clamped to ±1 change per cycle (no jumping 2→8): read JSON target, compare to a PERSISTED last-effective value, step ≤1 toward target, use + persist it. Change is SETTABLE in the queue manager and takes effect on the NEXT set of submits/releases — CANNOT change while jobs are running (new value is staged, applied at the next launch when the queue is idle; running jobs finish under their start value). So a "cycle" = a fresh set of submits/releases (queue idle→launching a new batch), not per-app-launch. (3) break out error counts by code in the Complete: … downloaded=X failed=Y logcat line → failed=Y [429=a 502=b 503=c] for visibility while tuning (no UI); (4) publish a tuning GUIDELINE — error-rate thresholds + how to step concurrency (highest concurrency where error rate stays under threshold). Rationale: current 2×8=16 concurrent (jobs×tiles) gave 0 429s → headroom exists, but more concurrency risks more 502s, so tune manually against visible error counts. "Cycle" for the ±1 clamp = per app launch (simplest); persisted last-effective value is the one bit of new state.

V2.7 — iPad / CROSS-PLATFORM (post-V2.6 target)
Standing awareness — not an active task. iPad IS the post-V2.6 target (this overturns the old V3.0 "no iPad support" line). Reasoning arc reconciled 07-04. The evolution below is written in so it's never lost.
The reconciled strategy (07-04) STRATEGY
  Key collapse: Convoy is a fork of Meshtastic's messaging (Android = a fork of Meshtastic-Android, Kotlin). The native-vs-PWA-vs-WKWebView arc was all answering "how do we get BLE on iOS?" — a question that dissolves once convoy is seen as a fork of the mesh app. So iPad = a fork of Meshtastic-Apple (Swift/SwiftUI + BLE + protobuf; GPL v3; App-Store-approved; universal). Mac + Xcode = the prerequisite. Flag: Meshtastic-Apple ships native TAK/CoT — reconcile vs the roadmap's "TAK as pattern only."
  Config write is offloaded: the planning side CREATES a Meshtastic restore FILE (pure file creation, no BLE in GroupTrack's code); Meshtastic's own "restore config" applies it. Confirm the backup/restore format + Apple acceptance at build time.
  Presentation ~90% shared because it's already web (Leaflet in a WebView). SwiftUI rejected for presentation — it doesn't port to a browser + gives zero reuse of the Android web layer. iPad presentation = the existing web layer in a WKWebView behind a native Swift shell; PC = the same web (planning half) in a browser; Android = the same web unchanged. Swift's only job = the native shell (mesh source + WebView host + JS↔native bridge, the WKScriptMessageHandler analog of Android's JavascriptInterface).
  Real cost driver = the bridge/I/O surface. What renders inside the WebView ports cleanly; every point where the web reaches out to the device (file I/O, GPS, radio/mesh, camera, share, persistence, offline-tile reads, native dialogs) is a bridge call re-implemented per platform, many with no browser equivalent (why PC is planning-only). Next action: enumerate that surface from the Android code (every JavascriptInterface method + evaluateJavascript/postMessage crossing) — = the true iPad build cost AND which functions can/can't go to PC.
  Three surfaces split on connectivity: PC = planning-only web app (routes/waypoints/library + config-file generation; no mesh/radio; online); Android + iPad = off-grid native convoy execution (BLE/radio/live mesh — convoy cannot be web). The A/B decision touches only the mobile mesh source; PC proceeds independently.
  Two candidate iPad-execution patterns (open): (A) BRIDGE — convoy is its own native iOS app consuming mesh over a local loopback port from the separate Meshtastic app (less code; adds a runtime dependency + iOS-lifecycle fragility — the neighbor app must stay foregrounded, a real mark against A for an off-grid safety app); (B) FORK — import Meshtastic's BLE/mesh and extend, exactly as on Android (more work; no runtime dependency; Android-sameness). Not decided; off-grid reliability leans B.
  Target end-state: a messaging/logic SERVICE LAYER + logic-free presentation panels (panels call the service for everything). Serving all three platforms = the logic rewritten ONCE into one platform-independent implementation, not three copies. Current code isn't built this way (logic woven into the Android fork) → a one-time extraction = the same effort as the bridge-surface inventory seen from the other end.
  KMP is the natural target: logic is already Kotlin; KMP migration is incremental (share networking/data/domain first; expect/actual IS the "configured API resolves per platform" idea). KMP produces a shared logic module a Swift UI/shell consumes (it does NOT fork Meshtastic-Apple — that's Swift). Readiness gauge: (1) mechanical — KMP plugin preflight + Qodana; (2) architectural — a logic-entanglement inventory vs where_used/function_universe xref (the real effort predictor).
Sequencing (firm) + next-session deliverables STRATEGY

  Then KMP plugin preflight + the entanglement inventory vs xref.

Rule: do NOT introduce KMP onto an unproven Mac — one unknown at a time (else a break is ambiguous between KMP and Mac setup). Building V2.6 on Mac is the first rung needed anyway (same env for preflight + eventual Xcode).
Deliverable 1 — Mac environment build-out: inventory required tools + install-and-confirm one at a time (Git + Terminal/zsh — macOS is real Unix, the Git-Bash/CRLF-heredoc pain may relax; Android Studio + SDK + Gradle + JDK/JavaVM; Python; keystore access — grouptrack-release-key.jks is in iCloud; clone + build V2.6; THEN the KMP plugin; MySQL — purpose TBD; Xcode + Apple Developer enrollment — later rung, iPad only). iPad EVOLUTION — how the thinking got here (the 4 prior positions) HISTORY
The iPad plan evolved four times before 07-04 reconciled it. Kept so the ground isn't re-walked:
  (1) Roadmap V9 (Mar 25): native-port via external dev.
  (2) Mar-14 discussion doc — staged Options A–D: (A) fork Meshtastic-Apple in Swift/SwiftUI (rated HIGH, needs Swift skills); (B) React Native/Flutter (LOW — explicitly excluded); (C) WKWebView hybrid reusing convoy_map.html + minimal Swift BLE bridge (MEDIUM, ~2-3 wk); (D) use unmodified Meshtastic-Apple as a display-only viewer (HIGH for viewing, LOW for full convoy). Recommended: D short-term → C (V3) → A (V4). Also recommended MapLibre GL + PMTiles/OpenMapTiles for offline, replacing Leaflet.
  (3) May notes: PWA-via-Bluefy-then-Capacitor.
  (4) Repeatedly flagged "iPad V2.5 vs V3.0, not resolved."
What 07-04 overturned: MapLibre + PMTiles DROPPED (V2.6 tile design went MBTiles-only, PMTiles rejected as immutable, stayed on Leaflet not MapLibre). The A/B/C/D ladder collapsed — since presentation is already web, the WKWebView shell is the presentation host in BOTH remaining candidates, and the open decision narrowed to A (fork) vs a bridge/port-listener for the MESH SOURCE, not a 4-option choice; SwiftUI rejected for presentation. iPad moved from "V4, viewer-only short-term" to "the post-V2.6 target," sequenced through KMP + Mac-first. Several Mar-14 open questions now answered: tile area = ½mi-padded bbox (track) / drawn bbox (area); download at ride/track creation under the app's own entitlement; same architectural relationship as Android (fork). ATAK/CoT-as-pattern-only still holds (mesh replaces the server; protobuf replaces CoT-over-UDP).

⭐ ESRI TILE DOWNLOAD STRATEGY — 4-phase plan (planning session 2026-07-09) STRATEGY
Origin (07-09): the V2.6b batch transport plan (Esri exportTiles → .tpkx → unpack) was de-risked and found unavailable. Curl against the keyed Location Platform imagery service (ibasemaps-api.arcgis.com/.../World_Imagery/MapServer?f=json, HTTP 200 with the AAPT key) returns only tileInfo — no exportTilesAllowed. The keyed Location Platform endpoint is per-tile only; exportTiles lives on the separate tiledbasemaps.arcgis.com "for Export" instance (a different org/subscription entitlement). So the .tpkx batch plan is dead on the current account, and V2.6b pivots to tile-fetch concurrency on the free endpoint (speed-up, not a transport rewrite).
The cost reality. Esri Location Platform = 2,000,000 tiles/month free, then $0.15/1,000 flat (no volume tiers; high-volume only via Esri sales). Real GroupTrack usage: track download 200–300k tiles, area download ~500k tiles, heavy users ~100&nbsp;GB ≈ 10.8M tiles. A 100&nbsp;GB cache is a lifetime accumulation (≈900k/mo over a year, under the free tier) — but one-shot bulk on a metered key is financially impossible. Key honesty: the concurrency rewrite speeds downloads up, it does NOT reduce tile volume — on the free tier, faster just means faster accumulation (today's 100&nbsp;GB caches were built under the free tier). Demand-shaping via cost only works on a paid path.
The four phases:
  Phase 1 — NOW / BETA: free arcgisonline.com endpoint for everyone; the concurrency patch speeds it up at no cost and no licensing dependency. (This is the immediate V2.6b work.)
  Phase 2 — OPTIONAL PAID PERSONAL TIER: users who want the faster keyed endpoint and/or big pre-downloads foot their own bill via their own entitlement (BYO-key / ~$100 ArcGIS Personal-Use). Cost self-selects and self-limits. Note: a personal license is still PER-TILE — not the batch/redistribution product.
  Phase 3 — ENTITY ACCOUNT: past enough $100 personal accounts, it pays to shift to one ArcGIS org/enterprise account + shared key behind the backend proxy + negotiated volume pricing (also the central usage dashboard/billing + the 3.0 key-security model). Crossover economics unknown — depends on Esri's negotiated volume quote (the single deciding number; not published).
  Phase 4 — FULLY OPTIMIZED ENDGAME: download-once / serve-many with dedup across the whole user base. Riders cluster in the same popular areas, so each region is fetched from Esri once and amortized across everyone who rides there — cost stops scaling with users and scales only with unique geography (bounded, slow-growing). Also solves key security (key server-only) + speed (users pull from GroupTrack) + control (one cache/dashboard/bill).
Phase-4 distribution refinement — self-managed AREA PACKS (Fred, 07-09). Rather than run a live tile CDN, self-manage distribution: a batch process pulls/builds an area's .mbtiles once, hosts the finished file (FTP or file host / URL+catalog), and GroupTrack devices fetch + import the pre-built .mbtiles into MBTilesStore. Much lighter infra (a file server, not a mapping service) and fits the app's existing MBTiles-file world (store already reads .mbtiles; X-plore flow already moves tile files; import is close to Pass 1). Productized = "download this area pack" through the same download pipeline, pointed at pre-built packs instead of Esri tiles.
⚠ THE REDISTRIBUTION LICENSE GATE (unchanged by any refinement). Hosting/FTPing an .mbtiles full of Esri tiles is redistribution just as much as live proxy-serving — legally identical on the point that matters. Phases 3–4 require a caching/redistribution-permitted Esri license (the "for Export" / offline entitlement) or a redistributable source. Lighter infra does not lighten the license requirement. The batch build's source is the same fork: free arcgisonline (ToS-gray bulk, just centralized), licensed for-Export (clean, negotiated/pricier), or USGS/USFS/BLM/Sentinel public-domain imagery (free + freely re-hostable — the clean fallback if Esri won't license redistribution).
The one gate that decides Phase 3 &amp; 4: a single Esri sales conversation — entity/enterprise volume price + whether caching/redistribution is licensed and at what cost (not published, not web-searchable). Also confirm: does Personal-Use / BYO-key permit third-party-app use; Personal-Use is non-commercial (GroupTrack free now, commercial revenue model — revisit on monetization).
Immediate next (code, safe under ALL phases): apply + build + test the tile-concurrency patch on the free endpoint (fetch-parallel / insert-serial, batch = 8). Do the db()/insertTile silent-failure hardening alongside (matters more once fetches are parallel). Do NOT switch the default to the keyed/metered endpoint. Current download speed is an adoption obstacle — this is the priority.

✅ 07-11 SHIPPED — LOAD-BALANCING SEGMENTATION + 2x10 concurrency (commit e38e43487) DONE
Commit e38e43487 "V2.6 tile segmentation: SAT-sized load-balancing grid across all sources; 2x10 download concurrency" — 3 files, +92/-3. ⚠ NOT build-verified after the final dry-run-scaffolding strip (mechanical removal, should compile; self-verifies at tomorrow's first build).
What shipped: ConvoyTileDownloader.segmentCells(n,s,e,w, sizeTiles, segCeilingTiles=50_000, overlapTiles=3, zMax=DOWNLOAD_ZOOM) REPLACES fixed-12-mile gridCells as the AREA-download bbox splitter. Splits into max(1, ceil(sizeTiles/50_000)) equal degree-slices of the LONGER axis; each cell a full z10–z18 slice (never zoom-banded); same List&lt;DoubleArray&gt; shape so the enqueue loop is unchanged. Logs each cell + SPLIT under "SEGMENT".
Sizing (all sources ride SAT grid): sizeTiles = quickEstimate(bbox).tileCount × satLayers (SAT=3 layers); every slot sizes off SAT so SAT/TOPO/TOPO+ get the identical grid. Per-cell totalTiles still uses the current slot's slotLayers (separate, correct). Overlap: if(n&gt;1) 3×(360/2^zMax) ≈0.004° at z18, seam-only, deduped by hasTile().
⚠ HARD-LEARNED: overlap must be TILE-WIDTHS not degrees — ⅛° = ~91 tiles/edge ballooned a 24,716-tile area to 155,674 (6×) in the dry-run. Three bugs caught before ship by the dry-run JSON + live logging (Fred insisted on visibility): (1) ⅛° overlap 6× blowup; (2) sizing under-count — quickEstimate is ONE layer but SAT is 3; (3) per-source grid mismatch — SAT split 2, TOPO/TOPO+ split 1 until sized off SAT. Dry-run scaffolding stripped before commit; the SEGMENT logcat is the permanent validation tool.
Concurrency (same commit): MAX_CONCURRENT=2, TILE_FETCH_CONCURRENCY=10 (was 8). RESULT (on-device): "ran faster with two queues than three" — balance now STRUCTURAL not accidental. Open follow-up (not run): time 2×10 vs 2×8; if faster probe 2×12, if flat keep 8.

The unified process (one spine, many origins, many destinations)
ORIGIN → NORMALIZE → EXPAND → CHOP → FETCH → [RETURN POINT] → WRITE → DESTINATION, pluggable at both ends.
  ORIGIN → (bbox, source-set) — the only place origins differ.
  NORMALIZE → (bbox, [sources]) — origins collapse to one canonical request; downstream is origin-blind.
  EXPAND → layers — each source → its layers via the source def (SAT → base + 2 overlays). "One SAT request → 3 destinations" happens here.
  CHOP → queue items — bbox → bounded cells; (layer, cell) = one queue item.
  FETCH → tiles — the ONE place the "miracle" varies: HTML per-tile, or batch export+unbundle, chosen per-layer by whether it has a batch process.
  RETURN POINT → uniform (type, z, x, y, bytes) stream — both transports emit this.
  WRITE → destination — the write contract resolves type → its .mbtiles and inserts.
Two fan points: fan-in at front (many origins → one canonical request); fan-out at back (one request → EXPAND layers → CHOP cells → many tiles → many DBs). Three extension points: add an origin = step 1 only; add a transport = step 5 miracle only; add a destination (new layer/type) = free.
MBTiles-only hard cutover (the decision)
Dual-path loose+MBTiles DROPPED — no state-file mode switch, no read/write fork, no Step-0 state-resolver. The ~5 map-invested testers re-download once. Storage format changes; HTML fetch survives. This supersedes the earlier "Steps 0 state-resolver → 1 write-fork → 2 read-fork → 3 batch-fetch" plan and the dual-path coexistence. GPX/track DBs stay separate. Worst case to design for: a tester at 80–90 GB of tiles (loose-file model = millions of files = the bloat/brick/slow-delete root cause).
Two-pass build
  Pass 1 — move current transport to spatial-DB storage. HTML fetch unchanged; only the WRITE changes (loose files → MBTiles). Covers all origins + all readers. MapView unchanged. = the V2.6 tile work + the "simplify" goal.
  Pass 2 — add a batch transport capability. New FETCH miracle built ALONGSIDE, gated off (layer.batch?.process), Esri first, provider-agnostic. Never touches Pass 1's storage — just a new way to feed the same write. Build-alongside-and-gate.
Write contract + the two "miracles"
Intercept at the RETURN POINT; everything above it is untouched. Two producers emit (type,z,x,y,bytes) into ONE shared write contract (MBTilesStore.insertTile + TileCodec + type→file resolve + y-flip):
  Miracle #1 (Pass 1): per-tile HTML write, redirected &lt;cache_dir&gt;/z/x/y.png → &lt;cache_dir&gt;.mbtiles.
  Miracle #2 (Pass 2): batch .tpkx → unbundle → same stream → same DBs.
The contract is producer-blind — that's why Pass 2 reuses Pass 1's write. Open: single insertTile vs transaction-batched insertTiles (faster for batch bulk); Miracle #2 streaming per-bundle vs collect-whole-package.
Schema — one MBTiles per TYPE (resolved 4 ways)
One MBTiles file per TYPE (= cache_dir = old directory name). No type column; base/overlay declared in each file's metadata; compositing at the Leaflet layer, not in storage. Confirmed by: (1) the render stacks separate per-type layers (we're not rewriting MapView); (2) the MBTiles spec mandates one tileset per file; (3) Esri best practice = base+reference separation; (4) Esri delivers per-service.
Canonical: tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row, tile_data) + metadata(name, value) + MANDATORY CREATE UNIQUE INDEX tile_index ON tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row). WebP yes; NEVER JPEG for overlays (kills alpha). FLAT vs NORMALIZED per type. PMTiles REJECTED (immutable — GroupTrack patches incrementally). TMS y-flip to settle.
DB naming = old directory names: cache_dir = type = old folder = convoy://tiles/&lt;type&gt;/… URL segment = .mbtiles filename. Migration: cache_dir folder → cache_dir.mbtiles. ⚠ TOPO+ has a + — verify it round-trips through the convoy:// URL + path open. Droid 2 has 5 type folders today: SAT, SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT, SAT_LABELS_PLACES, TOPO, TOPO+.
All download origins through the SAME area submission (audit + blast radius)
The unified process only holds if every origin funnels through the one area submission. Test per origin: does it end at the area submission with (bbox, sources), or bypass it (a second engine)?
  AREA — user-drawn bbox + selectable sources = the canonical engine.
  TRACK — bbox derived by padding the track's lat/long extents ½ mile + preference-sourced set → routes through area submission.
  ROUTE — "dupes track": same adapter shape (pad route extents → resolve sources from preference → area). Confirm it shares track's path.
  IMPORTED ARTIFACTS — an imported task WRITES A NEW ARTIFACT; the download panel has a "yes" import-maps toggle; if yes → the FIT PROCESS requests a map download for this track, right after track creation. So it is NOT a separate engine — it triggers a track-style download via the fit process → converges through track.
Prove the list exhaustive with a grep — enumerate every caller of the queue submission + every path reaching ConvoyTileDownloader/ConvoyDownloadWorker; classify each as canonical / adapter / rogue-bypass. May be unnamed origins — from code, not memory. Build a blast-radius process inventory (every process touching tile download/write + what it does) from the xref docs + code so a change doesn't underestimate what it breaks.
Source-set policy per origin: area = selectable; track/route = preference-default; artifacts = via track (likely track's preference).
Front-end standardization — WHY (inherit the large-bbox splitting)
Make each non-area origin a pure origin adapter — produce (bbox, source-set) and submit through the same area submission.
Primary reason: inherit the area process's large-bbox splitting. The area submission already chops a big bbox into bounded queue items (gridCells/tileBoundsLatLon) — real, tested. Track/route/artifacts on their own paths duplicate or lack it. Routing their bbox through the same submission → they inherit splitting for free. Triple duty: (i) splits big areas today; (ii) splits track/route/artifact downloads once standardized; (iii) sizes batch export jobs in Pass 2 (one split item = one Esri job under the 100k cap).
Other reasons: origins gain source control (fixed → selectable); convergence happens before the return point by construction → Pass 1's write-redirect is provably one seam. Confirm: does the area submission cleanly take (bbox, sources), or is it entangled with the drawing UI? If entangled, extract a pure (bbox, sources) → submit core first.
The ONE undefined region — the "miracle-happens" process (destination end)
Everything upstream is defined. The only open design work is the RETURN POINT → WRITE internals of MBTilesStore. It may already be a black box — before designing from scratch, find the existing tile-landing component and verify its internals against memory; reuse if it matches, design only the delta.
  (1) How many databases — dynamic: one MBTiles per type; count = however many distinct types across active sources (5 today). Open: who computes the DB set + when (up front from source defs vs lazy)? Rules-engine candidate.
  (2) How they're created — lifecycle: lazy create-if-absent on first insertTile, or provision up front? Creation writes canonical tiles + metadata + the mandatory tile_index, with metadata (name, base/overlay, format, bounds) at creation.
  (3) How overlays are linked — the base↔overlay relationship does NOT live in the tile DBs (each standalone, just tiles). It lives in the source definition (layers[] with role + render_order); MapView reads it at render to stack the right overlay DBs; each DB's metadata self-declares base-vs-overlay. Open: confirm nothing else needs the link (coverage? delete cascade?). Rules-engine candidate.
Pass 2 — batch transport (Esri) full design
  Core: the unit of variation is the provider's PROCESS, not just a key. Invoke the provider's own download+unbundle; one handler per provider protocol, reused across all its sources; the source def names the process + supplies parameters. One EsriExportTilesProcess serves all Esri sources.
  Schema: per-layer batch block — { "process":"esri_export_tiles", "export_endpoint":"&lt;MapServer&gt;/exportTiles", "package_format":"tpkx", "requires_key":true, "api_key_param":"token", "max_tiles_per_job":100000 }. process = dispatch key. No block → HTML per-tile.
  Request (async): POST exportTiles?f=json&amp;tilePackage=true&amp;exportBy=levelId&amp;levels={min-max}&amp;areaOfInterest={AOI wkid 4326}&amp;token={key} → jobId → poll /jobs/{jobId} until esriJobSucceeded → GET result → .tpkx.
  CompactV2 unpack (spec fully known): .tpkx = ZIP → root.json + iteminfo + thumbnail + tile/ of .bundle files. Each .bundle = 128×128 tile block: 64-byte header at offset 0 (LE) → tile index at byte 64 = 128×128 array of 8-byte records. TileIndexOffset = 64 + 8*(128*(row%128) + (col%128)). Each record: offset = bits 0–39, size = bits 40–63 → seek + read size bytes = raw tile. Absolute (row,col) = bundle base (from .bundle filename e.g. R0000C0000) + in-bundle row/col. Skip size-0. Port from Esri raster-tiles-compactcache (Vundler.py) / @syncpoint/compact-cache-bundle; GDAL 3.8+ ESRIC driver = cross-check oracle. .vtpk shares the same bundle format (vector pbf) → a future vector handler reuses the walk.
  SAT reassembly: exportTiles is per-service → 3 SAT services = 3 separate .tpkx, same unpack loop, only the destination DB differs (SAT / SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES). Separate, not combined.
  API key: reuse api_keys.json + getApiKey; inject ?token=&lt;key&gt;; never in source JSON, never logged; decrypt at call-time. Uses Fred's Esri Location Platform account (needs a token — the public tile endpoint doesn't).
  De-risk first: curl the exportTiles POST→poll→download flow against a real endpoint from Git Bash BEFORE any Kotlin. Confirm exportTiles is enabled on the public arcgisonline.com services.
Tile action plan (ordered Step 0 → 6)
  Step 0: verify the area download submission is the black box; origin audit + blast-radius inventory; scope the DB rules engine; pin down the fit process; standardize each non-area origin onto the area submission with a source preference (default = today's behavior).

⭐ ROUTE-STATE PERSISTENCE &amp; TEARDOWN — ⭐ #1 NEXT BUILD (resume here) OPEN
Root cause located 07-06 via fresh xref (recommit docs; navigation_xref regenerated 07-06 11:32). Fix design not yet locked — one source-check remains.
Problem (observed)
The route nav box disappears; states don't change as they should. Route-planning state is not reliably persisted across navigation, nor reliably torn down on exit. Two repro triggers (with a route open): (a) open/touch another item; (b) close the artifacts panel. Two failure modes: (1) route disappears from the map entirely; (2) route stays drawn but goes dead/inert (geometry visible, controls gone/unresponsive).
Root cause (located from xref)
Route mode is held in var routeMode by remember { mutableStateOf(false) } — ephemeral Compose state — at TWO independent copies: ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:129 and ConvoyScreen.kt:197. Both drive ONE shared window.__routeMode in convoy_map.html. Teardown = ~8 scattered hardcoded calls per screen of setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(); (ConvoyMapViewerScreen 955/1044/1075/1112, arm-on 996/1020, resume 1154; ConvoyScreen 1608/1684/1716/1743, arm-on 1648/1671, resume 1775). No single teardown funnel.
This one fact explains both failure modes: touching another item / closing the panel recomposes or orphans the remember boolean → Kotlin routeMode resets/desyncs but JS gets NO matching setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine(). Disappear = a path fired clearBuildLine / a redraw overlaid it. Stays-but-dead = Kotlin routeMode went false so controls detach, but JS still shows the line.
Intent — Fred's 3 requirements
  Persist route-planning state in the MAP JSON so nav away + back restores it (survives recomposition/nav, which remember does not).
  States unique per map — Planning (grouptrack_map.html) vs Convoy (convoy_map.html) must not collide on the shared JS flag; the two booleans need per-map identity.
  ⚠ SUPERSEDED by the 07-08 hard rule (below): NOT "every exit ends it." The correct rule is the OPPOSITE — while route-add is active the screen PERSISTS through every selection and the map/exits are INERT; the ONLY exit is an EXPLICIT CLOSE, which routes through ONE teardown funnel (the save/discard prompt), replacing the ~8 scattered teardowns. Nothing else tears it down.
Key principle: persist unless/until closed by an exit method — persist across nav, never past an exit.
Touchpoints + remaining source-check before locking
Touchpoints: setRouteMode (JS, convoy_map.html) toggled from both screens; window.__routeMode gate if(window.__routeMode)return; at convoy_map.html:495 (BUG A popup suppression — must stay mode-scoped); RouteManager holds build logic (snap/addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices, buildWktAndBbox, insertRoute); JS build fns drawBuildLine/clearBuildLine/updateRoutes/showRoutes; onTrackTap at ConvoyMapViewerScreen:515, ConvoyScreen:645 &amp; 895.
07-08 FIX SPEC (Fred, hard rule): while Route+ is active the route screen persists through ANY other selection (?, hamburger, search, item, panel — anything); the only exit is an explicit close, which prompts save-or-discard. This subsumes the persistence issue — state can never be implicitly abandoned, so it can't be orphaned. Same prompt on BOTH exits (planning-exit + convoy-return). Next-session pickup.
Before locking: the xref indexes definitions + bridge calls, not full handler bodies. Read the actual .kt for the artifact-panel-close (onDismiss/onClose) handler + the onTrackTap bodies and CONFIRM they lack a setRouteMode(false) teardown call (the diagnosis predicts they do). Then design = persist route state to the map JSON (per-map keyed) + single teardown funnel every exit routes through. Lock only after the two-handler read confirms.

Other V2.6 backlog (no-radio) OPEN
  ⚠ MAPS checkbox ignored when track already exists — fires only in the INSERT branch; move the maps call out of AddOutcome.INSERT -&gt; and gate on the checkbox for any non-error outcome.
  ⚠ CLEAR-AREA / DELETE-AREA for downloads — NEVER WIRED (add to 2.6). The per-area tile clear was deliberately left unwritten during the area-download build because the MBTiles cutover was pending (didn't want to write it against loose-file storage about to be replaced).   ⚠ UNEVEN QUEUE SEGMENT SIZES waste the concurrency (perf, new 07-09). SAT submits as TWO jobs — one ~60,000 tiles (starts at z18), one ~11,000 — wildly unequal. With MAX_CONCURRENT=2 the 11K finishes fast, then that slot idles / picks up TOPO while the 60K monster runs ~alone → parallelism collapses toward 1× for the long tail. Partly explains the 80 min, AND why raising MAX_CONCURRENT may not help much: an indivisible 60K job hogs one slot the whole download; more slots can't subdivide it. SEGMENTATION METHOD (Fred, 07-09 FINAL). Divide the area bbox into EQUAL AREAS sized so NO area exceeds 50,000 SAT tiles. SAT is the sizing driver (densest source — goes to z18); size the grid to keep SAT ≤50K/cell and every other source (shallower zoom, fewer tiles) is automatically well under 50K in the same cell. So: estimate SAT tiles for the bbox → divide into ceil(SAT_total / 50000) equal areas → ONE uniform grid, computed against SAT only, applied to ALL sources. The grid is UNIFORM (plain equal-area cells); applied to each source's tiles it yields even batches per segment. LOAD BALANCING = process segments sharing the SAME ZOOM VALUES FROM THE SAME SOURCE SEQUENTIALLY (queue homogeneous work → comparable batches → even flow); evenness is a PROCESSING-ORDER property (group like-with-like), not per-source count juggling. ⚠ LOAD-BALANCE PRINCIPLE (the why): each segment MUST be a COMPLETE VERTICAL SLICE OF THE ZOOM STACK (z-min..z-max) for its geographic cell — NOT segmented by zoom. Segmenting by zoom recreates the imbalance (z18-only = the 45K heavy monster; z10-16 = trivial). Full-stack-per-cell gives every segment the SAME SHAPE of work (its share of heavy z18 + light upper layers), so equal-area segments do equal work and finish together in parallel slots — that comparability IS the load balancing. Unit = a vertical column (full zoom) over a horizontal cell, sized so SAT full-stack ≤50K. NOTE the heavy part is z18: tiles there carry more DATA (imagery), so processing accelerates as it climbs past z18 — data-per-tile drives speed, not tile count; splitting the cell halves the heavy-z18 load per slot. Only SAT needs estimating (worst case); others ride the same grid under the ceiling. Slight overlap (~tile-width) prevents seam gaps; hasTile dedupes. Prerequisite for higher MAX_CONCURRENT to pay off; likely a bigger lever than raising it.
  ⚠ SAT OVERLAY DISPLAYING ON TOPO / TOPO+ (new 07-09). The SAT overlay tiles (labels / transportation — likely SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES) are rendering on top of the TOPO and TOPO+ base maps where they should not appear. Layer-compositing bug: the overlay isn't cleared/swapped when the active base map changes (SAT→TOPO), or overlays render regardless of the active base. Confirmed: ALWAYS ON, BOTH overlays (labels SAT_LABELS_PLACES + transportation SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT) — not intermittent, not download-dependent. "Always on, both" ⇒ overlays are unconditionally added and NOT gated on the active base; the fix is a "show these overlays only when base == SAT" condition in the Leaflet layer-stack logic (map HTML) / how MapSourceManager associates overlays with a base — not a swap-timing race. Add to 2.6.
  Tile download SPEED-UP (2.6b, 07-09) — concurrency + zoom-cap + 429 backoff. Parallelized the sequential tile-fetch loop in ConvoyTileDownloader.downloadTiles (fetch 8 concurrently via TILE_FETCH_CONCURRENCY, insert serially — single cached SQLite handle unsafe for concurrent writes). Removed the stale per-source download zoom cap in ConvoyTileCalculator.maxZoomForSource (TOPO+/TRAIL→17 was for the old hand-drawn source; now full range; JSON max_zoom retained as a display clamp). Added 429/503 backoff in fetchTileBytes (retry SAME tile, exponential, honors Retry-After; 404 fast-null) so concurrency can't silently drop tiles under throttling. Reason: current download speed is an adoption obstacle. Built + applied 07-09; testing on Droid 1. 125K-tile test (SAT+TOPO+TOPO+) = 80 min, ~100% success, ZERO 429s, 2 transient 502s [⭐ RECONCILED RESULT: 2 queues vs 3 queues, cause = segment balance. The 80-min run (2 queues) was balanced ONLY BY COINCIDENCE — the big SAT segment happened to have ~equal tiles to ALL other jobs combined, so a 2-slot split fell ~50/50 by luck. With 3 QUEUES that broke: the 3rd slot subdivided the "everything else" half, small jobs drained at ~45 min, and the big SAT job ran ALONE for the tail → ~113 min (92% at 104 min). So current balance is ACCIDENTAL/FRAGILE (holds only because big-segment ≈ sum-of-rest at 2 slots); changing concurrency/area/tile-mix breaks it. EVEN SEGMENTATION replaces luck with guarantee — equal ≤50K-SAT segments hold balance regardless of slot count or area shape. Keep concurrency modest (~2); segmentation is the fix. OPEN EXPERIMENT (post-segmentation): once segments are balanced, run the same area at MAX_CONCURRENT=2 then =3 to isolate concurrency (today's =3 was confounded by imbalance). If 3≈2 → resource-SATURATED, keep 2, SKIP the tuning rig; if 3&lt;2 → spare capacity, build the rig and tune up. Segmentation first (removes the confound), then this clean test. Fred's hypothesis — test as a GRID: the two multiplying levers are queues(MAX_CONCURRENT) × async(TILE_FETCH_CONCURRENCY); at the SAME total (e.g. 24), FEWER queues × MORE async each may WIN — 2×12 could beat 3×8 — because same request rate but parallelism concentrated as async-within-fewer-jobs avoids stranding, feeds the critical path directly, and wastes fewer slots on early-draining small jobs. Test {2,3 queues}×{8,12 async}, measure time + collisions. Rig should make BOTH knobs tunable.] (dropped — 502 not yet in retry set).
  TILE-DOWNLOAD TUNING RIG (planned, next session) — manual tuning, NOT auto-throttle. Decided against an adaptive feedback controller (overkill). Four pieces: (1) add 502 to the retryable set in fetchTileBytes (currently 429/503 only — the 2 dropped tiles were 502 transient server strain); (2) make MAX_CONCURRENT (job-level, ConvoyDownloadQueue) read from JSON so it's tunable without a rebuild — but clamped to ±1 change per cycle (no jumping 2→8): read JSON target, compare to a PERSISTED last-effective value, step ≤1 toward target, use + persist it. Change is SETTABLE in the queue manager and takes effect on the NEXT set of submits/releases — CANNOT change while jobs are running (new value is staged, applied at the next launch when the queue is idle; running jobs finish under their start value). So a "cycle" = a fresh set of submits/releases (queue idle→launching a new batch), not per-app-launch. (3) break out error counts by code in the Complete: … downloaded=X failed=Y logcat line → failed=Y [429=a 502=b 503=c] for visibility while tuning (no UI); (4) publish a tuning GUIDELINE — error-rate thresholds + how to step concurrency (highest concurrency where error rate stays under threshold). Rationale: current 2×8=16 concurrent (jobs×tiles) gave 0 429s → headroom exists, but more concurrency risks more 502s, so tune manually against visible error counts. "Cycle" for the ±1 clamp = per app launch (simplest); persisted last-effective value is the one bit of new state.

V2.7 — iPad / CROSS-PLATFORM (post-V2.6 target)
Standing awareness — not an active task. iPad IS the post-V2.6 target (this overturns the old V3.0 "no iPad support" line). Reasoning arc reconciled 07-04. The evolution below is written in so it's never lost.
The reconciled strategy (07-04) STRATEGY
  Key collapse: Convoy is a fork of Meshtastic's messaging (Android = a fork of Meshtastic-Android, Kotlin). The native-vs-PWA-vs-WKWebView arc was all answering "how do we get BLE on iOS?" — a question that dissolves once convoy is seen as a fork of the mesh app. So iPad = a fork of Meshtastic-Apple (Swift/SwiftUI + BLE + protobuf; GPL v3; App-Store-approved; universal). Mac + Xcode = the prerequisite. Flag: Meshtastic-Apple ships native TAK/CoT — reconcile vs the roadmap's "TAK as pattern only."
  Config write is offloaded: the planning side CREATES a Meshtastic restore FILE (pure file creation, no BLE in GroupTrack's code); Meshtastic's own "restore config" applies it. Confirm the backup/restore format + Apple acceptance at build time.
  Presentation ~90% shared because it's already web (Leaflet in a WebView). SwiftUI rejected for presentation — it doesn't port to a browser + gives zero reuse of the Android web layer. iPad presentation = the existing web layer in a WKWebView behind a native Swift shell; PC = the same web (planning half) in a browser; Android = the same web unchanged. Swift's only job = the native shell (mesh source + WebView host + JS↔native bridge, the WKScriptMessageHandler analog of Android's JavascriptInterface).
  Real cost driver = the bridge/I/O surface. What renders inside the WebView ports cleanly; every point where the web reaches out to the device (file I/O, GPS, radio/mesh, camera, share, persistence, offline-tile reads, native dialogs) is a bridge call re-implemented per platform, many with no browser equivalent (why PC is planning-only). Next action: enumerate that surface from the Android code (every JavascriptInterface method + evaluateJavascript/postMessage crossing) — = the true iPad build cost AND which functions can/can't go to PC.
  Three surfaces split on connectivity: PC = planning-only web app (routes/waypoints/library + config-file generation; no mesh/radio; online); Android + iPad = off-grid native convoy execution (BLE/radio/live mesh — convoy cannot be web). The A/B decision touches only the mobile mesh source; PC proceeds independently.
  Two candidate iPad-execution patterns (open): (A) BRIDGE — convoy is its own native iOS app consuming mesh over a local loopback port from the separate Meshtastic app (less code; adds a runtime dependency + iOS-lifecycle fragility — the neighbor app must stay foregrounded, a real mark against A for an off-grid safety app); (B) FORK — import Meshtastic's BLE/mesh and extend, exactly as on Android (more work; no runtime dependency; Android-sameness). Not decided; off-grid reliability leans B.
  Target end-state: a messaging/logic SERVICE LAYER + logic-free presentation panels (panels call the service for everything). Serving all three platforms = the logic rewritten ONCE into one platform-independent implementation, not three copies. Current code isn't built this way (logic woven into the Android fork) → a one-time extraction = the same effort as the bridge-surface inventory seen from the other end.
  KMP is the natural target: logic is already Kotlin; KMP migration is incremental (share networking/data/domain first; expect/actual IS the "configured API resolves per platform" idea). KMP produces a shared logic module a Swift UI/shell consumes (it does NOT fork Meshtastic-Apple — that's Swift). Readiness gauge: (1) mechanical — KMP plugin preflight + Qodana; (2) architectural — a logic-entanglement inventory vs where_used/function_universe xref (the real effort predictor).
Sequencing (firm) + next-session deliverables STRATEGY
  Ship V2.6 on Windows (cleanup + map-download rewrite).
  Set up the Mac Air and build/run known-good V2.6 on it FIRST — prove the environment with a known-good artifact before piling on KMP.
  Then KMP plugin preflight + the entanglement inventory vs xref.
  Then incremental KMP extraction (share domain/logic first).
  Then iPad.
Rule: do NOT introduce KMP onto an unproven Mac — one unknown at a time (else a break is ambiguous between KMP and Mac setup). Building V2.6 on Mac is the first rung needed anyway (same env for preflight + eventual Xcode).
Deliverable 1 — Mac environment build-out: inventory required tools + install-and-confirm one at a time (Git + Terminal/zsh — macOS is real Unix, the Git-Bash/CRLF-heredoc pain may relax; Android Studio + SDK + Gradle + JDK/JavaVM; Python; keystore access — grouptrack-release-key.jks is in iCloud; clone + build V2.6; THEN the KMP plugin; MySQL — purpose TBD; Xcode + Apple Developer enrollment — later rung, iPad only). Deliverable 2 — consolidated cross-domain tooling/stack inventory (PC/local dev, Data/MySQL, AWS/V3.0 backend, Google Play, runtimes) — assemble + confirm from the actual environment + docs, not memory. Feeds the shared-layer language decision.

⭐ ESRI TILE DOWNLOAD STRATEGY — 4-phase plan (planning session 2026-07-09) STRATEGY
Origin (07-09): the V2.6b batch transport plan (Esri exportTiles → .tpkx → unpack) was de-risked and found unavailable. Curl against the keyed Location Platform imagery service (ibasemaps-api.arcgis.com/.../World_Imagery/MapServer?f=json, HTTP 200 with the AAPT key) returns only tileInfo — no exportTilesAllowed. The keyed Location Platform endpoint is per-tile only; exportTiles lives on the separate tiledbasemaps.arcgis.com "for Export" instance (a different org/subscription entitlement). So the .tpkx batch plan is dead on the current account, and V2.6b pivots to tile-fetch concurrency on the free endpoint (speed-up, not a transport rewrite).
The cost reality. Esri Location Platform = 2,000,000 tiles/month free, then $0.15/1,000 flat (no volume tiers; high-volume only via Esri sales). Real GroupTrack usage: track download 200–300k tiles, area download ~500k tiles, heavy users ~100&nbsp;GB ≈ 10.8M tiles. A 100&nbsp;GB cache is a lifetime accumulation (≈900k/mo over a year, under the free tier) — but one-shot bulk on a metered key is financially impossible. Key honesty: the concurrency rewrite speeds downloads up, it does NOT reduce tile volume — on the free tier, faster just means faster accumulation (today's 100&nbsp;GB caches were built under the free tier). Demand-shaping via cost only works on a paid path.
The four phases:
  Phase 1 — NOW / BETA: free arcgisonline.com endpoint for everyone; the concurrency patch speeds it up at no cost and no licensing dependency. (This is the immediate V2.6b work.)
  Phase 2 — OPTIONAL PAID PERSONAL TIER: users who want the faster keyed endpoint and/or big pre-downloads foot their own bill via their own entitlement (BYO-key / ~$100 ArcGIS Personal-Use). Cost self-selects and self-limits. Note: a personal license is still PER-TILE — not the batch/redistribution product.
  Phase 3 — ENTITY ACCOUNT: past enough $100 personal accounts, it pays to shift to one ArcGIS org/enterprise account + shared key behind the backend proxy + negotiated volume pricing (also the central usage dashboard/billing + the 3.0 key-security model). Crossover economics unknown — depends on Esri's negotiated volume quote (the single deciding number; not published).
  Phase 4 — FULLY OPTIMIZED ENDGAME: download-once / serve-many with dedup across the whole user base. Riders cluster in the same popular areas, so each region is fetched from Esri once and amortized across everyone who rides there — cost stops scaling with users and scales only with unique geography (bounded, slow-growing). Also solves key security (key server-only) + speed (users pull from GroupTrack) + control (one cache/dashboard/bill).
Phase-4 distribution refinement — self-managed AREA PACKS (Fred, 07-09). Rather than run a live tile CDN, self-manage distribution: a batch process pulls/builds an area's .mbtiles once, hosts the finished file (FTP or file host / URL+catalog), and GroupTrack devices fetch + import the pre-built .mbtiles into MBTilesStore. Much lighter infra (a file server, not a mapping service) and fits the app's existing MBTiles-file world (store already reads .mbtiles; X-plore flow already moves tile files; import is close to Pass 1). Productized = "download this area pack" through the same download pipeline, pointed at pre-built packs instead of Esri tiles.
⚠ THE REDISTRIBUTION LICENSE GATE (unchanged by any refinement). Hosting/FTPing an .mbtiles full of Esri tiles is redistribution just as much as live proxy-serving — legally identical on the point that matters. Phases 3–4 require a caching/redistribution-permitted Esri license (the "for Export" / offline entitlement) or a redistributable source. Lighter infra does not lighten the license requirement. The batch build's source is the same fork: free arcgisonline (ToS-gray bulk, just centralized), licensed for-Export (clean, negotiated/pricier), or USGS/USFS/BLM/Sentinel public-domain imagery (free + freely re-hostable — the clean fallback if Esri won't license redistribution).
The one gate that decides Phase 3 &amp; 4: a single Esri sales conversation — entity/enterprise volume price + whether caching/redistribution is licensed and at what cost (not published, not web-searchable). Also confirm: does Personal-Use / BYO-key permit third-party-app use; Personal-Use is non-commercial (GroupTrack free now, commercial revenue model — revisit on monetization).
Immediate next (code, safe under ALL phases): apply + build + test the tile-concurrency patch on the free endpoint (fetch-parallel / insert-serial, batch = 8). Do the db()/insertTile silent-failure hardening alongside (matters more once fetches are parallel). Do NOT switch the default to the keyed/metered endpoint. Current download speed is an adoption obstacle — this is the priority.
REFERENCE (durable — always-loaded)
Track model + data-integrity architecture (locked) LOCKED
  SPATIAL tables PURE OGC; properties/surveys/aliases/queues in the EXTENSION db (grouptrack_data.db) by id. Separate SQLite files — NO cross-DB JOIN. Boundary change = stop-and-check. (Note: the tile MBTiles files are ALSO separate per-type SQLite DBs — the DB rules engine's reach over them vs only the GPX/track DBs is a tile Step-0 scope question.)
  tracks: track_id PK, name, bbox, timestamps, geometry, min/max lat/lon, type, geom_hash NOT NULL UNIQUE (SHA-256 of WKT). track_properties: track_id PK, filename UNIQUE, source_format, recorded_at, distance_miles, duration_minutes, max/avg_speed_mph, elevation_gain_ft, point_count, shared, ride_id, area_id. artifact_aliases: alias_id, artifact_type (SINGULAR), artifact_id, alias, is_preferred (LOCAL), source, geom_hash.
  Storage: my_tracks GPX (/sdcard/Documents/my_tracks) = SOURCE OF TRUTH; DBs + receipt at /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/; tiles at /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/maps today (→ MBTiles-only per-type hard cutover = V2.6 tile ITEM A; install/update will STOP creating maps). Track files &lt;track_id&gt;.gpx. DELETE-AND-RESYNC off the table for deletes; forced resync on install = additive rebuild-from-source. Recorder GPX = lat/lon/ele/time only, NO &lt;speed&gt;, 3s sampling (→ 2s change-gated V2.6).
  "Artifact builds, not process builds": complete tracks fully, test as a unit, THEN routes, THEN waypoints.
