GroupTrack — Quick Start, Installation &amp; TroubleshootingBeta Tester Reference · Updated August 9, 2026 (V2.6e)
Beta Tester Reference
&#9940; DO NOT CLEAR APP DATA OR CACHE
Android Settings &rarr; Apps &rarr; GroupTrack &rarr; Storage &rarr; Clear storage / Clear
cache will cost you your trails, tracks and routes.
Clearing app data makes GroupTrack lose its permission to reach its own files, while Android
still shows the permission as granted. The next time the app opens it cannot see your data,
treats the device as new, and rebuilds empty &mdash; over the top of everything you had.
If you have already cleared app data or cache: DO NOT OPEN GROUPTRACK. Uninstall it
first, then install it again. Your maps and trails live in
Documents/GroupTrack and survive an uninstall &mdash; they do not survive the app
opening without permission.
Do not copy your files anywhere and do not move them back by hand. A fresh install finds
them on its own. Copying them back into an app that cannot see them is how they get lost.
Clearing app data is never a fix for a GroupTrack problem. If something is
wrong, uninstall and reinstall instead &mdash; it is safe, and it keeps your data.
Updated August 9, 2026 (V2.6e)
Changing your satellite map source
Screens for this are shown step by step in the User Manual &mdash; tap the ? button in the app.
When you change the map source on the SAT slot, GroupTrack asks what to do with the map
tiles you have already downloaded. Your maps keep working the whole time — this is only about
tiles stored on your device. Online maps switch to the new source straight away.
You get three choices:
Delete and start over. Clears the stored tiles for that slot and lets you rebuild
from scratch. Best if you have only a little downloaded, or you would rather not think about
it — it cannot leave you half converted.
Move everything to the new source. Tick what you want moved: track maps, map
areas, or both. At least one must be ticked. Everything is submitted at once and runs in the
background.
Leave my maps in place. Nothing is downloaded or removed. Refresh ground yourself
from the downloads panel when you need it. You can also tick Add track maps now to
bring your trails over immediately and leave the areas for later.
If you have tracks, tick "Refresh track corridors". Leaving it off does not lose
your tracks — but the same ground gets covered as boxed areas instead, which downloads
roughly ten times as many tiles for it.
While the move runs, a panel lists each step as it finishes. Removing track maps is the
slow part and shows a progress bar. Leave the panel on screen until it is done — it cannot be
restarted from where it stopped.
Watching downloads
Screens for this are shown step by step in the User Manual &mdash; tap the ? button in the app.
Tap QUEUES to see what is downloading and what is waiting. The panel shows:
What is running and what is waiting — the number of jobs and the tile count for each,
with the estimated time remaining and the date and time it expects to finish.
Live speed — the combined tiles per second across everything currently downloading.
This is the total, not one job&rsquo;s share.
Slots — how many downloads run at once, 1 to 4. 4 is recommended and is the
default on a new install. Your setting is remembered. Lowering it does not stop jobs already
running; it takes effect as they finish.
Filter chips — ALL, AREA, CORR, RFSH, DEL — narrow the list to one kind of job. They
also scope the buttons: with a filter active, CANCEL and CLEAR act only on what you can see.
QUEUED and COMPLETED — tap the arrow beside either heading to collapse a long
list and move quickly to the section you want. Tap a completed job to see when it started, how
long it took, and its average speed.
Downloads run faster across different map sources than within one. Each source is a
separate server, so jobs spread over satellite, topo and topo+ finish sooner than the same number
of jobs all pulling from one source. A refresh that touches only one slot will take longer than a
mixed download of the same size &mdash; that is normal, not a fault.
For a long download, plug in and take the app off battery saving. A phone left on
battery overnight can run at a fraction of its daytime speed. Use a wall charger rather than a
computer &mdash; a sleeping computer can cut power to its USB ports. Then, in Android Settings,
find GroupTrack under Battery and set it to Unrestricted, and turn off any
standby or app optimisation settings for it. The exact wording varies by phone.
If the queue is holding, the panel says QUEUE HELD — nothing will start and offers
RELEASE. A held queue looks exactly like a stalled one, so check for that banner first
if nothing seems to be happening.
QUICK START
⚠️ Off-grid rule: trails have no cell/WiFi. Download your maps and import your trails BEFORE you ride — the app can't fetch them in the field. Un-downloaded areas show blank on the trail.
Before Your First Ride
Install GroupTrack APK on your Android device (see Installation below)Power on your T1000-E Meshtastic radioOpen GroupTrack — radio should connect via Bluetooth automaticallyVerify connection: radio icon shows connected in the app
⚠️ CRITICAL — Two Radio Restrictions
RESTRICTION 1 — T1000-E Firmware: DO NOT update beyond 2.6.11
The T1000-E Meshtastic radio firmware MUST stay at version 2.6.11 or earlier. Updating to any firmware version beyond 2.6.11 will make the radio unstable for Bluetooth connectivity and radio configuration. This is a known issue with newer Meshtastic firmware on the T1000-E hardware.
Check current firmware: Meshtastic app → Radio Config → Device InfoIf firmware is 2.6.11 or earlier: DO NOT UPDATEIf firmware was accidentally updated beyond 2.6.11: flash back to 2.6.11 using Meshtastic Flasher toolThis restriction applies to ALL T1000-E radios used with GroupTrack
RESTRICTION 2 — Keep Radio Within Bluetooth Range During Rides
When riding, ALWAYS keep your radio in your cart/vehicle within 50 feet of your phone. Do NOT carry the radio away from your phone (or vice versa) beyond Bluetooth effective range.
Bluetooth effective range: approximately 50 feet (15 meters)If radio exceeds BLE range while still "connected," the connection enters supervision timeoutSymptoms: app freezes/pauses, position updates stop, UI becomes unresponsiveThe BLE connection does not cleanly disconnect — it hangs in limbo waiting for the radio to reappearRecovery: force close GroupTrack, move radio back within range, reopen appPrevention: leave the radio mounted in your cart. Keep your phone in the cart. They travel together.
Pre-Ride Checklist
[ ] Phone charged[ ] Radio charged and firmware at 2.6.11 or earlier[ ] Radio mounted in cart (stays with phone during ride)[ ] GroupTrack installed and opens without errors[ ] Radio connects via Bluetooth (solid connection icon)[ ] Map tiles downloaded for the ENTIRE ride area (REQUIRED off-grid — check the blue overlay covers it on Planning Map)[ ] Trail data / trailheads imported for ride area (also needed before you lose connectivity)[ ] GPS lock acquired (position shows on map)
INSTALLATION
  &#9888;&#65039; Install with -r only &mdash; never -d
  The correct command is adb install -r &lt;apk&gt;. The -d flag allows a downgrade, and a downgrade makes Android treat the install as brand new. The app then starts without all-files access and can overwrite its own map databases with empty ones. Without -d, a bad version number simply makes the install fail with an error &mdash; which is what you want.
  &#9888;&#65039; If the install asks first-time setup questions on a phone that already has GroupTrack &mdash; CANCEL
  That means Android is treating it as a fresh install rather than an update, and continuing can cost your downloaded maps and trail data. Cancel, and check the version number before trying again.
  &#9888;&#65039; Sideloaded and Play Store builds cannot replace each other
  Both are named com.grouptrack.android, but they are signed with different keys. A sideloaded build blocks the Play Store from updating the app, and vice versa. Switching between them requires an uninstall first &mdash; which erases your downloaded maps. Pick one and stay with it.
  &#9989; Ten-second check after any install
  Open the app and confirm your trails and tracks are still listed. If everything looks empty, stop and report it before downloading anything &mdash; do not re-download over the top.
Installing GroupTrack APK
From Play Store (tester):
Accept tester invitation linkDownload from Play StorePackage: com.grouptrack.android
From local APK (developer/tester):
adb -s [device-serial] install -r app/build/outputs/apk/google/release/app-google-release.apk
⚠️ INSTALL RULE (CORRECTED 2026-08-02): use plain -r. NEVER add -d. The previous guidance here said to always use -r -d; that was wrong and it cost a full spatial database on 2026-08-01. -d permits a DOWNGRADE, a downgrade makes Android treat the install as brand new, the app then starts without all-files authority, and its create-if-missing database open writes empty schemas over the real ones. Without -d a regressed version code makes the install FAIL with an error instead of silently downgrading — the failure is the warning you want. Add -d only after establishing why the version code went backwards.
⚠️ If an install prompts FIRST-INSTALL questions on a device that already has GroupTrack: CANCEL. That is the signature of the above. Do not proceed.
✅ Ten-second post-install check: adb -s [device-serial] shell ls -la /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/*.db — a spatial database in the hundreds of KB rather than tens of MB means it has been replaced with an empty schema. Stop and restore rather than re-downloading over the top.
⚠️ Play Store vs local APK: DIFFERENT SIGNING KEYS, SAME PACKAGE NAME. Since the 07-26 package merge both are com.grouptrack.android, so a sideloaded build blocks the Play Store from installing or updating the app and vice versa (INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, or Play silently offers nothing). To move a device between the two you must UNINSTALL first — which wipes tiles and app data. Decide per device: sideload OR Play, not both.
Post-Install Steps
Launch GroupTrackGrant location permission when promptedOpen Planning Map and verify tile loading
First-Time Setup (do these in order)
Before your first ride, complete these three setup steps. For detailed, screen-by-screen walkthroughs with screenshots, open the in-app manual — tap the "?" icon anywhere in GroupTrack. The manual is cookbook-style (how you get there → what you do → where it leads); the steps below are the short version.
1. Settings → choose your map sources. Open Settings and select the map sources you want available. New installations use Google Hybrid for the satellite slot (SAT), with Esri Topographic (TOPO) and Esri USA Topo (TOPO+). Leave the defaults unless you have a reason to change them — these are what the download and map screens use. (Manual: "?" → Settings / Map Sources.)
⚠️ Upgrading testers: your satellite slot does NOT change. If you already have GroupTrack installed you keep whatever source you were using — the new default applies to fresh installations only, and nothing is downloaded or deleted behind your back. Google Hybrid is worth moving to: it carries roads and place names inside the satellite imagery, so it needs one tile store instead of three (Esri satellite needs two extra label stores) and shows street names offline. To switch, go to Settings → Map Sources → SAT and choose Google Hybrid; GroupTrack then walks you through what to do with the tiles you already stored. See Changing a map source below.
Changing a map source (SAT, TOPO or TOPO+)
Stored tiles came from the source that downloaded them and cannot be converted. When you change the source on a slot that already holds tiles, GroupTrack asks what to do with them.
⚠️ Please be advised: whichever option you choose, you lose Esri place and road label information. The new source does not fetch label overlays, so those label stores are removed either way — and their space (typically a few hundred MB) is reclaimed.
You will be asked to choose one of three:
Delete and start over — removes the stored maps for that slot and frees the space, so you can rebuild around your tracks. This cannot be undone and there is no backup. Your download history for that slot is cleared too, so note any areas you will want to redraw. Recommended when moving from Esri to Google Hybrid, unless you are already downloading by corridor.
Move everything to the new source — GroupTrack converts your existing maps in the background. All of the downloads are submitted at once and every image is slowly replaced from the new source, track maps first and then your areas. Your maps stay usable throughout. Best if you rely on road and place names. (Arriving shortly — not in this build.)
Move tracks and areas on my schedule — nothing is removed and nothing is downloaded. Your existing maps keep working, so you always have something to fall back on. Refresh ground as you need it from the downloads panel — by track, or by drawing an area — with Replace tiles ticked. Ground you have not refreshed stays without road and place names.
Nothing downloads automatically. When you are ready, use Download Tiles by Area or by Track. If you have imported tracks, downloading by corridor around those tracks is the better choice — it covers where you actually ride and uses roughly two thirds less storage than boxing the same ground by area. If you have no tracks yet, download by area and add corridors later; the two work together in the same store.
Your tracks, routes and trails are never affected — this only ever touches downloaded map tiles.
2. Import trails and trailheads, and DOWNLOAD MAPS for your ride area. Load the trail data for your riding area so trails and trailheads show on the map. Then, while on WiFi/cell, download the map tiles for the area you'll ride — use the Planning Map download and confirm the blue overlay covers your whole ride area. (Manual: "?" → Import Artifacts / Trail Sources, and Offline Maps &amp; Downloads.) If trails don't appear, see "Trail Display Issues" in Troubleshooting.
2b. Import OSM trail data (optional, and worth doing). GroupTrack can import free OpenStreetMap data for your state, which typically adds far more ground than the curated trail sources alone — for Utah, about 104,000 trails and unpaved roads against roughly 49,000 from the state source. It is a four-step process on one panel: Planning Map → Work with Artifacts → Import OSM Data.
DOWNLOAD — the panel opens the Geofabrik site in your browser. Choose your state and take the file ending in -latest-free.gpkg.zip (about 330 MB for Utah). ⚠️ The other formats on that page will download and then be rejected.CLICK HERE WHEN DOWNLOAD HAS COMPLETED — nothing happens automatically; GroupTrack does not watch your downloads folder. Tap the green bar and it finds the file.EXTRACT — unpacks and builds a trail database. Under a minute for most states.IMPORT — choose FULL STATE, or SELECTED AREA to draw a box on the map and take only what is inside it. The confirmation tells you how many trails are about to be added. There is no undo.CLEANUP — removes the working files. Not automatic; it waits for you.
Importing a state you already have is safe: it reports almost everything as dropped and adds nothing, so you will not get two copies of a trail.
(Manual: "?" → Planning Map → Work with Artifacts → Import OSM Data — an eight-screen walkthrough with captures of both the whole-state and drawn-area paths.)
⚠️ Downloading maps before you ride is REQUIRED for off-grid use. On the trail you are off the grid — no cell, no WiFi — so the app cannot fetch map tiles in the field. Any area you did not download ahead of time will show blank/grey on the trail. Download every area you plan to ride before you leave connectivity, and verify the blue overlay covers it. This applies to trails/trailheads too — import them ahead of time.
3. Set up the radio. Pair and connect the T1000-E (see Radio Setup below). Do this last, after maps and trails are in place. (Manual: "?" → Radio / Connection.)
Note for upgrading testers: if you're coming from a pre-V2.6 build, do the V2.6 One-Time Tile Migration (below) before step 2's tile downloads.
⚠️ V2.6 One-Time Tile Migration (upgrading testers)
V2.6 changes how offline map tiles are stored — from thousands of loose files to a single compact database per map type (about half the storage; satellite ~55% smaller, WebP-compressed). Old loose tiles must be cleared once and re-downloaded in the new format before maps will work.
Install X-plore File Manager (free, Play Store) — it shows a live progress count while deleting, so you always know it's working.In X-plore, go to Internal storage → Documents → GroupTrack → maps and delete the maps folder. A large old cache can take a while — keep the device plugged in; the on-screen count shows it's active.Back in GroupTrack, re-download your ride areas (by Area, or from a track/route). They save in the new format at roughly half the size.
Your tracks and routes are NOT affected — this clears only downloaded map tiles. This is one-time; future updates won't need it.

GroupTrack — Quick Start, Installation &amp; TroubleshootingBeta Tester Reference · Updated August 17, 2026 (V2.6f)
Beta Tester Reference
Updated August 17, 2026 (V2.6f)
Changing your satellite map source
ANNOTATE: screen capture needed — Map Sources screen, SAT slot selected, showing the
three migration options.
When you change the map source on the SAT slot, GroupTrack asks what to do with the map
tiles you have already downloaded. Your maps keep working the whole time — this is only about
tiles stored on your device. Online maps switch to the new source straight away.
You get three choices:
Delete and start over. Clears the stored tiles for that slot and lets you rebuild
from scratch. Best if you have only a little downloaded, or you would rather not think about
it — it cannot leave you half converted.
Move everything to the new source. Tick what you want moved: track maps, map
areas, or both. At least one must be ticked. Everything is submitted at once and runs in the
background.
ANNOTATE: screen capture needed — option 2 selected, showing both checkboxes and the
warning text under "Refresh track corridors".
Leave my maps in place. Nothing is downloaded or removed. Refresh ground yourself
from the downloads panel when you need it. You can also tick Add track maps now to
bring your trails over immediately and leave the areas for later.
If you have tracks, tick "Refresh track corridors". Leaving it off does not lose
your tracks — but the same ground gets covered as boxed areas instead, which downloads
roughly ten times as many tiles for it.
While the move runs, a panel lists each step as it finishes. Removing track maps is the
slow part and shows a progress bar. Leave the panel on screen until it is done — it cannot be
restarted from where it stopped.
ANNOTATE: screen capture needed — the step list mid-run, showing ticked steps and the
progress bar during "Removing corridor map N of M".
Watching downloads
ANNOTATE: screen capture needed — download queue panel, expanded, showing the aggregate
rate line and the slots stepper.
Tap the download queue button to see what is running. The panel shows:
Live speed — tiles per second across everything currently downloading.
Slots — how many downloads run at once, 1 to 4. Three is the default. More slots
downloads faster overall, though each individual job slows a little. Your setting is
remembered.
QUEUED and COMPLETED sections, each of which folds away. Tap a completed job
to see when it started, how long it took, and its average speed.
If the queue is holding, the panel says QUEUE HELD — nothing will start and offers
RELEASE. A held queue looks exactly like a stalled one, so check for that banner first
if nothing seems to be happening.
ANNOTATE: screen capture needed — the QUEUE HELD banner with the RELEASE button.
QUICK START
⚠️ Off-grid rule: trails have no cell/WiFi. Download your maps and import your trails BEFORE you ride — the app can't fetch them in the field. Un-downloaded areas show blank on the trail.
Before Your First Ride
Install GroupTrack APK on your Android device (see Installation below)Power on your T1000-E Meshtastic radioOpen GroupTrack — radio should connect via Bluetooth automaticallyVerify connection: radio icon shows connected in the app
⚠️ CRITICAL — Two Radio Restrictions
RESTRICTION 1 — T1000-E Firmware: DO NOT update beyond 2.6.11
The T1000-E Meshtastic radio firmware MUST stay at version 2.6.11 or earlier. Updating to any firmware version beyond 2.6.11 will make the radio unstable for Bluetooth connectivity and radio configuration. This is a known issue with newer Meshtastic firmware on the T1000-E hardware.
Check current firmware: Meshtastic app → Radio Config → Device InfoIf firmware is 2.6.11 or earlier: DO NOT UPDATEIf firmware was accidentally updated beyond 2.6.11: flash back to 2.6.11 using Meshtastic Flasher toolThis restriction applies to ALL T1000-E radios used with GroupTrack
RESTRICTION 2 — Keep Radio Within Bluetooth Range During Rides
When riding, ALWAYS keep your radio in your cart/vehicle within 50 feet of your phone. Do NOT carry the radio away from your phone (or vice versa) beyond Bluetooth effective range.
Bluetooth effective range: approximately 50 feet (15 meters)If radio exceeds BLE range while still "connected," the connection enters supervision timeoutSymptoms: app freezes/pauses, position updates stop, UI becomes unresponsiveThe BLE connection does not cleanly disconnect — it hangs in limbo waiting for the radio to reappearRecovery: force close GroupTrack, move radio back within range, reopen appPrevention: leave the radio mounted in your cart. Keep your phone in the cart. They travel together.
Pre-Ride Checklist
[ ] Phone charged[ ] Radio charged and firmware at 2.6.11 or earlier[ ] Radio mounted in cart (stays with phone during ride)[ ] GroupTrack installed and opens without errors[ ] Radio connects via Bluetooth (solid connection icon)[ ] Map tiles downloaded for the ENTIRE ride area (REQUIRED off-grid — check the blue overlay covers it on Planning Map)[ ] Trail data / trailheads imported for ride area (also needed before you lose connectivity)[ ] GPS lock acquired (position shows on map)
INSTALLATION
  &#9888;&#65039; Install with -r only &mdash; never -d
  The correct command is adb install -r &lt;apk&gt;. The -d flag allows a downgrade, and a downgrade makes Android treat the install as brand new. The app then starts without all-files access and can overwrite its own map databases with empty ones. Without -d, a bad version number simply makes the install fail with an error &mdash; which is what you want.
  &#9888;&#65039; If the install asks first-time setup questions on a phone that already has GroupTrack &mdash; CANCEL
  That means Android is treating it as a fresh install rather than an update, and continuing can cost your downloaded maps and trail data. Cancel, and check the version number before trying again.
  &#9888;&#65039; Sideloaded and Play Store builds cannot replace each other
  Both are named com.grouptrack.android, but they are signed with different keys. A sideloaded build blocks the Play Store from updating the app, and vice versa. Switching between them requires an uninstall first &mdash; which erases your downloaded maps. Pick one and stay with it.
  &#9989; Ten-second check after any install
  Open the app and confirm your trails and tracks are still listed. If everything looks empty, stop and report it before downloading anything &mdash; do not re-download over the top.
Installing GroupTrack APK
From Play Store (tester):
Accept tester invitation linkDownload from Play StorePackage: com.grouptrack.android
From local APK (developer/tester):
adb -s [device-serial] install -r app/build/outputs/apk/google/release/app-google-release.apk
⚠️ INSTALL RULE (CORRECTED 2026-08-02): use plain -r. NEVER add -d. The previous guidance here said to always use -r -d; that was wrong and it cost a full spatial database on 2026-08-01. -d permits a DOWNGRADE, a downgrade makes Android treat the install as brand new, the app then starts without all-files authority, and its create-if-missing database open writes empty schemas over the real ones. Without -d a regressed version code makes the install FAIL with an error instead of silently downgrading — the failure is the warning you want. Add -d only after establishing why the version code went backwards.
⚠️ If an install prompts FIRST-INSTALL questions on a device that already has GroupTrack: CANCEL. That is the signature of the above. Do not proceed.
✅ Ten-second post-install check: adb -s [device-serial] shell ls -la /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/*.db — a spatial database in the hundreds of KB rather than tens of MB means it has been replaced with an empty schema. Stop and restore rather than re-downloading over the top.
⚠️ Play Store vs local APK: DIFFERENT SIGNING KEYS, SAME PACKAGE NAME. Since the 07-26 package merge both are com.grouptrack.android, so a sideloaded build blocks the Play Store from installing or updating the app and vice versa (INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, or Play silently offers nothing). To move a device between the two you must UNINSTALL first — which wipes tiles and app data. Decide per device: sideload OR Play, not both.
Post-Install Steps
Launch GroupTrackGrant location permission when promptedOpen Planning Map and verify tile loading
First-Time Setup (do these in order)
Before your first ride, complete these three setup steps. For detailed, screen-by-screen walkthroughs with screenshots, open the in-app manual — tap the "?" icon anywhere in GroupTrack. The manual is cookbook-style (how you get there → what you do → where it leads); the steps below are the short version.
1. Settings → choose your map sources. Open Settings and select the map sources you want available. New installations use Google Hybrid for the satellite slot (SAT), with Esri Topographic (TOPO) and Esri USA Topo (TOPO+). Leave the defaults unless you have a reason to change them — these are what the download and map screens use. (Manual: "?" → Settings / Map Sources.)
⚠️ Upgrading testers: your satellite slot does NOT change. If you already have GroupTrack installed you keep whatever source you were using — the new default applies to fresh installations only, and nothing is downloaded or deleted behind your back. Google Hybrid is worth moving to: it carries roads and place names inside the satellite imagery, so it needs one tile store instead of three (Esri satellite needs two extra label stores) and shows street names offline. To switch, go to Settings → Map Sources → SAT and choose Google Hybrid; GroupTrack then walks you through what to do with the tiles you already stored. See Changing a map source below.
Changing a map source (SAT, TOPO or TOPO+)
Stored tiles came from the source that downloaded them and cannot be converted. When you change the source on a slot that already holds tiles, GroupTrack asks what to do with them.
⚠️ Please be advised: whichever option you choose, you lose Esri place and road label information. The new source does not fetch label overlays, so those label stores are removed either way — and their space (typically a few hundred MB) is reclaimed.
You will be asked to choose one of three:
Delete and start over — removes the stored maps for that slot and frees the space, so you can rebuild around your tracks. This cannot be undone and there is no backup. Your download history for that slot is cleared too, so note any areas you will want to redraw. Recommended when moving from Esri to Google Hybrid, unless you are already downloading by corridor.
Move everything to the new source — GroupTrack converts your existing maps in the background. All of the downloads are submitted at once and every image is slowly replaced from the new source, track maps first and then your areas. Your maps stay usable throughout. Best if you rely on road and place names. (Arriving shortly — not in this build.)
Move tracks and areas on my schedule — nothing is removed and nothing is downloaded. Your existing maps keep working, so you always have something to fall back on. Refresh ground as you need it from the downloads panel — by track, or by drawing an area — with Replace tiles ticked. Ground you have not refreshed stays without road and place names.
Nothing downloads automatically. When you are ready, use Download Tiles by Area or by Track. If you have imported tracks, downloading by corridor around those tracks is the better choice — it covers where you actually ride and uses roughly two thirds less storage than boxing the same ground by area. If you have no tracks yet, download by area and add corridors later; the two work together in the same store.
Your tracks, routes and trails are never affected — this only ever touches downloaded map tiles.
2. Import trails and trailheads, and DOWNLOAD MAPS for your ride area. Load the trail data for your riding area so trails and trailheads show on the map. Then, while on WiFi/cell, download the map tiles for the area you'll ride — use the Planning Map download and confirm the blue overlay covers your whole ride area. (Manual: "?" → Import Artifacts / Trail Sources, and Offline Maps &amp; Downloads.) If trails don't appear, see "Trail Display Issues" in Troubleshooting.
2b. Import OSM trail data (optional, and worth doing). GroupTrack can import free OpenStreetMap data for your state, which typically adds far more ground than the curated trail sources alone — for Utah, about 104,000 trails and unpaved roads against roughly 49,000 from the state source. It is a four-step process on one panel: Planning Map → Work with Artifacts → Import OSM Data.
DOWNLOAD — the panel opens the Geofabrik site in your browser. Choose your state and take the file ending in -latest-free.gpkg.zip (about 330 MB for Utah). ⚠️ The other formats on that page will download and then be rejected.CLICK HERE WHEN DOWNLOAD HAS COMPLETED — nothing happens automatically; GroupTrack does not watch your downloads folder. Tap the green bar and it finds the file.EXTRACT — unpacks and builds a trail database. Under a minute for most states.IMPORT — choose FULL STATE, or SELECTED AREA to draw a box on the map and take only what is inside it. The confirmation tells you how many trails are about to be added. There is no undo.CLEANUP — removes the working files. Not automatic; it waits for you.
Importing a state you already have is safe: it reports almost everything as dropped and adds nothing, so you will not get two copies of a trail.
(Manual: "?" → Planning Map → Work with Artifacts → Import OSM Data — an eight-screen walkthrough with captures of both the whole-state and drawn-area paths.)
⚠️ Downloading maps before you ride is REQUIRED for off-grid use. On the trail you are off the grid — no cell, no WiFi — so the app cannot fetch map tiles in the field. Any area you did not download ahead of time will show blank/grey on the trail. Download every area you plan to ride before you leave connectivity, and verify the blue overlay covers it. This applies to trails/trailheads too — import them ahead of time.
3. Set up the radio. Pair and connect the T1000-E (see Radio Setup below). Do this last, after maps and trails are in place. (Manual: "?" → Radio / Connection.)
Note for upgrading testers: if you're coming from a pre-V2.6 build, do the V2.6 One-Time Tile Migration (below) before step 2's tile downloads.
⚠️ V2.6 One-Time Tile Migration (upgrading testers)
V2.6 changes how offline map tiles are stored — from thousands of loose files to a single compact database per map type (about half the storage; satellite ~55% smaller, WebP-compressed). Old loose tiles must be cleared once and re-downloaded in the new format before maps will work.
Install X-plore File Manager (free, Play Store) — it shows a live progress count while deleting, so you always know it's working.In X-plore, go to Internal storage → Documents → GroupTrack → maps and delete the maps folder. A large old cache can take a while — keep the device plugged in; the on-screen count shows it's active.Back in GroupTrack, re-download your ride areas (by Area, or from a track/route). They save in the new format at roughly half the size.
Your tracks and routes are NOT affected — this clears only downloaded map tiles. This is one-time; future updates won't need it.
Radio Setup
Power on T1000-E radioVerify firmware is 2.6.11 or earlier — DO NOT UPDATEProgram the radio to the master config default. In GroupTrack, go to Convoy Map → Event Ride menu → Update Radio Config. This loads the T1000-E with the GroupTrack master configuration (the standard settings all convoy radios share) so your radio interoperates with the group. Do this before relying on the radio for a ride — a radio on different settings won't work with the convoy. (Manual: "?" → Radio / Connection.)Open GroupTrack → radio should appear in device listSelect radio to pairVerify connection: position icon, signal strength visible
Device Compatibility
Supported: Android 14 to 16 devices with a Bluetooth radio and a GPS chipset. Both are required — Bluetooth to hold the connection to the T1000-E radio, and an onboard GPS chipset for position. A device missing either (e.g. a Wi-Fi-only tablet with no GPS) is not compatible.
| Requirement | Needed | |-------------|--------| | Android version | 14, 15, or 16 | | Bluetooth | Required (BLE, to connect the T1000-E) | | GPS chipset | Required (onboard location) |
Known-incompatible pattern: budget tablets that lack a proper BLE radio (or a GPS chipset) cannot hold the connection to the T1000-E — symptom is a repeating connect/disconnect every 8–10 seconds (supervision timeout reason 0x0008). This is a hardware limitation of those devices, not an app bug; use a device meeting the requirements above.
TROUBLESHOOTING
BLE Connection Issues
Symptom: App freezes or pauses during ride
Cause: Radio moved beyond Bluetooth range (~50') while still connected. BLE supervision timeout.Fix: Force close GroupTrack. Move radio back within range of phone. Reopen app.Prevention: Keep radio mounted in cart with phone. They must stay within 50' of each other at all times during a ride.
Symptom: Radio connects then disconnects repeatedly (8-10 second cycle)
Cause: Device hardware incompatibility (Tab8NEU, budget Android tablets). Supervision timeout reason 0x0008.Fix: Use a compatible device (see Device Compatibility table above). This is a hardware issue, not an app bug.
Symptom: Radio won't connect at all after firmware update
Cause: T1000-E firmware updated beyond 2.6.11.Fix: Flash radio back to firmware 2.6.11 using Meshtastic Flasher tool. Do NOT use any firmware newer than 2.6.11.
Symptom: Radio connects but position doesn't update
Cause: Radio may be out of GPS fix, or BLE connection is degraded.Fix: Check radio has clear sky view for GPS. Force close and reconnect. Verify radio firmware is 2.6.11.
Map and Tile Issues
Symptom: Map shows blank/grey tiles
Cause: No tile cache for this area. Online tiles failed to load (no connectivity or tile source down).Fix: Check connectivity. Download tiles for this area while on WiFi. Check blue overlay on Planning Map to confirm tile coverage.
Symptom: Double labels on satellite map
Cause: Old cached tiles (from a hybrid URL) showing baked-in labels plus new overlay labels — typically pre-V2.6 tiles not yet migrated.Fix: Do the V2.6 one-time tile migration (Installation → V2.6 One-Time Tile Migration): delete the maps folder via X-plore and re-download. New-format tiles carry labels as a separate overlay, so the doubling goes away.
Symptom: Map tiles load online but show blank offline
Cause: Tiles not downloaded for this area.Fix: Before going to the field, download tiles for your ride area using Planning Map download function. Verify blue overlay covers your ride area.
Trail Display Issues
Symptom: No trails showing on map
Cause: No trail source downloaded, or trail database not loaded.Fix: Open Planning Map → Work with Artifacts → select and download a source (e.g., UGRC Utah Trails).
Symptom: Trails showing in wrong location
Cause: Coordinate system mismatch or corrupt GeoJSON source.Fix: Remove trail source and re-download/re-ingest.
App Issues
Symptom: App is slow or unresponsive on launch
Fix: Force close and reopen. If it keeps happening, report it to the GroupTrack team with your device model and what you were doing.
Symptom: Missing data after an update
Good news: Your saved content is stored outside the app. It always survives updates; on 2.6f and later it also survives a full uninstall and reinstall — recorded/imported tracks and routes (in Documents/GroupTrack/data/) and your downloaded map tiles (in Documents/GroupTrack/maps/) are kept.If maps look empty after a major update: you may need the one-time tile migration — see "V2.6 One-Time Tile Migration" in Installation.
⚠️ UPDATE FIRST — DO NOT UNINSTALL ON AN OLD BUILD.Before following any recovery step below, make sure you are on Rel 2.6f or later (Settings shows the release). On builds before 2.6f, uninstalling and reinstalling erased saved trails, tracks and waypoints — a one-time database upgrade step could not tell a reinstall from a brand-new install and cleared the databases. Downloaded map tiles were not affected. 2.6f fixes this, and also refuses to clear a database that still holds records. If you are on an older build, take the update from Play first — an update is safe and never triggered this.Emergency Recovery
If everything is broken:
Uninstall GroupTrackFlash the T1000-E to firmware 2.6.11Reinstall the APK with adb install -r (plain -r &mdash; do not add -d)Launch — spatial data in Documents/GroupTrack/ should still be thereReconnect the radioRe-download tiles if the cache was lost
⚠️ Your trails, tracks, routes and waypoints live in Documents/GroupTrack/ and on 2.6f and later they survive an uninstall — on earlier builds they did not, see the warning above. Downloaded map tiles do not survive an uninstall on any build.

GroupTrack — Quick Start, Installation &amp; Troubleshooting
Beta Tester Reference · Updated August 17, 2026 (V2.6f)
⚠️ UPDATE FIRST — DO NOT UNINSTALL ON AN OLD BUILD.
Before following any recovery step in this document, make sure you are on Rel 2.6f or later
(Settings shows the release). On builds before 2.6f, uninstalling and reinstalling erased saved
trails, tracks and waypoints — a one-time database upgrade step could not tell a reinstall from
a brand-new install and cleared the databases. Downloaded map tiles were not affected. 2.6f fixes
this, and additionally refuses to clear a database that still holds records. If you are on an
older build, take the update from Play first — an update is safe and never triggered this.
Which mode are you running?
GroupTrack works two ways. You do not need a radio to use the app. Pick the mode that
matches your situation — everything else in this document is the same for both.
1 · Solo mode — Android GPS DEFAULT
Your phone or tablet's own GPS provides your position. No Meshtastic radio, no Bluetooth
pairing, no radio firmware to worry about. You get offline maps, trail data, route planning and
track recording — everything except seeing other riders.
This is the default and it is what most testers should start with. If you have never used
GroupTrack before, use solo mode until you are comfortable with the app.
2 · Group mode — mesh radios OPTIONAL
Adds live tracking of everyone else in your convoy. Every rider you want to see needs their own
Meshtastic radio paired to their own device — the radios form the mesh that carries positions
where there is no cell signal.
Group mode is an addition to solo mode, not a replacement. Set the app up and get
comfortable first; add the radio afterwards. See Adding a radio below.
Device requirements
RequirementSolo modeGroup mode
Android version14, 15 or 1614, 15 or 16
Onboard GPS chipsetRequiredRequired
Bluetooth (BLE)Not neededRequired — to hold the radio connection
Free storagePlan on 50–60 GB if you download imagery for a large area
A Wi-Fi-only tablet with no GPS chipset cannot run GroupTrack in either mode. Budget tablets that
lack a proper BLE radio cannot hold a radio connection — see Troubleshooting.
FIRST RUN — do these steps in order
Steps 1–4 build on each other and should be done in order. Step 5 is optional. The in-app
manual is the reference throughout — this document tells you the order, the manual tells you the
detail.
Step 1 · Open the manual and get familiar with it
Open the manual from the "?" in the app and spend a few minutes on its structure —
what sections exist and roughly where things live. You are not reading it cover to cover. You are
learning where to look, because the next three steps each send you back to it.
Everything else in this quick start assumes you can find a topic in the manual when pointed at
one.
Step 2 · Import trails
Open the hamburger panel and go to the artifacts display — this is where trails,
tracks, routes and waypoints are managed.
Read the manual's "Import trails" section before you start. Then, in the app:
Select a source. Use the first entry — UGRC Utah Trails — as your starting point.
(This is the Utah Geospatial Resource Center's curated trail dataset.)
Validate the source.
Process the import.
This gives you a curated, agency-maintained trail set with use classifications — the coloured
trails you will see on the map. It is the smaller of the two trail sources but the better-described
one.
Step 3 · Import Open Source Maps (OSM) trail data
Look up the Open Source Maps import function in the manual first, then follow the prompts
and screens in the app. It is a four-stage process on a single panel and the app tells you what it
needs at each stage.
This adds substantially more ground than the curated source alone — for Utah roughly 104,000
trails and unpaved roads, against about 48,000 from the state source.
Two things the prompts will not tell you:
Take the file ending -latest-free.gpkg.zip (about 330 MB for Utah). The other
formats on that page will download and then be rejected.
When the download finishes, tap the green bar yourself. Nothing happens automatically —
GroupTrack does not watch your downloads folder.
Step 4 · Check your map source
Open the map source settings and confirm what you are using. The default values are chosen for
performance and usability — leave them alone unless you have a specific reason.
If you do change a source, the app will tell you what happens to any tiles you have already
downloaded. Read that screen rather than clicking through it.
Step 5 · Bring in your own tracks and waypoints OPTIONAL
If you already have riding history in onX, Gaia or another app, you can bring it
across. Nothing is lost by skipping this — but your own past rides are the most useful trail data
you own, because you know what they were like.
First, get the GPX files onto this device. Two routes, depending on where the other app
lives:
The other app is on this Android device — export to GPX from within it and download the
files here.
The other app is elsewhere (a different phone, a desktop) — export to GPX and
email the files to yourself as attachments, then open the mail on this device and download
them.
Either way the GPX files end up in this device's downloads. GroupTrack does not reach into onX or
Gaia — it reads files you have already put on the device.
Then import them:
Select Import artifacts. Your downloaded tracks will be listed.
Tick the tracks you want. You do not have to take everything you exported.
Tap Import selected at the bottom of the panel to process them.
Imported tracks behave like tracks you recorded yourself — they appear on the map, carry distance
and time, and can be used for planning.
After steps 1–4 you have the app, the manual, trail data from two sources, and a working
map — a complete solo-mode setup. Download map tiles for the area you ride and you are ready.
Step 5 is optional and can be done at any time, including months later.
Adding a radio OPTIONAL — GROUP MODE ONLY
Skip this entire section if you are running solo. Do it last, after maps and trails are in
place and you are comfortable with the app. The manual covers pairing under Radio /
Connection.
⚠️ T1000-E firmware: DO NOT update beyond 2.6.11.
T1000-E firmware must stay at 2.6.11 or earlier. Any newer version destabilises Bluetooth
connectivity and radio configuration — a known issue with newer Meshtastic firmware on this
hardware.
Check it in the Meshtastic app under Radio Config → Device Info. If it is 2.6.11 or
earlier, do not update. If it was updated by accident, flash back to 2.6.11 with the
Meshtastic Flasher tool. This applies to every T1000-E used with GroupTrack.
⚠️ Keep the radio within Bluetooth range during rides.
Keep your radio in your cart or vehicle, within about 50 feet of your phone, for the whole
ride. Carrying one away from the other breaks the Bluetooth link and the app will pause or freeze
until they are back in range.
Radio firmware reference
FirmwareStatusNotes
2.6.11✅ APPROVEDMaximum recommended version for T1000-E
2.6.12 and newer❌ DO NOT USEDestabilises BLE and radio configuration
Earlier than 2.6.11✅ OKWorks, but may lack features
Upgrading testers — one-time tile migration
Only if you are coming from a build earlier than V2.6. Do this before downloading any tiles.
V2.6 changed how offline tiles are stored — from thousands of loose files to one compact database
per map type, roughly half the storage (satellite about 55% smaller). Old loose tiles must be cleared
once and re-downloaded in the new format.
Install X-plore File Manager (free, Play Store). It shows a live progress count while
deleting, so you can see it working.
In X-plore go to Internal storage → Documents → GroupTrack → maps and delete the
maps folder. A large old cache takes a while — keep the device plugged in.
Back in GroupTrack, download the areas you need again. They are saved in the new format at
roughly half the previous size.
Your tracks, trails and routes are not affected — this clears downloaded map imagery only.
It is a one-time step; future updates will not need it.
TROUBLESHOOTING
Map and trail display
Trails do not appear. Check you completed Step 2 and Step 3 — with no trail import there is
nothing to draw. Then check your zoom level; trail detail appears as you zoom in.
Map is blank or grey offline. You have no downloaded tiles for that area at that zoom.
Download the area while you have a connection.
App behaviour
Missing data after an update. Your saved content is stored outside the app. It always
survives updates; on 2.6f and later it also survives a full uninstall and reinstall.
If trails or tracks are missing after an update, re-check the artifacts panel before assuming
loss — and see the warning at the top of this document if you are on an older build.
App asks for storage access on every launch. Grant "all files access" when asked.
GroupTrack keeps 50–60 GB of offline maps in shared storage so they survive updates and reinstalls,
which is why it needs that permission. Without it the app cannot open your maps, trails or tracks and
will not start.
Location prompt keeps appearing. If you skipped "allow all the time", GroupTrack reminds
you each launch. That is deliberate: without it, track recording stops when your screen
sleeps, and you will not find out until you get home to a short track. Grant it in Android
settings whenever you like.
Radio connection GROUP MODE ONLY
App freezes or pauses during a ride. The radio moved out of Bluetooth range while still
connected. Force close GroupTrack, bring the radio back within range, reopen. Prevention: radio
stays in the cart with the phone.
Radio connects then disconnects every 8–10 seconds. Device hardware incompatibility —
supervision timeout reason 0x0008, seen on budget tablets without a proper BLE radio.
Use a device that meets the requirements above. This is hardware, not an app bug.
Radio will not connect after a firmware update. Firmware went beyond 2.6.11. Flash back to
2.6.11 with the Meshtastic Flasher tool.
Emergency recovery
Check your version first. Everything below assumes 2.6f or later. On earlier builds
an uninstall erased saved trails, tracks and waypoints — take the update from Play before doing any
of this.
If the app is badly broken and an update has not fixed it:
Uninstall GroupTrack.
Reinstall from Play.
Grant all-files access when asked.
Launch. Your trails, tracks, routes and waypoints in Documents/GroupTrack/ will
still be there.
Downloaded map tiles do not survive an uninstall on any build — you will re-download those.
GroupTrack · Quick Start, Installation &amp; Troubleshooting · Updated August 17, 2026
(V2.6f)
Solo mode uses your Android GPS and needs no radio. Radios are optional and only add
multi-rider tracking. T1000-E firmware: lock to 2.6.11; radio stays in the cart during rides.

        IMPORT TRAILS
        Trail data has been assembled from a trusted group of public authorities. Some groups are regional or state-specific. Others are nationwide.
        We have crafted two import methods for you to identify the trails you may need.
        By source — Import by the source owner: Utah, USFS, BLM, and others.

        Browse the available sources to get comfortable with what they are and what they represent. Develop a strategy of which sources you want in their entirety and which areas you want to focus on.

(function(){
  var mode='Area';
  var data={Area:['Cedar City, UT','Cedar City Regional, UT','Cedar Fort, UT'],
            Track:['Cedar City to Newcastle','Old Irontown loop'],
            Route:['Sunday Desert Run'],
            Trail:['13th Hole','13th Hole','Jordan River Trail','Gooseberry Mesa'],
            Waypoint:['Gooseberry Trailhead','Water cache']};
  var $=function(id){return document.getElementById(id)};
  function step(t){$('step').textContent=t}
  function paint(){[].forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.chip'),function(c){
    c.classList.toggle('on',c.dataset.m===mode)});
    $('q').placeholder=mode==='Area'?'Search area (e.g. Cedar City)\u2026':'Search '+mode.toLowerCase()+' by name\u2026'}
  function openBar(){$('bar').classList.remove('hidden');$('list').classList.add('hidden');
    $('detail').classList.add('hidden');$('mapNote').textContent='';$('q').value='';$('q').focus();step('2 · pick type + type, enter')}
  function run(){$('bar').classList.add('hidden');step('3 · pick from matches');
    var items=data[mode]||[],seen={};
    $('rhead').textContent=items.length+' '+(mode==='Area'?'place':mode.toLowerCase())+' match'+(items.length===1?'':'es');
    $('rows').innerHTML=items.map(function(n){seen[n]=(seen[n]||0)+1;
      var dup=items.filter(function(x){return x===n}).length>1;
      var seq=dup?' #'+seen[n]+'':'';
      return ''+(mode==='Area'?'\u25C9 ':'\u203A ')+n+seq+''}).join('');
    $('list').classList.remove('hidden');
    [].forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.row'),function(b){b.onclick=function(){pick(b.dataset.n)}})}
  function pick(name){$('list').classList.add('hidden');
    if(mode==='Area'){$('mapNote').textContent='\u25CE centered on '+name;step('done · map recentered')}
    else{$('dName').textContent=name;$('dType').textContent=mode.toUpperCase();
      $('detail').classList.remove('hidden');step('done · detail open (FIT here)')}}
  $('fab').onclick=openBar;
  $('barX').onclick=function(){$('bar').classList.add('hidden');step('1 · tap the beacon')};
  $('dX').onclick=function(){$('detail').classList.add('hidden')};
  [].forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.chip'),function(c){c.onclick=function(){mode=c.dataset.m;paint()}});
  $('q').addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Enter')run()});
  $('reset').onclick=function(){$('bar').classList.add('hidden');$('list').classList.add('hidden');
    $('detail').classList.add('hidden');$('mapNote').textContent='';mode='Area';paint();step('1 · tap the beacon')};
  paint();
})();

⛔ Open tasks — UI data (finish these first; they complete the UI)
  Open · pick up first
  1 · FIT SEL/EDIT-panel row update (the one remaining FIT piece)
  Decision already made — implement Option B. No re-diagnosis needed.
    Symptom: FIT applies correctly (centers, selects, JSON perfect) but the SEL/EDIT panel is still open underneath. When that panel later closes, its launch-time state (all / none) takes precedence and overrides the FIT — the trail disappears or all artifacts show.
    Why: FIT never writes the panel's row state. A manual row-select writes it (proven: manually selecting the same row you just fitted works); FIT does not. The viewport query always runs and applies off/on/selected — FIT just never sets the panel row to SELECTED + the fitted id.
    Fix (Option B, chosen because it removes any user-interaction path that can break FIT state): on FIT / detail launch, close the SEL/EDIT panel and set its row + state to the one fitted artifact — i.e. selectedArtifactIds = setOf(fittedId) and activeListType = fittedType, plus showArtifactsPanel = false.
    Where: ConvoyScreen onOpenDetail ~line 1292 and ~1780 (both set pendingDetail* but never close the panel). Mirror the manual-select row write found in commit 35ccccc4a ~lines 1678-1679 (selectedArtifactIds = …; activeListType = typeName). Apply to both screens.
  Open
  2 · Widen artifact selection radius on the map (touch tolerance)
    Both map HTMLs use the default SVG renderer. Add renderer: L.svg({ tolerance: 12 }) to the L.map(...) call — one line per HTML (convoy_map.html and grouptrack_map.html). Widens the hit zone for all artifact taps. Tunable 12 → 15–18.
    Independent, low risk. Part of the "simple JS selection focus" change.
  Open
  3 · Trail info panel — display real data from the extension DB
    Current state: the map-tap popup shows "Unknown" for Surface / Uses / CartoCode. The map retrieve (queryTrailsByViewport → buildTrailGeoJson) reads only the spatial DB, where those property columns are blank. The real values (including carto_code) live in the extension DB trail_properties and are never retrieved by the map path.
    Approach (Fred's, additive — NOT a rewrite): after the existing spatial retrieve, additionally pull the wanted fields from trail_properties and emit them into the popup. Color the whole CartoCode line by carto code (mirror the 8-color cartoStyle in JS), trails only.
    Do not rewrite the working spatial retrieve; layer the extension lookup on top as a second step.
  Open · regression (new today)
  4 · Track arrows display when they shouldn't
    Symptom (new today, never before): track directional arrows still display when tracks are OFF, or when only one track is SELECTED. Arrows should show only when tracks show.
    convoy_map.html was not in today's commits, so the regression is either in how the Kotlin side calls track show/hide/update, or the arrow layer not being removed on hide.
    Next: read convoy_map.html ~lines 448–495 (trackArrows = L.polylineDecorator, showTracks/hideTracks/updateTracks). Confirm hideTracks removes trackArrows, and that updateTracks rebuilds arrows honoring the SELECTED filter (not all tracks). Not yet root-caused.

function showScreen(id) {
  document.querySelectorAll('.screen').forEach(s => s.classList.remove('active'));
  document.querySelectorAll('.nav-tab').forEach(t => t.classList.remove('active'));
  document.getElementById(id).classList.add('active');
  event.target.classList.add('active');
}
function showPanel(id) {
  // Hide all panels in current screen except display
  const screen = document.querySelector('.screen.active');
  screen.querySelectorAll('.panel').forEach(p => p.classList.remove('visible'));
  document.getElementById(id).classList.add('visible');
}
function hidePanel(id) {
  document.getElementById(id).classList.remove('visible');
}
function togglePanel(id) {
  document.getElementById(id).classList.toggle('visible');
}
function toggle(id) {
  const el = document.getElementById(id);
  el.style.display = el.style.display === 'none' ? 'block' : 'none';
}
function toggleAccordion(header) {
  const body = header.nextElementSibling;
  body.classList.toggle('open');
  const arrow = header.querySelector('span:last-child');
  arrow.textContent = body.classList.contains('open') ? 'v' : '>';
}
function setHud(mode) {
  // Hide all HUDs
  document.querySelectorAll('.hud-strip').forEach(h => h.classList.remove('visible'));
  document.querySelectorAll('.hud-btn').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
  hidePanel('c-cart-picker');
  if (mode === 'group') {
    document.getElementById('c-hud-group').classList.add('visible');
    document.getElementById('c-btn-group').classList.add('active');
  } else if (mode === 'mycart') {
    document.getElementById('c-hud-mycart').classList.add('visible');
    document.getElementById('c-btn-mycart').classList.add('active');
  } else if (mode === 'node') {
    document.getElementById('c-hud-node').classList.add('visible');
    document.getElementById('c-btn-select').classList.add('active');
  } else if (mode === 'hide') {
    document.getElementById('c-btn-hide').classList.add('active');
  }
}

E3. WRITE-FUNCTION DATA CONTRACT (so in-progress JSON mirrors it)
The completed-save consumes the RouteManager VERTEX chain (the only true source of shape). Each Vertex: lat, lon, lineId(String?), lineType(String?), segmentIndex(Int, -1 if free), t(Double 0..1), snapped(Boolean). It produces wkt + bbox via buildWktAndBbox and writes insertRoute(name,wkt,bbox...). The completed DB row stores ONLY wkt+bbox+name (resolved geometry) — it throws away HOW the route was built.
The DRAFT (in-progress) JSON must NOT throw that away — it stores the FULL vertex list so resume = true editing (undo to a snapped vertex, know which legs ride a trail, re-slice), not redrawing a frozen line. wkt is always re-derivable from vertices; the reverse is not. Draft schema (future build):
{ schemaVersion, draftId, name|null, createdAt, updatedAt, method,
  vertices:[ {lat,lon,lineId|null,lineType|null,segmentIndex,t,snapped}, ... ] }
  // NO wkt/bbox in draft — DERIVED at graduation by replaying buildWktAndBbox.
RESUME = parse → addVertex(Vertex(...)) each → drawBuildLine. GRADUATE = identical Build-1 onSaveCompleted path + delete draft JSON. The ONLY writes ever: create draft JSON (Save in-progress) · overwrite draft JSON (Save with changes) · insertRoute+delete-draft (Save as completed, graduation). A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both.
E4. ENGINE FRAMING (route creation is its OWN complex birth process)
STATES: Route(base) → New → In Progress → Completed. ACTIVITIES: Save, Discard (drive transitions). CONDITIONS: ≥2 pts? · new vs resumed · draft-on-disk? · delete-saved=NO · resave=YES may ALIAS per §K/§L. ACTIONS (reusable black boxes, params+execute): JSON write/open/delete · spatial-DB add/update/delete. Everything in-memory until deliberate Save. Each artifact has its OWN creation process — route is the COMPLEX one (heavy human contact); importing a trail / dropping a waypoint / recording a track are different. Completed tracks have their own lifecycle too (later).

E3. WRITE-FUNCTION DATA CONTRACT (in-progress JSON mirrors it)
Completed-save consumes the RouteManager VERTEX chain (only true source of shape). Vertex: lat, lon, lineId(String?), lineType(String?), segmentIndex(Int,-1 free), t(0..1), snapped(Bool). Produces wkt+bbox → insertRoute. Completed DB row stores ONLY wkt+bbox+name — throws away HOW it was built.
DRAFT JSON must NOT — stores the FULL vertex list so resume = true editing (undo to a snapped vertex, know which legs ride a trail, re-slice), not a frozen line. wkt re-derivable from vertices; reverse not. Schema (future):
{ schemaVersion, draftId, name|null, createdAt, updatedAt, method,
  vertices:[ {lat,lon,lineId|null,lineType|null,segmentIndex,t,snapped}, ... ] }
  // NO wkt/bbox — DERIVED at graduation by replaying buildWktAndBbox.
RESUME = parse → addVertex each → drawBuildLine. GRADUATE = identical Build-1 save path + delete draft. ONLY writes ever: create draft JSON · overwrite draft JSON · insertRoute+delete-draft. A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both.
E4. ENGINE FRAMING
STATES: Route(base)→New→In Progress→Completed. ACTIVITIES: Save, Discard. CONDITIONS: ≥2 pts? · new vs resumed · draft-on-disk? · delete-saved=NO · resave=YES may ALIAS (§K/§L). ACTIONS (black boxes, params+execute): JSON write/open/delete · spatial-DB add/update/delete. In-memory until deliberate Save. Each artifact has its OWN birth process — route is the COMPLEX one; trail-import / waypoint-drop / track-record differ. Completed tracks have their own lifecycle (later).

E5. SHARED TABLE RULE (folded from Decision Log §4.4/4.6, rules 32-33)
Tracks and routes share ONE table with a TYPE field (TRACK/ROUTE). "All imports are TRACKS, always. Convert-to-route is an explicit, REVERSIBLE type flip." source_track_id links a converted track to its route. Implication for snap-2: our insertRoute writes a row of type ROUTE in that shared table; route dedup therefore rides the same geom_hash/UNIQUE machinery as tracks (§K). Route delete is BLOCKED if type=ROUTE and assigned to an active ride with enrollments (V3.0 concern, not 2.5). Identity = geometry; display names in aliases.

P. Data Protection — backup / journal / rollback (deferred V2.5 schema spec)
Deferred (schema-hardening subsystem, not snap-2). Full spec: GroupTrack_V25_DataProtection_v1 (archived). Three layers on grouptrack_user.spatialite: (1) Backup — auto on launch + before destructive ops; last 5 retained; /Documents/GroupTrack/data/backups/. (2) Change journal — every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on user tables (waypoints/routes/tracks/ride_areas), before+after state as JSON, geometry as WKT, 12 triggers, 30-day retention. (3) Rollback — single-op undo, transaction rollback, point-in-time; creates backup first. Relevance to routes: when route create/edit/delete is journaled, the before/after must store geometry as WKT (matches our write-contract's vertex→wkt derivation). E3. ROUTE LIFECYCLE — SETTLED MODEL (Item 1 — ready to build)
Full spec: RouteLifecycle_SETTLED_DESIGN_2026-06-05. Reflects all 2026-06-05 simplifications.
Core rules:
R1 Either/or — a route is EITHER an in-progress draft (JSON) OR a completed DB row, never both; graduation writes the row + deletes the draft.
R2 Identity — in-progress identity = the typed NAME (set at New); route id assigned ONLY at graduation under DB dedup rules.
R3 Save exits — every save EXITS route mode; to continue editing, Save In Progress then RE-SELECT from the In-Progress list. NO mid-session "save &amp; continue", NO in-place state promotion.
R4 State fixed at launch — New ⇒ NEW whole session; Select In-Progress ⇒ RESUMED whole session. The entry row is the launch fork that sets the state the adaptive screens read.
R5 Writes minimal — only create-draft, overwrite-draft, insertRoute(+delete-draft), delete-draft. Roll-back / discard-new / cancel NEVER write.
R6 Both maps — ConvoyScreen (LF) + ConvoyMapViewerScreen (CRLF), shared RouteManager; toolbar CRLF; cat -A before every patch.
R7 Vertices not wkt — draft stores the full vertex chain; wkt/bbox derived at graduation (resumed draft graduates through the IDENTICAL completed-save path).
Save/Discard placement: on the COLLAPSED title bar (one-tap access, no real-estate cost) AND in the expanded panel. Each is ONE entry point opening an adaptive SCREEN; choices driven by fixed launch state.
Adaptive SAVE screen — NEW: [Save completed (≥2 pts, LIVE)] · [Save in-progress → writeDraft, exit (SOON)] · [Cancel]. RESUMED: [Graduate (+deleteDraft) (SOON)] · [Save with changes → overwriteDraft, exit (SOON)] · [Cancel].
Adaptive DISCARD screen — NEW: [Discard &amp; exit (LIVE, no write)] · [Keep building]. RESUMED: [Roll back = reload unchanged draft, no write (SOON)] · [Delete in-progress = deleteDraft (SOON)] · [Keep building].
Add ↔ Method coupling (CONFIRMED): Add is DEFAULT GREEN/on entering BOTH New and In-Progress. ASYMMETRIC — turns OFF/RED ONLY when Draw or Suggest is selected (no manual turn-off); the ONLY manual action is tapping Add to turn it back ON, reclaiming control from Draw/Suggest. Add = "design-control-is-here" indicator, NOT a free toggle.
SOON — Patch 1 (UI-first) routeState (NEW|RESUMED + name) · adaptive Save/Discard SCREENS · Save/Discard on collapsed bar · EMULATED Select-In-Progress (hardcoded list + vertex chain). All store calls STUBBED (log). Files: ConvoyRouteToolbar (CRLF) + ConvoyScreen (LF) + ConvoyMapViewerScreen (CRLF). Walk the ✓-stub checklist rows on BOTH maps.
SOON — Patch 2 Real RouteDraftStore.kt (Context-holding; RouteManager stays pure): writeDraft(name,vertices,method) · overwriteDraft · listDrafts→[{name,updatedAt,pointCount}] · openDraft(name)→{vertices,method} (resume AND roll-back) · deleteDraft(name). Storage /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/route_drafts/&lt;name&gt;.json; atomic temp+rename. JSON {schemaVersion,name,createdAt,updatedAt,method,vertices[…]} — no id, no wkt. Swap stubs for real calls; verify round-trip via logcat.
SOON — Patch 3 Wire graduate-delete + Discard-delete + roll-back-reload to real store. Full end-to-end, both maps.
OPEN — decide before functions (a) duplicate-name policy for drafts (block / overwrite / disambiguate-file); (b) Discard-on-NEW acts directly vs confirm prompt; (c) In-Progress over-limit threshold if any.
E4. WRITE-FUNCTION DATA CONTRACT
Completed-save consumes the RouteManager VERTEX chain. Vertex: lat, lon, lineId(String?), lineType(String?), segmentIndex(-1 free), t(0..1), snapped(Bool). Completed DB row stores ONLY wkt+bbox+name. DRAFT JSON stores the FULL vertex list (resume = true editing), NOT wkt. RESUME = parse→addVertex→drawBuildLine. GRADUATE = Build-1 save path + delete draft. A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row. Full spec: RouteWriteFunction_DataContract_2026-06-04.
E5. SHARED TABLE RULE
Tracks + routes share ONE table with a TYPE field (TRACK/ROUTE). insertRoute writes type=ROUTE; route dedup rides the same geom_hash/UNIQUE machinery as tracks (§K add-core bypass). Convert-to-route = reversible type flip; source_track_id links a converted track to its route. Route delete BLOCKED if type=ROUTE and assigned to an active ride with enrollments (V3.0 concern, not 2.5).
E6. FILE-ENDING FACTS

O. Standing Rules (pointer — full list in archived docs)
54 numbered Standing Rules live in MasterPlan + Decision Log (May 17), archived. Highlights: 1 never auto-delete user data (explicit confirm) · 2 never embed API keys · 3 share opt-in only · 4 offline-first · 26 schema hardened before app code · 28 patch scripts uniquely versioned · 29 never commit V3_FEATURES_ENABLED/V25_SPATIAL_ENABLED=true · 30 preserve full trail geometry precision (snap-to depends on it) · 31 impact analysis before ANY change · 32-33 all imports are tracks; tracks/routes share table · 43 NO MediaStore queries · 54 one comprehensive patch per agreed design. Full text: search Drive "MasterPlan" / "DecisionLog".
P. Data Protection — backup / journal / rollback (deferred V2.5 schema spec)
Deferred (schema-hardening subsystem, not snap-2). Full spec: GroupTrack_V25_DataProtection_v1 (archived). Three layers on grouptrack_user.spatialite: (1) Backup — auto on launch + before destructive ops; last 5 retained; /Documents/GroupTrack/data/backups/. (2) Change journal — every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on user tables, before+after as JSON, geometry as WKT, 12 triggers, 30-day retention. (3) Rollback — single-op undo, transaction rollback, point-in-time; creates backup first. Relevance to routes: when route create/edit/delete is journaled, before/after stores geometry as WKT (matches the write-contract's vertex→wkt derivation). NOT journaled: trail data (re-downloadable), transfer queue. Rules 23-25.

Picker-refresh (2c) bumps draftListTick on open so new/deleted drafts show in-session. Roll-back = reload draft + redraw + KEEP building.
  Repo is 3 commits ahead of origin/feature/convoy-event-ride (lifecycle work) — unpushed. Push at a convenient checkpoint.
B. Snap-2 — CONVOY MAP: DONE &amp; PROVEN ON DEVICE
  WIN Snap-2 now traces the route along trail/track geometry on the convoy map (ConvoyScreen.kt). Confirmed three ways: logcat (tracedLen grows far faster than vertex count as consecutive same-line snapped points fill in trail geometry — one run snapped 5→6 jumped tracedLen 709→2802 = a long trail slice; the pts= arrays contain intermediate trail vertices, not just taps), on-screen, and reproduced via undo/repost.
  What was wrong &amp; what fixed it
    Confirmed (branch A): snap COMPUTES &amp; STORES correctly. Draft JSON had vertices with "snapped":true, real lineId, lineType, segmentIndex, interpolation t. buildSegments() (RouteManager.kt:218) genuinely traces — walks consecutive pairs, sameLine = a.snapped &amp;&amp; b.snapped &amp;&amp; same lineId, slices the underlying line via sliceLine using pos=segmentIndex+t. Its ONLY caller was buildWktAndBbox (save-completed) — the draw paths bypassed it.
    Fix: the live draw now runs the snapped vertices through buildSegments against the viewport geometry, swaps [lon,lat]→[lat,lon], and feeds drawBuildLine. Patched block: addVertex(v); val pts = withContext(IO){ init; queryTrails+TracksByViewport; byId(trail_id/track_id→geometry); buildSegments{ lineId→byId[lineId]?.let{ parseWktLine } }.joinToString swap [lat,lon] }; drawBuildLine(pts).
    TWO handlers, both patched: ConvoyScreen has two onMapTap — site 544 in the if(existing != null) persistent-WebView branch, and site 694 in the else/factory branch. Fresh map sessions run the FACTORY (694) handler — patching 544 alone did nothing visible; the 694 patch is what made it work. (Recurring "two handlers" trap.) Patches: patch_v25_trailtrace_site1_544_v6.py, patch_v25_trailtrace_site2_694_v1.py.
  Behavior notes (not bugs)
    Snap catch-rate depends on ZOOM — radius is hardcoded 30.0 m real-world; zoomed out (~¼ mile) almost nothing snaps, zoomed in it catches reliably.
    Trace only draws between TWO CONSECUTIVE snapped vertices on the SAME line — isolated or cross-line snapped points draw straight to their neighbors, by design.
  Diagnostic logs retained in committed code: tracedLen at ConvoyScreen ~555 and S2 tracedLen at ~716. Harmless Log.d; strip at AAB prep (see §E).
C. Snap-2 + Undo — PLANNING MAP: NEXT (must work before AAB)
  NEXT ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt is the PLANNING map. Solving the convoy map did NOT solve this — separate onMapTap + draw per file (shared RouteManager/SpatialDbManager, separate display). TWO problems:
  C-1 · Snap-2 trace not working on planning map
    All planning-map draw sites still use RAW routeVertices().joinToString chords: 498 (onMapTap live), 982 (undo redraw), 1040 (rollback rbPts), 1075 (resume rsPts — call is setRouteMode(true); drawBuildLine(...)).
    Fix: mirror the convoy-map trace (withContext IO → query viewport → byId → buildSegments → swap → drawBuildLine) to these sites. Per-file indentation differs (dialogs nest deeper here). Confirm endings via raw Python rb read before patching (see §D).
  C-2 · Undo does not remove segments on planning map
    Undo handler at 981–983 LOOKS correct: RouteManager.undoVertex() → rebuild pts → redraw. Resume at 1072 DOES call RouteDraftStore.loadIntoRouteManager(d) (which clearRoute() + addVertex per vertex), so the builder list IS populated on resume — so "empty vertices" is NOT the obvious cause.
    MIXED SIGNALS to resolve first: Fred reported undo "does not remove segments" on a resumed in-progress route (opened with all its points), but ALSO that undo "works on new trails." RE-TEST cleanly next session: (1) New route on planning map → tap → undo (works?). (2) Resume a draft → undo (works?). That fork tells us undo-broken-generally vs undo-broken-only-after-resume.
