GroupTrack — User Manual (V2.5)
Cookbook style. Each section is one screen; every function on that screen is documented in place. The ? help icon on a screen deep-links to that screen's section here.
V2.5 · 2026-06-18 · Online edition: grouptrack.org/manual · Bundled offline copy ships in-app · Sections map 1:1 to the screens that carry a ? help icon.
How help links work: tapping ? on a screen opens this manual at that screen's section (the anchors below — #planning-map, #convoy-map, #radio-write, #artifacts). V2.5 scope for the ? icon: the screens that persist into 3.0 — Planning Map, Convoy Map (incl. the Meshtastic connection/monitoring panel), and the Convoy radio-write menu. The goal in 3.0 is ? on every screen.
Sections
1. Planning Map — explore trails, build routes, import/manage artifacts off-radio
2. Convoy Map — live group tracking + Meshtastic connection &amp; monitoring panel
3. Convoy Radio-Write Menu — apply / archive / restore radio config transitional, supported in V2.5
4. Work with Artifacts — trails, tracks, waypoints, routes (display, select/edit, create)
1 · Planning Map
Screen: Planning Map · ? help anchor: #planning-map
The Planning Map is the off-radio workspace: explore downloaded trails, import your track history, build and save routes, and manage what's displayed — all without a radio connected. It shares the spatial database and route engine with the Convoy Map, but keeps its own display state.
Map basics
Pan / zoom: drag to pan, pinch to zoom. These stay live at all times, even while building a route.
Base layers (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+): switch imagery from the layer control. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available.
Viewport-aware display: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes load for the area you're viewing. Zoom in to see more detail; the display fills in as you move.
Displaying trails, tracks, waypoints, routes
See Section 4 (Work with Artifacts) — the toggle/select/edit controls are shared and documented there.
Too many trails in view: if the current view contains more trails than can be displayed at once, the SEL/Edit control indicates "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." Zoom in to narrow the area until trails become selectable. guidance behavior — coming
Building a route
See the full cookbook entry in Section 4 → Creating a Route. Route building works identically on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Importing trails / tracks
Import tracks (GPX): bring in your recorded track history. Large files import via streaming; duplicates (same geometry) are skipped automatically, and a recap shows new vs. already-in-library.
Import trails by area: draw an area to list and download trail sources overlapping it. processing fix in progress
Coming: waypoint and route extraction from GPX (all GPX imports are currently treated as tracks); GPX/KML open-with handler.
2 · Convoy Map
Screen: Convoy Map (incl. Meshtastic connection / monitoring panel) · ? help anchor: #convoy-map
The Convoy Map is the live group-tracking screen used during a ride. It shows your position and the positions of other riders relayed over the Meshtastic LoRa mesh, plus the same trail/track/waypoint/route display and route-building tools as the Planning Map.
Connecting to your radio (connection &amp; monitoring panel)
Connect: open the connection panel and pair your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E) over Bluetooth. The panel shows connection state.
Monitoring: the panel reports link status and node activity. Use it to confirm the mesh is up before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
Live tracking
Rider positions: other riders appear as node markers, updated as mesh packets arrive.
Your position: driven by the phone GPS once location permission is granted.
Waypoints
Drop a waypoint: long-press the map to drop a waypoint pin.
Pin shape: waypoints display as teardrop pins — the pin's point marks the exact location you dropped it. Each waypoint type has its own color and icon.
Proximity: waypoints within 100 m are treated as the same location.
Help on this screen
? help: tap the ? button on the Convoy Map to open the release notes or the full user manual. (The same help is on the Planning Map; both open the same documents.)
Download QUEUES (tile downloads)
QUEUES: opens the live download monitor (top-right) showing tile-download progress.
Building a route on the Convoy Map
Identical to the Planning Map — see Section 4 → Creating a Route.
3 · Convoy Radio-Write Menu (Apply / Archive / Restore)
Screen: Convoy menu — radio configuration · ? help anchor: #radio-write
Transitional — current and supported in V2.5. These radio-configuration functions are how radio writes happen this release. They are slated to be replaced in 3.0, but they work now and you should use them. This manual fully covers them; the 3.0 manual will rewrite this section when the functions change.
Apply Convoy Config (write to radio)
Connect the radio first (Section 2 connection panel) — the write action is unavailable with no Bluetooth link.
Open the Convoy menu → radio configuration.
Review the config values (channel, encryption keys, device settings). Values are validated before writing.
Apply. The write proceeds screen-by-screen / in passes through the config groups; confirm each completes.
Field validation: the config is validated (e.g. full field check) before programming. A two-pass programming approach is used so all config groups are written and confirmed.
Archive radio config
Save the current working radio configuration so it can be restored later. Use this before making changes.
Restore radio config
Re-apply a previously archived configuration to the connected radio.
Coming (replaces this menu in a future build): a screen-by-screen radio-config writer that mirrors each Meshtastic config screen, pre-populated and read-only, with a PROCEED button that is disabled (red) until the radio is connected (then green), saving after each screen through all config groups.
4 · Work with Artifacts
Screen: Work with Artifacts (shared by both maps)
"Work with Artifacts" is the control center for everything you display and create on the map: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes. The toggle and select/edit controls are the same on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Display toggles (ON / OFF / SELECTED)
ON: show all artifacts of that type in view.
OFF: hide that type.
SELECTED: show only the items you've checked in that type's select/edit list.
Select / Edit list (per type)
Open a type's SEL/Edit list to check individual items for SELECTED display, or to open an item's detail.
Search by name: choose an artifact type, type a name, and press Enter to find matching trails, tracks, waypoints, or routes by name across your whole database (not just what's on screen). Search is case-insensitive and matches partial names. Tap a result to open its detail. new in this build
Item detail: tapping an item's name (from a search result or the select/edit list) opens its detail card. The left side lists the actions available for that item's type; the right side shows the item's information. For trails this includes designated uses, surface type, classification (carto code), county, managing agency, and data source. Less-used technical values — bounding coordinates, created/updated dates, and the geometry hash — are tucked under a ▸ technical toggle so the useful information shows first; tap it to expand. Where a trail has alternate names on record, they appear here too. On the Convoy Map the detail is view-only; full editing is on the Planning Map.
FIT (fit to map): from an item's detail card, tap FIT to frame that item on the map. The map flies to the item and zooms to fit it, the item is selected and drawn on its own, and the other artifact types are turned off — so you see just the one you picked. Works for trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes, on both maps. FIT is how you go from finding a name to seeing it on the map.
List limit: the list currently shows up to 200 items. paging — coming
Trails over-limit: when more trails are in view than can be shown, SEL/Edit shows "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." coming
Track display
Tracks display as dashed green lines from your device's spatial database. When Tracks are on, each track shows direction-of-travel arrows along the line so you can read which way it runs — useful for telling a single looping track from two overlapping ones. The arrows are evenly spaced on screen and stay readable as you zoom, and are drawn in the same neon green as the track.
Routes display
Routes display as magenta lines, loaded from your device's spatial database the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Build a route with + ROUTE (see Creating a Route). (Importing routes from GPX, and the Draw / Suggest build methods, are coming in upcoming updates.)
Creating a Route (early access)
A route is a planned path you build by tapping the map, then save with a name for later use. Route building works on both the convoy map and the planning map.
Open the map (convoy or planning).
Open "Work with Artifacts" and tap + ROUTE. The Route+ toolbar appears.
Tap New. A "Name this route" box appears with a suggested name — accept it or type your own — then start building.
Add is on by default (green): tap the map to drop points. If a trail or track is nearby, the point snaps to it and the magenta route line follows the trail's actual shape between your points — so the route traces real trails instead of cutting straight across. Tap away from any trail to place a free point exactly where you tapped. Tip: zoom in while building for the most reliable snapping.
Use Undo to remove the most recent point.
Pan and zoom freely between taps to position the map.
Tap Save to store the route. It is saved on your device, redraws on the map in magenta, and appears in Work with Artifacts → Routes under the name you gave it.
Tap Discard to leave without saving.
Coming next (not in this build):
Save In Progress / Resume: save a half-finished route and re-open it later to keep editing (the "In Progress" entry).
Draw and Suggest build methods (placeholders today).
Renaming/editing a saved route from the Routes list (route maintenance).
Route maintenance (rename, edit geometry, delete a completed route) lives in Work with Artifacts → Routes (SEL/Edit), not in the Route+ toolbar. The toolbar is for building only.
Track / Trail / Waypoint maintenance
Per-type maintenance (rename, detail, delete) is reached from each type's SEL/Edit list. trail/route/waypoint maintenance — in progress
Unnamed trails display as "Not Named." consistent labeling — being aligned at import
Manual maintenance note (internal): when a screen's functions change AND are complete, update that screen's section here and re-point its ? help anchor. Transitional radio-config sections (Section 3) are removed/rewritten in the 3.0 manual when those functions are replaced.

GroupTrack — User Manual (V2.5)
Cookbook style. Each section is one screen; every function on that screen is documented in place. The ? help icon on a screen deep-links to that screen's section here.
V2.5 · 2026-06-18 · Online edition: grouptrack.org/manual · Bundled offline copy ships in-app · Sections map 1:1 to the screens that carry a ? help icon.
How help links work: tapping ? on a screen opens this manual at that screen's section (the anchors below — #getting-started, #planning-map, #convoy-map, #artifacts, #radio-write). V2.5 scope for the ? icon: the screens that persist into 3.0 — Planning Map, Convoy Map (incl. the Meshtastic connection/monitoring panel), Work with Artifacts, and the Convoy radio-write menu. The goal in 3.0 is ? on every screen.
About the screen images: each chapter opens with an image of that landing screen — the screen you navigate from to reach its functions. Images show the landing screen, not every individual tap. (Image slots are marked below with their filenames; capture each screen and save it under the filename shown to drop it in.)
Contents
1. Getting Started — install, trails, map sources, radio
  1.1 Installing the software
  1.2 Downloading trails
  1.3 Adding / updating map sources
  1.4 Adding / updating trail sources
  1.5 Setting up your radio (optional)
2. Planning Map — explore trails, build routes, import/manage artifacts off-radio
3. Convoy Map — live group tracking + Meshtastic connection &amp; monitoring panel
4. Work with Artifacts — trails, tracks, waypoints, routes (display, select/edit, create)
5. Convoy Radio-Write Menu — apply / archive / restore radio config transitional, supported in V2.5
1 · Getting Started
First-time setup, in order. Do these once before your first ride; trail and tile data then persist on the device.
This chapter walks first-time setup from a fresh install through optional radio pairing. Each step persists: once you've imported trails and downloaded map tiles, they stay on the device across app updates and restarts — you don't redo this before every ride.
Draft note (remove before publish): the procedures in this chapter are drafted from current app behavior and prior notes. Steps marked [verify] need a confirming pass on the device to lock exact button labels / order before this ships to testers.
1.1 · Installing the software
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Install / first launchgs_install.png
Updating from an earlier version? Install as an update through the Play Store — do not uninstall the old version and clean-install, which breaks the installation. After updating, on first launch the trail/track database is rebuilt: re-import your trails (1.2), and your recorded tracks return automatically from your saved GPX files (open the track import screen and tap RESYNC TRACKS if any are missing).
Install GroupTrack from the Play Store internal-testing link the organizer sent you. [verify exact install path for testers]
Open the app. Grant the permissions it requests — location (for your position on the map) and storage/files (for trail data and map tiles). On first launch the app prepares its on-device databases.
If this is a fresh device (not an update), there is no trail data yet — continue to 1.2 to import trails for your area.
Requirements: Android 8.0+ (a tablet is recommended for map work). ~500 MB+ free for map tiles; trail data is roughly 15–30 MB per state. A radio (Meshtastic SenseCAP T1000-E or a LoRa device on firmware 2.6+) is only needed for convoy tracking, not for maps. Internet is needed once, to import trails and download tiles.
1.2 · Downloading trails
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail import (source / area)gs_download_trails.png
What you're doing: trail data is no longer bundled with the app. You import the trails for the regions where you ride, once, and they become permanent on your device.
Open the Planning Map.
Open Work with Artifacts and tap Import Trails. The trail source list appears.
Choose a method:
  Import by Source — select a land-management agency dataset (e.g. UGRC Utah Trails — ~49,000 trails + ~591 trailheads).
  Import by Area — draw a box on the map and see the sources that overlap it, with overlap percentages. processing fix in progress
On the validation screen, review the trail count and file size, then confirm to download. Trails and trailhead waypoints download as artifacts.
Fully close the app (force stop) and reopen so the new trail data loads.
If imported trails don't show: (1) fully close and reopen the app so trail data loads; (2) zoom in — trails draw at zoom level 8 and above, so a large dataset only appears when you're zoomed in enough. This is intentional for performance.
Full detail in Chapter 4 (Work with Artifacts).
1.3 · Adding / updating map sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Map sources / tile settingsgs_map_sources.png
What you're doing: map sources are the base imagery behind your trails (satellite, topo, outdoor, etc.). V2.5 offers 16 sources across 6 categories, and any source can be assigned to any of the three toolbar slots (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+).
Open Settings &gt; Map Sources. [verify menu path]
For each toolbar slot (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+), choose which of the 16 sources to assign.
For premium sources that require an API key (e.g. Thunderforest), enter the key when prompted; keys are stored locally on the device.
Changing a source triggers a background tile refresh for the new imagery.
Offline tiles: download tiles while you have internet so they're cached for offline use in the field. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available. See the Download Queue (Chapter 3) for managing tile downloads.
1.4 · Adding / updating trail sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail source cataloggs_trail_sources.png
What you're doing: beyond your first import (1.2), you can add more trail sources as you ride new areas, or update existing ones. Multiple sources and agencies can be active at once.
Open Work with Artifacts → Import Trails to return to the trail source catalog.
Add a source: pick another agency dataset (by source) or draw a new area (by area) and import, exactly as in 1.2.
Update a source: re-importing a source you already have is de-duplicated — trails already on the device are recognized and skipped, so re-import is safe and only adds what's new. [verify trail-source re-import dedupe state]
Agencies: UGRC Utah Trails is the first catalog source; BLM and USFS are planned.
1.5 · Setting up your radio (optional)
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Radio setup / pairinggs_radio_setup.png
What you're doing: the radio is only needed for live convoy tracking — maps, trails, and routes all work without it. If you're riding solo or just planning, you can skip this.
Power on your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E).
Open the Convoy Map and open the connection panel (Chapter 3). Pair the device over Bluetooth; the panel shows connection state.
Apply the convoy radio configuration so all riders share the same channel and encryption — see Chapter 5 (Convoy Radio-Write Menu): Apply / Archive / Restore.
Confirm the mesh is up in the monitoring panel before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
2 · Planning Map
Screen: Planning Map · ? help anchor: #planning-map
SCREEN IMAGE — Planning Map (landing)planning_map.png
The Planning Map is the off-radio workspace: explore downloaded trails, import your track history, build and save routes, and manage what's displayed — all without a radio connected. It shares the spatial database and route engine with the Convoy Map, but keeps its own display state.
Map basics
Pan / zoom: drag to pan, pinch to zoom. These stay live at all times, even while building a route.
Base layers (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+): switch imagery from the layer control. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available. (Assign sources to these slots in Settings &gt; Map Sources — see 1.3.)
Viewport-aware display: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes load for the area you're viewing. Zoom in to see more detail; the display fills in as you move.
Displaying trails, tracks, waypoints, routes
See Chapter 4 (Work with Artifacts) — the toggle/select/edit controls are shared and documented there.
Too many trails in view: if the current view contains more trails than can be displayed at once, the SEL/Edit control indicates "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." Zoom in to narrow the area until trails become selectable. guidance behavior — coming
Building a route
See the full cookbook entry in Chapter 4 → Creating a Route. Route building works identically on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Importing trails / tracks
Import tracks (GPX): bring in your recorded track history. Large files import via streaming; duplicates (same geometry) are skipped automatically, and a recap shows new vs. already-in-library.
Import trails by area: draw an area to list and download trail sources overlapping it. processing fix in progress
Coming: waypoint and route extraction from GPX (all GPX imports are currently treated as tracks); GPX/KML open-with handler.
3 · Convoy Map
Screen: Convoy Map (incl. Meshtastic connection / monitoring panel) · ? help anchor: #convoy-map
SCREEN IMAGE — Convoy Map (landing)convoy_map.png
The Convoy Map is the live group-tracking screen used during a ride. It shows your position and the positions of other riders relayed over the Meshtastic LoRa mesh, plus the same trail/track/waypoint/route display and route-building tools as the Planning Map.
Connecting to your radio (connection &amp; monitoring panel)
Connect: open the connection panel and pair your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E) over Bluetooth. The panel shows connection state.
Monitoring: the panel reports link status and node activity. Use it to confirm the mesh is up before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
Live tracking
Rider positions: other riders appear as node markers, updated as mesh packets arrive.
Your position: driven by the phone GPS once location permission is granted.
Waypoints
Drop a waypoint: long-press the map to drop a waypoint pin.
Pin shape: waypoints display as teardrop pins — the pin's point marks the exact location you dropped it. Each waypoint type has its own color and icon.
Proximity: waypoints within 100 m are treated as the same location.
Help on this screen
? help: tap the ? button on the Convoy Map to open the release notes or the full user manual. (The same help is on the Planning Map; both open the same documents.)
Download QUEUES (tile downloads)
SCREEN IMAGE — Download Queues monitorqueues_download.png
QUEUES: opens the live download monitor (top-right) showing tile-download progress.
Manage the queue: hold (pause all processing, resume when ready), cancel a single entry, or cancel all. Downloaded tiles are preserved when you cancel a partial download.
Building a route on the Convoy Map
Identical to the Planning Map — see Chapter 4 → Creating a Route.
4 · Work with Artifacts
Screen: Work with Artifacts (shared by both maps)
SCREEN IMAGE — Work with Artifacts panel (landing)work_with_artifacts.png
"Work with Artifacts" is the control center for everything you display and create on the map: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes. The toggle and select/edit controls are the same on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Display toggles (ON / OFF / SELECTED)
ON: show all artifacts of that type in view.
OFF: hide that type.
SELECTED: show only the items you've checked in that type's select/edit list.
Select / Edit list (per type)
Open a type's SEL/Edit list to check individual items for SELECTED display, or to open an item's detail.
Search by name: choose an artifact type, type a name, and press Enter to find matching trails, tracks, waypoints, or routes by name across your whole database (not just what's on screen). Search is case-insensitive and matches partial names. Tap a result to open its detail.
Item detail: tapping an item's name (from a search result or the select/edit list) opens its detail card. The left side lists the actions available for that item's type; the right side shows the item's information. For trails this includes designated uses, surface type, classification (carto code), county, managing agency, and data source. Less-used technical values — bounding coordinates, created/updated dates, and the geometry hash — are tucked under a ▸ technical toggle so the useful information shows first; tap it to expand. Where a trail has alternate names on record, they appear here too. On the Convoy Map the detail is view-only; full editing is on the Planning Map.
FIT (fit to map): from an item's detail card, tap FIT to frame that item on the map. The map flies to the item and zooms to fit it, the item is selected and drawn on its own, and the other artifact types are turned off — so you see just the one you picked. Works for trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes, on both maps. FIT is how you go from finding a name to seeing it on the map.
List limit: the list currently shows up to 200 items. paging — coming
Trails over-limit: when more trails are in view than can be shown, SEL/Edit shows "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." coming
Track display
Tracks display as dashed green lines from your device's spatial database. When Tracks are on, each track shows direction-of-travel arrows along the line so you can read which way it runs — useful for telling a single looping track from two overlapping ones. The arrows are evenly spaced on screen and stay readable as you zoom, and are drawn in the same neon green as the track.
Routes display
Routes display as magenta lines, loaded from your device's spatial database the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Build a route with + ROUTE (see Creating a Route). (Importing routes from GPX, and the Draw / Suggest build methods, are coming in upcoming updates.)
Creating a Route (early access)

Open the map (convoy or planning).
Open "Work with Artifacts" and tap + ROUTE. The Route+ toolbar appears.
Tap New. A "Name this route" box appears with a suggested name — accept it or type your own — then start building.
Add is on by default (green): tap the map to drop points. If a trail or track is nearby, the point snaps to it and the magenta route line follows the trail's actual shape between your points — so the route traces real trails instead of cutting straight across. Tap away from any trail to place a free point exactly where you tapped. Tip: zoom in while building for the most reliable snapping.

Pan and zoom freely between taps to position the map.
Tap Save to store the route. It is saved on your device, redraws on the map in magenta, and appears in Work with Artifacts → Routes under the name you gave it.

5 · Convoy Radio-Write Menu (Apply / Archive / Restore)
Screen: Convoy menu — radio configuration · ? help anchor: #radio-write
SCREEN IMAGE — Convoy Radio-Write menu (landing)radio_write.png
Transitional — current and supported in V2.5. These radio-configuration functions are how radio writes happen this release. They are slated to be replaced in 3.0, but they work now and you should use them. This manual fully covers them; the 3.0 manual will rewrite this section when the functions change.
Apply Convoy Config (write to radio)
Connect the radio first (Chapter 3 connection panel) — the write action is unavailable with no Bluetooth link.
Open the Convoy menu → radio configuration.
Review the config values (channel, encryption keys, device settings). Values are validated before writing.
Apply. The write proceeds screen-by-screen / in passes through the config groups; confirm each completes.
Field validation: the config is validated (e.g. full field check) before programming. A two-pass programming approach is used so all config groups are written and confirmed.
Archive radio config
Save the current working radio configuration so it can be restored later. Use this before making changes.
Restore radio config
Re-apply a previously archived configuration to the connected radio.
Coming (replaces this menu in a future build): a screen-by-screen radio-config writer that mirrors each Meshtastic config screen, pre-populated and read-only, with a PROCEED button that is disabled (red) until the radio is connected (then green), saving after each screen through all config groups.

SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail import (source / area)gs_download_trails.png
What you're doing: trail data is no longer bundled with the app. You import the trails for the regions where you ride, once, and they become permanent on your device.
Open the Planning Map.
Open Work with Artifacts and tap Import Trails. The trail source list appears.
Choose a method:
  Import by Source — select a land-management agency dataset (e.g. UGRC Utah Trails — ~49,000 trails + ~591 trailheads).
  Import by Area — draw a box on the map and see the sources that overlap it, with overlap percentages. processing fix in progress
On the validation screen, review the trail count and file size, then confirm to download. Trails and trailhead waypoints download as artifacts.
Fully close the app (force stop) and reopen so the new trail data loads.
If imported trails don't show: (1) fully close and reopen the app so trail data loads; (2) zoom in — trails draw at zoom level 8 and above, so a large dataset only appears when you're zoomed in enough. This is intentional for performance.
Full detail in Chapter 4 (Work with Artifacts).
1.3 · Adding / updating map sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Map sources / tile settingsgs_map_sources.png
What you're doing: map sources are the base imagery behind your trails (satellite, topo, outdoor, etc.). V2.5 offers 16 sources across 6 categories, and any source can be assigned to any of the three toolbar slots (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+).
Open Settings &gt; Map Sources. [verify menu path]
For each toolbar slot (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+), choose which of the 16 sources to assign.
For premium sources that require an API key (e.g. Thunderforest), enter the key when prompted; keys are stored locally on the device.
Changing a source triggers a background tile refresh for the new imagery.
Offline tiles: download tiles while you have internet so they're cached for offline use in the field. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available. See the Download Queue (Chapter 3) for managing tile downloads.
1.4 · Adding / updating trail sources
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Trail source cataloggs_trail_sources.png
What you're doing: beyond your first import (1.2), you can add more trail sources as you ride new areas, or update existing ones. Multiple sources and agencies can be active at once.
Open Work with Artifacts → Import Trails to return to the trail source catalog.
Add a source: pick another agency dataset (by source) or draw a new area (by area) and import, exactly as in 1.2.
Update a source: re-importing a source you already have is de-duplicated — trails already on the device are recognized and skipped, so re-import is safe and only adds what's new. [verify trail-source re-import dedupe state]
Agencies: UGRC Utah Trails is the first catalog source; BLM and USFS are planned.
1.5 · Setting up your radio (optional)
SCREEN IMAGE — Getting Started: Radio setup / pairinggs_radio_setup.png
What you're doing: the radio is only needed for live convoy tracking — maps, trails, and routes all work without it. If you're riding solo or just planning, you can skip this.
Power on your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E).
Open the Convoy Map and open the connection panel (Chapter 3). Pair the device over Bluetooth; the panel shows connection state.
Apply the convoy radio configuration so all riders share the same channel and encryption — see Chapter 5 (Convoy Radio-Write Menu): Apply / Archive / Restore.
Confirm the mesh is up in the monitoring panel before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
2 · Planning Map
Screen: Planning Map · ? help anchor: #planning-map
SCREEN IMAGE — Planning Map (landing)planning_map.png
The Planning Map is the off-radio workspace: explore downloaded trails, import your track history, build and save routes, and manage what's displayed — all without a radio connected. It shares the spatial database and route engine with the Convoy Map, but keeps its own display state.
Map basics
Pan / zoom: drag to pan, pinch to zoom. These stay live at all times, even while building a route.
Base layers (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+): switch imagery from the layer control. Tiles are served from your offline cache when available. (Assign sources to these slots in Settings &gt; Map Sources — see 1.3.)
Viewport-aware display: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes load for the area you're viewing. Zoom in to see more detail; the display fills in as you move.
Displaying trails, tracks, waypoints, routes
See Chapter 4 (Work with Artifacts) — the toggle/select/edit controls are shared and documented there.
Too many trails in view: if the current view contains more trails than can be displayed at once, the SEL/Edit control indicates "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." Zoom in to narrow the area until trails become selectable. guidance behavior — coming
Building a route
See the full cookbook entry in Chapter 4 → Creating a Route. Route building works identically on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Importing trails / tracks
Import tracks (GPX): bring in your recorded track history. Large files import via streaming; duplicates (same geometry) are skipped automatically, and a recap shows new vs. already-in-library.
Import trails by area: draw an area to list and download trail sources overlapping it. processing fix in progress
Coming: waypoint and route extraction from GPX (all GPX imports are currently treated as tracks); GPX/KML open-with handler.
3 · Convoy Map
Screen: Convoy Map (incl. Meshtastic connection / monitoring panel) · ? help anchor: #convoy-map
SCREEN IMAGE — Convoy Map (landing)convoy_map.png
The Convoy Map is the live group-tracking screen used during a ride. It shows your position and the positions of other riders relayed over the Meshtastic LoRa mesh, plus the same trail/track/waypoint/route display and route-building tools as the Planning Map.
Connecting to your radio (connection &amp; monitoring panel)
Connect: open the connection panel and pair your Meshtastic device (e.g. T1000-E) over Bluetooth. The panel shows connection state.
Monitoring: the panel reports link status and node activity. Use it to confirm the mesh is up before relying on positions.
Device compatibility: some budget Android devices cannot hold a stable Bluetooth link to the radio (the connection drops after several seconds). If positions stop updating and the panel shows repeated disconnects, the device may be incompatible — see the tester compatibility list.
Live tracking
Rider positions: other riders appear as node markers, updated as mesh packets arrive.
Your position: driven by the phone GPS once location permission is granted.
Waypoints
Drop a waypoint: long-press the map to drop a waypoint pin.
Pin shape: waypoints display as teardrop pins — the pin's point marks the exact location you dropped it. Each waypoint type has its own color and icon.
Proximity: waypoints within 100 m are treated as the same location.
Help on this screen
? help: tap the ? button on the Convoy Map to open the release notes or the full user manual. (The same help is on the Planning Map; both open the same documents.)
Download QUEUES (tile downloads)
SCREEN IMAGE — Download Queues monitorqueues_download.png
QUEUES: opens the live download monitor (top-right) showing tile-download progress.
Manage the queue: hold (pause all processing, resume when ready), cancel a single entry, or cancel all. Downloaded tiles are preserved when you cancel a partial download.
Building a route on the Convoy Map
Identical to the Planning Map — see Chapter 4 → Creating a Route.
4 · Work with Artifacts
Screen: Work with Artifacts (shared by both maps)
SCREEN IMAGE — Work with Artifacts panel (landing)work_with_artifacts.png
"Work with Artifacts" is the control center for everything you display and create on the map: trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes. The toggle and select/edit controls are the same on the Planning Map and the Convoy Map.
Display toggles (ON / OFF / SELECTED)
ON: show all artifacts of that type in view.
OFF: hide that type.
SELECTED: show only the items you've checked in that type's select/edit list.
Select / Edit list (per type)
Open a type's SEL/Edit list to check individual items for SELECTED display, or to open an item's detail.
Search by name: choose an artifact type, type a name, and press Enter to find matching trails, tracks, waypoints, or routes by name across your whole database (not just what's on screen). Search is case-insensitive and matches partial names. Tap a result to open its detail.
Item detail: tapping an item's name (from a search result or the select/edit list) opens its detail card. The left side lists the actions available for that item's type; the right side shows the item's information. For trails this includes designated uses, surface type, classification (carto code), county, managing agency, and data source. Less-used technical values — bounding coordinates, created/updated dates, and the geometry hash — are tucked under a ▸ technical toggle so the useful information shows first; tap it to expand. Where a trail has alternate names on record, they appear here too. On the Convoy Map the detail is view-only; full editing is on the Planning Map.
FIT (fit to map): from an item's detail card, tap FIT to frame that item on the map. The map flies to the item and zooms to fit it, the item is selected and drawn on its own, and the other artifact types are turned off — so you see just the one you picked. Works for trails, tracks, waypoints, and routes, on both maps. FIT is how you go from finding a name to seeing it on the map.
List limit: the list currently shows up to 200 items. paging — coming
Trails over-limit: when more trails are in view than can be shown, SEL/Edit shows "Too many trails in view — zoom in to reduce." coming
Track display
Tracks display as dashed green lines from your device's spatial database. When Tracks are on, each track shows direction-of-travel arrows along the line so you can read which way it runs — useful for telling a single looping track from two overlapping ones. The arrows are evenly spaced on screen and stay readable as you zoom, and are drawn in the same neon green as the track.
Routes display
Routes display as magenta lines, loaded from your device's spatial database the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Build a route with + ROUTE (see Creating a Route). (Importing routes from GPX, and the Draw / Suggest build methods, are coming in upcoming updates.)
Creating a Route (early access)
A route is a planned path you build by tapping the map, then save with a name for later use. Route building works on both the convoy map and the planning map.
Open the map (convoy or planning).
Open "Work with Artifacts" and tap + ROUTE. The Route+ toolbar appears.
Tap New. A "Name this route" box appears with a suggested name — accept it or type your own — then start building.
Add is on by default (green): tap the map to drop points. If a trail or track is nearby, the point snaps to it and the magenta route line follows the trail's actual shape between your points — so the route traces real trails instead of cutting straight across. Tap away from any trail to place a free point exactly where you tapped. Tip: zoom in while building for the most reliable snapping.
Use Undo to remove the most recent point.
Pan and zoom freely between taps to position the map.
Tap Save to store the route. It is saved on your device, redraws on the map in magenta, and appears in Work with Artifacts → Routes under the name you gave it.
Tap Discard to leave without saving.
Coming next (not in this build):
Save In Progress / Resume: save a half-finished route and re-open it later to keep editing (the "In Progress" entry).
Draw and Suggest build methods (placeholders today).
Renaming/editing a saved route from the Routes list (route maintenance).
Route maintenance (rename, edit geometry, delete a completed route) lives in Work with Artifacts → Routes (SEL/Edit), not in the Route+ toolbar. The toolbar is for building only.
Track / Trail / Waypoint maintenance
Per-type maintenance (rename, detail, delete) is reached from each type's SEL/Edit list. trail/route/waypoint maintenance — in progress
Unnamed trails display as "Not Named." consistent labeling — being aligned at import
5 · Convoy Radio-Write Menu (Apply / Archive / Restore)
Screen: Convoy menu — radio configuration · ? help anchor: #radio-write
SCREEN IMAGE — Convoy Radio-Write menu (landing)radio_write.png
Transitional — current and supported in V2.5. These radio-configuration functions are how radio writes happen this release. They are slated to be replaced in 3.0, but they work now and you should use them. This manual fully covers them; the 3.0 manual will rewrite this section when the functions change.
Apply Convoy Config (write to radio)
Connect the radio first (Chapter 3 connection panel) — the write action is unavailable with no Bluetooth link.
Open the Convoy menu → radio configuration.
Review the config values (channel, encryption keys, device settings). Values are validated before writing.

GroupTrack &mdash; EOD Handoff2026-07-27 &middot; INTERNAL &middot; OSM trail import BUILT &middot; 106,879 trails staged offline &middot; AllDocs root cause fixed &middot; commit 7e2173da2
Read with GroupTrack_workplan_2026-07-28.html. Everything below is committed and pushed; working tree is clean.
&#11088;&#11088; THE ARCHITECTURE DECIDED AT END OF DAY (Fred) &mdash; TWO-TIER STAGING
Fred: "end with an import spatial DB we can use the download map regions tools to draw areas to be imported from second spatial DB."
A STAGED reference DB sits on the device; the LIVE spatial DB holds only what the user deliberately pulls. The user draws an area with the existing region tools and imports just that area's trails across.
&#11088; This solves the volume problem outright. 106,879 trails never need to land in grouptrack_spatial.db &mdash; so the worry about tripling the viewport bbox-scan working set disappears. The full state costs disk, not query time.
The subset schema ALREADY supports it: every row carries min_lat/max_lat/min_lon/max_lon with a bbox index, so an area query against the staged DB is fast. Built for the import step; exactly what this needs.
It also makes the 50-state ambition clean &mdash; each state is another staged file and nothing changes app-side. Fred: "we need a process that is repeatable for other states &hellip; identify the state, download and process without intervention." DISCUSS AFTER the three states are imported.
&#9989; STAGED AND READY &mdash; 106,879 TRAILS, OFFLINE
file (on D:)trailssizedupes pruned
osm_trails_utah.db87,533108 MB2,021
osm_trails_az_strip.db10,71412.3 MB7
osm_trails_nv_corner.db8,6327.9 MB41
TOTAL106,879~128 MB
Against 49,125 UGRC trails today. Source: Geofabrik -latest-free.gpkg.zip per state, subset by osm_gpkg_subset_v2_2026-07-27.py.
&#11088; DEDUP MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Utah: 9 hash matches out of 89,554. AZ and NV: ZERO. So OSM and UGRC are INDEPENDENT SURVEYS, not a shared import &mdash; which was genuinely open this morning. Name-matches (same trail, two drawings) were 2,021 / 7 / 41 and are all pruned. Fred: "skip the 2000+ trails identified as dupes, not worth the hassle when we are talking about 120,000 trails."
&#9888; The hash only catches BYTE-IDENTICAL geometry. Independent surveys of the same trail produce different WKT and therefore different hashes &mdash; dedup is blind to them. That is why name-matching was used as the second filter, and why the pruning happened on the laptop rather than being left to the app.
&#11088; THE FINDING THAT MATTERS &mdash; and the cost of the Geofabrik path
OSM is the ONLY source in the database carrying motorized_allowed. Measured on the live DB:
source_id          rows    motorized  surface  uses   carto
osm_trails            9        7         0       7       0
nps_public_trails    18        0        18      18      18
ugrc_utah_trails  49,098        0    49,098  44,583  49,098
UGRC has 49,098 trails and not one carries a motorized value. Neither does NPS. For an OHV app that reframes OSM from a coverage supplement into the only source of legal-access data.
&#9888; BUT THAT FIELD DOES NOT SURVIVE THE GEOFABRIK PATH. The free roads layer columns are osm_id, code, fclass, name, ref, oneway, maxspeed, layer, bridge, tunnel &mdash; confirmed against the real file. No motor_vehicle / atv / 4wd_only / surface at any price (surface is commercial-only; the access tags do not exist in either tier).
What is gained instead: fclass carries track_grade1..5, real OHV difficulty data, and it is present on every track rather than sparsely tagged. Utah: track 49,499 &middot; grade5 9,840 &middot; grade3 5,507 &middot; grade2 3,868 &middot; grade4 3,479 &middot; grade1 327 &middot; path 15,563 &middot; bridleway 1,471.
&#9940; motorized_hint in the subset is INFERRED from fclass &mdash; a track is physically wide enough for a vehicle, a footway is not. That is PHYSICAL CAPABILITY, NOT LEGAL ACCESS. It sits in its own column so it can never be mistaken for the real field. Do not map it onto motorized_allowed without deciding, deliberately, that an inference is acceptable there.
&#128295; WHAT SHIPPED IN CODE (commit 7e2173da2)
Patch R &mdash; OSM as trail source #9. sourceType on Src (defaulted arcgis_rest, so all 8 existing entries untouched), buildUrl branches to Overpass, response transform, catalog entry. &#11088; Fred's insight made it small: buildUrl appends f=geojson, so nothing Esri-specific is in the RESPONSE, only the QUERY STRING &mdash; insertFeature and everything below it stayed untouched.
Patch S &mdash; Overpass gets a 180s read timeout; ArcGIS keeps 60s. The first import died at exactly 60s while the server was still working.
Patch T &mdash; an Overpass source with no bbox is now REFUSED. It used to default to -90,-180,90,180 and ask for every track and path on Earth. Harmless for ArcGIS (it pages and the server caps records); catastrophic for Overpass. A default meaning "everything" is only safe when the consumer is bounded.
Patch U &mdash; reverted a name fallback I should never have added. SpatialDbManager.notNamed() (:1297) already turns blank into the 'Not Named' SENTINEL for all four artifact types, and search deliberately EXCLUDES it (:422). My synthesized "OSM track 12345678" looked real, so search would have INCLUDED it &mdash; filling results with numeric IDs. Check whether the shared core already applies a fallback before adding one.
Patch V &mdash; httpGet now logs the HTTP code, the server's error body, and the exception CLASS. This was the most valuable thing built today (see below).
launchMode fix &mdash; the execute button at MVS:1608 wrote the pending area but never set launchMode = BY_AREA, so the trail screen opened on SELECT_SOURCE and ignored the bbox just written. The panel callback at :1711 always did it. Pre-existing and invisible, because for ArcGIS a missing bbox degrades into an ordinary full-source import.
Re-selectable sources &mdash; B2 blocked already-imported sources three ways; A1 was fixed for this in 60a7c6de2 and B2 never was. Also isSourceFullyImported now requires trail_count &gt; 0: three FAILED runs had marked OSM permanently imported.
&#128196; ALLDOCS &mdash; ROOT CAUSE FOUND AFTER TWO WEEKS
Not one HTML doc had ever reached GroupTrack_AllDocs.txt. Every section marker was === GroupTrack_*.docx ===; zero HTML markup anywhere.
Cause: Step 4's HTML-folding loop (added in V13) was CORRECT &mdash; but Steps 2/3 copy into $DOCS with the glob "$DOWNLOADS"/GroupTrack*."$ext", and bash globs are CASE-SENSITIVE. Filenames like grouptrack_*, SCOPING_*, BLUEPRINT_* matched none of it. V13 fixed the folding; the copy filter silently starved it.
Fixed via patches O &rarr; P &rarr; Q: collect by EXTENSION not name prefix (a prefix whitelist is the same bug in a new coat), drop json, exclude the script's own generated outputs (a stale Downloads copy would CLOBBER the fresh xref), skip (n) duplicates, 10 MB cap, 45-day recency window.
&#9940;&#9940; SECURITY INCIDENT ALONG THE WAY. Patch P removed the name filter with NOTHING in its place, so the sweep committed and pushed ngrok_recovery_codes.txt, MySQL connection details and a personal PDF in 151fffb79. Removed from HEAD in ddb48650b; STILL PRESENT IN THAT COMMIT'S HISTORY. &#9888; REVOKE THE NGROK CODES if not already done, and decide separately about scrubbing history with filter-repo. Patch Q added a hard secrets gate (ngrok/mysql/credential/password/secret/token/apikey/recovery/regform/.pem/.jks/.p12/.env/id_rsa), logged when it fires.
&#9888; After the first successful backlog run, drop DOC_MAX_AGE_DAYS from 45 to ~14 &mdash; older files will already be tracked.
&#9888; WHAT WENT WRONG TODAY, AND WHY (worth not repeating)
&#11088; THE SINGLE BIGGEST CAUSE: every HTTP failure looked identical. httpGet read only inputStream, which THROWS on any non-2xx, and logged ex.message &mdash; which for several common exceptions IS THE URL. So a timeout, a rate limit, a rejected query and an OOM all produced the same line. Overpass had been explaining itself in the response body the whole time, into a stream never opened.
The moment patch V landed, the answer appeared immediately: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout &mdash; "Dispatcher_Client::request_read_and_idx::timeout. The server is probably too busy." Nothing was broken after the launchMode and bbox fixes; the public Overpass instances were simply overloaded all afternoon.
&#9940; I switched the endpoint to kumi.systems on a hunch that it was the faster mirror. It refused every request for hours. Overpass Turbo then answered the SAME query against the main endpoint in seconds. Changing a working default on an untested assumption cost most of the afternoon.
&#9940; I sized cells from one bad sample. A 63-second query on a congested server became "3-mile cells", which for Utah is 29,299 cells. The real capacity, measured in the browser: 2,658 ways over 900 square miles in a couple of seconds. ~640&times; the area I had assumed was the limit.
&#9940; I chased alternatives for an hour &mdash; PBF (needs a node index; no maintained Android library), Bunting Labs (right shape, EXPIRED CERTIFICATE on the endpoint), BBBike (right output, request-and-email). Fred's original instinct &mdash; bulk extract, process locally &mdash; was correct; I just picked a QUERY api when the job needed an EXTRACT service.
&#9888; My laptop certificate failures were REAL but unrelated &mdash; Python (stale CA bundle), curl (HTTP 000), Chrome (ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID on buntinglabs). Clock was correct. Android uses the system trust store and was unaffected throughout.

✅ CLOSED 07-23 — the 62K/152-job investigation (segmentation was NEVER the bug)
RESOLVED A logcat trace of the tester's 10-track import (3 sources → 215 queued) proved every segmentation split was mathematically correct: sizeTiles 894507→18 cells · 550635→12 · 505047→11 · 388032→8 · 361305→8 · 226395→5 · 218007→5 · 72018→2 · 60057→2 · 43509→1 — all satisfy ceil(sizeTiles/50000). Segments = 72 per source × 3 = 216 ≈ the 215 observed, so the job count is fully explained. Single-track re-test: track 1 alone, 3 sources → 54 queued, exactly as predicted (18×3).
⭐ THE REAL FINDING — the bbox is the wrong MODEL for a line feature. Track 1 is a single path ~100 miles long with a ~10-mile spread at the top ("like a figure 7") and alone accounted for 22% of all tiles in the group. Its bbox is ~100×10 miles while the ridden corridor is ~half a mile wide — the enclosing rectangle is ~95% empty desert. Fred: "8 hours to download an area that will not be ridden." → see the two new open items below.
Four theories died on inspection today — the "two unsegmented bypasses" (downloadMapsForTrackHash has ZERO callers, it's dead code); "satLayers doesn't resolve at import time" (getDownloadSources() calls ensureInit(), it's self-initialising); "imports use the old 12-mile calc"; and "the tracks are bigger than Fred thinks". Lesson: isolate with DATA, not theory.
⛔ My SIZECALC logging patch is BROKEN — fix before relying on it. It applied and built, but every value printed as literal text (sizeTiles=$sizeTiles) because I wrote ${'$'} escapes into the Kotlin. Fix: emit plain $slotName. The pre-existing SEGMENT logs are what actually carried the data. Backup at ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt.bak_20260723_134052.

The ceiling is enforced against sizeTiles = quickEstimate × satLayers, but each entry's totalTiles is calculateTiles(cell) × slotLayers — two separate calculations that can disagree (~23%). To confirm: one entry's N/S/E/W + totalTiles, recompute for that box.

🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #1 — TURN OFF MAP REFRESH ON SOURCE CHANGE (do first)
DO FIRST stop-the-bleeding, not a root-cause fix
What happened (07-23, on the shipped 2.6c build)
The REPLACE/refresh function on the map-source select screen “does not behave”: it spawned 3287 downloads in the queue, lat/long spanning the whole continental US. Downloads then stopped working entirely (“system just sits”).
⚠ Cancel All does NOT persist. Cancel appeared to clear the queue, but all 3287 jobs resurfaced on restart — the clear happens in memory and is never written to disk, so loadQueue re-reads the stale file every launch. This is the boot-loop mechanism, demonstrated — just without a crash.
⛔ No recovery path exists on a release build. adb run-as = access denied (debuggable only). X-plore CANNOT reach Android/data/com.geeksville.mesh/ and offers no grant option — Android 13+ removed third-party file-manager access to Android/data entirely; MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE explicitly excludes it and the document-tree picker refuses it. Only root, adb-on-debuggable, or the app itself can read there. The only escape is Clear-App-Data.
Resolution this time: the queue eventually drained on its own (ended at 4 entries processing normally). App data was NOT cleared — but the queue file was never inspected, so the bad bbox was never captured.
The decision (Fred 07-23)
Turn off the JSON write / auto-refresh when a map source is changed. Refresh becomes manually requested as an Area download — which rides the already-hardened submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells path. This removes the thing that spawned 3287 entries without needing the bounds bug diagnosed first.
Build notes
Scope it first: sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt (the enqueueRefresh call site at :271) and the state at :81-83 (refreshSlot / refreshTileCount / refreshEnqueued). Determine whether refresh fires AUTOMATICALLY on source selection or sits behind a button — that decides whether to gate the call or disable the control.
DISABLE, don't delete. Gate it behind a clearly-marked constant or comment it out. The bug is still undiagnosed and the path will be wanted when it's revisited — deleting now means reconstructing later.
⚠ This does NOT fix Cancel All. The persistence failure is a separate defect: any future bad queue still resurrects on restart. Turning off refresh removes the most likely source of a bad queue and buys time; it does not close the hole.
⛔ DO NOT run replace-map-source again until this ships — recovery costs an hour and possibly all app-internal data.
Root cause still open (for when it's revisited)
Leading hypothesis, unverified: the bbox handed to enqueueRefresh is not the user's viewport — a default/zero-initialised value, or swapped bounds arguments. Bounds-order is already the standing suspect for the “map REFRESH no longer works” regression; these may be one defect. Note 3287 ≈ ceil(enormous/50K) — segmentation worked correctly on garbage input, so the bug is upstream of segmentCells. Compare sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt against sed -n '218,250p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt side by side for argument order. Also read sed -n '440,490p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt — :473 declares val bad = File(..., "download_queue/" + QUEUE_FILE), suggesting some quarantine handling already exists, and it is likely the same function where cancel's persistence is failing.
🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #2 — RECOVERY SYSTEM FOR APPLICATION-PROTECTED DATA (the “Repair Area”)
NEW 07-23 full design below — buildable
Why this exists
07-23 proved that bad on-disk state in filesDir is unreachable AND unrecoverable on a release build except by Clear-App-Data. The app itself has unrestricted access to its own filesDir — the OS only blocks other apps — so the escape hatch must be built INTO GroupTrack.
⭐ What actually lives in filesDir (inventory built 07-23 from xrefs)
PathPurposeSourceLoss if wiped
download_queue/download_queue.jsontile download queueConvoyDownloadQueue:444/461, QUEUE_FILE:86none — rebuildable
convoy_apply_list.jsonradio apply listConvoyApplyList:107/110/133low
convoy_users.jsonuser recordsConvoyUser:113/119/133meaningful
master_config.jsonT1000-E MASTER radio configConvoyMasterConfig:152/217; MasterCapture:557meaningful
convoy_backups/&lt;id&gt;/per-radio config backupsConvoyRadioManager:34/146; ViewModel:266HIGH
convoy_rides/ride recordsConvoyViewModel:273meaningful
convoy_events/event configsConvoyEventConfig:176/178meaningful
convoy_profiles/&lt;file&gt;radio profilesConvoyProfileBuilder:212meaningful
convoy_import/, docType import dirsimport stagingViewModel:345; FileReceiver:74/87none — transient
cacheDir/*.gpx, transfer filestemp export/transferTrackOps:684; TransferRide:65none
⭐⭐ KEY CONSEQUENCE: filesDir holds radio configs, radio backups, users, rides and events — not just the queue. Clear-App-Data is NOT a clean fallback: it destroys every radio backup and the master config alongside the bad file. (Tracks and TILES survive — they live outside app storage in Documents/GroupTrack/data/ and /maps/.) This is exactly why per-file repair is worth far more than a reset button.
Design — the flow
Password gate. Threat model is NOT snooping — it's a tester deleting the wrong thing while following phone instructions, or tapping through out of curiosity. A build-time constant checked against a text field is sufficient (anything in the APK is extractable; the gate exists to make the action deliberate).
Test for repair-area existence FIRST. If one exists → WARN + DISPLAY CONTENTS, and allow adding a new (different) item.
Extract — ONE ENTITY AT A TIME via file picker. NO MASS COPY (“that is too scary”). Each extract writes TWO copies: the working file into the repair area (Downloads), and a pristine pre-edit snapshot into the dated archive.
Edit the file in the repair area, with normal tools.
Copy back AS A GROUP (see below), then remove the repair area.
State rules
NO REPLACEMENT of an already-staged item without an EXPLICIT DELETE. Re-extracting the same filename is REFUSED — it would silently overwrite the working copy (and any editing done) with a fresh pull from filesDir. The repair area is effectively append-only; removal is always a deliberate act.
DISPLAY what's staged. CANCEL-AND-RETURN discards the repair area, writes nothing to filesDir — and KEEPS the dated archive (an abandoned repair still leaves evidence of the original state).
⭐ The repair area is a HOLDING area — copy-back is GROUPED
Items are staged across separate one-at-a-time extracts, and the contents are copied back as a group — the staged set is the unit of repair. Extraction is one-at-a-time; restoration is grouped. Rationale: related files that must change together (users + rides, or a config + its backup) would leave inconsistent intermediate state if restored individually.
⭐ Archive naming + retention
Archived files are DATE AND TIME STAMPED — a unique occurrence per extract — held 30 days. Timestamp (not just date) so two repairs of the SAME file on the SAME day cannot collide or silently overwrite each other; every extract is its own recoverable point-in-time snapshot. Mirror the filesDir structure so different files can't collide either:
Documents/GroupTrack/saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json
⭐ The retention sweep runs ON APP OPEN, EVERY OPEN — not on repair-screen entry. A phone that did one repair months ago must not quietly hold stale copies forever just because nobody revisits the screen. Keep it cheap, non-blocking, and fail-safe — a sweep error must NEVER block or crash startup.
⭐⭐ The manifest JSON — work order + audit record
Finishing a repair writes/updates a manifest saying “apply this repair on startup.” It is not just a flag — it carries the work order and makes the apply crash-safe.
{
  "created": "2026-07-23T14:12:05",
  "status":  "pending",
  "problem": "&lt;WHAT ARE WE SOLVING&gt;   — captured at EXTRACT time",
  "repair":  "&lt;WHAT CHANGES DID WE MAKE&gt; — captured at COPY-BACK time",
  "items": [
    { "source":   "repair/download_queue.json",
      "target":   "download_queue/download_queue.json",
      "archived": "saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json" }
  ]
}
problem and repair are captured at DIFFERENT moments. The problem is known when you start (prompt at extract); the repair description isn't known until you finish (prompt at copy-back).
target settles the destination-mapping problem — recorded at extract time, so there is no guessing and no user re-selection at apply time.
Crash-safe: status stays pending until the group write fully succeeds; if the app dies mid-apply the next launch sees pending and retries. Clear only on success. Combined with all-or-nothing validation, a half-applied restore is impossible.
Single source of truth: the manifest is also what the repair screen reads to display staged contents, rather than inferring from a directory listing.
Placement: in the repair area (Downloads) so it travels with the staged files and is readable/editable. Startup code must tolerate a missing or malformed manifest by simply skipping the apply.
⭐⭐ Apply on RESTART, not on exit
Apply-on-exit still races: Android doesn't guarantee clean shutdown, subsystems may be mid-write on the way down, and saveQueue firing during teardown is the same mechanism that made Cancel All appear to work and then resurrect. Apply at startup, VERY EARLY — before loadQueue, before MapStateStore, before anything opens a filesDir file. That is the only genuinely quiescent moment: nothing holds a handle, nothing has read state into memory, nothing can overwrite the repair afterward. This also resolves the live-handle hazard — the download worker hasn't started yet.
Startup order: APPLY FIRST, then the 30-day sweep (housekeeping must not delay the repair). ⚠ The apply must be as fail-safe as the sweep — an exception there would block startup, the exact failure this feature exists to prevent. Wrap it, log it, leave the marker pending for a retry, and let the app boot regardless.
⭐ Applied-repair HISTORY
On successful apply the record moves to a persistent history file with outcome + applied-timestamp appended (applied, or failed + reason). History persists; the manifest is consumed. Value: three weeks later, “has anyone hand-edited this file, and why?” becomes answerable — a question that is currently unanswerable at all. Keep history entries indefinitely (they're small text); losing the record of what changed is worse than losing the copies. Note a history entry's archived path will eventually point at a purged file once the 30-day sweep runs — fine, as long as the entry says so.
Still open
Validate before overwriting — at minimum, confirm each staged JSON parses. Restoring a truncated file would manufacture the exact poison-file scenario this feature exists to escape. With a grouped copy-back: validate EVERY staged item first and abort the whole group if any fails.
Auto-backup the current filesDir file(s) before the group write, making the restore itself reversible.
Cheaper complements (consider alongside, not instead)
“Reset download queue” button (~30 lines) — clears memory AND deletes the file atomically. Would have solved 07-23 in one tap.
Diagnostic mirror — copy queue state to Documents/GroupTrack/ on every save, making it readable via X-plore with no browser at all. Would have shown the 3287 entries and the bad bbox immediately.
NOTE: access and resilience are alternative solutions to the same problem. The repair area makes emergencies survivable; loadQueue tolerant-parse makes them rare. Both are wanted; neither replaces the other.

🟢🟢🟢 OSM TRAIL IMPORT — BUILT 07-27 (commit 7e2173da2)
WORKING Nine trails imported live from Overpass on 07-27, correct geometry and field mapping. Then superseded by a better acquisition path — see the three-step process below.
⭐⭐⭐ THE STRATEGY (Fred) — DOWNLOAD → SUBSET → IMPORT
DOWNLOAD — the USER fetches &lt;state&gt;-latest-free.gpkg.zip from Geofabrik. One file per state, public, ODbL. GroupTrack hosts nothing.
SUBSET — osm_gpkg_subset_v2_2026-07-27.py turns 631 MB of everything into a small trails-only SQLite DB: filters fclass, optionally clips to a bbox, decodes GPKG-binary geometry to the app's exact WKT format, computes geom_hash the way the app computes it, and reports duplication against the live DB.
IMPORT — the app reads that staged DB. ⭐ NOT wholesale: the user draws an area with the existing region tools and pulls only that area across.
⭐⭐⭐ TWO-TIER STAGING (Fred, 07-27 EOD) — the decision that makes volume a non-issue
"End with an import spatial DB we can use the download map regions tools to draw areas to be imported from second spatial DB."
A STAGED reference DB sits on the device; the LIVE spatial DB holds only what the user deliberately pulls. So 106,879 trails never land in grouptrack_spatial.db at all — and the concern about tripling the viewport bbox-scan working set disappears. The full state costs disk, not query time.
The subset schema already supports it — every row carries min_lat/max_lat/min_lon/max_lon with a bbox index. It also makes the 50-state ambition clean: each state is another staged file and nothing changes app-side.
Staged and ready (on D:, pruned, import-ready)

osm_trails_az_strip.db10,71412.3 MB7

Against 49,125 UGRC trails today.
⭐ Dedup MEASURED, not assumed
Utah: 9 hash matches out of 89,554. AZ and NV: ZERO. So OSM and UGRC are INDEPENDENT SURVEYS, not a shared import — genuinely open until measured. Name-matches (same trail, two drawings) were 2,021 / 7 / 41, all pruned on the laptop. Fred: "skip the 2000+ dupes, not worth the hassle when we are talking about 120,000 trails."
⚠ geom_hash only catches BYTE-IDENTICAL geometry — SHA-256 over the WKT string. Independent surveys of the same trail produce different WKT and different hashes, so app dedup is blind to them. Hence name-matching as the second filter, done on the laptop where both datasets sit.
⭐⭐ THE FINDING — and what the Geofabrik path costs
source_id          rows    motorized  surface  uses   carto
osm_trails            9        7         0       7       0
nps_public_trails    18        0        18      18      18
ugrc_utah_trails  49,098        0    49,098  44,583  49,098
OSM is the ONLY source carrying motorized_allowed. UGRC has 49,098 trails and not one has a motorized value. For an OHV app that makes OSM the only source of legal-access data.
⚠ BUT THAT FIELD DOES NOT SURVIVE THE GEOFABRIK PATH. The free roads layer is osm_id, code, fclass, name, ref, oneway, maxspeed, layer, bridge, tunnel and nothing else — no motor_vehicle / atv / 4wd_only / surface at any tier. What is gained instead: fclass = track_grade1..5, real OHV difficulty on EVERY track rather than sparse tagging.
⛔ motorized_hint in the subset is INFERRED from fclass — a track is physically wide enough for a vehicle, a footway is not. PHYSICAL CAPABILITY, NOT LEGAL ACCESS. It sits in its own column so it cannot be mistaken for the real field. Do NOT map it onto motorized_allowed without deciding, deliberately, that an inference belongs in a legal-access column.

Area query against the staged DB — the bbox index is already there.

⛔ NO DELETE-TRAIL IN THE RELEASE (Fred). A route's snapped vertices carry lineId, so deleting a trail orphans them silently. Cleanup stays a LAPTOP operation — pull DBs, DELETE ... WHERE source_id='osm_trails', push back. Bulk delete-by-source in-app was considered and rejected on that dependency.
📐 DESIGN — STAGED-DB IMPORT BY AREA (build this next)
1. The staged DB schema (produced by osm_gpkg_subset_v2_2026-07-27.py)
CREATE TABLE osm_trails (
    osm_id          TEXT,      -- OSM way id. STABLE across extracts -> source_unique_id
    fclass          TEXT,      -- track | track_grade1..5 | path | bridleway
    name            TEXT,      -- OSM name, else ref, else '' (see note)
    ref             TEXT,      -- route designation e.g. '28G', 'FR 008'
    maxspeed        INTEGER,
    wkt             TEXT NOT NULL,   -- APP-EXACT format, see §2
    geom_hash       TEXT NOT NULL,   -- SHA-256(wkt utf-8) hex lower
    min_lat REAL, max_lat REAL, min_lon REAL, max_lon REAL,
    motorized_hint  TEXT       -- 'capable' | ''  INFERRED, NOT legal access
);
CREATE INDEX ix_hash ON osm_trails(geom_hash);
CREATE INDEX ix_name ON osm_trails(name);
CREATE INDEX ix_bbox ON osm_trails(min_lat,max_lat,min_lon,max_lon);
CREATE TABLE subset_meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
  -- source_file, classes, bbox, feature_count, built_at,
  -- wkt_format, hash_algo, attribution, motorized_hint_note
⚠ The dupe pruning already happened on the laptop — hash-matches and name-matches against the live DB were DELETEd before staging, and subset_meta.pruned records it. The app does not need to re-filter; it imports what is in the file.
2. ⭐ WKT format and hash — these MUST stay byte-exact
The subset writes WKT in the app's exact format, because geom_hash is a hash of that string and one differing character produces a completely different hash:
TrailImporter.coordRingToWkt (:545)
   joinToString(",") { "${'$'}{c.getDouble(0)} ${'$'}{c.getDouble(1)}" }
   -> COMMA WITH NO SPACE, single space between lon and lat,
      Kotlin Double.toString() = shortest round-trip, NOT fixed precision
SpatialDbManager.computeGeomHash (:1288)
   SHA-256(wkt.toByteArray(UTF_8)), hex lowercase
Result:  LINESTRING(-112.771625 37.069884,-112.770892 37.070113)
⚠ v1 of the subset script wrote ", " at %.6f and would have reported every one of 89,554 features as new. Caught before it ran. If the subset script is ever regenerated, re-verify against these two functions first.
⚠ Known edge: Kotlin and Python agree on shortest-round-trip decimals for ordinary coordinates but diverge on exponent notation (Kotlin 1.0E-6 vs Python 1e-06). Never fires for Utah/AZ/NV magnitudes; the script warns if it sees one.
3. Opening the staged DB — NOT through httpGet
httpGet does URL(urlStr).openConnection() as HttpURLConnection, which THROWS on a file:// URL. The staged file is SQLite, so it is opened directly and never touches the HTTP path:
val staged = SQLiteDatabase.openDatabase(
    path, null, SQLiteDatabase.OPEN_READONLY)
Read-only on purpose — the staged DB is reference data and nothing in the app should ever write to it.
4. The area query — same predicate the viewport queries already use
SELECT osm_id, fclass, name, ref, wkt, geom_hash,
       min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon, motorized_hint
  FROM osm_trails
 WHERE max_lat >= ? AND min_lat <= ?      -- south, north
   AND max_lon >= ? AND min_lon 
OVERLAP, not containment — a trail crossing the drawn edge is kept whole, matching how queryTrailsByViewport behaves. ix_bbox covers it.
Count first, then confirm. Run SELECT COUNT(*) with the same predicate and show it in a gated confirm — the user should know they are about to add 4,000 trails before they do, not after.
5. Field mapping — staged row → live DB
