Prefer routing through the existing insert path (SpatialDbManager.insertTrail) rather than raw INSERTs, so the INSERT/DROP/ALIAS decision, the notNamed() fallback and trail_properties all behave exactly as they do for the eight catalog sources. The staged row is already in the shape that path wants.
6. ⚠ TWO DECISIONS — make these deliberately, not by drift
(a) Where does fclass go? The obvious target is carto_code, but that drives trail line colour and the mapping is duplicated in THREE hand-synchronised places: ArtifactDetailPanel.kt (~:316, carries an explicit PAIRED-EDIT WARNING), convoy_map.html (FROZEN) and grouptrack_map.html. Colour keys off the LEADING DIGIT.
Leave carto_code BLANK → renders cyan "Unspecified", visually distinct from every coded government source, honest, and touches none of the three files. Recommended for the first import.
Or add codes for track grades → real difficulty colouring, at the cost of a three-file paired edit including a frozen file.
Either way fclass is worth storing somewhere for filtering later — designated_uses is the least-bad existing column, or accept losing it initially.
(b) Does motorized_hint become motorized_allowed? ⛔ Default answer: NO. It is inferred from fclass — physical capability, not legal access — and that column's entire purpose is legal access. A wrong "Yes" there is worse than an empty field. If it is ever mapped, it must be a conscious decision recorded here, not a convenience during implementation.
7. Getting the staged file onto the device
Testing: adb push /d/osm_trails_utah.db /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/staged/.
Real mechanism — undecided. Candidates: a file picker (SAF) pointing at a user-downloaded file; a fixed watched folder; or the app downloading the Geofabrik file itself and subsetting on-device. ⚠ The last one requires GPKG-binary decoding in Kotlin — the same work the Python script does — and would need the 631 MB source on the phone. Not for the first build.
8. Verification order (Droid 2 first — Droid 1 holds the real data)
Push a staged file, draw ONE riding area, import a few hundred trails.
Trails render; OSM visually distinguishable from UGRC.
Snap-2 picks them up — RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) is source- and renderer-independent, so this should be free. Confirm rather than assume.
Search behaves with a large unnamed population (the 'Not Named' sentinel is excluded by design).
Viewport paint speed — the one thing that genuinely changes at volume. Measure before and after.
Re-import the SAME area → expect already-imported, not new. That proves source_unique_id dedup works and re-import is safe.
9. Repeatability — the 50-state plan (discuss AFTER the three states land)
Fred: "identify the state, download and process without intervention." Geofabrik's URL pattern is uniform (&lt;state&gt;-latest-free.gpkg.zip), layer names are identical across states, and the subset script already runs unchanged — Utah, Arizona and Nevada all worked with no modification. So automation is a driver script around a proven step, not new logic.
⚠ One gap already known: the three subsets are each compared against the LIVE DB but not against each other, so a trail crossing a state line can appear in two staged files. Small, and it may be cheaper to let the app's source_unique_id dedup absorb it — the OSM way id is the same in both extracts, so the second import would UPDATE rather than duplicate. Worth verifying rather than assuming.
📱 REVISED — FULLY ON-DEVICE, SELF-CONTAINED (Fred, 07-27 late)
Fred: "on the device itself. this has to be a self contained android process for testers." and "the db is transient — created at the start of the run and removed once data is added to the spatial db."
⭐ THIS SUPERSEDES the laptop-staging design above. Nothing is prepared on a PC; the whole pipeline runs on the phone, and the intermediate DB is a TRANSPORT STRUCTURE THAT IS DESTROYED — the same principle already applied to the OSM licensing position.
⭐ NO FILE PICKER — THE APP OWNS THE WHOLE CHAIN (Fred, 07-27 late)
Fred: "not like the file picker — prefer an app design where we control the handling and processing."
The app downloads the file itself. User picks a state from an in-app list; the app fetches &lt;state&gt;-latest-free.gpkg.zip from Geofabrik straight into its own storage. This is strictly better than a picker:
Kills the content:// problem outright — real filesystem paths end to end, so SQLiteDatabase.openDatabase() just works. A SAF picker would have forced a copy first.
No storage permissions — getExternalFilesDir() is app-private, and everything in it is removed on uninstall. No orphaned 600 MB files if a tester gives up.
The app can VERIFY before processing — expected size from the HTTP header, complete-file check — rather than trusting whatever a user selected.
Cleanup on failure is possible, because the app knows every path it created. With a picker it would not.
No tester confusion about where a browser put the file, or which of three downloads is the right one.
⚠ Licensing is unchanged: this is still the USER'S DEVICE fetching a public file from Geofabrik. GroupTrack neither hosts nor distributes anything. Same position as the Overpass path.
The state list ships in the app — slugs verified 07-27 against Geofabrik. Pattern: https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/&lt;slug&gt;-latest-free.gpkg.zip. ⚠ California is the one exception — no flat state file, only california/norcal and california/socal.
⚠ THE DOWNLOAD ITSELF IS A LARGE JOB — 314 MB for Utah, 1.6 GB for Florida. It needs the same treatment as a tile download: WorkManager foreground job, progress, and RESUMABLE via HTTP Range (the laptop equivalent is curl -C -). A tester on mobile data who loses signal at 80% must not start over. The download-queue pattern is already proven for exactly this.
The lifecycle, app-controlled end to end
User picks a state from the in-app list.
App downloads the .zip into app-private storage — foreground job, progress, resumable.
Unzip to app storage. java.util.zip.ZipInputStream is BUILT INTO ANDROID — no dependency for standard zip. (BBBike's .xz would have needed one; Geofabrik's zip does not.)
DELETE THE ZIP IMMEDIATELY — see the storage note below.
SKINNY PASS — read the .gpkg, filter to trail classes, decode geometry, write the INTERIM trails DB.
DELETE THE .gpkg — 631 MB, done with.
User draws areas, imports from the interim DB into the live spatial DB.
DELETE THE INTERIM DB when finished.
⭐⭐ THE LAUNCH PANEL — FOUR STAGES (Fred, 07-27 late)
Fred: "launch panel should show four stages: download, skinny select, import to spatial, process cleanup."
One panel, four rows, always visible. Each row shows its own state and what it holds; the gate is the action button on the row that is next. The unzip is folded into DOWNLOAD rather than shown separately — it is machinery, not a decision the user makes.
  OSM TRAIL DATA - UTAH
  1  DOWNLOAD            utah .gpkg  631 MB            ✓ DONE
  2  SKINNY SELECT       89,554 trails available       [ EXTRACT ]   <- gate
  3  IMPORT TO SPATIAL   0 areas imported              -- waiting
  4  CLEANUP             739 MB reclaimable            -- waiting
⭐⭐⭐ SIMPLIFIED &mdash; TWO RECOVERY POINTS ONLY (Fred, 07-27 late, SUPERSEDES the 5-gate model)
Fred: "simplify the process. two recovery points: zipped, and skinnied file ready for import. pick up is either file. when skinny is created the zip is removed."
⭐ THE KEY MOVE: the .gpkg is NEVER a recovery point. Unzip and skinny-select are ONE ATOMIC OPERATION &mdash; the extracted .gpkg exists only inside it and is gone when it ends, whether it succeeded or not. So there are only ever two files worth resuming from:
RECOVERY POINT 1   utah-latest-free.gpkg.zip     314 MB   -> next: PROCESS
RECOVERY POINT 2   osm_trails_utah.db            108 MB   -> next: IMPORT
DERIVED STAGE  (three checks, that is the whole state machine)
   skinny db exists          -> IMPORT
   zip exists, no skinny db  -> PROCESS   (unzip + skinny + delete zip & gpkg)
   neither                   -> DOWNLOAD
⭐ Why holding the zip until the skinny succeeds is the right trade
The zip is not deleted after extraction &mdash; it survives until the skinny DB exists. That costs storage but buys the recovery point:
during PROCESS:  314 MB zip + 631 MB gpkg + ~108 MB skinny  = ~1.05 GB PEAK
after  PROCESS:  108 MB skinny only
⚠ ~1.05 GB peak &mdash; check free space BEFORE starting PROCESS, not during. Roughly 100 MB more than deleting the zip mid-operation would need. Worth every megabyte: if the skinny pass dies at 80%, the zip is still there and PROCESS simply re-runs. Deleting the zip early would turn a retry into a 314 MB re-download over mobile data.
The .gpkg is deleted alongside the zip once the skinny DB is written. Nothing but the 108 MB skinny survives.
What this simplifies
Three file checks ARE the state machine. No stage counter, no status field, no partial-extract case to reason about &mdash; a half-written .gpkg is simply invisible, because only the zip and the skinny DB are ever consulted.
Failure is always resumable from a whole file. Every recovery point is a complete artifact; there is no "is this file finished?" question, which is exactly the ambiguity that makes partial downloads painful.
Testing stays trivial &mdash; delete the skinny DB to redo PROCESS, delete both to redo DOWNLOAD. Two files, two levers.
The four panel rows are unchanged (download / skinny select / import to spatial / cleanup) &mdash; they are what the USER sees. This changes only where the process can be RESUMED, and the answer is now: at a whole file, always.
⭐⭐ THE CONTROL JSON &mdash; a LEDGER, not a state machine
Fred: "json to control process in case we crash in the middle? it will also make testing easy as a step by step process continually picking up at a point while we polish."
Yes &mdash; but with a hard distinction, and TODAY'S OWN BUG is why.
⚠ THE CAUTIONARY TALE, from this very feature, this afternoon: isSourceFullyImported() reads status == "processed" from the area-record JSON &mdash; but writeTrailAreaJson() writes status = "processed" UNCONDITIONALLY, including after a failed run. Three FAILED OSM imports (0 rows inserted) therefore marked the source permanently imported and un-selectable. A JSON that stores STATE lies the moment anything goes wrong.
So the rule:
DISK  says WHERE YOU ARE   -- which files exist -> which stage is next
JSON  says WHAT HAPPENED   -- outcomes, counts, timings, provenance
WHEN THEY DISAGREE, DISK WINS. The JSON never gates behaviour.
This is the STATUS-IS-DERIVED rule again, and the JSON is the same exception the route draft is: durable FACTS are safe to persist; runtime STATUS is not.
What goes in it
{
  "state": "utah",
  "slug":  "utah",
  "url":   "https://download.geofabrik.de/.../utah-latest-free.gpkg.zip",
  "download": { "expected_bytes": 329252864, "actual_bytes": 329252864,
                "started": "...", "completed": "..." },
  "extract":  { "gpkg_bytes": 661331968, "completed": "..." },
  "skinny":   { "classes": ["track","track_grade1", "..."],
                "candidate_rows": 89554, "kept": 89554,
                "bad_geometry": 0, "completed": "..." },
  "imports":  [ { "bbox": "-113.70,37.00,-113.40,37.25",
                  "found": 1204, "inserted": 1198, "aliased": 6,
                  "at": "..." } ],
  "cleanup":  { "deleted": ["utah.gpkg.zip","utah.gpkg"],
                "bytes_reclaimed": 990584832, "at": "..." }
}
Every entry is an OUTCOME with a count and a timestamp. Nothing reads "stage: 3". Nothing reads "status: processed". If a stage did not finish, its key is simply absent &mdash; and absence is unambiguous in a way that a stale "processed" is not.
⭐ Why this is exactly what makes testing cheap
Jump to any stage by managing files. Delete the interim DB &rarr; the panel offers SKINNY SELECT again. Keep the .gpkg, delete nothing else &rarr; re-run the extract with different classes. No flag to reset, no state to unwind.
Crash recovery is free &mdash; there is nothing to recover. The next open re-derives the stage from what is on disk, exactly as it would have anyway.
The ledger survives the files. After cleanup deletes 990 MB, the JSON still records that Utah was processed, 89,554 trails were extracted, and which areas were imported. That is the part worth keeping, and it costs kilobytes.
It makes a partial run diagnosable. "download completed, extract absent" is a precise statement about where it stopped &mdash; the same reason the four gates beat one unattended run.
⚠ One thing it must NOT do: the panel must never trust the JSON over the filesystem. If the ledger says the skinny pass completed but the interim DB is gone, the stage is "needs skinny pass" &mdash; the user deleted it, or storage was reclaimed, and the app must handle that rather than showing a completed tick for a file that is not there.
Where it lives: beside the data, in app-private storage, one per state. trail_areas/*.json is the existing precedent &mdash; and also the existing warning, since that is the file whose status field caused today's bug.
Progress bar on every row &mdash; and they are NOT the same kind of bar
Fred: "progress bar on each item. downloads process will be lengthy."
Each stage row carries its own bar. But the four stages know their totals to very different degrees, and pretending otherwise produces the bar that sits at 99% for a minute &mdash; which is worse than no bar.
1 DOWNLOAD        DETERMINATE, and reliably so.
                  Content-Length is known up front -> bytes/total.
                  SHOW MB AND RATE, not just a percentage:
                  "184 / 314 MB  ·  1.2 MB/s  ·  ~2 min left".
                  ⚠ On resume the bar must start at the RESUMED offset,
                  not zero -- HTTP Range means the first byte of the
                  session is not the first byte of the file.
2 SKINNY SELECT   DETERMINATE. SELECT COUNT(*) with the fclass filter
                  gives the exact row total BEFORE the pass starts, so
                  the bar is honest end to end. ~89,554 for Utah.
                  Update per batch (5,000), not per row.
3 IMPORT TO AREA  DETERMINATE per area. Count the bbox query first,
                  then insert -- same "count, confirm, then act"
                  discipline as the queue panel's scoped CANCEL.
                  Repeats, so this bar RESETS per import rather than
                  accumulating.
4 CLEANUP         INDETERMINATE, and brief. File deletes do not report
                  progress. A spinner is honest; a fake percentage is not.
⚠ DOWNLOAD AND SKINNY SELECT ARE BOTH LENGTHY &mdash; both need WorkManager foreground jobs, not dialogs. 314 MB on mobile data, then ~89,000 rows decoded and hashed on a phone. Progress must survive backgrounding and the bar must repopulate correctly when the panel is reopened. Derive it from the job's reported progress, not from a value held in the composable &mdash; the same reason the queue panel reads from the queue rather than remembering.
⚠ Never show a bar with no total. If a stage cannot know its total, say so in words rather than animating a bar that means nothing &mdash; the corridor download work already learned this: an estimate that is confidently wrong is worse than an honest absence.
Mechanism: checkbox marks completion, popup is the gate
Fred: "popup and checkbox as completed."
Each row carries a CHECKBOX that ticks when that stage is complete. Tapping the action on the next incomplete row opens a POPUP announcing what will happen and what it costs; on confirm the stage runs, and its checkbox ticks when it finishes.
The popup reuses the gated-confirm pattern already built for the queue panel's scoped CANCEL/CLEAR — name the action, state the count or size, require confirmation. Consistent with what testers already know, and no new pattern to design.
⚠ ONE SEMANTIC TRAP WORTH DECIDING DELIBERATELY. On the download panel next door, a checkbox is an INPUT — tick Tiles or Trails to choose what to fetch. Here it would be an OUTPUT — this stage is done. Same control, opposite meaning, on adjacent screens. A tester who taps a completed stage's box expecting it to do something will be confused, and worse, may think they have deselected work.
Mitigations, pick one: render it read-only / non-interactive (greyed tick, no touch target); or use a distinct glyph — a filled ✓ for done versus an empty box for pending — so it reads as a status light rather than a control; or keep the checkbox purely decorative and put the action entirely in a separate labelled button on the row. Do not ship an interactive-looking checkbox that does nothing.
⭐ EVERY ROW'S STATE IS DERIVED FROM DISK, never from a stored flag — see the rule below. So the panel is correct on first open, after a crash, after a force-close, and after the app is killed mid-download. There is no stage counter to drift out of step with reality.
Stage 3 is the one that repeats. Download, extract and cleanup happen once per state; importing by area happens as many times as the user draws. The row should show a count ("3 areas, 4,182 trails") rather than a done/not-done tick, because "finished" is the user's judgement, not the app's.
Stage 4 is the only destructive row and should read as such — it names what it will remove and how much space comes back. ⚠ It is also the RE-RUN escape: leaving stage 4 undone keeps the .gpkg, so stage 2 can be re-run with different classes or a tighter bbox without re-downloading 314 MB.
Where it lives: the trail-source screen already lists sources and their import state, so this is a per-source detail view rather than a new top-level screen. ⚠ Note that screen's existing quirks are documented above &mdash; it opens on A1_SOURCE_SELECT, its back exits to the map, and B1_DRAW_AREA is an unimplemented stub. Read those before adding to it.
⭐⭐ CHECKPOINT GATES BETWEEN STAGES (Fred, 07-27 late)
Fred: "gates/stops between stages announcing what will happen next. checkpoint gates stop next process."
Every stage ends at a gate that states what comes next AND WHAT IT COSTS, then waits. Nothing large happens without the user having just been told what it is.
GATE 1  "Utah - 314 MB download. 2.1 GB free, ~950 MB needed. Download?"
        -> DOWNLOAD  (foreground job, progress, resumable)
GATE 2  "Downloaded 314 MB. Extract to 631 MB? Peak usage 945 MB."
        -> UNZIP, then DELETE THE ZIP IMMEDIATELY
GATE 3  "Extracted 631 MB. Extract trails? ~89,000 expected, a few minutes."
        -> SKINNY PASS  (foreground job, progress)
GATE 4  "108 MB trail database ready. Delete the 631 MB source file?"
        -> DELETE .gpkg
        -> DRAW AREAS, IMPORT   (repeatable, many times)
GATE 5  "Finished importing? Delete the 108 MB trail database?"
        -> DELETE interim DB
⭐ THE STAGE IS DERIVED FROM DISK, NEVER STORED AS A FLAG
This is the STATUS-IS-DERIVED rule already established app-wide (route draw-mode, online/offline, bar visibility). Applied here:
.zip present, no .gpkg          -> next gate is UNZIP
.gpkg present, no interim DB    -> next gate is SKINNY PASS
interim DB present              -> next gate is IMPORT
nothing present                 -> next gate is DOWNLOAD
So a crash, force-close or battery death resumes at the correct gate rather than trusting a persisted status a crash may have frozen mid-flight. No stage flag to drift. Durable data on disk is the ground truth; the stage is recomputed from it every time.
Why gates rather than one unattended run
The stages have wildly different costs — a 314 MB download on mobile data, a 945 MB storage peak, minutes of CPU. Bundling them hides all three.
Failure becomes attributable. "Something went wrong" becomes "the extract failed" — the same reason one state at a time beats ten.
Storage can be checked AT THE GATE, before committing, with a real number: "needs 945 MB, you have 600 MB free." Failing before starting beats dying mid-extraction with a partial file.
The user can stop and resume later — leave it after the download, finish on wifi tonight.
Deletion is confirmed, never silent. Gates 4 and 5 remove hundreds of megabytes; the user should agree to that, not discover it.
⚠ Gate 4 and Gate 5 are also the RE-RUN escape. Declining Gate 4 keeps the .gpkg, so the skinny pass can be re-run with different classes or a different bbox without re-downloading 314 MB. Declining Gate 5 keeps the interim DB for more area imports later.
⚠ A picker returns content://, and SQLite cannot open that
SQLiteDatabase.openDatabase() needs a real filesystem path. A SAF picker gives a content:// URI. So the file must be copied into app storage regardless — and the unzip step IS that copy. The zip is not an obstacle here; it happens to be exactly the operation that was needed anyway.
⚠⚠ PEAK STORAGE ≈ 950 MB — design for it, check for it
314 MB zip  +  631 MB extracted .gpkg   = ~945 MB   <- PEAK, during extraction
     delete zip                          =  631 MB
     + ~108 MB interim trails DB         =  739 MB
     delete .gpkg                        =  108 MB   
The peak is unavoidable — SQLite needs random access, so the .gpkg must be fully written before it can be read. There is no streaming shortcut.
So: check free space BEFORE starting and fail early with a clear message, rather than dying mid-extraction with a partial file. And delete the zip the moment extraction completes, not at the end of the run.
⚠ WHY A SKINNY PASS AT ALL, rather than querying the .gpkg directly
The .gpkg is 631 MB across twenty layers, and gis_osm_roads_free alone is ~700,000 rows once footways (241,360 in Utah) and residential streets are counted. Querying it per area draw would scan that every time. One skinny pass produces ~108 MB of trails-only rows WITH A BBOX INDEX, after which every area query is instant. Slow once, rather than slow repeatedly — and it lets the 631 MB source be deleted immediately.
The only genuinely new Kotlin
GPKG-binary → WKT. ~60 lines: a short header (magic GP, version, flags, srs_id, optional envelope) wrapping standard WKB. osm_gpkg_subset_v2_2026-07-27.py is a WORKING REFERENCE to port from.
⚠ THE TRAP: the envelope size is encoded in flags bits 1-3 (0/32/48/48/64 bytes). Get it wrong and the WKB starts at the wrong offset, producing plausible-looking garbage coordinates rather than an error.
⚠ AND THE WKT MUST BE APP-EXACT — comma with NO space, Kotlin Double.toString(), per coordRingToWkt (:545). In Kotlin that is native, so this is actually EASIER on-device than it was in Python, where matching it took a second attempt.
⚠ Both long steps need WorkManager, not a dialog
Python did Utah's 89,554 rows in 24 seconds on a laptop. On a phone the unzip and the skinny pass are each likely minutes. Same territory as the delete worker: foreground jobs, progress, survives backgrounding, cancellable. A modal spinner would be wrong for both.
What this makes of the laptop tooling
osm_gpkg_subset_v2_2026-07-27.py and process_state_2026-07-27.py become reference implementations and test-data generators, not the shipping path. They remain useful for: porting the GPKG decoder, generating a staged DB to test the import half before the unzip half exists, and measuring duplication against the live DB (which the phone will not do).
The three staged files on D: (Utah 87,533 / AZ 10,714 / NV 8,632) are still the fastest way to test step 3 tomorrow — push one with adb and exercise the import path without waiting for the unzip and skinny-pass work.
📚 OVERPASS PATH — built, working, superseded (keep for reference)
Patch R added source_type: overpass as trail source #9 — buildUrl branches, the response transforms, insertFeature untouched. ⭐ Fred's insight made it small: buildUrl appends f=geojson, so nothing Esri-specific is in the RESPONSE, only in the QUERY STRING.
⚠ Why it is not the primary path: Overpass is a QUERY api, not an extract service. It does not page, it caps request size, and the public instances returned HTTP 504 "server is probably too busy" repeatedly on 07-27 — including for a half-mile box. Measured capacity when the server is healthy: 2,658 ways over 900 sq mi in a couple of seconds. The limit is server load, not query breadth.
If that path is ever revived: detect 504 and say "server busy" rather than a generic error; retry with backoff; rotate endpoints. The Geofabrik path likely makes this moot.
⛔ An Overpass source with no bbox is now REFUSED (patch T). It used to default to -90,-180,90,180 and request every track and path on Earth. Harmless for ArcGIS (it pages, the server caps records); catastrophic for Overpass. A default meaning "everything" is only safe when the consumer is bounded.
🔧 ALSO FIXED 07-27
⭐ httpGet now logs the HTTP code, the server's error body, and the exception CLASS (patch V). Previously it read only inputStream — which THROWS on non-2xx — and logged ex.message, which for many exceptions IS THE URL. Timeout, rate limit, rejection and OOM were indistinguishable. The moment this landed, the answer appeared: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout. This was the most valuable change of the day.
launchMode fix — the execute button (MVS:1608) wrote the pending area but never set launchMode = BY_AREA, so the trail screen opened on SELECT_SOURCE and ignored the bbox just written. The panel callback at :1711 always did it. Pre-existing and invisible, because for ArcGIS a missing bbox degrades into an ordinary full-source import.
Re-selectable sources — B2 blocked already-imported sources three ways; A1 was fixed for this in 60a7c6de2 and B2 never was. isSourceFullyImported now also requires trail_count &gt; 0: three FAILED runs had marked OSM permanently imported.
Name fallback REVERTED (patch U) — SpatialDbManager.notNamed() already turns blank into the 'Not Named' SENTINEL for all four artifact types, and search deliberately EXCLUDES it. A synthesized "OSM track 12345678" looks real, so search would have INCLUDED it. Check whether the shared core already applies a fallback before adding one.
AllDocs root cause — Step 4's HTML folding (V13) was correct, but Steps 2/3 copied with GroupTrack* and bash globs are CASE-SENSITIVE, so grouptrack_* / SCOPING_* / BLUEPRINT_* never reached $DOCS. Patches O→P→Q collect by EXTENSION with a secrets gate and a recency window. Claude now also prefixes docs GroupTrack_ so they match the original glob regardless.
🟢🟢 NEXT BUILD — OSM TRAIL IMPORT (designed 07-26, ready to patch)
DESIGNED, NOT BUILT Extends trail coverage and snap-2 reach by importing OSM tracks/paths alongside UGRC/BLM. Independent of the renderer decision — it is data, not display.
⭐⭐⭐ THE MANDATE (Fred) — this governs every design choice below
"We are doing a lot of manual steps. This has to be a repeatable rinse-and-repeat process when we are finished. IMPORTS DONE BY USERS."
⛔ Any design requiring a PC, a downloaded script, a hand-typed bbox, or a file moved between machines is WRONG. The bar is the flow that already exists for the 8 catalog sources: open the app → Method B → pick an area → import. Identical to importing UGRC.
⛔⛔ THE LICENSING CONSTRAINT (Fred) — no OSM data on GroupTrack infrastructure, ever
"Cannot put on AWS for licensing reason, has to be a temporary transport structure that is destroyed."
An AWS endpoint serving OSM-derived GeoJSON would be distribution by Fred and would trigger ODbL share-alike. So: nothing OSM-derived is hosted, cached or served from GroupTrack infrastructure — not even transiently. This kills the "AWS endpoint speaking ArcGIS-REST" idea outright, and it is the correct call.
⭐ THE COMPLETE LICENSING POSITION: user's device fetches public OSM data → user's device transforms it → user's device imports it → transport structure destroyed → only the user's own local DB holds the result. GroupTrack never obtains, hosts, or distributes OSM-derived data. Attribution still applies to what is displayed. Consistent with treating OSM exactly like the Utah trails database: a separate source, user-initiated import of a publicly available dataset, not shipped as a derivative product.
⭐⭐ THE KEY INSIGHT (Fred) — the ArcGIS contract IS GeoJSON
buildUrl appends f=geojson, so what httpGet receives and insertFeature parses is a plain GeoJSON FeatureCollection. There is nothing Esri-specific in the RESPONSE — only in the QUERY STRING.
So OSM adapts to a format the importer already speaks. The work is in the FETCH, not the pipeline. Everything downstream is already source-agnostic: insertTrail, source-uid dedup, the INSERT/DROP/ALIAS decision, trail_properties, logIngestion, writeTrailAreaJson.
The flow, end to end
User picks an area (existing Method B UI).
App queries Overpass directly from the device — [out:json];way["highway"~"^(track|path)$"](S,W,N,E);out geom; (out geom; returns way geometry inline, so no node resolution).
App transforms Overpass elements[] → the ArcGIS-shaped GeoJSON FeatureCollection the importer consumes.
Existing insertFeature loop runs unchanged.
Transport structure destroyed. Simplest form = never persist it (transform in memory, let it be garbage-collected). If it must be inspectable mid-import, cacheDir and delete on completion — never shared or app-visible storage.
The field mapping (catalog fields block → trail_properties)
catalog keyDB columnfrom OSM
idsource_unique_idOSM way id — stable across extracts, so re-import UPDATES rather than duplicates
nametrails.namename
typecarto_codeBLANK — see below
usedesignated_usessynthesized from the access tag set
motorizedmotorized_allowedONE synthesized Yes/No from motor_vehicle/atv/motorcycle/4wd_only
surfacesurface_typesurface
stewardowner_stewardoperator (sparse)
countycounty—
⚠ WHY THE ACCESS TAGS MUST COLLAPSE TO ONE FIELD: fieldExtras collects every non-core catalog key, but insertFeature only READS four — motorized, surface, county, manager/steward. Anything else is parsed and silently dropped. Live proof: usgs_national_trails declares atv, motorcycle, ohv50 and none of the three ever reach the DB. Emitting OSM's four access tags separately would send them nowhere.
⭐ carto_code stays BLANK on first import
carto_code drives trail line colour, and that mapping is duplicated in THREE hand-synchronised places: ArtifactDetailPanel.kt (~:316, which carries an explicit PAIRED-EDIT WARNING), convoy_map.html (FROZEN), and grouptrack_map.html. Colour keys off the leading digit, so blank falls through to cyan "Unspecified" — visually distinct from every coded government source, honest (OSM has no carto classification), and it touches none of those three files. Assign a real code later, deliberately, once seen rendered. (Alternative "0 - OSM Community" costs a three-file paired edit including a frozen file.)
⚠ TWO TRAPS THAT WILL BITE IF MISSED
PAGING. ArcGIS pages via resultOffset/resultRecordCount; the loop is hasMore = features.length() >= PAGE_SIZE (PAGE_SIZE from max_records, default 2000). Overpass does not page — one bbox query returns everything. A response of ≥ max_records features would loop forever re-fetching the same page (dedup skips the rows, but the import never terminates). Either treat an Overpass source as single-page, or chunk the bbox.
file:// IS NOT AN OPTION. httpGet does URL(urlStr).openConnection() as HttpURLConnection — that cast throws on a file:// URL. A local-file source is impossible without touching that method.
What actually has to be written
source_type in trail_sources.json — arcgis_rest (default, all 8 existing) | overpass.
buildUrl branches on it — Overpass POST/GET body instead of the Esri query string.
Response transform branches on it — elements[] → FeatureCollection with the mapped property names. This is where OSM semantics live (the Yes/No collapse, the uses synthesis), so insertFeature stays untouched.
Catalog entry #9 — osm_trails, JSON only.
⚠ highway=track with no access tag → leave motorized_allowed BLANK, do not guess "Yes". A track is by definition wide enough for a vehicle, but that is physical capability, not legal access — and legal access is the entire purpose of that column. A wrong Yes is worse than an empty field.
📚 TRAIL INGESTION — CODE FACTS CONFIRMED 07-26 (read before touching this)
Catalog = app/src/main/assets/trail_sources.json, 8 sources, all ArcGIS REST. loadCatalog (TrailImporter:620) builds Src(id, name, queryUrl, maxRecords, fieldId, fieldName, fieldType, fieldUse, fieldExtras); fieldExtras auto-collects every non-core fields key. status: "display_only_not_queryable" entries are filtered at :627 — the catalog already anticipates non-queryable entries.
Two-part entity. trails (SPATIAL db) = trail_id, name, geometry, min/max lat/lon, created_at, updated_at, geom_hash, + carto_code added later via ALTER TABLE (SpatialDbManager:161). trail_properties (EXTENSION db) = trail_id, source_id, source_unique_id, designated_uses, motorized_allowed, surface_type, carto_code, owner_steward, county, agency_id, ingested_at. Plus source_ingestions (ingestion_id, source_id, ingested_at, trail_count, dupes_skipped, bounds_json).
⭐ DEDUP IS TWO-LEVEL. (1) geom_hash UNIQUE catches identical geometry. (2) source_id + source_unique_id is SOURCE identity — insertFeature checks sourceUidSeen() and routes to updateExistingFeature (update in place, NOT skip) so a re-run refreshes carto/name/properties.
⭐⭐ CROSS-SOURCE DUPLICATES ARE ALREADY HANDLED. insertTrail() returns AddDecision.INSERT | DROP | ALIAS — OSM geometry matching an existing UGRC trail becomes an ALIAS, not a second row. Different geometry (the "mostly coexistence" case) inserts as new. No new work needed for the duplicate question.
⚠ COTREX IS MISCONFIGURED — cotrex_colorado maps "type": "feature_id" and "use": "place_id", so carto_code is being filled with record IDs (107313, 110092…). Polluting that column for Colorado. Not urgent, but wrong.
⚠ Of UGRC's 26 GeoJSON properties, only ~10 survive ingestion. Dropped: Status, SystemName, RecreationArea, OtherRestrictions, and Comments — which carries pipe-delimited structured data (OVAccessPUBLIC|OVRdMaintLvl2|ROAD? = OV access + road maintenance level). Worth PARSING, not displaying, if it ever matters. No column exists to hold it.
UGRC file reality (utah_trails_stgeorge.geojson): 5,732 features, bbox W-114.05 S36.93 E-111.87 N38.72 — southern Utah, not just St George. Status = EXISTING implies other values (proposed/planned/decommissioned) — filter on Status before ingestion.
🔵🔵 V2.7 KICKOFF — VECTOR RENDERING / MapLibre (scoped 07-26, nothing decided)
SCOPED Full analysis: SCOPING_v2.7_vector_rendering_2026-07-26.html. Raised mid-release on 07-26; parked here because Fred: "2.7 is a rewrite of convoy tracking functionality — may be the point we need to introduce these discussions."
⭐ The measurement
The delete log showed DEL SAT walking three stores in near-perfect thirds. Two of the three are TEXT, not photography — road names and place labels delivered as photographs of words, at satellite cost per tile, re-fetched at every zoom. Fred: "if vectors eliminated the street name and points of interest overlays we are downloading 1/3 of what we download as sat images."
On bar 10: 107,000 raster tiles → ~21,700 (only base imagery stays raster). ≈80%, and it STACKS on the corridor work — that track was 1,000,000+ before corridor, 107,000 after, and ~21,700 with vector labels.
⭐⭐ Why 2.7 and not later — the sequencing argument
The dominant cost is not MapLibre. It is operating on frozen code. ConvoyScreen.kt is frozen to protect the Kotlin↔JS↔Leaflet↔setView↔MapStateStore tangle — and a tracking rewrite must open exactly that tangle anyway. So the choice is: rewrite that layer ONCE with MapLibre as the target, or TWICE. Convoy tracking may benefit more than the map does — live cart positions are the textbook case for data-driven styling (heading, speed, staleness, lead-cart status driving symbol rotation and colour from feature properties, instead of rebuilding markers).
⭐⭐ The cross-platform multiplier
Per the 07-04 planning session, the presentation layer is ALREADY web and is the ~90% shared surface for iPad and PC; SwiftUI was rejected for presentation precisely because it gives zero reuse of it. MapLibre GL JS is a web library — it runs identically in an Android WebView, an iPad WKWebView, and a PC browser. So this is a one-time change to the layer all three surfaces inherit, and the PC planning app gains the most (terrain and vector styling with no offline-tile constraint).
⚠ The corollary is a real risk: doing the tracking rewrite on Leaflet bakes Leaflet into the layer iPad and PC are both waiting on — a long-tailed decision made by omission.
Validated in a browser prototype (no build, no device)
✅ Esri raster imagery + OSM vector labels composite correctly — "the image overlays look perfect."
✅ THE SURPRISE: OSM vector labels carry MORE data than Esri's downloaded roads/places layers — "much more data in the vector labels then the downloaded esri roads and places db." The predicted outcome was the opposite.
⛔ OSM TRAIL coverage is sparse — "i see very few trails render." So OSM is a BASEMAP, not a trail source. grouptrack.gpkg stays the authority. This closes a question that was genuinely open.
✅ 3D terrain works; Leaflet cannot do it at all. Terrain-RGB encodes raw elevation, so slope-angle shading computed on device is available — arguably more useful to an OHV rider than imagery.
⛔ Corrections to my own analysis (do not repeat)
I leaned on Esri per-tile cost. Fred: "we pay nothing for esri downloads and data." That pillar is gone — the case must stand on storage, time and capability.
MapLibre is FREE (BSD, no key, no tier). The cost is developer time on frozen code, nothing else.
My first sizing was wrong by half (~39%, assuming satellite stays whole). Fred corrected it via the three-store split. The delete log had shown this hours earlier and I did not connect it.
Vector cannot replace satellite imagery — physics, not tooling.
Nothing is obsoleted
Untouched: grouptrack.gpkg and the national trail model, both DBs, all three engines, SpatialDbManager, corridor downloads, the queue and delete worker (all format-agnostic — MBTiles stores blobs by z/x/y). Artifacts stay GeoJSON overlays — tiles are static and read-only, wrong for user-edited data; tiling is for DISTRIBUTED REFERENCE data. Satellite stays as a toggleable raster layer.
⚠ Do not start this as a V2.6 task. It earns its place only inside the 2.7 tracking rewrite. Planning map first, always — one unknown at a time.
🔴🔴 OPEN — THREE DEFECTS FOUND ON DEVICE 07-24 PM (gate the Play upload, not the build)
FOUND ON THE H+J BUILD Installed and exercised on device. The panel itself works — but three things are wrong, and all three were found by looking at the screen rather than reasoning about the code.
1. ⏱ The ETA finish DATE is wrong (the duration is right)
Panel read ~1d 4h · done Jul 28 6:28 PM, captured 2026-07-24 at 2:28 PM. One day four hours from then is Jul 25 6:28 PM. The time-of-day is exactly right, so the duration→clock conversion works; the date arithmetic is off by three days.
Why it matters: a tester reading "done Jul 28" leaves a queue running for days it doesn't need, or cancels a job that would have finished tonight. ⚠ The 2.6d release notes advertise "a projected finish time" — that claim ships wrong until this is fixed (Fred: post as-is, internal field-test track).
Where to look: whatever formats the completion stamp beside estimateRemaining(). Suspect adding the duration to the wrong field, or day-of-month vs day-of-year. Since the time is correct, the bug is isolated to the date component.
2. ⚠⚠ Corridor jobs are marked Done while still counting tiles
Entry2:232:252:28
CORR SAT151515
CORR TOPO4,4755,1255,774
CORR TOPO+4,5505,1756,175
All three sit under COMPLETED, labelled Done, and TOPO/TOPO+ keep climbing across three captures minutes apart. A finished job must not still accumulate. So markComplete is firing before the work stops.
⚠ This poisons the ETA (defect 1's likely feeder): completedAt gets stamped early, so the elapsed time used for the rate is shorter than the real work, and estimateRemaining() computes from an inflated rate. Fix this before trusting any ETA number.
⭐ Same family as the refresh bug — completion state and actual work drifting apart. Two symptoms, likely one root: how and when workers report terminal state.
3. ⚠⚠ CORR SAT frozen at 15 tiles
SAT sat at exactly 15 across all three captures while its siblings climbed ~650 each. SAT should be the LARGEST of the three — it carries three layers where the others carry fewer.
⛔ The benign explanation is now dead. First read was "hasTile skipped tiles already on disk, so 15 is honest remaining work." But then it would be a different number per run and would sit above the others, not 300× below, and it would not stay pinned while the others move.
THE ONE TEST THAT SETTLES IT: run the same track's corridor with REPLACE ticked. Replace bypasses the hasTile pre-fetch filter, so SAT must derive and fetch its full corridor.
SAT returns in the thousands → filter was working, nothing broken, 15 was honest.
SAT returns 15 again → SAT corridor derivation/fetch is broken, and the ≈90% headline measures what was queued, not what landed.
⚠ If SAT is broken, testers get corridor downloads with no satellite imagery — the primary source — which is a worse regression than anything the cutover fixed. Do this before promoting past the internal track.
Likely shape (unverified): defects 2 and 3 are probably one investigation. "Stops after the first handful, marks Done, siblings keep going" is what a layer loop exiting early on the multi-layer source looks like. Read ConvoyCorridorWorker's per-layer loop and its completion call together.

🔵 NEXT BUILD — G5: ROUTE CORRIDORS (design settled 07-24, not yet written)
READY TO PATCH Fred's rule: the route key goes where the track hash goes. The rest of the code is the same. No new identity concept, no discriminator debate.
⭐ The blocker dissolved on inspection: the routes table already carries geom_hash (insert at SpatialDbManager:900), and the comment block at :1278-1287 states all four artifact types funnel through one core that computes it, with per-type tables making UNIQUE(geom_hash) express identity. computeGeomHash is public at :1288.
What actually has to change
getTrackPoints (SpatialDbManager:1927) hardcodes FROM tracks at :1933. This file already has the table-parameterised pattern ($table/$idCol at :421, :464, :1332) — follow it. Also drop the .gpx strip (:1928) for routes; it encodes "tracks live in hash-named .gpx files".
⚠ getTrackBbox (SpatialDbManager:1975) is a SECOND hardcoded FROM tracks (:1981) and it runs BEFORE the confirm dialog. For a route it returns null → the user taps SAVE MAPS and gets "No geometry for this track". The button would look dead and the message would point at the wrong thing. Routes have min/max lat/lon (written at :900), so it is the same parameterisation.

Route import — it exists: ConvoyTrackOps:662, beside the track import at :586. ⚠ Unlike the track path it does not have the hash in hand — insertRoute (SpatialDbManager:892) returns route_id and computes gh internally at :896 without exposing it. Caller calls computeGeomHash(wkt) (public, :1288).
⚠ Defects to fix while in there
Zero-tile derivation returns SUCCESS. ConvoyCorridorWorker :75-78 does markComplete(entryId, 0, 0); return Result.success() on an empty corridor. Geometry that exists but yields no tiles is a derivation failure, not a completion — and a zero-tile "completion" enters the ETA sample set as work-done-in-no-time. (The no-geometry path at :69-72 is already correct: markFailed + Result.failure().)
⚠ insertRoute returns a fabricated id on duplicates — newId(), then INSERT OR IGNORE, then returns the new id even when nothing was inserted. The track path handles this at :971-972 by resolving the existing row's id from the unique hash; routes never got that treatment. Silent wrong-id generator. Another argument for keying corridors off the hash: the hash is correct on a duplicate, the returned id is not.
Buffer/derivation need no change — routes are plain LINESTRING and the G1 parser already handles LINESTRING and MULTILINESTRING. Fred on density: snap-2 means routes inherit the trail's own vertex density, and with a half-mile buffer either side, coverage is fine — no interpolation needed.
🔴🔴 OPEN — markComplete refreshMode COLLISION (found 07-26, one line, high value)
FOUND WHILE READING THE QUEUE FOR DELETE markComplete (ConvoyDownloadQueue:549) branches on entry.refreshMode and SILENTLY REMOVES the entry from the queue:
if (entry?.refreshMode == true) {
    // Refresh cells: silently remove from queue, no log clutter
    current.removeAll { it.id == entryId }
⚠ But enqueueArea AND enqueueCorridor both set refreshMode = replaceExisting. So ANY area or corridor download submitted with REPLACE ticked is deleted from the queue on completion instead of being marked COMPLETE — no completion row, no completedAt stamp, no ETA sample.
⭐ Strong candidate for BOTH the refresh-never-completes report AND a large share of the ETA starvation. The comment at :350 warns about exactly this drift — "refreshMode stays as the REPLACE-TILES flag; downloadType now carries the KIND. Do not let the two drift into meaning the same thing" — but markComplete predates the split and still reads it as "is a refresh".
Fix: branch on downloadType == MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH. One line. Give it its own patch so its verification is not tangled with delete's. ⚠ This is also why enqueueDelete leaves refreshMode = false — a delete entry with it set would vanish on completion.
🔴 OPEN ITEM — REFRESH DOES NOT LOG AS A COMPLETED JOB (new 07-24)
NEW 07-24 A map-source refresh job never registers as completed.
⚠ Why this is bigger than a cosmetic status
It may be why the ETA has no samples. estimateRemaining() reads the last two COMPLETE entries and completedAt is stamped in markComplete. A job that never reaches COMPLETE contributes nothing — the ETA line would silently not render, looking like a UI bug rather than a missing write. This is the identical failure mode as patch A2 (a field added but never written), one layer further out.
CLEAR won't clear it. CLEAR currently means COMPLETE+FAILED+CANCELLED — "all terminal". A job stuck in a non-terminal status is unclearable from the panel, and accumulates.
⚠⚠ Does it hold a concurrency slot? If the entry never leaves a running/active status, startNextIfAvailable may count it against MAX_CONCURRENT forever. That is a queue-stall mechanism, and "system just sits" is exactly what 07-23 reported. Check this first — it is the difference between a reporting bug and a throughput bug.
Where to look
grep -n "markComplete" app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/*.kt — establish which workers call it and which don't.
Then read ConvoyDownloadWorker's refresh branch end-to-end: does it return Result.success() without notifying the queue, or take a different terminal path (removed rather than marked)?
⭐ Check ConvoyCorridorWorker in the SAME pass. The corridor worker deliberately duplicates the completion plumbing rather than sharing it — that was an accepted trade. This bug is that trade coming due: if refresh can miss markComplete, so can corridor, independently. Confirm corridor stamps completion BEFORE spending hours waiting on a download to prove the ETA — otherwise the wait proves nothing.
Note the sequencing risk: the ETA is currently untestable for an unrelated reason too — it needs two downloads that start and finish on a stamped build, since older completed entries have completedAt=0L and are filtered out permanently. Don't conflate "no samples yet" with "completion is broken"; separate them by checking the code, not by waiting.
🔴 OPEN ITEM — RESTORE PER-SOURCE Z-LEVEL DOWNLOAD LIMITS
CONFIRMED REAL Fred: "return the z-level download limits per map source. we are downloading tiles — or at least requesting tile downloads — where tiles do not exist." Affects both the area and corridor paths.
⛔ ConvoyTileCalculator.maxZoomForSource(sourceName) (:72) is a STUB: = ConvoyConfig.DOWNLOAD_ZOOM, ignoring its argument entirely. So calculateTiles's per-source cap effectiveZMax = minOf(zMax, maxZoomForSource(name)) always computes minOf(18,18) = 18.
quickEstimate has no sourceName parameter at all, so it cannot cap even in principle — sizing and fetching disagree today, which is its own latent bug.
⚠ corridorTiles INHERITS THE SAME GAP — it takes zMin/zMax defaulting to DOWNLOAD_ZOOM with no source awareness. Fixing the stub alone will NOT fix corridor; the source must be passed in.
⚠ The cost is severe — tile counts QUADRUPLE per zoom level. For a source really capped at z15, levels 16+17+18 are roughly 84× the z15 count, and every one of those requests is a 404 or upsampled junk. TOPO+ maps to esri-usa-topo at max_zoom 15, so this is not hypothetical.
The fix: (1) give maxZoomForSource a real per-source lookup — the ceiling lives in the source definitions MapSourceManager parses, so read it from there rather than hardcoding; (2) add a sourceName parameter to quickEstimate so sizing agrees with fetching; (3) pass the source into corridorTiles.
⭐ It also affects MAP DISPLAY, not just downloads (Fred): "we should not zoom to levels where tiles do not exist." Same root cause, different symptom — the map lets the user zoom past a source's real max, showing upsampled mush and firing requests that 404. Once maxZoomForSource returns a real value it should feed the Leaflet layer's maxZoom/maxNativeZoom. Fred: "that is for another day" — deferred, but kept attached here so the display half isn't lost when the download half gets fixed.
⚠ SEQUENCING: capping z will change the corridor baseline numbers. The bar-10 measurement (~107,000) was taken before the cap, so it isolates the MODEL change. The z-cap saving compounds on top and must be measured separately — two variables, two measurements.

GroupTrack V2.5 User Manual
Drill-down edition · device screenshots · 2026-06-23
Organized the way you navigate the app. Open a map to see its launch points; open a launch point to see its options; drill into an option to reach a single screen. Opening one branch collapses the others, so you always see just where you are.
Convoy MapEvery lettered control on the Convoy map toolbar. Open a launch point below to drill into it.
A — GroupTrack → Radio SetupGroupTrack menu
Convoy Map › GroupTrack icon (Meshtastic left sidebar)
Tap the GroupTrack icon in the Meshtastic left-hand sidebar (the last icon) to open the GroupTrack menu — a slide-up panel. This is the entry to radio setup, the prerequisite for using GroupTrack with your Meshtastic radios.
The menu has two sections:
Event / Ride — the ride and radio options (expand to see them). covered below
Map Settings — an older submenu of map instructions, now built into the map panel itself. no longer used
Tap Event / Ride to expand it (next screen).
Setup Radio5 screensEvent / Ride menu
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride
Expanding Event / Ride reveals five options. In V2.5 only the two radio functions are used — ride creation and sharing are moving to the Release 3.0 cloud app.
Create a Ride coming in 3.0
Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email — “select a ride and send via email attachment” coming in 3.0
Import Ride from Downloads — “scan Downloads for .convoy files and import” coming in 3.0
Apply Ride Info to Radio — “apply master config or ride to connected radio.” used — see below
Restore Prior Config Post Ride — “select and restore from saved archive.” used — see below
Tap Apply Ride Info to Radio to begin applying config to a connected radio (next screen).
Apply Radio Config
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio
This screen applies a configuration to the connected radio so it reports each cart’s location to the Convoy map. The bar at the top shows the connection state — here ● CONNECTED, with the radio model (tracker-t1000-e) and firmware version. A radio must be connected before a config can be applied.
Apply Master Config — applies your saved master template to the connected radio. This is the function used in V2.5 to set a radio up for a ride. used
Apply Ride — applies a specific ride’s config. coming in 3.0
Review Changes → — shows what will change on the radio before you commit.
Tap Apply Master Config, then Review Changes to proceed (next screen).
Review — Changes to be Applied
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review
The review panel shows exactly what will be written to the radio before you commit. At the top, Long Name lets you set a name for the radio (here “Mike McKinney”) — edit it if you want this radio to carry a specific rider/cart name. Below, the New Channel (here Convoy, AES-256 encrypted) is the channel the radio will join.
The change table (Field · Current · New Value · Rule) is grouped into accordions you can expand to inspect each setting and see where its value is derived from:
LoRa — radio/region + modem settings
Channel — channel name, key, encryption
Device — device role and behavior
Position — GPS / position reporting
Display — on-radio display settings
Modules — module settings (telemetry, etc.)
Scrolling to the bottom of the panel shows the full accordion list and the action bar:
The action bar has two buttons: Cancel (red) backs out without changing the radio, and Proceed to Update (green) writes the config. Tap Proceed to Update to apply (next screen).
Reconnect Check
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review › Proceed to Update
After you proceed, the config is written and the radio reboots. This screen runs a 60-second countdown while the update is applied and the radio reconnects — the radio reboots, Bluetooth auto-disconnects, then auto-reconnects (shown in the log: “waiting for binary install reboot,” “auto BT disconnect,” “auto BT reconnect”). Let it run; Cancel stops the wait if needed.
When the countdown finishes, an update-apply recap is shown summarizing what was applied. Check the recap: if any settings did not apply correctly, simply reapply the update (return to Apply Master Config and proceed again).
Verify Config (apply recap)
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › … › Reconnect Check › Verify
After the reconnect, the app reads the radio back and compares every field against what it tried to write — only errors are shown. The header reports the result, e.g. “5 of 40 fields failed.” A group summary at the bottom shows pass/fail per category (Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module).
In this example all five failures are in the Position group (Position 1/6) — the table lists each failed field with its Expected vs Actual value (e.g. Broadcast Interval expected 5, actual 0).
If any fields failed, reapply the update — go back to Apply Master Config and proceed again. Radios sometimes need a second pass for a group (often Position) to take. Re-verify until the recap shows all fields passed.
Restore Radio3 screensArchive Restore
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride
A key GroupTrack safety feature: before it writes any configuration to a radio, it first saves that radio’s current config to a timestamped archive. Nothing you apply is ever destructive — the prior state is always recoverable. This screen lists the saved archives for the connected radio so you can restore any of them at any time.
The header shows the radio node and how many archives were found. Each entry is a saved config with its date and time and filename — note the pre_master suffix here, which is the config that was auto-saved just before the master config was applied. The size (e.g. 391b) is shown at right.
Tap an archive to restore it to the radio. Restore writes the saved config back and runs the same reconnect + verify sequence as Apply, so the radio reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified.
Restore — confirm (gated)
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › select archive
Selecting an archive highlights it (blue, with a check) and reveals a confirmation gate before anything is written. The warning makes the consequences explicit:
⚠ Restore will overwrite current radio config — the selected archive replaces whatever is on the radio now.
Selected: the archive’s date/time, so you confirm you picked the right one.
Radio will reboot after restore.
Tap ↻ Restore This Archive to proceed. The radio then reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified — the same reconnect + verify sequence shown for Apply (above).
Restore — write &amp; reconnect
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › Restore This Archive
After you confirm, Restore writes the archived config to the radio and runs the same write · reconnect · verify process documented under Apply (the 60-second Reconnect Check, then the Verify recap). When the recap shows all fields passed, the radio is back on the chosen prior configuration.
✓ This completes Convoy launch point A — GroupTrack / Radio Setup.
B — REC (record ride track)Recording in progress
Convoy Map › REC
The REC button starts track recording for the ride. It works two ways depending on your setup: with no radios it records a track for just this cart (this device’s GPS path); with radio-equipped carts it activates group tracking for the whole convoy. Either way it creates and saves a track for the ride.
Tap REC and recording begins immediately — no prompt. The button changes to ❚❚ PAUSE, and a live Distance readout appears at the bottom-right and counts up as you move.
Tap Pause to interrupt recording (next screen).
Pause3 screensPaused — End or continue
Convoy Map › REC › Pause
When you pause, recording holds and an End button appears below the Pause button. From here you choose:
Pause (top) — hold here; the button changes to Resume so you can continue when ready (see below).
End (below) — finish the recording and save the track.
Tap End to finish — you’ll be prompted to name the track (Save Track, below). Or, to continue the ride, the button shows Resume.
Resume
Convoy Map › REC › Pause › (continue)
If you don’t end, the recording stays paused and the button shows ▶ RESUME. Tap it to continue recording the same track from where you left off — the Distance readout picks back up. This lets you pause during stops and resume without starting a new track.
Save Track (name prompt)
Convoy Map › REC › Pause › End
Tapping End stops recording and opens the Save Track prompt. Type a Track name and tap Save to store the recorded track under that name. Skip discards the track (it is not saved). After saving, the REC button returns to its idle state.
The saved track becomes an artifact you can view, select, and export later from Work with Artifacts and from search.
C — Zoom (+/−)Zoom
Convoy Map › Zoom (+/−)
The + and − buttons at the top-left zoom the map in and out. You can also pinch-to-zoom directly on the map. The current zoom level is shown in the header readout (e.g. N · Z13).
D — PLAN (launch Planning Map)PLAN
Convoy Map › PLAN
The PLAN button switches from the Convoy (live) map to the Planning Map, where you search, download tiles, build routes, and manage artifacts. See Planning Map for everything you can do there. Use BACK on the Planning map to return to the Convoy map.
E — GROUP (whole group + group HUD)GROUP display + HUD
Convoy Map › GROUP
GROUP shows the entire ride group on the map and displays the group heads-up display (HUD) at the bottom-left. It’s one of the bottom-bar view modes (GROUP · MY CART · SELECT CART · HIDE).
The group HUD reports the whole convoy at a glance:
Span — the distance from the lead cart to the tail cart (how spread out the group is).
Carts — total carts in the group.
Active — carts currently reporting.
Lost — carts not heard from within the set time window. (The active threshold and the “lost” minutes are both set in setup.)
△ Lead / ▽ Tail — the front and rear carts, with distance.
CH% — mesh channel utilization. Radios broadcast position every 5 seconds; if CH% turns red the channel is too busy — slow the broadcast frequency (slide the broadcast interval up) to reduce congestion.
F — MY CART (my cart + my HUD)MY CART display + HUD
Convoy Map › MY CART
MY CART centers the map on your own cart (the starred marker, labeled with your cart name) and shows your cart’s heads-up display — your telemetry plus where you sit within the convoy.
The my-cart HUD shows:
Cart name — your cart’s name (e.g. “Fred &amp; June”).
Heading — your direction of travel.
Battery — your device/radio battery level.
Altitude — your elevation.
Speed — your current speed.
To Lead / To Tail — your distance to the lead cart and to the tail cart.
Gap Ahead / Gap Behind — the gap to the cart immediately ahead of and behind you.
G — SELECT CART (detail on selected cart)SELECT CART
Convoy Map › SELECT CART
SELECT CART opens a list of the carts in the group at the top of the screen. Tap the cart you want to view — the map centers on that cart and its heads-up display appears at the bottom-left. The cart currently being viewed is marked CURRENT in the list.
The selected-cart HUD shows the same details as MY CART, but for the chosen cart: Heading, Battery, Altitude, Speed, To Lead / To Tail, and Gap Ahead / Gap Behind. This lets you check any cart in the convoy, not just your own.
(pick a cart)1 screenSelected cart — detail &amp; actions
Convoy Map › SELECT CART › (pick a cart)
With a cart selected, its detail panel shows its live status and two action buttons. The detail fields include Status (Active), Spd (speed), Bat (battery), Pos # (its position/order in the convoy), Hdg (heading), Alt (altitude), and Seen (time since its last report).
Set as Lead — designate this cart as the lead cart for the ride.
Remove from Ride — remove this cart from the group. Use this when a cart is no longer part of the ride (breakdown, left early, etc.). Removing a cart stops “lost” messages for it and keeps the group span and stats accurate to the active riders only — so the GROUP view’s span no longer stretches out to a cart that has dropped off.
H — HIDE (clear the HUD)HIDE
Convoy Map › HIDE
HIDE clears the heads-up display from the map for a clean, unobstructed view. The cart markers stay on the map and the Distance readout remains, but the detailed HUD block is removed. Tap any of the other modes (GROUP, MY CART, or SELECT CART) to bring the HUD back.
I — Settings gear (Convoy Settings)Convoy Settings (panel 1)
Convoy Map › Settings gear
The gear opens Convoy Settings — a list of options that control the app’s behavior. This is where the thresholds referenced elsewhere in the manual are set.
Map Sources → Change Map Sources — assign tile sources to the SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ slots. (This is the one setting that opens its own screen — see below.)
Alert Thresholds → Signal Drop — minutes before the radio-disconnect warning fires (e.g. 2 min).
Signal Lost — minutes without a packet before a node is considered lost (e.g. 10 min). This is the “lost” window reflected in the group HUD’s Lost count.
Off Track — miles from the convoy track before the off-route alert fires (e.g. 0.5 mi).
Node Filter — admission settings for which nodes join the group (continues on panel 2).
(scroll down)1 screenConvoy Settings (panel 2)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › (scroll down)
Scrolling down reveals the rest of Convoy Settings:
Node Filter → Admission Window — a node must have been heard within this window today to appear on the map (e.g. 1 hr).
Track Display → Multicolor Track — when on, the track is colored by node position.
Track Recording → Lead Cart Only — record the lead cart’s track only.
Track Recording Format — KML / GPX — the saved track format (GPX works with Garmin, Strava, AllTrails).
Removed Carts — lists carts you removed from the ride today (via SELECT CART → Remove from Ride); shows “No carts removed today” when none.
The app version and build are shown at the bottom of this screen.
Change Map Sources3 screensMap Sources (drill-down)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources
This is the one Convoy Settings option that opens its own screen. Map Sources assigns a tile source to each of the three fixed map slots used by the SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ buttons on the map toolbar.
SAT — the satellite slot (e.g. Esri Imagery + Roads + Labels).
TOPO — the topo slot (e.g. Esri World Topo).
TOPO+ — the detailed-topo slot (e.g. Esri USA Topo Maps).
Each slot has a Change button to pick a different source.
API Keys — some sources (e.g. Thunderforest Outdoors) require an API key; tap to enter the key to unlock them.
Tap Change on a slot to pick a new source (next screen).
Change source (picker)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources › Change
Tapping Change opens a list of available tile sources, grouped by category. Tap a source to assign it to that slot; the currently-assigned source is checked.
Hybrid — imagery with roads/labels (Google Hybrid, Esri Imagery + Roads + Labels, USGS Imagery + Topo).
Satellite — plain imagery (Google Satellite, Esri World Imagery).
Topographic — topo maps (Esri USA Topo, Esri World Topo, OpenTopoMap, USGS Topo).
Street — road maps (Google Roads, OpenStreetMap, CartoDB Voyager).
Terrain — terrain maps (Google Terrain, and more).
Select a source and you return to the Map Sources screen with the slot updated (next screen).
Refresh Tiles (after a source change)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources › Change › (select source)
After you assign a new source to a slot, the app offers to refresh the cached map tiles from the new source. It reports how many existing tiles it found and explains that the refresh downloads them at low priority, with progress visible in Work with Queues, and that it restarts automatically if interrupted.
Refresh Now — start re-downloading the tiles from the new source right away (low priority).
Later — keep the new source assignment but don’t refresh the cached tiles now.
✓ This completes Convoy launch point I — Settings (Convoy Settings → Map Sources → Change → Refresh).
J / K / L — SAT, TOPO, TOPO+ (map source buttons)SAT · TOPO · TOPO+
Convoy Map › SAT / TOPO / TOPO+
These three toolbar buttons switch the displayed map source immediately. Each shows the source assigned to that slot in Convoy Settings → Map Sources (e.g. SAT = Esri Imagery, TOPO = Esri World Topo, TOPO+ = Esri USA Topo).
They work in either NET or LOCAL mode (see the NET/Local toggle). In local mode they display from tiles downloaded in advance — so you can switch sources and ride with no connection, as long as those map tiles were downloaded ahead of time.
M — NET / Local (network vs downloaded tiles)NET / Local toggle
Convoy Map › NET / Local
This toggle switches between NET (network) and Local map modes:
NET — fetches map tiles live over the network (online).
Local — displays only from maps you have downloaded prior to your ride. If you haven’t downloaded the area in advance, local mode will have no maps to show — so download your ride area ahead of time to use it offline.
N — QUEUES (download queues)Download Queues
Convoy Map › QUEUES
Queues opens the Download Queues panel, which manages map-tile downloads. The header shows the current state (e.g. “2 active, 1 queued”), and entries are grouped by status:
Active — downloads in progress, each showing tiles downloaded and percent, with an X to cancel that entry.
Queued — downloads waiting to start (numbered #1, #2…), each with a timestamp and an X to remove it.
Completed — finished downloads, each listing the source (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+) and tile count.
Global controls: Hold pauses the queue, Cancel All stops everything, and Clear Done removes completed entries from the list. Close dismisses the panel.
O — Search (universal search)Universal Search
Convoy Map › Search
The magnifying glass opens Universal Search — one search across five modes, shown as tabs: Area · Track · Route · Trail · Waypoint. Pick a tab, type in the field (the prompt changes per mode), and press Enter. There are two kinds of search:
Area — a place search. Type a place name (a town or a feature such as a park, e.g. “Bryce”) and the map repositions there. For common names, include the state to disambiguate — e.g. “Kanab, UT” — so it lands on the right place.
Track / Route / Trail / Waypoint — artifact searches. These search your saved and imported artifacts by name. The search presents a list of matching hits; select one and its artifact detail panel opens. From the detail panel, use FIT to center the map on it.
Example — Area search for “Panguitch, UT”: the map repositions to Panguitch and the trails and tracks for that area draw immediately.
Example — artifact search: searching a name returns a list of matching hits (here two results for “Panguitch”), each with its name and ID.
Selecting a hit opens that artifact’s detail panel:
The detail panel shows the artifact’s name and type, an Aliases field, and a Details section — including the Carto Type band, its ID and bounding box, and an expandable technical section. Down the left is the action column: Rename, Delete, Share, Export, and FIT. Tap FIT to center and frame the map on that one artifact. Close dismisses the panel.
After FIT the panel closes and the map zooms to frame that artifact — here the selected track centered and fit to the view:
In short: Area moves the map to a place; the artifact modes find a saved item by name and open its details (then FIT centers the map on it).
P — Work with ArtifactsWork with Artifacts panel
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts (hamburger)
The hamburger opens the Work with Artifacts panel, which controls the four artifact types — Tracks, Trails, Waypoints, Routes — on the map. Important: all of these controls operate on the bounding box of the current display — i.e. the artifacts within the area you’re currently viewing, not the whole database.
Each type row has three buttons (the highlighted one is the current state):
OFF — hide that artifact type on the map.
ALL — show all artifacts of that type within the current view.
SEL/EDIT — opens a list of that type’s artifacts in the current view for per-artifact control: Select All, Deselect All, or check a custom combination to choose exactly which are shown. (OFF and ALL are in-panel toggles; only SEL/EDIT opens a screen.)
A + Route button at the top starts building a new route.
SEL/EDIT1 screenSEL/EDIT list (per-artifact)
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › SEL/EDIT
Tapping SEL/EDIT on a type opens its list — here Trails (23), all the trails in the current view. Each has a checkbox, with Select All and Deselect All at the top, so you can show every one, hide every one, or pick a custom mix.
You can also tap an artifact’s name in this list to open its detail info panel (the same panel shown under Search — name, type, Carto Type, IDs, with Rename / Delete / Share / Export / FIT). Tap FIT there to center that one artifact on screen.
+ Route4 screens+ Route — start a route
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route
Before you start: zoom into the area where you want to build the route. It helps to display Trails and Tracks (turn them on in Work with Artifacts) as a visual guide — the snap-to function works over both tracks and trails, so your route follows a known track or trail wherever one is available, keeping it on established paths.
Tapping + Route opens the Start a route dialog:
New Route — create and name a new route to build.
In Progress — resume an unfinished route you started earlier.
The only difference is whether you create a new named route or select an existing in-progress one. Choose New Route to begin building (next screen).
Building the route
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › New Route
The Route panel opens for building. Tap the map to place points — the route draws as a pink line, and each new point adds length and snaps to a nearby trail/track when one is available, keeping the route on known paths.
The panel controls:
Method — Point (live; tap to place points). Draw and Suggest are marked “soon.”
Build (n pts) — shows how many points the route has so far.
Add ON — toggles point-adding on/off as you tap.
Undo — removes the last point.
Save — saves the finished route.
Discard — abandons the route without saving.
Keep tapping to extend the route; each point snaps to the underlying track/trail.
Extending &amp; saving the route
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › (building)
As you keep tapping, the route grows and the Build point count climbs (here 26 points). The pink route traces the chosen path, snapped to the underlying tracks/trails.
When you tap Save, you can save the route as a work in progress (to resume and finish later via + Route → In Progress) or as a completed route.
Save route
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › Save
The Save route dialog offers two ways to save:
Save as in progress — keep editing later; resume it via + Route → In Progress.
Save as completed route — graduate it to a finished, saved route (then searchable and listed like any other artifact).
✓ This completes Convoy launch point P — Work with Artifacts.
Q — ? (Help &amp; Info)Help &amp; Info
Convoy Map › ?
The ? button opens Help &amp; Info, with two choices:
Full Manual — opens the complete user manual, bundled in the app (a screen-by-screen cookbook with its own search box and contents).
Release Notes — opens the release notes for the current version.
Full Manual:
Release Notes — includes the important upgrade warning (install as an update, do not clean-install) and the “What’s new” list for the build:

E — QUEUES (download queues)Download Queues
Planning Map › QUEUES
Queues opens the Download Queues panel, which manages map-tile downloads. The header shows the current state (e.g. “2 active, 1 queued”), and entries are grouped by status:
Active — downloads in progress, each showing tiles downloaded and percent, with an X to cancel that entry.
Queued — downloads waiting to start (numbered #1, #2…), each with a timestamp and an X to remove it.
Completed — finished downloads, each listing the source (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+) and tile count.
Global controls: Hold pauses the queue, Cancel All stops everything, and Clear Done removes completed entries from the list. Close dismisses the panel.
F — Search (universal search)Universal Search
Planning Map › Search
The magnifying glass opens Universal Search — one search across five modes, shown as tabs: Area · Track · Route · Trail · Waypoint. Pick a tab, type in the field (the prompt changes per mode), and press Enter. There are two kinds of search:
Area — a place search. Type a place name (a town or a feature such as a park, e.g. “Bryce”) and the map repositions there. For common names, include the state to disambiguate — e.g. “Kanab, UT” — so it lands on the right place.
Track / Route / Trail / Waypoint — artifact searches. These search your saved and imported artifacts by name. The search presents a list of matching hits; select one and its artifact detail panel opens. From the detail panel, use FIT to center the map on it.
Example — Area search for “Panguitch, UT”: the map repositions to Panguitch and the trails and tracks for that area draw immediately.
Example — artifact search: searching a name returns a list of matching hits (here two results for “Panguitch”), each with its name and ID.
Selecting a hit opens that artifact’s detail panel:
The detail panel shows the artifact’s name and type, an Aliases field, and a Details section — including the Carto Type band, its ID and bounding box, and an expandable technical section. Down the left is the action column: Rename, Delete, Share, Export, and FIT. Tap FIT to center and frame the map on that one artifact. Close dismisses the panel.
After FIT the panel closes and the map zooms to frame that artifact — here the selected track centered and fit to the view:
In short: Area moves the map to a place; the artifact modes find a saved item by name and open its details (then FIT centers the map on it).

The screen header shows how many files were found; each entry lists its name, size, date, and format. A RESYNC TRACKS button is also here — the same one referenced in the upgrade notes for bringing recorded tracks back after an update.
