Reconnect Check
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review › Proceed to Update
After you proceed, the config is written and the radio reboots. This screen runs a 60-second countdown while the update is applied and the radio reconnects — the radio reboots, Bluetooth auto-disconnects, then auto-reconnects (shown in the log: “waiting for binary install reboot,” “auto BT disconnect,” “auto BT reconnect”). Let it run; Cancel stops the wait if needed.
When the countdown finishes, an update-apply recap is shown summarizing what was applied. Check the recap: if any settings did not apply correctly, simply reapply the update (return to Apply Master Config and proceed again).
Verify Config (apply recap)
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › … › Reconnect Check › Verify
After the reconnect, the app reads the radio back and compares every field against what it tried to write — only errors are shown. The header reports the result, e.g. “5 of 40 fields failed.” A group summary at the bottom shows pass/fail per category (Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module).
In this example all five failures are in the Position group (Position 1/6) — the table lists each failed field with its Expected vs Actual value (e.g. Broadcast Interval expected 5, actual 0).
If any fields failed, reapply the update — go back to Apply Master Config and proceed again. Radios sometimes need a second pass for a group (often Position) to take. Re-verify until the recap shows all fields passed.
Restore Radio3 screensArchive Restore
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride
A key GroupTrack safety feature: before it writes any configuration to a radio, it first saves that radio’s current config to a timestamped archive. Nothing you apply is ever destructive — the prior state is always recoverable. This screen lists the saved archives for the connected radio so you can restore any of them at any time.
The header shows the radio node and how many archives were found. Each entry is a saved config with its date and time and filename — note the pre_master suffix here, which is the config that was auto-saved just before the master config was applied. The size (e.g. 391b) is shown at right.
Tap an archive to restore it to the radio. Restore writes the saved config back and runs the same reconnect + verify sequence as Apply, so the radio reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified.
Restore — confirm (gated)
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › select archive
Selecting an archive highlights it (blue, with a check) and reveals a confirmation gate before anything is written. The warning makes the consequences explicit:
⚠ Restore will overwrite current radio config — the selected archive replaces whatever is on the radio now.
Selected: the archive’s date/time, so you confirm you picked the right one.
Radio will reboot after restore.
Tap ↻ Restore This Archive to proceed. The radio then reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified — the same reconnect + verify sequence shown for Apply (above).
Restore — write &amp; reconnect
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › Restore This Archive
After you confirm, Restore writes the archived config to the radio and runs the same write · reconnect · verify process documented under Apply (the 60-second Reconnect Check, then the Verify recap). When the recap shows all fields passed, the radio is back on the chosen prior configuration.

// Focus: opening one sibling section at the same level collapses the others.
function wireSiblings(container, selector){
  var items=container.querySelectorAll(selector);
  items.forEach(function(it){
    it.addEventListener('toggle',function(){
      if(it.open){ items.forEach(function(o){ if(o!==it && o.parentNode===it.parentNode) o.open=false; }); }
    });
  });
}
document.querySelectorAll('details.map').forEach(function(mp){
  wireSiblings(mp.querySelector(':scope > .mapbody'), ':scope > details.lp');
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.lp').forEach(function(lp){
  var b=lp.querySelector(':scope > .lpbody'); if(b){ wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.sf'); wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.screen'); }
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.sf').forEach(function(sf){
  var b=sf.querySelector(':scope > .sfbody'); if(b){ wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.screen'); }
});
// Filter: match against data-search across all levels; reveal & open the path to hits.
var Q=document.getElementById('q');
function flt(){
  var t=Q.value.trim().toLowerCase();
  // reset
  if(t===''){
    document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(function(d){
      d.classList.remove('nohit');
      d.open = d.classList.contains('map');   // only maps open at rest
    });
    return;
  }
  // hide everything first
  document.querySelectorAll('details.lp, details.sf, details.screen').forEach(function(d){ d.classList.add('nohit'); d.open=false; });
  // any details whose own text matches => show it and its ancestors+descendants
  document.querySelectorAll('details.screen, details.sf, details.lp').forEach(function(d){
    var hay=((d.getAttribute('data-search')||'')+' '+d.textContent).toLowerCase();
    if(hay.indexOf(t)>=0){
      d.classList.remove('nohit');
      // open & reveal ancestors
      var p=d.parentNode;
      while(p && p!==document){
        if(p.tagName && p.tagName.toLowerCase()==='details'){ p.classList.remove('nohit'); p.open=true; }
        p=p.parentNode;
      }
      d.open=true;
    }
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('details.map').forEach(function(mp){ mp.open=true; });
}

Workplan &mdash; 2026-07-28Read with GroupTrack_handoff_2026-07-27.html &middot; working tree clean at 7e2173da2
Ordered so nothing blocks on an unmade decision, and so the risky step comes after the cheap ones. Steps 1&ndash;2 are small and have been displaced twice already.
0 &middot; Revoke the ngrok codes (if not already done)
SECURITY They were committed and pushed in 151fffb79. Removal from HEAD (ddb48650b) does NOT undo that &mdash; anyone with the repo can check out that commit. Revoking takes two minutes and closes the actual exposure. Scrubbing history with filter-repo is a separate, lower-priority decision.
1 &middot; The markComplete refreshMode collision &mdash; ONE LINE
DISPLACED TWICE ALREADY ConvoyDownloadQueue:549 branches on entry.refreshMode and silently removes the entry from the queue. But enqueueArea AND enqueueCorridor both set refreshMode = replaceExisting.
So any download submitted with REPLACE ticked is deleted on completion instead of marked COMPLETE &mdash; no row, no completedAt, no ETA sample. Strong candidate for BOTH the refresh-never-completes report AND much of the ETA being ~50&times; long. Fix: branch on downloadType == MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH. Own patch &mdash; and any ETA measurement taken before it is untrustworthy.
2 &middot; Settle SAT-frozen-at-15 &mdash; one download, no code
Run the same track's corridor with REPLACE TICKED. Replace bypasses the hasTile pre-fetch filter, so SAT must derive and fetch its full corridor. Thousands &rarr; the filter was working and 15 was honest. 15 again &rarr; SAT corridor derivation is broken, and the &asymp;90% corridor headline measures what was QUEUED, not what LANDED. Costs one download. Still the only open defect that changes what a tester receives.
3 &middot; THE DAY'S BUILD &mdash; staged-DB import by area
Fred's architecture (decided 07-27 EOD): a STAGED reference DB on the device; the user draws an area with the existing region tools and pulls only that area's trails into the LIVE spatial DB. The 106,879 trails never land wholesale &mdash; which removes the concern about tripling the viewport bbox-scan working set.
What has to be built
A local-file read path. httpGet does URL(urlStr).openConnection() as HttpURLConnection &mdash; that cast THROWS on file://. The staged DB is SQLite, so this is not an httpGet variant at all: it is a direct SQLiteDatabase.openDatabase(path, null, OPEN_READONLY) against the staged file.
An area query against the staged DB. Every row already carries min_lat/max_lat/min_lon/max_lon WITH A BBOX INDEX &mdash; built for exactly this. Same overlap predicate the viewport queries already use.
Insert into the live DB via the existing path so dedup, ALIAS and trail_properties all behave normally. The staged rows carry wkt in the app's EXACT format and a matching geom_hash, so this is close to a table copy.
Get the staged file onto the device &mdash; adb push for testing; a real mechanism later.
Field mapping from the staged schema
osm_id &rarr; source_unique_id &middot; name &rarr; name (blank takes the 'Not Named' sentinel; ref is already folded into name at subset time) &middot; wkt &rarr; geometry &middot; geom_hash &rarr; geom_hash &middot; fclass &rarr; ? &middot; min/max &rarr; bbox columns.
&#9888; TWO DECISIONS, both deliberate rather than drifted into: (a) does fclass go to carto_code (drives line colour, and that mapping is duplicated in THREE hand-synchronised places including a FROZEN file), or somewhere else? Leaving carto_code BLANK renders cyan "Unspecified" and touches none of them. (b) Do NOT map motorized_hint onto motorized_allowed without consciously accepting an inference in a legal-access column.
4 &middot; Verify small before large
Droid 2 first &mdash; it is sacrificial; Droid 1 holds the real data. Push a staged file, draw ONE riding area, import a few hundred trails.
Trails render, and OSM is visually distinguishable from UGRC
Snap-2 picks them up &mdash; RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) is renderer- and source-independent, so this should be free. Confirm it.
Search behaviour with a large unnamed population (the 'Not Named' sentinel is excluded from search by design)
Viewport paint speed &mdash; the one thing that genuinely changes at volume
&#9940; NO delete-trail in the release (Fred): a route's snapped vertices carry lineId, so deleting a trail orphans them silently. Cleanup stays a LAPTOP operation &mdash; pull the DBs, DELETE ... WHERE source_id='osm_trails', push back. Same pattern as the EMPTY_BASELINE reset.
5 &middot; Later &mdash; not tomorrow
50-state automation. Fred: "identify the state, download and process without intervention." Geofabrik's URL pattern is uniform (&lt;state&gt;-latest-free.gpkg.zip), the layer names are identical, and the subset script already runs unchanged. DISCUSS AFTER the three states are imported.
ETA startedAt &mdash; only meaningful after step 1. Three timestamps: submit (createdAt, exists), start-execution (MISSING), finish (completedAt, exists). Stamp in DownloadQueueManager where status goes active, NOT per worker. Sampling policy still needs Fred's call.
Rotation clears source selections (remember &rarr; rememberSaveable) &middot; VACUUM / space reclamation, blocked on the unexplained "0 MB reclaimable" &middot; COTREX catalog misconfiguration (type: feature_id fills carto_code with record IDs) &middot; V2.7 vector rendering, parked for the convoy tracking rewrite.
Overpass resilience, IF that path is kept at all: detect 504 and say "server busy" rather than a generic error, retry with backoff, rotate endpoints. The Geofabrik path may make this moot.

Meshtastic Config Guide - Convoy Tracker
Meshtastic
Radio Configuration Guide — Convoy Tracker
Purpose: Complete configuration reference for
Meshtastic radios being repurposed for convoy tracking.
Important: These radios have been in service. Before
configuring for convoy use, review ALL settings below — previous
configurations may conflict with convoy tracker requirements.
Configuration Tool: Meshtastic Web Client at
https://client.meshtastic.org via Bluetooth
Date: March 2, 2026
BEFORE YOU START: Reset
vs. Reconfigure
Since these radios have prior configurations, you have two
options:
Option A: Factory Reset (Recommended for clean
start)
Connect to the device via Web Client (Bluetooth).
Go to Config → Device and look for a
Factory Reset or Reset to Defaults
option.
After reset, the device reboots and all settings return to
defaults.
You will need to set the Region again before the device will
transmit.
Option B: Reconfigure in place
Keep existing settings but review and change each section below. This
preserves any custom hardware GPIO settings that may be specific to your
board.
Configuration
Section 1: USER (Device Identity)
Web Client Path: Config → User
Setting
Description
Convoy Recommended Value
Long Name
Friendly name shown on other devices and the mesh
Name each by role: Convoy-Lead,
Convoy-Mid, Convoy-Tail,
Convoy-4, etc.
Short Name
4-character ID shown on small displays
LEAD, MID1, TAIL,
CV04, etc.
Is Licensed (HAM)
Enables HAM mode: higher TX power but disables encryption
OFF — Leave disabled. Convoy needs encryption for
private channel.
Is Unmessageable
Tells other nodes this device won’t read direct messages
OFF — Convoy nodes should be messageable for
alerts.
Why it matters for convoy: Clear naming lets you
instantly identify which vehicle is which on the mesh, in the Web
Client, and in your Python tracker.
Configuration
Section 2: DEVICE (Role &amp; Behavior)
Web Client Path: Config → Device
Setting
Description
Convoy Recommended Value
Role
Defines how the device behaves on the mesh
See role guide below
Rebroadcast Mode
How the device relays other nodes’ packets
ALL (default) — Every convoy node should relay
packets to extend the chain
Node Info Broadcast Seconds
How often the device announces itself
900 (15 min, default) — No need to change
Double Tap as Button Press
Accelerometer double-tap acts as button
OFF — Not needed for convoy
Disable Triple Click
Disables triple-press GPS toggle on the button
ON — Prevents accidental GPS disable while
driving
LED Heartbeat Disabled
Turns off the blinking LED
Your preference. OFF saves a tiny bit of power.
Device Role Guide for
Convoy Tracking
Role
Use For
Description
CLIENT (recommended)
All convoy vehicles
Full functionality: sends, receives, relays messages. GPS active.
Screen active. Best for vehicles where someone can see the screen.
CLIENT_MUTE
Vehicles that don’t need to relay
Sends and receives but does NOT rebroadcast other nodes’ messages.
Use only if the convoy is small and every node is in direct range of
every other node.
ROUTER
DO NOT USE for convoy
Designed for fixed infrastructure. No screen, no Bluetooth after
initial config. Will break your convoy tracker connection.
TRACKER
Unattended asset tracking
Sleeps aggressively, wakes only to send position. No message relay.
Only use if a vehicle has no driver monitoring the device.
REPEATER
DO NOT USE for convoy
Retransmits only. No GPS, no messages, no screen. Infrastructure
role only.
Convoy recommendation: Set ALL convoy nodes to
CLIENT.
Configuration

identical LoRa settings or they cannot communicate.

Good range with reasonable speed.

convoy distances.

id="configuration-section-4-channels-communication-encryption">Configuration
Section 4: CHANNELS (Communication &amp; Encryption)
Web Client Path: Channels
Channels define who can communicate and how messages are encrypted.
For convoy use, you want a private encrypted channel.
Channel 0 (Primary Channel)
Setting
Description
Convoy Recommended Value
Name
Channel identifier (must match on all nodes)
CONVOY
PSK (Pre-Shared Key)
Encryption key
Click Generate to create a random AES256 key. All
nodes must have the same PSK.
Downlink Enabled
Allow messages from MQTT to this channel
OFF — Keep convoy communications local to the mesh
only.
Uplink Enabled
Send messages from this channel to MQTT
OFF — Don’t upload convoy data to the
internet.
Position Enabled
Share GPS position on this channel
ON — This is essential for the convoy tracker.
Position Precision
How precise the shared location is
Full precision (32) — Convoy tracking needs exact
positions, not approximate.
Important Notes on Channels
The PSK must match exactly on all convoy nodes. The
easiest way: configure Channel 0 on one device, then use the
Share/QR/URL feature to copy the exact settings to all
other devices.
If the radios had a different primary channel from previous use
(like the default LongFast), you MUST change it on ALL
devices. Mismatched channel names or PSKs mean devices cannot
communicate.
Position is only automatically broadcast on the
lowest-indexed channel with position enabled. Make sure Channel
0 (CONVOY) has position enabled.
You can add a secondary public channel (Channel 1) set to
LongFast with default PSK if you also want to participate
in the public mesh, but this is optional and not needed for convoy
tracking.
How to Copy Channel
Settings to All Devices
Configure Channel 0 on the first device with name
CONVOY and a generated PSK.
In the Web Client Channels page, find the Share or
QR code button.
Copy the Channel URL (looks like
https://meshtastic.org/e/#...).
Save this URL — it contains all channel and LoRa
settings.
Connect to each additional device via Bluetooth.
In Channels, use Import or paste the URL to apply
the same settings.
Verify by checking that the Channel name and PSK match on all
devices.
Configuration
Section 5: POSITION (GPS Settings)
Web Client Path: Config → Position
This is the second most critical section for convoy tracking. These
settings control how often and how accurately GPS positions are shared
across the mesh.
Setting
Description
Convoy Recommended Value
GPS Mode
Whether GPS hardware is active
ENABLED — Must be on for position tracking.
GPS Update Interval
How often the device reads GPS (seconds)
15 seconds — Frequent enough for real-time tracking
without excessive power draw.
GPS Attempt Time
How long to try for a GPS fix each cycle
0 (default: 15 min) — Leave at default unless GPS
is slow to lock.
Fixed Position
Lock position to a saved coordinate
OFF — Convoy vehicles are moving. Only use for a
fixed base station.
Smart Broadcast
Increase broadcast frequency when moving
ON (recommended) — Broadcasts more often while
driving, less when stopped. Ideal for convoy.
Smart Broadcast Min Distance
Minimum meters traveled before broadcasting
50 meters — Lower than default (100m) for tighter
convoy tracking.
Smart Broadcast Min Interval
Minimum seconds between broadcasts
15 seconds — Matches GPS update interval.
Broadcast Interval
Fixed interval for broadcasting position (when not moving)
30 seconds — More frequent than default (15 min) so
the tracker always has recent data.
Position Flags
Which data to include in position packets
Enable: ALTITUDE, SPEED,
HEADING, TIMESTAMP — All useful for
convoy tracking.
Understanding
GPS Update vs. Broadcast Interval
These are two different things:
GPS Update Interval (15 sec): How often the device
checks with the GPS chip for a new location. This happens locally on the
device.
Broadcast Interval (30 sec): How often the device
sends its position to the mesh network so other nodes can see it.
Smart Broadcast: When enabled, it overrides the
broadcast interval when the device is moving — sending updates more
frequently based on distance traveled and the smart minimum
settings.
For convoy tracking, you want both intervals short so your Python
tracker gets fresh data. The tradeoff is more mesh traffic and slightly
higher battery usage.
Convoy-Optimized
Position Settings Summary
GPS Mode:                    ENABLED
GPS Update Interval:         15 seconds
Fixed Position:              OFF
Smart Broadcast:             ON
Smart Min Distance:          50 meters
Smart Min Interval:          15 seconds
Broadcast Interval:          30 seconds
Position Flags:              ALTITUDE + SPEED + HEADING + TIMESTAMP

GroupTrack — Route Builder Blueprint
Method-1 (point-to-point snap-2) deliverable + scaffold for Methods 2/3 and drafts. Full flow, function targets, persistence model.
Captured 2026-06-03 from design session &nbsp;·&nbsp; TEMPORARY — fold into Living Checklist §E at recommit, then retire this file.
Status of this doc: scratch reference for the scaffolding pass. Everything here was decided in the 06-03 session and exists nowhere else yet. Once the scaffold is implemented and folded into the Living Checklist (§E Route Creation), delete this file.
A. The model in one paragraph
+ROUTE already exists on the Work-with-Artifacts panel (both maps). Tapping it collapses the artifacts panel and launches the Route+ toolbar in its place. The toolbar offers a single entry — "Start / Continue planning your route" — which opens a source picker (New / Continue in-progress / Copy completed). Three planning methods (point-to-point, draw, suggest) are toggles switchable mid-route, all feeding one shared vertex chain. The build loop is tap-to-place (snap-2) with Add/Undo. Editing is entirely in-memory until a deliberate Save. Exits are explicit and persistence-aware.
B. Snap-2 rule (Method 1, LIVE)
  Trail-first, strict. Within the radius, if ANY trail is in range, snap to the nearest point-on-line of a trail. Tracks are consulted ONLY when no trail is in range (a trail at 40m beats a track at 5m). Tracks fill gaps where no trail exists.
  Nearest-point-on-line, not nearest vertex. Radius is in meters (ground distance, haversine).
  No-snap = free-place. If neither trail nor track is in range, the point lands at the raw tapped coordinate. The segment to it is a straight line (crossing open ground / bridging a network gap). Final geometry, not a placeholder — no deferred snapping.
  Junction discipline. User drops a point AT each junction and selects the next trail explicitly. Between two consecutive snapped points on the SAME line, the segment is the trail-slice (sub-path of that line). Different line, or free point → straight segment. The route never auto-connects past a junction.
  WKT is LON-FIRST (LINESTRING(lon lat, ...)) — confirmed against SpatialDbManager.wktToGeoJsonCoords.
C. The three methods (toggle mid-route, shared chain)
  MethodGesturePan/zoomState
  1 · Point-to-point snap-2 LIVETap = place vertexPan + zoom livetapIntent=PLACE_VERTEX, dragIntent=PAN
  2 · Draw route SOONFinger-trace; snap-2 on each lift; line led ahead of finger (visual offset only — store true/snapped point)Pan OFF during trace, explicit toggle to repositiondragIntent=TRACE
  3 · Suggest routes SOONDrop key points → planner returns ~3-5 candidates w/ distance + POIsPan + zoom liveNeeds trail-network graph (topology) — far future; shapes .gpkg work
Two-axis rail: tapIntent (what a tap means) and dragIntent (PAN vs TRACE) are independent. A method is a named preset over the two. Build the dragIntent axis in from day one (pinned to PAN for Method 1) so Method 2 fills a branch instead of re-architecting the drag handler.
Methods combine per-segment. Finger-draw is specifically for paths VISIBLE on the tile but NOT in the spatial model. One route freely mixes tapped trail-slices, straight gap-bridges, and hand-traced segments — chosen per-segment, switched via the toolbar toggle.
D. Persistence model — in-memory until Save
  While working: in-memory only. The vertex chain lives in RouteManager.vertices. Zero file or DB impact during editing. The on-disk draft (if resumed) stays exactly as opened.
  In-progress drafts = private JSON in app-internal storage (context.filesDir, NOT the public Documents drive — not synced, not media-indexed, not user-visible as files). Carries the full vertex chain (lat/lon/lineId/lineType/segmentIndex/t/snapped) + name + last-modified. The chain preserves snap provenance so resume restores the builder exactly.
  Completed routes = spatial DB row (the routes table). Drafts NEVER touch the spatial DB. Only completed routes are eligible for AWS sync — this keeps the shared spatial model clean (no half-built routes propagate).
  A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both. The transition is the one moment a delete pairs with an insert.
  Save = the only write (temp-then-rename for safety; create for NEW, overwrite for RESUMED). Discard = no write (drop memory, file untouched). Delete = remove file. No original-chain snapshot needed — disk is always the last-saved state.
E. Exit model (the part to get right)
Save completed (toolbar, always available, requires ≥2 vertices): buildWktAndBbox → insertRoute → delete draft file if one existed (graduation) → exit. This is the one affirmative "done" save.
Guarded exit — leaving with an un-completed route prompts, and the options depend on origin:
  OriginExit options
  NEW route (no file yet)Save as draft (create JSON) &nbsp;|&nbsp; Discard (no save, nothing was on disk)
  RESUMED draft (file exists)Save changes (overwrite JSON) &nbsp;|&nbsp; Discard changes (no save, file stays as opened) &nbsp;|&nbsp; Delete in-progress (remove file)
F. Work with Drafts
  List in-progress drafts (name + last-modified) — reads the private draft dir.
  Resume → load chain into memory → redraw partial route on current map → re-arm toolbar in add-point mode.
  Delete → remove draft file (nothing in DB to touch — no orphans).
G. Edit-of-existing
Completed routes are immutable (snap provenance is lost once flattened to LINESTRING). To change one: Copy a completed route as the starting chain for a NEW route (original untouched). Rename/delete of completed routes lives on the route maintenance screen (separate open item). True in-place re-edit deferred.
H. Deploy checklist — 13 user-contact points
  #ControlFunction targetFirst pass
  1+ROUTE (artifacts panel)onAddRoute → collapse panel + launch toolbarDEPLOY

  4Continue in-progressload draft JSON → repopulate + redrawSCAFFOLD

Everything else scaffolded as a visible "coming soon" placeholder linked to its checklist item. Discard exit works trivially (drop memory). Draft Save + RESUMED path activate with the draft-I/O patch.

J. Scaffold build order
  +ROUTE → collapse artifacts panel + launch Route+ toolbar — BOTH screens, identical, one pass (avoid drift).
  Bridge: onMapTap mirroring onMapLongPress, gated on route mode — both screens.
  JS: route-mode polyline draw (feed building chain via existing route path) — both map HTMLs.

  var d=document.getElementById('demo');

Route+ Toolbar — UI PACT
The agreed UI spec for route creation. Build the actual Route+ toolbar against this. Approved look &amp; feel: RouteBuilder_Toolbar_FINAL_v3.
Locked 2026-06-04 &nbsp;·&nbsp; supersedes the look-and-feel mockups &nbsp;·&nbsp; the build target for the snap-2 slice
The test this pact enforces: when the panel is built, every use case with a defined action must appear on the panel (or be explicitly assigned to Work-with-Artifacts → Routes) with its proper action associated. No orphan actions; no actions without a home.
1. Panel split rule
The Route+ toolbar is for CREATE / BUILD only. Every other route action — copy a completed route, edit / rename / delete a completed route, view detail — lives in the Work-with-Artifacts panel under Routes (SEL/EDIT). Toolbar = build; artifacts panel = manage.
2. Panel behavior (real-estate)
  BehaviorHowNote
  Accordion collapse / expandchevron on header; collapses to header (Route+ + point count)same pattern as Work-with-Artifacts panel
  Draggablededicated grip handle (top strip)drag on the handle ONLY — never on a tap control (avoids the QUEUES tap-vs-drag collision)
  Save / Discard always visiblesingle-level toolbar row; stays reachable even when the build controls are collapsedfrequently-used exit actions — never hidden behind the accordion
  Position + state persistenceremember last position + collapsed state, per mapties to the session map-JSON idea (TBD when built)

4. Lives elsewhere — Work-with-Artifacts → Routes (SEL/EDIT)

5. The only write points (persistence model)
Everything is in-memory while building. The ONLY writes: Save in-progress (create draft JSON), Save with changes (overwrite draft JSON), Save as completed (insertRoute DB row + delete draft JSON if one existed — graduation). NEVER written on: Roll back, Discard, remove-unsaved. A route is EITHER a draft-file OR a DB-row, never both. Drafts = private JSON in app-internal storage; completed = spatial DB row.
6. First-pass working loop (the snap-2 slice we build next)
+ROUTE → New (Add ON) → place snapped points → toggle Add OFF / collapse / drag aside to see the map → Undo as needed → Save as completed → buildWktAndBbox → insertRoute → route saved as DB row, drawn gold dashed → exit. Discard (new route) clears the screen, no write. Everything marked "soon" is a visible placeholder linked to its checklist item; the draft-JSON legs (Amend In-Progress, in-progress Save, roll-back) activate with the draft-I/O pass.
7. Logic already built (RouteManager, undeployed)
SnapResult, parseWktLine (lon-first), haversineMeters, nearestOnSegment, nearestPointOnLines, snap (trail-first/track-fallback), Vertex, addVertex/undoVertex/clearRoute/routeVertices, sliceLine, buildSegments, buildWktAndBbox. DB: insertRoute, queryRoutesByViewport; JS bridge updateRoutes/showRoutes wired (gold dashed). Nav route ConvoyRoutes.ConvoyRouteCreate wired to a stub screen. The snap-2 slice wires the toolbar to this existing logic.

Route Lifecycle — Adaptive Save / Discard
DESIGN + STUB→FUNCTION MANIFEST · for approval before any code is written
2026-06-05 · based on RouteBuilder_Toolbar_FINAL_v3, RouteSaveDiscard_Rules, RouteWriteFunction_DataContract, RouteCreation_Screen_ProcessFlow · recovery base commit 204405fc7
  LIVE (built, committed)
  SOON (to be written — this work)
  SAVE surface
  DISCARD surface
  annotation / rule callout
  Core rule (governs the whole flow): a route is EITHER an in-process JSON file OR a completed spatial-DB row — never both. The JSON is interim storage holding the SAME data the completed-save consumes (the vertex chain), so a route can be picked up, redisplayed, and editing continued. Graduation writes the DB row and deletes the JSON.
  Adaptive principle: Save and Discard are each ONE entry point that opens a CHOICE SCREEN. The current route STATE (new vs resumed · ≥2 pts · draft-on-disk) determines which choices the screen presents. Both behave symmetrically.
1 · The toolbar (build-only) — current approved design, annotated
  Panel-split rule: the Route+ toolbar BUILDS only. Copy / rename / edit / delete a COMPLETED route lives in Work-with-Artifacts → Routes (SEL/EDIT), never here. The toolbar's only persistence actions are Save and Discard, both adaptive.

2 · Adaptive SAVE screen — choices driven by route state
  Tapping Save opens a full screen. What it offers depends on whether the route is NEW or a RESUMED draft, and on point count. The screen is the disambiguator — one Save entry, state-driven choices.
      Save route
      How do you want to save?
      STATE: new route · 3 pts placed
         Save as completed route LIVE
        Finish it. Builds WKT + bbox from the vertex chain and writes ONE route row to the spatial DB. Appears in Work-with-Artifacts → Routes.Condition: needs ≥2 points (else disabled w/ hint).
         Save in progress SOON
        Keep working later. Writes a DRAFT JSON holding the full vertex chain. NOT in the spatial DB. Resume via "Amend In-Progress".
         Cancel
        Back to building. No write.
    SAVE screen when route is new.
      Save route
      This route was opened from a saved draft.
      STATE: resumed draft "Bar 10 North" · 6 pts
         Save as completed (graduate) SOON
        Finish it. Same completed-save path → DB row, THEN delete the draft JSON (route becomes a DB-row, no longer a draft).Condition: needs ≥2 points.
         Save changes to draft SOON
        Keep it a draft. OVERWRITES the existing draft JSON with the current vertex chain.
         Cancel
        Back to building. No write.
    SAVE screen when route is a resumed draft.
3 · Adaptive DISCARD screen — same pattern, state-driven
  Tapping Discard opens a full screen, symmetric to Save. A NEW route just clears (with a confirm). A RESUMED draft offers roll-back vs delete. Discard NEVER writes except the explicit "delete draft" choice.
      Discard route
      Leave without saving?
      STATE: new route · not saved anywhere
         Discard &amp; exit LIVE
        Clears the unsaved route from the screen and exits route mode. NO write (nothing was ever persisted).
         Keep building
        Back to building. Route stays on screen.
    DISCARD screen when route is new.
      Discard route
      This route was opened from a saved draft.
      STATE: resumed draft "Bar 10 North"
         Roll back to last save SOON
        Drop THIS session's edits. The draft JSON on disk is UNTOUCHED — exiting just abandons in-memory changes. (Revert = reload the unchanged file.) NO write.
         Delete in-progress route SOON
        Remove the draft JSON entirely (prune a dead in-process route). This is the ONLY discard path that writes (a delete).
         Keep building
        Back to building. No change.
    DISCARD screen when route is a resumed draft.
4 · The rules that control the process flow
  STATESave tapped → screen offersDiscard tapped → screen offers
    NEW, &lt;2 pts
    Save-completed disabled (need ≥2) · Save in-progress soon · Cancel
    Discard &amp; exit live · Keep building
    NEW, ≥2 pts
    Save-completed live · Save in-progress soon · Cancel
    Discard &amp; exit live · Keep building
    RESUMED, &lt;2 pts
    Graduate disabled · Save-changes-to-draft soon · Cancel
    Roll back soon · Delete in-progress soon · Keep building
    RESUMED, ≥2 pts
    Graduate (+delete draft) soon · Save-changes-to-draft soon · Cancel
    Roll back soon · Delete in-progress soon · Keep building
  The deciding conditions (what the adaptive screens read): currentDraftId (null = NEW · set = RESUMED) · routeVertexCount() ≥ 2 · (implicitly) draft-on-disk = same as RESUMED. These are the ONLY inputs that shape the screens.
5 · The three writes — the entire persistence surface
  WriteTriggered byStatus
  create draft JSONSave → "Save in progress" (NEW)SOON
  overwrite draft JSONSave → "Save changes to draft" (RESUMED)SOON
  insertRoute (+ delete draft if resumed)Save → "Save as completed" / "Graduate"LIVE (insertRoute half) · SOON (draft-delete half)
  delete draft JSONDiscard → "Delete in-progress"SOON
Everything else is in-memory until a deliberate Save. Roll-back, discard-new, and cancel NEVER write.

    var pts=[[15,20],[80,75],[150,40],[215,60]];
    for(var i=0;i<pts.length-1;i++){var x1=pts[i][0],y1=pts[i][1],x2=pts[i+1][0],y2=pts[i+1][1];
      var len=Math.round(Math.hypot(x2-x1,y2-y1)),ang=Math.atan2(y2-y1,x2-x1)*180/Math.PI;
      var s=document.createElement('div');s.className='seg';s.style.left=x1+'px';s.style.top=y1+'px';s.style.width=len+'px';s.style.transform='rotate('+ang+'deg)';d.appendChild(s);}
    pts.forEach(function(p){var el=document.createElement('div');el.className='pin';el.style.left=p[0]+'px';el.style.top=p[1]+'px';d.appendChild(el);});}
  draw('demo');

Route Lifecycle — SETTLED MODEL + Work Sequence
Hit-the-ground-running spec. Reflects all 2026-06-05 simplifications. Build directly from this.
2026-06-05 · recovery base 204405fc7 (HEAD 984e6e54d, docs-only ahead) · supersedes earlier draft of this doc · sources: RouteSaveDiscard_Rules, RouteWriteFunction_DataContract, RouteCreation_ProcessFlow, Blueprint Addendum 9 (FINAL exit model)
  WHAT CHANGED TODAY (simplifications that make this clean):
  1. NO interim "save &amp; continue." Save always EXITS. To keep working: Save In Progress → then RE-SELECT the route from the In-Progress list. Save closes; select reopens. No mid-session state promotion.
  2. In-progress identity = the typed NAME (set at New). A route ID is assigned ONLY when it graduates to the spatial DB (under DB dedup rules). Draft world = name; DB world = id.
  3. State is set at LAUNCH and never changes mid-session. New = new route. Select In-Progress = resumed draft. The adaptive screens read a state that's fixed for the whole editing session.
  4. Test before functions: EMULATE the In-Progress selector (hardcoded draft list + hardcoded vertex chain). The entire adaptive flow becomes walkable with ZERO file I/O.

Each item gets its own detailed design pass (like this doc) before code. Item 1 is fully specced below and ready to build once the fallback AAB is live on Play.
1 · Core rules (govern the whole lifecycle)
  R1 — Either/or: a route is EITHER an in-progress draft (JSON file) OR a completed route (spatial-DB row). Never both. Graduation writes the DB row and deletes the draft.
  R2 — Identity: in-progress identity = the typed NAME. DB identity = route id, assigned at graduation under dedup/alias rules. No route id exists while a route is a draft.
  R3 — Save exits: every Save action (completed or in-progress) EXITS route mode. To continue editing an in-progress route, re-select it from the In-Progress list. No mid-session continue, no in-place state promotion.
  R4 — State fixed at launch: New ⇒ NEW for the whole session. Select In-Progress ⇒ RESUMED for the whole session. Adaptive screens read this fixed state.
  R5 — Writes are deliberate &amp; minimal: the ONLY writes are create-draft, overwrite-draft, insertRoute(+delete-draft), delete-draft. Roll-back, discard-new, cancel NEVER write. Everything else in-memory.
  R6 — Both maps: identical on convoy map (ConvoyScreen) and planning map (ConvoyMapViewerScreen), driving shared RouteManager. Two-file mirror. Endings: ConvoyScreen LF · ViewerScreen CRLF · Toolbar CRLF. cat -A before every patch.
  R7 — Vertices not wkt: the draft stores the full vertex chain (lat,lon,lineId,lineType,segmentIndex,t,snapped). wkt/bbox are DERIVED at graduation by replaying buildWktAndBbox, so a resumed draft graduates through the IDENTICAL completed-save path.
2 · The toolbar — Save/Discard on the COLLAPSED bar
Placement decision: Save and Discard live on the collapsed title bar (always reachable in one tap, no real-estate cost) AND in the expanded panel. Build-only toolbar; copy/rename/delete completed routes live in Work-with-Artifacts → Routes.

      Save route

         Cancel
        Back to building. No write.
    SAVE — NEW route.
      Save route
      Editing in-progress "Bar 10 North".
      STATE: RESUMED · name "Bar 10 North" · 6 pts
         Save as completed (graduate) SOON
        Same completed-save path → DB row, THEN deleteDraft (R1: no longer a draft). Needs ≥2 pts. → exit.
         Save with changes SOON
        overwriteDraft (same name) → EXIT. Reselect to continue again.
         Cancel
        Back to building. No write.
    SAVE — RESUMED draft.
4 · Adaptive DISCARD — symmetric, state-fixed
      Discard route
      Leave without saving?
      STATE: NEW · nothing on disk
         Discard &amp; exit LIVE
        clearRoute + clearBuildLine + exit route mode. NO write (nothing persisted).
         Keep building
        Back to building.
    DISCARD — NEW route (acts directly; prompt only if you want a confirm).
      Discard route
      Editing in-progress "Bar 10 North".
      STATE: RESUMED · name "Bar 10 North"
         Roll back to last save SOON
        Drop THIS session's edits; draft JSON on disk UNTOUCHED. Implemented as: re-run openDraft (reload the unchanged file). NO write.
         Delete in-progress SOON
        deleteDraft — remove the JSON entirely. The ONLY discard path that writes (a delete).
         Keep building
        Back to building.
    DISCARD — RESUMED draft (prompt: roll back | delete).

6 · Rules table — what each state presents
  STATE (fixed at launch)Save tapped → screenDiscard tapped → screen
  NEW, &lt;2 ptsSave-completed disabled · Save-in-progress soon · CancelDiscard&amp;exit live · Keep building
  NEW, ≥2 ptsSave-completed live · Save-in-progress soon · CancelDiscard&amp;exit live · Keep building

  RESUMED, ≥2 ptsGraduate(+deleteDraft) soon · Save-with-changes soon · CancelRoll back soon · Delete soon · Keep building

7 · Functions to be written (LAST — after UI hardens)
RouteManager stays pure (no Context/file I/O). The draft store is a NEW Context-holding component RouteDraftStore. JSON shape: { schemaVersion, name, createdAt, updatedAt, method, vertices:[{lat,lon,lineId,lineType,segmentIndex,t,snapped}…] }. No id, no wkt, no bbox. Name is identity (R2). V2.7 SCOPING &mdash; vector rendering &amp; the MapLibre question2026-07-26 &middot; INTERNAL &middot; kickoff input for the CONVOY TRACKING REWRITE &middot; nothing built, nothing decided
Why this document exists. The question came up mid-release on 07-26 while 2.6d was uploading, and it turned out to bear directly on 2.7. Fred's framing is the reason it is scoped here rather than deferred: "2.7 is a rewrite of convoy tracking functionality &mdash; may be the point we need to introduce these discussions." That is correct, and it changes the economics completely (see &#11088; THE SEQUENCING ARGUMENT). This is analysis, not a plan. Nothing here is committed.
&#11088;&#11088; THE MEASUREMENT THAT STARTED IT
The 07-26 delete-area log showed a single DEL SAT job walking three separate stores:
storez18 removedwhat it holds
SAT10,295base imagery &mdash; photographic
SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT10,292road names
SAT_LABELS_PLACES10,294place names
Near-perfect thirds. Fred's read, and it is the whole insight: "it is 65,000 tiles because of the three layers. if vectors eliminated the street name and points of interest overlays we are downloading 1/3 of what we download as sat images."
&#9888; TWO OF THE THREE ARE TEXT, NOT PHOTOGRAPHY. Road names and place labels are the single most compressible thing on a map &mdash; a few hundred strings and coordinates per tile &mdash; and they are currently delivered as photographs of words, at the same cost per tile as satellite imagery, re-fetched at every zoom level.
The arithmetic, on bar 10
sourcetodaywith vector labels + vector topo
SAT base imagery~21,700~21,700 raster (unavoidable)
SAT transport labels~21,700vector
SAT place labels~21,700vector
TOPO21,000vector
TOPO+21,000vector
RASTER TOTAL107,000~21,700
&asymp;80% reduction &mdash; and it stacks on the corridor work already shipped. Bar 10 went from 1,000,000+ tiles (bbox) to 107,000 (corridor) this week. Vector labels would take the same track to ~21,700.
&#9888; WHY VECTOR IS SMALL &mdash; the mechanism, not the format. Vector tiles stop at ~z14 and the client renders deeper by scaling geometry. Since tile counts QUADRUPLE per zoom, z15&ndash;18 is roughly 98% of everything downloaded. Vector does not shrink those levels; it removes them. That is why a whole-state vector extract is comparable in size to a handful of today's raster corridors.
&#11088;&#11088;&#11088; THE SEQUENCING ARGUMENT &mdash; why 2.7 and not later
The dominant cost of this work is NOT MapLibre. It is operating on frozen code.
ConvoyScreen.kt is frozen to protect the Kotlin&harr;JS&harr;Leaflet&harr;self-saving-setView&harr;shared-MapStateStore tangle. A convoy tracking rewrite has to open exactly that tangle anyway.
So the choice is not "rewrite convoy now, renderer later." It is: rewrite that layer ONCE with MapLibre as the target, or TWICE.
Doing it once is dramatically cheaper.
The tracking rewrite then gets built against rotation, pitch and data-driven styling rather than being ported onto them afterwards.
Convoy tracking may benefit more than the map does: live cart positions are the textbook case for data-driven styling &mdash; heading, speed, staleness and lead-cart status driving symbol rotation and colour from feature properties, instead of tearing down and rebuilding markers. A tilted terrain view is also arguably more useful while riding than while planning.
&#9888; This is the single strongest argument in this document. Everything else is secondary to it.
&#11088;&#11088;&#11088; THE CROSS-PLATFORM MULTIPLIER (the point that was nearly missed)
Per [[grouptrack-crossplatform]], the 07-04 planning session established that the convoy/planning presentation is ALREADY web (Leaflet/HTML/JS in a WebView), and that the leverage for iPad and PC lives in the web layer, not in Swift. SwiftUI was rejected for presentation precisely because it gives zero reuse of that layer.
&#11088; MapLibre GL JS is a WEB library. It runs identically in an Android WebView, an iPad WKWebView, and a PC browser.
So a renderer swap done in the shared web layer is not an Android cost. It is a one-time change to the ~90% presentation layer that all three surfaces inherit:
Android &mdash; the immediate target.
iPad &mdash; inherits it free, whichever way the A/B mesh-source decision goes. The iPad app is a native shell hosting this same web layer.
PC planning app &mdash; inherits it free, and gains the most: terrain, pitch and vector styling in a plain browser, with no offline-tile constraint at all.
&#9888; The corollary is a REAL RISK: doing the tracking rewrite on Leaflet bakes Leaflet into the layer iPad and PC are both waiting on. That is a decision with a long tail, made by omission.
Also aligns with the service-layer mandate: the renderer is presentation. Swapping it should touch logic-free panels, not the service layer &mdash; and the degree to which it does NOT is a useful read on how entangled the current code really is (the 07-04 "logic-entanglement inventory" question, answered from a different angle).
What was actually validated (browser prototype, 07-26)
vector_label_prototype.html &mdash; Esri World Imagery raster + OSM vector labels + Esri's own raster label layers as toggles, over identical imagery. No build, no device, no touching frozen code.
CONFIRMED Esri raster imagery and OSM vector labels composite correctly. Fred: "the image overlays look perfect."
CONFIRMED &mdash; AND THE SURPRISE OSM vector labels carry MORE data than Esri's downloaded roads and places layers. Fred: "much more data in the vector labels then the downloaded esri roads and places db." &#9888; This was the OPPOSITE of the predicted outcome &mdash; the expectation was thin OSM coverage in remote Utah and a coverage-for-size trade. Instead: more content AND less storage.
CONFIRMED NEGATIVE OSM TRAIL coverage is sparse. Fred: "i see very few trails render." &#11088; So OSM is a BASEMAP, not a trail source. grouptrack.gpkg and the national trail model remain the authority. This closes a question that was genuinely open at the start of the discussion.
CONFIRMED 3D terrain works and Leaflet cannot do it at all &mdash; not tilt, not rotation, not terrain. Elevation comes from a separate raster-DEM source (terrarium encoding), capped ~z13, so a whole-state DEM is small.
&#11088; Terrain-RGB is worth more than the 3D view. Those tiles encode metres-above-sea-level in RGB rather than a pre-rendered grey hillshade, so the CLIENT holds raw elevation. That enables slope-angle shading computed on device &mdash; which for an OHV app is arguably more useful than satellite imagery, and costs a fraction of it.
&#9940; CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN ANALYSIS (recorded so they are not repeated)
&#9940; I leaned on Esri per-tile cost. Fred: "we pay nothing for esri downloads and data." That pillar is GONE. Any future argument for this work must stand on storage, download time and capability &mdash; not economics.
MapLibre is FREE &mdash; BSD, no API key, no usage tier. (Fred asked whether it carried a cost; it does not. The prototype uses it with no key.) The cost of this work is developer time on frozen code, nothing else.
&#9940; My first sizing was wrong by half. I said ~39% because I assumed satellite stays whole. Fred corrected it by pointing at the three-store split &mdash; two of the three are labels. The real figure is ~80%. The delete log had shown this hours earlier and I did not connect it.
Vector cannot replace satellite imagery. Aerial photography is inherently raster. This is physics, not tooling &mdash; no vector source substitutes for it, ever.
The five work items
THE RENDERER (the real work). Leaflet cannot draw vector tiles. MapLibre GL JS in the same WebView. spatial_artifacts.js is rewritten: L.polyline calls become GeoJSON sources + layer specs; per-feature click handlers become queryRenderedFeatures (MapLibre gives NO DOM per feature). The data path from SpatialDbManager is UNCHANGED &mdash; MapLibre takes GeoJSON natively, exactly as Leaflet does.
TILE INTERCEPTION. Same shape, different hook: MapLibre's addProtocol replaces the WebView request intercept. Still serving bytes out of MBTiles.
&#9888; GLYPHS &mdash; the requirement that is easy to miss. MapLibre renders text from font PBFs fetched by URL. Offline means BUNDLING them in assets (a few MB per fontstack). There is no equivalent in the raster world, so nothing in the pipeline handles it today. Miss it and labels silently do not render offline.
MAP STATE. MapLibre's camera adds bearing and pitch to centre/zoom &mdash; MapStateStore and the self-saving setView need rework. This is the piece nearest the frozen tangle.
GETTING LABEL TILES ONTO THE DEVICE. planetiler --only-layers=place,poi,transportation_name,water_name,mountain_peak over a Utah bbox produces a labels-only tileset. Then a product decision: bundle it, or a "download this region" flow &mdash; one file once, versus per-corridor forever.
&#9888; ONLY THEN drop the two overlay layers from SAT's entry in getDownloadSources(). That is a one-line config change &mdash; but it must come LAST, or satellite ships with no labels at all.
What does NOT change (important &mdash; nothing is obsoleted)
Fred asked directly whether this obsoletes the artifact data. It leverages it. The base layer and the artifacts are separate concerns sharing a canvas.
Untouched: grouptrack.gpkg and the national trail model &middot; both databases &middot; all three engines (ingestion, AWS bbox distribution, viewport lazy-load) &middot; SpatialDbManager WKT storage and geom_hash identity &middot; ArtifactListPanel, search, CRUD &middot; the rating/share work &middot; corridor downloads (they derive from YOUR geometry, not the base) &middot; the queue, priorities, and the new delete worker (all format-agnostic &mdash; MBTiles stores blobs by z/x/y and does not care what is in them).
Satellite does not have to go. MapLibre handles raster and vector sources in ONE map, so SAT stays a toggleable raster layer exactly as today.
Your artifacts stay GeoJSON overlays. Tiles are a static read-only artifact &mdash; a poor fit for tracks the user records and edits. Tiling is for DISTRIBUTED REFERENCE data (the national trail model), not user-authored data.
&#11088; The gain for artifacts: DATA-DRIVEN STYLING. MapLibre paint properties are expressions over feature properties &mdash; so the 1&ndash;5 star rating being added to track_properties, plus tracktype or shared, can drive colour and width directly from the data, with no extra layers and no per-feature style callbacks. Leaflet cannot do this natively. Demonstrated working in the prototype.
&#9888; One real design tension: OSM's vector base ALREADY CONTAINS trails (highway=track, highway=path). You would have OSM trails underneath and curated GeoPackage trails on top &mdash; duplicated and possibly offset by metres. Filter them from the base style, or style them very faintly. The second option is an opportunity: faint "unverified" OSM trails become a discovery surface &mdash; showing riders what exists on the ground that is not yet curated, and showing you where the national trail model has gaps.
Sequencing (if it proceeds)
PLANNING MAP FIRST. ALWAYS. MapLibre with EXISTING raster sources and EXISTING GeoJSON overlays &mdash; no vector tiles, no terrain. This proves the renderer swap in isolation. &#9888; Otherwise you are debugging a rendering swap AND a tracking rewrite simultaneously, and neither failure is attributable &mdash; the same one-unknown-at-a-time rule that governs the Mac/KMP sequencing.
Add the vector label source alongside, so the on-device comparison matches what the browser prototype showed.
Then drop the Esri label layers from getDownloadSources().
Convoy last, and carefully &mdash; as part of the tracking rewrite, not before it.
Open questions
Label coverage at z16&ndash;18. The browser comparison was at mid-zoom. Vector labels come from a z14 tile and should render crisp at any zoom &mdash; but Esri's raster labels are densest at high zoom and that is the fair test. Not yet done.
Does TOPO/TOPO+ go vector too, or only the labels? The ~80% figure assumes both. Labels alone is ~40% and a much smaller change.
Distribution model for label tiles: bundled in the APK (bigger install, zero friction) vs downloadable region packs (smaller install, a new flow to build). Ties to V3.0 ride-package distribution.
Contours. OSM has none &mdash; they come from DEM. USGS 1/3 arc-second is the US source; OpenMapTiles also publishes worldwide contour datasets. Only matters if TOPO goes vector.
Does this pull the KMP/service-layer work forward? The renderer swap is a natural moment to test how cleanly presentation separates from logic &mdash; which is the 07-04 entanglement inventory by another name.
Ruled out
&#9940; Vector satellite imagery &mdash; does not exist, cannot exist.
&#9940; OSM as a trail data source &mdash; coverage confirmed sparse on device. Basemap only.
&#9940; Tiling user-authored artifacts &mdash; tiles are static and read-only; tracks and routes are edited constantly. GeoJSON overlays stay.
&#9940; Doing this as a standalone V2.6 task &mdash; weeks of surgery on frozen code, while SAT-frozen-at-15, the ETA at ~50&times;, and the markComplete refreshMode collision are all still open. It earns its place ONLY as part of the 2.7 tracking rewrite.
Artifacts from this session
vector_label_prototype.html &mdash; browser prototype: Esri raster + OSM vector labels + Esri raster labels for comparison + 3D terrain + hillshade + a file loader for your own GeoJSON, with rating-driven line colour.
gpx_to_geojson_2026-07-26.py &mdash; standard-library GPX&rarr;GeoJSON converter for feeding the prototype real tracks.
Sources: OpenMapTiles (BSD + CC-BY, self-hostable) &middot; Protomaps/PMTiles (single-file, bbox-extractable, ODbL) &middot; Tilemaker and Planetiler (build your own, Lua/CLI tag selection) &middot; OpenTrailMap at opentrailmap.us (OSM trail review) &middot; AWS terrarium DEM tiles (public, no key).

Snap-2 Implementation Plan
Pre-flight research for the snap-2 logic slice. The toolbar UI is pact-compliant (this session); this plan is the wiring that comes next.
Researched 2026-06-04 from function_universe / where_used / field_crossref · NO code written · walk in and patch
Headline finding: the entire snap-2 path composes from functions that ALREADY EXIST and already compile. No new parsing, no new query, no new geometry code. Two call-site edits + one stub fill. The types line up end-to-end — verified below.
1. The snap data-source question — RESOLVED
The open question was: snap(tapLat, tapLon, trails, tracks, radiusM) needs trail + track line lists at tap time, but the tap handler only has lat/lon. Where do the lists come from?
Answer: query the viewport at tap time. The types match exactly with zero transformation:
queryTrailsByViewport(south,west,north,east,limit): List&lt;Map&lt;String,String?&gt;&gt; (SpatialDbManager:265)
queryTracksByViewport(...): List&lt;Map&lt;String,String?&gt;&gt; (SpatialDbManager:342)
snap() wants exactly trails: List&lt;Map&lt;String,String?&gt;&gt;, tracks: List&lt;Map&lt;String,String?&gt;&gt;
And the KEYS match: snap→nearestPointOnLines reads line["geometry"] (RouteManager:114) and line[idKey] (115), where idKey is "trail_id"/"track_id". The viewport queries return maps with exactly those keys (same maps buildTrailGeoJson consumes via trail["geometry"]). Drop-in.
Recommendation: query the viewport ONCE when route mode is entered (or on viewport change), cache trails+tracks in two vals the tap handler closes over. Re-querying on every tap is wasteful and risks lag. The current map already tracks lastViewportSouth/West/North/East (seen in onEditDisplay) — reuse those bounds. Cache invalidates on pan/zoom (the viewport-change callback already fires).
2. The two edits (exact call sites)
Edit A — snap on tap (replace free-place)
Both screens, the onMapTap bridge. Today (ConvoyScreen ~522-525, ConvoyMapViewerScreen ~476-479):
RouteManager.addVertex(RouteManager.freeVertex(lat, lon))
val pts = RouteManager.routeVertices().joinToString(...) { "[${it.lat},${it.lon}]" }
webViewRef...evaluateJavascript("drawBuildLine('" + pts + "')", null)
Becomes:
val s = RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, cachedTrails, cachedTracks, SNAP_RADIUS_M)
val v = if (s != null) RouteManager.snapToVertex(s) else RouteManager.freeVertex(lat, lon)
RouteManager.addVertex(v)
val pts = RouteManager.routeVertices().joinToString(...) { "[${it.lat},${it.lon}]" }
webViewRef...evaluateJavascript("drawBuildLine('" + pts + "')", null)
Only fires when Add is ARMED (green). The toolbar now owns addArmed; the host must know the armed state at tap time. Cleanest: onAddPointModeArmed already pushes setRouteMode(true/false) to JS — extend it to carry the armed flag, and gate the JS tap-emit on it (tap only emits when armed). Decide next session: gate in JS (cleaner — pan works when disarmed) vs gate in Kotlin.
Edit B — Save completed (fill the stub)
The onSaveCompleted = { } stub at both call sites. Fill with:
// lineGeom lambda: lineId -> that line's WKT -> List&lt;DoubleArray&gt;
val byId: Map&lt;String, String&gt; = (cachedTrails + cachedTracks)
    .mapNotNull { m -> val id = m["trail_id"] ?: m["track_id"]; val g = m["geometry"]
                       if (id != null && g != null) id to g else null }.toMap()
val res = RouteManager.buildWktAndBbox { lineId -> byId[lineId]?.let { RouteManager.parseWktLine(it) } }
if (res != null) {
    val (wkt, bbox) = res   // bbox = [minLat,maxLat,minLon,maxLon]
    val name = "Route " + System.currentTimeMillis()   // naming UX = later
    SpatialDbManager.insertRoute(name, wkt, bbox[0], bbox[1], bbox[2], bbox[3])
    RouteManager.clearRoute()
    // redraw: re-fire route lazy-load so the new DB row draws gold dashed
    // (reuse existing queryRoutesByViewport -> buildRouteGeoJson -> updateRoutes/showRoutes)
    webViewRef...evaluateJavascript("setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine();", null)
}
parseWktLine(wkt): List&lt;DoubleArray&gt; (RouteManager:42) is EXACTLY the return type buildWktAndBbox's lambda needs. The lambda is a one-liner over the cached maps. No new code.

4. Open questions to settle next session (not blockers)
Q1 — armed-state gating: when Add is RED (off), a tap should PAN, not place. Gate the tap-emit in JS (cleaner) or in Kotlin? The toolbar owns addArmed; the host needs it. Likely: extend onAddPointModeArmed to push the flag to JS, JS only emits onMapTap when armed.
Q2 — SNAP_RADIUS_M value: blueprint says meters, tune by testing. Start ~30m? Define as a const, adjust on device.
Q3 — cache timing: query trails/tracks on route-mode entry, or on every viewport change while in route mode? (Pan during build → stale cache → snaps to off-screen geometry.) Recommend: re-query on viewport-change while routeMode is true.
Q4 — VERIFY on the box: confirm drawBuildLine, setRouteMode, clearBuildLine exist in convoy_map.html (they're called today, so they should — but the HTML wasn't fully in AllDocs to confirm here). One grep: grep -n "function drawBuildLine\|function setRouteMode\|function clearBuildLine" app/src/main/assets/convoy_map.html
Q5 — naming UX: first pass auto-names ("Route &lt;timestamp&gt;"). A name prompt is a later refinement, not the proven slice.
5. Suggested slice order (smallest first)
Save-completed first (Edit B) using the current free-place tap. This proves the whole spine end-to-end: place free points → Save → buildWktAndBbox → insertRoute → DB row → redraw. No snap yet. Smallest provable win.
Then snap-on-tap (Edit A) + the cache. Now points snap to trails.
Then armed-state gating (Q1) so RED actually pans.
This order means the FIRST build proves "a route reaches the DB and draws" — the highest-value, lowest-risk confirmation — before adding snap complexity. Matches the one-use-case-end-to-end discipline.
6. One-file-per-patch note
Edits A and B touch the SAME two screen files (ConvoyScreen.kt, ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt). Per one-file-per-patch: do ConvoyScreen first, build, test on device, then mirror to ConvoyMapViewerScreen. OR — since they must stay identical (drift risk) — do both in one patch but treat it as one logical change, build once. Recommend the latter for route mode (the two must match), as the blueprint's scaffold build-order already notes ("BOTH screens, identical, one pass").

Snap-2 Implementation Plan (v2)
Pre-flight for the snap-2 logic slice. v2 corrects the data-source section after reviewing the lazy-load code.
Researched 2026-06-04 from function_universe / where_used / field_crossref · NO code written · supersedes v1's data-source recommendation
Headline: the entire snap-2 path composes from functions that ALREADY EXIST and compile. Two call-site edits + one stub fill. Types verified end-to-end.
1. Snap data source — CORRECTED after code review
Fred's read was right: the displayed trails/tracks are NOT retained in a Kotlin var. The lazy-load uses LOCAL vals inside the viewport-change callback, builds GeoJSON, hands it to JS, and they go out of scope:
// ConvoyScreen ~720/726, ConvoyMapViewerScreen ~596/601
val trailResultsRaw = queryTrailsByViewport(south, west, north, east, ...)   // local, dropped after JS
val trackResultsRaw = queryTracksByViewport(south, west, north, east, ...)   // local, dropped after JS
... buildTrailGeoJson -> updateTrails(json) ...   // handed to JS, not kept
But the viewport BOUNDS are retained — lastViewportSouth/West/North/East (ConvoyScreen 200-203; same on the viewer). So the fix is trivial and needs ZERO new state.
Recommended: re-query at tap (option 1)
The tap handler already has the retained bounds. Query the same small on-screen set right there and feed snap():
val trails = SpatialDbManager.queryTrailsByViewport(
    lastViewportSouth, lastViewportWest, lastViewportNorth, lastViewportEast)
val tracks = SpatialDbManager.queryTracksByViewport(
    lastViewportSouth, lastViewportWest, lastViewportNorth, lastViewportEast)
val s = RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, SNAP_RADIUS_M)
val v = if (s != null) RouteManager.snapToVertex(s) else RouteManager.freeVertex(lat, lon)
RouteManager.addVertex(v)
Why option 1 over retaining a displayedTrails var: (a) zero new state; (b) zero staleness — it always matches the current viewport bounds, which are kept current by the existing viewport-change callback; (c) it's a handful of items (viewport-limited, 50–200 rows), one fast indexed query per tap. The snap radius then narrows that set to what's near the tap. This is exactly Fred's "retrieve from spatial DB for a handful of items."
Alt (option 2), if tap-query lag ever shows: add var displayedTrails/displayedTracks, assign in the lazy-load where the raw lists are built, tap reads them. More state, small staleness window on fast pan-then-tap. Not needed unless profiling says so.
2. The two edits (exact call sites)
Edit A — snap on tap
Replace the free-place block at ConvoyScreen ~522-525 and ConvoyMapViewerScreen ~476-479 with the option-1 snippet above (query bounds → snap → snapToVertex/freeVertex → addVertex → drawBuildLine). Only when Add is ARMED.
Edit B — Save completed (fill the onSaveCompleted stub)
// build lineId -> WKT lookup from a fresh viewport query (same bounds)
val lines = (queryTrailsByViewport(...bounds...) + queryTracksByViewport(...bounds...))
val byId = lines.mapNotNull { m -> val id = m["trail_id"] ?: m["track_id"]; val g = m["geometry"]
                                   if (id != null && g != null) id to g else null }.toMap()
val res = RouteManager.buildWktAndBbox { id -> byId[id]?.let { RouteManager.parseWktLine(it) } }
if (res != null) {
    val (wkt, bbox) = res                    // bbox = [minLat,maxLat,minLon,maxLon]
    SpatialDbManager.insertRoute("Route " + System.currentTimeMillis(), wkt, bbox[0], bbox[1], bbox[2], bbox[3])
    RouteManager.clearRoute()
    webViewRef...evaluateJavascript("setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine();", null)
    // then re-fire the route lazy-load so the new DB row draws gold dashed
}
For snapped routes that ride a trail, buildSegments needs the line geometry of the snapped vertices' lineIds — hence the byId lookup. For a first proof with FREE points only (no snap), the lambda can return null and segments are straight lines between points — so Edit B works even before Edit A. That's the slice order below.
3. Slice order (smallest provable first)
Edit B with free points — prove: place free points → Save → buildWktAndBbox (straight segments) → insertRoute → DB row → redraw gold dashed. The whole spine, no snap. Highest-value lowest-risk first build.
Edit A — add snap-on-tap (query bounds → snap). Points now snap to trails; buildSegments slices trail geometry via the byId lambda.
Armed-state gating — RED Add actually pans (gate the JS tap-emit on armed).
4. Open questions (next-session decisions, not blockers)
Q1 armed gating: when Add is RED, tap should pan not place. Extend onAddPointModeArmed to push the armed flag to JS; JS emits onMapTap only when armed. (Toolbar owns addArmed now.)
Q2 SNAP_RADIUS_M: const, start ~30m, tune on device.
Q4 VERIFY on box: grep -n "function drawBuildLine\|function setRouteMode\|function clearBuildLine" app/src/main/assets/convoy_map.html (called today, should exist).
Q5 naming: first pass auto-names "Route &lt;ts&gt;"; prompt is a later refinement.
5. Function inventory — all present, all compile
FunctionLocation
snap / snapToVertex / freeVertex / addVertex / undoVertex / clearRoute / routeVertices / buildWktAndBbox / parseWktLineRouteManager (138/169/172/180-184/246/42)

6. One-patch note
Both edits touch ConvoyScreen.kt AND ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt and the two must stay identical (route mode parity). Per the blueprint scaffold order ("BOTH screens, identical, one pass"), do both screens in one patch, build once. This is the documented exception to one-file-per-patch — route mode is inherently a two-file mirror.

Run and paste.You said: does  that mean every page load in the app was running a synch process?does  that mean every page load in the app was running a synch process?7:20 AMClaude responded: Not every page load in the app — specifically every time the map WebView finished loading a page.Not every page load in the app — specifically every time the map WebView finished loading a page. That's onPageFinished on the convoy map's WebView, so it fired when:
the map screen first opens, and
any time that WebView reloads its page (navigating back to the map, the WebView getting recreated on a config change, certain reloads).
It was not firing on non-map screens (settings, import list, etc.) — those don't have this WebView. So "every page load" in the browser-WebView sense, not every Compose screen.
But here's the part that made it a storm rather than just "once per map open": the 06-28 disk log showed the same files processed 5-6× across six different thread IDs with === sync start === appearing mid-stream. A single onPageFinished would be one run. Getting six overlapping runs means the WebView's onPageFinished was firing multiple times in one map session — which it can do (initial load, then re-fires on internal reloads/redraws) — and each fire launched a fresh MainScope().launch with no guard, so they stacked and ran concurrently. Fred pressing RESYNC twice (the :1316 button) on top of that added two more.
And critically: nothing cancelled the previous run before starting the next. MainScope() isn't tied to the screen lifecycle, so even leaving the map didn't stop an in-flight sync. They just piled up.
Why it was wasteful but not destructive: sync is idempotent — every already-processed file just computes its hash, finds it in the DB, and skips. So six concurrent runs over the same 71 files = a lot of redundant parsing and the occasional rename race, but no data loss. That's why it went unnoticed as a correctness bug for a while — it only showed up as the confusing concurrent-thread mess in the log and the "why did RESYNC do nothing visible" feedback gap.
This is also exactly why the clean-room test you proposed needs the :601 trigger gated first. If you restore the 71 originals and then open the map, that loose trigger will immediately fire (possibly several times) and sync the whole collection before you can test create or import in isolation — silently, concurrently, the very behavior we're removing. Kill :601, add the single-flight guard, stand up the control screen to own the run, then do the clean-room restore.

Reading it confirms what we need:
The logic is correct and idempotent. Every file: parse → coords → WKT → computeGeomHash (the key) → trackHashExists(gh) checks the DB by hash → insert if new, rename to &lt;hash&gt;.gpx non-destructively (never deletes, leaves the file in place if target exists). This is the verified-good rewrite. We don't touch the per-file logic.
What's missing for today — three things, all additive:
No single-flight guard. The function has nothing stopping two callers from running the loop concurrently over the same directory. With six overlapping runs that's a rename race (two threads both see EXISTS → will rename, one wins renameTo, the other hits TARGET ALREADY EXISTS). Non-destructive, but it's the storm. A module-level AtomicBoolean running-flag that the function checks at entry and clears in a finally closes this regardless of who calls.
No progress callback. The rolling file-by-file status the control screen needs to display — right now L(...) only writes to logcat + the disk log. We add an optional onProgress: ((String) -&gt; Unit)? param that L also calls, so the screen can stream the same lines live. Disk log stays as-is (it's our ground truth).
skipped is dead — declared, never incremented, always 0 in the recap. Cosmetic, but since we're touching the recap surface we should either wire it or drop it. (Files with no geometry currently continue without counting as skipped — that's arguably what skipped should track.)
The single-flight guard is the one that actually fixes the bug. The callback is what makes the control screen possible. Both are surgical.

Let me play it back to make sure I build the right thing:
Sync's purpose is being redefined. It was built as an always-on, self-healing reconciler that silently masks failures in the create/import paths (a track doesn't save right → sync quietly fixes it on next map load → you never learn create is broken). You want the opposite: sync becomes a manual diagnostic tool — you invoke it deliberately when something looks wrong, and it reports what it found so you can see which process is broken, rather than papering over it.
That means the recap isn't a courtesy toast — it's the diagnostic output. It should tell you, per run, what state the files+DB were actually in:
How many files were already correct (hash-named + in DB) — the healthy baseline
How many were missing from the DB (← create or import failed to insert — this is the signal)
How many were mis-named (not &lt;hash&gt;.gpx — ← a process didn't rename)
How many had no geometry / failed to parse (← corrupt save)
The actual filenames in each problem bucket, so you can trace which track and which process
The current recap (processed / addedRenamed / renamed) half-does this but frames it as healing ("added", "renamed" = "I fixed it"). The diagnostic framing wants it as findings ("N files were missing from the DB — create didn't insert them"). Same data, but the report should make a broken upstream process visible, not silently absorbed.
This also retroactively justifies everything we just did: removing the loose :601 auto-sync wasn't only about the concurrency storm — it was removing the automatic masking. Sync firing on every map load is exactly the mechanism that hid the broken create path for so long. Now it only runs when you ask.
So the SYNC CONTROL SCREEN's job sharpens to: a diagnostic screen. Start tap → runs once → streams per-file findings → ends with a categorized report (healthy / missing-from-DB / mis-named / no-geometry, with filenames). The onProgress feed we just added carries the live findings; the TrackSyncResult recap needs to grow to carry the diagnostic buckets.

The real point you're making is the one that matters:
We've been asking "does sync do what it does correctly" when we should be asking "what should sync actually do." And the answer exposes a hole: sync currently writes only the spatial row (geometry + hash) and renames the file. It does not write the extension DB (track_properties) — so mileage, average speed, duration, etc. are never populated by sync. Those are GPX-derivable (distance from the coords, duration from timestamps, speed from both) — sync parses every point already, so it has the data in hand and throws it away.
This is exactly the paired add/delete contract from the checklist's design queue — and you're right that it's not a "later" item, it belongs in the sync process we're building the surface for:
every spatial track add should ALSO add its track_properties (distance/duration/speed from GPX, filename, shared=0); if the spatial add fails on hash → skip the extension add too.
So the sync process, properly specified, is: per file → parse → hash → (a) present spatial row (existing) and (b) present the extension track_properties row with the derived metrics → rename to &lt;hash&gt;.gpx. Both tables, paired. Right now only (a) happens. That's a genuine functional gap, and the diagnostic value compounds: when you run sync to find what's broken, "N tracks missing their properties" is exactly the kind of finding the visible report should surface.
This means the build order I was about to do (surface first) is backwards. The process has to be correct before we wrap a reporting surface around it — otherwise we build a panel that faithfully reports an incomplete process. So:
First: fix what sync does — add the track_properties write (distance / duration / avg speed / filename / shared=0) paired with the spatial insert, per the add/delete contract.
Then: the control surface reports the now-complete work (spatial + extension, per file).

While you run those, here's the extension-field spec as I understand the design, so we can lock the values sync should populate. These are the track_properties fields and where each comes from in the GPX:
GPX-derivable (sync computes these per file — it already parses every point):
filename — the &lt;hash&gt;.gpx name after rename (trivial, already known)
distance — sum of haversine between consecutive (lon,lat) points; the coords are already parsed for the WKT
duration — last &lt;time&gt; minus first &lt;time&gt; in the trackpoints (requires reading &lt;time&gt; tags, which the current parseGpxTrackPoints may not extract — flagging that)
avg_speed — distance ÷ duration (derived from the two above)
shared — 0 (default; set by share action later)
NOT GPX-derivable (user input — sync must NOT fabricate these):
enjoyment (1-5) and ride_again — these live in track_surveys, not track_properties, and are user-entered. Sync leaves them alone. (Important: sync populates track_properties only; it never touches track_surveys.)
The one real dependency to confirm: duration and avg_speed need timestamps from the GPX. If parseGpxTrackPoints only returns (lon, lat) and drops &lt;time&gt;, then sync can compute distance but not duration/avg_speed without a second parse pass that pulls &lt;time&gt;. That's the thing the greps + a look at the parser will settle — and it decides whether the "process within/behind the fix" is one pass or needs a timestamp-aware parse.
So the sequence you're describing:
Fix process writes spatial (done) + now also presents track_properties with distance/duration/avg_speed/filename/shared=0 — paired.
A pass within/behind it to backfill those values for the existing tracks that were inserted without properties (the ones already in the DB from prior runs). This is the "run a process to update those values" you mean — sync, on its diagnostic run, detects a spatial row that has no matching track_properties and fills it.
Later, import routes through the same primitive so it populates identical fields.

The principle: don't persist metrics at track-build time. Derive them from the GPX whenever a process ingests the file — and write them to the extension then. The GPX is the source of truth; distance/duration/speed are a function of the file, computed at ingest (sync, import), not captured live and stored at save.
That's correct because:
The file already contains everything needed (coords for distance, &lt;time&gt; for duration/speed). The live HUD distance in ConvoyViewModel is just for display — irrelevant to persistence.
All three processes end up holding the parsed GPX, so all three can derive identically. One derivation function, called wherever a GPX is processed for the extension.
It means create doesn't need to write metrics at build time at all — when the recorded file is later synced (or on the create path's own ingest step), the same GPX-derive runs. One code path, no drift, no record-time timestamp dependency.
So the shape is:
A single GPX-metrics derivation — input: parsed GPX (coords + times); output: distance, duration, avg_speed. Called by sync now, by import later. Writes track_properties (filename, distance, duration, avg_speed, shared=0) keyed by track_id, paired with the spatial insert.
This still hinges on one fact I haven't confirmed: does the GPX actually contain &lt;time&gt; per trackpoint? Distance is pure geometry (have it). Duration and speed need timestamps in the file. Let me state it back precisely:
One standalone process. Input: a track_id. It looks up the track's &lt;hash&gt;.gpx, parses the GPX, derives the metrics (distance/duration/avg_speed from coords + &lt;time&gt;, elevation if wanted), and writes/updates the track_properties extension row keyed by that track_id. Called at the tail of each capture process — create, sync, import — once per track, after the spatial row + file exist.
Why this is the better design:
Single source of derivation. One function computes metrics; create/sync/import don't each re-implement it. No drift — the thing you were worried about across three paths is structurally impossible because there's one path.
Decoupled by track_id, not by call context. It doesn't care who calls it or how the track arrived. Spatial row exists + file exists → it can populate properties. That's the clean contract.
It's also the backfill tool, for free. Run it over every track_id that has a spatial row but no track_properties → fills the existing hole for all the tracks already in the DB without properties. Same function, batch-applied. No separate backfill code.
It's idempotent and re-runnable. Re-running on a track just recomputes the same values from the same file (INSERT OR REPLACE / upsert on track_id). Safe to call redundantly — matches the DB-controls-writes principle.
It survives the import repair. When we later fix import, import just calls this same process at its tail like the others. Nothing to redesign.
