GroupTrack — Design Record
2026-08-17 &middot; Trail data reality · route-suggestion scoring · the width ruler
SOURCE: measured against utah.gpkg (Geofabrik free, OSM as of 2026-07-29) and the
2026-08-11 spatial DB backup from Droid 1. Every number below came off those two files, not from
estimation.
⭐ WHY THIS EXISTS. The 2.7 "most interesting route" feature was moved up into 2.6g on
the reasoning that we are already inside route handling and the authority/install work that pushed it
out resolved in two days rather than the protracted slog budgeted for. That is a sound reason to
reverse the decision. But moving it up made the data question urgent, and investigating it changed
the design substantially &mdash; the differentiator does not rest where we assumed it did.
1. What the trail data actually contains
⛔ Finding 1 — the OSM import carries geometry and name, nothing else
Rows in trails from the OSM imports have carto_code and
source_id both empty. No class, no grade, no width, no access. The extract's class
list (track, track_grade1&ndash;5, path,
bridleway, unclassified) was used to decide what to keep and then
discarded rather than written to the row.
Scale of it: 112,696 trails with no carto_code against ~47,600 classified. The
classified ones are the Utah government trail dataset from the V2.5 work, carrying that agency's
permitted-use taxonomy. The OSM imports never had a mapping written, because the two vocabularies
describe different things.
⛔ Finding 2 — OSM grade does NOT mean OHV permission. They are orthogonal.
tracktype (grade1&ndash;5) classifies surface firmness, construction and
maintenance &mdash; grade1 hardest/paved, grade5 unimproved. It began life as a passability measure
and drifted to firmness. Legal access is a different tag entirely (access,
motor_vehicle, atv, ohv/orv,
maxwidth), and access defaults are country- and land-manager-specific.
⚠ In arid regions specifically &mdash; i.e. Utah and Arizona &mdash; the OSM wiki
notes mappers often cannot apply the drainage/maintenance criteria that separate grade3 from grade4 and
fall back on firmness or smoothness. So the middle of the scale is least reliable exactly where we
operate.
What OSM does give us: highway=track implies the way is wide enough for a typical
four-wheeled vehicle. path and bridleway do not. That is a real rideability
signal even with no permission data.
⚠ Finding 3 — the free Geofabrik extract cannot supply permission or width
gis_osm_roads_free columns, read from the file:
fid · geom · osm_id · code · fclass · name · ref · oneway · maxspeed · layer · bridge · tunnel
No motor_vehicle, no atv, no ohv, no maxwidth,
no separate tracktype. Those tags exist in OSM but are not in the free export. Getting
them means the full PBF or Geofabrik's paid extended export &mdash; a different pipeline, real work.
⭐ But fclass IS present, and Geofabrik folds tracktype into it: the values
are exactly track_grade1&ndash;5, track, path,
bridleway, unclassified. The grade data we thought was missing is in the
file we already have. It is one field away from being usable.
Finding 4 — the grade distribution, measured (Utah)
fclasscountread
track49,514vehicle-width, no grade given
path15,567not vehicle-width &rarr; exclude
unclassified14,459minor public road &mdash; real road, include
track_grade59,832unimproved &mdash; largest graded group
track_grade35,508middle, least reliable in arid terrain
track_grade23,863unpaved, imported material
track_grade43,477middle, least reliable in arid terrain
bridleway1,471not vehicle-width &rarr; exclude
track_grade1327paved &mdash; almost absent
⭐⭐ 68% of tracks (49,514 of 72,521) carry NO grade. A ride-quality term built on
grade is blind on two-thirds of the network. And grade5 is the largest graded group &mdash;
this is a backcountry network, so grade5 cannot be a rejection criterion without discarding the biggest
classified set in the state.
2. The rideability rule (settled)
Fred's stance, and the data forces it anyway: "error on the side of inclusive" and
"go one layer up in classification just to be more inclusive." Excluding a rideable trail is
worse than including a marginal one &mdash; a rider can look at a route and reject it, but cannot see
what was filtered out.
DecisionApplies to
INCLUDEtrack + all track_grade* + unclassified
EXCLUDEpath + bridleway (17,038 ways &mdash; not vehicle-width)
GRADEa weak SCORING term, never a filter, applied only where present
⭐ Grade-as-score rather than grade-as-filter also keeps the network connected: a single
grade5 link between two grade2 stretches must not break a route. The suggester prefers firmer ground
when it has a choice and accepts rough ground to complete a good loop.
THE CHANGE THIS REQUIRES: carry fclass into the trails table at
import. One field, in a pipeline already built. It pays off three times &mdash; the path/bridleway
exclusion, the map colouring something meaningful instead of 70% cyan, and the routing objective
getting its rideability input.
⚠ Also worth pulling from the same GPKG while there:
gis_osm_water_a_free (lakes/reservoirs as scenic attractors &mdash; we currently only have
springs as points) and gis_osm_protected_areas_a_free. The second is the one permission
signal the free extract does give us: designated wilderness prohibits motorized use entirely, so a
route crossing it is a hard error, not a preference.
3. Scenic scoring — what is available today
reference_points: 16,992 rows, fclass-indexed and bbox-indexed. This
was the good surprise &mdash; the scenic layer is already imported.
Attractors (~11,773)Settlement / navigational (~5,220)
peak 6,051 · spring 4,855 · cliff 525 · volcano 131 · cave_entrance 96 · tree 80 · island 26 · beach 8
locality 3,271 · hamlet 1,220 · village 436 · town 143 · suburb 47 · county 42 · city 40 · farm 21
Separately, waypoints holds 559 rows, all trailhead &mdash; trail-network
access points, a different job.
The objective function
Maximize interestingness subject to constraints &mdash; not minimize distance. That inversion
is the differentiator; existing nav optimizes shortest/fastest and cannot easily do this because they
lack OHV trail data and the objective is wrong for them.
Hard constraints (a candidate fails): total distance within 45&ndash;60 mi · estimated ride
time 5&ndash;9 h (RideCalc, 10&ndash;15 mph) · passes through all assigned drop points · connected on
the trail graph.
Score termComputed fromAvailable
Scenic proximityweighted attractor count within a buffer of the path✅ 11,773 pts, indexed
Loop closurestart/end distance ratio✅ geometry
Varietypenalty for re-traversing a segment✅ graph
Settlement avoidancenegative weight near town/village/hamlet✅ 5,220 pts
Ride quality (grade)fclass grade where present⚠ after import change; blind on 68%
Elevation gain / variety&mdash;❌ no elevation data anywhere
Legal OHV permission&mdash;❌ Utah state data only; nothing for Arizona
⚠⚠ THE CONCLUSION THAT MATTERS: v1 is carried by scenic proximity, loop closure,
variety and the distance/time envelope. Grade is a tiebreaker on a third of the network. "Trail
quality and difficulty" &mdash; named first when the feature was described &mdash; is not
available and should not be claimed.
Open design decisions: (a) buffer distance for "passes near" &mdash; a peak two miles off
trail is not part of the ride; half a mile is a starting value, needs tuning. (b) Does v1 produce
ONE route or 3&ndash;4 distinct ones? Multi-route with coverage across all drop points is a
substantially harder optimization than best-single-route. Recommendation: v1 = one route per drop-point
set, and the user groups the points themselves.
⛔ The safety boundary — non-negotiable
For Arizona there is no permission data at all, and OSM lags real-world closures everywhere.
Routing a rider onto a trail where motorized use is prohibited &mdash; by travel management plan,
wilderness designation, or private land &mdash; is a different class of error from a dull route.
Any suggested route built from OSM-only trails must say so in the UI and point at the land
manager's MVUM / BLM designation as the authority. This is not legal cover; it is the difference
between a useful tool and one that strands someone on a closed trail.
4. The width ruler (Fred, 2026-08-17)
⭐ The problem it solves: at z16 and below on satellite imagery a rider can tell a
hiking/biking/bridle trail from a vehicle track, but cannot tell a 54" trail from a 72" one
&mdash; and that is exactly the fact OSM cannot supply either.
The mechanic: a rotatable on-map reference, positioned along a trail, sized in real-world
units. Meters-per-pixel is known exactly at any zoom and latitude, so the scale is exact even though
the imagery is not.
Two bands, not one and not a tick scale: inner mark at 50", outer at 72"
&mdash; the UTV range. Three readable outcomes: narrower than inner · between the bands · wider than
outer. Between-the-bands is the honest "go check the MVUM" signal rather than a number to trust.
⛔ Deliberately NOT a tick-marked scale. Ticks invite reading a measurement off
imagery that cannot support one. The tool answers "which side of these two widths", not "how many
inches".
⚠ Honest limits — these belong in the UI, not just this doc
Imagery resolution is the real limit, not zoom. Google Hybrid is roughly 0.3&ndash;0.6 m/px
in rural terrain. 50" = 1.27 m ≈ 2&ndash;4 px; 72" = 1.83 m ≈ 3&ndash;6 px. Beyond a point you are
looking at upsampled tiles, not more detail &mdash; the tool is honest at some scales and misleading at
others, and should say which.
The gap between the bands is only ~0.56 m &mdash; a pixel or two. They will often look
nearly coincident. That is the correct behaviour: it shows the rider the distinction is at the
edge of what the imagery resolves. The visual must survive near-overlap without looking broken.
What you see is the disturbed corridor, not the legal tread &mdash; often wider than the
tread, sometimes narrower under tree cover. Eight feet of visible scar may be a 50" trail with
braiding.
Erring large is the right failure mode. Fred: "error on the large side, 74"
vs 50" &mdash; that should be discernable." A marginal trail gets flagged for verification rather
than a rider being sent home on a false negative, and a wide machine is never told a narrow trail
fits.
Colour: desert imagery is tan/orange, so warm colours vanish. Cyan + magenta hold up on arid
ground and stay distinguishable for most colour-vision types. Avoid a red/green pair.
Sequencing: the ruler is a 2D overlay computed from meters-per-pixel &mdash; it works
on the existing Leaflet map today, standalone, with no dependency on the renderer decision. Build it in
2.6g. When MapLibre lands it gains terrain context for free.
5. Terrain — why it is 2.7, and what it drags with it
3D terrain would address what the data cannot: no elevation column, no grade on 68% of tracks, no
width. A rider could judge steepness, exposure and drainage crossings directly &mdash; which is most of
what "is this rideable" actually means.
But it rides on the MapLibre swap, the largest single piece on the roadmap, and the convoy
tracking rewrite depends on the same decision. The ruler does not need to wait for it; terrain does.
⚠ For the 2.7 scoping, flag now: terrain rendering needs an elevation source
(DEM tiles / terrain-RGB) &mdash; that is another offline data store alongside the 50&ndash;60 GB of
imagery, so it is a storage and download-pipeline question as much as a rendering one. It belongs
in the MapLibre scoping rather than being discovered afterwards.
5b. CORRECTIONS to sections 1–2 (same session, later in the conversation)
⛔ fclass as an EXCLUSION FILTER is WITHDRAWN
Section 2 above proposed excluding path and bridleway using
fclass. Fred's objection kills it: "it would not add it as allowed usage, it
would eliminate some trails from the planning process and we have no idea what some is."
Acting on a crowd-sourced classification with no accuracy guarantee means removing trails from
planning based on a tag we cannot audit. That is a worse failure than the one it fixes. A hiking
trail appearing in the candidate set is VISIBLE — the rider sees it and rejects it. A rideable trail
silently filtered out is INVISIBLE. It also contradicts the inclusive stance the same section
adopts.
If fclass has a role it is a display hint or a soft score — colour a trail
differently, rank it lower, leave it visible and selectable. That is a much smaller claim and does not
justify an upsert redesign plus a two-state re-import.
⚠ The re-import is NOT a prerequisite — sequence corrected
Section 7 lists carrying fclass as item 3, a gate before the suggester. That was
wrong. Two reasons:
The exclusion it was meant to enable is withdrawn (above), so most of its value evaporates.
The Utah subset already has this signal. carto_code drives the map colours today
(yellow Hiking Only, purple Biking Only). On the 30% with Utah data, exclusion information already
exists. fclass would only add it for the OSM 70%.
And the mechanics are worse than assumed: SpatialDbManager.kt:1659 is
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO trails (...) and the column list does not include
carto_code at all. Against UNIQUE(geom_hash) a re-import would skip every
existing row and change nothing. Carrying a new field needs an upsert or a targeted
UPDATE keyed on geom_hash — bulk writes to a spatial DB that has been emptied
three times this month, with refuse-to-create still unbuilt.
⭐ Net: the trail-data work comes OFF the critical path. It is a route-quality
improvement, not a gate. ⭐ Extract-time filtering was raised as an alternative (no upsert, no
bulk write — the extract already filters, candidate_rows 201757 → kept 104186). Right
mechanism, wrong policy for a classification we do not trust: it makes the exclusion permanent AND
invisible. Better version: carry fclass at extract and filter nothing — the field
lands, everything stays visible, the app decides reversibly.
⚠ Context that softened this: trails visible on the basemap imagery are NOT limited to
what is in the DB. A rider always sees more than we catalogue, and can evaluate anything with the width
ruler. So DB exclusion removes a trail from the ROUTING CANDIDATE SET, not from view. ⬜ OPEN:
does the planner allow drawing a route over terrain with no DB trail underneath, or does route-building
SNAP to catalogued trails? If it snaps, an excluded trail really is unusable for planning and the ruler
only helps evaluate something that cannot be planned through.
The trail attribute layer, as it actually stands (measured)
trail_properties — 160,628 rows, one per trail, in the EXTENSION DB
(grouptrack_data.db), not the spatial DB.
ColumnPopulatedNote
source_id, agency_id160,628 (all)⭐ provenance DOES exist — it is here, not on trails
surface_type, carto_code, county47,932the Utah (UGRC) subset
designated_uses43,417Multiuse 38,688 · Pedestrian 2,746 · Bike 1,459
motorized_allowed0 — EMPTYcolumn designed for it, nothing ever written
surface_type is a genuine addition: Unpaved 30,576 / Paved 17,046 — complete
across the Utah subset, unlike OSM grade which is missing on 68%.
⚠ But designated_uses is NOT permission. "Multiuse" does not say
whether motorized is included. Same shape as carto_code: a use taxonomy separating
hiker-only from shared, not motorized from non-motorized. Nothing in either dataset affirmatively
says "OHVs are allowed here."
SOURCES, measured: osm 112,696 · ugrc_utah_trails 47,932. No BLM
data at all — the Utah set is UGRC, the state geographic resource center. ⚠ And
trail_sources — the registry table — is EMPTY, while every trail carries a
source_id string. Provenance is written without a corresponding source record.
⚠ Data hygiene for anyone switching on these strings: the literal text
null appears in designated_uses (459) and surface_type (309),
plus a blank-with-space and a trailing-space "Paved ".
5c. BLM RESTRICTIONS — the real permission source (researched 2026-08-17)
⭐⭐⭐ Fred's framing, which is the correct one: what we want to process is
BLM restrictions, by area or trail — and BLM only has authority over BLM land. This is a
RESTRICTIONS layer, not a geometry source. BLM was previously evaluated and set aside on coverage
grounds (OSM and UGRC give far more trails) — that judgement was about GEOMETRY. The designation
attributes are a different axis and nothing else provides them.
What BLM publishes
DatasetScopeCarries
State OHV Designation polygonsOHV_DSG_PUB_POLY (e.g. "BLM UT Off-Highway Vehicle Designations (Polygon)")STATE-level — not per-field-office, not nationalOpen / Limited / Closed per CFR 8342, plus special restrictions (designated-routes-only, seasonal-use-only). Set through the RMP process.
BLM_Natl_GTLF (Ground Transportation Linear Features)NATIONAL, route-levelPLAN_OHV_ROUTE_DSGNTN Open/Closed/Limited · PLAN_MODE_TRNSPRT Motorized/Non-Motorized/Non-Mechanized · PLAN_ALLOW_MODE_TRNSPRT (HIK_ONLY, EQU_ONLY, +19) · PLAN_ASSET_CLASS (road / primitive road = 4WD high-clearance / trail) · OHV_DSGNTN_LIM_EXPLAIN (250 chars)
BLM Natl NLCS Wilderness Areas PolygonsNATIONALWilderness, WSAs, Other Related Lands — motorized prohibited outright
All downloadable from the BLM Geospatial Business Platform Hub as Shapefile, File
Geodatabase, GeoJSON, KML, CSV or GeoServices. For two states that is two polygon downloads, not
fifty.
⭐⭐ "LIMITED" IS THE DESIGNATION THAT MATTERS, and it is almost certainly dominant in
our riding areas. It does not mean vaguely-restricted — it means you must stay on designated
routes. So an area being Limited is NOT permission to plan freely within it. This is precisely
where the two layers compose:
Area polygons answer can I be here at all — Closed blocks outright, Open permits free
routing, Limited means routes-only
GTLF routes resolve the Limited case — which specific routes carry the designation
This is the first thing that lets the planner say something AFFIRMATIVE rather than "not
obviously prohibited."
⛔ Limits that belong in the UI, not just this doc
BLM land only. USFS MVUM is a separate dataset; state, tribal and private land are covered by
neither. Outside BLM land the layer is SILENT, and silence must not read as "open." Shading only
BLM-restricted areas means unshaded ground includes land under entirely different rules.
BLM explicitly says to verify current limitations with the local field office, as restrictions
may vary from what the data depicts.
Routes may be additionally limited by time and/or season — so "Open" is not unconditional.
Some legacy field-office datasets carry scale limits (e.g. not to be used beyond 1:24,000).
The planner behaviour Fred specified
Highlight restricted areas in colour, and block vertex dropping inside them. Mechanically:
polygon overlay for display, point-in-polygon on tap for the block.
Blocking silently is worse than blocking with a reason. A tap that does nothing
reads as a bug. Show the area name and its designation — same reasoning as the authority gate's
declined screen.
A route can CROSS a closed area with no vertex inside it. Two points either side
and the path between crosses. So the polygon test must also run on the route line, not just on
the tap.
Label honestly. Until MVUM is ingested, the layer shows BLM designations — say that, rather
than "restricted areas", which implies coverage we do not have.
5d. THE SOURCE REGISTRY + BBOX SELECTION MODEL (Fred, 2026-08-17)
⭐⭐ The design: rather than a per-state checklist, the user selects an AREA;
sources are chosen by intersecting that area against each source's recorded coverage boundary; each
selected source is then imported within the same bbox. Ride area, not administrative geography —
which matches how people plan, since trips cross state lines without anyone caring.
TWO ENTRY POINTS, ONE PIPELINE. States have bboxes, so "pick Utah" and "draw a rectangle" both
resolve to a bbox. The state list is a convenience layer over well-known extents — no separate code
path, no parallel checklist to maintain.
The registry already exists and is already the right shape. trail_sources:
source_id · name · agency · url · format · trail_types · coverage_state · boundary · approved ·
last_checked_at. Someone designed exactly this and never populated it. Seeding it makes the
"what sources cover this area" checklist a QUERY rather than a maintained document.
source_idagencykindstatus
ugrc_utah_trailsUGRCtrailsin use — 47,932
osmGeofabriktrailsin use — 112,696
blm_ohv_areas_&lt;st&gt;BLMrestriction polygonsidentified, not built
blm_natl_gtlfBLMroute designationsidentified, not built
What this forces us to design
boundary must be populated per source before intersection is possible. Geofabrik
extracts have state bounds, UGRC is Utah, GTLF is national, BLM area layers are per-state. Some are
rectangles, some real polygons.
The registry needs a kind alongside format. Sources
produce different things — trails, restriction polygons, route designations. bbox selection is uniform;
what happens after it branches by kind. Restrictions are NOT trails and must not be forced into
trails/trail_properties — they have their own lifecycle and update
cadence, and forcing them in is how a fourth thing fails to fit later.
format is the real work. GPKG, Shapefile, GeoJSON and ArcGIS REST are four
fetch-and-parse paths. Listing a source is data entry; importing it is not.
State bbox ≠ state. Utah's rectangle clips corners of NV/AZ/CO/WY. ⭐ Fred: "that's ok,
better more than not enough — our trails already show completely if they cross state lines." So
spillover is a feature. ⬜ Worth confirming clipped trails arrive WHOLE in the routing graph too, or the
suggester would treat a clipped segment as a dead end.
Natural starting point, testable against data already held: populate
trail_sources for the two sources in use, with boundaries, and confirm the intersection
picks them correctly. No new source required to prove the model.
6. RideCalc and the ride envelope (settled 2026-08-17)
RideCalc is PURE EXTRACTION &mdash; no new capability. One calculation applied to any
polyline, three callers: artifact detail (tracks and trails), Route+ (planned routes), and the
suggester (candidate routes). Exactly the shape the overriding module rule wants, and the reason it
must be extracted before the suggester rather than alongside it &mdash; it is currently
duplicated across artifact detail and Route+, so building on the duplicate means doing it twice.
ParameterRoleAdjustable
Speed range (mph)Estimation only &mdash; a RANGE, not a point value✅ default in settings, user-adjustable
Distance bounds (mi)The hard constraint the suggester satisfies &mdash; upper AND lower✅ default in settings, user-adjustable
Ride timeDerived output, reported as a range&mdash; never entered directly
⭐ Why distance carries the constraint and time does not: the two are coupled
through speed, so making both hard bounds creates a which-one-bound-first problem and a route that
silently fails the limit the rider cared about. One constraint to satisfy, one range to report. A
55-mile suggestion reports e.g. 4.5&ndash;6.5 h rather than a single figure that will be wrong.
⚠ The LOWER bound matters as much as the upper and is easy to overlook: without
it the suggester satisfies "under 60 miles" with a 12-mile loop that technically touches every drop
point. The lower bound is what makes it a day's ride rather than a shortcut.
Why both are adjustable: an experienced group on fast desert two-track and a mixed group
with newcomers on technical ground need different envelopes, and the app should not try to infer
which. A rider who sets 6&ndash;10 mph gets an estimate reflecting their reality instead of a default
that flatters it. Multi-day trip planning falls out of the same control rather than needing separate
logic.
⬜ OPEN, not a blocker: the default speed range could be MEASURED from the 88
recorded tracks (real distances and durations, sitting in the 08-16 backup) rather than assumed at
10&ndash;15 mph. Cheap to compute, and it would make the estimate defensible instead of guessed
&mdash; potentially per-rider, since someone's own history predicts their pace better than an
average.
7. Build sequence &mdash; plumbing first
⭐ Fred, 2026-08-17: "must is to get all the plumbing out of the way before
addressing the route suggestion build." Items 1&ndash;5 are all plumbing &mdash; none is the
feature; all are things the feature would trip over, or that would make it harder to build cleanly.
Building the suggester on duplicated RideCalc and six discard variants would ADD to the tangle rather
than work from a clean base.
#ItemWhy here
1Radio-meter removal (app cancels when selected with no radio attached)Hard crash, reachable from the dashboard, and testers are on radio-less devices for the next 14 days
2Refuse-to-createSmall, and it protects everything downstream &mdash; bulk DB writes are coming
3Carry fclass at import + RE-IMPORT Utah/AZ⚠ THE LONG POLE, and it is not code time. Utah alone was 104,186 trails from a 663 MB source; AZ on top. Start the clock EARLY &mdash; it finishes on its own schedule. Backfills 112,696 rows.
4RideCalc extractionThe suggester needs the envelope; extract before, not during
5Discard/save standardizationFive-plus-one boundary, six sites classified by destination
6Suggest-trail-routeDepends on 3 and 4
7Width rulerStandalone, 2D, no dependencies &mdash; fits any gap
6. What this changes about the plan
Route dedup comes OFF the 2.6g list &mdash; hash-naming is the dedup method, same as tracks.
Already solved by the naming scheme.
The second route-mode disarm path comes OFF as a separate item &mdash; it is absorbed by the
discard/save consolidation. Standardize the five, leave the exit/return decision in the calling stream.
⭐ Consequence: "did we find every disarm path" stops being a discoverable question and becomes a
classification question &mdash; every one of the six sites gets a deliberate exit-or-stay
answer. Nothing left to inference. That is the actual fix for the tangle.
Carry fclass at import &mdash; new, small, and it unblocks rideability, the map
colouring, and the routing objective at once.
RideCalc extraction moves ahead of the suggester &mdash; the suggester needs the time
envelope, and RideCalc is currently duplicated across artifact detail and Route+. Build on the
duplicate and you either do it twice or block later.
The width ruler is new scope, standalone, 2D, no renderer dependency.
The suggester's claim shrinks to what the data supports: scenic + loop + variety +
envelope. Still a real differentiator &mdash; big nav optimizes shortest/fastest and lacks OHV trail
data &mdash; but "trail quality and difficulty" is not part of v1.

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   SAMPLE GEOMETRY — deterministic, generated from real Moab-area anchors.
   Stands in for grouptrack.gpkg so the display model is visible immediately.
   Replace any layer with a real export using the file pickers.

let seed = 20260726;
const rnd = () => (seed = (seed * 1664525 + 1013904223) % 4294967296) / 4294967296;
function walk(lon, lat, steps, spread, drift) {
  const pts = []; let h = rnd() * Math.PI * 2;
  for (let i = 0; i < steps; i++) {
    h += (rnd() - 0.5) * drift;
    lon += Math.cos(h) * spread; lat += Math.sin(h) * spread * 0.8;
    pts.push([+lon.toFixed(5), +lat.toFixed(5)]);
  }
  return pts;
}
const fc = (f) => ({ type:'FeatureCollection', features:f });
const line = (coords, props) =>
  ({ type:'Feature', geometry:{ type:'LineString', coordinates:coords }, properties:props });
const point = (c, props) =>
  ({ type:'Feature', geometry:{ type:'Point', coordinates:c }, properties:props });

function boot() {
const map = new maplibregl.Map({
  container:'map', style, center:[-109.5498,38.5733], zoom:11.4, maxZoom:19, hash:true
});
map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl({visualizePitch:true}),'bottom-right');
map.addControl(new maplibregl.ScaleControl({unit:'imperial'}),'bottom-right');
/* ---- counts ---- */
const counts = () => {
  document.getElementById('nTrail').textContent = TRAILS.features.length;
  document.getElementById('nTrack').textContent = TRACKS.features.length;
  document.getElementById('nRoute').textContent = ROUTES.features.length;
  document.getElementById('nWpt').textContent   = WAYPOINTS.features.length;
};
/* ---- toggles ---- */
const vis = (layers, on) => layers.forEach(l =>
  map.getLayer(l) && map.setLayoutProperty(l,'visibility', on ? 'visible':'none'));
const bind = (id, layers) => {
  const el = document.getElementById(id);
  el.addEventListener('change', () => vis(layers, el.checked));
};
map.on('load', () => {
  counts();
  bind('sat',['sat']);
  bind('lbl',['lblRoad','lblWater','lblPeak','lblPlace']);
  bind('osmTrk',['osmTrk']);
  bind('trailOn',['trailLine']);
  bind('trackOn',['trackCase','trackLine']);
  bind('trackLbl',['trackLbl']);
  bind('routeOn',['routeCase','routeLine']);
  bind('wptOn',['wptDot']);
  bind('wptLbl',['wptLbl']);
  const exag = document.getElementById('exag');
  const terr = document.getElementById('terr');
  const applyTerrain = () => {
    if (terr.checked) {
      map.setTerrain({ source:'dem', exaggeration:parseFloat(exag.value) });
      if (map.getPitch() < 20) map.easeTo({ pitch:60, duration:900 });
    } else {
      map.setTerrain(null);
      map.easeTo({ pitch:0, bearing:0, duration:700 });
    }
  };
  terr.addEventListener('change', applyTerrain);
  exag.addEventListener('input', () => {
    if (terr.checked) map.setTerrain({ source:'dem', exaggeration:parseFloat(exag.value) });
  });
  // ---- inspector: MapLibre has no DOM per feature, so hit-test instead.
  // This is exactly the change spatial_artifacts.js needs — click handlers
  // bound per feature become one queryRenderedFeatures call.
  const HIT = ['trackLine','trailLine','routeLine','wptDot','osmTrk'];
  map.on('click', (e) => {
    const f = map.queryRenderedFeatures(e.point, { layers:HIT })[0];
    const box = document.getElementById('insp');
    if (!f) { box.style.display='none'; return; }
    document.getElementById('inspT').textContent =
      (f.properties.type || 'FEATURE').toUpperCase();
    document.getElementById('inspB').innerHTML = Object.entries(f.properties)
      .map(([k,v]) => `${k}${v}`).join('');
    box.style.display='block';
  });
  HIT.forEach(l => {
    map.on('mouseenter', l, () => map.getCanvas().style.cursor='pointer');
    map.on('mouseleave', l, () => map.getCanvas().style.cursor='');
  });
});
document.getElementById('inspX').onclick = () =>
  document.getElementById('insp').style.display='none';
/* ---- load your own exports ---- */
const loadInto = (inputId, srcId, store, countId) => {
  document.getElementById(inputId).addEventListener('change', (ev) => {
    const file = ev.target.files && ev.target.files[0]; if (!file) return;
    const rd = new FileReader();
    rd.onload = () => {
      try {
        const gj = JSON.parse(rd.result);
        const feats = gj.type==='FeatureCollection' ? gj.features
                    : gj.type==='Feature' ? [gj] : [];
        if (!feats.length) { alert('No features in that file.'); return; }
        store.features = feats;
        map.getSource(srcId).setData(store);
        document.getElementById(countId).textContent = feats.length;
        let n=-90,s=90,e=-180,w=180;
        const walkC = (c) => { if (typeof c[0]==='number'){
          if(c[1]>n)n=c[1]; if(c[1]e)e=c[0]; if(c[0]<w)w=c[0];
        } else c.forEach(walkC); };
        feats.forEach(ft => ft.geometry && walkC(ft.geometry.coordinates));
        if (w<=e && s<=n) map.fitBounds([[w,s],[e,n]],{padding:70,maxZoom:15});
      } catch (err) { alert('Could not parse: ' + err.message); }
    };
    rd.readAsText(file);
  });
};
loadInto('fTrail','trails',TRAILS,'nTrail');
loadInto('fTrack','tracks',TRACKS,'nTrack');
loadInto('fRoute','routes',ROUTES,'nRoute');
loadInto('fWpt','wpts',WAYPOINTS,'nWpt');
const read = document.getElementById('read');
const upd = () => { const c = map.getCenter();
  read.textContent = `z${map.getZoom().toFixed(1)}   ${c.lat.toFixed(4)}, ${c.lng.toFixed(4)}   pitch ${map.getPitch().toFixed(0)}°`; };
map.on('move',upd); map.on('load',upd);
// A blank map must explain itself rather than failing silently.
map.on('error',(e)=>{
  const m = (e && e.error && e.error.message) ? e.error.message : String(e && e.error || 'unknown');
  console.warn('map error:', e && e.error);
  const box = document.getElementById('err');
  const msg = document.getElementById('errmsg');
  if (!box.style.display || box.style.display === 'none') {
    box.style.display = 'block';
    msg.textContent = m;
  } else if (msg.textContent.indexOf(m) === -1) {
    msg.textContent += '  |  ' + m;
  }
});
// If the style never finishes loading, say so rather than showing an empty box.
setTimeout(() => {
  if (!map.isStyleLoaded()) {
    const box = document.getElementById('err');
    if (box.style.display !== 'block') {
      box.style.display = 'block';
      document.getElementById('errmsg').textContent =
        'Style did not finish loading after 12s. Check the browser console (F12).';
    }
  }
}, 12000);
}  // end boot()
/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   MapLibre is loaded from a CDN. If one is blocked or unreachable the library
   never defines `maplibregl` and every line above throws. Try three in turn and
   say so plainly if none answers, rather than leaving a blank page.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
(function () {
  const V = '4.7.1';
  const JS = [
    'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/maplibre-gl@' + V + '/dist/maplibre-gl.js',
    'https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@' + V + '/dist/maplibre-gl.js',
    'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/maplibre-gl/' + V + '/maplibre-gl.js'
  ];
  const CSS = [
    'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/maplibre-gl@' + V + '/dist/maplibre-gl.css',
    'https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@' + V + '/dist/maplibre-gl.css',
    'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/maplibre-gl/' + V + '/maplibre-gl.css'
  ];
  const fatal = (msg) => {
    const box = document.getElementById('err');
    box.style.display = 'block';
    document.getElementById('errmsg').textContent = msg;
  };
  const loadCss = (i) => {
    if (i >= CSS.length) return;
    const l = document.createElement('link');
    l.rel = 'stylesheet'; l.href = CSS[i];
    l.onerror = () => loadCss(i + 1);
    document.head.appendChild(l);
  };
  const loadJs = (i) => {
    if (i >= JS.length) {
      fatal('Could not load the MapLibre library from any CDN (jsdelivr, unpkg, cdnjs). ' +
            'Something on this network is blocking them, or there is no internet. ' +
            'Note the satellite tiles need internet too.');
      return;
    }
    const sc = document.createElement('script');
    sc.src = JS[i];
    sc.onload = () => {
      if (window.maplibregl) { loadCss(0); boot(); }
      else loadJs(i + 1);
    };
    sc.onerror = () => loadJs(i + 1);
    document.head.appendChild(sc);
  };
  loadJs(0);
})();

  GroupTrack — Droid 1 Install Procedure
    Written 2026-08-01, after the same-day spatial-DB loss on Droid 2.
    Droid 1 = 8624SBCEDF00001789 — PRIMARY field device. Its data is the one to protect.
  ⛔ READ THIS BEFORE INSTALLING ANYTHING ON DROID 1
  Today an adb install -r -d destroyed the entire spatial database on Droid 2 — ~89 k trails, all tracks, waypoints and routes. The app did not warn; it reported 0 trails, 0 tracks, 0 waypoints, 0 routes and carried on.
  The underlying defect is NOT yet fixed. SpatialDbManager still opens with create-if-missing, so any install that costs the app its all-files authority will overwrite Droid 1's databases exactly the same way.
  Recommendation: do not install to Droid 1 until the DB open-failure fix ships — unless you back up first (Step&nbsp;2 below) and accept the risk.
Pre-flight — three questions that decide everything
  Q1 · Is Droid 1 running a SIDELOADED build or a PLAY build?
  Since the 07-26 package merge, both are com.grouptrack.android but they are signed with different keys — local APKs with grouptrack-release-key.jks, Play builds with Play App Signing.
  You cannot cross from one to the other without uninstalling, and uninstalling wipes tiles and app data. Expect INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, or Play silently offering nothing.
  MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 adb -s 8624SBCEDF00001789 shell dumpsys package com.grouptrack.android | grep -E "versionCode|versionName|firstInstallTime|lastUpdateTime|installerPackageName"
  installerPackageName=com.android.vending → Play build. Null or a shell installer → sideload.
  ⛔ Decide per device: sideload OR Play. Not both. If Droid 1 is on Play and you want to sideload, that is a stop-and-think moment, not a retry.
  Q2 · Is the APK's version code HIGHER than what's installed?
  versionCode is git-derived (gitVersionProvider.get() + vcOffset) and can regress. A regression is what turned today's install into a fresh install.
  Note the versionCode from Q1. The build prints its own — line 213 of build.gradle.kts logs "Version code is set to:". Let it through the filter:
  ./gradlew assembleGoogleRelease -x uploadCrashlyticsMappingFileGoogleRelease 2>&amp;1 | grep -E "Version code|^e:|BUILD|FAILED"
  If the new one is lower, do not install. Override for that build instead:
  -Pandroid.injected.version.code=NNNNNNNN    # pick a value above what's on the device
  Q3 · Is USB stable, or should this be wireless?
  Droid 1's USB is temperamental — moving the cable drops adb, and a drop mid-install is exactly when things go wrong.
  Prefer wireless: Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging → pair → adb connect ip:port.

Cause: two callers use bare DownloadQueueManager.enqueue(), which computes the whole box in one entry (calculateTiles, ConvoyDownloadQueue:127) with no split and no cap:
SpatialDbManager.kt:1973 (downloadMapsForTrackHash) — the track-import path, the 62K source. Its bypass comment was VALID against the old fixed-12-mile gridCells (which returned NOTHING for a sub-12-mile box → totalTiles=0).
ConvoyViewModel.kt:989 (startDownload) ← ConvoyScreen:472, fed by setPendingDownload at :645/:876 — no stated reason, simply predates segmentation.
⭐ Migration is SAFE — the blocker is cleared. segmentCells (ConvoyTileDownloader:254) cannot return empty: Math.max(1, ceil(sizeTiles/50_000)) floors at 1 and slices the ACTUAL bbox fractionally instead of snapping to a fixed grid, so a tiny per-track box yields exactly ONE cell. The documented reason for the SpatialDbManager bypass is dead.
Fix: route both through submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells. Do NOT call segmentCells directly — it needs sizeTiles = layer-aware volume (quickEstimate × slotLayers), which enqueueArea already computes. getTrackBbox() (SpatialDbManager:1915) already exists as the correct replacement shape.
⚠ Dependency: sizeTiles comes from quickEstimate, which has the known source-awareness bug — a bad estimate UNDER-SPLITS even after migration. Test entry sizes after; don’t assume 62K is gone.

Why auto-resume was DEFERRED (the core lesson)
Processing before render. Three approaches all failed the same way — armed but not drawable:
Seeding routeMode true at init — armed the route before the map/desktop rendered → route "started" into an unrendered surface (no draw, "no prompt", message swallowed). ALSO broke compile: MVS:204 BackHandler back-gate uses routeMode before a moved declaration; and seeding the LIVE field fought the back-gate's need for blank-on-launch AND reintroduced the old convoy stuck-arm. REVERTED — routeMode stays mutableStateOf(false).
Direct load in onPageFinished (loadIntoRouteManager + routeMode=true) — came up armed but NOT drawable because it SKIPPED the geometry redraw the In-Progress picker does (queryGeomByIds → buildSegments → JS drawBuildLine).
Manual In-Progress resume works flawlessly (Fred verified: exit → +ROUTE → In Progress → auto-saved route loads + draws + arms). So the interim ships the notice and defers automation.
Auto-resume — the plan when back
After settle, TRIGGER THE EXISTING In-Progress picker path (it does the redraw correctly) — do NOT rebuild the load in onPageFinished. Cleanest: give the recovery popup a "Resume" button → showInProgressPicker = true → user taps the "Auto Saved In Progress" draft → proven path (loadIntoRouteManager → routeName/routeMethod/routeLifecycleState=ROUTE_LS_RESUMED → routeEntryNonce++ → routeMode=true → savePlanningState → scope.launch{ BY-ID rederive → drawBuildLine }). The In-Progress select handler is at MVS ~1159-1195; mirror or invoke it.
Save-name — the "everything is auto-saved" fix (committed a5a33dbfa)
Problem: every route saved silently keeping the auto-name "Auto Saved In Progress". The auto-name was introduced so a crash leaves a recoverable named draft; the name requirement moved from up-front to SAVE but was never wired.
Key structural fact (Fred): the draft writes on EVERY data point, so the save action only needs a RENAME — not a re-write.
Save-choice panel ("Save route" AlertDialog, MVS ~1091)
Required name field (OutlinedTextField) in the text={} block. Value blank if current name == "Auto Saved In Progress", else editable. Both buttons gated on a non-blank, non-auto name (toast "Enter a route name" otherwise).
Original on-disk name captured when the panel opens: onSaveRequested = { saveOrigName = routeName; showSaveChoice = true }. saveOrigName declared near ~146. This is the rename SOURCE (correct whether auto-named or already-named).
Save as in progress (dismissButton): renameDraft(saveOrigName, newName) ONLY (dropped the old writeDraft/overwriteDraft — draft already written per point) → clearRoute + routeMode=false. Runs in scope.launch{ withContext(IO){ rename } }.
Save as completed (confirmButton): gated on pts≥2 → scope.launch{ withContext(IO){ renameDraft(saveOrigName,newName) }; routeName=newName; delay(400); saveCompleted() }. The delay(400) lets the async rename settle before saveCompleted()'s insertRoute (MVS ~984) reads the renamed routeName. saveCompleted's spatial-DB write logic UNCHANGED.
renameDraft (RouteDraftStore:225): writes new-name file (tmp→rename), src.delete() on success, isNameTaken guard. VERIFY a leftover "Auto Saved In Progress" file appeared ONCE then was gone on retest — run several cycles when back to confirm cleanup is reliable; if it recurs, inspect the isNameTaken false-block and whether a COMPLETED save should DELETE the graduated draft (route now lives in spatial DB, draft's job done).
Architecture settled — DO NOT re-litigate
routeMode stays mutableStateOf(false) at init (MVS ~137). It is LIVE session state read by the back-gate (MVS:204 BackHandler { if (routeMode) toast else onBack() }). NOT seeded from persistence. Seeding created a chicken-and-egg (back wants blank-on-launch; seed wants true-after-crash — same var, opposite needs) AND reintroduced the convoy stuck-arm.
"Every field writes on every update" is THE RULE and STAYS (Fred: "it's not the writes that failed, it's the seeding, and that is on us"). Do NOT propose write-only markers / omitting fields from saves / separate marker stores.
Recovery DETECTION = isolated duplicate JSON read; recovery ACTION only after render (onPageFinished postDelayed), never during init.

⭐⭐⭐ FIRST OPEN ITEM — unsegmented enqueue() bypasses (root-caused, NOT patched)
Symptom: artifact/track imports with “download maps” selected produce SAT submissions of 62,000+ tiles in a SINGLE queue entry, though segmentation caps cells at 50,000.
Cause: two callers use bare DownloadQueueManager.enqueue(), which computes the whole box in one entry (calculateTiles, ConvoyDownloadQueue:127) with no split and no cap:
SpatialDbManager.kt:1973 (downloadMapsForTrackHash) — the track-import path, the 62K source. Its bypass comment was VALID against the old fixed-12-mile gridCells (which returned NOTHING for a sub-12-mile box → totalTiles=0).
ConvoyViewModel.kt:989 (startDownload) ← ConvoyScreen:472, fed by setPendingDownload at :645/:876 — no stated reason, simply predates segmentation.
⭐ Migration is SAFE — the blocker is cleared. segmentCells (ConvoyTileDownloader:254) cannot return empty: Math.max(1, ceil(sizeTiles/50_000)) floors at 1 and slices the ACTUAL bbox fractionally instead of snapping to a fixed grid, so a tiny per-track box yields exactly ONE cell. The documented reason for the SpatialDbManager bypass is dead.
Fix: route both through submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells. Do NOT call segmentCells directly — it needs sizeTiles = layer-aware volume (quickEstimate × slotLayers), which enqueueArea already computes. getTrackBbox() (SpatialDbManager:1915) already exists as the correct replacement shape.
⚠ Dependency: sizeTiles comes from quickEstimate, which has the known source-awareness bug — a bad estimate UNDER-SPLITS even after migration. Test entry sizes after; don’t assume 62K is gone.
✅ Fred’s source-switch hypothesis — DISCONFIRMED 07-23 (xref trace). startDownload is NOT the source refresh: both setPendingDownload sites (ConvoyScreen :645/:876) are inside onAreaSelected, declared TWICE (:629, :860) as duplicate copies in two WebView JS-interface blocks — so bypass #2 is the convoy draw-area selection path. The map-source refresh lives in ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt (:81-83) and calls enqueueRefresh at :271 → segmentCells = ALREADY SEGMENTED. Bypass / boot-loop / source-switch are NOT one thread. ⚠ AM FIRST STEP: Fred says there are no active downloads on convoy — if draw-area selection is unreachable in the UI, bypass #2 is DEAD CODE (delete, don’t migrate). Route recovery — what landed (interim) + exact mechanism
Shipped behavior: crash mid-route → relaunch → planner settles → notice popup: "A route was left open from your last session. To resume it, tap +ROUTE and choose In Progress." → OK. User resumes via the proven In-Progress picker path. Clean exit → NO popup (verified — the important negative test).
Detection (isolated second read)
At the routeMode declaration (MVS ~136-137): val routeSeedOpen = remember { MapStateStore.readMap("planning").routeState?.open == true }. This is a DUPLICATE JSON read, independent of pmSeed (which is read later at ~224). Do NOT move pmSeed up to share it — scope risk; Fred explicitly chose to duplicate the read.
Trigger (after render)
In onPageFinished's postDelayed block (MVS ~645), immediately AFTER SpatialDisplayManager.drawPersistedState("planning", view, context) and BEFORE return@postDelayed: a one-shot guarded flag set — if (routeSeedOpen && !recoveryLaunched) { recoveryLaunched = true; recoveryPending = true }. Guard vars declared near ~146: recoveryLaunched, recoveryPending (plus recoveryDetected from the earlier detect patch).
The popup
An AlertDialog gated on recoveryPending, placed just BEFORE the showInProgressPicker dialog (MVS ~1160). Single OK button sets recoveryPending = false. Purely informational — no load, no arm.
Why auto-resume was DEFERRED (the core lesson)
Processing before render. Three approaches all failed the same way — armed but not drawable:
Seeding routeMode true at init — armed the route before the map/desktop rendered → route "started" into an unrendered surface (no draw, "no prompt", message swallowed). ALSO broke compile: MVS:204 BackHandler back-gate uses routeMode before a moved declaration; and seeding the LIVE field fought the back-gate's need for blank-on-launch AND reintroduced the old convoy stuck-arm. REVERTED — routeMode stays mutableStateOf(false).
Direct load in onPageFinished (loadIntoRouteManager + routeMode=true) — came up armed but NOT drawable because it SKIPPED the geometry redraw the In-Progress picker does (queryGeomByIds → buildSegments → JS drawBuildLine).
Manual In-Progress resume works flawlessly (Fred verified: exit → +ROUTE → In Progress → auto-saved route loads + draws + arms). So the interim ships the notice and defers automation.
Auto-resume — the plan when back
After settle, TRIGGER THE EXISTING In-Progress picker path (it does the redraw correctly) — do NOT rebuild the load in onPageFinished. Cleanest: give the recovery popup a "Resume" button → showInProgressPicker = true → user taps the "Auto Saved In Progress" draft → proven path (loadIntoRouteManager → routeName/routeMethod/routeLifecycleState=ROUTE_LS_RESUMED → routeEntryNonce++ → routeMode=true → savePlanningState → scope.launch{ BY-ID rederive → drawBuildLine }). The In-Progress select handler is at MVS ~1159-1195; mirror or invoke it.
Save-name — the "everything is auto-saved" fix (committed a5a33dbfa)
Problem: every route saved silently keeping the auto-name "Auto Saved In Progress". The auto-name was introduced so a crash leaves a recoverable named draft; the name requirement moved from up-front to SAVE but was never wired.
Key structural fact (Fred): the draft writes on EVERY data point, so the save action only needs a RENAME — not a re-write.
Save-choice panel ("Save route" AlertDialog, MVS ~1091)
Required name field (OutlinedTextField) in the text={} block. Value blank if current name == "Auto Saved In Progress", else editable. Both buttons gated on a non-blank, non-auto name (toast "Enter a route name" otherwise).
Original on-disk name captured when the panel opens: onSaveRequested = { saveOrigName = routeName; showSaveChoice = true }. saveOrigName declared near ~146. This is the rename SOURCE (correct whether auto-named or already-named).
Save as in progress (dismissButton): renameDraft(saveOrigName, newName) ONLY (dropped the old writeDraft/overwriteDraft — draft already written per point) → clearRoute + routeMode=false. Runs in scope.launch{ withContext(IO){ rename } }.
Save as completed (confirmButton): gated on pts≥2 → scope.launch{ withContext(IO){ renameDraft(saveOrigName,newName) }; routeName=newName; delay(400); saveCompleted() }. The delay(400) lets the async rename settle before saveCompleted()'s insertRoute (MVS ~984) reads the renamed routeName. saveCompleted's spatial-DB write logic UNCHANGED.
renameDraft (RouteDraftStore:225): writes new-name file (tmp→rename), src.delete() on success, isNameTaken guard. Architecture settled — DO NOT re-litigate
routeMode stays mutableStateOf(false) at init (MVS ~137). It is LIVE session state read by the back-gate (MVS:204 BackHandler { if (routeMode) toast else onBack() }). NOT seeded from persistence. Seeding created a chicken-and-egg (back wants blank-on-launch; seed wants true-after-crash — same var, opposite needs) AND reintroduced the convoy stuck-arm.
"Every field writes on every update" is THE RULE and STAYS (Fred: "it's not the writes that failed, it's the seeding, and that is on us"). Do NOT propose write-only markers / omitting fields from saves / separate marker stores.

⭐⭐⭐ THE NUMBER — corridor proven on device
Tester track bar 10, the ~100-mile figure-7 that started the whole investigation:
bbox 1,000,000+ tiles → corridor 65,000 + 21,000 + 21,000 ≈ 107,000. A ≈90% reduction. Built, queued and downloaded end to end on the planning map. G1–G4 compiled first try (14m03s).
⚠ Three caveats that must travel with that number. (1) Bar 10 is the best case — the longest, thinnest track available; a compact track's bbox is already close to its corridor and will gain far less. (2) It is BEFORE the z-cap; if TOPO+ really tops out at z15 a slice of its 21,000 is 404s, and that saving must be measured separately — two variables, two measurements. (3) The old 894,507 baseline was never the comparable figure — that was sizeTiles (SAT sizing), not the total queued across sources.
The cutover (patch H) — corridor is now the only track path
Area SAVE MAPS button DELETED from the artifact panel, not flagged off. Leaving a disabled path behind is exactly how gridCells and downloadMapsForTrackHash both outlived their replacements and later looked like live code. The onDownloadMaps parameter stays (two screens still pass it) but nothing renders it.
Track import swapped bbox → corridor at ConvoyTrackOps:586. It became a LOOP, not a substitution — the old call was one submitDownload covering all slots; corridor is one entry per source. ⚠ Ten tracks × three sources = 30 rows, not 10.
⚠ enqueueCorridor derives the corridor to get its tile count, per track per source, on the IO thread. A 10-track import spends real time in derivation before the first tile moves. That is Option B's deliberate trade (pay once per entry, not 5–10s per run-box) — it is not a hang.
Draw-a-box area downloads from the map are untouched.
⛔ Patch I failed — a wrong diagnosis worth keeping
The convoy download-confirm dialog overflows the bottom of the screen, buttons unreachable without rotating. Planning's is centred. Convoy's chain was Modifier.padding(16.dp); planning's was Modifier.align(Alignment.Center).padding(16.dp) — it looked like the same drift as the 07-22 queues-width bug, so patch I just added .align().
It did not compile: 'fun Modifier.align' cannot be called in this context with an implicit receiver. Modifier.align() is a BoxScope extension — planning's dialog sits in a Box, convoy's sits in a Column (ConvoyScreen ~1495). Never drift; a consequence of different containers.
Patch J fixed it properly — wrap the call in Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize(), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center), which centres without needing the scope extension. The anchor deliberately spans the whole call through the enclosing if's closing brace, so the wrapper's braces cannot land in the wrong place.
⭐ LESSON: a matching symptom is not a matching cause. The previous bug's shape actively misled — its fix was scope-illegal here.

🔴 NEW BUG: refresh does not log as a completed job. See below — check this before spending hours waiting on the ETA.
🔴 NEW OPEN — refresh never registers as COMPLETE
A map-source refresh job never reaches a completed state. Three consequences, in order of severity:
⚠⚠ Does it hold a concurrency slot? If the entry never leaves a running status, startNextIfAvailable may count it against MAX_CONCURRENT indefinitely. That is a queue-stall mechanism — and "system just sits" is exactly what 07-23 reported. Check this first; it is the difference between a reporting bug and a throughput bug.
It starves the ETA. estimateRemaining() reads the last two COMPLETE entries and completedAt is stamped in markComplete. Same failure mode as patch A2 — a value that is never written, presenting as a silent UI absence rather than an error.
CLEAR cannot clear it — CLEAR means COMPLETE+FAILED+CANCELLED, so a non-terminal job is unclearable from the panel and accumulates.
Start here: grep -n "markComplete" app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/*.kt, then read ConvoyDownloadWorker's refresh branch end to end — does it return Result.success() without notifying the queue, or take a different terminal path?
⭐ Check ConvoyCorridorWorker in the same pass. The corridor worker deliberately duplicates the completion plumbing rather than sharing it — an accepted trade at design time. This bug is that trade coming due: if refresh can miss markComplete, so can corridor, independently. Confirming corridor stamps completion is a five-minute read that could save an evening of waiting on an ETA that was never going to appear.

⭐⭐⭐ FIRST OPEN ITEM — unsegmented enqueue() bypasses (root-caused, NOT patched)
Symptom: artifact/track imports with “download maps” selected produce SAT submissions of 62,000+ tiles in a SINGLE queue entry, though segmentation caps cells at 50,000.
Cause: two callers use bare DownloadQueueManager.enqueue(), which computes the whole box in one entry (calculateTiles, ConvoyDownloadQueue:127) with no split and no cap:
SpatialDbManager.kt:1973 (downloadMapsForTrackHash) — the track-import path, the 62K source. Its bypass comment was VALID against the old fixed-12-mile gridCells (which returned NOTHING for a sub-12-mile box → totalTiles=0).
ConvoyViewModel.kt:989 (startDownload) ← ConvoyScreen:472, fed by setPendingDownload at :645/:876 — no stated reason, simply predates segmentation.
⭐ Migration is SAFE — the blocker is cleared. segmentCells (ConvoyTileDownloader:254) cannot return empty: Math.max(1, ceil(sizeTiles/50_000)) floors at 1 and slices the ACTUAL bbox fractionally instead of snapping to a fixed grid, so a tiny per-track box yields exactly ONE cell. The documented reason for the SpatialDbManager bypass is dead.
Fix: route both through submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells. Do NOT call segmentCells directly — it needs sizeTiles = layer-aware volume (quickEstimate × slotLayers), which enqueueArea already computes. getTrackBbox() (SpatialDbManager:1915) already exists as the correct replacement shape.
⚠ Dependency: sizeTiles comes from quickEstimate, which has the known source-awareness bug — a bad estimate UNDER-SPLITS even after migration. Test entry sizes after; don’t assume 62K is gone.
✅ Fred’s source-switch hypothesis — DISCONFIRMED 07-23 (xref trace). startDownload is NOT the source refresh: both setPendingDownload sites (ConvoyScreen :645/:876) are inside onAreaSelected, declared TWICE (:629, :860) as duplicate copies in two WebView JS-interface blocks — so bypass #2 is the convoy draw-area selection path. The map-source refresh lives in ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt (:81-83) and calls enqueueRefresh at :271 → segmentCells = ALREADY SEGMENTED. Bypass / boot-loop / source-switch are NOT one thread. ⚠ AM FIRST STEP: Fred says there are no active downloads on convoy — if draw-area selection is unreachable in the UI, bypass #2 is DEAD CODE (delete, don’t migrate). Confirm reachability on the device. Only SpatialDbManager:1973 (track import) is confirmed live.

Route recovery — what landed (interim) + exact mechanism
Shipped behavior: crash mid-route → relaunch → planner settles → notice popup: "A route was left open from your last session. To resume it, tap +ROUTE and choose In Progress." → OK. User resumes via the proven In-Progress picker path. Clean exit → NO popup (verified — the important negative test).
Detection (isolated second read)
At the routeMode declaration (MVS ~136-137): val routeSeedOpen = remember { MapStateStore.readMap("planning").routeState?.open == true }. This is a DUPLICATE JSON read, independent of pmSeed (which is read later at ~224). Do NOT move pmSeed up to share it — scope risk; Fred explicitly chose to duplicate the read.
Trigger (after render)
In onPageFinished's postDelayed block (MVS ~645), immediately AFTER SpatialDisplayManager.drawPersistedState("planning", view, context) and BEFORE return@postDelayed: a one-shot guarded flag set — if (routeSeedOpen && !recoveryLaunched) { recoveryLaunched = true; recoveryPending = true }. Guard vars declared near ~146: recoveryLaunched, recoveryPending (plus recoveryDetected from the earlier detect patch).
The popup
An AlertDialog gated on recoveryPending, placed just BEFORE the showInProgressPicker dialog (MVS ~1160). Single OK button sets recoveryPending = false. Purely informational — no load, no arm.
Why auto-resume was DEFERRED (the core lesson)
Processing before render. Three approaches all failed the same way — armed but not drawable:
Seeding routeMode true at init — armed the route before the map/desktop rendered → route "started" into an unrendered surface (no draw, "no prompt", message swallowed). ALSO broke compile: MVS:204 BackHandler back-gate uses routeMode before a moved declaration; and seeding the LIVE field fought the back-gate's need for blank-on-launch AND reintroduced the old convoy stuck-arm. REVERTED — routeMode stays mutableStateOf(false).
Direct load in onPageFinished (loadIntoRouteManager + routeMode=true) — came up armed but NOT drawable because it SKIPPED the geometry redraw the In-Progress picker does (queryGeomByIds → buildSegments → JS drawBuildLine).
Manual In-Progress resume works flawlessly (Fred verified: exit → +ROUTE → In Progress → auto-saved route loads + draws + arms). So the interim ships the notice and defers automation.
Auto-resume — the plan when back
After settle, TRIGGER THE EXISTING In-Progress picker path (it does the redraw correctly) — do NOT rebuild the load in onPageFinished. Cleanest: give the recovery popup a "Resume" button → showInProgressPicker = true → user taps the "Auto Saved In Progress" draft → proven path (loadIntoRouteManager → routeName/routeMethod/routeLifecycleState=ROUTE_LS_RESUMED → routeEntryNonce++ → routeMode=true → savePlanningState → scope.launch{ BY-ID rederive → drawBuildLine }). The In-Progress select handler is at MVS ~1159-1195; mirror or invoke it.
Save-name — the "everything is auto-saved" fix (committed a5a33dbfa)
Problem: every route saved silently keeping the auto-name "Auto Saved In Progress". The auto-name was introduced so a crash leaves a recoverable named draft; the name requirement moved from up-front to SAVE but was never wired.
Key structural fact (Fred): the draft writes on EVERY data point, so the save action only needs a RENAME — not a re-write.
Save-choice panel ("Save route" AlertDialog, MVS ~1091)
Required name field (OutlinedTextField) in the text={} block. Value blank if current name == "Auto Saved In Progress", else editable. Both buttons gated on a non-blank, non-auto name (toast "Enter a route name" otherwise).
Original on-disk name captured when the panel opens: onSaveRequested = { saveOrigName = routeName; showSaveChoice = true }. saveOrigName declared near ~146. This is the rename SOURCE (correct whether auto-named or already-named).
Save as in progress (dismissButton): renameDraft(saveOrigName, newName) ONLY (dropped the old writeDraft/overwriteDraft — draft already written per point) → clearRoute + routeMode=false. Runs in scope.launch{ withContext(IO){ rename } }.
Save as completed (confirmButton): gated on pts≥2 → scope.launch{ withContext(IO){ renameDraft(saveOrigName,newName) }; routeName=newName; delay(400); saveCompleted() }. The delay(400) lets the async rename settle before saveCompleted()'s insertRoute (MVS ~984) reads the renamed routeName. saveCompleted's spatial-DB write logic UNCHANGED.
renameDraft (RouteDraftStore:225): writes new-name file (tmp→rename), src.delete() on success, isNameTaken guard. VERIFY a leftover "Auto Saved In Progress" file appeared ONCE then was gone on retest — run several cycles when back to confirm cleanup is reliable; if it recurs, inspect the isNameTaken false-block and whether a COMPLETED save should DELETE the graduated draft (route now lives in spatial DB, draft's job done).
Architecture settled — DO NOT re-litigate
routeMode stays mutableStateOf(false) at init (MVS ~137). It is LIVE session state read by the back-gate (MVS:204 BackHandler { if (routeMode) toast else onBack() }). NOT seeded from persistence. Seeding created a chicken-and-egg (back wants blank-on-launch; seed wants true-after-crash — same var, opposite needs) AND reintroduced the convoy stuck-arm.
"Every field writes on every update" is THE RULE and STAYS (Fred: "it's not the writes that failed, it's the seeding, and that is on us"). Do NOT propose write-only markers / omitting fields from saves / separate marker stores.
Recovery DETECTION = isolated duplicate JSON read; recovery ACTION only after render (onPageFinished postDelayed), never during init.
Convoy map (ConvoyScreen.kt) FROZEN — layered Kotlin↔JS↔Leaflet↔self-saving-setView↔shared-MapStateStore process undocumented. Route+ is planner-only. 07-12 Direction-2 convoy-first plan SUPERSEDED. Known pre-existing convoy bbox-padding cumulative-zoom-out bug left as-is.
The compiler self-documents forward-reference errors — let it review rather than hand-auditing uses (that's how the MVS:204 conflict surfaced).

&#128309;&#128309; DESIGNED TODAY (not built) &mdash; full detail is in the LIVING MASTER
1. OSM TRAIL IMPORT. Governed by two Fred constraints that decide everything: imports are a repeatable USER process (app &rarr; Method B &rarr; pick area &rarr; import; no PC, no script, no hand-typed bbox), and no OSM data on GroupTrack infrastructure ever (an AWS endpoint would be distribution and trigger ODbL share-alike). 2. V2.7 VECTOR RENDERING &mdash; SCOPING_v2.7_vector_rendering_2026-07-26.html. Headline: two of SAT's three stores are LABELS, not photography, so bar 10 goes 107,000 raster tiles &rarr; ~21,700 (&asymp;80%), stacking on the corridor work. The real argument is sequencing &mdash; the dominant cost is operating on frozen code, and a tracking rewrite opens that tangle anyway, so it is rewrite once with MapLibre as the target, or twice.
&#11088; THREE FINDINGS THAT CAME OUT OPPOSITE TO PREDICTION
OSM labels are RICHER than Esri's downloaded roads/places layers &mdash; Fred, on device. The prediction was thin OSM coverage in remote Utah and a coverage-for-size trade. Got more content AND less storage.
OSM trails are COMPLEMENTARY to UGRC, not redundant &mdash; "some duplication but mostly coexistence." ⚠ This read changed TWICE before landing: (1) "very few trails render" at low zoom &rarr; looked negligible; (2) UGRC's property dump showed OSM carries no comparable attributes &rarr; looked useless; (3) both drawn at z15+ over real geography &rarr; complementary. Do not re-open from (1) or (2). OSM minor ways only appear from ~z14 in the OpenMapTiles schema &mdash; any coverage comparison must be at z15+.
SNAP-2 IS ALREADY RENDERER-INDEPENDENT &mdash; RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) at ConvoyMapViewerScreen:441 is Kotlin, no Leaflet API. And the redraw path already resolves by database ID, not by viewport (comment at :1240). That is exactly the discipline that makes it vector-tile-safe &mdash; already in place, by design.
&#128308; OPEN &mdash; carried forward
&#9888;&#9888; markComplete refreshMode COLLISION (ConvoyDownloadQueue:549) &mdash; it branches on entry.refreshMode and silently REMOVES the entry from the queue, but enqueueArea and enqueueCorridor both set refreshMode = replaceExisting. So ANY download submitted with REPLACE ticked is deleted from the queue on completion instead of marked COMPLETE &mdash; no row, no completedAt, no ETA sample. One line (branch on downloadType == MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH), and a strong candidate for BOTH refresh-never-completes AND much of the ETA starvation.
SAT frozen at 15 &mdash; still the only defect that changes what testers receive. Settled by one corridor run with REPLACE ticked.
ETA ~50&times; long &mdash; startedAt missing; queue WAIT time counted as download time. Resettable-accumulator design settled (start date + running tiles + running execution-ms &rarr; tiles/min, persisted in settings NOT the queue file so CLEAR cannot wipe it). Sampling policy still open (all jobs vs first-2-of-day vs rolling).
Rotation clears source selections &mdash; remember &rarr; rememberSaveable.
VACUUM / space reclamation &mdash; blocked on the unexplained "0 MB reclaimable".
G5 route corridors &mdash; design settled, anchors captured.
Per-source z-level caps &mdash; affects both paths; will change the corridor baseline, so measure separately.
&#9888; METHOD NOTES FROM TODAY
&#11088; Reach for the EXISTING model first. I proposed a separate OSM table on provenance + duplicate grounds &mdash; both answerable by a COLUMN. Then weighted ODbL against a paid product; the product is free, and the user-initiated-import model means the question never arises. Fred's instinct was right both times.
&#9888; Shipped three prototype builds that did not render. Causes: a type:'sky' layer (MapLibre v5+; on v4 an unknown layer type rejects the entire style &rarr; blank canvas), and a single hard-coded CDN. Untested code shipped as if tested. Fix carried: multi-CDN fallback + an on-screen error box, because a blank page must explain itself.
&#9888; A blank canvas in MapLibre = style validation failure, not a data problem. One invalid layer aborts everything.
&#9888; Windows Python ships its own CA bundle rather than using the OS trust store &mdash; hence CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on a machine whose browser is fine. pip install --upgrade certifi. Android uses the system trust store and is unaffected.

3 · Convoy architecture — findings that cost the day
  ⭐ Convoy is a PERSISTENT composable. It has no entry event.
  Fred: "convoy map is a persistent function it underlies all activity. it never goes away."
  This is the fact that made most of the day's route-mode work futile. Every anchor proposed for a "convoy entry reset" assumed an entry that does not exist:
    onPageFinished — fires once per page load, and the page loads once
    onViewportChanged — fires on every viewport event, not per entry
    LaunchedEffect(Unit) — never recomposes
    The [Fix2] block at ~732 whose comment says "re-entry" — it means re-reads the JSON fresh instead of trusting cmSeed, a staleness concern, not a lifecycle event. It sits inside onPageFinished's postDelayed(600).
  Conclusion: convoy needs no reset. The planner resets on entry, and convoy's tap handler resets at tap time. Both are sufficient. Do not re-litigate this.
  Convoy has TWO JavaScript bridges
    LineRegistered ononViewportChangedNotes
    ~596existing (reused WebView)~633No reseed, no lastMapProcessed
    ~831fresh WebView~860Has the reseed run { } block, sets lastMapProcessed
  Convoy is persistent, so on re-entry it takes the existing path. Verified identical structure on 07-24 (703625fb8) — this is how convoy has always been built, not a regression.
  Convoy's reseed gate was REMOVED on 07-01
  The run { } block in onViewportChanged carries its own comment: "gate removed: reseed convoy state EVERY viewport event (automatic refresh)". It is not per-entry — it fires on every pan and zoom.
  Naming collisions still unresolved
    ConvoyScreen.kt = the convoy map. ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt = the planner. Neither name says "planner."
    routeState in ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt means two things: local var (Routes artifact display state) and MapSnapshot.routeState (route session record).
4 · The two convoy breaks — both mine, both the same shape
  ⛔ LESSON 1 — ?: return inside an argument exits the whole function
  The morning's observe patch added to onPageFinished:
  android.widget.Toast.makeText(view?.context ?: return, ...)
  This reads like a null-safe accessor. It is an early exit from the entire override. When view was null it bailed before tile setup, setTileUrl, the persisted-frame restore, and drawPersistedState. Convoy drew nothing. No error, no log, no JS exception — just silence.
  It also displaced the original guard: val ctx = view?.context ?: return had been rewritten to view.context, moving the null check earlier into a place where failing it is catastrophic.
  ⛔⛔ LESSON 2 — @JavascriptInterface methods run on a BACKGROUND thread
  onViewportChanged is a @JavascriptInterface method. evaluateJavascript and Toast.makeText both require the main thread and throw when called off it. The throw aborts the rest of the method — including the processViewport call that draws every artifact.
  The existing code already knew this. It wraps its work in Thread { } and SpatialDisplayManager uses main.post { } for every evaluateJavascript. Two patches added today ignored that pattern:
  webViewRef.value?.evaluateJavascript("window.__routeMode = false;", null)   // line 890
android.widget.Toast.makeText(context, "ROUTE MODE OFF 
  Both removed. var routeModeResetLogged remains at ~247, now unused — harmless, comes out with the rest of the instrumentation.
  RULE: anything touching the UI or the WebView inside a @JavascriptInterface method must go through Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { }.
  Process failure worth naming
  A blanket git checkout 00826fb55 -- ConvoyScreen.kt was proposed and executed on the claim that it "only costs toasts." It also removed the reseed block. The surgical alternative — restore from af17c85dd and delete the three offending lines — was available the whole time and is what finally worked. Prefer targeted removal over blanket revert when the file contains a day's work.
5 · ⛔ DATA LOSS INCIDENT — 2026-08-01 ~11:41 device time
  What happened
  An adb install -r -d registered as a fresh install rather than an update. The app lost all-files authority. On next launch SpatialDbManager opened the spatial DB, was denied, and its create-if-missing path wrote empty schemas over the existing databases.
  Evidence, device log 11:44:04.805:
  avc: denied { ioctl } for path=".../grouptrack_spatial.db" dev="fuse"
ioctlcmd=0xf50c scontext=u:r:untrusted_app:s0:c178,c256,c512,c768
tclass=file permissive=0 app=com.grouptrack.android
I/SpatialDbMgr: Spatial DB: 0 trails, 0 tracks, 0 waypoints, 0 routes
  Result: grouptrack_spatial.db = 118 KB, grouptrack_data.db = 208 KB, both rewritten at 11:41. ~89 k trails and all artifacts gone. The app reported zero rows and carried on as if that were normal.
  Fred: "11:41 was the first set of install questions. I should have pulled the plug then."
  ⭐ 2.6e BLOCKER — the defect, independent of what triggered it
    Never open with create-if-missing when the file already exists. Check existence first; on a failed open with a file present, surface an error and stop.
    Verify access behaviourally, not by permission API. The app believed it had all-files access while the OS denied the ioctl. Attempt a real read.
    Fresh-install marker. Write a marker into filesDir (row counts, DB sizes, last-good timestamp). Private storage is wiped by a fresh install; external storage is not. Marker absent + external DB present = a fresh install just happened over existing data → stop, report.
    Row-count sanity. A DB that had 89 k trails yesterday reporting 0 today is not a valid state.
    Belt and braces: copy to grouptrack_spatial.db.lastgood after each successful startup.
  A Play Store update could produce the same sequence on a user's device, silently. This outranks the panel work.
  ⭐ OPERATIONAL RULES — effective immediately
    Install with plain -r. Never -d. Without -d, a regressed version code makes the install fail with an error instead of silently downgrading. The failure is the warning you want.
    If an install prompts first-install questions on an already-installed app: CANCEL. Do not proceed.
    Ten-second check after any install: adb shell ls -la /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/*.db — spatial DB in the hundreds of KB rather than tens of MB means it has been replaced.
  Note: the standing -r -d convention in the environment file is now superseded. Update it.
  Why the install registered as new — UNRESOLVED
  versionCode is git-derived: gitVersionProvider.get().toInt() + vcOffset (app/build.gradle.kts:65). A derived code that can regress, combined with -d, forces the downgrade path which resets app identity.
  Two earlier installs the same day (08:32, 10:47 builds) were fine. The 11:41 one was not. dumpsys evidence for that specific install was overwritten by the 12:05 recovery install — firstInstallTime and lastUpdateTime both read 12:05.
  Signing key ruled out — same AAB key for three months, two successful installs the same day.
  Next step: grep -rn "gitVersionProvider" --include=*.kts . — determine what it derives from and whether it can decrease. Fix by pinning the version code for local test builds, or by bumping VERSION_CODE_OFFSET. Single-build override available: -Pandroid.injected.version.code=NNNNNNNN.
  Recovery — the good outcome
  Complete data model rebuilt in under one hour: OSM import, Utah state trails, tracks, waypoints. GPX files in my_tracks/, tiles in maps/, OSM extracts in osm/ and the per-map JSONs all survived — only the two DBs were replaced.
  This is a measured fact worth carrying into the delete-by-source decision (§7): full reconstruction is cheap.

1 · Headline — Google Hybrid was never a dead source
  FIXED + VERIFIEDIt was a missing {s} substitution, in two places
  HYB had been written off as a withdrawn service and sat in the checklist as "disable it or ship a known-issue
  note." That was wrong. Two separate bugs, one root cause, both now fixed and proven on device.
  ⭐ What settled it: curling the endpoint by hand — 200, image/jpeg,
  29,722 bytes. Proving the service was alive before theorising about the app. Ten seconds. Do that first
  next time.
  ⭐ The URLs are not in Kotlin — that is why the first greps found nothing
  ConvoyConfig.kt:15 says it plainly: "TILE_SOURCES — reads from MapSourceManager
  (map_sources.json)." MapSourceManager.kt:90 reads url_template out of JSON.
  So grep lyrs= across app/src returns nothing and sends you looking in the wrong place.
  Asset: app/src/main/assets/map_sources.json.
  Template: https://mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=y&amp;x={x}&amp;y={y}&amp;z={z}.
  Five sources use {s}: google-hybrid, -satellite, -roads, -terrain, cartodb-voyager.
  Everything else uses literal hostnames — which is why only the Google sources looked dead.
  BUG 1 — download path
  ConvoyTileDownloader.buildTileUrl substituted {z}/{x}/{y}
  and nothing else. {s} was handled nowhere — grep across all Kotlin returned zero hits.
  The literal string mt{s}.google.com went to DNS and every tile failed silently.
  .replace("{s}", (((tile.x + tile.y) % 4 + 4) % 4).toString())   // SUBDOMAIN-2026-08-02
  Added as the first replace. Double-modulo guards negative x at antimeridian wrap; % 4
  gives mt0–mt3, deterministic per tile so a retry hits the same host.
  BUG 2 — display path
  Leaflet does expand {s} — but its default subdomain set is 'abc', so it
  requested mta/mtb/mtc.google.com, which do not exist. Neither map set a
  subdomains option.
  subdomains: (url.indexOf('google.com') !== -1 ? '0123' : 'abc')   // SUBDOMAINS-2026-08-02
  In both convoy_map.html (~:47) and grouptrack_map.html (~:111).
  Derived from the URL, not hardcoded — Google needs 0123, Carto needs abc.
  ⚠ The subdomains option is still missing on the overlay layers
  (convoy_map.html ~:71, grouptrack_map.html ~:138). Inert today; a subdomain'd overlay
  source would fail the same way.
  Verified end to end
    Display: TILE URL: https://mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=y… LABEL: SAT with no
    TILE ERROR after it
    Download: SAT.mbtiles mtime advanced 06:16 → 06:17 with size unchanged
    (INSERT OR REPLACE reuses pages)
    Offline: ConvoyIntercept: TILE mbtiles hit=true at z17/z18 — Google tiles
    rendering from the store
