4 · ⛔ The lesson of the week
  THREE-FOR-THREE: every convoy rendering failure in this arc was instrumentation aborting a method before its real work
    ?: return inside a toast argument killed onPageFinished — no tile setup, no
    setTileUrl, no persisted-frame restore, no drawPersistedState
    evaluateJavascript / Toast on a @JavascriptInterface background thread
    killed onViewportChanged — no processViewport, so no artifacts drew
    The offline render failure, cleared by removing ten more toasts from the same file
  All three landed in or around onPageFinished.
  Instrumentation is not free, and on this codebase it has cost more than the bugs it
  was added to find. When adding a trace to an override or a bridge method, ask what happens if that line
  throws or returns.
  ⭐ The counter-example is 08-02's tap fix: using instrumentation that already existed
  found the defect in three taps with no new code at all. Read the logs before adding to them.
5 · Source configuration has no persistence layer — root cause found
  ROOT CAUSENothing is putting Esri back. The choice was never saved.
  Fred: "Something keeps placing Esri hybrid in slot 1 even after I replaced with Google."
  XREF EVIDENCE (field_crossref_raw.txt): MapSourceManager has exactly
  two writes — :62 (dir.mkdirs()) and :248
  (apiKeysFile().writeText). The API keys file is the only thing it persists. Slot fields
  are read-only: :113 slot, :114 source_id, :115
  legacy_key.
  DEVICE EVIDENCE: adb shell find /sdcard -name "map_sources.json" returns
  nothing. The external override anticipated at MapSourceManager.kt:66 does not exist.
  ⭐ One missing layer, three symptoms: slot 1 reverting to Esri ·
  activeSourceKey resetting to SAT on every restart (declared = "SAT", in-memory only) ·
  possibly the Google download abort itself.
  ⛔ It was built, then deliberately removed — and why matters
  git log -S "externalJsonFile" returns exactly two commits:
    49bc8cecb — V2.5 Map Source Selection — ADDED it
    79251ae72 — 2026-05-21, "Fix tile download — read asset JSON only" —
    REMOVED it
  Both halves went: the read-external-first-with-copy-on-first-run block, and the entire body of
  saveExternalJson() — replaced with // Disabled — asset is single source of truth.
  ⚠ The empty function still exists and is still called, silently doing nothing.
  ⭐⭐ Why it was removed vindicates the fix. The external file held the
  entire catalogue, URLs included — so a stale copy served stale URLs and broke tile
  downloads, which is exactly what that commit was fixing. Ripping it out was correct for a real bug.
  ⭐⭐ The architecture (Fred) — two structures, two functions
  "There are two structures — the CATALOG which should be distributed, and the SLOT ASSIGNMENT of catalog to
  user's map slot. Two separate functions."
  CATALOG = map_sources.json in assets. Sources, templates, layers,
  default_slots, versions. Distributed with the app, read-only, replaced every release.
  ⭐ This is what makes a URL correction reach existing users — the {s} fix lives in a template here.
  Had the catalogue been copied to user space on first run, no existing user would ever receive it.
  SLOT ASSIGNMENT = which source_id occupies each user map slot, plus
  the active slot. User-owned, persisted, survives reinstall. Fred: "The slot assignment is a
  JSON that should exist in user space and be populated from default asset on install."
  ⛔ Do NOT restore 49bc8cecb as-was — that reintroduces the stale-URL
  bug. Persist only {slot, source_id, legacy_key} plus the active key, never the sources
  array. ⚠ Seed only when the user file is ABSENT — re-seeding on every install recreates the bug.
6 · Refresh is still on the bbox model and old segmentation
  568 entries at 60–70K tiles each
  Downloads cut over to corridors on 07-24. Refresh was never migrated — still bbox, still on the
  old gridCells instead of segmentCells. A map-source refresh enqueued
  568 entries at 60–70K tiles each (~37 million tiles). Not the 3,287-entry continental blowup of
  07-23, but the same root path.
  ⛔ Bbox refresh jobs RESET rather than complete — observed twice: a job at 5% went
  back to 4%, then a second reset the same way. Distinct from the known never-completes stall.
  ⭐ Design decision (Fred) — refresh gets two methods
  CORRIDOR IS THE DEFAULT. Route refresh through the track selection process —
  reuses proven code, kills the oversized-cell problem for free (the corridor worker re-derives tiles at run time),
  and matches what refresh is actually for.
  AREA REFRESH STAYS AS AN OPTION for users who downloaded areas. Same shape as the
  download side (downloadType selects the worker).
  The area path must move from gridCells to segmentCells.
  Corridor-by-default only reduces how often the defect is hit.
  ⚠ A select-all-tracks refresh needs an estimate-and-confirm gate — the import path
  does one submitDownload per track with no estimate, which is how 10 tracks became 215 jobs.
  ⚠ A failed queue job records no reason
  A corridor job failed and the entry said only "CORR SAT failed" — no exception, no HTTP status.
  The cause was unrecoverable because TRACK-DBG: TICK (twice every 5 s) had already rolled it out of the
  logcat ring buffer.
  Fix: put the failure cause in the queue entry AND the log. ⚠ TRACK-DBG actively
  destroys evidence — add it to the pre-release removal list alongside WAYPOINT-TRACE.
  To catch it next time, start the capture BEFORE queueing:
  adb logcat -c then adb logcat | grep -viE "TRACK-DBG|DetailGate|NetworkStateTracker|WM-|chromium|ConvoyIntercept" &gt; /d/corr_run.txt

4 · ⛔ Corrections to the record (Fred, 08-03)
  1 · The 215 jobs were NOT a submit-per-track
  Fred: "the import by track does not exist in area refresh. all track boundaries became bboxes and that is how we
  ended up with 215 jobs." Refresh converted each track BOUNDARY into a BBOX and enqueued area jobs
  from them. A switchbacked trail's bounding box covers the whole mountain; its corridor covers a line buffer.
  That difference IS the 215 jobs — and it is the same reason corridor downloads were built on 07-24.
  2 · Corridor refresh does not exist
  Fred: "the refresh does not currently support corridor imports." So step 5 is BUILD, not
  MIGRATE. The 08-02 wording — "reuses proven code" — understates it.
  ⭐ Follow-on: the corridor worker re-derives its tiles at run time from track geometry, so it never
  builds oversized cells. The gridCells → segmentCells migration is an AREA-path
  problem only, and area stays as an option, so that migration is still owed.
  3 · "Corridor is the default" is wrong
  Fred: "during the refresh the user must select if he prefers area or corridor imports." It is a
  choice presented at refresh time, not a default the app applies. ⚠ Record it this way or a future
  session builds a silent default and the prompt never appears.
5 · ⭐⭐⭐ THE COLUMN FILE — design session, and what it revealed
  The split (Fred's architecture, unchanged)
  CATALOG = map_sources.json in assets. Sources, templates, layers,
  default_slots. Ships with the app, read-only, replaced every release. This is what made the
  {s} fix reach existing users — had the catalogue been copied to user space on first run, no
  existing user would have received it.
  COLUMN FILE = the user's table. Slot → source, plus the active key and the URL template.
  A mapping table, not a replication of the catalogue.
  Why this is not a reversion of 79251ae72
  That commit killed an external file that held the whole catalogue, URLs included — a stale copy
  served stale URLs and broke tile downloads. The column file holds three rows and points at names. Different thing.
The five catalogue rules (Fred)
    Names never change. A rename is a tombstone plus a new entry appended at the bottom.
    Only the URL value is mutable, applied at release.
    Deletes tombstone — entries never leave the list, so sequence holds.
    The user owns slot assignment, active slot, and API keys. Everything else seeds from the catalogue.
    A scheme change is a delete-and-append, not a URL edit (Claude's addition, accepted) — different
      projection or max native zoom means the tiles already in that column's store stop matching the template.
⭐⭐ What the blast radius actually found
  1 · defaultSlots is not a constant. It is mutable in-memory state.
  :50   private var defaultSlots: List&lt;SlotConfig&gt; = emptyList()
:118  defaultSlots = slots                    &lt;- loaded from the asset
:142  defaultSlots = listOf(...)              &lt;- hardcoded fallback
:218  defaultSlots = defaultSlots.toMutableList().apply { ... }   &lt;- the user's slot change
  Line 218 is the user's selection. Nothing persists it. Six read sites — :153, :163, :172,
  :187, :215, :273 — all funnel through this one field, which is why the fix is smaller than the FIX 1/2/3
  framing suggested: you do not convert the readers, you change where the field is loaded from.
  2 · The asset is read exactly ONCE per process
  init() guards at :72 with if (initialized) return, set at :119.
  Every ensureInit() call returns immediately after the first. Nothing else opens
  map_sources.json. So the asset cannot be overwriting a selection mid-session, and no tripwire is
  needed — reading the code answered it.
  3 · ⛔ THE ORDERING HAZARD — ensureInit() / loadFallback()
  ensureInit() at :282–286 calls loadFallback() when not initialized — and
  loadFallback() sets initialized = true at :147. So:
    any getter fires before init(context) → hardcoded Esri loads → initialized = true
    the real init() runs later → sees initialized already true → returns
      immediately and never reads the asset
    the process runs entirely on hardcoded Esri, announced by a single Log.w nobody is watching for
  That would look exactly like the reported symptom — slot 1 back on Esri, no explanation. It is an
  ordering bug, independent of persistence.
  ⭐ Fred's call: "sounds like a trap … i am afraid of why it is there." Rather than remove
  it blind, phase 1 logs the request with a stack trace naming the caller and refuses to write
  the column file at all when fallback ran. Nothing removed, nothing commented, no risk — and if it fires, the
  caller names itself.
  4 · Resolution is LATE, and the job carries a slot name
  [W] ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:706   .putString("refresh_slot", entry.refreshSlot)
[R] ConvoyCorridorWorker.kt:52   val slotName = inputData.getString("refresh_slot") ?: ""
[R] ConvoyDownloadWorker.kt:39   val refreshSlot = inputData.getString("refresh_slot") ?: ""
  The worker resolves slot → source → URL at execution time. A slot that changes between queue and
  execution silently redirects the download — and stores are keyed by the layer's cache_dir, so the wrong
  tiles land in the store you believe holds the right ones. No error. Quiet success against the wrong source.
  ⭐ This is why the column file is load-bearing, not merely correct: it makes late resolution safe.
  5 · Fred's mechanism for the download failure
  "esri would not work when the connection was established with google … the reason for the failure." If the
  downloader holds a client configured for the Google host and the slot re-resolves mid-run to an Esri template on a
  different host, in-flight requests aim at the wrong endpoint and fail silently — which is exactly what
  "CORR SAT failed" with no exception and no HTTP status looks like.
  ⚠ Hypothesis, not finding. Unknown whether the downloader keeps a persistent client per host or
  builds a request per tile. Per-tile would mean contamination rather than failure. Both disappear once resolution is
  stable, which is the useful part.
  6 · The verification loop was itself the contamination loop
  Fred's method for confirming tiles were being replaced was to view offline maps of that column —
  which required switching sources to flush the cache. Switching sources is what triggers the re-resolve. So checking
  whether the swap was working is what broke the swap, and repeating the check repeated the damage.
  ⭐ This likely also explains the refresh "reset" (5%→4%). A job re-resolving mid-run and restarting
  its accounting against a different tile set would look exactly like a percentage going backwards. Retest after
  phase 2 — a free measurement that may retire a P0-shaped item.
  Two other things found
  The write hook already exists. updateSlotSource() at :213 already calls
  saveExternalJson() at :221 — an empty body. Persistence was one function to fill, no new call
  sites.
  ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt:59 claims something untrue: "Writes slot changes to
  external Documents/GroupTrack/map_sources.json." It does not. The comment describes the feature being built now,
  left behind when saveExternalJson() was gutted.
  An orphan local: ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:97 — var activeSource by remember {
  mutableStateOf("SAT") }, never synced to the global, and it drives the map-bar highlight via
  isActive = activeSource == label. The UI can show SAT highlighted while the source is something
  else. Convoy has no equivalent. Independent of the file work.
6 · ⭐ STEP 1 — PHASE 1 PATCH: written, compiled, awaiting device test
  READYpatch_column_file_phase1b_2026-08-03.py · marker COLUMNFILE-2026-08-03
  Applied and compiled — compileGoogleReleaseKotlin BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m 04s. Full build running at
  session close. Not yet committed.
  ⭐ WRITE ONLY. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. That is the point.
  getSlotSources, getDownloadSources, getSourceByKey and
  getAllOverlayLayers still read defaultSlots — the patch's own verification
  refuses to write if they do not. The app behaves exactly as it does today, which is what makes this half independently
  testable and safe to commit before the reader work.
What the patch does — five anchored edits
  EDIT 1 · Column-file plumbing, inserted after apiKeysFile():
  columnFile() → Documents/GroupTrack/map_slots.json, currentVersionCode(),
  syncColumnFile(), readTerminated(), writeColumnFile(),
  terminatedColumns().
  EDIT 2 · syncColumnFile(context) called at the END of init(),
  after the asset parses so defaultSlots and sources are populated.
  EDIT 3 · saveExternalJson() filled in — was an empty body that was
  still being called. Plus readColumnFileOrNull().
  EDIT 4 · setActive() persists the active key. It was in-memory only,
  defaulting to "SAT" at :53.
  EDIT 5 · loadFallback() records that it was requested — sets a flag and
  logs with a stack trace. Its own behaviour is unchanged.
The rules the patch encodes
    ConditionAction
    Column file absentSeed from defaultSlots + catalogue, stamp version code
    Present, same version codeLoad only. No install pass.
    Present, different version codeINSTALL PASS — refresh
      url_template per column from the catalogue by source_id; mark
      status: "terminated" where the source is gone; slot assignments never touched; re-stamp
    Present but unreadableLOG AND STOP. No seed, no overwrite.
    Fallback ranNO WRITE AT ALL. Log and return.
  Why "unreadable ≠ absent" is not pedantry
  Treating a read failure as absent is the create-if-missing shape that destroyed the spatial DB on
  08-01 (~89k trails). All-Files access has been observed reporting true while denied. If an
  unreadable column file were treated as absent, seeding would overwrite the user's assignments with catalogue defaults —
  the exact bug being fixed, arriving through the back door.
File shape
Documents/GroupTrack/map_slots.json
{
  "version_code": 2060512,
  "active": "SAT",
  "columns": [
    { "slot": 1, "legacy_key": "SAT",   "source_id": "esri-imagery-overlays",
      "short_label": "SAT", "url_template": "https://...", "requires_key": false,
      "status": "active" },
    { "slot": 2, "legacy_key": "TOPO",  ... },
    { "slot": 3, "legacy_key": "TOPO+", ... }
  ]
}
  Design points inside the patch
    Stores the URL TEMPLATE, not a resolved URL. resolveUrl() at :277
      injects {key} at use time, and keys are persisted separately in api_keys.json.
    Atomic write — temp file then rename. A truncated column file read at worker start is a mystery
      a week later.
    map_slots.json, not map_sources.json. externalJsonFile()
      at :66 already claims that name and it is the file 79251ae72 killed.
    The install pass carries the user's assignment forward — priorById wins over
      slot.sourceId. A release may retire a source; it may not repoint a column the user chose.
  DECISION OWEDWhat "terminated" means
  The patch currently marks a column terminated when its source_id is not found in the
  catalogue. Fred's rules call for an explicit tombstone instead — a status field on the catalogue entry, so
  a retired source stays in the list and keeps the sequence. That is an asset change plus one line here.
  Absence works today because nothing has been retired yet; the explicit tombstone is what rule 3 requires.
⭐ TEST PLAN — Droid 2, four checks
    Seeds on first run. Cold start, then
      adb shell cat /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/map_slots.json. Expect three columns plus
      version_code and active.
    Regenerates if deleted. Delete, force-stop, cold start, cat again.
    Does not overwrite on restart. Cold start twice; logcat should read
      column file current (vc=…), no install pass.
    Persists a slot change. Change a source in Map Sources, then cat. The new
      source_id must be in the file. This is the check that proves
      saveExternalJson() is wired — and it also shows whether the slot change now survives a
      restart, which is the symptom that started all of this.

adb -s 24039703201775 logcat -v time -s MapSourceMgr:V

7 · Steps 2–6 — goals
  STEP 2 · The app reads the column file
  Goal: nothing resolves from default_slots at run time once the user file exists.
  defaultSlots becomes seed-only. Because all six readers funnel through that one field,
  this is a change to where the field is loaded, not a conversion of every call site.
  Also owed here: the orphan local at ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:97, and reconciliation on
  init — walk the columns, expire any pointing at a retired or missing source.
  STEP 3 · Test a Google download
  Goal: measure HYB against ground that has stopped moving. ⭐ Fred placed the test here
  deliberately — before any download-shape work. The result is diagnostic either way: if the failure
  disappears, resolution was the cause; if it persists, resolution is eliminated for good and you are debugging a real
  download problem on solid ground.
  ⚠ Start the capture before queueing, and remove TRACK-DBG: TICK first — it fires twice every
  5 s and destroyed the evidence last time. Log the resolved URL per job; that single line separates
  slot-resolution from a genuine download failure.
  STEP 4 · Corridor checkbox on the download panel
  Goal: a second checkbox beside Area. Area → draw box (existing). Corridor → a list of
  tracks, select all or check as many as needed. ⭐ Every download origin already routes through one panel
  (ConvoyDownloadConfirm → submitDownload), so this lands in one place.
  ⚠ Select-all needs an estimate-and-confirm gate — the user should see the count before it queues.
  STEP 5 · Refresh becomes area OR corridor, user chooses
  Goal: the refresh asks which method. Corridor refresh must be BUILT — it does not
  exist. The track-list picker from step 4 is reused here; build it once, use it twice.
  STEP 6 · Route the choice to the right enqueue
  Goal: enqueueArea or the corridor enqueue, submitting jobs for the changed source.
  ⚠ Still owed alongside: the gridCells → segmentCells migration on the AREA
  path (corridor re-derives at run time and never builds oversized cells), and a check of
  enqueueRefresh's argument order against enqueueArea — swapped bounds remains the
  leading unverified hypothesis for the 07-23 continental incident.
  Terminated-source behaviour, as settled
    The installer expires the source and stops. Notification is somebody else's task.
    On map load with a terminated column, the selector fires. User picks or cancels; cancel means it
      returns next restart.
    The column keeps serving its current maps throughout — offline tiles are unaffected, nothing
      blanks, nothing blocks an off-grid start.
    A terminated column is unchecked and not selectable for new downloads or refresh.
8 · Lesson of the day
  ⭐⭐ The method is trusted. The mistake was not removing the instrumentation.
  Fred, correcting the record: "the breakthrough on route was trapping the state and visually seeing what triggers
  were failing. i chose the method is trusted. the mistake was not removing the instrumentation when we finished."
  So the lesson is not "instrumentation is expensive." It is:
    Instrumentation is temporary by definition. It comes out when the task closes, in the same commit
      that closes it — not on a cleanup list where it accumulates until it does damage.
    All three of this week's rendering failures happened in the window between "found it" and
      "someday we'll clean that up."
    The mechanical rules still hold — Log.d not Toast, nothing in an argument position,
      off-main-thread awareness — but those are about what you write, not whether.
  ⚠ Live instance: showProximityPopup and the Kotlin onProximityTap are dead
  but still present. Same pattern, smaller stakes. They come out with their caller.
  ⚠ And one about direction
  Fred called the direction on the FIT bug — "every fiber of my body blames proximity" — while my elimination
  of that code range was wrong twice. Recorded because the reasoning pattern matters more than the fix: I was scanning for
  one shape of evidence (function name() and reported the range clean when the scan could not have seen what
  was there.

  FOUND + FIXEDA real bug in phase 1 — caught by check 4
  Symptom: changing a source logged both wrote 3 columns and Slot SAT
  updated to source google-satellite — and the file still read esri-imagery-overlays. The mutation
  happened, the write happened, and the change was discarded.
  Cause (my design error): saveExternalJson() passed readColumnFileOrNull()
  as existing, so writeColumnFile() applied its install-pass rule
  priorById[slot.legacyKey] ?: slot.sourceId. priorById is built from the file on
  disk, which still held the old source — so every save let the stale value overwrite the fresh selection.
  ⭐ The distinction: "prior assignment wins" is correct for the INSTALL PASS — a
  release may retire a source but must never repoint a column the user chose. It is exactly wrong for the SAVE
  PATH, where defaultSlots is the truth. Fix: the save path passes null. Install pass
  untouched. COLUMNFILE-SAVEFIX-2026-08-03.
  ✅ Verified: slot 1 now writes google-satellite with template
  https://mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=s&amp;x={x}&amp;y={y}&amp;z={z}, carrying the {s} fix.
  ⭐⭐ Checks 1–3 all passed and the file looked correct
  Only changing a source exposed it. A phase built to be "write-only, safe to commit" would have been
  committed broken. Check 4 existed precisely to catch this, and it did. The value of a test plan is the
  check you were tempted to skip.
  Minor, not fixed
  Three wrote 3 columns lines per interaction — both setActive() and
  updateSlotSource() call saveExternalJson(), and entering Map Sources appears to trigger
  setActive on its own. Harmless (atomic, idempotent content) but more disk traffic than needed.
  ⭐⭐⭐ The display model — settled this evening, NOT built
  The workflow: find your area → look at tracks around it → drop waypoints → now turn trails
  on. Trails come last, after you know what you want.
  Why: "see the ground, see the features, see the trail — not a 100 mile line on the map."
  Drilling into the yarnball, a thick blue line resolves into 30 trails, and there are hundreds of such spots. That
  intimidates rather than helps. ⭐ The panel is a participation switch, not a density filter —
  "you are not using select/omit to turn trails on and off, you are using zoom to narrow what appears; the right tool
  for the job."
  Seven items: 5,000 ceiling flat at every zoom · toggle disabled below z11 with
  Trails (Z11 or greater to display) · trails forced off on map change (not every panel entry) ·
  viewport state still restores, only visibility overridden · search by track/trail/town/park returning ~100 sq mi ·
  no GPS snapback on the planner · manual. Full detail in the Living Master under 00-DISPLAY.
  ⭐ Tunables named in one place (TRAILS_MIN_ZOOM, TRAILS_MAX_ROWS), with a
  temporary dev control to tune live — 39-minute builds make tuning by rebuild expensive.
  ⛔ It comes out in the commit that closes the task.
  ⭐ The stated endstate — Suggest
  Fred: "set your points of interest, your waypoint to embark and return from, the range of distance and time,
  and let the software recommend routes that touch all your points. That is my vision for endstate." That is the
  Suggest button already in the Route panel marked "soon".
  The product in one line: "the route map is the palette — the routes and trails and the infinite
  combinations to create a unique experience visiting points of interest."
  ⚠ Connectivity is the hard part, not the routing. ⚠ Time is harder than distance — start distance-only.
  ⭐ This is why track-to-trail matters: tracks are certainty, trails are a claim, and FILL closes
  exactly the junctions the router needs. Detail in the Living Master under 00-ENDSTATE.

1 &middot; The day in one line
A single line on the wrong thread had been stopping the planner from drawing for three days.
ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:717   inside @JavascriptInterface onViewportChanged
    webViewRef?.evaluateJavascript("setRouteMode(false)", null)
java.lang.RuntimeException: A WebView method was called on thread 'JavaBridge'.
The throw aborted the method before the state reads, before lastMapProcessed was set, and before
processViewport — the actual draw. And because the flag was never set, the gate it sits in stayed
open forever, so every later viewport event re-entered and threw again.
⭐ Everything followed from it: nothing drew on direct entry; artifacts appeared only after a convoy
visit (residue on the shared WebView); the trails toggle did nothing (assigned two lines after the throw); the
restore logged a continental bbox (assigned before the throw, never refreshed). 08-03's "FIT bug closed,
mechanism not established" was the same defect — removing the proximity block changed timing enough to mask it.

3 &middot; The queue was deleting its own successes
markComplete() branched on entry.refreshMode and silently removed the entry —
no status, no stamp, no row. But refreshMode is also the REPLACE-TILES flag, and both of the
day's Google corridor runs logged replace=true:
08:31:29  Corridor complete: CORR SAT downloaded=561 failed=0
08:47:04  Corridor complete: CORR SAT downloaded=681 failed=0
⛔ Both flawless. Neither visible. markFailed does not take that path, so
the only download entries that ever survived were the ones that FAILED — which is why 08-02's
"CORR SAT failed" was the only artifact left to reason from.
⭐ THE PRINCIPLE: the queue is the RECORD. Deleting rows to reduce clutter destroys evidence
permanently; filtering hides it reversibly. Display concerns do not mutate state.
⚠ Still owed: the flag is overloaded — split isRefreshCell from replaceTiles.
The schema comment at :442-444 already forbids the conflation; markComplete was the drift.

no harm done — 561 tiles wrote straight afterwards). It is the same denial class that preceded the 08-01 data
loss. Refuse-to-create is guarding a condition that occurs regularly, and SAT.mbtiles is
4.2 GB of unbacked work behind it.

6 &middot; Method notes worth keeping
⭐ Read the HEAD of a stack trace before theorising. The root cause sat at frame 99 of a trace
present in every capture from 09:00. The exception type was one line above it. Nobody read up until the afternoon.
⭐ Filter the FILE, not the stream. adb logcat -d &gt; file then grep. A bad pattern on a
live stream is indistinguishable from a silent app — and Ctrl-C does not reach adb.exe in Git-Bash,
so the redirect stops advancing while the prompt looks stuck.
⭐ A negative grep is only as good as its pattern. Twice today a scan reported "clean" when it could not
have matched what was there (log tags held in TAG constants; a range inside a
&lt;script src&gt; whose inline body never executes).
⭐⭐ Convoy is the reference implementation; divergence is a defect until proven intentional.
Four times this week convoy had a fix the planner did not. Three are now closed; the reseed gate is the one
legitimate difference.
⚠⚠ PATCH VERIFIERS MUST DERIVE THEIR EXPECTATIONS, NOT ASSERT THEM. Five rollbacks today were
the verifier, never the change: brace counts including comment text, a global string check catching an untouched
block, an identifier matching the patch's own explanatory comment, and twice a hand-counted marker total.
The guards behaved correctly every time — they refused writes they could not prove and left the tree clean —
but each cost a re-run.
⛔ An --apply whose output was never read is NOT applied.
CORRIDORQUERY was recorded as landed and was not; it surfaced two patches later as an unresolved
reference. git diff --stat is the authoritative answer to what is really in the tree.

HEAD a0675be42 &middot; three commits pushed &middot; APK built 23:04 and installed on Droid 2
1 &middot; The day in one line
Source map migration went from a reload engine to one question with three answers, and the code shrank with it.
The morning built and proved the destructive half. The afternoon and evening was design — and most of it was spent removing things. What shipped is smaller than what was written.
⭐ THE UNLOCK, and it was Fred's: "remove the tracks — the things we could put back." Every earlier design tried to preserve both storage shapes at once, which forced detection logic, decision matrices and per-item pickers. Take the tracks out and the area bounds become honest by themselves, and tracks cost ~10 minutes each to restore.
2 &middot; What shipped
CommitContents
27dfb433d
Migration record + guarded clear. ConvoySourceMigration.kt, ConvoySourceClear.kt, screen wiring. 3 files, 723 insertions. Clear proven on Droid 2 — 3 stores removed, TOPO/TOPO+ untouched.
54a62e4f6
Migration panel: three selectable rows, one CONTINUE disabled until a row is chosen, title "Source Map Migration". +111/&minus;71.
a0675be42
MBTilesStore.deleteTiles(type, tiles: List&lt;TileKey&gt;). 63 insertions. Step 1a of 3. Nothing calls it yet.
⭐ Verified on device tonight: three rows render, radios work, headings bold and larger, CONTINUE gated on selection, both live options behave. Fred: "all good except automated refresh" — which is the option deliberately left disabled.
3 &middot; The design, settled
1  DELETE AND START OVER    protect NOTHING     clear · rebuild around tracks · draw new areas
2  MOVE EVERYTHING          protect the AREA    delete track tiles · refresh area · re-import tracks
   (automatic, background)                      all downloads submitted at once; every image slowly
                                                replaced from the new source
3  MOVE ON MY SCHEDULE      protect EVERYTHING  nothing touched; convert manually, ground by ground,
                                                with Replace tiles ticked
⭐ No map-type question. "How were these downloaded?" only existed to route an automated refresh — which is just as well, because nothing on disk records how a store was built.
⭐ Clear is now only ever chosen on purpose. No case is forced into it, which is what removed the "are you riding soon?" question entirely.
⭐ The governing constraint (Fred): these screens process ALL or delete ALL. No partial conversion. That single rule removed the detection logic, the matrices and the pickers.
4 &middot; What is left
The one new function the whole design needs
1a  MBTilesStore.deleteTiles        ✅ DONE, committed a0675be42
1b  ConvoyCorridorDeleteWorker.kt   NEW FILE. Mirrors ConvoyCorridorWorker's discovery
                                    (geomHash → getTrackPoints → corridorTiles → loop
                                    layers) with deleteTiles instead of downloadTiles.
                                    Nothing dispatches to it, so it compiles alone.
1c  QUEUE WIRING — ⛔ ATOMIC
      · DownloadType.DELETE_CORRIDOR_TILES
      · DownloadPriority.forType() → DELETE
      · launchWorker dispatch → ConvoyCorridorDeleteWorker
      · enqueueDeleteCorridor + batch, DEFAULT = ALL TRACKS (no picker, no list)
⛔ 1c cannot be split. The when at ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:797 is exhaustive by design — its own comment says a fifth DownloadType should become a compile error rather than a silent fallthrough. Adding the enum breaks the build until the dispatch branch lands.
⛔ WHY deleteTiles HAD TO EXIST — the crux. The store could previously delete only a RANGE (deleteTileRange, min/max x and y) or a WHOLE SOURCE. A corridor is neither. Pointing the existing ConvoyDeleteWorker at a corridor deletes its bounding box — the hull problem inverted: instead of downloading ground the user never had, it would delete ground the user still wants.
Four quick items, per Fred
Delete track maps — 1b + 1c above.
Artifact popups in route mode. ⛔ Two blockers first: checkLayer(layer, typeName, color) has no visible parameter, and two copies exist in grouptrack_map.html (~18 and ~854) — a duplicate proximity scan, two popups racing per tap — while convoy_map.html has neither. Resolve the duplication before patching. ⚠ Do NOT null the layer on hide; it is a cache, and nulling forces a full rebuild per toggle at 10,000 trails.
Google Hybrid as new-install default. patch_default_slot1_hybrid_2026-08-06.py, written and never applied. One value in default_slots; no migration code needed because writeColumnFile:253 already keeps existing users on their saved column. ⚠ Neither Droid can verify it — both have map_slots.json, so it needs a genuine fresh install on Droid 2.
z7 trails and tracks. A minZoom change. ⚠ 11→10 was reverted the same session after ANRs, and z7 is four levels lower. Mitigation is the 40,000→10,000 trail cut. ⭐ Tracks are cheap; trails are the risk. Row cap is if (z &lt; 14) 500 else 2000, and the z10 ANR cause was never established.
⭐ Manual impact: only items 2 and 4 — tap behaviour, and what is visible at low zoom.
5 &middot; Open defects
⛔ THE ×3 ESTIMATE. A Google corridor download estimated 1,560 tiles and downloaded 520 — ratio exactly 3 = Esri's layer count. Estimate uses getDownloadSources().filter{...}.sumOf{...} → 3; worker uses getSourceByKey(slot)?.layers → 1. The worker is right. ⭐ Second site: ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:183 sums layers across EVERY slot with no filter and takes no slotName, so it cannot price a selection — callers ConvoyViewModel:987 and SpatialDbManager:2085 (track import). Fred: search git for the total-tiles calc, it was modified to correct display values. ⛔ Fix before any screen quotes times or sizes — the migration panel is about to.
5-second settle delay before resumeQueue(), after the delete loop. One line. FUSE needs a beat between unlink and the re-create that a resuming worker triggers.
Record hygiene — begin() runs unconditionally but the dialog only shows if (count &gt; 0), leaving records at "phase": "opened" (8 on Droid 2).
Bytes accounting — report from_bytes_total across all runs so the store count and the MB figure agree.
Track name on corridor queue jobs — reinstated for testing legibility. Resolve from geomHash at display time, batched; no schema change.
Is "Replace tiles" plainly reachable on the AREA download path? Option 3's instructions depend on it. Unverified.
6 &middot; Method notes from today
⛔⛔ A GREEN BUILD PROVES NOTHING IF THE APPLY DID NOT RUN. Three phantom applies today, each hidden by a successful compile of unchanged code. ⭐ The fix that worked: append the marker count to the gate — ./gradlew compile... && grep -c MARKER file — so the build result and the file state come back together. git diff --stat is the authoritative answer.
⚠⚠ A CHECK ABOUT CODE MUST RUN ON CODE, NOT ON PROSE. Two more patches aborted on their own doc comments — one grepping for a forbidden string that appeared in the KDoc explaining why it was forbidden. Strip comments before checking. Third occurrence of this class in two days.
⚠ VERIFIERS MUST DERIVE, NOT ASSERT. A patch aborted asserting zero dismissible dialogs when the correct derived answer was one. count before − removed + added = expected after.
⭐⭐ SCOPE-CREEP DETECTOR (Fred): "When scope expands and focus is lost and you cannot precisely describe the options and their benefits — back up." The inability to state each option and what it is for is the symptom. ⭐ Recovery move: ask what we are trying to accomplish and what the obstacles are — not what to build next. The design got smaller every time that was asked.
⭐ Render before shipping a screen. Drawing the panel at real dialog proportions exposed ~320 words with the actions below the fold, and three stacked buttons that read as a layout accident. Neither was visible in code.
7 &middot; Rejected, and why
DesignWhy
runMigration with TileChoice/ReloadChoice enumsWritten, never applied. Repopulation is the existing Download Tiles by Area / by Track.
ConvoyReloadHolder — park queue entries in JSONBuilt, compiled, deleted unused. Solved an ordering problem that step-splitting removes.
Rename instead of delete (SAT→SAT__old)Patch written, never applied. Unnecessary once the queue drain and the file delete are separated.
A dedicated refresh panelForced an either/or. A real user can have both shapes, and the downloads panel already offers both with Replace.
Map-type question / detection / decision matrixRemoved entirely by the all-or-nothing rule.
Corridor/area coverage overlayRight visualisation, wrong cost. There is no bbox rendering anywhere in the app today.
8 &middot; Facts learned today
Google Hybrid's cache dir is google_hybrid, not SAT — one layer, its own file. The SAT column changes store FILENAME with its source. ⚠ Anything keyed on the literal "SAT" is reasoning about a store that only exists under Esri.
Under Esri the worker DOES fetch all three layers. They were stale since 08-02 only because everything since ran on Hybrid. So the ×3 is correct under Esri and wrong only under Hybrid — fix the estimate to read the live assignment, do not remove the multiplier.
⛔ enqueueRefresh shares segmentCells with enqueueArea (parity comment dated 07-22). The "second chopper needs retiring" claim in 00-ENQUEUE-PRINCIPLE is WRONG — correct it there.
tileBoundsLatLon(:201) derives its box as min/max over tiles at the densest zoom only — a hull, not a coverage map.
Droid 2 SAT column: SAT.mbtiles 5,314,371,584 (was 4.24 GB on 08-02) + labels 210,006,016 + 251,092,992 = ≈5,507 MB. ✅ The app runs fine with no SAT.mbtiles present — db() is open-or-create.
9 &middot; The bigger idea, recorded late
⭐⭐ Fred: "I do not care about route. I am trying to create a method where a PRE-RIDE ROUTE CAN BE DISTRIBUTED AND IMPORTED WITH MAPS, allowing a rider to download accurate maps with efficient space utilisation BEFORE TRAILS ARE CAPTURED."
The route is the distribution unit. A leader plots the ride, emails it out, and each rider imports it and downloads exactly the corridor that ride needs. Nobody has to have ridden the ground, and nobody has to box a region.
⭐ Why it is accurate: a SNAPPED route's geometry IS trail geometry — snap-2 pulls the trail's own vector points — padded half a mile either side. Corridor-quality coverage for ground never ridden.
⭐ Email survives it. The snapping happened at authoring time, so the coordinates already follow the trail. What does not travel is the per-vertex lineId — a local DB reference. So a shared route downloads maps and draws perfectly; re-snapping is re-established locally by adding or removing a point.
What it needs: route geom_hash (a column, one call at insert, a backfill — computeGeomHash(wkt) exists and insertRoute already receives the WKT) · artifact TYPE carried alongside the hash so the worker looks in the right table · a distribution format and import path, mirroring track import's corridor option.
⛔ Without the hash, ConvoyCorridorWorker resolves against TRACKS, finds nothing, and fails quietly — the batch counts no-geometry as skipped.

1 &middot; The day in one line
We built the automated tile refresh, ran it end to end, and the run told us the
design was wrong.
The corridor delete works — 617,255 tiles removed across 88 tracks on Droid 2, verified against
a prediction that differed only by a change Fred made in between. But watching it run surfaced the
arithmetic that kills the design it belongs to: a full store refresh at real scale is 50-60 GB
and days of downloading. The redesign that came out of that is in
00-MIGRATION-V2 and it is smaller, additive, and has no irreversible step.

4 &middot; The design conclusion
"This is a trail riding decision. Google maps is available ONLINE in either map as
soon as the change in map sources is made."
⛔ The migration concerns OFFLINE STORED TILES ONLY. Online rendering switches instantly.
"Refreshing 50-60 GB of data is just not an option."
Which is why mandatory-delete-then-rebuild cannot be offered. Full detail in
00-MIGRATION-V2; the short version:
Delete becomes OPTIONAL everywhere, default off. Replace overwrites in place, so the
delete is only for reclaiming space. With it off the operation is ADDITIVE — no point of no
return, no permanent gate.
Areas stay on original map data until refreshed. Nothing blank, nothing deleted; only
Esri\u2019s label overlays are lost.
Option 2 = corridors and areas, each optional. Option 3 = leave maps in place,
with optional immediate corridor refresh. Option 1 = clear and start over, for anyone
uncertain.
⭐ The scan\u2019s real job is helping the user choose, not verifying the delete.

6 &middot; Method notes worth keeping
⚠⚠ RENAMING A PATCH RENAMES THE MARKERS IT LEAVES BEHIND. New failure mode
from the never-reuse-a-name rule: patch 07e was re-issued as 07f, and patch 07g then anchored on
the 07E marker that no longer existed. The guard caught it and refused the write.
⛔ A LOCAL DECLARED INSIDE if (showDownloadPanel) CEASES TO EXIST
WHEN THE PANEL CLOSES — and was also 300 lines below its use. TWO faults in one placement, ~36
cascade errors from one root. Same trap as the 08-01 webViewRef error.
⭐ PATCH GUARDS SHOULD CHECK ORDERING, NOT JUST PRESENCE. The fix patch added "declaration
index must precede use index" and "each var declared exactly once" — both derived, both would have
caught the above at patch time instead of after a 2m13s build.
⭐ FILTER THE FILE, NOT THE STREAM (re-learned). ./gradlew ... | grep
buffers and the terminal looks identical whether the build is working or wedged. Redirect to a file
and tail it from a second window.
⚠ A CHAIN OF &amp;&amp;-LINKED GREPS DIES ON THE FIRST EMPTY RESULT — everything
after it silently never runs, and reads as "the code does not exist". Use semicolons.
⚠ git diff --stat DOES NOT SHOW NEW FILES — an untracked file looks like a
failed patch. Check git status or grep the file directly.
⭐⭐ THE DESIGN GOT SMALLER EVERY TIME FRED ASKED WHAT WE WERE TRYING TO
ACCOMPLISH. Started as a new worker file plus an atomic four-part queue patch with a
deliberate build-breaking window; ended as one function calling four existing production
components in order. The atomic patch disappeared entirely because deletes never enter the queue.
⚠ I OFFERED TO ROLL BACK WHEN THE TREE WENT RED. Fred said continue; the errors were one
misplaced declaration block. The rollback would have cost the evening.
⚠ I ASSERTED THINGS ABOUT THE PANEL FROM MEMORY AND WAS WRONG TWICE (hold-state
invisible; slot-is-not-the-store). Read before claiming.

5 &middot; The estimator was 8-10x long
The panel said Aug 12 5 AM (~86h) for 1.5M tiles. Real rate ~140,000/hour ≈ 10h.
Three compounding causes: the rate came from ONE entry (a per-slot rate while 3-4 slots ran);
averaging two entries did not fix it because concurrent windows overlap; and
createdAt is queue time, so a job that waited behind 87 others carried hours of
waiting in its elapsed.
⭐ Replaced with your formulation: total tiles completed ÷ elapsed since the
earliest job started. That IS the aggregate rate by construction — concurrency cannot fool it, and
it absorbs stalls, holds and slot changes. Same arithmetic as the yardstick ledger, so the two
finally agree.

Three times today. ⭐ Fixed structurally: every patch script now self-tests each guard string
against every replacement block before shipping. Describe the old code, never quote it.
⛔ MULTI-LINE ANCHORS FROM sed OUTPUT ARE UNRELIABLE — blank lines
between statements are invisible there. Two anchors failed on it. Use cat -A, or
anchor on one unique line.

flagged a legitimate call. Guard the expression, not the token.
⚠ A WINDOW ANCHORED ON THE FIRST OCCURRENCE LANDS IN THE WRONG PLACE — the
finally check searched from the option ROW, hundreds of lines above the branch.
⚠ A PATCH INTRODUCING A COMPOSE SYMBOL MUST ADD ITS IMPORT IN THE SAME EDIT. Twice today
a patch named the imports in its own output and shipped without them.

already built and proven. Calling them in order from a different screen introduced two defects and

All three are per-connection — not stored in the file, nothing already written is touched,

⭐ RECOVERED — the 08-07 discussion that was never documented
Found in the transcript at 2026-08-07 20:30-20:40, during the first corridor delete run.
Fred remembered it existed; none of it had been written down.
The number was a BATCH SIZE, not a journal mode: batch into moderate transactions,
one commit per 25-50k deletes. Not 88, not one giant one.
⛔ An explicit warning against what was proposed again today. SQLite's own docs: the
write-ahead option works best with smaller transactions, is slower above ~100 MB, and can fail
outright above a gigabyte. A 617k-tile delete is a very large transaction — so "one big
transaction in WAL" was named the worst combination available.
⭐ The reasoning that was lost: SQLite executes millions of statements per second, so
1.1M delete attempts cannot take ten minutes on statement cost — pointing at commit overhead
(fsync per transaction).
Fred asked about turning journaling off and back on. Answer then: it leaves an undefined
state on a crash, on a store with no backup — same class as the 08-01 loss.
synchronous=NORMAL was the safe lever, and it is now in the patch.

⭐⭐ THE ANSWER: IT IS NOT SLOW. Deletes run at ~100 tiles/sec; downloads run at
~20-62. The delete is FASTER PER TILE THAN THE DOWNLOAD. Removing 633k tiles in under two
hours is proportionate to the ten hours it took to fetch them.
⭐ And the baseline that matters: before MBTiles there was NO removal option at all —
testers factory-reset their devices. Two hours unattended replaced days of manual work or a wipe.
⚠ THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON, by accident: the five tracks deleted this morning were
re-visited tonight and returned tiles=0 in 0.4 seconds each. Bar 10 overnighter:
189 s with rows, 0.4 s without. Same corridor, same statements. The cost is the physical
row removal, nothing else.
⭐⭐ THE IDEA WORTH KEEPING — A REBUILD MANIFEST
Fred, 08-09: "save downloads in queue and flag source area or corr. if we lose
data we can recreate by resubmitting areas and corridors that have been completed — kind of a
rebuild my map script." And: "if you store it on Google Drive it can be used to seed another
device." And: "and a DR tool."
Keep completed download jobs — scope and kind — and you have a MANIFEST of how the store was
built. Every corridor by geom hash, every area by bbox, each tagged. Not a log, a recipe.
What it gives:
DR. Two data-loss events in nine days, both ending in manual reconstruction. With a
manifest: reinstall, pull, resubmit, walk away. ⚠ Covers TILES only — tracks and trails are
captured data and need real backup.
Device seeding. A manifest is kilobytes; 14 GB of tiles is not. New phone: install, pull,
rebuild. A seed, not a transfer.
Coverage sharing. A ride leader builds the coverage for a trip and shares the recipe.
⭐ The route-import goal generalised to whole stores.
It dissolves the delete ordering constraint. Area scope currently must be inferred from
what survives on disk, which is WHY corridors must be deleted first. A manifest records what was
requested, so scope no longer comes from disk.
⚠ The pieces mostly exist — completed entries already carry geomHash, bbox,
slot and tile counts. Missing: an explicit kind flag, and CLEAR currently destroys them.
⭐ The hide-not-delete change already designed for the yardstick serves both.
⚠ It must not live in download_queue.json — that file quarantines to
.corrupt on a bad parse and has boot-looped the app. A DR tool cannot share fate with
the thing it protects. ⭐ Off-device, which is what the Drive idea already does.
⚠ A shared manifest carries where you ride. Be deliberate before it becomes a sharing
feature.
⚠⚠ WHY TILE-BY-TILE REFRESH WAS REJECTED (considered and killed tonight): a single job
over 1.28M tiles is one unit with no restart point. Fred: "one two week job with no
restart for failsafe. not buying it." The corridors and areas are not just scope — they are
the FAILURE BOUNDARIES that make a multi-day job survivable. Chunking by count (~40k per job)
would work, but the payload must be a re-queryable range, not a tile list.
⚠ And the MBTiles metadata carries nothing useful — name, format, scheme. Checked day one.
There is no record of how any tile got there, which is the same gap behind the coverage-confidence
question. It is our file; we can add rows.

SAVE MAPS on a route&rsquo;s artifact panel derives and queues a corridor, same pipeline

⭐⭐⭐ The design collapsed from a cross-file refactor to three small commits
because the device schema says
CREATE TABLE routes (... geom_hash TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(geom_hash)) and
insertRoute already computes it. The hash is content-addressed and unique in both
tables, so the same hash means the same geometry wherever stored — no artifact-type parameter,
no QueueEntry field, no inputData change, no worker change.
⚠ The 07-27 note had this right all along. The 08-06 note claiming routes lacked
geom_hash was WRONG and drove a much larger design.
⭐⭐ CHECK THE SCHEMA BEFORE DESIGNING AROUND A DATA MODEL.
⛔ NOT done, and it blocks GPX import: insertRoute does
newId() → INSERT OR IGNORE → return id. On duplicate
geometry nothing inserts and a fabricated id is returned. Fix: read back the surviving
route_id by geom_hash. The panel path does not need it.

same corridorTiles. A capped delete computes a SMALLER set than an older build stored,
leaving z17-z18 tiles nothing can ever remove. Empty slot = no cap; only the two DOWNLOAD
paths pass one.

rather than stopping. Agreed as the better behaviour — artifact overlays stay sharp, so a waypoint
can still be placed precisely over a soft basemap.

First pass logged failures; the second popped through in seconds, which is the signature of
nothing left to delete. The tiles came off and the record said otherwise. The delete and
recordCompletedDelete are not atomic, so a failure in the RECORD is indistinguishable
from a failure to DELETE.
⚠ This is what made an hour of diagnosis necessary, and on a destructive operation it is
worse than cosmetic — a user either re-runs needlessly or believes their data survived when it did
not.

(mt0.google.com/vt/lyrs=y) matches neither. Widen the trace filter first.
🔴 ISSUE 2 — the horizon. Not a bug; a design gap with a 4% fix.
At z16 the screen fills. At z15 and z14 the corners go white. ⭐ The corridor is a half-mile
band and the view widens faster than the band does.
⚠ Each zoom is an INDEPENDENT tile set. Having z18 gives you nothing at z13 —
they are separate downloads of the same ground at different resolutions. "Less detail" does not
mean "less data": it means more ground per tile, so a wider view, so more of it outside your
coverage.
⭐⭐ The fix Fred arrived at — a horizon measured in TILES, not miles
buffer(z) = H &times; tileWidth(z)
tiles(z)  = (trackLength / tileWidth(z) + 1) &times; (2H + 1)
H = 2  ->  always two tiles of map beyond the track, at every zoom
Cost: 4%. For the 42-mile Parowan track — 10,791 tiles today at half a mile everywhere —
H=2 with z16-18 left unchanged comes to 11,214 tiles, and it fills the view all the way down
to z9.
ZoomBufferTiles
z978 mi10
z129.8 mi48
z142.4 mi177
z16-18&frac12; mi (unchanged)595 &middot; 2,094 &middot; 7,807
⭐ z9 at seventy-eight miles of buffer costs TEN TILES, because one z9 tile is 156 km wide.
The same widening at z18 would cost hundreds of thousands. The count is dominated by
trackLength / tileWidth; the buffer is only a constant multiplier.
⚠ corridorTiles already loops per zoom with bufferDeg as a parameter —
the buffer just becomes a function of z. ⚠ Existing stores keep their shape; only new downloads get
the horizon.
⛔ The OOM — and the last link in root cause 1 was mine
The first Recreate job killed the app: 512 MB, OutOfMemory.
⛔ I recorded "the worker was never the problem" because it filters to
hasTile. It does — but only AFTER calculateTiles materialises the WHOLE
RECTANGLE. A Recreate box holds at most 50,000 STORED tiles but can span degrees of ground: at
z18 a three-degree box is roughly 4.8 million TileKey objects built into a list before one is
filtered.
⭐ Fixed e128cfc65 — MBTilesStore.tilesInBounds() asks the store
what it holds. Bounded by what is stored, not by the size of the box, and faster: one indexed range
scan per level instead of millions of allocations plus a per-tile existence check.
Fred&rsquo;s original sentence, finally built: stream real tiles in existence by zoom for x lon
and lat.
⚠ The old code even LOGGED the ratio — "N in bounds, M exist on disk". The waste was
visible all along; it only mattered when a box got big enough to exhaust the heap.

Cache-buster on the asset URL &mdash;
file:///android_asset/grouptrack_map.html?v=&lt;versionCode&gt;. The query changes
every build, so a stale entry cannot be served. ⭐ Self-maintaining, and the one that actually
forces it.
setCacheMode(LOAD_NO_CACHE) on the WebView settings. Simpler, but a hint
rather than a guarantee for file:// assets.
⭐ Do both. ⚠ And it explains at least some of the 08-11 evening: a device running new Kotlin
against old HTML would behave exactly as described and defeat every bisect.

Root cause (proven by reading the branch, not theorizing)
The toolbar Discard button (ConvoyRouteToolbar:196) branches:
if (routeLifecycleState == ROUTE_LS_RESUMED) onDiscardRequested() else onExit()
For a NEW route (ROUTE_LS_NEW) it calls onExit() — which cleared
the route from screen and memory but had no deleteDraft. So the per-point autosave
had already written Auto Saved In Progress.json to disk, and discard never removed it.
⭐ There was never a "phantom" being recreated on entry. It was one legitimate
autosave that discard failed to delete — it looked like it "kept coming back" because it never
left. The old comment on onExit assumed "new route = no draft on disk," which was false.
The fix

RouteDraftStore.deleteDraft(routeName)
draftListTick++

bolted on during the earlier DISCARDWINS attempts (they fought the flow). Net

2026-08-16 EOD &middot; HEAD a9f327780 &middot; branch test/authority-api36
REINSTALL WAS DELETING BOTH DATABASES — FOUND, FIXED, CERTIFIED &middot; AUTHORITY GATE DEVICE-VERIFIED ON ALL THREE PATHS &middot; TARGET 36 CONFIRMED CLEAN &middot; 2.6f IS FOUR ITEMS FROM THE AAB
⭐ The session opened on what looked like an API-36 question and closed on a data-loss
defect that had been live for months. Along the way the April blocker that created this branch turned
out not to exist, one earlier diagnosis was withdrawn, and a fix built on a wrong theory was corrected
by its own instrumentation before it shipped. Full detail in Living Master v19 —
00-STARTHERE 08-16, then 00-MARKER-LIFETIME.
⛔⛔ The headline — a plain reinstall was deleting both databases
Root cause
The v3 delete-gate in SpatialDbManager.init() was gated on
db_schema_marker in SharedPreferences (app-private). The databases it deletes live
in Documents/GroupTrack/ (public). An uninstall wipes the marker and not the data,
so every reinstall read marker was 0, concluded "pre-v3", and deleted both files.
08:15:02.463  DB v3 migration: delete grouptrack_spatial.db = true
08:15:02.503  DB v3 migration: delete grouptrack_data.db = true
08:15:02.514  DB v3 migration: spatial-clean=true extension-clean=true (marker was 0)
08:15:02.978  Spatial DB: 0 trails, 0 tracks, 0 waypoints, 0 routes
⭐ Three wipes in twelve hours traced to this one defect — 08-15 23:22, 08-16 07:10,
08-16 08:15. Not a failed open, not an authority problem: the app deliberately deleted the data because
it could not tell "never migrated" from "migrated, then reinstalled." The authority canary ran 340 ms
BEFORE the deletion and passed.
⭐⭐ AutoResyncHost's conviction is WITHDRAWN. Killing it on 08-15 was
correct — vestigial startup migration opening the DB pre-authority — but it did not cause these wipes,
and yesterday's EOD credited it with the whole thing.
⚠ This is the inverted form of the guard specced after 08-01: marker absent + external DB
present = fresh install over existing data → STOP. The marker was designed as a stop condition and
implemented as a delete trigger.
The fix — two commits, two independent halves
CommitWhat
233e61e50Marker moves to a FILE, .db_schema_version, beside the DBs so its lifetime matches theirs. Read order file → legacy prefs → 0 (the prefs fallback carries existing installs across; without it the fix would itself have wiped every current install once). Plus a row-count guard: populated DBs mean already-migrated whatever the marker says → stamp and skip. An unreadable count returns −1 and is treated as populated — refuse to delete on uncertainty.
c503b3247Stamp-if-missing. Caught on device, not in review: an install whose marker came from legacy prefs reached neither writing branch, so the file was never laid down and the install stayed protected by app-private state — the exact mismatch being fixed.
Certification (Droid 2)
Install over live data → marker file appears containing 3, sizes unchanged.
Uninstall → marker survives in Documents/, prefs gone with the package.
Reinstall → no migration block in the log at all, and
Spatial DB: 152200 trails, 88 tracks, 559 waypoints. Byte-identical sizes.
⭐ That proves the marker path, not the row guard catching a miss — belt and braces
verified independently.
✅ Authority gate — settled, and the correction worth keeping
SituationBehaviour
Authority real on the FIRST evaluationNo gate — straight to Convoy.
Became Granted during the sessionContinue barrier retained (the flash-past race is still real).
Returned from settings without grantingStorageDeclined — states the app will not open, and that exiting is safe. Try again / Exit. No proceed door.
Background location ungrantedAdvisory. Skip for now proceeds; deliberately NOT remembered, so it recurs every launch.
Fred's rules behind it: storage — "the app is unusable without that authority, period",
"cancel is the option that should be taken." Background — "not destructive, it reduces
functionality and can be quickly changed", and the repeat is wanted because "it warns of
degradation when recording a track with an app that goes to sleep."
⚠⚠ The diagnosis correction — record this, not the first story
Grant all-files, return, screen stayed declined; force-close then passed immediately.
Claude's theory was a settle race and built a 5×400 ms retry loop on it.
The logs disproved it the moment they existed: every retry read
realStorage=false through attempt 4, and the successful grant passed on attempt 0.
The retries never rescued a grant.
Real defect: LifecycleResumeEffect evaluated once and latched
StorageDeclined with nothing left to re-evaluate. Latched state, not a timing race.
The fix that mattered was re-evaluating on resume. ⭐ A fix built on an unverified theory can pass its
test for a reason unrelated to the theory — the instrumentation added in the same patch is the only
reason this did not ship recorded as a race that never existed.
Also fixed: Exit was a dead button — popBackStack() from the nav START
destination has nothing to pop and no-ops. Now finishes the activity.
New: gate logging, tag ConvoyGate —
adb -s &lt;serial&gt; logcat -s ConvoyGate. ⚠ MediaProvider "Failed to update
quota type for .authority_probe" is noise, present on clean passes too.
✅ API 36 — the April blocker does not exist
⭐⭐ The all-files toggle does NOT grey out at target 36 on Android 16. Confirmed on
device. This kills the whole worst-case branch: no force-off-then-grant, no gated explainer bracketing
two OS-settings trips, no double-prompt UX. That question is why this branch exists.
Nothing in Android 16's documented behaviour changes touches MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE —
the API-36 storage changes are photo-picker/selected-media. April's retreat to 35 was far more likely
the record-vs-UID divergence than a platform rule.
⚠ Naming, so it stays out of the release notes: Android 16 IS API 36. There is no "Android 16
API level 15." From Aug 31 every update must target 36; API 35 only keeps a published build
discoverable.

requirement only) · cache-buster (no asset update, and clear-cache is a working remedy again) ·
credential rotation (ngrok never used, MySQL creds already changed).
⚠ Held OUT of 2.6f, deliberately
Discard refactoring, map-recipe re-import and route recovery were floated for this release
("that will bulletproof the app") and held to 2.6g on the 08-15 reasoning: 2 weeks +
hard deadline = do ONE thing well. All three touch save paths or new code paths — and the save path
is what graduates a WIP into a permanent route, i.e. the machinery behind the only unrecoverable data
class. Designs are captured in Living Master 00-DISCARD-DESIGN and 00-STARTUP-SURVEY so
nothing is re-derived.
⭐ If time opens up, the cheapest real win is archive-on-graduate: copy the WIP JSON
into a completed/ subfolder at save time. No new read path, no format decision, and it
closes the only unrecoverable class on its own.
⚠ Method — what today reinforced
The cheaper test passing is not evidence the expensive one will. Clear-cache passed
byte-identical and would have been accepted as proof the install work was done. Fred pushed for the
uninstall/reinstall anyway — that is the run that found the defect.
Capture the log before the buffer rolls. 353,608 lines; the answer was three
I/ lines in it. Five-minute diagnosis instead of another evening.
A guard and the thing it guards must share a lifetime. App-private state protecting
public-storage data. It reads as correct in review because both halves are individually sensible — look
for the shape wherever a flag decides whether to touch data that outlives the flag.
Instrumentation before theorising, again. The gate emitted nothing, so its decisions had to be
inferred from platform quota noise. One log line per evaluation turned the next question into a reading
— and immediately disproved the theory a fix had just been built around.
cat -A when an anchor spans lines. A sed-derived anchor missed a
blank line; the patch aborted at anchor 6 of 6, no write, tree clean. Re-issued as
...16b.py with the rationale in the header rather than reusing the name.
Unplug the protected device. Droid 1 was on the bus with an uninstall queued
next. Two devices attached means a missing -s errors rather than picking one, so the real
exposure was a mistyped serial — still a stop-and-unplug moment on 89K trails with no backup.

⛔⛔ The correction that matters — discard was never diverged
Fred: "the issue was standardizing the discard function. i have seen no
divergence in discard. our divergence is in save correct?" — and the code agrees.
onExit (~1646) and the in-progress dialog (~1775) both do all five operations,
identically. No drift. The "six variants of discard" plan was built on a survey table that
counted SAVE sites and LIST-MANAGEMENT sites as discard variants.
~1834 resolver presents the discard CHOICE when an in-progress file is found on
entry — nothing loaded yet, so its omissions are correct.
~1923 picker is the In-Progress list, a reminder when more than one autosave exists.
"Not part of the discard process." Nothing to tear down.
~1539 and ~1717 are saves, not discards — and save-as-WIP renames, so it correctly
has no deleteDraft.
setRouteMode "just does not belong in the discard function" — it is
ambient exit behaviour that got copied in because it sat nearby.
⚠ Method note, worth more than the fix. Claude built an elaborate consolidation
plan from a grep table; Fred dismantled it by asking what each site is. The tell was that
the "variants" needed increasingly baroque justification to remain variants. The real defect sat
in code nobody had looked at, because the 08-13 survey filed it under a different word.
⚠⚠ A guard that was never reached — second time in two days
ConvoyViewModel.setGpsInterval already wrapped setConfig in
try/catch, logging "Failed to set GPS interval" — and the app still died. setConfig
returns before the binder throws, so the exception fires outside the try block.
⭐ When a guard exists and the failure happens anyway, the guard is not being reached
— check that before adding another one. Yesterday's latched gate state was the same shape: code
that reads correct, behaves otherwise.
Two more things banked from that crash:
R8-minified stacks are actively misleading. That trace named coil3,
okhttp3, RoomRawQuery and UsbKt — all nonsense. Trust only
frames naming real behaviour; file attribution is a hint, not a fact. It sent Claude to the wrong
file twice.
Find a UI element by its LABEL. Greps for "meter", "broadcast" and "Slider" all missed it.
grep -n '"INT"' found it in one shot.

⭐ RideCalc — calibrated against 88 real tracks
Filtering avg_speed_mph to 3–25 as "actually riding":
distance bandnavg mphrange
under 10 mi96.13.2 – 13.2
10 – 25312.410.2 – 16.3
25 – 45911.88.5 – 24.0
45+3115.38.9 – 23.6
Default speed range: 12–18 mph for 45–60 mile planning, from 31 filtered tracks. Fred's
SWAG of 12–17 was essentially right.
⭐⭐ But the mechanism is not what it looks like. Claude read the rising trend as
terrain. Fred's explanation is better and simpler: "a break or two and lunch on a short ride is a
higher percent of the total time." So avg_speed_mph is an elapsed-time
average including stops — which is exactly what a day-planner wants, and removes the need for a
separate stopped-time parameter. ⚠ It also means the short bands measure lunch, not riding — do not
extrapolate 6.1 mph downward.
Parameters: speed range (estimation only) and distance bounds (the hard constraint, upper
and lower) both user-adjustable with defaults in settings. Time is derived and reported as a
range, never a point figure.
⚠ Track data quality, found in passing: max_speed_mph pins at
199–200 constantly · one row shows 99,379 ft gain on 57 miles · one row 0.0 hours on 50 miles ·
several rows at 47–66 mph avg are almost certainly trailer miles.

1 · Headline — Google Hybrid was never a dead source
  FIXED + VERIFIEDIt was a missing {s} substitution, in two places
  HYB had been written off as a withdrawn service and sat in the checklist as "disable it or ship a known-issue
  note." That was wrong. Two separate bugs, one root cause, both now fixed and proven on device.
  ⭐ What settled it: curling the endpoint by hand — 200, image/jpeg,
  29,722 bytes. Proving the service was alive before theorising about the app. Ten seconds. Do that first
  next time.
  ⭐ The URLs are not in Kotlin — that is why the first greps found nothing
  ConvoyConfig.kt:15 says it plainly: "TILE_SOURCES — reads from MapSourceManager
  (map_sources.json)." MapSourceManager.kt:90 reads url_template out of JSON.
  So grep lyrs= across app/src returns nothing and sends you looking in the wrong place.
  Asset: app/src/main/assets/map_sources.json.
  Template: https://mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=y&amp;x={x}&amp;y={y}&amp;z={z}.
  Five sources use {s}: google-hybrid, -satellite, -roads, -terrain, cartodb-voyager.
  Everything else uses literal hostnames — which is why only the Google sources looked dead.
  BUG 1 — download path
  ConvoyTileDownloader.buildTileUrl substituted {z}/{x}/{y}
  and nothing else. {s} was handled nowhere — grep across all Kotlin returned zero hits.
  The literal string mt{s}.google.com went to DNS and every tile failed silently.
  .replace("{s}", (((tile.x + tile.y) % 4 + 4) % 4).toString())   // SUBDOMAIN-2026-08-02
  Added as the first replace. Double-modulo guards negative x at antimeridian wrap; % 4
  gives mt0–mt3, deterministic per tile so a retry hits the same host.
  BUG 2 — display path
  Leaflet does expand {s} — but its default subdomain set is 'abc', so it
  requested mta/mtb/mtc.google.com, which do not exist. Neither map set a
  subdomains option.
  subdomains: (url.indexOf('google.com') !== -1 ? '0123' : 'abc')   // SUBDOMAINS-2026-08-02
  In both convoy_map.html (~:47) and grouptrack_map.html (~:111).
  Derived from the URL, not hardcoded — Google needs 0123, Carto needs abc.
  ⚠ The subdomains option is still missing on the overlay layers
  (convoy_map.html ~:71, grouptrack_map.html ~:138). Inert today; a subdomain'd overlay
  source would fail the same way.
  Verified end to end
    Display: TILE URL: https://mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=y… LABEL: SAT with no
    TILE ERROR after it
    Download: SAT.mbtiles mtime advanced 06:16 → 06:17 with size unchanged
    (INSERT OR REPLACE reuses pages)
    Offline: ConvoyIntercept: TILE mbtiles hit=true at z17/z18 — Google tiles
    rendering from the store

4 · ⛔ The lesson of the week
  THREE-FOR-THREE: every convoy rendering failure in this arc was instrumentation aborting a method before its real work
    ?: return inside a toast argument killed onPageFinished — no tile setup, no
    setTileUrl, no persisted-frame restore, no drawPersistedState
    evaluateJavascript / Toast on a @JavascriptInterface background thread
    killed onViewportChanged — no processViewport, so no artifacts drew
    The offline render failure, cleared by removing ten more toasts from the same file
  All three landed in or around onPageFinished.
  Instrumentation is not free, and on this codebase it has cost more than the bugs it
  was added to find. When adding a trace to an override or a bridge method, ask what happens if that line
  throws or returns.
  ⭐ The counter-example is 08-02's tap fix: using instrumentation that already existed
  found the defect in three taps with no new code at all. Read the logs before adding to them.
5 · Source configuration has no persistence layer — root cause found
  ROOT CAUSENothing is putting Esri back. The choice was never saved.
  Fred: "Something keeps placing Esri hybrid in slot 1 even after I replaced with Google."
  XREF EVIDENCE (field_crossref_raw.txt): MapSourceManager has exactly
  two writes — :62 (dir.mkdirs()) and :248
  (apiKeysFile().writeText). The API keys file is the only thing it persists. Slot fields
  are read-only: :113 slot, :114 source_id, :115
  legacy_key.
  DEVICE EVIDENCE: adb shell find /sdcard -name "map_sources.json" returns
  nothing. The external override anticipated at MapSourceManager.kt:66 does not exist.
  ⭐ One missing layer, three symptoms: slot 1 reverting to Esri ·
  activeSourceKey resetting to SAT on every restart (declared = "SAT", in-memory only) ·
  possibly the Google download abort itself.
  ⛔ It was built, then deliberately removed — and why matters
  git log -S "externalJsonFile" returns exactly two commits:
    49bc8cecb — V2.5 Map Source Selection — ADDED it
    79251ae72 — 2026-05-21, "Fix tile download — read asset JSON only" —
    REMOVED it
  Both halves went: the read-external-first-with-copy-on-first-run block, and the entire body of
  saveExternalJson() — replaced with // Disabled — asset is single source of truth.
  ⚠ The empty function still exists and is still called, silently doing nothing.
  ⭐⭐ Why it was removed vindicates the fix. The external file held the
  entire catalogue, URLs included — so a stale copy served stale URLs and broke tile
  downloads, which is exactly what that commit was fixing. Ripping it out was correct for a real bug.
  ⭐⭐ The architecture (Fred) — two structures, two functions
  "There are two structures — the CATALOG which should be distributed, and the SLOT ASSIGNMENT of catalog to
  user's map slot. Two separate functions."
  CATALOG = map_sources.json in assets. Sources, templates, layers,
  default_slots, versions. Distributed with the app, read-only, replaced every release.
  ⭐ This is what makes a URL correction reach existing users — the {s} fix lives in a template here.
  Had the catalogue been copied to user space on first run, no existing user would ever receive it.
  SLOT ASSIGNMENT = which source_id occupies each user map slot, plus
  the active slot. User-owned, persisted, survives reinstall. Fred: "The slot assignment is a
  JSON that should exist in user space and be populated from default asset on install."
  ⛔ Do NOT restore 49bc8cecb as-was — that reintroduces the stale-URL
  bug. Persist only {slot, source_id, legacy_key} plus the active key, never the sources
  array. ⚠ Seed only when the user file is ABSENT — re-seeding on every install recreates the bug.
6 · Refresh is still on the bbox model and old segmentation
  568 entries at 60–70K tiles each
  Downloads cut over to corridors on 07-24. Refresh was never migrated — still bbox, still on the
  old gridCells instead of segmentCells. A map-source refresh enqueued
  568 entries at 60–70K tiles each (~37 million tiles). Not the 3,287-entry continental blowup of
  07-23, but the same root path.
  ⛔ Bbox refresh jobs RESET rather than complete — observed twice: a job at 5% went
  back to 4%, then a second reset the same way. Distinct from the known never-completes stall.
  ⭐ Design decision (Fred) — refresh gets two methods
  CORRIDOR IS THE DEFAULT. Route refresh through the track selection process —
  reuses proven code, kills the oversized-cell problem for free (the corridor worker re-derives tiles at run time),
  and matches what refresh is actually for.
  AREA REFRESH STAYS AS AN OPTION for users who downloaded areas. Same shape as the
  download side (downloadType selects the worker).
  The area path must move from gridCells to segmentCells.
  Corridor-by-default only reduces how often the defect is hit.
  ⚠ A select-all-tracks refresh needs an estimate-and-confirm gate — the import path
  does one submitDownload per track with no estimate, which is how 10 tracks became 215 jobs.
  ⚠ A failed queue job records no reason
  A corridor job failed and the entry said only "CORR SAT failed" — no exception, no HTTP status.
  The cause was unrecoverable because TRACK-DBG: TICK (twice every 5 s) had already rolled it out of the
  logcat ring buffer.
  Fix: put the failure cause in the queue entry AND the log. ⚠ TRACK-DBG actively
  destroys evidence — add it to the pre-release removal list alongside WAYPOINT-TRACE.
  To catch it next time, start the capture BEFORE queueing:
  adb logcat -c then adb logcat | grep -viE "TRACK-DBG|DetailGate|NetworkStateTracker|WM-|chromium|ConvoyIntercept" &gt; /d/corr_run.txt
