  GroupTrack — Install &amp; Reinstall Design
    Design conversation, 2026-08-04 &middot; NOT BUILT — this is the agreed design, not code
    Supersedes the manual-only approach in grouptrack_reinstall_procedure_2026-08-03.html,
    which remains valid as the fallback for anyone who does not use the in-app path.
1 · The problem this solves
  What happened on 2026-08-01
  A reinstall destroyed the spatial database — roughly 89,000 trails. The mechanism:
    The app was reinstalled over existing data in Documents/GroupTrack/.
    Android reported All-Files access as GRANTED — the grant record survives an
      uninstall because the package name is unchanged. The new install did not actually
      hold that authority; the OS denied at the filesystem layer while the permission screen said
      otherwise.
    The app could not read the existing databases, and its create-if-missing open
      wrote empty schemas over them.
    It then reported 0 trails, 0 tracks, 0 waypoints, 0 routes as if normal.
  ⚠⚠ There is no backup. The map databases are 50–60 GB.
  Why the obvious defences do not work
  The permission API cannot be trusted.
  Environment.isExternalStorageManager() returns true in this state and is
  wrong. It reads the stale grant record; the filesystem enforces the truth. There is no
  API question that returns the right answer — only a real read attempt does.
  Blocking startup until the app can read would DEADLOCK the device. The app must
  run before it can be granted authority, so refusing to start until it can read means a reinstalled
  device can never be recovered. This was proposed and correctly rejected.
  The app cannot act at uninstall time. Android has no uninstall hook.
  ACTION_PACKAGE_REMOVED is broadcast to other apps — your own process is already
  gone. A companion app could hear it, but only after removal, which is too late to be useful:
  the danger is not the uninstall, it is the next install running blind.
2 · ⭐ The design — GroupTrack triggers its own uninstall
  The key realisation
  The app can uninstall itself. Intent.ACTION_DELETE /
  ACTION_UNINSTALL_PACKAGE launches the system uninstall dialog — and at that moment the app
  is alive and holds authority. So it can do the dangerous bookkeeping itself, while it
  still can.
  That converts the ten-step manual procedure into two taps.
The flow
1 · User taps "Prepare for reinstall" in the app.
2 · The app renames its own data directories — it has authority right
now, so this simply works:
Documents/GroupTrack  →  Documents/GroupTrack.bak
My Tracks             →  My Tracks.bak
Renaming is instant regardless of size — it does not copy 50–60 GB.
3 · The app fires the uninstall intent on itself. The user confirms the
system dialog.
4 · User installs the new build and launches it. The app finds no
GroupTrack/, creates fresh empty directories, and completes first run.
This is expected and is the point — it is creating blanks where there is nothing to
destroy, because the real data is out of reach under .bak.
5 · The All-Files grant is requested FIRST, before anything touches the
database. See §3 — this is the ordering half of the design and it matters as much as the
rename.
6 · After the grant, the app attempts a REAL READ of the .bak
directories. Not isExternalStorageManager() — an actual read. That is the only
proof that authority is real.
7 · If the read succeeds and .bak exists → prompt:
"Found your previous data. Restore it?"
8 · On confirm: verify the blank directories are EMPTY, delete them,
rename the .bak directories back.
⚠⚠ THIS IS THE REVERSE-RISK MOMENT. Everything up to here protected against
overwriting real data with blanks. This step DELETES directories. If the empty-check is wrong, it
deletes the wrong thing. Refuse if non-empty, log what was found, and ask — a user who
recorded a track or downloaded tiles between steps 4 and 7 has real data in those "blanks".
3 · ⭐⭐ The ordering fix — grant BEFORE the database
  This is the half that prevents 08-01 rather than working around it
  The 08-01 failure was an ordering failure. The app opened the DB before authority
  was real. It did not prompt, because it tested and the test lied.
  So: make the All-Files prompt UNCONDITIONAL on first run, and put it FIRST. Fred:
  "we never got the prompt in the failed install as the app looked like it had authority. probably
  should not be a test but unconditional grant there."
  ⭐ The app already knows it is a fresh install — it is already asking first-run
  questions. That IS the signal. No new detection is needed: move the grant to the front of the existing
  first-run sequence, before SpatialDbManager opens anything.
  Cost: one extra tap for a user who already has the permission. Against
  losing 50–60 GB, that is not a close call.
  ⚠ A reinstall-over-existing-data IS a fresh install from the app's point of view —
  which is exactly what you want here: grant first, then the behavioural read finds either the
  .bak directories or the real ones.
  Verify behaviourally, then recover
  After the prompt, attempt a real read. If it still fails, the app is in the stale-grant
  state — and it should say so, at the moment it matters, with the recovery step:
  toggle All-Files access OFF and back ON in Settings.
  ⭐ And if that does not clear it, the message must say: "Reinstalling is safe — your maps
  and tracks are stored outside the app and are not removed." That single sentence turns a
  data-loss panic into a two-minute fix. Nothing in the app currently says it.
4 · The first-run marker
  Where it lives, and why not in shared storage
  A small JSON recording first-run state — but it must go in app-private storage
  (filesDir), NOT Documents/GroupTrack/.
  ⛔ The trap, if it went in shared storage: that file lives in the very storage the
  authority question is about. If All-Files is not granted the app cannot read it — so
  "file absent" and "cannot see the file" look identical. That is precisely the
  confusion that caused 08-01, reproduced in a new file.
  ✅ filesDir needs no authority and is always readable. And it is wiped by
  uninstall, which makes it a better signal, not a worse one:
  marker ABSENT + data PRESENT in Documents/ = a reinstall over
  existing data. That is the detector 08-01 needed, and it comes free with the same file.
  Contents: a status field and the version code —
  {"status":"in_progress"} → {"status":"complete","version_code":N}. Keeping it
  after completion (rather than deleting) answers both questions with one file: has setup run?
  and is this a reinstall? It also gives crash recovery — if the app dies mid-first-run the
  marker survives as in_progress, and the next launch knows setup never finished.
5 · Still owed in code, regardless of any of the above
  The procedure and the flow protect whoever uses them. These protect everyone else,
  and neither blocks anything:
    ⭐⭐ REFUSE-TO-CREATE. SpatialDbManager must never create-if-missing
      on a path it cannot verify. A failed open must ABORT, not write an empty schema.
      This alone would have prevented 08-01 and costs nothing at runtime. It is the
      single highest-value item on this page.
    ROW-COUNT SANITY + .lastgood copy. Copy the DB after each
      successful startup. A startup reporting zero rows where the previous run reported 89,000 is a red
      flag the app should raise, not report as normal.
  ✅ Already fixed 2026-08-04: SpatialDbManager :166/:168 logged the
  LITERAL ${spatialFile.absolutePath} because the $ was backslash-escaped — so
  the DB path never appeared in the log. That was the diagnostic that would have made the 08-01 loss
  obvious immediately.
6 · Open questions
    What if the user cancels the uninstall dialog? The directories are already
      renamed and the app is still installed — it would find no data. Needs an undo path: on next
      launch, if .bak exists and the app is clearly NOT freshly installed, offer to rename
      back. (Doing the rename only after removal is confirmed is not possible — the app cannot observe
      its own uninstall.)
    Uninstalls done from Settings or the launcher bypass the button entirely. The
      manual procedure stays documented as the fallback, and refuse-to-create covers the case where
      neither was used.
    ⚠ Worth verifying on Droid 2 rather than assuming: that an uninstall really does
      leave Documents/GroupTrack/ intact. It should — public shared storage — but Android
      has changed storage behaviour repeatedly, and this entire design rests on that
      assumption.
  Why the rename works when checking does not
  Every detection approach fails for the same reason: the app creates blanks before authority
  arrives, and the permission API reports the wrong answer at exactly that moment. The rename
  does not detect anything — it removes the data from the path the app will write to, until authority is
  real. Nothing to detect, nothing to destroy.

⭐ FIRST OPEN ITEM — Unsegmented download bypasses (enqueue())
DO FIRST root-caused 07-22, not yet patched
Symptom (Fred, on device): artifact/track imports with “download maps” selected produce SAT submissions of 62,000+ tiles in a single queue entry, despite segmentation capping cells at 50,000.
Root cause — two callers bypass segmentation entirely
Every area origin routes submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells (≤50K per cell). But two callers call bare DownloadQueueManager.enqueue(), which computes the whole box in ONE entry via calculateTiles (ConvoyDownloadQueue:127) with no split and no cap:
SpatialDbManager.kt:1973 — downloadMapsForTrackHash(), the track-import “download maps” path. This is the 62K source. Bypass is commented and was once VALID: “Use enqueue() … NOT enqueueArea() (grid-cell split → empty for a sub-cell-sized per-track box → totalTiles=0)” — true against the OLD fixed-12-mile gridCells, which steps in 12-mile increments from south and returns NOTHING for a box smaller than one step.
ConvoyViewModel.kt:989 — startDownload(context, pending), called from ConvoyScreen:472; fed by setPendingDownload at ConvoyScreen:645 and :876. NO stated reason for the bypass — it simply predates segmentation. (The nearby comment “Enqueue to background download queue instead of inline coroutine” refers to an older refactor, not to segmentation.)
⭐ The blocker is CLEARED — migration is safe
segmentCells (ConvoyTileDownloader:254) cannot return an empty list: val n = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(sizeTiles / segCeilingTiles)) floors the count at 1, and it slices the ACTUAL bbox into n fractional pieces rather than snapping to a fixed grid. A tiny per-track box therefore yields exactly ONE cell covering that box. The documented reason for the SpatialDbManager bypass is dead. (Verified by reading source 07-22.)
Fix
Route BOTH callers through the existing feeder submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells. Do not call segmentCells directly — it needs sizeTiles = the layer-aware real volume (quickEstimate × slotLayers); enqueueArea already computes that, and a wrong sizeTiles would under-split and reproduce the bug in a new place. SpatialDbManager.getTrackBbox() already exists as the correct replacement shape (“returns the bbox … so the caller can feed box 1 (source selection) and submitDownload, identical to the area path”) — the import path apparently still calls the older downloadMapsForTrackHash.
⚠ Dependency — may not fully resolve on its own
sizeTiles comes from quickEstimate, which has the KNOWN source-awareness bug (was hardcoded z18). A bad estimate under-splits even after migration. Test entry sizes after the migration; do not assume the 62K is gone.
❓ OPEN QUESTION — is this the source-switch / boot-loop link? — ANSWERED 07-23: NO
Fred’s hypothesis: ConvoyViewModel.startDownload may be on the map-source-change / refresh-existing-tiles path. 🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #1 — TURN OFF MAP REFRESH ON SOURCE CHANGE (do first)
DO FIRST stop-the-bleeding, not a root-cause fix
What happened (07-23, on the shipped 2.6c build)
The REPLACE/refresh function on the map-source select screen “does not behave”: it spawned 3287 downloads in the queue, lat/long spanning the whole continental US. Downloads then stopped working entirely (“system just sits”).
⚠ Cancel All does NOT persist. Cancel appeared to clear the queue, but all 3287 jobs resurfaced on restart — the clear happens in memory and is never written to disk, so loadQueue re-reads the stale file every launch. This is the boot-loop mechanism, demonstrated — just without a crash.
⛔ No recovery path exists on a release build. adb run-as = access denied (debuggable only). X-plore CANNOT reach Android/data/com.geeksville.mesh/ and offers no grant option — Android 13+ removed third-party file-manager access to Android/data entirely; MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE explicitly excludes it and the document-tree picker refuses it. Only root, adb-on-debuggable, or the app itself can read there. The only escape is Clear-App-Data.
Resolution this time: the queue eventually drained on its own (ended at 4 entries processing normally). App data was NOT cleared — but the queue file was never inspected, so the bad bbox was never captured.
The decision (Fred 07-23)
Turn off the JSON write / auto-refresh when a map source is changed. Refresh becomes manually requested as an Area download — which rides the already-hardened submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells path. This removes the thing that spawned 3287 entries without needing the bounds bug diagnosed first.
Build notes
Scope it first: sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt (the enqueueRefresh call site at :271) and the state at :81-83 (refreshSlot / refreshTileCount / refreshEnqueued). Determine whether refresh fires AUTOMATICALLY on source selection or sits behind a button — that decides whether to gate the call or disable the control.
DISABLE, don't delete. Gate it behind a clearly-marked constant or comment it out. The bug is still undiagnosed and the path will be wanted when it's revisited — deleting now means reconstructing later.
⚠ This does NOT fix Cancel All. The persistence failure is a separate defect: any future bad queue still resurrects on restart. Turning off refresh removes the most likely source of a bad queue and buys time; it does not close the hole.
⛔ DO NOT run replace-map-source again until this ships — recovery costs an hour and possibly all app-internal data.
Root cause still open (for when it's revisited)
Leading hypothesis, unverified: the bbox handed to enqueueRefresh is not the user's viewport — a default/zero-initialised value, or swapped bounds arguments. Bounds-order is already the standing suspect for the “map REFRESH no longer works” regression; these may be one defect. Note 3287 ≈ ceil(enormous/50K) — segmentation worked correctly on garbage input, so the bug is upstream of segmentCells. Compare sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt against sed -n '218,250p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt side by side for argument order. Also read sed -n '440,490p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt — :473 declares val bad = File(..., "download_queue/" + QUEUE_FILE), suggesting some quarantine handling already exists, and it is likely the same function where cancel's persistence is failing.
🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #2 — RECOVERY SYSTEM FOR APPLICATION-PROTECTED DATA (the “Repair Area”)
NEW 07-23 full design below — buildable
Why this exists
07-23 proved that bad on-disk state in filesDir is unreachable AND unrecoverable on a release build except by Clear-App-Data. The app itself has unrestricted access to its own filesDir — the OS only blocks other apps — so the escape hatch must be built INTO GroupTrack.
⭐ What actually lives in filesDir (inventory built 07-23 from xrefs)
PathPurposeSourceLoss if wiped
download_queue/download_queue.jsontile download queueConvoyDownloadQueue:444/461, QUEUE_FILE:86none — rebuildable
convoy_apply_list.jsonradio apply listConvoyApplyList:107/110/133low
convoy_users.jsonuser recordsConvoyUser:113/119/133meaningful
master_config.jsonT1000-E MASTER radio configConvoyMasterConfig:152/217; MasterCapture:557meaningful
convoy_backups/&lt;id&gt;/per-radio config backupsConvoyRadioManager:34/146; ViewModel:266HIGH
convoy_rides/ride recordsConvoyViewModel:273meaningful
convoy_events/event configsConvoyEventConfig:176/178meaningful
convoy_profiles/&lt;file&gt;radio profilesConvoyProfileBuilder:212meaningful
convoy_import/, docType import dirsimport stagingViewModel:345; FileReceiver:74/87none — transient
cacheDir/*.gpx, transfer filestemp export/transferTrackOps:684; TransferRide:65none
⭐⭐ KEY CONSEQUENCE: filesDir holds radio configs, radio backups, users, rides and events — not just the queue. Clear-App-Data is NOT a clean fallback: it destroys every radio backup and the master config alongside the bad file. (Tracks and TILES survive — they live outside app storage in Documents/GroupTrack/data/ and /maps/.) This is exactly why per-file repair is worth far more than a reset button.
Design — the flow
Password gate. Threat model is NOT snooping — it's a tester deleting the wrong thing while following phone instructions, or tapping through out of curiosity. A build-time constant checked against a text field is sufficient (anything in the APK is extractable; the gate exists to make the action deliberate).
Test for repair-area existence FIRST. If one exists → WARN + DISPLAY CONTENTS, and allow adding a new (different) item.
Extract — ONE ENTITY AT A TIME via file picker. NO MASS COPY (“that is too scary”). Each extract writes TWO copies: the working file into the repair area (Downloads), and a pristine pre-edit snapshot into the dated archive.
Edit the file in the repair area, with normal tools.
Copy back AS A GROUP (see below), then remove the repair area.
State rules
NO REPLACEMENT of an already-staged item without an EXPLICIT DELETE. Re-extracting the same filename is REFUSED — it would silently overwrite the working copy (and any editing done) with a fresh pull from filesDir. The repair area is effectively append-only; removal is always a deliberate act.
DISPLAY what's staged. CANCEL-AND-RETURN discards the repair area, writes nothing to filesDir — and KEEPS the dated archive (an abandoned repair still leaves evidence of the original state).
⭐ The repair area is a HOLDING area — copy-back is GROUPED
Items are staged across separate one-at-a-time extracts, and the contents are copied back as a group — the staged set is the unit of repair. Extraction is one-at-a-time; restoration is grouped. Rationale: related files that must change together (users + rides, or a config + its backup) would leave inconsistent intermediate state if restored individually.
⭐ Archive naming + retention
Archived files are DATE AND TIME STAMPED — a unique occurrence per extract — held 30 days. Timestamp (not just date) so two repairs of the SAME file on the SAME day cannot collide or silently overwrite each other; every extract is its own recoverable point-in-time snapshot. Mirror the filesDir structure so different files can't collide either:
Documents/GroupTrack/saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json
⭐ The retention sweep runs ON APP OPEN, EVERY OPEN — not on repair-screen entry. A phone that did one repair months ago must not quietly hold stale copies forever just because nobody revisits the screen. Keep it cheap, non-blocking, and fail-safe — a sweep error must NEVER block or crash startup.
⭐⭐ The manifest JSON — work order + audit record
Finishing a repair writes/updates a manifest saying “apply this repair on startup.” It is not just a flag — it carries the work order and makes the apply crash-safe.
{
  "created": "2026-07-23T14:12:05",
  "status":  "pending",
  "problem": "&lt;WHAT ARE WE SOLVING&gt;   — captured at EXTRACT time",
  "repair":  "&lt;WHAT CHANGES DID WE MAKE&gt; — captured at COPY-BACK time",
  "items": [
    { "source":   "repair/download_queue.json",
      "target":   "download_queue/download_queue.json",
      "archived": "saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json" }
  ]
}
problem and repair are captured at DIFFERENT moments. The problem is known when you start (prompt at extract); the repair description isn't known until you finish (prompt at copy-back).
target settles the destination-mapping problem — recorded at extract time, so there is no guessing and no user re-selection at apply time.
Crash-safe: status stays pending until the group write fully succeeds; if the app dies mid-apply the next launch sees pending and retries. Clear only on success. Combined with all-or-nothing validation, a half-applied restore is impossible.
Single source of truth: the manifest is also what the repair screen reads to display staged contents, rather than inferring from a directory listing.
Placement: in the repair area (Downloads) so it travels with the staged files and is readable/editable. Startup code must tolerate a missing or malformed manifest by simply skipping the apply.
⭐⭐ Apply on RESTART, not on exit
Apply-on-exit still races: Android doesn't guarantee clean shutdown, subsystems may be mid-write on the way down, and saveQueue firing during teardown is the same mechanism that made Cancel All appear to work and then resurrect. Apply at startup, VERY EARLY — before loadQueue, before MapStateStore, before anything opens a filesDir file. That is the only genuinely quiescent moment: nothing holds a handle, nothing has read state into memory, nothing can overwrite the repair afterward. This also resolves the live-handle hazard — the download worker hasn't started yet.
Startup order: APPLY FIRST, then the 30-day sweep (housekeeping must not delay the repair). ⚠ The apply must be as fail-safe as the sweep — an exception there would block startup, the exact failure this feature exists to prevent. Wrap it, log it, leave the marker pending for a retry, and let the app boot regardless.
⭐ Applied-repair HISTORY
On successful apply the record moves to a persistent history file with outcome + applied-timestamp appended (applied, or failed + reason). History persists; the manifest is consumed. Value: three weeks later, “has anyone hand-edited this file, and why?” becomes answerable — a question that is currently unanswerable at all. Keep history entries indefinitely (they're small text); losing the record of what changed is worse than losing the copies. Note a history entry's archived path will eventually point at a purged file once the 30-day sweep runs — fine, as long as the entry says so.
Still open
Validate before overwriting — at minimum, confirm each staged JSON parses. Restoring a truncated file would manufacture the exact poison-file scenario this feature exists to escape. With a grouped copy-back: validate EVERY staged item first and abort the whole group if any fails.
Auto-backup the current filesDir file(s) before the group write, making the restore itself reversible.
Cheaper complements (consider alongside, not instead)
“Reset download queue” button (~30 lines) — clears memory AND deletes the file atomically. Would have solved 07-23 in one tap.
Diagnostic mirror — copy queue state to Documents/GroupTrack/ on every save, making it readable via X-plore with no browser at all. Would have shown the 3287 entries and the bad bbox immediately.
NOTE: access and resilience are alternative solutions to the same problem. The repair area makes emergencies survivable; loadQueue tolerant-parse makes them rare. Both are wanted; neither replaces the other.
🔵 NEW OPEN ITEM #3 — PHASE 1: QUEUE (DownloadType, ordering, filter-scoped deletes, scrolling)
DO FIRST — build, test, CERTIFY, then Phase 2
Sequencing (Fred): queue work first, certified against all existing functions, then corridor. Rationale: don't debug two new things at once — if corridor later needs queue changes we didn't anticipate, it's a modification to something already proven rather than a second unknown.
⚠ There is NO priority mechanism in the queue today
QueueEntry (ConvoyDownloadQueue:24-39) has no priority field, and startNextIfAvailable (:417-429) does filter { status == QUEUED }.take(slotsAvailable) — list order, no sort. Refreshes appearing to run ahead of area jobs is an artifact of insertion order, not a rule. (refreshMode/refreshSlot are behaviour flags passed to the worker, not selection inputs.) So ordering is NEW behaviour, not a new value in an existing scheme.
Scope
Enum: DownloadType { AREA, CORRIDOR, MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH, DELETE_AREA_TILES }. The fourth value is defined NOW because delete-area-tiles is already in the panel and has never been written — one definition avoids a second migration. Note it's a genuinely different KIND of job (removes rather than fetches), so when wired, launchWorker must dispatch on type. That's also the strongest argument for a real field over a label prefix — Fred: "we cannot bastardize the name for expediency."
Field: QueueEntry.downloadType: DownloadType = DownloadType.AREA, put in toJson. ⚠ fromJson MUST read it with a DEFAULT of AREA when the key is absent — every entry already on a tester's device lacks it, and a throw there IS the boot-loop mechanism.
Ordering: corridor AHEAD of area (corridor jobs are small and targeted; a user tapping SAVE MAPS shouldn't wait behind a large drawn-area download). A real sort on downloadType — more honest than head-insertion and it doesn't depend on insertion sequence surviving a save/load round-trip.
⭐ Filter view — and THE FILTER SCOPES DELETES. Fred: "control deletes functions with filter. all is only for selected filtered items." The filter is not a view convenience, it's the safety scoping mechanism: filter to CORRIDOR → cancel → area jobs untouched. Unfiltered behaves as today. CLEAR DONE follows the same rule.
⚠ Labels must state scope + count — "CANCEL CORRIDOR (54)" vs "CANCEL ALL (215)". If it reads "CANCEL ALL" while filtered, someone will eventually cancel a subset believing they cleared the queue, or refuse to press it believing it wipes everything.
⭐ Confirmation dialog with a GATED PROCEED — destructive actions are never single-tap. The message names the scope and count ("Cancel 54 CORRIDOR downloads?"). This is the direct answer to 07-23, when the only control was one all-or-nothing CANCEL ALL that didn't even persist.
Queue panel scrolling fix — the panel doesn't scroll. Independent of everything else, and needed just to READ 215 entries. Cheapest item here.
⚠ Certification checklist (existing functions that must still work)
Area download end-to-end · map-source refresh · cancel · resume after kill · and a queue that survives a save/load round-trip both WITH the new field and with legacy entries that LACK it. The ordering sort changes which job runs first — that's visible behaviour, confirm it deliberately.
Suggested split: two patches, not one — persistence (enum + field + serialization + type assignment) first, testable in isolation including the legacy round-trip; then panel (sort + filter + scoped deletes + scrolling). A round-trip problem shouldn't get tangled with UI changes.
⚠ refreshMode carries TWO meanings today — "this is a refresh" AND "replace existing tiles". Once MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH exists as a type, refreshMode must keep only the replace-behaviour meaning, or they'll drift (same class as gridCells surviving its replacement).
🔵 NEW OPEN ITEM #4 — PHASE 2: DOWNLOAD MAPS BY CORRIDOR
after Phase 1 certifies
⭐ The rule
Anything TRACK-based or ROUTE-based submits a CORRIDOR download. User-DRAWN area downloads keep the BBOX. The user drew a rectangle → the rectangle IS the request. The user picked a track/route → they want the line and its immediate surroundings.
Architecture (no branching, no parameter-steered core)
TWO self-contained functions — downloadMapsByArea (existing, bbox) and downloadMapsByCorridor (new, line). Fred: "Both will use the shared pgm for prompt and submit their own download queue components." The prompt is shared and isolated (source selection + replace Y/N — that's user intent, identical regardless of geometry); each path passes its own onProceed lambda in, so there is no mode flag and no branch.
Signature: downloadMapsByCorridor(context, geomHash, selectedSlots, replaceExisting) — the hash identifies the track (the panel already hands back geom_hash). Callable from convoy, planning, and import. The import swap is ONE LINE — ConvoyTrackOps:586 already has gh, downloadMapSlots, replaceExisting in hand, and the import has its own source/replace prompt already.
⭐ What the entry carries — Option B
⛔ Run-boxes are RULED OUT. Fred: "cannot use boxes, the startup time for new area requests is long 5-10 seconds added to every new bbox request. not workable." 30 run-boxes = 3-5 minutes of pure startup overhead before a tile moves.
Option B: the entry stores a geometry reference, not a tile list — geomHash + buffer width + downloadType=CORRIDOR (+ bbox for display/progress). The worker re-derives the tile list at run time: AREA → calculateTiles(N,S,E,W); CORRIDOR → corridor tiles from geometry + buffer. Startup cost paid ONCE per entry. Option A (serializing the tile list) rejected — a 60K-tile list is megabytes per entry in download_queue.json, the file with no recovery path on a release build.
Resume is free: hasTile() means the mbtiles store is the source of truth for what's already down, so a re-derived list simply skips what landed. The tile list never needs persisting.
Derivation
Standard GIS name is buffering a linestring, but no polygon is needed — walk the line's points and, for each, emit tiles within the buffer radius at each zoom, deduped into a set. Overlaps and self-intersections (the figure-7 doubles back) collapse automatically. Buffer width: start at the SAME half-mile the bbox path uses (getTrackBbox pads 0.00724° lat, 0.00724/cos(midLat) lon) so the PoC is directly comparable to the 894,507 baseline.
Geometry format: tracks are MULTILINESTRING or LINESTRING; routes are plain LINESTRING. ⚠ WKT coordinate order is lon lat — SpatialDbManager:1763 flips with parts[1], parts[0]. Getting this backwards puts the box in the wrong hemisphere. Parse model to copy: wktToGeoJsonCoords (:340-361) handles both shapes (for MULTI, split on "),(" then trim parens) — it returns a JSON string, so write a sibling returning POINTS. ⭐ MULTILINESTRING matters: disjoint segments must be walked separately — exactly the case where the bbox spans the empty gap and the corridor doesn't.
Routes: the routes table HAS min/max lat/lon (queried at :767) and geometry is fetchable by id (:1755), but there is no getRouteBbox and no download-by-route path today — the route corridor is a NEW capability, nothing legacy to preserve.
⚠ Open question — does hasTile() skip the REQUEST or only the WRITE?
Matters for resume cost. If the check is at INSERT only, a resumed corridor re-requests every tile from Esri and only then discovers it has them — full network cost twice, and on per-tile pricing that's real money. Resolve with grep -n "hasTile" .../convoy/*.kt. If write-only, add a pre-fetch filter (derive → filter against hasTile → fetch only what's missing), which also makes the progress count honest.
Rollout
Add SAVE MAPS (CORRIDOR) alongside the existing SAVE MAPS in ArtifactDetailPanel — side by side, so the same track runs both ways on real geography and nothing regresses for testers. Insertion point: ArtifactDetailPanel.kt:97-102; the panel is SHARED (track-tap opens it from ConvoyMapViewerScreen:522 and ConvoyScreen:650/914) so one button appears on both maps. Currently gated to artifactType == "Tracks" only.
Compare corridor tiles vs the 894,507 bbox baseline on track 1.
Remove the area button from the artifact panel once corridor proves out.
Replace the bbox derivation in track import last.
PoC scope: NO SPLIT — one entry per track per source. Measure first; decide on splitting after.

🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #1 — TURN OFF MAP REFRESH ON SOURCE CHANGE (do first)
DO FIRST stop-the-bleeding, not a root-cause fix
What happened (07-23, on the shipped 2.6c build)
The REPLACE/refresh function on the map-source select screen “does not behave”: it spawned 3287 downloads in the queue, lat/long spanning the whole continental US. Downloads then stopped working entirely (“system just sits”).
⚠ Cancel All does NOT persist. Cancel appeared to clear the queue, but all 3287 jobs resurfaced on restart — the clear happens in memory and is never written to disk, so loadQueue re-reads the stale file every launch. This is the boot-loop mechanism, demonstrated — just without a crash.
⛔ No recovery path exists on a release build. adb run-as = access denied (debuggable only). X-plore CANNOT reach Android/data/com.geeksville.mesh/ and offers no grant option — Android 13+ removed third-party file-manager access to Android/data entirely; MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE explicitly excludes it and the document-tree picker refuses it. Only root, adb-on-debuggable, or the app itself can read there. The only escape is Clear-App-Data.
Resolution this time: the queue eventually drained on its own (ended at 4 entries processing normally). App data was NOT cleared — but the queue file was never inspected, so the bad bbox was never captured.
The decision (Fred 07-23)
Turn off the JSON write / auto-refresh when a map source is changed. Refresh becomes manually requested as an Area download — which rides the already-hardened submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells path. This removes the thing that spawned 3287 entries without needing the bounds bug diagnosed first.
Build notes
Scope it first: sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt (the enqueueRefresh call site at :271) and the state at :81-83 (refreshSlot / refreshTileCount / refreshEnqueued). Determine whether refresh fires AUTOMATICALLY on source selection or sits behind a button — that decides whether to gate the call or disable the control.
DISABLE, don't delete. Gate it behind a clearly-marked constant or comment it out. The bug is still undiagnosed and the path will be wanted when it's revisited — deleting now means reconstructing later.
⚠ This does NOT fix Cancel All. The persistence failure is a separate defect: any future bad queue still resurrects on restart. Turning off refresh removes the most likely source of a bad queue and buys time; it does not close the hole.
⛔ DO NOT run replace-map-source again until this ships — recovery costs an hour and possibly all app-internal data.
Root cause still open (for when it's revisited)
Leading hypothesis, unverified: the bbox handed to enqueueRefresh is not the user's viewport — a default/zero-initialised value, or swapped bounds arguments. Bounds-order is already the standing suspect for the “map REFRESH no longer works” regression; these may be one defect. Note 3287 ≈ ceil(enormous/50K) — segmentation worked correctly on garbage input, so the bug is upstream of segmentCells. Compare sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt against sed -n '218,250p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt side by side for argument order. Also read sed -n '440,490p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt — :473 declares val bad = File(..., "download_queue/" + QUEUE_FILE), suggesting some quarantine handling already exists, and it is likely the same function where cancel's persistence is failing.
🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #2 — RECOVERY SYSTEM FOR APPLICATION-PROTECTED DATA (the “Repair Area”)
NEW 07-23 full design below — buildable
Why this exists
07-23 proved that bad on-disk state in filesDir is unreachable AND unrecoverable on a release build except by Clear-App-Data. The app itself has unrestricted access to its own filesDir — the OS only blocks other apps — so the escape hatch must be built INTO GroupTrack.
⭐ What actually lives in filesDir (inventory built 07-23 from xrefs)
PathPurposeSourceLoss if wiped
download_queue/download_queue.jsontile download queueConvoyDownloadQueue:444/461, QUEUE_FILE:86none — rebuildable
convoy_apply_list.jsonradio apply listConvoyApplyList:107/110/133low
convoy_users.jsonuser recordsConvoyUser:113/119/133meaningful
master_config.jsonT1000-E MASTER radio configConvoyMasterConfig:152/217; MasterCapture:557meaningful
convoy_backups/&lt;id&gt;/per-radio config backupsConvoyRadioManager:34/146; ViewModel:266HIGH

convoy_events/event configsConvoyEventConfig:176/178meaningful

cacheDir/*.gpx, transfer filestemp export/transferTrackOps:684; TransferRide:65none
⭐⭐ KEY CONSEQUENCE: filesDir holds radio configs, radio backups, users, rides and events — not just the queue. Clear-App-Data is NOT a clean fallback: it destroys every radio backup and the master config alongside the bad file. (Tracks and TILES survive — they live outside app storage in Documents/GroupTrack/data/ and /maps/.) This is exactly why per-file repair is worth far more than a reset button.
Design — the flow
Password gate. Threat model is NOT snooping — it's a tester deleting the wrong thing while following phone instructions, or tapping through out of curiosity. A build-time constant checked against a text field is sufficient (anything in the APK is extractable; the gate exists to make the action deliberate).
Test for repair-area existence FIRST. If one exists → WARN + DISPLAY CONTENTS, and allow adding a new (different) item.
Extract — ONE ENTITY AT A TIME via file picker. NO MASS COPY (“that is too scary”). Each extract writes TWO copies: the working file into the repair area (Downloads), and a pristine pre-edit snapshot into the dated archive.
Edit the file in the repair area, with normal tools.
Copy back AS A GROUP (see below), then remove the repair area.
State rules
NO REPLACEMENT of an already-staged item without an EXPLICIT DELETE. Re-extracting the same filename is REFUSED — it would silently overwrite the working copy (and any editing done) with a fresh pull from filesDir. The repair area is effectively append-only; removal is always a deliberate act.
DISPLAY what's staged. CANCEL-AND-RETURN discards the repair area, writes nothing to filesDir — and KEEPS the dated archive (an abandoned repair still leaves evidence of the original state).
⭐ The repair area is a HOLDING area — copy-back is GROUPED
Items are staged across separate one-at-a-time extracts, and the contents are copied back as a group — the staged set is the unit of repair. Extraction is one-at-a-time; restoration is grouped. Rationale: related files that must change together (users + rides, or a config + its backup) would leave inconsistent intermediate state if restored individually.
⭐ Archive naming + retention
Archived files are DATE AND TIME STAMPED — a unique occurrence per extract — held 30 days. Timestamp (not just date) so two repairs of the SAME file on the SAME day cannot collide or silently overwrite each other; every extract is its own recoverable point-in-time snapshot. Mirror the filesDir structure so different files can't collide either:
Documents/GroupTrack/saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json
⭐ The retention sweep runs ON APP OPEN, EVERY OPEN — not on repair-screen entry. A phone that did one repair months ago must not quietly hold stale copies forever just because nobody revisits the screen. Keep it cheap, non-blocking, and fail-safe — a sweep error must NEVER block or crash startup.
⭐⭐ The manifest JSON — work order + audit record
Finishing a repair writes/updates a manifest saying “apply this repair on startup.” It is not just a flag — it carries the work order and makes the apply crash-safe.
{
  "created": "2026-07-23T14:12:05",
  "status":  "pending",
  "problem": "&lt;WHAT ARE WE SOLVING&gt;   — captured at EXTRACT time",
  "repair":  "&lt;WHAT CHANGES DID WE MAKE&gt; — captured at COPY-BACK time",
  "items": [
    { "source":   "repair/download_queue.json",
      "target":   "download_queue/download_queue.json",
      "archived": "saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json" }
  ]
}
problem and repair are captured at DIFFERENT moments. The problem is known when you start (prompt at extract); the repair description isn't known until you finish (prompt at copy-back).
target settles the destination-mapping problem — recorded at extract time, so there is no guessing and no user re-selection at apply time.
Crash-safe: status stays pending until the group write fully succeeds; if the app dies mid-apply the next launch sees pending and retries. Clear only on success. Combined with all-or-nothing validation, a half-applied restore is impossible.
Single source of truth: the manifest is also what the repair screen reads to display staged contents, rather than inferring from a directory listing.
Placement: in the repair area (Downloads) so it travels with the staged files and is readable/editable. Startup code must tolerate a missing or malformed manifest by simply skipping the apply.
⭐⭐ Apply on RESTART, not on exit
Apply-on-exit still races: Android doesn't guarantee clean shutdown, subsystems may be mid-write on the way down, and saveQueue firing during teardown is the same mechanism that made Cancel All appear to work and then resurrect. Apply at startup, VERY EARLY — before loadQueue, before MapStateStore, before anything opens a filesDir file. That is the only genuinely quiescent moment: nothing holds a handle, nothing has read state into memory, nothing can overwrite the repair afterward. This also resolves the live-handle hazard — the download worker hasn't started yet.
Startup order: APPLY FIRST, then the 30-day sweep (housekeeping must not delay the repair). ⚠ The apply must be as fail-safe as the sweep — an exception there would block startup, the exact failure this feature exists to prevent. Wrap it, log it, leave the marker pending for a retry, and let the app boot regardless.
⭐ Applied-repair HISTORY
On successful apply the record moves to a persistent history file with outcome + applied-timestamp appended (applied, or failed + reason). History persists; the manifest is consumed. Value: three weeks later, “has anyone hand-edited this file, and why?” becomes answerable — a question that is currently unanswerable at all. Keep history entries indefinitely (they're small text); losing the record of what changed is worse than losing the copies. Note a history entry's archived path will eventually point at a purged file once the 30-day sweep runs — fine, as long as the entry says so.
Still open
Validate before overwriting — at minimum, confirm each staged JSON parses. Restoring a truncated file would manufacture the exact poison-file scenario this feature exists to escape. With a grouped copy-back: validate EVERY staged item first and abort the whole group if any fails.
Auto-backup the current filesDir file(s) before the group write, making the restore itself reversible.
Cheaper complements (consider alongside, not instead)
“Reset download queue” button (~30 lines) — clears memory AND deletes the file atomically. Would have solved 07-23 in one tap.
Diagnostic mirror — copy queue state to Documents/GroupTrack/ on every save, making it readable via X-plore with no browser at all. Would have shown the 3287 entries and the bad bbox immediately.
NOTE: access and resilience are alternative solutions to the same problem. The repair area makes emergencies survivable; loadQueue tolerant-parse makes them rare. Both are wanted; neither replaces the other.

🔴🔴 OPEN — THREE DEFECTS FOUND ON DEVICE 07-24 PM (gate the Play upload, not the build)
FOUND ON THE H+J BUILD Installed and exercised on device. The panel itself works — but three things are wrong, and all three were found by looking at the screen rather than reasoning about the code.
1. ⏱ The ETA finish DATE is wrong (the duration is right)
Panel read ~1d 4h · done Jul 28 6:28 PM, captured 2026-07-24 at 2:28 PM. One day four hours from then is Jul 25 6:28 PM. The time-of-day is exactly right, so the duration→clock conversion works; the date arithmetic is off by three days.
Why it matters: a tester reading "done Jul 28" leaves a queue running for days it doesn't need, or cancels a job that would have finished tonight. ⚠ The 2.6d release notes advertise "a projected finish time" — that claim ships wrong until this is fixed (Fred: post as-is, internal field-test track).
Where to look: whatever formats the completion stamp beside estimateRemaining(). Suspect adding the duration to the wrong field, or day-of-month vs day-of-year. Since the time is correct, the bug is isolated to the date component.
2. ⚠⚠ Corridor jobs are marked Done while still counting tiles
Entry2:232:252:28
CORR SAT151515
CORR TOPO4,4755,1255,774
CORR TOPO+4,5505,1756,175
All three sit under COMPLETED, labelled Done, and TOPO/TOPO+ keep climbing across three captures minutes apart. A finished job must not still accumulate. So markComplete is firing before the work stops.
⚠ This poisons the ETA (defect 1's likely feeder): completedAt gets stamped early, so the elapsed time used for the rate is shorter than the real work, and estimateRemaining() computes from an inflated rate. Fix this before trusting any ETA number.
⭐ Same family as the refresh bug — completion state and actual work drifting apart. Two symptoms, likely one root: how and when workers report terminal state.
3. ⚠⚠ CORR SAT frozen at 15 tiles
SAT sat at exactly 15 across all three captures while its siblings climbed ~650 each. SAT should be the LARGEST of the three — it carries three layers where the others carry fewer.
⛔ The benign explanation is now dead. First read was "hasTile skipped tiles already on disk, so 15 is honest remaining work." But then it would be a different number per run and would sit above the others, not 300× below, and it would not stay pinned while the others move.
THE ONE TEST THAT SETTLES IT: run the same track's corridor with REPLACE ticked. Replace bypasses the hasTile pre-fetch filter, so SAT must derive and fetch its full corridor.
SAT returns in the thousands → filter was working, nothing broken, 15 was honest.
SAT returns 15 again → SAT corridor derivation/fetch is broken, and the ≈90% headline measures what was queued, not what landed.
⚠ If SAT is broken, testers get corridor downloads with no satellite imagery — the primary source — which is a worse regression than anything the cutover fixed. Do this before promoting past the internal track.
Likely shape (unverified): defects 2 and 3 are probably one investigation. "Stops after the first handful, marks Done, siblings keep going" is what a layer loop exiting early on the multi-layer source looks like. Read ConvoyCorridorWorker's per-layer loop and its completion call together.

🔵 NEXT BUILD — G5: ROUTE CORRIDORS (design settled 07-24, not yet written)
READY TO PATCH Fred's rule: the route key goes where the track hash goes. The rest of the code is the same. No new identity concept, no discriminator debate.
⭐ The blocker dissolved on inspection: the routes table already carries geom_hash (insert at SpatialDbManager:900), and the comment block at :1278-1287 states all four artifact types funnel through one core that computes it, with per-type tables making UNIQUE(geom_hash) express identity. computeGeomHash is public at :1288.
What actually has to change
getTrackPoints (SpatialDbManager:1927) hardcodes FROM tracks at :1933. This file already has the table-parameterised pattern ($table/$idCol at :421, :464, :1332) — follow it. Also drop the .gpx strip (:1928) for routes; it encodes "tracks live in hash-named .gpx files".
⚠ getTrackBbox (SpatialDbManager:1975) is a SECOND hardcoded FROM tracks (:1981) and it runs BEFORE the confirm dialog. For a route it returns null → the user taps SAVE MAPS and gets "No geometry for this track". The button would look dead and the message would point at the wrong thing. Routes have min/max lat/lon (written at :900), so it is the same parameterisation.
Panel gate — artifactType == "Tracks" at ArtifactDetailPanel:111 opens to Routes. Confirm detailFields["geom_hash"] is populated for routes (generic lookup at :464 is table-parameterised, so it should be) — if blank, the button silently does nothing (if (!gh.isNullOrBlank())).
Route import — it exists: ConvoyTrackOps:662, beside the track import at :586. ⚠ Unlike the track path it does not have the hash in hand — insertRoute (SpatialDbManager:892) returns route_id and computes gh internally at :896 without exposing it. Caller calls computeGeomHash(wkt) (public, :1288).
⚠ Defects to fix while in there
Zero-tile derivation returns SUCCESS. ConvoyCorridorWorker :75-78 does markComplete(entryId, 0, 0); return Result.success() on an empty corridor. Geometry that exists but yields no tiles is a derivation failure, not a completion — and a zero-tile "completion" enters the ETA sample set as work-done-in-no-time. (The no-geometry path at :69-72 is already correct: markFailed + Result.failure().)
⚠ insertRoute returns a fabricated id on duplicates — newId(), then INSERT OR IGNORE, then returns the new id even when nothing was inserted. The track path handles this at :971-972 by resolving the existing row's id from the unique hash; routes never got that treatment. Silent wrong-id generator. Another argument for keying corridors off the hash: the hash is correct on a duplicate, the returned id is not.
Buffer/derivation need no change — routes are plain LINESTRING and the G1 parser already handles LINESTRING and MULTILINESTRING. Fred on density: snap-2 means routes inherit the trail's own vertex density, and with a half-mile buffer either side, coverage is fine — no interpolation needed.
🔴 OPEN ITEM — REFRESH DOES NOT LOG AS A COMPLETED JOB (new 07-24)
NEW 07-24 A map-source refresh job never registers as completed.
⚠ Why this is bigger than a cosmetic status
It may be why the ETA has no samples. estimateRemaining() reads the last two COMPLETE entries and completedAt is stamped in markComplete. A job that never reaches COMPLETE contributes nothing — the ETA line would silently not render, looking like a UI bug rather than a missing write. This is the identical failure mode as patch A2 (a field added but never written), one layer further out.
CLEAR won't clear it. CLEAR currently means COMPLETE+FAILED+CANCELLED — "all terminal". A job stuck in a non-terminal status is unclearable from the panel, and accumulates.
⚠⚠ Does it hold a concurrency slot? If the entry never leaves a running/active status, startNextIfAvailable may count it against MAX_CONCURRENT forever. That is a queue-stall mechanism, and "system just sits" is exactly what 07-23 reported. Check this first — it is the difference between a reporting bug and a throughput bug.
Where to look
grep -n "markComplete" app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/*.kt — establish which workers call it and which don't.
Then read ConvoyDownloadWorker's refresh branch end-to-end: does it return Result.success() without notifying the queue, or take a different terminal path (removed rather than marked)?
⭐ Check ConvoyCorridorWorker in the SAME pass. The corridor worker deliberately duplicates the completion plumbing rather than sharing it — that was an accepted trade. This bug is that trade coming due: if refresh can miss markComplete, so can corridor, independently. Confirm corridor stamps completion BEFORE spending hours waiting on a download to prove the ETA — otherwise the wait proves nothing.
Note the sequencing risk: the ETA is currently untestable for an unrelated reason too — it needs two downloads that start and finish on a stamped build, since older completed entries have completedAt=0L and are filtered out permanently. Don't conflate "no samples yet" with "completion is broken"; separate them by checking the code, not by waiting.
🔴 OPEN ITEM — RESTORE PER-SOURCE Z-LEVEL DOWNLOAD LIMITS
CONFIRMED REAL Fred: "return the z-level download limits per map source. we are downloading tiles — or at least requesting tile downloads — where tiles do not exist." Affects both the area and corridor paths.
⛔ ConvoyTileCalculator.maxZoomForSource(sourceName) (:72) is a STUB: = ConvoyConfig.DOWNLOAD_ZOOM, ignoring its argument entirely. So calculateTiles's per-source cap effectiveZMax = minOf(zMax, maxZoomForSource(name)) always computes minOf(18,18) = 18.
quickEstimate has no sourceName parameter at all, so it cannot cap even in principle — sizing and fetching disagree today, which is its own latent bug.
⚠ corridorTiles INHERITS THE SAME GAP — it takes zMin/zMax defaulting to DOWNLOAD_ZOOM with no source awareness. Fixing the stub alone will NOT fix corridor; the source must be passed in.
⚠ The cost is severe — tile counts QUADRUPLE per zoom level. For a source really capped at z15, levels 16+17+18 are roughly 84× the z15 count, and every one of those requests is a 404 or upsampled junk. TOPO+ maps to esri-usa-topo at max_zoom 15, so this is not hypothetical.
The fix: (1) give maxZoomForSource a real per-source lookup — the ceiling lives in the source definitions MapSourceManager parses, so read it from there rather than hardcoding; (2) add a sourceName parameter to quickEstimate so sizing agrees with fetching; (3) pass the source into corridorTiles.
⭐ It also affects MAP DISPLAY, not just downloads (Fred): "we should not zoom to levels where tiles do not exist." Same root cause, different symptom — the map lets the user zoom past a source's real max, showing upsampled mush and firing requests that 404. Once maxZoomForSource returns a real value it should feed the Leaflet layer's maxZoom/maxNativeZoom. Fred: "that is for another day" — deferred, but kept attached here so the display half isn't lost when the download half gets fixed.
⚠ SEQUENCING: capping z will change the corridor baseline numbers. The bar-10 measurement (~107,000) was taken before the cap, so it isolates the MODEL change. The z-cap saving compounds on top and must be measured separately — two variables, two measurements.

🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #1 — TURN OFF MAP REFRESH ON SOURCE CHANGE (do first)
DO FIRST stop-the-bleeding, not a root-cause fix
What happened (07-23, on the shipped 2.6c build)
The REPLACE/refresh function on the map-source select screen “does not behave”: it spawned 3287 downloads in the queue, lat/long spanning the whole continental US. Downloads then stopped working entirely (“system just sits”).
⚠ Cancel All does NOT persist. Cancel appeared to clear the queue, but all 3287 jobs resurfaced on restart — the clear happens in memory and is never written to disk, so loadQueue re-reads the stale file every launch. This is the boot-loop mechanism, demonstrated — just without a crash.
⛔ No recovery path exists on a release build. adb run-as = access denied (debuggable only). X-plore CANNOT reach Android/data/com.geeksville.mesh/ and offers no grant option — Android 13+ removed third-party file-manager access to Android/data entirely; MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE explicitly excludes it and the document-tree picker refuses it. Only root, adb-on-debuggable, or the app itself can read there. The only escape is Clear-App-Data.
Resolution this time: the queue eventually drained on its own (ended at 4 entries processing normally). App data was NOT cleared — but the queue file was never inspected, so the bad bbox was never captured.
The decision (Fred 07-23)
Turn off the JSON write / auto-refresh when a map source is changed. Refresh becomes manually requested as an Area download — which rides the already-hardened submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells path. This removes the thing that spawned 3287 entries without needing the bounds bug diagnosed first.
Build notes
Scope it first: sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt (the enqueueRefresh call site at :271) and the state at :81-83 (refreshSlot / refreshTileCount / refreshEnqueued). Determine whether refresh fires AUTOMATICALLY on source selection or sits behind a button — that decides whether to gate the call or disable the control.
DISABLE, don't delete. Gate it behind a clearly-marked constant or comment it out. The bug is still undiagnosed and the path will be wanted when it's revisited — deleting now means reconstructing later.
⚠ This does NOT fix Cancel All. The persistence failure is a separate defect: any future bad queue still resurrects on restart. Turning off refresh removes the most likely source of a bad queue and buys time; it does not close the hole.
⛔ DO NOT run replace-map-source again until this ships — recovery costs an hour and possibly all app-internal data.
Root cause still open (for when it's revisited)
Leading hypothesis, unverified: the bbox handed to enqueueRefresh is not the user's viewport — a default/zero-initialised value, or swapped bounds arguments. Bounds-order is already the standing suspect for the “map REFRESH no longer works” regression; these may be one defect. Note 3287 ≈ ceil(enormous/50K) — segmentation worked correctly on garbage input, so the bug is upstream of segmentCells. Compare sed -n '255,290p' ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt against sed -n '218,250p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt side by side for argument order. Also read sed -n '440,490p' ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt — :473 declares val bad = File(..., "download_queue/" + QUEUE_FILE), suggesting some quarantine handling already exists, and it is likely the same function where cancel's persistence is failing.
🔴 NEW OPEN ITEM #2 — RECOVERY SYSTEM FOR APPLICATION-PROTECTED DATA (the “Repair Area”)
NEW 07-23 full design below — buildable
Why this exists
07-23 proved that bad on-disk state in filesDir is unreachable AND unrecoverable on a release build except by Clear-App-Data. The app itself has unrestricted access to its own filesDir — the OS only blocks other apps — so the escape hatch must be built INTO GroupTrack.
⭐ What actually lives in filesDir (inventory built 07-23 from xrefs)
PathPurposeSourceLoss if wiped
download_queue/download_queue.jsontile download queueConvoyDownloadQueue:444/461, QUEUE_FILE:86none — rebuildable
convoy_apply_list.jsonradio apply listConvoyApplyList:107/110/133low
convoy_users.jsonuser recordsConvoyUser:113/119/133meaningful
master_config.jsonT1000-E MASTER radio configConvoyMasterConfig:152/217; MasterCapture:557meaningful
convoy_backups/&lt;id&gt;/per-radio config backupsConvoyRadioManager:34/146; ViewModel:266HIGH
convoy_rides/ride recordsConvoyViewModel:273meaningful
convoy_events/event configsConvoyEventConfig:176/178meaningful
convoy_profiles/&lt;file&gt;radio profilesConvoyProfileBuilder:212meaningful
convoy_import/, docType import dirsimport stagingViewModel:345; FileReceiver:74/87none — transient
cacheDir/*.gpx, transfer filestemp export/transferTrackOps:684; TransferRide:65none
⭐⭐ KEY CONSEQUENCE: filesDir holds radio configs, radio backups, users, rides and events — not just the queue. Clear-App-Data is NOT a clean fallback: it destroys every radio backup and the master config alongside the bad file. (Tracks and TILES survive — they live outside app storage in Documents/GroupTrack/data/ and /maps/.) This is exactly why per-file repair is worth far more than a reset button.
Design — the flow
Password gate. Threat model is NOT snooping — it's a tester deleting the wrong thing while following phone instructions, or tapping through out of curiosity. A build-time constant checked against a text field is sufficient (anything in the APK is extractable; the gate exists to make the action deliberate).
Test for repair-area existence FIRST. If one exists → WARN + DISPLAY CONTENTS, and allow adding a new (different) item.
Extract — ONE ENTITY AT A TIME via file picker. NO MASS COPY (“that is too scary”). Each extract writes TWO copies: the working file into the repair area (Downloads), and a pristine pre-edit snapshot into the dated archive.
Edit the file in the repair area, with normal tools.
Copy back AS A GROUP (see below), then remove the repair area.
State rules
NO REPLACEMENT of an already-staged item without an EXPLICIT DELETE. Re-extracting the same filename is REFUSED — it would silently overwrite the working copy (and any editing done) with a fresh pull from filesDir. The repair area is effectively append-only; removal is always a deliberate act.
DISPLAY what's staged. CANCEL-AND-RETURN discards the repair area, writes nothing to filesDir — and KEEPS the dated archive (an abandoned repair still leaves evidence of the original state).
⭐ The repair area is a HOLDING area — copy-back is GROUPED
Items are staged across separate one-at-a-time extracts, and the contents are copied back as a group — the staged set is the unit of repair. Extraction is one-at-a-time; restoration is grouped. Rationale: related files that must change together (users + rides, or a config + its backup) would leave inconsistent intermediate state if restored individually.
⭐ Archive naming + retention
Archived files are DATE AND TIME STAMPED — a unique occurrence per extract — held 30 days. Timestamp (not just date) so two repairs of the SAME file on the SAME day cannot collide or silently overwrite each other; every extract is its own recoverable point-in-time snapshot. Mirror the filesDir structure so different files can't collide either:
Documents/GroupTrack/saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json
⭐ The retention sweep runs ON APP OPEN, EVERY OPEN — not on repair-screen entry. A phone that did one repair months ago must not quietly hold stale copies forever just because nobody revisits the screen. Keep it cheap, non-blocking, and fail-safe — a sweep error must NEVER block or crash startup.
⭐⭐ The manifest JSON — work order + audit record
Finishing a repair writes/updates a manifest saying “apply this repair on startup.” It is not just a flag — it carries the work order and makes the apply crash-safe.
{
  "created": "2026-07-23T14:12:05",
  "status":  "pending",
  "problem": "&lt;WHAT ARE WE SOLVING&gt;   — captured at EXTRACT time",
  "repair":  "&lt;WHAT CHANGES DID WE MAKE&gt; — captured at COPY-BACK time",
  "items": [
    { "source":   "repair/download_queue.json",
      "target":   "download_queue/download_queue.json",
      "archived": "saved/2026-07-23_141205/download_queue/download_queue.json" }
  ]
}
problem and repair are captured at DIFFERENT moments. The problem is known when you start (prompt at extract); the repair description isn't known until you finish (prompt at copy-back).
target settles the destination-mapping problem — recorded at extract time, so there is no guessing and no user re-selection at apply time.
Crash-safe: status stays pending until the group write fully succeeds; if the app dies mid-apply the next launch sees pending and retries. Clear only on success. Combined with all-or-nothing validation, a half-applied restore is impossible.
Single source of truth: the manifest is also what the repair screen reads to display staged contents, rather than inferring from a directory listing.
Placement: in the repair area (Downloads) so it travels with the staged files and is readable/editable. Startup code must tolerate a missing or malformed manifest by simply skipping the apply.
⭐⭐ Apply on RESTART, not on exit
Apply-on-exit still races: Android doesn't guarantee clean shutdown, subsystems may be mid-write on the way down, and saveQueue firing during teardown is the same mechanism that made Cancel All appear to work and then resurrect. Apply at startup, VERY EARLY — before loadQueue, before MapStateStore, before anything opens a filesDir file. That is the only genuinely quiescent moment: nothing holds a handle, nothing has read state into memory, nothing can overwrite the repair afterward. This also resolves the live-handle hazard — the download worker hasn't started yet.
Startup order: APPLY FIRST, then the 30-day sweep (housekeeping must not delay the repair). ⚠ The apply must be as fail-safe as the sweep — an exception there would block startup, the exact failure this feature exists to prevent. Wrap it, log it, leave the marker pending for a retry, and let the app boot regardless.
⭐ Applied-repair HISTORY
On successful apply the record moves to a persistent history file with outcome + applied-timestamp appended (applied, or failed + reason). History persists; the manifest is consumed. Value: three weeks later, “has anyone hand-edited this file, and why?” becomes answerable — a question that is currently unanswerable at all. Keep history entries indefinitely (they're small text); losing the record of what changed is worse than losing the copies. Note a history entry's archived path will eventually point at a purged file once the 30-day sweep runs — fine, as long as the entry says so.
Still open
Validate before overwriting — at minimum, confirm each staged JSON parses. Restoring a truncated file would manufacture the exact poison-file scenario this feature exists to escape. With a grouped copy-back: validate EVERY staged item first and abort the whole group if any fails.
Auto-backup the current filesDir file(s) before the group write, making the restore itself reversible.
Cheaper complements (consider alongside, not instead)
“Reset download queue” button (~30 lines) — clears memory AND deletes the file atomically. Would have solved 07-23 in one tap.
Diagnostic mirror — copy queue state to Documents/GroupTrack/ on every save, making it readable via X-plore with no browser at all. Would have shown the 3287 entries and the bad bbox immediately.
NOTE: access and resilience are alternative solutions to the same problem. The repair area makes emergencies survivable; loadQueue tolerant-parse makes them rare. Both are wanted; neither replaces the other.
