🔴 00-INSTALL (08-04, DESIGNED — NOT BUILT) — GroupTrack TRIGGERS ITS OWN UNINSTALL
PURPOSE: remove the new-install data-loss exposure that destroyed ~89,000 trails on 08-01.
STATE: DESIGN AGREED 08-04. No code.
DOCUMENT OF RECORD: grouptrack_install_design_2026-08-04.html — full design, flow, and reasoning.
SUPERSEDES: the manual-only approach in grouptrack_reinstall_procedure_2026-08-03.html, which stays valid as the fallback for anyone not using the in-app path.
The key realisation
The app can uninstall itself. Intent.ACTION_DELETE launches the system uninstall dialog — and at that moment the app is alive and holds authority, so it can do the dangerous bookkeeping while it still can. Ten manual steps become two taps.
THE FLOW: user taps "Prepare for reinstall" → app renames Documents/GroupTrack → .bak and My Tracks → .bak (instant regardless of 50–60 GB) → fires the uninstall intent on itself → user installs the new build → All-Files grant requested FIRST, before anything touches the DB → REAL READ of the .bak dirs → prompt to restore → on confirm, verify the blanks are EMPTY, delete them, rename back.
⭐ WHY RENAMING BEATS DETECTING: every detection approach fails for the same reason — the app creates blanks BEFORE authority arrives, and the permission API reports the wrong answer at exactly that moment. The rename does not detect anything; it removes the data from the path the app will write to until authority is real. Nothing to detect, nothing to destroy.
⭐⭐ The ordering half — grant BEFORE the database
08-01 was an ORDERING failure. The app opened the DB before authority was real, and did not prompt because it TESTED and the test lied — Environment.isExternalStorageManager() returns true in the stale-grant state and is wrong. It reads the stale grant record; the filesystem enforces the truth. No API question returns the right answer — only a real read attempt does.
Fred: "we never got the prompt in the failed install as the app looked like it had authority. probably should not be a test but unconditional grant there." → make the All-Files prompt UNCONDITIONAL on first run and put it FIRST. The app already knows it is a fresh install — it is already asking first-run questions. No new detection needed.
⛔ REJECTED — AND WHY: blocking startup until the app can read would DEADLOCK the device. The app must run before it can be granted authority, so refusing to start until it can read means a reinstalled device can never be recovered. Also rejected: acting at uninstall time — Android has no uninstall hook; ACTION_PACKAGE_REMOVED goes to OTHER apps and arrives too late anyway. The danger is not the uninstall, it is the next install running blind.
The first-run marker — filesDir, NOT shared storage
⛔ THE TRAP if it lived in Documents/: that file sits in the very storage the authority question is about. Without All-Files the app cannot read it, so "file absent" and "cannot see the file" look identical — the exact confusion that caused 08-01, reproduced in a new file.
✅ filesDir needs no authority and is always readable, and is wiped by uninstall — which makes it a better signal, not a worse one:
marker ABSENT + data PRESENT in Documents/ = a reinstall over existing data. That is the detector 08-01 needed, free with the same file.
Contents: {"status":"in_progress"} → {"status":"complete","version_code":N}. Retaining it after completion answers both has setup run? and is this a reinstall?, and gives crash recovery for a first run that dies midway.
🔴 OPEN ITEMS
⚠⚠ FIRST ACTION — VERIFY ON DROID 2 THAT AN UNINSTALL LEAVES Documents/GroupTrack/ INTACT. It should — public shared storage — but Android has changed storage behaviour repeatedly, and the entire design rests on this assumption. Minutes to test. Promoted from "open question" because if it is wrong the whole flow inverts.
Cancelled uninstall dialog: directories already renamed, app still installed, finds no data. Needs an undo path — on next launch, if .bak exists and the app is clearly NOT freshly installed, offer to rename back. (Renaming only after removal is confirmed is impossible; the app cannot observe its own uninstall.)
Settings/launcher uninstalls bypass the button entirely. The manual procedure stays documented as fallback — and refuse-to-create (below) is the floor under everything.
⚠⚠ THE REVERSE-RISK MOMENT is step 8 — it DELETES directories. Everything before it protected against overwriting real data with blanks; this step can delete the wrong thing if the empty-check is wrong. Refuse if non-empty, log what was found, and ask — a user who recorded a track between install and restore has real data in those "blanks".
🔴🔴 00-REFUSE (2.6e P0) — REFUSE-TO-CREATE. THE FLOOR UNDER EVERYTHING.
⭐⭐⭐ LIFTED OUT OF THE INSTALL DESIGN ON PURPOSE (08-05). The install flow protects users who tap the button. This protects everyone else — including every Settings/launcher uninstall, every revoked permission, every FUSE/SELinux hiccup. Different priority, different item.
SpatialDbManager must NEVER create-if-missing on a path it cannot verify. A failed open must ABORT, not write an empty schema. The install design names this as "the single highest-value item on this page" — it alone would have prevented 08-01, and it costs nothing at runtime.
⚠ And it is not hypothetical maintenance: the SELinux ioctl denial on the FUSE-mounted store fires on ordinary download runs (observed 08-05, see 00-HYB-PROVEN). The trigger condition is present regularly; only the create-if-missing turns it into data loss.
Also owed with it: ROW-COUNT SANITY + a .lastgood copy after each successful startup. A startup reporting zero rows where the previous run reported 89,000 is a red flag the app should RAISE, not report as normal.
✅ Fixed 08-04: SpatialDbManager :166/:168 logged the LITERAL ${spatialFile.absolutePath} because the $ was backslash-escaped — so the DB path never appeared in the log. That was the diagnostic that would have made the 08-01 loss obvious immediately.

🧰 00-TOOLS (08-05) — TROUBLESHOOTING TOOLS AND USES
DOCUMENT OF RECORD: grouptrack_troubleshooting_tools_and_uses_2026-08-05.html — six sections: the three xrefs and their blind spots · layer contracts · divergence · the 2.7 dead-code prune recipe · the draw-failure recipe · pre-build hazards.
⭐⭐ WHY IT EXISTS: four defects this week shared one shape — a method aborted before its real work, silently — and no structural tool could have found any of them. The xrefs answer where is this touched. Every one of these lived on a different axis: on what thread, in what lifecycle phase, against which page. There is no index for that axis.
The layer contracts — the rules with no tooling
BoundaryRuns onRule
@JavascriptInterface methodsJavaBridgeANY WebView or UI call MUST go through Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { }. They throw off-main and the throw aborts the method silently. Four-for-four now — mechanical rule, no case-by-case judgement.
Argument positions—Never ?: return inside an argument. Reads as a null-safe accessor, is an early exit from the whole function.
onPageFinishedmainPage not ready until the postDelayed completes. Earlier Kotlin→JS calls fail with &lt;fn&gt; is not defined, visible only in a console log.
evaluateJavascript(fn)main onlyThe named function must exist in BOTH map HTMLs. SpatialDisplayManager's jsUpdate/jsShow/jsHide contract assumes hand-maintained parity.
WorkManager workersfresh processJobs survive app death. ensureInit() re-reads config from scratch — never trust in-memory state across the process boundary.
shouldInterceptRequestnetworkNo UI, no WebView calls.
⭐⭐ navigation_xref.txt — the one xref that gives CALL SITES
Four sections. A nav-host routes (every registered destination) · C navigation triggers — navigate() calls and onNavigate* params with the line where each is invoked · D screen composables + exit callbacks · E user-visible labels.
⭐ SECTION A vs SECTION C MAKES THE DEAD-DESTINATION CHECK MECHANICAL: a route registered in A with no navigate() in C is unreachable. Proven: ConvoyRouteCreate is registered at ConvoyNavigation.kt:87 (A), its composable declared at ConvoyRouteCreateScreen.kt:18 (D), and it appears nowhere in C — a 27-line stub reachable from nothing. Do this before any manual grepping in the 2.7 prune.
⭐ Section E is the MANUAL-WRITING tool — it is what the user actually taps, which is the vocabulary the manual has to use.
⚠ Check its Generated: timestamp against the last commit. A call-site index that lags the code produces confident wrong answers. (Current copy: generated 2026-08-05 09:14.)
⚠ The xrefs' documented blind spots — each cost real time
Lambda parameters — onDownloadMaps appears in no xref; looked dead, was live in two screens.
var X by remember { } locals — addPointMode is in none of them.
Tags held in constants — 08-05: a grep for Log.x("LITERAL" returned nothing across four well-instrumented files, because the tags are TAG constants. The scan reported a silence that did not exist.
Anything inside a non-executing block — 08-03: a def-scan called a range clean; it was inside a &lt;script src&gt; tag whose inline body never executes by spec.
⛔ THE PATTERN BEHIND ALL OF THEM: scanning for one shape of evidence and reporting "clean" when the scan could not have seen what was there. A negative grep result is only as good as its pattern. Before trusting an empty result, prove the pattern matches a known-present case.
⚠ These blind spots apply to field_crossref / where_used / function_universe — declaration indexes. navigation_xref is the exception (above): for screen routing and reachability, read it FIRST rather than grepping.
⭐⭐ CONVOY IS THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION — divergence is a defect until proven intentional
Four times this week convoy had a fix the planner did not, and nobody knew until it broke: (1) [Fix2] fresh re-read; (2) seeding lastViewport* before draw; (3) posting evaluateJavascript to main; (4) the reseed gate — this one IS intentional (convoy is persistent and owns one map identity; the planner is entered and left, and the gate prevents cross-map bleed).
⚠ THE LIMIT: the maps are not symmetric by nature and must not be forced to be. The target is SHARED CODE, not MATCHED CODE — two hand-maintained copies drift again however carefully aligned today. SpatialDisplayManager has been the reliable layer all week precisely because there is ONE copy. ⭐ This is the same argument that makes the 2.7 service-layer work worth doing.
⛔ THE TRAP UNIQUE TO THIS CODEBASE — read before any 2.7 dead-code prune
Kotlin calls JavaScript functions BY NAME, from inside a string. ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:578 calls showProximityPopup that way. No JS tool sees that call. No Kotlin tool sees it either. A JS function with zero references in the HTML can be fully live; a Kotlin function whose only caller is a nav registration can be fully dead. Neither toolchain crosses the boundary — you are the only thing that does.
TOOLING OWED (none of it exists yet): a bridge-thread scanner (WebView/UI calls inside @JavascriptInterface bodies — would have caught :717 the day it was written, and run against both screens it answers the divergence question for free); a cross-boundary name checker (every evaluateJavascript("fn(...)") has a matching function fn in BOTH HTMLs); a screen-parity diff.
🔵 00-CORRIDOR-REFRESH (08-05) — NEXT BUILD, AFTER THE AAB
PURPOSE: refresh existing downloads by CORRIDOR, not by bounding box.
STATE: agreed 08-05, not started. Steps 4–6 of the 08-03 six-step plan.
⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN "a nicer option": the 215-job incident was area refresh converting each track BOUNDARY into a BBOX. A switchbacked trail's bbox covers the whole mountain; its corridor covers a line buffer. Corridor refresh is the fix for the thing that produced 215 jobs — the same problem corridor downloads were built for on 07-24.
⚠ Corridor refresh DOES NOT EXIST. Fred 08-03: "the refresh does not currently support corridor imports." Step 5 is BUILD, not MIGRATE.
The shape (Fred 08-05)
Both enqueue functions become callable with parameters, from anywhere: enqueueArea(bbox, …) for bbox items, enqueueCorridor(track, …) for track submissions. The PICKER is then just a caller, not part of either — build it once for corridor download, reuse it for corridor refresh. Corridor stacks per-track submissions.
⭐ The payoff: every download origin already routes through ConvoyDownloadConfirm → submitDownload. If refresh routes through the same picker and the same two enqueue functions, there stops being a separate refresh code path at all — refresh becomes "download, with replace on." That kills the gridCells problem rather than migrating it.
⚠ replace is a PARAMETER, not a separate function. Refresh re-fetches tiles already on disk, bypassing the hasTile pre-fetch filter. ⛔ And that flag is the same refreshMode field that was deleting completions until 08-05 — verify entries survive when the new refresh path passes it.
⚠ The estimate-and-confirm gate belongs in the PICKER, once — both callers go through it. One track was 561 tiles; select-all across a track list times the map slots is how 10 tracks became 215 jobs.
⚠ The AREA path still needs gridCells → segmentCells — corridor re-derives at run time and never builds oversized cells, so keeping area as an option keeps that defect live.
⚠ Compare enqueueRefresh's argument order against enqueueArea while in there — swapped bounds is the leading unverified hypothesis for the 07-23 continental incident, and this work touches that call site.
⛔ Must work in a FRESH PROCESS. WorkManager jobs survive app death; the worker's ensureInit() re-reads config from scratch. The column file is what makes that safe — which is why step 3 was placed before this.
OPEN: the picker lists TRACKS or TRAILS? Corridor derivation runs off track geometry (getTrackPoints, corridorTiles); trails would need a different path. Settle before writing.

⭐⭐⭐ 00-DISPLAY — THE TELESCOPE MODEL (settled 08-03 evening). NOT YET BUILT.
⭐ THIS IS THE DISPLAY PHILOSOPHY THE APP HAS BEEN MISSING. Seven items, one coherent build.
Everything below follows from one idea: zoom is the density control, not the artifact panel.
THE WORKFLOW (Fred, verbatim intent):
(1) find your area — search by name, or your own tracks;
(2) look at tracks around it — where you have actually ridden;
(3) drop waypoints — the points of interest;
(4) NOW turn trails on — the palette, at the scale you chose.
⭐ Trails come LAST, after you know what you want.
⭐⭐ WHY: "see the ground, see the features, see the trail — not a 100 mile line on the
map." At wide zoom 140,000 trails is a blob of colour with no information in it. Drilling into the yarnball, a thick
blue line resolves into 30 trails, and there are hundreds of such spots. That intimidates users rather than helping
them. The far view must carry enough to RECOGNISE a place by — your tracks, waypoints, town and park names — not
enough to plan with.
⭐ THE INSIGHT ABOUT THE PANEL: "you are not using select/omit to turn trails on and off, you
are using zoom to narrow what appears — the right tool for the job." The artifact panel is a participation
switch, not a density filter. Thinning 3,600 trails by picking items is the wrong instrument. That is why the
toggles always felt inadequate — they were being asked to do a job they were never shaped for.
THE SEVEN ITEMS:
(1) Trail ceiling 5,000, flat, every zoom that displays — inert at z16/z18 where the viewport is already
small; a ceiling only for z11–z12.
(2) Trails toggle disabled below z11, label reads Trails (Z11 or greater to display) on the
text line when ALL is not selectable.
(3) Trails forced OFF on MAP CHANGE — convoy→planner and planner→convoy, in the
lastMapProcessed gate. ⚠ Not on every panel entry: only crossing between the two maps clears it.
(4) Viewport state still restores normally — pan and zoom come back as they do now. Only artifact
visibility is overridden. Where you were is a fact worth restoring; what you had switched on is a choice worth
re-making.
(5) Search by track / trail / town / park name, returning a ~100 sq mi area around the point — the
planning frame, not a pin.
(6) No GPS snapback on the planning map after search — if search is the first move in planning, the map
must stay where it was sent.
(7) Manual: the telescope workflow, and "turn trails on when you have found your area."
⭐ ONE TAP TO GET IT BACK. That is what makes the reset acceptable rather than an imposition.
Conservative default, trivial override, no persistence fighting the user's judgement.
⭐ TUNABLES, NAMED AND IN ONE PLACE — TRAILS_MIN_ZOOM and
TRAILS_MAX_ROWS. ⚠ At ~39 minutes a build, tuning by rebuild is expensive: a TEMPORARY dev control to
move both values live would let a full tuning pass happen in one session on real ground.
⛔ It comes out in the commit that closes the task — that is the instrumentation lesson, not a cleanup-list item.
⚠ ARGUED AND REJECTED — a permanent user-facing "max trails" number. It asks the rider to solve a
problem they did not create and cannot reason about (what number? ordered by what? re-spent per viewport?), and it makes
the yarnball their fault for setting it wrong. If ever exposed, use words not digits — Fewer / Balanced / More —
so the rider expresses a preference they can judge.
⚠ Most planners will settle at z12–z13, so the yarnball case is rarer than it looks — z11 is the
boundary where trails are admissible, not where people will live. ⭐ And scale of ride sets the zoom: "nobody wants to
travel 100 miles and plan it at z13." Be permissive above z11; give the boundary and get out of the way.
⭐⭐⭐ 00-ENDSTATE — SUGGEST. Fred's stated vision for the product.
THE VISION (Fred 08-03): "one of the unfinished buttons is just that — set your points of
interest, your waypoint to embark and return from, the range of distance and time, and let the software recommend routes
that touch all your points. That is my vision for endstate." ⭐ That is the Suggest button already
sitting in the Route panel marked "soon".
THE PRODUCT, IN ONE LINE (Fred): "the route map is the palette — the routes and trails and
the infinite combinations to create a unique experience visiting points of interest."
⭐ A palette only works if you can see the colours. That is what 00-DISPLAY exists to protect.
WHY IT IS CLOSER THAN IT LOOKS: the graph is already in the spatial DB, snapping works, and
route vertices already carry lineId. What is missing is traversal — connectivity between segments at
their intersections, and a cost model.
⚠ CONNECTIVITY IS THE HARD PART, NOT THE ROUTING. OSM ways are segments; whether two segments
actually connect at a shared point — or merely cross without a junction — is the difference between a route and a
fantasy. ⚠ TIME IS HARDER THAN DISTANCE: distance falls out of geometry, time needs a speed model per trail type
and grade, and riders vary enormously. Start distance-only.
⭐⭐ THIS IS WHY TRACK-TO-TRAIL MATTERS. Tracks are certainty — you rode it, it exists.
Trails are a claim — someone mapped it, sometime, with some accuracy. Three operations, different confidence:
CONFIRM (track matches a trail — raises confidence, adds nothing) · APPEND (track extends past a trail's
endpoint — adds geometry) · FILL (track where no trail exists — creates the trail, or the junction).
⭐ FILL is the direct feed into Suggest: routing fails on gaps, and your tracks close exactly the junctions you
physically rode through. ⚠ The hard part is the same tolerance question as proximity snap — GPS wander means a track
along a trail is NEAR it, not coincident with it.
⭐ THE HONEST STATEMENT, worth saying plainly to users (Fred): "between trails and tracks you
know for certain what areas are known — the rest is up to you." A planner told where knowledge ends makes better
decisions than one handed a confident-looking line that turns out to be a fence.

⭐⭐ 00-GOOGLE-DETAIL — FUNCTIONALITY PER STEP (settled 08-03, build to this)
⭐ STEP 1 IS WRITTEN AND COMPILED — patch_column_file_phase1b_2026-08-03.py, marker

STEP 1 · COLUMN FILE — CREATE AND MAINTAIN (write-only)
FILE: Documents/GroupTrack/map_slots.json, beside api_keys.json.
⛔ NOT map_sources.json — externalJsonFile() at :66 already claims that
name and it is the file 79251ae72 deliberately killed. Different name, different meaning.
CONTENTS: version_code, active, and three column rows —
{slot, legacy_key, source_id, short_label, url_template, requires_key, status}.
⚠ Stores the URL TEMPLATE, never a resolved URL. resolveUrl() at :277 injects
{key} at use time and keys persist separately. ⛔ Never the sources array — that is what made
79251ae72 necessary.
RULES, in precedence order:
(a) fallback ran → NO WRITE AT ALL, log and return — hardcoded data must never reach the user table by any route;
(b) unreadable → LOG AND STOP, no seed, no overwrite (unreadable ≠ absent; treating it as absent is the
create-if-missing shape that destroyed the spatial DB on 08-01);
(c) absent → SEED from defaultSlots + catalogue, stamp the version code;
(d) present, same version code → LOAD ONLY, no install pass;
(e) present, different version code → INSTALL PASS.
THE INSTALL PASS: refresh url_template per column from the catalogue by
source_id; mark status: "terminated" where the source is gone; re-stamp.
⛔ SLOT ASSIGNMENTS ARE NEVER TOUCHED — priorById wins over slot.sourceId. A release may
retire a source; it may not repoint a column the user chose. ⭐ The installer expires the source and stops.
Notification is somebody else's task (Fred).
PERSISTS: updateSlotSource() already called saveExternalJson() at
:221 — an empty body, now filled. setActive() also persists; the active key was in-memory only,
defaulting to "SAT" at :53. Atomic write, temp-then-rename.
⚠ DECISION OWED — what "terminated" means. The patch marks a column terminated when its
source_id is not found. Rule 3 calls for an explicit tombstone — a status field on the
catalogue entry so retired sources stay in the list and the sequence holds. Asset change plus one line here.
Absence works today only because nothing has been retired yet.
STEP 2 · THE APP READS THE COLUMN FILE
GOAL: nothing resolves from default_slots at run time once the user file exists.
defaultSlots becomes SEED-ONLY.

:163 getDownloadSources, :172 getSourceByKey, :187 getAllOverlayLayers,
:215 updateSlotSource, :273 getSlotAssignments — funnel through one mutable field.
You change where that field is loaded from; you do not convert the call sites. And
ConvoyConfig.TILE_SOURCES at :17-19 is already a computed property with no cache, so every
consumer inherits the fix automatically.
ALSO IN STEP 2 — RECONCILIATION ON INIT: walk the columns, check each source_id

STEP 3 · TEST A GOOGLE DOWNLOAD
GOAL: measure HYB against ground that has stopped moving. ⭐ Fred placed the test here
deliberately, before any download-shape work.
⭐⭐ DIAGNOSTIC EITHER WAY. Failure disappears → resolution was the cause. Failure persists →
resolution is eliminated for good and you are debugging a real download problem on solid ground. There is no outcome
that wastes the step.
INSTRUMENTATION DISCIPLINE: start the capture before queueing; remove
TRACK-DBG: TICK first (twice every 5 s, it destroyed the evidence last time); Log.d only — the
worker is off the main thread and a Toast there is the 08-01 failure again; nothing in an argument position.
⭐ Log the RESOLVED URL per job — that single line separates slot-resolution from a genuine download failure.
⛔ Remove it in the commit that closes the task.
DURABLE: put the failure cause in the queue entry, not only the log. "CORR SAT failed"
with no reason is what turned five minutes into an evening of reconstruction.
CANDIDATE MECHANISM (Fred, hypothesis): "esri would not work when the connection was
established with google." If the downloader holds a client for the Google host and the slot re-resolves mid-run to an
Esri template on a different host, in-flight requests aim at the wrong endpoint and fail silently. ⚠ Unknown whether the
downloader keeps a persistent client per host or builds per tile — per-tile would mean contamination rather than failure.
Both disappear once resolution is stable.

STEP 5 · REFRESH BECOMES AREA OR CORRIDOR — THE USER CHOOSES
GOAL: refresh asks which method at refresh time. ⛔ NOT a default the app applies — see
the correction below.
⛔⛔ CORRIDOR REFRESH MUST BE BUILT. IT DOES NOT EXIST. Fred: "the refresh does not currently
support corridor imports." This is BUILD, not MIGRATE — the 08-02 wording "reuses proven code" understates it
badly.
⭐ THE TRACK-LIST PICKER IS SHARED WITH STEP 4. Build it once for download, reuse it when
refresh asks.
REPLACE-IN-PLACE IS THE MODEL (Fred). A source change submits a refresh of the column store with
replace=yes at low priority, so current maps stay usable offline while they are being swapped.
INSERT OR REPLACE reuses pages — which is why the 08-02 signal was mtime advancing with size unchanged.
⚠ Convergence depends on the refresh COMPLETING. A half-swapped store has no record of which tiles are which, so
there is no way to resume intelligently. That is what makes "refresh must finish reliably" a correctness item, not
tidiness.
⚠ PRECONDITION ON SLOT REASSIGNMENT: queue on hold AND no active job on that column. Hold alone
is insufficient — it stops dispatch, not a worker already running. Block the reassignment, not the navigation —
opening Map Sources to look must stay safe; committing a change to a column with live work is what is refused, with the
reason named.
STEP 6 · ROUTE THE CHOICE TO THE RIGHT ENQUEUE
GOAL: enqueueArea or the corridor enqueue, submitting jobs for the changed source.
⚠ STILL OWED ALONGSIDE — gridCells → segmentCells ON THE AREA PATH.
⭐ The corridor worker re-derives its tiles at run time from track geometry, so it never builds oversized cells —
the migration is an AREA-path problem only. Area stays as an option, so it is still owed.
⚠ CHECK enqueueRefresh's ARGUMENT ORDER against enqueueArea — swapped
bounds remains the leading unverified hypothesis for the 07-23 continental incident, and the migration touches that call
site anyway.
⛔ THE ORDERING HAZARD — ensureInit() / loadFallback() (found 08-03)
WHAT IT IS: ensureInit() at :282-286 calls loadFallback()
when not initialized — and loadFallback() sets initialized = true at :147.
init() starts with if (initialized) return at :72.
⛔⛔ CONSEQUENCE: any getter firing before init(context) loads hardcoded Esri and
sets the flag — then the real init() returns immediately and never reads the asset. The whole process
runs on hardcoded Esri, announced by one Log.w nobody is watching for.
That looks exactly like the reported symptom: slot 1 back on Esri, no explanation. It is an ORDERING bug,
independent of persistence.
⭐ FRED'S CALL — do not remove it blind: "sounds like a trap … i am afraid of why it is
there." Phase 1 instead logs the request with a stack trace naming the caller and refuses to write the
column file at all when fallback ran. Nothing removed, nothing commented, no risk. If it fires, the caller names
itself. ⚠ Watch logcat for COLUMNFILE-2026-08-03: FALLBACK REQUESTED.
⚠ RESOLUTION IS LATE — the job carries a slot name, not a URL (proven 08-03)
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:706 writes putString("refresh_slot", …);
ConvoyCorridorWorker.kt:52 and ConvoyDownloadWorker.kt:39 read it back. The worker resolves
slot → source → URL at EXECUTION time.
⛔ THE DANGEROUS OUTCOME IS NOT FAILURE, IT IS QUIET SUCCESS. A slot that changes between queue
and execution silently redirects the download, and stores are keyed by the layer's cache_dir — so the wrong
tiles land in the store you believe holds the right ones. No error to notice.
⭐ THIS IS WHY THE COLUMN FILE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT MERELY CORRECT. With the mapping stable,
late resolution becomes correct rather than hazardous — the worker resolves the same column to the same source
whenever it runs, regardless of process or navigation.
⚠ THE VERIFICATION LOOP WAS THE CONTAMINATION LOOP (Fred 08-03)
Fred's method for confirming tiles were being replaced was to view offline maps of that column —
which required switching sources to flush the cache. Switching sources is what triggers the re-resolve. So
checking whether the swap was working is what broke the swap, and repeating the check repeated the damage.
⚠ UNTIL STEP 2 LANDS, VERIFY WITHOUT A SOURCE SWITCH. Store mtime advancing with size steady was
the clean signal on 08-02 — no UI interaction, no re-resolve.

⛔ THE LESSON OF THE WEEK — three-for-three
Every convoy rendering failure in this arc was instrumentation aborting a method before its real work:
?: return inside a toast argument killed onPageFinished — no tile setup, no persisted-frame
restore, no drawPersistedState
evaluateJavascript/Toast on a @JavascriptInterface background thread killed
onViewportChanged — no processViewport
The offline render failure, cleared by removing ten more toasts from the same file
All three landed in or around onPageFinished.
⚠⚠ Instrumentation is not free, and on this codebase it has cost more than the bugs it was added to
find. When adding a trace to an override or a bridge method, ask what happens if that line throws or returns.
⭐ The counter-example is today's tap fix: using instrumentation that ALREADY EXISTED found the
defect in three taps, with no new code and no build. Fred's call — "Why don't we use the existing instrumentation to
see what tap handler is executing?" Read the logs before adding to them. ⚠ Planner console tag is
MapJS; convoy's is ConvoyJS.
⚠ Also corrected today: a &lt;script src="…"&gt; tag NEVER executes its inline body.
grouptrack_map.html had an entire proximity scan inside one — dead since written, removed (lines 11–58).
⛔ This invalidates the standing "two proximity scans racing per tap" note — one was never executable.

⛔ IT WAS BUILT, THEN DELIBERATELY REMOVED — AND WHY MATTERS
git log -S "externalJsonFile" returns exactly two commits:
49bc8cecb — V2.5 Map Source Selection, "updated MapSourceManager with external JSON" — ADDED it
79251ae72 — 2026-05-21, "V2.5: Fix tile download — read asset JSON only" — REMOVED it
79251ae72 deleted both halves: the read-external-first-with-copy-on-first-run block in init
(including extFile.writeText(assetJson)), and the entire body of saveExternalJson() — replaced with
// Disabled — asset is single source of truth. ⚠ The empty function still exists and is still called,
silently doing nothing.
⭐⭐ WHY IT WAS REMOVED VINDICATES THE FIX. The external file held the ENTIRE CATALOGUE, URLs
included — saveExternalJson did root.put("default_slots", …) on a full copy of the catalog JSON.
So a stale external copy served stale URLs and broke tile downloads, which is exactly what that commit was fixing.
Ripping it out was a correct fix for a real bug.
⭐⭐ THE ARCHITECTURE (Fred 08-02) — TWO STRUCTURES, TWO FUNCTIONS
Fred: "There are two structures — the CATALOG which should be distributed, and the SLOT ASSIGNMENT of catalog to
user's map slot. Two separate functions."
CATALOG = map_sources.json in assets. Sources, url_templates, layers,
default_slots, catalog_version/schema_version. Distributed with the app,
read-only, replaced every release. ⭐ This is what makes a URL correction reach existing users — the {s}
fix lives in a template here. Had the catalogue been copied to user space on first run, no existing user would ever
receive it.
SLOT ASSIGNMENT = which catalog source_id occupies each user map slot, plus the
active slot. User-owned, persisted, survives reinstall. Fred: "The slot assignment is a JSON that should exist
in user space and be populated from default asset on install."
Why two structures rather than one copied file: a single copied file needs a merge on every
catalog_version bump — take new sources from the asset, preserve the user's slots. More code, more to go
wrong, same outcome. Separate structures never overlap, so there is nothing to merge and nothing to go stale.
⛔ Do NOT restore 49bc8cecb as-was — that reintroduces the stale-URL bug. Restore the
mechanism, but persist only {slot, source_id, legacy_key} plus the active key, never the sources array.
· ⚠ Seed-on-install needs a guard: seed only if the user file is ABSENT. Re-seeding on every install recreates
exactly the bug being fixed. · default_slots is named correctly and behaves as named — they ARE defaults;
the bug is that no user layer sits above them.
⭐⭐ 00-HYB (08-02) — GOOGLE HYBRID WAS NEVER DEAD. IT WAS A MISSING {s}.
FIXED + VERIFIED ON DEVICEHYB had been written off as a withdrawn service and was sitting in
this checklist as "DECIDE: disable behind a marked constant, or ship with a known-issue note."
That was wrong. It was two separate bugs with one root cause, and both are now fixed.
⭐ The URLs are NOT in Kotlin. ConvoyConfig.kt:15 — "TILE_SOURCES — reads from MapSourceManager
(map_sources.json)". That is why grep lyrs= across app/src returns NOTHING, and it sent two
people looking in the wrong place. Asset: app/src/main/assets/map_sources.json.
The two bugs
Template: https://mt{s}.google.com/vt/lyrs=y&amp;x={x}&amp;y={y}&amp;z={z}. Five sources use
{s}: google-hybrid, -satellite, -roads, -terrain, cartodb-voyager. Everything else (all Esri, USGS,
OpenTopoMap, OSM) uses literal hostnames — which is why only the Google sources looked dead.
BUG 1 — DOWNLOAD PATH. ConvoyTileDownloader.buildTileUrl substituted
{z}/{x}/{y} and nothing else. {s} was handled nowhere —
grep across all Kotlin returned zero hits. The literal string mt{s}.google.com went to DNS and every tile
failed silently. Fix (SUBDOMAIN-2026-08-02): .replace("{s}", (((tile.x + tile.y) % 4 + 4) % 4).toString())
as the first replace. Double-modulo guards negative x at antimeridian wrap; % 4 gives mt0–mt3.
BUG 2 — DISPLAY PATH. Leaflet DOES expand {s}, but its default subdomain set is
'abc' → it requested mta/mtb/mtc.google.com, which do not exist.
Neither map set a subdomains option. Fix (SUBDOMAINS-2026-08-02):
subdomains: (url.indexOf('google.com') !== -1 ? '0123' : 'abc') on the tile layer in BOTH
convoy_map.html (~:47) and grouptrack_map.html (~:111). Derived from the URL, not hardcoded —
Google needs 0123, Carto needs abc.
Verified: display logs TILE URL: https://mt{s}.google.com/... LABEL: SAT with no TILE ERROR after
it. Download: SAT.mbtiles mtime advanced with size unchanged (INSERT OR REPLACE reuses pages).
Offline: ConvoyIntercept: TILE mbtiles hit=true at z17/z18 — Google tiles rendering from the store.
⚠ The subdomains option is still missing on the OVERLAY layers
(convoy_map.html ~:71, grouptrack_map.html ~:138). Inert today; a subdomain'd overlay source
would fail the same way. · ⭐ METHOD: what settled this was curl-ing the endpoint by hand (200, image/jpeg,
29,722 bytes) — proving the service was alive BEFORE theorising about the app. Ten seconds. Do it first next time.
📊 MEASURED STORE SIZES — the 66% figure was wrong
StoreBytes

⭐⭐ Retiring both label stores saves 461 MB of 4.70 GB — about 9.8%, NOT 66%. The two-thirds figure
came from TILE COUNT; label tiles are mostly transparent and sparse, so they are two thirds of the count but a tenth of
the BYTES. This materially weakens the case for disabling WebP.
⚠ Google Hybrid tiles are DENSER than bare Esri imagery (roads + labels baked in), so SAT.mbtiles may
GROW as it is replaced. Re-measure after a completed run before deciding anything.
The real argument for HYB was never storage: one store instead of three, and street names without
MapLibre. SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT was the piece parked to 2.7 — HYB delivers it now. That is what could
move places-from-spatial OUT of 2.6e entirely rather than merely deferring it.
⚠ Google tiles are already JPEG. Re-encoding JPEG → WebP is generation loss on generation loss — an
argument for dropping WebP independent of the volume math. Possible future: WebP as a selectable DOWNLOAD option (not
per-map — stores are shared across both maps; and it leaves mixed encodings in a store, so confirm the reader handles
all formats).
⛔ SOURCE SELECTION DOES NOT PERSIST
OPENMapSourceManager.kt:53 — var activeSourceKey: String = "SAT".
In-memory ONLY. Written at :193, read by ConvoyConfig.ACTIVE_TILE_SOURCE (a getter).
There is NO read from disk anywhere.
The selection survives exactly as long as the process. Any force-stop, reinstall or background reclaim silently drops
the user back to the Esri default. Fred 08-02: "WE HAVE AN ISSUE WITH MAP SOURCE BEING RESET."
⚠⚠ This CONTAMINATES test results: if the source resets mid-download the job keeps writing into the same
store with the OTHER source's tiles. Any conclusion drawn from SAT.mbtiles after a reset is suspect.
Fix: persist on write, read in init. Small, but it is a behaviour change on a shared object — its
own patch, not bundled. ⚠ Distinguish SLOT ASSIGNMENT (applySource, probably persisted) from ACTIVE KEY.
⚠⚠ ESRI AND GOOGLE SHARE ONE SAT.mbtiles — SLOT-KEYED, NOT SOURCE-KEYED
Google Hybrid occupies the SAT slot (log reads LABEL: SAT while the URL is
mt{s}.google.com). Both sources write into the SAME file. Nothing in a stored tile records which source
produced it.
Consequences for the swap/prune design: (1) a source swap CONTAMINATES rather than replaces — refresh
only rewrites tiles in the refreshed geography at the covered zooms, so the store becomes a permanent Esri/Google
patchwork; (2) a clean volume comparison is impossible from a mixed file; (3) the prune is not just "drop the two label
stores" — the base store needs clearing before a swap, then refilling. MBTilesStore.deleteSource()
already exists and drops the whole file.
Fred's prune design stands otherwise: leave the overlay wiring intact, empty the label stores, and the
overlay draws nothing. No conditional logic, Esri stays selectable, stores refill on demand — so it is reversible.
Order matters: config first (drop from getDownloadSources()), THEN deleteSource(). Reversed,
the next download refills what you just emptied.
🔴 00-REFRESH (08-02) — REFRESH IS STILL ON THE BBOX MODEL AND THE OLD SEGMENTATION
Downloads cut over to corridors on 07-24. Refresh was never migrated — still bbox, and still on the old
gridCells instead of segmentCells. Same omission, two symptoms.
INCIDENT 08-02A map-source refresh enqueued 568 entries at 60–70K tiles each
(~37 million tiles — would never finish). The ≤50K ceiling was not applied because enqueueRefresh does not
use segmentCells. Not the 3,287-entry continental blowup of 07-23, but the same root path.
⛔ BBOX REFRESH JOBS RESET RATHER THAN COMPLETE — observed TWICE: a job at 5% went back to 4%, then
a second job reset the same way. Fred: "second job just reset again." This is DISTINCT from the known
refresh-never-completes stall, and it means a long run may never finish.
⭐⭐ DESIGN DECISION (Fred 08-02) — REFRESH GETS TWO METHODS
CORRIDOR IS THE DEFAULT. Route refresh through the track selection process — it reuses proven
code, kills the oversized-cell problem for free (the corridor worker re-derives tiles at run time), and matches what
refresh is actually for. Nobody refreshes a rectangle any more; they refresh the terrain they ride.
AREA REFRESH STAYS AS AN OPTION for users who downloaded areas. Same shape as the download side
(downloadType selects the worker, launchWorker dispatches).
AND the area path MUST move from gridCells to segmentCells. Keeping
the option means keeping enqueueRefresh, so the 60–70K-cell defect stays live for anyone who chose areas.
Corridor-by-default only reduces how often it is hit.
⭐ Suggestion: derive the offered methods from what is actually stored — corridors present → corridor refresh;
areas present → offer both. A user is then never given a button that cannot do anything.
⚠ A select-all-tracks refresh needs an estimate-and-confirm gate. The import path already does one
submitDownload per track with NO estimate and NO confirm — that is how 10 tracks became 215 jobs. ⛔ CAUSE CORRECTED 08-03 (Fred): the import path is not what did this. Refresh turned each track boundary into a bbox and enqueued area jobs — the bbox of a switchbacked trail covers the whole mountain while its corridor covers a line buffer. That difference IS the 215 jobs. Without a
gate, "refresh all tracks" becomes the new way to enqueue thousands of jobs by accident. · ⚠ Fix the completion plumbing
in BOTH workers — ConvoyCorridorWorker duplicates ConvoyDownloadWorker's, so the same miss can
exist independently. · ⚠ While migrating, compare enqueueRefresh's argument order against
enqueueArea — swapped bounds is the leading unverified hypothesis for the 07-23 continental incident, and
the migration touches that call site anyway.
⚠ A FAILED QUEUE JOB RECORDS NO REASON
08-02: a corridor job failed and the entry said only "CORR SAT failed" — no exception, no HTTP status, nothing
actionable. The cause was unrecoverable because TRACK-DBG: TICK (twice every 5 s) had already rolled it out
of the logcat ring buffer.
Fix: put the failure cause in the queue entry AND the log. Small change; the difference between five minutes
and another evening of reconstruction.
⚠ TRACK-DBG: TICK floods the buffer and actively destroys evidence. Add to the
pre-release removal list alongside WAYPOINT-TRACE.
To catch it next time, start the capture BEFORE queueing:
adb logcat -c then adb logcat | grep -viE "TRACK-DBG|DetailGate|NetworkStateTracker|WM-|chromium|ConvoyIntercept" &gt; /d/corr_run.txt
and leave it running.

⛔⛔ 00-DATA (08-01) — DATA LOSS EVENT: THE APP DESTROYED ITS OWN DATABASE. P0.
P0 BLOCKERAn adb install -r -d on Droid 2 cost the entire spatial database —
~89,000 trails plus every track, waypoint and route. The app did not report a failure. It logged
0 trails, 0 tracks, 0 waypoints, 0 routes and carried on as though that were a normal state.
This is not an adb problem. It is an application defect, and a Play Store update could
reproduce it on a user's device with no warning and no recovery.
⛔ The mechanism, in order
The install registered as a fresh install rather than an update (first-install questions appeared).
The app lost all-files authority; its SELinux category labels are assigned per-install.
SQLite's lock ioctl on the FUSE-mounted .db was denied — device log 11:44:04.805,
permissive=0, so enforced:
avc: denied { ioctl } for path=".../grouptrack_spatial.db" dev="fuse" ioctlcmd=0xf50c
scontext=u:r:untrusted_app:s0:c178,c256,c512,c768 tclass=file permissive=0 app=com.grouptrack.android
SpatialDbManager opens with create-if-missing. The failed open wrote empty schemas over the
existing files — same path, same names, replaced in place. Nothing called delete.
The app started clean and presented itself as empty.
Fingerprint sizes — memorise these: grouptrack_spatial.db = 118,784 bytes,
grouptrack_data.db = 208,896 bytes. Those are empty schemas. A live spatial DB is tens of MB.
🔴 THE FIX — 2.6e, outranks the panel work
Never open with create-if-missing when the target file exists. Check existence first; on a failed open
with a file present, surface an error and stop. This one change converts silent data loss into a
message.
Verify access BEHAVIOURALLY, not by permission API. The app believed it had all-files access while the OS
denied the ioctl. The permission query lied; a real read attempt would not have.
Fresh-install marker in filesDir — row counts, DB sizes, last-good timestamp. Private storage is
wiped by a fresh install; external storage is not. Marker absent + external DB present = a fresh install just
happened over existing data → stop, report.
Row-count sanity. A database that held 89 k trails yesterday reporting 0 today is not a valid state.
Belt and braces: copy to grouptrack_spatial.db.lastgood after each successful startup.
Fix the log line. SpatialDbMgr prints the LITERAL ${spatialFile.absolutePath} —
interpolation is broken, so the path never appears. That is the one diagnostic that would have made
this obvious in seconds.
⛔ OPERATIONAL RULES — effective immediately, supersede the standing convention
Install with plain -r. Never -d. Without -d, a regressed
version code makes the install fail with an error instead of silently downgrading. The failure is the warning.
First-install questions on an already-installed app → CANCEL. Do not proceed.
Fred: "11:41 was the first set of install questions. I should have pulled the plug then."
Ten-second post-install check:
adb shell ls -la /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/*.db — hundreds of KB instead of tens of MB means replaced.
The -r -d rule in the environment file is now superseded. The quickstart still
documents the old flag — see §05.
🔴 WHY THE INSTALL REGISTERED AS NEW — unresolved
versionCode is git-derived: gitVersionProvider.get().toInt() + vcOffset
(app/build.gradle.kts:65). A derived code that can regress, combined with -d, forces the
downgrade path — which resets app identity.
Two earlier installs the same day (08:32, 10:47 builds) were fine. The 11:41 one was not.
The dumpsys evidence for that specific install was overwritten by the 12:05 recovery install —
firstInstallTime and lastUpdateTime both read 12:05.
Signing key ruled out — same AAB key for three months, two successful installs the same day.
Next step: grep -rn "gitVersionProvider" --include=*.kts . — establish what it derives from and
whether it can decrease. Fix by pinning for local builds or bumping VERSION_CODE_OFFSET.
Single-build override: -Pandroid.injected.version.code=NNNNNNNN.
✅ RECOVERY — the good outcome, and a number worth keeping
Complete data-model reconstruction in UNDER ONE HOUR — OSM import, Utah state trails, tracks, waypoints.
GPX files in my_tracks/, tiles in maps/, OSM extracts in osm/ and the per-map JSONs
all survived; only the two .db files were replaced.
This materially lowers the stakes on §06 (delete-by-source) — a full rebuild is cheap, and the pipeline
was proven under real conditions rather than in theory.

⛔⛔ 00a-TRAP (08-01) — TWO SELF-INFLICTED BREAKS. Both killed convoy's entire artifact draw.
Convoy stopped drawing trails, tracks and waypoints twice during the session. Neither was a convoy bug.
Both were instrumentation aborting a method before its real work — and both were silent: no error, no JS
exception, no log.
⛔ TRAP 1 — ?: return inside an argument exits the whole function
android.widget.Toast.makeText(view?.context ?: return, ...)
Reads like a null-safe accessor. Is an early exit from the entire override. Placed in
onPageFinished, it bailed before tile setup, setTileUrl, the persisted-frame restore and
drawPersistedState. It also displaced the original val ctx = view?.context ?: return guard
into a position where failing it is catastrophic.
Never put ?: return in an argument position.
⛔⛔ TRAP 2 — @JavascriptInterface methods run on a BACKGROUND thread
evaluateJavascript and Toast.makeText both require the main thread and
throw when called off it — and the throw aborts the rest of the method, including the
processViewport call that draws every artifact.
webViewRef.value?.evaluateJavascript("window.__routeMode = false;", null)   // in onViewportChanged
android.widget.Toast.makeText(context, "ROUTE MODE OFF 
The existing code already knew this. It wraps its work in Thread { }, and
SpatialDisplayManager uses main.post { } for every evaluateJavascript.
RULE: anything touching the UI or the WebView inside a @JavascriptInterface method must go
through Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { }.
⚠ PROCESS — three lessons that cost real time
Prefer targeted removal over blanket revert when a file holds a day's work. A
git checkout &lt;baseline&gt; -- ConvoyScreen.kt was executed on the claim it "only costs toasts"; it also
took the reseed block. Restoring from the day's commit and deleting the three offending lines was available the
whole time and is what worked.
Cheap compile gate: ./gradlew compileGoogleReleaseKotlin — Kotlin front-end only, minutes rather
than 30–50. A patch script proves the anchor matched; only the compiler proves the code is valid. A
forward-reference error (a local fun at ~251 could not see a val declared at ~304) surfaced
at 4m26s into a full release build.
Build times 08-01: 44m, 35m, 26m, 17m, 11m. Incremental builds are far cheaper than the standing ~40m
assumption — a small fix does not cost a cold build.
Device is on Utah time, laptop on Eastern — logcat timestamps are DEVICE time. A two-hour
misread sent one diagnosis down the wrong path. · Long cat &gt; file &lt;&lt; 'PYEOF' heredocs containing
triple-quoted Python repeatedly mangle on paste in Git-Bash; python - &lt;&lt; 'PYEOF' with string
concatenation survives, sed -i survives best. · Use git --no-pager for diffs.

Save — session ends

🔴🔴 HIDE MUST MEAN ABSENT, NOT INVISIBLE (Fred, 07-31)
Fred: "hide keeps them from being placed on the map, not just invisible" and "the
behaviour we are looking for is focusing on artifacts we are displaying."
THE RULE: a hidden artifact type contributes NOTHING — not taps, not proximity, not snap, not
selection. Visibility IS the selection. What is on screen is what you are working with.
⚠ Observed defect that proves it
Trails OFF, tap a track on the planner, get a list of TRAIL names.
Cause: hideTrails() does map.removeLayer(trailLayer) and sets
trailsVisible = false — it does NOT null the variable. The proximity scan at
grouptrack_map.html:831 calls checkLayer(trailLayer, …), which skips a layer
only if it is null. So a detached-but-populated layer is still fully walkable, and hidden
trails contribute to the proximity list.
⚠ It also explains "occasionally the detail panel instead" — the scan is a MAP-level click handler
running alongside the track layer's own handler. Whichever resolves first wins the screen.
⚠ And the behaviour currently depends on HOW you turned it off: clearTrails() DOES
null the variable, hideTrails() does not.
The fix — and why NOT to null on hide
⛔ Do not null the layer on hide. The retained variable is a CACHE —
loadTrails rebuilds from a fresh GeoJSON payload, so nulling means a full query and
rebuild on every toggle. At 10,000 trails that is a visible cost.
⭐ Fix checkLayer to test visibility instead of null:
function checkLayer(layer, visible, typeName, color) {
  if (!layer || !visible) return;
Four call sites, both maps. Correct regardless of which path turned the type off.
⚠ AND CHECK SNAP — likely the same bug in a different place
RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) is fed from
queryTrailsByViewport / queryTracksByViewport — database queries, not
layers. Those know nothing about display state, so a route vertex can probably snap to a HIDDEN
trail. Under this rule it should not.
⚠ Not verified — ConvoyScreen.kt:596 builds the byId map from both
queries and I saw no visibility filter, but only read part of it. Check before assuming.
⚠⚠ ROUTE DRAWING IS BLOCKED AS OF 07-31 EOD — and canvas is not the cause
Before today: a tap was SHARED — you got a popup AND a vertex. Messy but usable.
After canvas: the artifact consumes the tap. No vertex lands. Route drawing does not
work.
⚠ Under SVG the artifact layer did not consume the event, so taps fell through to the map by
accident. Canvas did not break the suppression — it removed the accident that was masking it.
The mechanism has been broken since 43ab77e16 (07-03) either way.
⛔ Reverting canvas is the wrong trade (Fred: "more work to strip out today's changes than
to fix the route state"). It would restore a broken mechanism to a merely tolerable failure mode
while giving back the trail hit-rate fix — 3 hits in 40 taps at z18.
⛔ AND THERE IS NO WORKAROUND
Turning trails and tracks off lets the tap through — but then there is no snap and no
guidance. Tracks were removed from snap on 07-30 (snapTrailsOnly, because a track is
one geometry so snapping pulled the whole thing), and hidden trails are not in the query result. You
get free vertices only.
⭐⭐ SO THE FIX MUST DELIVER VISIBLE + SNAPPABLE + NON-INTERACTIVE SIMULTANEOUSLY. During a
route draw you need to SEE trails, SNAP to them, and NOT TAP them. Three concerns the code currently
collapses into one flag.
⚠ Which rules out the SVG approach. sub._path.style.pointerEvents — the line
43ab77e16 deleted — is an SVG DOM property, and canvas paths are not DOM elements. Under
canvas the mechanism is:
lyr.eachLayer(function(sub) { sub.options.interactive = !on; });
Stateless, survives layer rebuilds, works under canvas, and replaces the stash/restore block
entirely. ⚠ VERIFY THIS FIRST — it is the one unknown between the spec and the patch.
⭐⭐ THE SPECIFICATION (Fred, 07-31, verbatim intent)
ConceptMeansRule
Persistencestate RECREATION — position, zoom, artifact display states,
checked listsBoth maps write on every screen refresh. Puts the map back as you left it.
Route modeACTIVELY PLOTTING POINTS RIGHT NOW
⭐ FALSE ON EVERY MAP ENTRY, BOTH MAPS, UNCONDITIONALLY. Entered ONLY by choosing Add
Route. Never restored from persistence.
Draft filea route was not finished
Produces ONE MESSAGE on planner entry: "you have an unsaved route". That is all it does.
No arming, no geometry restore, no drawBuildLine.
routeState.opena session ended without terminating
An END-STATE write. Records only; never arms anything.
THE TAP RULE, entire:
Route mode OFF → tap opens artifacts (popup / detail panel)
Route mode ON → tap places a route point. Nothing else consumes it.
⭐⭐ THEREFORE POPUPS NEVER NEED SUPPRESSING. If the tap does not reach the artifact layer,
no popup can open. Every unbind, stash, restore and bind-gate in the codebase exists to solve a
problem that correct tap routing makes impossible.
THREE EXITS, one entry. Save · save in progress · discard. Each terminates route mode and
writes the end state. To save a recovered draft you go through Add Route like any other route — no
special-cased recovery path.
⚠ Route mode is an ACTIVITY, not restorable state. Fred: "a file on disk means you have
not finished a route. The state is actively plotting points." Two different things, and conflating
them is the whole mess.
⚠ Fred on why a boolean was not enough: "I have had continue messages with no in-flight
files." The flag claimed a state nothing verified — and setting it false does not undo what
setting it true DID (unbound popups, changed pointer events). Termination must REASSERT consequences,
not just write a value.
⛔ THE REGRESSION — commit 43ab77e16, 07-03
Titled "suppress artifact popups during route-build on both maps (unbind/rebind + bind-gate +
force-flag)". It replaced a working stateless mechanism with a broken stateful one:
- if (sub &amp;&amp; sub._path) sub._path.style.pointerEvents = on ? 'none' : '';
+ if (on)  { sub._savedPopupContent = sub.getPopup().getContent(); sub.unbindPopup(); }
+ else     { sub.bindPopup(sub._savedPopupContent); sub._savedPopupContent = null; }
⭐ The deleted line was correct. Stateless, nothing stashed, and it suppressed the TAP
rather than the popup — which is what let route-build taps fall through to the map. The function's own
surviving comment still describes that behaviour: "route their pointer events out so the tap falls
through to map.on('click') → Android.onMapTap (real coords)."
⚠ Why stash/restore cannot work: the viewport lazy-load rebuilds layers on every pan.
_savedPopupContent lives on layer objects that get replaced, so the stash is lost and
popups unbind PERMANENTLY. Observed 07-31: route mode off, popups still gone.
⚠⚠ AND THE GATES ARE INVERTED BETWEEN MAPS — Fred spotted this from behaviour alone:
Planner gates at BIND time (if (!window.__routeMode) layer.bindPopup(...)) —
so it does nothing to layers already drawn. Arming on a populated map has no effect. Ineffective on
the map that owns route mode.
Convoy guards at TAP time (if (window.__routeMode) return;) — always
effective. On the map that cannot create routes at all.

NOT STARTED · THE 2.6e DECISION08-01: design settled, nothing built. This is the release's actual purpose and it is the item that did not get touched.
Three checkboxes, one line, CHECKED = HIDES (matches the existing removeTilesChecked idiom rather than introducing a second polarity in the same panel):
☐ Esri places      ☐ Esri streets      ☐ OSM places
All unchecked = today's map. OSM places ships CHECKED by default so the new layer stays hidden — one polarity on the line, and the default is a persistence value rather than a design compromise.
Location: planner upload/download panel, first section, Map Controls.
Persistence: new keys in the per-map JSON via savePlanningState(), safe-load-with-defaults, no schema bump. Must go in the capture-and-reseed block in both screens, inside the lastMapProcessed gate. Write through the existing helper only.

It needs no build — the Esri toggles are existing stores — and it empirically inventories what SAT_LABELS_PLACES actually contains. If street names vanish too, the split is not clean in the stored mbtiles and the answer is no. That single observation may settle the tile decision before a line of code is written.
Sampling: three fixed area types — town (Esri densest), trailhead/junction cluster (navigational value), open backcountry (noise test). Same zoom, same viewport, screenshot each state. Weight gaps by navigational value, not count. No automation is possible — Esri labels are pixels baked into raster tiles, so the comparison is necessarily eyeball.
OSM side: add a Places TypeBinding to SpatialDisplayManager — it is already map-agnostic, so one binding serves both maps; only jsUpdate/jsShow/jsHide need to exist in both HTMLs. minZoom per binding gives fclass thinning a home — city/town/village first, locality last (2,846 of Utah's 3,674, the noisy class). Make the divIcons visually distinct from Esri labels so agreement and disagreement read differently.
⚠ Cross-state boundary caveat: OSM points import whole-state; tiles are corridor-scoped. A rider who imports Utah and rides into Nevada gets no OSM place labels across the line, where the Esri store would have covered wherever tiles were downloaded. reference_points holds Utah 7,723 / Arizona 9,324 and nothing renders them —

creation.

be hand-mirrored into both HTML files through the orphaned spatial_artifacts.js. They do
not. SpatialDisplayManager is already map-agnostic:
drawPersistedState(mapKey, webView, context) at :116 — takes the map key and
reads MapStateStore.readMap(mapKey)
TypeBinding registry at :31 carrying query / build /
jsUpdate / jsShow / jsHide / minZoom
bindingFor(type) at :41 — adding a type is adding a registry entry
DS_OFF / DS_ON / DS_SELECTED — the ON/OFF persistence pattern
already exists
So: add a Places TypeBinding and the Kotlin side serves both maps for free. Only the

🔴 04 — 2.6e RELEASE TASK: SNAP-2 APPLIES TO TRAILS ONLY
2.6e route planning only — NOT track recording
⭐⭐ Fred 07-29: "tracks can appear on map but snap2 should not be applied to tracks." Route planning snaps to trails only. Tracks keep rendering and stay tappable for details.
Two independent reasons it is right, not a workaround:
Coverage. Track-snapping existed because UGRC's 49,125 trails left real ground unreferenced. At 89,527 OSM trails that gap is largely closed.
lineId correctness. A snapped vertex stores lineId, and a track's lineId is per-rider — ten riders on one trail produce ten tracks with ten IDs. Snapping a route to a track never denoted shared geometry, so it was already wrong for the lead-cart contract.
⭐ SNAP-2 HAS TWO APPLICATIONS AND ONLY ONE CHANGES. Fred: "i am talking about route planning, not track recording. snap2 applies to each cart's track recording individually currently." The recording side snaps each cart's track ONTO trails — it consumes trails as targets, never tracks — so removing tracks from the target set cannot break it. ⚠ One track per cart per database currently.
Likely small: stop passing the track list to RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0). Snap eligibility separates cleanly from display and from tap-for-details.
⚠⚠ VERIFY: this AVOIDS the whole-line bug, it does not fix it. A recorded track is ONE continuous LineString while curated trail networks are pre-segmented — that is why dropping a point ingested the whole track and trails behaved. But Geofabrik ships OSM ways, and a long way is a long single LineString. Test route-drawing on one deliberately long OSM trail before concluding the symptom is gone.
⛔ Do NOT physically split stored tracks or trails. Changing geometry changes geom_hash → breaks dedup and orphans every lineId. If a fix is needed it is linear referencing in Kotlin: record the snapped POINT and its position along the line, never the line's whole geometry.

⚠⚠ THE FINDING THAT OUTRANKS THE REST — BOTH MAPS LOAD LEAFLET FROM THE INTERNET
Both map assets pull their core library from public CDNs:
convoy_map.html:7 and grouptrack_map.html:7 —
https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js
convoy_map.html:10 and grouptrack_map.html:10 —
https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/.../leaflet.draw.js
⭐ Line 8 on both is leaflet.polylineDecorator.js with no protocol — a local
asset. So the vendoring pattern already exists in these very files; two libraries simply did not follow it.
⚠ Fred reports all maps render offline today, so this is NOT confirmed as a live defect. The
likely benign explanation is shouldInterceptRequest — the app already intercepts
convoy://tiles/ and may also serve these URLs from assets, in which case the CDN strings are
addresses that are never fetched and there is nothing to fix.
Two commands settle it, no build:
ls app/src/main/assets/ | grep -i "\.js$"
grep -rn "unpkg\|cdnjs\|leaflet" app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/ --include=*.kt | grep -v "\.bak"
How to read it: local copy and an interception rule → working as designed, withdraw the
concern. Local copy but no interception → the local file is unused. No local copy → offline rendering is
riding the WebView cache, which survives normal use but not Clear Storage, not cache eviction, and is
not guaranteed across app updates. The equivalent field test is airplane mode after Clear Storage.
If it does need fixing: download both files into assets/ and change four
src attributes. No logic change, no version drift, and it removes a runtime dependency on two
third-party CDNs from an app whose purpose is working with no signal.

Rule: for anything JS-side, grep the assets. The xref is necessary and not sufficient.

🔵🔵 08 — RELEASE TARGET 2.7 — CONVOY TRACKING REWRITE + MapLibre / VECTOR RENDERING
4-WEEK FRAME (FRED) scoped, nothing built
PURPOSE
Rewrite convoy tracking — the originating requirement — on a renderer that can carry it. Fred: "2.7 is a rewrite of convoy tracking functionality — may be the point we need to introduce these discussions."
SCOPE — 2.7 owns all of this
1a Lead track replacement · 1b Lead cart lock ("In Progress (Not Yet Built)") · 1c Snap-2 on the lead cart track · 1d Vector rendering / MapLibre · 1e spatial_artifacts.js
2 Roads / street names — ingest only · 3 Reprocess / refresh driver · 4 Removals and edits (open, not decided)
⚠ Why this section exists: the convoy tracking rewrite was assigned to 2.7 in session more than two weeks ago and never reached AllDocs — 07-29 was spent reconstructing it from GroupTrack_LeadTrackReplacement_Spec.docx, the Lead Cart Lock section and MAP-06 instead of reading it.
⭐⭐⭐ THE SEQUENCING ARGUMENT (strongest point; survives any storage number)
The dominant cost is not MapLibre — it is operating on FROZEN CODE. ConvoyScreen.kt is frozen to protect the Kotlin↔JS↔Leaflet↔self-saving-setView↔shared-MapStateStore tangle. A convoy tracking rewrite must open exactly that tangle anyway. → The choice is not "rewrite convoy now, renderer later"; it is rewrite that layer ONCE with MapLibre as the target, or TWICE.
⭐⭐ THE onX BENCHMARK (Fred 07-30) — the structural case
onX is vector-based, does three presentations, allows the map to be changed, at ~¼ our storage. Our own device data agrees: the 07-26 delete log showed one SAT job walking three near-identical stores at z18 (SAT 10,295 · SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT 10,292 · SAT_LABELS_PLACES 10,294). Bar 10 post-corridor ≈ 107,000 raster tiles (SAT ~21,700 + transport ~21,700 + places ~21,700 + TOPO 21,000 + TOPO+ 21,000). Strip everything that is not photography → ~21,700, one fifth.
Vector is paid once and serves every presentation. One dataset restyled client-side gives satellite-with-labels, topo and road. Raster pays the full price per presentation — five stores today.
Switching maps becomes free — a consequence of the data being geometry rather than pictures. Not matchable with raster at any storage budget.
Vector stops at ~z14 and the client renders deeper. Since z15–18 is ~98% of raster tile count, vector does not shrink those levels — it removes them.
⭐⭐ DOWNLOAD TIME IS A RELIABILITY METRIC, not a storage complaint (Fred). "8 hours to download an area that will not be ridden." A long job fails partway, needs retry logic we know is imperfect, demands mains power, and gates ride-readiness. The yardstick is time-to-ride-ready and probability of completion. Every open queue defect is amplified by long jobs and materially reduced by short ones.
⛔ CORRECTION TO MY OWN ANALYSIS: I talked the saving down to ≈20% and let that stand as if it settled the question. It answers a narrower one — retiring one label store, on one corridor, in one presentation. The "whole-state road vectors don't shrink with corridor" objection holds for a single corridor in a single presentation and stops being decisive once amortised across three presentations and repeat rides in a region. I was defending a narrow reading of a number instead of testing the case.
⭐ What stays true regardless: satellite imagery is raster, permanently — roughly the ~21,700 floor. The saving is everything that is not photography.
🔴 THE GATE — WebGL on the cheapest field device (NOT YET RUN, half a day)
MapLibre GL JS requires WebGL in the WebView. The fleet includes $60 tablets, and one documented class already cannot hold a BLE connection. onX ships native rendering on modern phones; we would ship GL JS in a WebView on budget hardware. If WebGL will not perform there, this model is unavailable to us at any storage saving — and learning that during the rewrite is the expensive way.
TEST: load vector_label_prototype.html in a plain WebView on Droid 2 and on the cheapest tablet. Check WebGL context creation, pan/zoom at z16–18, frame rate, memory. No frozen code touched. Do this before 2.7 commits to MapLibre.
🔴 TWO MEASUREMENTS OUTSTANDING (seconds each, gpkgs already on D:)
How many gis_osm_roads_free rows carry a non-blank name (Arizona total 1,205,574; trails filter to 134,242 — named roads across all classes could be several hundred thousand, and road labels need LINE geometry for placement, so potentially 300 MB+ on a 108 MB skinny).
How many carry a non-blank ref. If named roads come back ~50k, extract now and never revisit. If ~500k, ref-only is likely the answer — forest/county road numbers (FR 123, CR 45) are worth more than street names for OHV and are renderable in Leaflet today as a midpoint divIcon.
⚠ The "revisit the data" cost is worse than a re-extract: C4 deletes the zip, so adding a layer to the catalog later means users re-download ~600 MB per state.
THE FIVE WORK ITEMS (renderer)
THE RENDERER. Leaflet cannot draw vector tiles → MapLibre GL JS in the same WebView. spatial_artifacts.js rewritten: L.polyline → GeoJSON sources + layer specs; per-feature click handlers → queryRenderedFeatures (MapLibre gives NO DOM per feature). The data path from SpatialDbManager is UNCHANGED.
TILE INTERCEPTION — MapLibre's addProtocol replaces the WebView request intercept; still serving bytes from MBTiles.
⚠ GLYPHS — easiest requirement to miss. MapLibre renders text from font PBFs fetched by URL. Offline means bundling them in assets. No equivalent exists in the raster world, so nothing in the pipeline handles it. Miss it and labels silently do not render offline.
MAP STATE — MapLibre's camera adds bearing and pitch; MapStateStore + the self-saving setView need rework. Nearest the frozen tangle.
GETTING LABEL TILES ON DEVICE — planetiler --only-layers=place,poi,transportation_name,water_name,mountain_peak over a state bbox = a labels-only tileset. Then a product decision: bundle it, or a "download this region" flow.
⚠ ONLY THEN drop the two overlay layers from SAT's entry in getDownloadSources(). One-line config change, but it MUST come LAST or satellite ships with no labels.
⭐⭐ THE CROSS-PLATFORM MULTIPLIER
The presentation layer is already web (Leaflet/HTML/JS in a WebView) and is the ~90% shared surface for iPad and PC; SwiftUI was rejected for presentation precisely because it gives zero reuse of it. MapLibre GL JS is a web library — identical in an Android WebView, an iPad WKWebView and a PC browser. A renderer swap is a one-time change the layer all three surfaces inherit. ⚠⚠ The corollary is a real risk: doing the tracking rewrite on Leaflet BAKES LEAFLET into the layer iPad and PC are both waiting on — a long-tailed decision made by omission.
✅ Validated in a browser prototype 07-26 (no build, no device, no frozen code)
Esri raster imagery + OSM vector labels composite correctly — "the image overlays look perfect."
⭐ OSM vector labels carry MORE data than Esri's downloaded roads/places layers — the opposite of the predicted outcome.
✅ 3D terrain works; Leaflet cannot do it at all. Terrain-RGB encodes metres above sea level in RGB, so the client holds raw elevation → slope-angle shading computed on device, arguably worth more than satellite imagery for an OHV app and a fraction of the cost.
⛔ OSM trail coverage is sparse at low zoom — OSM is a BASEMAP, not a trail source. ⚠ Minor ways only appear from ~z14, so any coverage comparison must be at z15+.
⛔ RULED OUT
Vector satellite imagery (cannot exist) · OSM as a trail authority · tiling user-authored artifacts (tiles are static; tracks are edited constantly) · doing this as a standalone 2.6 task.
Sources: SCOPING_v2.7_vector_rendering_2026-07-26.html · 07-26 Living Master V2.7 KICKOFF · GroupTrack_NewTick_Design_2026-07-01.md (tick/lead/identity rewrite) · GroupTrack_LeadTrackReplacement_Spec.docx · convoy_mapping_ipad_discussion.md (Mar 14) · Fred 07-30 (onX).
🆕 2.7 FEATURE — TRAIL GAP FILL FROM RIDDEN TRACKS (Fred 07-31)
THE PROBLEM, in Fred's words: "trying to draw a route using bits of a track you have
already ridden but trails still do not show."
Route building composes from trails. A stretch you have ridden but which the trail
collection does not cover exists only inside a track — and a track cannot be composed with,
because it is stored as ONE geometry. So when planning, you cannot see all your real choices even
though you have the ground truth on the device.
⭐ These are not a new class of artifact. Fred: "they are trails that simply do not
appear in that collection. you need a trail to ride." Same table, same rendering — the collection
is just missing a piece.
⭐⭐ DISPLAY FIRST, INSERT SECOND — the shape that makes it tractable
Fred: "may be simpler to have a function that shows the map with a colour segment that is
missing and can be added."
Show uncovered stretches as an overlay; the rider decides which become trails.
For tracks in view, compute which point runs have no trail within tolerance
Render those runs as a distinct overlay
Tap the track → artifact detail panel → Add Trail Segment
Only then does anything enter the trails table
⭐ This removes three problems at once, which is why it is better than automatic insertion
at import time:
Tolerance stops being critical. A false positive is visible noise the rider ignores, not a
duplicate trail silently written to the DB.
Naming resolves itself — the user is looking at it.
Nothing accumulates against dedup, and GPS wobble never becomes authoritative geometry by
accident.
⭐ And it is useful before the insert step is written at all. Simply SEEING where ridden
ground is missing from the collection answers the original frustration; adding it becomes optional.
Design detail settled 07-31
Detection. Sample the track's points; for each, test distance to trail geometry returned by
queryTrailsByViewport for a small bbox. Consecutive points with nothing within tolerance
form an uncovered run. Discard runs below a minimum length.
⭐ RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) already performs this proximity
test and returns null when nothing is near — "null" IS "uncovered", so detection is mostly
free.
Tolerance 20–30 m, matching the existing snap radius. ⚠ Too tight and GPS wobble alongside a
mapped trail reads as uncovered, producing a shadow trail parallel to a real one — that is the failure
mode to design against, and it is the argument for showing rather than auto-inserting.
Naming — Fred's rule: inherit the name ONLY if the trail either side of the gap carries the
same name. Both endpoints agreeing is strong evidence it is one trail; disagreeing means it
connects two, and inventing a name there would be wrong. Otherwise leave it unnamed.
⚠ Unnamed is correct, not a fallback. Fred: "most of our trails are unnamed now and named
would have a major trail connotation." A named trail SIGNALS significance to a rider, and today's
ORDER BY sorts named first — so auto-naming gap fills would both inflate that signal and
outrank real named trails at low zoom.
Colour. ⚠ Dashed is already taken — tracks are #39FF14 dashed, routes
#FF00FF dot-dash, trails carry carto_code colours. A solid line in an unused
colour will read more clearly than another dash pattern.
🔴 OPEN QUESTION — which gap, when a track has several
The detail panel opens for the WHOLE track, but uncovered stretches are specific sub-ranges. A
track with three gaps makes "Add Trail Segment" ambiguous — and that is exactly the case that
motivated this.
⭐ Fred's motivating case: several tracks named Broken Ridge in one area. From a
route-planning standpoint that is unusable, because you can only select whole tracks. Segmenting the
uncovered stretches makes it a set of distinct short pieces you can assemble — and "which Broken
Ridge" stops mattering, because you are choosing a STRETCH, not a name.
Likely resolution: the overlay lines are separate L.polyline objects, so each
can carry its own point-range identity and pass that through — rather than routing everything via
track_id alone.
⚠ Worth measuring before building
How much would this actually find? Utah now carries 89,536 OSM trails. If ridden tracks are
95% covered, this produces stubs and the effort is not repaid; at 40% it is a substantial feature.
⭐ Measurable PC-side in minutes against the spatial DB — sample a track's points, test
distance to trail geometry, report the uncovered fraction. No app code. And measure it on the
Broken Ridge area specifically, not statewide — that is the case that motivates it.
⚠ Depends on today's detail-panel work. The flow ends at "tap the track → panel → Add Trail
Segment", which only became possible once addPointMode stopped suppressing planner track
taps and __detailPanelEnabled was re-enabled. Both landed 07-31.

NEXT: read Complete Task List + StubbedProcesses + PickupGuide end to end and reconstruct the actual completion state — what is built, what is stubbed, what remains — as this block's content. Fred to state 3.0's PURPOSE in his own words; it is not inferred here.
Server-side function that belongs under a hosting release (NOT a release title)
Same-ride track dedup — pruning duplicate recordings when tracks are served. ⚠ This is a HOSTING problem and only exists once tracks are served. Locally, ten riders each holding their own recording of one ride is CORRECT.
⛔ geom_hash cannot do this job. Perfect for trails (89,536 rows / 89,536 hashes; the 313 UT/AZ border trails collapsing automatically prove it). Useless for tracks from one ride: ten devices drop GPS points at different moments → ten point sets, ten hashes, all legitimately the same ride.
⭐ COLLAPSE FOR PRESENTATION, DO NOT DELETE. Canonical track per hash, hash + date → alias. Nobody loses their own ride and the collapse stays reversible. Server-side, not on the phone. Scope is bounded (same bbox + date window). Goal is "prune as best we can", not perfect matching.
Candidate metrics (none chosen): bbox overlap + Hausdorff/Fréchet · rounded/simplified-geometry hash · start/stop coordinates + time window (Fred 07-29, cheaper than either) ⚠ needs tolerance on both axes.
⭐ CROSS-REFERENCE, not scope: 2.7's snap-2 makes recorded tracks converge on shared trail geometry, so part of this becomes hash-matchable outright. That work belongs to 2.7.
⚠ Two riders on the same ground can store different lineIds. For DRAWING it does not matter; it matters only when two routes are COMPARED. Fix at compare time by geometry proximity, never by making snap pick differently.
