⭐⭐⭐ WHY IT COLLAPSED FROM A REFACTOR TO THREE SMALL COMMITS
CREATE TABLE routes (... geom_hash TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(geom_hash))
geom_hash is CONTENT-ADDRESSED and UNIQUE in BOTH tables, and
insertRoute already computes it. The same hash therefore means the same geometry
wherever it is stored, so a corridor derived from either table is identical.
⭐ That removed all of it: no artifact-type parameter, no new
QueueEntry field, no inputData change, no worker change, and no
serialisation risk to a queue already persisted on devices.
⚠ The 07-27 note in section 17 had this right all along — "the blocker dissolved on
inspection: the routes table already carries geom_hash." The 08-06 note claiming otherwise was
WRONG and drove a far larger design. ⭐⭐ CHECK THE SCHEMA BEFORE DESIGNING AROUND A DATA
MODEL. One query would have saved the detour.
⚠ A FOURTH track-only lookup surfaced only on inspection: the SAVE MAPS lambda calls
getTrackBbox BEFORE the pipeline is reached, so a route would have failed at the very
first step and been told it had no geometry. ⚠ Two call sites, and each file ALSO has an
onDownloadMaps (AREA) lambda with an identical bbox line that must stay tracks-only —
a bare-line anchor would have patched the wrong one.
⛔ insertRoute DEFECT, real now that UNIQUE is confirmed:
newId() → INSERT OR IGNORE → return id. On duplicate
geometry nothing inserts and a fabricated id is returned. Blocks reliable GPX route
import; the panel path does not need it. Fix: read back the surviving route_id by
geom_hash.
⭐ ZOOM CAP — SAT z18, RENDERED z16, DOWNLOAD AND DISPLAY
490096e49 (ZOOMSLOT-2026-08-10D, corridor downloads) +
151febe07 (both HTML maps).
⭐ KEYED ON THE SLOT, NOT THE SOURCE. Every download path already carries the
slot — enqueueCorridor takes slotName, the worker reads
refresh_slot, the area path carries selectedSlots. None carry the source:
corridorTiles had no source parameter at all. So the slot needs no new plumbing,
and it publishes as one sentence a rider can understand instead of a table of vendor ceilings.
Fred&rsquo;s economics: each level quadruples the tile count. Satellite is upscaled rather
than sharper above z18 in open country; a topo map has said everything it has by z16. "most data
in the least space."
⛔⛔ THE CAP IS OPT-IN AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. ConvoyCorridorDelete calls the
same corridorTiles. A capped delete computes a SMALLER set than an older build stored,
leaving z17-z18 tiles that nothing can ever find or remove on a multi-gigabyte store. Empty
slot = no cap; only the two DOWNLOAD paths pass one, and the patch VERIFIES the delete path did not
gain one.
⚠ STILL UNCAPPED: the AREA path — calculateTiles has a
sourceName parameter that NOTHING passes, so its cap never fires; nine call
sites would need the slot. And quickEstimate has no slot either, so the live preview
overstates against a capped download.
⭐ Display uses maxNativeZoom, so zoom CONTINUES past the cap and upscales
rather than stopping. That is the better behaviour: artifact overlays stay sharp at any zoom, so a
rider can still place a waypoint precisely over a soft basemap. ⚠ Cost: pre-cap z17-18 topo tiles
stop being drawn. They are not deleted and cost nothing; they age out at the next source change.
⚠ setMaxOfflineZoom/maxOfflineZoom is an INDICATOR, not a
ceiling — its body writes a text element and never touches currentMaxNative. It is
fed by a scan for z-named DIRECTORIES, a layout MBTiles replaced, so it likely reports nothing now.
Separate cleanup.
⛔⛔ THE ROTATION BUG — A TESTER LOST A RUNNING MIGRATION
MainActivity declared NO configChanges, so Android destroyed and recreated it
on rotation — taking the composable, its state, and the coroutine scope the corridor delete runs
on. A tester rotated their phone mid-delete and the panel vanished with no way to tell whether
the work was still running.
FIXED 15e1acebf (ROTATE-2026-08-10F):
configChanges="orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|keyboardHidden".
Fred: "just leave the screen open unless an action is taken to end it. period."
⭐ Chosen over rememberSaveable deliberately: saving state would rebuild the
panel with the right numbers, but the coroutine would still have been cancelled — it would look
alive while doing nothing, which is worse than a blank screen. Keeping the activity is what
keeps the WORK.
⚠ NOT a full fix — a swipe-away or a kill still ends it. Moving the delete off the UI
scope remains the real answer. ⚠ Watch for orientation-qualified resources no longer reloading.
⛔ WHAT THE TESTER'S RUN EXPOSED — TWO DEFECTS BEYOND THE ROTATION
1 — STRANDED: the delete completed, the submit never ran. Corridors removed,
queue EMPTY, coverage gone, and no indication anything was wrong. The code already warns
about this shape: "killing the process mid-run strands the user with removed coverage and
nothing scheduled to rebuild it."
⭐ Recovery is a re-run — already-deleted corridors skip at ~0.4 s each, so it moves through and
reaches the submit. ⚠ But the app cannot DETECT this state. A check on launch for "coverage
removed, nothing scheduled" would turn a confusing hour into a prompt.
⛔ 2 — A SUCCESSFUL DELETE WAS RECORDED AS FAILED. The first pass logged
failures; the second pass popped through in seconds, which is the signature of nothing left to
delete. The tiles came off and the record said otherwise. The delete and
recordCompletedDelete are not atomic, so a failure in the RECORD is indistinguishable
from a failure to DELETE.
⚠ This is what made an hour of diagnosis necessary — and on a destructive operation it is
worse than cosmetic: a user either re-runs needlessly, or believes their data survived when it did
not.
⭐⭐ THE DELETE IS DEVICE-BOUND, NOT CODE-BOUND — SETTLED FOR GOOD
Samsung tablet: 99 tracks in 15 SECONDS. Droid 2: ~1.8 hours. Same build.
⛔ Every hypothesis chased on 08-09 was looking for a defect in code that runs hundreds of
times faster on ordinary hardware. Seven died; the answer was that Droid 2 has slow storage.
⛔ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DOCS: the panel copy saying "a few hours" is calibrated to the slowest
device owned and will alarm everyone else. Say it depends on the device and how much is held,
and let the progress meter carry the rest. No duration claim.

⭐⭐ THE ETA WAS TWO CALCULATIONS THAT DISAGREED BY 6x
The panel displayed 37.2 tiles/sec and "3 hours" for 69,000 tiles. 69,000 ÷ 37.2 is
31 minutes; a 3-hour ETA implies ~6.4 tiles/sec — a sixth of the number on the same screen.
estimateRemaining() ignored the displayed rate and computed its own from all tiles
ever completed over elapsed-since-the-earliest-job. ⛔ Its firstStart block fell back to
createdAt — QUEUE TIME — for completed entries, so hours of waiting before the
first tile downloaded counted as elapsed. Its own comment says createdAt is queue time and that
this is what made the estimates unusable. The code then used it.
⚠ It was asymmetric too: the denominator reached back to the first job QUEUED while the numerator
only counted entries still present — so clearing completed rows shrank one side and not the
other.
⭐ FIX (Fred): one rate. liveRate() extracted as the single
definition; the display and the estimate divide by the same value. 22 lines deleted.
If the panel says 37 tiles/sec and 69,000 remain, the estimate is 31 minutes — the arithmetic the
user can do in their head.
⚠ STILL TO BUILD (Fred's spec): first sample at 5 minutes, recalc hourly from the
last hour, tiles as the unit — so a rate step is followed rather than averaged away.
⚠ Tolerance: "an estimate of 6 days is not going to be managed to the minute. but it shouldn't go
to 12 or 2."
THE CORRIDOR DELETE — SETTLED. NOT A DEFECT.
~95-100 tiles/sec, linear with tile count. 88 of 88 completed.
⛔⛔ SEVEN HYPOTHESES, ALL DEAD: missing transaction (already one, 500
rows/statement) · missing index (already exists) · O(n²) re-derivation (the preview did 88 tracks in
40 s) · concurrent deletes (one SQLite writer per file) · delete the union (re-deleting absent rows
costs 0.4 s) · drop/rebuild the index (it is the only way to find rows) ·
the pragmas (applied and confirmed on device, NO EFFECT).
⭐⭐ THE ANSWER: IT IS NOT SLOW. Deletes run ~100 tiles/sec; downloads run
20-62. The delete is faster per tile than the download. And before MBTiles there was no
removal option at all — testers factory-reset their devices. Two hours unattended replaced
days of manual work or a wipe.
⚠ THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON, by accident: tracks deleted in the morning were re-visited at
night and returned tiles=0 in 0.4 s. Bar 10 overnighter: 189 s with rows, 0.4 s
without. Same corridor, same statements. The cost is the physical row removal, nothing
else.

generalised.
⭐ It dissolves the delete ordering constraint — area scope currently must be inferred

replaced.
⛔ execSQL REJECTS ANY STATEMENT THAT RETURNS A ROW. Two of three pragmas
used it, the first threw, and the shared try took the other two down with it — so the
pragma hypothesis went a whole build cycle untested. ⭐ Separate try per pragma, and log what
SQLite actually reports back.

SWALLOWED THE BUILD — Gradle printed its help banner and reported BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 14 s with
no APK. Run builds on their own line.

e.createdAt) created by an unquoted &gt; in a grep pattern.

⛔⛔ 00-INCIDENT (08-08) — THE UNRECOVERABLE QUEUE. SPATIAL DB LOST ON DROID 2.
WHAT HAPPENED, IN ORDER
Option 2 was run with corridors selected. The delete never executed —
optTracks was false at the confirm handler although the box appeared ticked.
Corridor tiles therefore stayed on disk. The area pass read them as area coverage and
queued 172 jobs to re-download that ground as rectangles.
The panel stayed up: refreshEnqueued was only set at the END of the coroutine, so
nothing dismissed it.
Queue entries were cleared while WorkManager still held the jobs. Workers take every parameter
from inputData and never consult the queue, so they kept starting — running
20 minutes at 0 tiles, with no failure.
The panel returns early when the queue is empty, so RELEASE and CANCEL were not on
screen. Force-stop did not help: WorkManager exists to survive process death and rescheduled
them.
The only exit was clearing app data. The spatial DB went with it.
⭐ THE COST OF NOT DELETING, MEASURED: 30 tracks swept up as areas cost
2M+ tiles on ONE source. 89 tracks as proper corridors cost 1.5M across THREE.
Corridors were designed for a ~90% reduction and that holds. The delete is not space
reclamation — it is what stops corridor ground being re-covered as boxes.
WHAT WAS FIXED (all in c5fc7985b and d92e472fb)
Orphan block. Both workers look their entry up immediately after init. No
entry, no work. ⚠ Returns failure, not success — an orphan reporting success writes a lie
into the log, and failure() is terminal where retry() would resurrect it
on backoff. ⚠ Deliberately does NOT call markFailed: there is no entry to mark, and
writing one would trade a running ghost for a permanent row.
Held-queue escape. The panel now computes qoHeld from
isQueuePaused() and both early returns respect it. A held queue renders even with zero
entries, showing QUEUE HELD — nothing will start with RELEASE, and
CANCEL WORKERS whenever held or empty.
Always exitable. The migration run sets its terminal state in a finally, so
a throw cannot strand the panel.
Step 0 records what the handler received — tracks=$optTracks areas=$optAreas
to the log AND the first on-screen line. ⚠ THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO READ ON THE NEXT RUN.
If it disagrees with what was ticked, the original defect is still live and it is visible in one
second rather than twenty minutes.

🔴 00-ESTIMATOR (08-08) — WAS 8-10x LONG. REWRITTEN.
MEASURED: the panel said Aug 12 5 AM (~86 hours) for 1.5M remaining tiles. The real
rate was ~140,000/hour — about 10 hours.
Two defects compounded:
The rate came from ONE entry's elapsed time, which is a per-slot rate, while 3-4 slots
run concurrently.
Averaging the last two entries does not fix it — if those two ran concurrently their
windows overlap, so the average is still a slot rate.
⚠ And createdAt is queue time, not start time. A job that waited behind 87
others carried hours of waiting in its elapsed. That alone was worth an order of magnitude.
⭐ REPLACED WITH FRED'S FORMULATION (08-08): total tiles completed since the run
began, divided by elapsed wall-clock since the earliest job started. That IS the aggregate rate
by construction. Concurrency cannot fool it, it absorbs stalls, holds and slot changes, and it
needs no MAX_CONCURRENT multiplier — every failure mode above disappears rather than
being corrected for. It is also the same arithmetic the yardstick ledger does across sessions, so
the two finally agree.
Supporting work: startedAt stamped at dispatch, tilesPerSec computed at
completion and stored on the entry (Fred: "the job knows duration and tiles — that is where the
calc belongs"), both persisted and backward-compatible on read.
⚠ LAYER COUNT — ONE ENQUEUE PATH WAS WRONG
enqueueArea's UNSEGMENTED path summed layers across every download source
(its own log line said layerCountAllSlots, slot=ALL). Under Esri that
summed to 3 and happened to match what one Esri download wrote, so it looked correct. Under Google
Hybrid one layer is written and the estimate stayed at 3x.
MEASURED 08-08: a job estimated 19,000 and finished at 6,463 — 2.94x.
⭐ Every other enqueue path (:257, :279, :612) already
filtered by slot. Only the unsegmented one was missed. ⚠ Fixed by filtering to the SAT slot, NOT by
removing the multiplier — a slot back on Esri must still count its 3 layers.

🟢 00-CORRIDOR-DELETE (08-07 built, 08-09 A-01 CERTIFIED + PERFORMANCE DIAGNOSED) — CORRIDOR DELETE
⭐⭐ 08-09 — A-01 PASSED. THE 08-08 DATA-LOSS DEFECT IS FIXED.
Build d92e472fb installed on Droid 2, option 2 with BOTH boxes ticked.
Step 0 logged:

The checkbox state reached the handler correctly. On 08-08 optTracks was

the area pass read them as area coverage and queued 172 jobs. That is the failure that ended in
the lost spatial DB, and it is closed.
The delete then ran for real: preview done: 88 tracks, 633050 distinct tiles, 472129
shared, ON DISK=633050 across 1 store(s) {SAT=633050} → delete start: 88 tracks.
⚠ 08-09 — TWO UI DEFECTS FOUND BY RUNNING IT
NO PROGRESS METER ON SCREEN. The design specified "Removing corridor map N of M" with a
moving bar. onProgress fires per track and the log records each one, so the data
exists — it is not reaching the UI. On a multi-minute irreversible operation that is not
cosmetic: it is why Fred tapped CONTINUE twice, believing the first tap had not registered.
CONTINUE IS NOT GUARDED AGAINST A SECOND TAP. Two taps six seconds apart launched two
preview threads (16315 and 16202). Harmless this time — one preview was discarded and only one
reached delete start — but two DELETES racing would not be harmless.
⭐ Fix: disable CONTINUE on first tap, or render the step list immediately so the tap is visibly
acknowledged.
⛔⛔ 08-09 — THE DELETE IS ~30x TOO SLOW. FIVE CAUSES RULED OUT BY READING THE CODE.
MEASURED, per-track, from logcat:

⭐ Cost is PER-TILE and LINEAR — ~98 tiles/sec. The 591-tile track took 5 seconds, exactly
proportional, so there is no fixed per-track setup cost. Full run ≈ 633,050 ÷ 98 ≈ 1.8 hours.
⛔⛔ FIVE HYPOTHESES WERE PROPOSED AND THE CODE CONTRADICTED EVERY ONE. Recorded
so none of them is re-proposed:
ProposedWhy it is wrong
Per-tile transaction / missing transaction wrapper
deleteTiles ALREADY wraps one beginTransaction() and batches
500 rows per statement, grouped by (z,x). MBTilesStore:317-340
Missing index on the tiles table
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS tile_index ALREADY exists and runs on every
open. MBTilesStore:94
O(n²) shared-tile re-derivation across 88 tracks
The PREVIEW did all 88 tracks in 40 seconds (10:51:34 → 10:52:14) doing the same
getTrackPoints + corridorTiles per track. Derivation is not the cost.
Run the deletes concurrently
One SQLite file, one writer at a time — parallel threads queue at the DB level. And with
all 88 corridors going, there is no shared-tile hazard to guard: every tile goes regardless.
Batch the deletes / fewer larger transactions
Already batched. See row 1.
⭐⭐ WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY SHOWED: NO PRAGMAS ARE SET ANYWHERE IN
MBTilesStore. Only two read-only reporting queries at :359-360
(freelist_count, page_size). Every store runs on Android defaults —
and Android ships secure_delete ON, which overwrites freed content with zeros
rather than marking pages free.
THE ARITHMETIC FITS: 14.4 GB across ~633,000 tiles ≈ 23 KB per tile. Deleting
21,852 tiles frees ~500 MB of page data; 500 MB in 189 s ≈ 2.6 MB/s. That is disk write
throughput, not query cost.
⭐ THE FIX — TWO PER-CONNECTION PRAGMAS (MBPRAGMA-2026-08-09C, written, not built)
d.execSQL("PRAGMA secure_delete=OFF")      // stop zeroing freed tile blobs
d.execSQL("PRAGMA journal_mode=TRUNCATE")  // truncate the journal, don't recreate it
Anchored in ensureSchema(), which runs on EVERY open
(MBTilesStore.db() :64) — not only on creation.
⭐⭐ WHY THERE IS NO DISTRIBUTION PROBLEM — the question Fred raised. Both are
PER-CONNECTION: they are not stored in the database file, they apply fresh at each open, and
they touch nothing already written. No migration, no upgrade path, no user action, no setup
value. Ship the build and every existing store gets the behaviour on its next open.
⚠ Why ensureSchema and not inside the delete function. The delete WOULD work
— the handle is cached (handles[type]) so one pragma would hold for all 88 tracks.
But (a) tile WRITES pay the same cost — INSERT OR REPLACE over an existing tile
frees the old blob and secure_delete zeroes it, which is every Replace-mode refresh
across the whole store; and (b) a pragma inside one function is a fact about that function, where in
ensureSchema it is a fact about the store and the next code path inherits it.
⛔⛔ DO NOT "IMPROVE" THIS TO journal_mode=MEMORY, OFF, OR WAL.
MEMORY and OFF leave a CORRUPT DATABASE if a write is interrupted. WAL is persistent,
changes the file format and adds -wal/-shm companions — that one WOULD
need a migration, which is the real answer to "why not do it in the refresh process."
⚠ These stores are ~14 GB with NO BACKUP, and a database the framework considers corrupt can
be DELETED by the default error handler (see 00-REFUSE). Crash-safety is not
tradeable here for delete speed.
⚠ MEASURING IT: force-stop first so the cached handles close and stores reopen with the
new settings. Baseline to beat: 21,852 tiles in 189 s · 9,427 in 116 s · 591 in 5 s ≈ 98
tiles/sec. The patch logs SQLite's actual answer, so logcat shows whether it took.
⚠ SEPARATE, STILL AVAILABLE: 472,129 of the 633,050 tiles are SHARED between
corridors, and the loop deletes PER TRACK — so a tile in five corridors gets five DELETE statements,
four of them no-ops. The preview already computes the distinct union. One pass over it would
remove that redundancy. Cost: the per-track "N of M" progress reporting would need chunking instead.

⛔⛔ SIX SUCCESSIVE MECHANISMS WERE PROPOSED FOR THIS ONE PERFORMANCE PROBLEM, AND
FIVE WERE CONTRADICTED BY CODE THAT COULD HAVE BEEN READ FIRST. The same pattern ran earlier in
the day on the All-Files defect (six mechanisms, each corrected by Fred against observed device
behaviour, ended by ONE grep finding ConvoyScreen.kt:145) and again on the z10 ANR

⭐⭐ THE RULE: READ THE FUNCTION BEFORE PROPOSING A MECHANISM FOR IT. Every one of these
was settled by a single grep or sed -n, and in each case the reading took under a

⭐⭐⭐ 00-MIGRATION-V2 (08-07) — THE REDESIGN. SUPERSEDES 00-MIGRATION BELOW.
⭐⭐⭐ THE FRAMING THAT CHANGES EVERYTHING (Fred 08-07)
"This is a trail riding decision. Google maps is available ONLINE in either map as
soon as the change in map sources is made."
⛔ The migration is about OFFLINE STORED TILES ONLY. Online rendering switches the
instant the slot is reassigned — nothing to migrate, nothing to wait for. Everything below
concerns only what is already on disk.
⛔ AND THE ARITHMETIC THAT KILLS THE ORIGINAL DESIGN
Fred: "Refreshing 50-60 GB of data is just not an option."
617,005 tiles is one device's SAT store. A full store refresh is DAYS. There is no
automated flow that makes "re-download everything you own" reasonable. The original
00-MIGRATION option 2 — mandatory delete then full rebuild — cannot be offered at real scale.
⚠ AND THE DELETE MAY BUY LESS THAN WE THOUGHT (Fred 08-07, unresolved)
The delete existed to stop corridor tiles being swept into the area refresh as rectangles.
But Fred's observation stands and is not yet disproven: the area refresh box already
covers overlapping corridor tiles, and where a corridor runs outside any area, the corridor
requeue puts those tiles back. Between the two, everything gets refreshed anyway — the
delete may only make tiles come back twice.
⭐ THE ONE THING IT DOES BUY: the store's derived extent shrinks when corridors go, so
the area refresh covers less blank ground between corridors. Real for a
predominantly-corridor map, but smaller than the original framing claimed.
⚠ OPEN — SETTLES THIS IN FIVE MINUTES: read tileBoundsLatLon(slotName) in
ConvoyTileDownloader. Single min/max box over every tile → corridors at the edges
stretch it, delete helps. Segmented/per-zoom following actual coverage → the blank space was
never covered and the delete buys much less.
⭐ THE OPTIONS AS FRED SETTLED THEM 08-07
#OptionForWhat runs
1Clear and start overlight coverage, few tracks; or anyone who
does not want to think about it or fears getting it wrongclear the column, rebuild what
you need. Cannot leave you half-converted.
2Refresh — corridors and areas, each optional
no tracks → areas only · heavy in both → tick both, "click a button and come back in two
days"Replace ON, delete OPTIONAL (default off)
3Leave my maps in place, replace at my leisure — with the option of
track processing immediatelyheavy trackscorridors refreshed IN PLACE, no
delete, areas skipped entirely
⭐⭐ AREAS STAY ON ORIGINAL MAP DATA UNTIL REFRESHED. Nothing goes blank, nothing is
deleted. The only degradation is that Esri's label overlays are gone once the column moves off
Esri — the base imagery stays. That is what makes option 3 safe rather than merely deferred.
⭐ WHY THE DELETE BECAME OPTIONAL: Replace overwrites in place, so the delete is not
needed for correctness — only for reclaiming space. Default off. With it off the whole
operation is ADDITIVE: no irreversible step, no point of no return, no permanent gate. The
gate appears only if the user opts in.
⭐ USERS ARE ONE OR THE OTHER (Fred, from experience): a corridor-based map has few
areas; an area-based map has few tracks. Two independent checkboxes let the user say which rather
than the panel guessing.
⭐ THE SCAN IS WHAT LETS SOMEONE CHOOSE. "This many track tiles, this many area cells"
turns an abstract decision into an arithmetic one. Someone with 50-60 GB reads the number and
takes option 3. That is the scan's real job — not verifying the delete.
⚠ WITH 5 TRACKS THE DISTINCTION STOPS MATTERING — box them, accept a few more tiles.
The failure mode is benign, so the design only has to be careful for the heavily-invested case.
WHAT TODAY’S CODE BECOMES UNDER THE REDESIGN
"Remove Tiles by Track" — stands alone as a downloads-menu feature, the by-track
counterpart to Remove Tiles by Area. ⚠ Its gate text must NOT promise a rebuild: delete-only
means coverage is gone until re-downloaded by track.
Corridor refresh (Replace on, no delete) — one call,
enqueueCorridorBatch(hashes, listOf("SAT"), replaceExisting = true), production code
already. ⭐ Needs to be reachable OUTSIDE the migration flow: option 3 + immediate corridor
refresh is the path most heavy-track users will take.
Preview / on-disk counting / roll-up / progress meter — all reusable, all serve the
optional-delete path.
⚠ VERIFY BEFORE RELYING ON IT: enqueueCorridor passes
refreshMode = replaceExisting, and that flag is OVERLOADED (isRefreshCell vs
replaceTiles — the markComplete bug came from exactly that conflation).
Corridor + Replace may never have been exercised together.
⚠ PERFORMANCE — INVESTIGATED, THEN DELIBERATELY DROPPED
Fred: "I could spend a month on this and it will be run once." Correct call —
recorded so it is not re-opened.
~25 min for 88 tracks. Five theories were floated (recompute · SQL · transaction-per-track ·
index traversal · cross-track duplicates) and NONE were measured. The benchmark is free and
still available: adb logcat -d | grep "deleteTiles SAT" — consecutive timestamps give
per-track duration, and each line carries its tile count. Flat ~7s/track regardless of size →
fsync/transaction overhead. Scales with tile count → statement volume.
Evidence found but not acted on: the default rollback journal does at least two disk
writes per transaction plus an fsync — 88 transactions, 88 fsyncs, on FUSE storage already logging
SELinux ioctl denials. SQLite itself executes millions of statements/sec, so 1.1M delete attempts
should NOT cost 25 minutes on statement volume alone.
⛔ DO NOT "FIX" THIS WITH ONE BIG TRANSACTION. SQLite’s own docs: WAL does not work well
for very large transactions; past ~100 MB rollback journal is faster, past a gigabyte WAL may fail
with an I/O or disk-full error. 617k deletes in one transaction is the worst available
combination. Moderate batches (~25-50k) if this is ever revisited.
⛔ DO NOT TURN JOURNALING OFF. No rollback means a crash leaves an UNDEFINED database —
5.3 GB, no backup, storage already throwing ioctl denials. Same exposure class as the 08-01 loss.
PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL is the safe lever if one is ever needed.
Also explored and dropped: origin column on tiles / stamp-at-write /
temp-table join / sorted-scan dedup. All sound; none worth the work for a once-per-source-change
operation. ⚠ If ever revisited: insertTile uses INSERT OR REPLACE, which would blank
an origin mark — a side table keyed on z/x/y avoids that entirely.
SCHEMA FACT WORTH KEEPING
ensureSchema creates stock MBTiles and nothing more:
tiles (zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row, tile_data)
UNIQUE INDEX tile_index ON tiles(zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row)
No timestamp, no source, no origin. Nothing distinguishes a corridor tile from an area
tile, and nothing can be inferred. Any origin tracking must be added.

🟢 00-MIGRATION (08-06 EOD) — SOURCE MAP MIGRATION. ⭐ START HERE ON PICK-UP.
⭐⭐⭐ THE OPEN TASK IS THE AUTOMATED REFRESH — option 2 on the migration panel.
It is the only option not selectable, and it waits on one thing: deleting the maps created from tracks as corridor downloads. Everything else in this section is finished and committed.
DONE   1a  MBTilesStore.deleteTiles          committed a0675be42
NEXT   1b  ConvoyCorridorDeleteWorker.kt     new file, compiles alone
THEN   1c  queue wiring                      ⛔ ATOMIC — see below
PURPOSE: when a user changes the source on a map slot, decide what happens to the tiles already stored for it.
⭐⭐⭐ THE DESIGN, SETTLED — ONE QUESTION, THREE ANSWERS, each protecting something different:
1  DELETE AND START OVER    protect NOTHING     clear · rebuild around tracks · draw new areas
2  MOVE EVERYTHING          protect the AREA    delete track tiles · refresh area · re-import tracks
   (automatic, background)                      all downloads submitted at once; every image slowly
                                                replaced from the new source
3  MOVE ON MY SCHEDULE      protect EVERYTHING  nothing touched; convert manually, ground by ground,
                                                with Replace tiles ticked
⭐ NO MAP-TYPE QUESTION. "How were these downloaded?" only ever existed to route an automated refresh. Option 3 has none, and option 2 handles both shapes together — which is just as well, because nothing on disk records how a store was built (the mbtiles schema does not carry it, and the queue's downloadType is wiped by clears with pre-08-05 completions deleted by the old markComplete bug).
⭐ Clear is now only ever chosen ON PURPOSE — a clean start, reclaiming space, or converting to corridors. No case is forced into it, which is what removed the earlier "are you riding soon?" question entirely.

⛔ SEQUENCING — the part that passes a design review and fails on device
PRIORITY IS NOT SEQUENCING. A delete sorts to the front, but at MAX_CONCURRENT = 2 another job can run alongside it.
⭐ The order that works for option 2 — derive the area bounds while the queue is HELD and the store is track-free:
holdQueue()
  1  delete track tiles     must COMPLETE — the one read that matters
  2  derive area refresh    bounds captured track-free, FROZEN onto each QueueEntry
  3  queue track re-imports geometry-based, needs no store read
resumeQueue()
  tracks execute first (CORRIDOR outranks REFRESH), area rebuilds underneath
⭐ Track tiles are absent for seconds, not hours — corridor outranks refresh in priority so the re-imports run before the slow area work even starts, and area imagery is never absent because enqueueRefresh replaces in place.
⚠⚠ VERIFY BEFORE RELYING ON ANY OF THAT: that enqueueRefresh genuinely derives once and stores north/south/east/west on each entry, rather than the worker re-deriving from slotName. This is a reading of the code, NOT confirmed in the worker, and the whole "execution order does not matter" property rests on it.

⭐⭐ THE BIGGER GOAL BEHIND ROUTE CORRIDORS — pre-ride map distribution
Fred 08-06, late: "I do not care about route. I am trying to create a method where a PRE-RIDE ROUTE CAN BE DISTRIBUTED AND IMPORTED WITH MAPS, allowing a rider to download accurate maps with efficient space utilisation BEFORE TRAILS ARE CAPTURED."
The route is the DISTRIBUTION UNIT, not a planning toy. A ride leader plots the route, emails it out, and each rider imports it and downloads exactly the corridor that ride needs. Nobody has to have ridden the ground, and nobody has to box a region.
⭐ It solves the case that has been forcing area downloads all along: ground with no tracks yet. You cannot corridor what nobody has ridden — unless someone plots it first. This is why routes belong in final 2.6e rather than 2.7.
⭐ Why it is accurate: a SNAPPED route's geometry IS trail geometry — snap-2 pulls the trail's own vector points — padded half a mile either side, so the corridor follows the real path rather than a straight line between waypoints. Corridor-quality coverage for ground never ridden.
⭐ Email survives it. The snapping happened at authoring time, so the coordinates already follow the trail. What does not travel is the per-vertex lineId — a local DB reference. So a shared route downloads maps and draws perfectly; re-snapping is re-established locally by adding or removing a point. ⚠ If the recipient's trail set differs, a re-snap could pull a point onto a different nearby trail — irrelevant for downloading, relevant if they extend it.
WHAT IT NEEDS, in order: (1) route geom_hash — computeGeomHash(wkt) exists and insertRoute already receives the WKT, so it is a column, one call at insert, and a backfill; (2) artifact TYPE carried alongside the hash through the corridor path — spatialTableFor(type) already exists; (3) a distribution format and import path, mirroring track import's existing corridor-download option.
⛔ Without the hash, ConvoyCorridorWorker resolves against TRACKS, finds nothing, and FAILS QUIETLY — the batch counts no-geometry as skipped.
⚠ Open: whether an UNSNAPPED route can be corridor-downloaded at all. A drawn line cuts across country between its points — its corridor covers ground the rider will not travel and misses the trail where it bends away.
⭐ TRACK NAME ON CORRIDOR QUEUE JOBS — REINSTATED
Fred 08-06 late: "retrieve the hash to retrieve track name on corridor download queue tasks" — and the reason: "it is important to know what are completed as we move along so I can drill down and test results without waiting for the whole batch to finish."
⚠ This REVERSES the rejection in the table below. It was dropped earlier the same day as scope creep, when the justification was user-facing polish. The new justification is INCREMENTAL VERIFIABILITY — with 262 rows all reading CORR SAT, a test run is unreadable. Treat this entry as authoritative.
⭐ No schema change: geomHash is already on every corridor entry. Resolve the name at display time, so enqueue, batch and worker are untouched and a renamed track shows its new name. ⚠ Batch the lookup — one query for all distinct hashes, not a read per row.
✅ Half of it already works: completed entries now survive in the queue (markComplete() was silently removing them until SHOWALLCOMPLETE-2026-08-05). ⚠ Expect one row per track per slot, so with three sources a single track produces three entries — cap the name (~20 chars) so the SOURCE stays visible.

⭐⭐ TRACK NAME ON CORRIDOR QUEUE JOBS (Fred 08-05, requested). "It would be nice to know what tracks have processed and what is next in the queue — handy on committed jobs." With 262 rows all reading CORR SAT, the queue says nothing about progress. The label is already the right place — enqueueCorridor builds label = "CORR $slotName", so it becomes "CORR $slotName · $trackName" and flows through to the panel and to completed entries. ⭐ Pass the name IN from the picker rather than looking it up: the picker already resolves duplicates to Pine Valley (1)/(2), which is exactly what should appear, and it avoids a second DB read per track. ⚠ Cap the name (~20 chars) — the source must stay visible; SAT vs TOPO matters as much as which track.
⭐⭐ CORRIDOR JOBS ARE NOT SPLIT. Area submissions chop a large bbox into consistently-sized jobs; enqueueCorridor emits ONE entry per track per slot at any size. Deliberate on 07-24 ("decide after real numbers") — and the real numbers now exist: 561, 681 and 18,000 tiles in single jobs today, all under the cutoff, but bar 10 measured ~107,000 corridor tiles across three sources. ⛔ An oversized job holds a concurrency slot for its whole duration, cannot be partially cancelled, and shows one long bar instead of steps. Per-submission balance breaks: the queue is only as balanced as its least-balanced producer. ⚠ Use the SAME constant and chunking shape as the area splitter — a parallel implementation is the defect, not the fix.
OSM row is not rendering greyed on device (observed 08-05). enabled = false was set. Candidates: the 0.4 alpha is too subtle against that background, NET MODE is active, or the edit landed on the wrong row. Not a blocker.
ORIGIN-DEPENDENT PANEL EXPANSION (Fred 08-05, agreed, not built). The panel opens showing the section relevant to how it was reached — from the BUTTON expand the actionable rows; from a TRAIL or OSM import expand those. ⚠ Requires a launch-origin value alongside showDownloadPanel, which is a plain boolean today: nothing currently records WHY the panel opened. ⛔ Reset it on close or the second opening inherits the first one's expansion.
Only the PLANNER is wired. ConvoyScreen and ConvoyTrackImportScreen also call the panel; their new params are defaulted so they compile and behave as before. ⚠ The import path is the one that produced 215 jobs — it deserves its own pass, not a ride-along.
⭐⭐⭐ 00-ENQUEUE-PRINCIPLE (08-05) — ONE SUBMISSION MODEL FOR EVERY TILE REQUEST
⭐⭐⭐ Fred 08-05, the governing statement: "the queuing and sizing method should be consistent to all tile requests."
THE SHAPE:
bbox producers            ONE chopper           queue jobs
  drawn area          →   (consistently    →    balanced,
  area refresh             sized cells,          similar size
  selective source         cut at the
    refresh                threshold)
track producers           ONE deriver           queue jobs
  artifact panel      →   (corridorTiles   →    (NOT SPLIT YET
  corridor download        + the same             — see above)
  corridor refresh         cutoff)
⭐ BALANCING IS PER SUBMISSION (one area, one track), not across the queue. It needs no global view and no reshuffling, and it holds whether you submit one area or twenty tracks. A large bbox becomes 1/2, 2/2; one submission may be three jobs depending on tiles and sources.
⛔ A SECOND CHOPPER IS THE DEFECT. enqueueRefresh has its own 12×12 grid (gridCells) while enqueueArea segments properly — so the same bbox produces different job shapes depending which door it came through. That is how 08-02 produced 568 entries at 60–70K tiles each. It is not a sizing bug; it is a second sizing implementation.
⭐ THEREFORE enqueueRefresh IS RETIRED, NOT MIGRATED. Refresh becomes area-or-corridor enqueue with replace = true and downloadType = MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH — the type carries the KIND, the enqueue carries the SIZING, and there is exactly one place where a bbox becomes queue entries.
⚠ Confirm the threshold against the code before building — Fred 08-05 states 60,000 tiles; earlier notes say a ≤50K ceiling. One is stale. The corridor splitter must use whichever the area path actually uses.
⚠ While in that call site, compare enqueueRefresh's argument order against enqueueArea — swapped bounds is the leading unverified hypothesis for the 07-23 continental incident, and this work touches exactly that line.
🔵 00-REFRESH-DESIGN (08-05) — REFRESH IS TOTAL. TWO METHODS. THE CLEAR DECISION.
STATE: designed 08-05, NOT BUILT. Deliberately separated from the corridor download work so the shared enqueueCorridorBatch is proven by one caller before a second arrives.
⭐ REFRESH IS FULL TILE REPLACEMENT BY DEFINITION — there is NO picker. Per-track selection belongs to the DOWNLOAD panel. Refresh uses one of two methods: corridor replacement of all tiles (all known tracks) or area replacement of all tiles (every stored bbox).
REFRESH IS ONE MAP COLUMN, not all slots — so enqueueCorridorBatch serves it with a single-element slot list and replace = true. Same call, different arguments; that is what makes it reusable rather than two functions wearing one name.
⛔ The SAT column owns THREE stores
Fred 08-05: "there is no sat location and places label database — the SAT column owns SAT label and SAT places. If one is deleted they all are."
SAT column
  SAT.mbtiles              4.24 GB
  SAT_LABELS_PLACES         210 MB
  SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT      251 MB
  ─────────────────────────────────
  total                    ~4.70 GB     (Droid 2, measured 08-02)
⚠ The panel must show live sizes, not these — a user's store will differ. And the real number is 4.70 GB, not 4.24: the label stores are the part people forget they are carrying.
⛔ TOPO and TOPO+ are their own columns and are NOT touched. Clearing SAT must never take topo — a rider who cleared satellite to rebuild by corridor finding their topo coverage gone is a silent, expensive failure nobody notices until they are off-grid.
⚠ A HYB rebuild will not refill the label stores — Google Hybrid bakes labels into the imagery and fetches no overlays. After clear + HYB refresh those two files are simply gone and the ~461 MB stays freed. That is the intended end state, not a loss — the panel must say so, or "two files didn't come back" reads as a bug.
⭐⭐ THE RULE: CLEAR ⇒ REPLACE = FALSE. Change the displayed value and LOCK it.
On a store that was just cleared, replace = true is pure waste — replace exists to bypass the hasTile pre-fetch filter, and on an empty store every tile is missing anyway.
⭐ AND IT ACTIVELY HURTS ON OVERLAPPING TRACKS. Corridors from tracks sharing a trailhead or an approach road overlap heavily. With replace FALSE the second track's corridor hits hasTile and skips what the first already fetched. With replace TRUE it re-downloads every shared tile. The clear runs as its own job ahead of the batch, so by the time any corridor job executes the store is empty and hasTile deduplicates across the WHOLE batch.
UI: selecting clear forces replace false, renders it false, and locks it — greyed with the reason beside it ("store will be empty — nothing to replace"), restored on deselect, visibly disabled rather than hidden.
⛔ The batch must refuse the impossible pair too — not silently: log it and force false. The UI is the enforcement; the function is the backstop, because refresh will be a second caller and must not be able to reintroduce it.
⚠ The clear is its OWN QUEUED JOB, ordered ahead of the batch — DELETE_AREA_TILES already has priority 0 reserved. ⛔ NOT a flag on the first entry: queue order is not guaranteed under MAX_CONCURRENT = 2, and a per-entry flag means whichever job runs first wipes what the others already wrote.
The transition grid — what the panel must recommend
From → ToClear SAT columnRefresh methodWhy
Area → CorridorYES — recommendedCorridorThe area store is ~90% tiles the corridor model will never use. Refreshing without clearing leaves the bulk as stale area fill with fresh corridors through it.
Corridor → CorridorNoCorridorSame footprint — overwrite in place.
Corridor → AreaNoAreaArea is a superset; existing corridor tiles are valid fill.
Area → Corridor AND Esri → HYBYES — the clean-slate caseCorridor⭐ One store, single-source, corridor-shaped, labels baked in. This is the coherent end state and the panel should name it.
⚠ Label deletion is conditional on the SOURCE change, not the shape — Esri → HYB. The grid carries it as a column because it is part of the same decision, but shape does not drive it.
⭐ OVERWRITE IS ONLY CLEAN WITH ALL TRACKS SELECTED. If the corridors cover everything the store legitimately holds, overwrite-in-place ends single-source without discarding 4.7 GB. Refresh a SUBSET after a source change and everything outside those corridors stays the old source — a permanent patchwork, and nothing in a stored tile records which source produced it.
⚠ ALL means all TRACKS, not all TILES. Area downloads drawn by box, and corridors from tracks since deleted, still sit outside every current corridor. Overwrite-with-ALL is clean only if the store was built from corridors alone.
The panel's exits — three, not two
If you are looking at this panel you have already chosen corridor refresh and the method. The panel explains the consequence and offers:
Clear and refresh — clean slate, with live sizes and the no-backup warning
Refresh without clearing — proceed, area files retained, ⚠ patchwork accepted knowingly
⭐ ← Back to the refresh selection — you did not intend to give up the area coverage. The selection must survive the trip back, or nobody uses it: they will press forward rather than redo the work. ⚠ Back means back to the SELECTION, not out to the map. ⭐ Render the panel OVER the selection rather than replacing it — the state stays live underneath and there is nothing to rebuild.
⛔ NO BACKUP EXISTS and the store is GB-scale. Any clear names the column and its measured size before it does anything.

✅ 00-COMPLETIONS (08-05) — THE QUEUE WAS DELETING ITS OWN SUCCESSES
⭐⭐ markComplete() branched on entry.refreshMode and silently REMOVED the entry — no COMPLETE status, no completedAt stamp, no row. The comment read "Refresh cells: silently remove from queue, no log clutter."
But refreshMode is ALSO the REPLACE-TILES flag. Both of 08-05's Google Hybrid corridor runs logged replace=true, so both took the silent-remove branch:
08:31:29  CorridorWorker: Corridor complete: CORR SAT downloaded=561 failed=0
08:47:04  CorridorWorker: Corridor complete: CORR SAT downloaded=681 failed=0
⛔ Both flawless. Neither visible. markFailed does NOT take that path — so the only download entries that ever survived were the ones that FAILED. That is why 08-02's "CORR SAT failed" was the only artifact left to reason from, and why the whole "Google downloads abort" framing looked worse than reality.
FIXED (Fred's call): the branch is gone. One path for every completion. "We know it's a refresh type and we have a filter — all completions should log."
⭐ THE DURABLE PRINCIPLE: the queue is the RECORD. Deleting rows to reduce clutter destroys evidence permanently; filtering hides it reversibly. Display concerns do not get to mutate state. Same rule as "hide means absent from the map, not absent from the database".
⭐ Side benefit: refresh cells now reach COMPLETE with a stamp, so they finally contribute samples to estimateRemaining() instead of vanishing from the pool.
⚠ Still owed: the flag is OVERLOADED — refreshMode means "refresh cell" in markComplete and "replace tiles" at the call sites. Split into isRefreshCell / replaceTiles. Note enqueueDelete deliberately leaves it false and its comment at :328-331 documents this exact trap.

🔴 00-INSTALL (08-04 designed, UPDATED 08-09 — NOT BUILT) — SELF-UNINSTALL FLOW + THE ALL-FILES AUTHORITY DEFECT AND ITS FIX
PURPOSE: remove the new-install data-loss exposure that destroyed ~89,000 trails on 08-01.
STATE: DESIGN AGREED 08-04. No code.
DOCUMENT OF RECORD: grouptrack_install_design_2026-08-04.html — full design, flow, and reasoning.
SUPERSEDES: the manual-only approach in grouptrack_reinstall_procedure_2026-08-03.html, which stays valid as the fallback for anyone not using the in-app path.
The key realisation
The app can uninstall itself. Intent.ACTION_DELETE launches the system uninstall dialog — and at that moment the app is alive and holds authority, so it can do the dangerous bookkeeping while it still can. Ten manual steps become two taps.
THE FLOW: user taps "Prepare for reinstall" → app renames Documents/GroupTrack → .bak and My Tracks → .bak (instant regardless of 50–60 GB) → fires the uninstall intent on itself → user installs the new build → All-Files grant requested FIRST, before anything touches the DB → REAL READ of the .bak dirs → prompt to restore → on confirm, verify the blanks are EMPTY, delete them, rename back.
⭐ WHY RENAMING BEATS DETECTING: every detection approach fails for the same reason — the app creates blanks BEFORE authority arrives, and the permission API reports the wrong answer at exactly that moment. The rename does not detect anything; it removes the data from the path the app will write to until authority is real. Nothing to detect, nothing to destroy.
⭐⭐ The ordering half — grant BEFORE the database
08-01 was an ORDERING failure. The app opened the DB before authority was real, and did not prompt because it TESTED and the test lied — Environment.isExternalStorageManager() returns true in the stale-grant state and is wrong. It reads the stale grant record; the filesystem enforces the truth. No API question returns the right answer — only a real read attempt does.
Fred: "we never got the prompt in the failed install as the app looked like it had authority. probably should not be a test but unconditional grant there." → make the All-Files prompt UNCONDITIONAL on first run and put it FIRST. The app already knows it is a fresh install — it is already asking first-run questions. No new detection needed.
⛔ REJECTED — AND WHY: blocking startup until the app can read would DEADLOCK the device. The app must run before it can be granted authority, so refusing to start until it can read means a reinstalled device can never be recovered. Also rejected: acting at uninstall time — Android has no uninstall hook; ACTION_PACKAGE_REMOVED goes to OTHER apps and arrives too late anyway. The danger is not the uninstall, it is the next install running blind.
The first-run marker — filesDir, NOT shared storage
⛔ THE TRAP if it lived in Documents/: that file sits in the very storage the authority question is about. Without All-Files the app cannot read it, so "file absent" and "cannot see the file" look identical — the exact confusion that caused 08-01, reproduced in a new file.
✅ filesDir needs no authority and is always readable, and is wiped by uninstall — which makes it a better signal, not a worse one:
marker ABSENT + data PRESENT in Documents/ = a reinstall over existing data. That is the detector 08-01 needed, free with the same file.
Contents: {"status":"in_progress"} → {"status":"complete","version_code":N}. Retaining it after completion answers both has setup run? and is this a reinstall?, and gives crash recovery for a first run that dies midway.
🔴 OPEN ITEMS
⚠⚠ FIRST ACTION — VERIFY ON DROID 2 THAT AN UNINSTALL LEAVES Documents/GroupTrack/ INTACT. It should — public shared storage — but Android has changed storage behaviour repeatedly, and the entire design rests on this assumption. Minutes to test. Promoted from "open question" because if it is wrong the whole flow inverts.
Cancelled uninstall dialog: directories already renamed, app still installed, finds no data. Needs an undo path — on next launch, if .bak exists and the app is clearly NOT freshly installed, offer to rename back. (Renaming only after removal is confirmed is impossible; the app cannot observe its own uninstall.)
Settings/launcher uninstalls bypass the button entirely. The manual procedure stays documented as fallback — and refuse-to-create (below) is the floor under everything.
⚠⚠ THE REVERSE-RISK MOMENT is step 8 — it DELETES directories. Everything before it protected against overwriting real data with blanks; this step can delete the wrong thing if the empty-check is wrong. Refuse if non-empty, log what was found, and ask — a user who recorded a track between install and restore has real data in those "blanks".
⭐⭐ 08-09 UPDATE — THE AUTHORITY DEFECT, LOCATED IN CODE, AND ITS FIX (SUPERSEDES the permission reasoning above)
PURPOSE: the shared root cause of BOTH data-loss events — 08-01 (~89,000 trails) and
08-08 (the whole spatial DB). STATE: design agreed 08-09. No code.
DOCUMENT OF RECORD: grouptrack_allfiles_fix_strategy_2026-08-09_v1.html.
CORRECTS the permission reasoning in 00-INSTALL above, which assumed a stale grant left over
from a previous install.
The defect, located in code
ConvoyScreen.kt:145   mutableStateOf(!Environment.isExternalStorageManager())
ConvoyScreen.kt:151   if (!Environment.isExternalStorageManager()) { ... }
ConvoyScreen.kt:433   ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION
OsmImportStage.kt:575 Environment.isExternalStorageManager()
ONE FAULT, NOT TWO: THE TEST ASKS THE WRONG SOURCE.
isExternalStorageManager() reads the AppOps record. In the failure state that record
says granted while the filesystem refuses. So the expression initialises the dialog flag to
false and the prompt never fires. Fred: "the app said it had all authority, the checkbox
was yes, but the app did not have all authority."
⭐ THE POSITION OF THE CHECK IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE MOVED. An earlier draft of this
section claimed the check ran too late because it sits inside a Composable. Fred disproved it:
it works on every new install. On a new install the value genuinely reads no, the prompt fires,
the grant lands, and the DB is built afterwards. Same code, same position, correct outcome —
the ONLY difference on the broken path is the API lying. The fix is a substitution, not a
restructure.
⭐⭐ WHY IT HAPPENS — THE CHANGE IS ACTED ON, NOT THE VALUE
AOSP: storage access is enforced by a per-process mount view, not by the permission
record. A mount namespace is created for each app at Zygote fork time and the appropriate
view bind-mounted in. Then — critically — "when permissions are granted, vold jumps into the
mount namespace of already-running apps and bind mounts the upgraded view into place", and
downgrades always result in the app being killed.
"WHEN GRANTED" — THE ACTION FIRES ON THE TRANSITION. Nothing recomputes the mount
view from the current value. That is Fred's question answered, and it explains every observed
behaviour:
PathTransitionMount updated?
New installno → yes✅ event fires
The broken stateyes → yes
⛔ no event — nothing happens
Uninstall + reinstallfresh fork✅ view computed at fork
Toggle off then onyes → no → yes✅ two events
⭐ THIS IS WHY OPENING THE SETTINGS SCREEN ON ITS OWN DOES NOTHING — Fred's point, and it
is right: entry state and exit state are identical, so there is no transition to act on.
The transition has to be manufactured.
⚠ CAVEAT — NOT PROVEN. The AOSP passage says runtime permissions.
MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is an AppOp / special access, not a runtime permission. If the
vold path does not cover AppOps at all, then no in-place grant ever updates the mount and only a
fresh process fork works — meaning reinstall really is the only cure. ⚠ Several mechanisms
proposed during the 08-09 session were wrong and were corrected against observed behaviour.
Nothing below depends on this being right.
⭐ WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT RISK — read this before panicking
ThingAt risk?
Data in Documents/GroupTrack/
NO. Public shared storage — survives clear-cache, clear-data, uninstall, all of it.
Lost storage accessRecoverable. Uninstall + reinstall works (observed).
The app writing a blank over the real DB
THE ONLY PERMANENT LOSS.
⭐ We do not have to fix the permission to stop losing data. We have to stop the app
proceeding when it cannot see its own files.
THE FIX — in build order
STEP 1 — REPLACE THE TEST. Never ask the API. The only truthful question is a real read of
a path All-Files actually governs. filesDir/cacheDir always work, so
reading those proves nothing.
fun hasRealStorageAccess(): Boolean = try {
    val d = File(Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory(), "Documents/GroupTrack")
    d.exists() &amp;&amp; d.canRead() &amp;&amp; d.list() != null      // plain File I/O — NO SQLite
} catch (e: Exception) { false }
⛔ "Cannot see it" and "it is not there" get the SAME treatment — treat invisibility as
UNKNOWN and refuse. Reading invisibility as emptiness is exactly what built blanks over real data.
⚠ Same substitution at :151 and OsmImportStage.kt:575.
STEP 2 — MANUFACTURE THE TRANSITION. Two panels, two settings trips. Each trip needs its
own instruction panel first, because the settings screen tells the user nothing about which way to
move the toggle.
1  real read fails, value says YES
2  PANEL A  "Storage access isn't working. The permission shows as ON
             but isn't working. On the next screen turn All-Files
             access OFF. It will look correct already — turn it off
             anyway."                                [ Open settings ]
   ↓ fires ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION
   ↓ PROCESS LIKELY DIES HERE — the downgrade kills it
3  verify by VALUE that it now reads NO   ← the one place the API is
                                            the correct thing to ask
4  PANEL B  "Now turn it back on."        [ Open settings ]
5  value reads YES — a genuine no→yes transition this time
6  RE-RUN THE REAL READ
       succeeds → carry on
       fails    → uninstall + reinstall message
⚠ PERSIST THE CYCLE STAGE (filesDir or SharedPreferences). The process dying
between 2 and 3 is EXPECTED, not a failure — without a marker the user returns to an app that has
forgotten it was mid-cycle. ⭐ It degrades safely: a lost marker means step 1 re-runs, finds the
value now reads no, and prompts normally.
⚠ PANEL A CARRIES THE HARDEST WORDING IN THE FLOW. The user is being asked to switch off a
permission that appears correct. Without the "it will look right — turn it off anyway" line, most
people back out.
STEP 2b — LOOP BACK. THE READ IS A GATE, NOT A ONE-SHOT CHECK.
⭐⭐ THE APP NEVER PROCEEDS BECAUSE THE USER CAME BACK FROM SETTINGS. IT PROCEEDS
ONLY BECAUSE A READ PASSED. Returning from the settings screen proves nothing — the user may
have changed nothing, changed the wrong thing, or changed it correctly and had it not take. The
only evidence that counts is the read.
fun gate(): Boolean {                    // ONE function, called at EVERY entry
    if (hasRealStorageAccess()) return true
    runPanelCycle()                      // Panel A → settings → Panel B → settings
    return hasRealStorageAccess()        // ← RE-TEST. Never assume.
}
CALL IT AT EVERY ENTRY POINT, not once at startup:
on resume from the settings screen — every return, both trips
before any SpatialDbManager open
before any MBTilesStore open
before any import, download or migration run
on app resume from background — authority can be lost while the app lives
⛔ NO CACHED "we checked at startup" FLAG AS THE ONLY SOURCE. A flag set once at launch is
the same class of mistake as trusting the API: it answers from a record instead of from reality.
Cache the RESULT for the current screen if needed, but re-read before anything that opens or
creates.
⚠ THE FAIL PATH NEVER FALLS THROUGH. If the final read fails, the app shows Step 4's
message and stops there. There is no "continue anyway", no timeout that proceeds, no dismissible
dialog that lets the user past. Backing out of any panel leaves the app in the refused state —
which is correct, because the alternative is what destroyed the DB twice.
⭐ WHY THE LOOP MATTERS MORE THAN THE CYCLE: the two-panel cycle is a REMEDY and is
unproven. The loop is a GUARANTEE and needs nothing to be true about the permission mechanism.
Even if every remedy fails, the loop means the app sits refusing rather than proceeding
blind.
STEP 2c — THREE ATTEMPTS, THEN ABORT SETUP. Do not loop forever.
⭐⭐ AFTER THREE FAILED CYCLES THE APP STOPS OFFERING THE REMEDY AND ABORTS SETUP
WITH A TERMINAL MESSAGE. The two-panel cycle is unproven. If it has not worked in three
attempts it is not going to, and continuing to send the user back to the same settings screen is
worse than useless — it teaches them to tap past the warning that is protecting their data.
allfiles_attempts   persisted in filesDir  (NOT shared storage —
                    the app can always read filesDir, no authority needed)
on gate() failure:
    attempts += 1
    if attempts &lt; 3  → run the panel cycle, re-test
    if attempts &gt;= 3 → ABORT SETUP. Terminal screen. No further cycles.
on a PASSING read → attempts = 0        ← reset, so a later unrelated
                                          failure gets its own three
THE TERMINAL SCREEN — abort, do not continue:
"GroupTrack cannot reach its map storage and could not repair it.
 SETUP HAS BEEN STOPPED. Nothing has been changed or deleted.
 Your maps and tracks are safe in Documents/GroupTrack.
 To fix this:  uninstall GroupTrack, then install it again.
 A reinstall does NOT remove your maps or tracks.
 DO NOT move or copy your map files anywhere while this
 message is showing, and do not put them back by hand
 afterwards. The app will find them on its own.
 Do not clear app data or cache — that is what caused this."
⛔⛔ THE MESSAGE MUST TELL THE USER NOT TO RESTORE BY HAND — that is how BOTH
stores were actually lost on 08-08. Fred saved the tile stores before clearing cache and lost
them moving them back while authority was still broken; the hand-restored spatial DB was zeroed the
same way. A helpful user who copies their data back into a blind app is deleting it. The
reinstall path needs no manual file handling at all — say so explicitly.
⛔ ABORT MEANS ABORT. No "continue anyway", no dismiss, no proceed-after-timeout. Setup does
not run, the DB is not opened, tile stores are not opened. The app sits on this screen until it
is uninstalled or storage access genuinely returns. The alternative to sitting there is the
thing that destroyed the spatial DB twice.
⭐ THE COUNTER LIVES IN filesDir FOR TWO REASONS: the app can always read it
with no authority at all, and an uninstall wipes it — so a genuine reinstall starts fresh at
zero automatically, with no reset logic to get wrong. ⚠ Note clear-data also wipes it, which is
correct: that is a new episode and deserves its own three attempts.
⚠ THE COUNTER MUST SURVIVE THE PROCESS DEATH between Panel A and Panel B — increment and
persist BEFORE firing the settings intent, never after returning from it, or a cycle that kills the
app never counts and the loop runs forever.
⚠ KEEP STEP 5's DIAGNOSTICS ON THE TERMINAL SCREEN. This is the moment worth
photographing — three failed repairs is the strongest evidence we will ever get about what is
actually wrong.
STEP 3 — REFUSE TO CREATE. ⭐⭐ THIS ALREADY HAS ITS OWN SECTION — SEE
00-REFUSE BELOW. DO NOT RE-DESIGN IT HERE. It was lifted out of the install design
on purpose on 08-05: the install flow protects users who tap the button, 00-REFUSE
protects everyone else. The 08-09 additions (MBTilesStore, the DatabaseErrorHandler question,
the hand-restored DB) are recorded THERE, not here.
What the 08-09 work adds to it in one line: the gate function from Step 2b is what
00-REFUSE gates on — a real read, not the permission API.
STEP 4 — SAY ONLY WHAT HAS BEEN OBSERVED. When the read still fails after the cycle:
"GroupTrack cannot reach its map storage. Your maps and tracks are safe in Documents/GroupTrack —
nothing has been changed or deleted. Uninstall GroupTrack and install it again to fix it."
⚠ DO NOT PROMISE THE TOGGLE CYCLE WORKS. It has never been demonstrated — by the time it
was tried on 08-08 the data was already gone, so nothing was proven.
Uninstall + reinstall is the ONLY remedy actually observed to work.
STEP 5 — INSTRUMENT THE REFUSAL SCREEN. This has cost data twice and the behaviour is not
understood. Put the evidence on screen so the next occurrence is a photograph, not an evening of
reconstruction: what the API claims · whether the plain read succeeded · what
filesDir contains · what is visible in Documents/GroupTrack/ and file
sizes if readable · what triggered this startup path.
🔴 STILL UNKNOWN — do not build past these

Testing — and why it is awkward

What the 08-09 work CORRECTS in the 08-04 design above
KEEP: grant before the database · filesDir marker (not shared storage) ·
refuse-to-create as the floor · the rejection of blocking startup entirely.
CORRECT: 00-INSTALL says the API "reads the stale grant record" from a previous install.
It is not stale — the grant was live and the enforcement disagreed. No permission API returns
the right answer at any time.
CORRECT: "make the prompt unconditional and put it first" is necessary but not
sufficient — the user was already granted, so an unconditional prompt shows a permission that

NOTE: the self-uninstall rename flow only covers the path where the user taps the button.
Settings-initiated clear-data and clear-cache bypass it entirely — and that is what bit us both

🔴🔴 00-REFUSE (2.6e P0, UPDATED 08-09) — REFUSE-TO-CREATE. THE FLOOR UNDER EVERYTHING.
⭐⭐⭐ LIFTED OUT OF THE INSTALL DESIGN ON PURPOSE (08-05). The install flow protects users who tap the button. This protects everyone else — including every Settings/launcher uninstall, every revoked permission, every FUSE/SELinux hiccup. Different priority, different item.
SpatialDbManager must NEVER create-if-missing on a path it cannot verify. A failed open must ABORT, not write an empty schema. The install design names this as "the single highest-value item on this page" — it alone would have prevented 08-01, and it costs nothing at runtime.
⚠ And it is not hypothetical maintenance: the SELinux ioctl denial on the FUSE-mounted store fires on ordinary download runs (observed 08-05, see 00-HYB-PROVEN). The trigger condition is present regularly; only the create-if-missing turns it into data loss.
Also owed with it: ROW-COUNT SANITY + a .lastgood copy after each successful startup. A startup reporting zero rows where the previous run reported 89,000 is a red flag the app should RAISE, not report as normal.
⭐⭐ 08-09 — WHAT THE GATE MUST BE. The 08-09 investigation located the
authority defect in code (ConvoyScreen.kt:145, see 00-INSTALL above) and
it changes what 00-REFUSE tests on: NOT the permission API — a REAL READ of
Documents/GroupTrack/ using plain File I/O, no SQLite.
isExternalStorageManager() returns true in the failure state and the settings
toggle shows granted, so any check built on either is the same bug wearing a different hat.
⛔ "Cannot see it" and "it is not there" get the SAME treatment — refuse.
⚠⚠ 08-09 — MBTilesStore IS NOT COVERED AND MUST BE. This section has only
ever named SpatialDbManager. ⛔ CORRECTION 08-09: THE MAPS DID NOT "SURVIVE BY
LUCK" — THEY WERE LOST TOO. Fred saved them deliberately before clearing cache, and lost them
on the way back in: he moved them back after the install while the authority failure was
still live, and the app built new empty stores instead of reading them. Same mechanism as the
hand-restored spatial DB — one story, not two. Both get the gate.
⛔⛔ 08-09 — THE SIGNATURE, IN FRED'S WORDS: "the app recreated but had no
authority to what existed before." This is the failure in one line, and it happened to BOTH
stores. A hand-restored file is not safe. Fred restored a real populated spatial DB and the app
zeroed it out and reset it; he restored the saved tile stores and the app built empty ones over
that ground. The files were physically present and visible to a file manager the entire time.
The app could not reach them, so it created — and creation is what destroys.
⚠ MECHANISM STILL UNVERIFIED. Leading candidate for the DB: SpatialDbManager
opening without passing a DatabaseErrorHandler, so Android's default handler deletes a
database it deems corrupt and recreates it — an unreadable file is indistinguishable from a corrupt
one. A custom handler that logs and throws is a one-parameter change and would close that half
independently of every permission question.
GREP BEFORE BUILDING:
grep -rn "openOrCreateDatabase\|DatabaseErrorHandler" SpatialDbManager.kt
⭐⭐ THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE — THIS IS THE PART THAT CHANGES USER ADVICE:
RESTORING FILES BY HAND WHILE AUTHORITY IS BROKEN DESTROYS THEM. Any recovery instruction —
manual, quickstart, in-app message — must say restore ONLY after a real read succeeds, never
before. Telling a user to copy their data back into a blind app is telling them to delete it.
⭐ Consequence: the gate sits ahead of every OPEN, not merely ahead of CREATION. Refusing
to create is not enough if the framework can delete on a failed open before our code decides
anything.
✅ Fixed 08-04: SpatialDbManager :166/:168 logged the LITERAL ${spatialFile.absolutePath} because the $ was backslash-escaped — so the DB path never appeared in the log. That was the diagnostic that would have made the 08-01 loss obvious immediately.

🧰 00-TOOLS (08-05) — TROUBLESHOOTING TOOLS AND USES
DOCUMENT OF RECORD: grouptrack_troubleshooting_tools_and_uses_2026-08-05.html — six sections: the three xrefs and their blind spots · layer contracts · divergence · the 2.7 dead-code prune recipe · the draw-failure recipe · pre-build hazards.
⭐⭐ WHY IT EXISTS: four defects this week shared one shape — a method aborted before its real work, silently — and no structural tool could have found any of them. The xrefs answer where is this touched. Every one of these lived on a different axis: on what thread, in what lifecycle phase, against which page. There is no index for that axis.
The layer contracts — the rules with no tooling
BoundaryRuns onRule
@JavascriptInterface methodsJavaBridgeANY WebView or UI call MUST go through Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { }. They throw off-main and the throw aborts the method silently. Four-for-four now — mechanical rule, no case-by-case judgement.
Argument positions—Never ?: return inside an argument. Reads as a null-safe accessor, is an early exit from the whole function.
onPageFinishedmainPage not ready until the postDelayed completes. Earlier Kotlin→JS calls fail with &lt;fn&gt; is not defined, visible only in a console log.
evaluateJavascript(fn)main onlyThe named function must exist in BOTH map HTMLs. SpatialDisplayManager's jsUpdate/jsShow/jsHide contract assumes hand-maintained parity.
WorkManager workersfresh processJobs survive app death. ensureInit() re-reads config from scratch — never trust in-memory state across the process boundary.
shouldInterceptRequestnetworkNo UI, no WebView calls.
⭐⭐ navigation_xref.txt — the one xref that gives CALL SITES
Four sections. A nav-host routes (every registered destination) · C navigation triggers — navigate() calls and onNavigate* params with the line where each is invoked · D screen composables + exit callbacks · E user-visible labels.
⭐ SECTION A vs SECTION C MAKES THE DEAD-DESTINATION CHECK MECHANICAL: a route registered in A with no navigate() in C is unreachable. Proven: ConvoyRouteCreate is registered at ConvoyNavigation.kt:87 (A), its composable declared at ConvoyRouteCreateScreen.kt:18 (D), and it appears nowhere in C — a 27-line stub reachable from nothing. Do this before any manual grepping in the 2.7 prune.
⭐ Section E is the MANUAL-WRITING tool — it is what the user actually taps, which is the vocabulary the manual has to use.
⚠ Check its Generated: timestamp against the last commit. A call-site index that lags the code produces confident wrong answers. (Current copy: generated 2026-08-05 09:14.)
⚠ The xrefs' documented blind spots — each cost real time
Lambda parameters — onDownloadMaps appears in no xref; looked dead, was live in two screens.
var X by remember { } locals — addPointMode is in none of them.
Tags held in constants — 08-05: a grep for Log.x("LITERAL" returned nothing across four well-instrumented files, because the tags are TAG constants. The scan reported a silence that did not exist.
Anything inside a non-executing block — 08-03: a def-scan called a range clean; it was inside a &lt;script src&gt; tag whose inline body never executes by spec.
⛔ THE PATTERN BEHIND ALL OF THEM: scanning for one shape of evidence and reporting "clean" when the scan could not have seen what was there. A negative grep result is only as good as its pattern. Before trusting an empty result, prove the pattern matches a known-present case.
⚠ These blind spots apply to field_crossref / where_used / function_universe — declaration indexes. navigation_xref is the exception (above): for screen routing and reachability, read it FIRST rather than grepping.
⭐⭐ CONVOY IS THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION — divergence is a defect until proven intentional
Four times this week convoy had a fix the planner did not, and nobody knew until it broke: (1) [Fix2] fresh re-read; (2) seeding lastViewport* before draw; (3) posting evaluateJavascript to main; (4) the reseed gate — this one IS intentional (convoy is persistent and owns one map identity; the planner is entered and left, and the gate prevents cross-map bleed).
⚠ THE LIMIT: the maps are not symmetric by nature and must not be forced to be. The target is SHARED CODE, not MATCHED CODE — two hand-maintained copies drift again however carefully aligned today. SpatialDisplayManager has been the reliable layer all week precisely because there is ONE copy. ⭐ This is the same argument that makes the 2.7 service-layer work worth doing.
⛔ THE TRAP UNIQUE TO THIS CODEBASE — read before any 2.7 dead-code prune
Kotlin calls JavaScript functions BY NAME, from inside a string. ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:578 calls showProximityPopup that way. No JS tool sees that call. No Kotlin tool sees it either. A JS function with zero references in the HTML can be fully live; a Kotlin function whose only caller is a nav registration can be fully dead. Neither toolchain crosses the boundary — you are the only thing that does.
TOOLING OWED (none of it exists yet): a bridge-thread scanner (WebView/UI calls inside @JavascriptInterface bodies — would have caught :717 the day it was written, and run against both screens it answers the divergence question for free); a cross-boundary name checker (every evaluateJavascript("fn(...)") has a matching function fn in BOTH HTMLs); a screen-parity diff.
🔵 00-CORRIDOR-REFRESH (08-05) — NEXT BUILD, AFTER THE AAB
PURPOSE: refresh existing downloads by CORRIDOR, not by bounding box.
STATE: agreed 08-05, not started. Steps 4–6 of the 08-03 six-step plan.
⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN "a nicer option": the 215-job incident was area refresh converting each track BOUNDARY into a BBOX. A switchbacked trail's bbox covers the whole mountain; its corridor covers a line buffer. Corridor refresh is the fix for the thing that produced 215 jobs — the same problem corridor downloads were built for on 07-24.
⚠ Corridor refresh DOES NOT EXIST. Fred 08-03: "the refresh does not currently support corridor imports." Step 5 is BUILD, not MIGRATE.
The shape (Fred 08-05)
Both enqueue functions become callable with parameters, from anywhere: enqueueArea(bbox, …) for bbox items, enqueueCorridor(track, …) for track submissions. The PICKER is then just a caller, not part of either — build it once for corridor download, reuse it for corridor refresh. Corridor stacks per-track submissions.
⭐ The payoff: every download origin already routes through ConvoyDownloadConfirm → submitDownload. If refresh routes through the same picker and the same two enqueue functions, there stops being a separate refresh code path at all — refresh becomes "download, with replace on." That kills the gridCells problem rather than migrating it.
⚠ replace is a PARAMETER, not a separate function. Refresh re-fetches tiles already on disk, bypassing the hasTile pre-fetch filter. ⛔ And that flag is the same refreshMode field that was deleting completions until 08-05 — verify entries survive when the new refresh path passes it.
⚠ The estimate-and-confirm gate belongs in the PICKER, once — both callers go through it. One track was 561 tiles; select-all across a track list times the map slots is how 10 tracks became 215 jobs.
⚠ The AREA path still needs gridCells → segmentCells — corridor re-derives at run time and never builds oversized cells, so keeping area as an option keeps that defect live.
⚠ Compare enqueueRefresh's argument order against enqueueArea while in there — swapped bounds is the leading unverified hypothesis for the 07-23 continental incident, and this work touches that call site.
⛔ Must work in a FRESH PROCESS. WorkManager jobs survive app death; the worker's ensureInit() re-reads config from scratch. The column file is what makes that safe — which is why step 3 was placed before this.
OPEN: the picker lists TRACKS or TRAILS? Corridor derivation runs off track geometry (getTrackPoints, corridorTiles); trails would need a different path. Settle before writing.
