🔴🔴 HIDE MUST MEAN ABSENT, NOT INVISIBLE (Fred, 07-31)
Fred: "hide keeps them from being placed on the map, not just invisible" and "the
behaviour we are looking for is focusing on artifacts we are displaying."
THE RULE: a hidden artifact type contributes NOTHING — not taps, not proximity, not snap, not
selection. Visibility IS the selection. What is on screen is what you are working with.
⚠ Observed defect that proves it
Trails OFF, tap a track on the planner, get a list of TRAIL names.
Cause: hideTrails() does map.removeLayer(trailLayer) and sets
trailsVisible = false — it does NOT null the variable. The proximity scan at
grouptrack_map.html:831 calls checkLayer(trailLayer, …), which skips a layer
only if it is null. So a detached-but-populated layer is still fully walkable, and hidden
trails contribute to the proximity list.
⚠ It also explains "occasionally the detail panel instead" — the scan is a MAP-level click handler
running alongside the track layer's own handler. Whichever resolves first wins the screen.
⚠ And the behaviour currently depends on HOW you turned it off: clearTrails() DOES
null the variable, hideTrails() does not.
The fix — and why NOT to null on hide
⛔ Do not null the layer on hide. The retained variable is a CACHE —
loadTrails rebuilds from a fresh GeoJSON payload, so nulling means a full query and
rebuild on every toggle. At 10,000 trails that is a visible cost.
⭐ Fix checkLayer to test visibility instead of null:
function checkLayer(layer, visible, typeName, color) {
  if (!layer || !visible) return;
Four call sites, both maps. Correct regardless of which path turned the type off.
⚠ AND CHECK SNAP — likely the same bug in a different place
RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) is fed from
queryTrailsByViewport / queryTracksByViewport — database queries, not
layers. Those know nothing about display state, so a route vertex can probably snap to a HIDDEN
trail. Under this rule it should not.
⚠ Not verified — ConvoyScreen.kt:596 builds the byId map from both
queries and I saw no visibility filter, but only read part of it. Check before assuming.
⚠⚠ ROUTE DRAWING IS BLOCKED AS OF 07-31 EOD — and canvas is not the cause
Before today: a tap was SHARED — you got a popup AND a vertex. Messy but usable.
After canvas: the artifact consumes the tap. No vertex lands. Route drawing does not
work.
⚠ Under SVG the artifact layer did not consume the event, so taps fell through to the map by
accident. Canvas did not break the suppression — it removed the accident that was masking it.
The mechanism has been broken since 43ab77e16 (07-03) either way.
⛔ Reverting canvas is the wrong trade (Fred: "more work to strip out today's changes than
to fix the route state"). It would restore a broken mechanism to a merely tolerable failure mode
while giving back the trail hit-rate fix — 3 hits in 40 taps at z18.
⛔ AND THERE IS NO WORKAROUND
Turning trails and tracks off lets the tap through — but then there is no snap and no
guidance. Tracks were removed from snap on 07-30 (snapTrailsOnly, because a track is
one geometry so snapping pulled the whole thing), and hidden trails are not in the query result. You
get free vertices only.
⭐⭐ SO THE FIX MUST DELIVER VISIBLE + SNAPPABLE + NON-INTERACTIVE SIMULTANEOUSLY. During a
route draw you need to SEE trails, SNAP to them, and NOT TAP them. Three concerns the code currently
collapses into one flag.
⚠ Which rules out the SVG approach. sub._path.style.pointerEvents — the line
43ab77e16 deleted — is an SVG DOM property, and canvas paths are not DOM elements. Under
canvas the mechanism is:
lyr.eachLayer(function(sub) { sub.options.interactive = !on; });
Stateless, survives layer rebuilds, works under canvas, and replaces the stash/restore block
entirely. ⚠ VERIFY THIS FIRST — it is the one unknown between the spec and the patch.
⭐⭐ THE SPECIFICATION (Fred, 07-31, verbatim intent)
ConceptMeansRule
Persistencestate RECREATION — position, zoom, artifact display states,
checked listsBoth maps write on every screen refresh. Puts the map back as you left it.
Route modeACTIVELY PLOTTING POINTS RIGHT NOW
⭐ FALSE ON EVERY MAP ENTRY, BOTH MAPS, UNCONDITIONALLY. Entered ONLY by choosing Add
Route. Never restored from persistence.
Draft filea route was not finished
Produces ONE MESSAGE on planner entry: "you have an unsaved route". That is all it does.
No arming, no geometry restore, no drawBuildLine.
routeState.opena session ended without terminating
An END-STATE write. Records only; never arms anything.
THE TAP RULE, entire:
Route mode OFF → tap opens artifacts (popup / detail panel)
Route mode ON → tap places a route point. Nothing else consumes it.
⭐⭐ THEREFORE POPUPS NEVER NEED SUPPRESSING. If the tap does not reach the artifact layer,
no popup can open. Every unbind, stash, restore and bind-gate in the codebase exists to solve a
problem that correct tap routing makes impossible.
THREE EXITS, one entry. Save · save in progress · discard. Each terminates route mode and
writes the end state. To save a recovered draft you go through Add Route like any other route — no
special-cased recovery path.
⚠ Route mode is an ACTIVITY, not restorable state. Fred: "a file on disk means you have
not finished a route. The state is actively plotting points." Two different things, and conflating
them is the whole mess.
⚠ Fred on why a boolean was not enough: "I have had continue messages with no in-flight
files." The flag claimed a state nothing verified — and setting it false does not undo what
setting it true DID (unbound popups, changed pointer events). Termination must REASSERT consequences,
not just write a value.
⛔ THE REGRESSION — commit 43ab77e16, 07-03
Titled "suppress artifact popups during route-build on both maps (unbind/rebind + bind-gate +
force-flag)". It replaced a working stateless mechanism with a broken stateful one:
- if (sub &amp;&amp; sub._path) sub._path.style.pointerEvents = on ? 'none' : '';
+ if (on)  { sub._savedPopupContent = sub.getPopup().getContent(); sub.unbindPopup(); }
+ else     { sub.bindPopup(sub._savedPopupContent); sub._savedPopupContent = null; }
⭐ The deleted line was correct. Stateless, nothing stashed, and it suppressed the TAP
rather than the popup — which is what let route-build taps fall through to the map. The function's own
surviving comment still describes that behaviour: "route their pointer events out so the tap falls
through to map.on('click') → Android.onMapTap (real coords)."
⚠ Why stash/restore cannot work: the viewport lazy-load rebuilds layers on every pan.
_savedPopupContent lives on layer objects that get replaced, so the stash is lost and
popups unbind PERMANENTLY. Observed 07-31: route mode off, popups still gone.
⚠⚠ AND THE GATES ARE INVERTED BETWEEN MAPS — Fred spotted this from behaviour alone:
Planner gates at BIND time (if (!window.__routeMode) layer.bindPopup(...)) —
so it does nothing to layers already drawn. Arming on a populated map has no effect. Ineffective on
the map that owns route mode.
Convoy guards at TAP time (if (window.__routeMode) return;) — always
effective. On the map that cannot create routes at all.

violation: persistence arming a live session flag

that discard actually terminate it?" is currently unanswerable

✅ SOLVED 08-01 — detail panel: the bridge was tested at BIND time

🔴 04 — 2.6e RELEASE TASK: SNAP-2 APPLIES TO TRAILS ONLY
2.6e route planning only — NOT track recording
⭐⭐ Fred 07-29: "tracks can appear on map but snap2 should not be applied to tracks." Route planning snaps to trails only. Tracks keep rendering and stay tappable for details.
Two independent reasons it is right, not a workaround:
Coverage. Track-snapping existed because UGRC's 49,125 trails left real ground unreferenced. At 89,527 OSM trails that gap is largely closed.
lineId correctness. A snapped vertex stores lineId, and a track's lineId is per-rider — ten riders on one trail produce ten tracks with ten IDs. Snapping a route to a track never denoted shared geometry, so it was already wrong for the lead-cart contract.
⭐ SNAP-2 HAS TWO APPLICATIONS AND ONLY ONE CHANGES. Fred: "i am talking about route planning, not track recording. snap2 applies to each cart's track recording individually currently." The recording side snaps each cart's track ONTO trails — it consumes trails as targets, never tracks — so removing tracks from the target set cannot break it. ⚠ One track per cart per database currently.
Likely small: stop passing the track list to RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0). Snap eligibility separates cleanly from display and from tap-for-details.
⚠⚠ VERIFY: this AVOIDS the whole-line bug, it does not fix it. A recorded track is ONE continuous LineString while curated trail networks are pre-segmented — that is why dropping a point ingested the whole track and trails behaved. But Geofabrik ships OSM ways, and a long way is a long single LineString. Test route-drawing on one deliberately long OSM trail before concluding the symptom is gone.
⛔ Do NOT physically split stored tracks or trails. Changing geometry changes geom_hash → breaks dedup and orphans every lineId. If a fix is needed it is linear referencing in Kotlin: record the snapped POINT and its position along the line, never the line's whole geometry.

08-01 EVIDENCEMeasured: a complete data-model rebuild takes UNDER ONE HOUR — OSM import, Utah state trails, tracks, waypoints. This materially lowers the stakes on this item. The argument for in-app delete-by-source rests on avoiding a costly rebuild; the rebuild is not costly. Worth re-weighing before it consumes 2.6e time.
exposure grew by 89,527 rows on 07-29
89,527 OSM trails are in the production spatial DB and there is no in-app way to remove them. deleteAllOsmPoints exists (unwired) for points; there is no trail equivalent.
⚠ Recovery today is a laptop operation: pull the DBs, DELETE ... WHERE source_id='osm', push back. Fine on Droid 2 (sacrificial), not fine for a tester.
⛔ It cannot simply be added: a route's snapped vertices carry lineId, so deleting a trail orphans them silently. That is why bulk delete-by-source was considered and rejected for the release. ⭐ This now needs a decision rather than another deferral.
⚠ Points differ — they carry no source_id; reference_points is OSM-only by construction, so that is a full-table delete. Any delete-by-source must also check for other sources aliasing a row first.

⚠⚠ THE FINDING THAT OUTRANKS THE REST — BOTH MAPS LOAD LEAFLET FROM THE INTERNET
Both map assets pull their core library from public CDNs:
convoy_map.html:7 and grouptrack_map.html:7 —
https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js
convoy_map.html:10 and grouptrack_map.html:10 —
https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/.../leaflet.draw.js
⭐ Line 8 on both is leaflet.polylineDecorator.js with no protocol — a local
asset. So the vendoring pattern already exists in these very files; two libraries simply did not follow it.
⚠ Fred reports all maps render offline today, so this is NOT confirmed as a live defect. The
likely benign explanation is shouldInterceptRequest — the app already intercepts
convoy://tiles/ and may also serve these URLs from assets, in which case the CDN strings are
addresses that are never fetched and there is nothing to fix.
Two commands settle it, no build:
ls app/src/main/assets/ | grep -i "\.js$"
grep -rn "unpkg\|cdnjs\|leaflet" app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/ --include=*.kt | grep -v "\.bak"
How to read it: local copy and an interception rule → working as designed, withdraw the
concern. Local copy but no interception → the local file is unused. No local copy → offline rendering is
riding the WebView cache, which survives normal use but not Clear Storage, not cache eviction, and is
not guaranteed across app updates. The equivalent field test is airplane mode after Clear Storage.
If it does need fixing: download both files into assets/ and change four
src attributes. No logic change, no version drift, and it removes a runtime dependency on two
third-party CDNs from an app whose purpose is working with no signal.

⚠⚠ DURABLE — WHAT THE XREFS CAN AND CANNOT CONFIRM (blast radius)
Established 07-31 while checking exactly this. The xrefs are the blast-radius tool, but their coverage is
narrower than it looks:
where_used_raw.txt is 253 lines and indexes .kt ONLY. Zero HTML, zero
JS. function_universe and navigation_xref likewise.
⛔ So an empty result for a JS symbol means THE TOOL DID NOT LOOK — it is byte-identical to "safe
to delete". This is a false-safety trap and it is how a live function gets removed.
⭐ field_crossref is the strongest of the four: SECTION 4 bridge-method caller
analysis, SECTION 5 state-field [R]/[W] map, SECTION 7 code issues and warnings.
The [R]/[W] markers are what actually answer "who writes this, who reads it".
⚠ It picks up JS fields it tracks (e.g. convoy_map.html:514) but not JS
functions — coverage is field-shaped, not file-shaped.
Rule: for anything JS-side, grep the assets. The xref is necessary and not sufficient.
⚠ .bak_* files in assets/ pollute every grep — four convoy backups
matched the spatial_artifacts search alone. Use --exclude='*.bak*'.

🔵🔵 08 — RELEASE TARGET 2.7 — CONVOY TRACKING REWRITE + MapLibre / VECTOR RENDERING
4-WEEK FRAME (FRED) scoped, nothing built
PURPOSE
Rewrite convoy tracking — the originating requirement — on a renderer that can carry it. Fred: "2.7 is a rewrite of convoy tracking functionality — may be the point we need to introduce these discussions."
SCOPE — 2.7 owns all of this
1a Lead track replacement · 1b Lead cart lock ("In Progress (Not Yet Built)") · 1c Snap-2 on the lead cart track · 1d Vector rendering / MapLibre · 1e spatial_artifacts.js
2 Roads / street names — ingest only · 3 Reprocess / refresh driver · 4 Removals and edits (open, not decided)
⚠ Why this section exists: the convoy tracking rewrite was assigned to 2.7 in session more than two weeks ago and never reached AllDocs — 07-29 was spent reconstructing it from GroupTrack_LeadTrackReplacement_Spec.docx, the Lead Cart Lock section and MAP-06 instead of reading it.
⭐⭐⭐ THE SEQUENCING ARGUMENT (strongest point; survives any storage number)
The dominant cost is not MapLibre — it is operating on FROZEN CODE. ConvoyScreen.kt is frozen to protect the Kotlin↔JS↔Leaflet↔self-saving-setView↔shared-MapStateStore tangle. A convoy tracking rewrite must open exactly that tangle anyway. → The choice is not "rewrite convoy now, renderer later"; it is rewrite that layer ONCE with MapLibre as the target, or TWICE.
⭐⭐ THE onX BENCHMARK (Fred 07-30) — the structural case
onX is vector-based, does three presentations, allows the map to be changed, at ~¼ our storage. Our own device data agrees: the 07-26 delete log showed one SAT job walking three near-identical stores at z18 (SAT 10,295 · SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT 10,292 · SAT_LABELS_PLACES 10,294). Bar 10 post-corridor ≈ 107,000 raster tiles (SAT ~21,700 + transport ~21,700 + places ~21,700 + TOPO 21,000 + TOPO+ 21,000). Strip everything that is not photography → ~21,700, one fifth.
Vector is paid once and serves every presentation. One dataset restyled client-side gives satellite-with-labels, topo and road. Raster pays the full price per presentation — five stores today.
Switching maps becomes free — a consequence of the data being geometry rather than pictures. Not matchable with raster at any storage budget.
Vector stops at ~z14 and the client renders deeper. Since z15–18 is ~98% of raster tile count, vector does not shrink those levels — it removes them.
⭐⭐ DOWNLOAD TIME IS A RELIABILITY METRIC, not a storage complaint (Fred). "8 hours to download an area that will not be ridden." A long job fails partway, needs retry logic we know is imperfect, demands mains power, and gates ride-readiness. The yardstick is time-to-ride-ready and probability of completion. Every open queue defect is amplified by long jobs and materially reduced by short ones.
⛔ CORRECTION TO MY OWN ANALYSIS: I talked the saving down to ≈20% and let that stand as if it settled the question. It answers a narrower one — retiring one label store, on one corridor, in one presentation. The "whole-state road vectors don't shrink with corridor" objection holds for a single corridor in a single presentation and stops being decisive once amortised across three presentations and repeat rides in a region. I was defending a narrow reading of a number instead of testing the case.
⭐ What stays true regardless: satellite imagery is raster, permanently — roughly the ~21,700 floor. The saving is everything that is not photography.
🔴 THE GATE — WebGL on the cheapest field device (NOT YET RUN, half a day)
MapLibre GL JS requires WebGL in the WebView. The fleet includes $60 tablets, and one documented class already cannot hold a BLE connection. onX ships native rendering on modern phones; we would ship GL JS in a WebView on budget hardware. If WebGL will not perform there, this model is unavailable to us at any storage saving — and learning that during the rewrite is the expensive way.
TEST: load vector_label_prototype.html in a plain WebView on Droid 2 and on the cheapest tablet. Check WebGL context creation, pan/zoom at z16–18, frame rate, memory. No frozen code touched. Do this before 2.7 commits to MapLibre.
🔴 TWO MEASUREMENTS OUTSTANDING (seconds each, gpkgs already on D:)
How many gis_osm_roads_free rows carry a non-blank name (Arizona total 1,205,574; trails filter to 134,242 — named roads across all classes could be several hundred thousand, and road labels need LINE geometry for placement, so potentially 300 MB+ on a 108 MB skinny).
How many carry a non-blank ref. If named roads come back ~50k, extract now and never revisit. If ~500k, ref-only is likely the answer — forest/county road numbers (FR 123, CR 45) are worth more than street names for OHV and are renderable in Leaflet today as a midpoint divIcon.
⚠ The "revisit the data" cost is worse than a re-extract: C4 deletes the zip, so adding a layer to the catalog later means users re-download ~600 MB per state.
THE FIVE WORK ITEMS (renderer)
THE RENDERER. Leaflet cannot draw vector tiles → MapLibre GL JS in the same WebView. spatial_artifacts.js rewritten: L.polyline → GeoJSON sources + layer specs; per-feature click handlers → queryRenderedFeatures (MapLibre gives NO DOM per feature). The data path from SpatialDbManager is UNCHANGED.
TILE INTERCEPTION — MapLibre's addProtocol replaces the WebView request intercept; still serving bytes from MBTiles.
⚠ GLYPHS — easiest requirement to miss. MapLibre renders text from font PBFs fetched by URL. Offline means bundling them in assets. No equivalent exists in the raster world, so nothing in the pipeline handles it. Miss it and labels silently do not render offline.
MAP STATE — MapLibre's camera adds bearing and pitch; MapStateStore + the self-saving setView need rework. Nearest the frozen tangle.
GETTING LABEL TILES ON DEVICE — planetiler --only-layers=place,poi,transportation_name,water_name,mountain_peak over a state bbox = a labels-only tileset. Then a product decision: bundle it, or a "download this region" flow.
⚠ ONLY THEN drop the two overlay layers from SAT's entry in getDownloadSources(). One-line config change, but it MUST come LAST or satellite ships with no labels.
⭐⭐ THE CROSS-PLATFORM MULTIPLIER
The presentation layer is already web (Leaflet/HTML/JS in a WebView) and is the ~90% shared surface for iPad and PC; SwiftUI was rejected for presentation precisely because it gives zero reuse of it. MapLibre GL JS is a web library — identical in an Android WebView, an iPad WKWebView and a PC browser. A renderer swap is a one-time change the layer all three surfaces inherit. ⚠⚠ The corollary is a real risk: doing the tracking rewrite on Leaflet BAKES LEAFLET into the layer iPad and PC are both waiting on — a long-tailed decision made by omission.
✅ Validated in a browser prototype 07-26 (no build, no device, no frozen code)
Esri raster imagery + OSM vector labels composite correctly — "the image overlays look perfect."
⭐ OSM vector labels carry MORE data than Esri's downloaded roads/places layers — the opposite of the predicted outcome.
✅ 3D terrain works; Leaflet cannot do it at all. Terrain-RGB encodes metres above sea level in RGB, so the client holds raw elevation → slope-angle shading computed on device, arguably worth more than satellite imagery for an OHV app and a fraction of the cost.
⛔ OSM trail coverage is sparse at low zoom — OSM is a BASEMAP, not a trail source. ⚠ Minor ways only appear from ~z14, so any coverage comparison must be at z15+.
⛔ RULED OUT
Vector satellite imagery (cannot exist) · OSM as a trail authority · tiling user-authored artifacts (tiles are static; tracks are edited constantly) · doing this as a standalone 2.6 task.
Sources: SCOPING_v2.7_vector_rendering_2026-07-26.html · 07-26 Living Master V2.7 KICKOFF · GroupTrack_NewTick_Design_2026-07-01.md (tick/lead/identity rewrite) · GroupTrack_LeadTrackReplacement_Spec.docx · convoy_mapping_ipad_discussion.md (Mar 14) · Fred 07-30 (onX).
🆕 2.7 FEATURE — TRAIL GAP FILL FROM RIDDEN TRACKS (Fred 07-31)
THE PROBLEM, in Fred's words: "trying to draw a route using bits of a track you have
already ridden but trails still do not show."
Route building composes from trails. A stretch you have ridden but which the trail
collection does not cover exists only inside a track — and a track cannot be composed with,
because it is stored as ONE geometry. So when planning, you cannot see all your real choices even
though you have the ground truth on the device.
⭐ These are not a new class of artifact. Fred: "they are trails that simply do not
appear in that collection. you need a trail to ride." Same table, same rendering — the collection
is just missing a piece.
⭐⭐ DISPLAY FIRST, INSERT SECOND — the shape that makes it tractable
Fred: "may be simpler to have a function that shows the map with a colour segment that is
missing and can be added."
Show uncovered stretches as an overlay; the rider decides which become trails.
For tracks in view, compute which point runs have no trail within tolerance
Render those runs as a distinct overlay
Tap the track → artifact detail panel → Add Trail Segment
Only then does anything enter the trails table
⭐ This removes three problems at once, which is why it is better than automatic insertion
at import time:
Tolerance stops being critical. A false positive is visible noise the rider ignores, not a
duplicate trail silently written to the DB.
Naming resolves itself — the user is looking at it.
Nothing accumulates against dedup, and GPS wobble never becomes authoritative geometry by
accident.
⭐ And it is useful before the insert step is written at all. Simply SEEING where ridden
ground is missing from the collection answers the original frustration; adding it becomes optional.
Design detail settled 07-31
Detection. Sample the track's points; for each, test distance to trail geometry returned by
queryTrailsByViewport for a small bbox. Consecutive points with nothing within tolerance
form an uncovered run. Discard runs below a minimum length.
⭐ RouteManager.snap(lat, lon, trails, tracks, 30.0) already performs this proximity
test and returns null when nothing is near — "null" IS "uncovered", so detection is mostly
free.
Tolerance 20–30 m, matching the existing snap radius. ⚠ Too tight and GPS wobble alongside a
mapped trail reads as uncovered, producing a shadow trail parallel to a real one — that is the failure
mode to design against, and it is the argument for showing rather than auto-inserting.
Naming — Fred's rule: inherit the name ONLY if the trail either side of the gap carries the
same name. Both endpoints agreeing is strong evidence it is one trail; disagreeing means it
connects two, and inventing a name there would be wrong. Otherwise leave it unnamed.
⚠ Unnamed is correct, not a fallback. Fred: "most of our trails are unnamed now and named
would have a major trail connotation." A named trail SIGNALS significance to a rider, and today's
ORDER BY sorts named first — so auto-naming gap fills would both inflate that signal and
outrank real named trails at low zoom.
Colour. ⚠ Dashed is already taken — tracks are #39FF14 dashed, routes
#FF00FF dot-dash, trails carry carto_code colours. A solid line in an unused
colour will read more clearly than another dash pattern.
🔴 OPEN QUESTION — which gap, when a track has several
The detail panel opens for the WHOLE track, but uncovered stretches are specific sub-ranges. A
track with three gaps makes "Add Trail Segment" ambiguous — and that is exactly the case that
motivated this.
⭐ Fred's motivating case: several tracks named Broken Ridge in one area. From a
route-planning standpoint that is unusable, because you can only select whole tracks. Segmenting the
uncovered stretches makes it a set of distinct short pieces you can assemble — and "which Broken
Ridge" stops mattering, because you are choosing a STRETCH, not a name.
Likely resolution: the overlay lines are separate L.polyline objects, so each
can carry its own point-range identity and pass that through — rather than routing everything via
track_id alone.
⚠ Worth measuring before building
How much would this actually find? Utah now carries 89,536 OSM trails. If ridden tracks are
95% covered, this produces stubs and the effort is not repaid; at 40% it is a substantial feature.
⭐ Measurable PC-side in minutes against the spatial DB — sample a track's points, test
distance to trail geometry, report the uncovered fraction. No app code. And measure it on the
Broken Ridge area specifically, not statewide — that is the case that motivates it.
⚠ Depends on today's detail-panel work. The flow ends at "tap the track → panel → Add Trail
Segment", which only became possible once addPointMode stopped suppressing planner track
taps and __detailPanelEnabled was re-enabled. Both landed 07-31.

Server-side function that belongs under a hosting release (NOT a release title)
Same-ride track dedup — pruning duplicate recordings when tracks are served. ⚠ This is a HOSTING problem and only exists once tracks are served. Locally, ten riders each holding their own recording of one ride is CORRECT.
⛔ geom_hash cannot do this job. Perfect for trails (89,536 rows / 89,536 hashes; the 313 UT/AZ border trails collapsing automatically prove it). Useless for tracks from one ride: ten devices drop GPS points at different moments → ten point sets, ten hashes, all legitimately the same ride.
⭐ COLLAPSE FOR PRESENTATION, DO NOT DELETE. Canonical track per hash, hash + date → alias. Nobody loses their own ride and the collapse stays reversible. Server-side, not on the phone. Scope is bounded (same bbox + date window). Goal is "prune as best we can", not perfect matching.
Candidate metrics (none chosen): bbox overlap + Hausdorff/Fréchet · rounded/simplified-geometry hash · start/stop coordinates + time window (Fred 07-29, cheaper than either) ⚠ needs tolerance on both axes.
⭐ CROSS-REFERENCE, not scope: 2.7's snap-2 makes recorded tracks converge on shared trail geometry, so part of this becomes hash-matchable outright. That work belongs to 2.7.
⚠ Two riders on the same ground can store different lineIds. For DRAWING it does not matter; it matters only when two routes are COMPARED. Fix at compare time by geometry proximity, never by making snap pick differently.
🟣 11 — RELEASE TARGET 4.0 — PAYGATED BACK-END SERVER-SIDE FUNCTIONS

📱 12 — iPAD — POST-V2.6 TARGET (restored 07-30; was absent from the checklist entirely)
185 AllDocs mentions · 0 in the Living Master before today
The evolution — four iterations, all in the corpus
Native port via external dev — Roadmap V9, Mar 25 (iOS-01..08: fork Meshtastic-iOS, Apple Developer enrollment $99/yr, port the coordination layer, WKWebView + convoy_map.html, offline tiles in Swift, Apple IAP, TestFlight, com.grouptrack.ios).
Staged Options A–D incl. WKWebView hybrid — Mar 14 discussion doc (short term: Meshtastic Apple as a display-only viewer, zero dev cost; medium: WKWebView hybrid, 2–3 weeks; long: full Swift fork).
PWA-via-Bluefy-then-Capacitor — May notes.
Repeatedly flagged "iPad V2.5 vs V3.0, not resolved."
⭐ THE COLLAPSE (07-04) — the whole PWA arc solved a non-problem
Convoy is a fork/extension of core Meshtastic's messaging. The native-vs-PWA-vs-WKWebView arc was all answering "how do we get BLE on iOS?" — a question that dissolves once convoy is understood as a fork of the mesh app. So iPad = a fork of Meshtastic-Apple (Swift/SwiftUI + Core Data + BLE + protobuf; already App-Store-approved; universal incl. iPad; ships an offline map + radio config). Mac + Xcode is the prerequisite. ⚠ FLAG: Meshtastic-Apple ships native TAK/CoT — reconcile against the roadmap's "TAK as design pattern only."
🔴 STILL OPEN — the A/B decision
(A) BRIDGE — convoy is its own native iOS app consuming mesh messages from the separate Meshtastic app over a local port. Less code; adds a runtime dependency + iOS-lifecycle fragility. (B) FORK — import Meshtastic's BLE/mesh and extend, as on Android. More work; no runtime dependency; same architecture as Android. Trade: effort favours A; field reliability + Android-sameness favour B. For an off-grid safety app, "bridge dies if iOS backgrounds the neighbour app" is a real mark against A — leans B, not decided.
Settled
Three surfaces split on connectivity: PC = planning-only web app (no mesh, no radio, online) · Android + iPad = off-grid native convoy execution. Convoy cannot be web.
SwiftUI REJECTED for presentation — does not port to a browser, zero reuse of the Android web layer. Swift's only job on iPad is the native shell (mesh source + WebView host + JS↔native bridge).
Config write is offloaded: the planning side creates a Meshtastic restore FILE; Meshtastic's own restore applies it. GroupTrack never does BLE for config.
KMP is the natural target — logic is already Kotlin; migration is incremental, expect/actual is literally "configured API resolves per platform." Does not let you fork Meshtastic-Apple (that is Swift); produces a shared logic module a Swift shell consumes.
Target end-state: a messaging/logic service layer behind an interface + logic-free presentation panels. Serving three platforms means logic written ONCE, not three copies.
🔴 NEXT ACTION (unchanged since 07-04, still not done)
Enumerate the bridge/IO surface from the current Android code — every JavascriptInterface method + every evaluateJavascript/postMessage crossing. That inventory is the true iPad build cost AND which functions can/cannot go to PC. It is the blast-radius question the xref docs answer.
Sources: GroupTrack_CrossPlatform_iPad_Strategy_2026-07-04.md · convoy_mapping_ipad_discussion.md (Mar 14) · Roadmap V9 §iPad Strategy + iOS-01..08.

A dead source can still be chosen and queued — jobs segment and enqueue normally, then every tile fails. Burns queue time; may leave an empty/partial .mbtiles that later looks like a corrupt download.
⚠ Rule it in or out as a feeder for the open queue defects — markComplete refreshMode collision, refresh-never-completes, ETA starvation. A source where every fetch fails is exactly the input that would make completion accounting behave strangely.

⛔ REJECTED — AND WHY (this section is new and belongs on every release block)
Google Hybrid / Google tiles: rejected on download reliability, field-observed — free Google download resources proved slow and unreliable at bulk scale — and now on dead endpoint. NOT rejected on quality or storage, and NOT reversible by a storage argument.
⚠ THE ARCHIVE CURRENTLY ARGUES THE OPPOSITE. GroupTrack_V25_MapTileSourceReference_v1.md (May 9) says Google tiles "work reliably and have for years" and recommends them as "the best free option for off-road", calling Google Hybrid "best overall hybrid." Fred's field evidence overturned that and the overturning was never written down. A future session scouring the corpus finds "one store instead of three, saves 3×" and re-proposes exactly what already failed. This entry exists to close that loop.
⭐⭐ THE METHOD LESSON (Fred 07-30) — why this happened
That May 9 document is 19,514 chars and eight sections: every URL template, {y}/{x} ordering gotchas, rate limits, API-key tiers, a tile_sources table design, Leaflet integration code. It is a thorough catalogue with no risk analysis, no strengths/weaknesses column, and no storage arithmetic — and the consequence sat in its own text: Google Hybrid = satellite + labels in ONE stream (1×); Esri World Imagery = no labels, therefore two extra raster label stores (3×). SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES appear in the handoffs from May 10 — the very next day — and the multiplication was never performed. It surfaced on 07-26 from a delete log, and Fred spotted it: "it is 65,000 tiles because of the three layers."
The Esri choice was right on the axis that governs (bulk download reliability beats storage efficiency for an offline-first app). A risk table would not have changed the source — it would have moved the vector conversation to May, before Leaflet was wired in and before the tangle froze.
⚠ Also unweighed at the time and still live: Esri World Imagery is flagged in that same doc as legacy "mature support" — Esri pushing migration, max zoom 19 vs Google's 20. Both are risk-column entries about the dependency the whole map rests on.
⭐ STANDING STRUCTURE, all release blocks: options side by side · strengths · weaknesses · what it costs later · the risk that would reverse the choice · the cheap test that would settle it. Applied now: the WebGL-on-cheap-device test before MapLibre is committed to.
🔴🔴 14 — CARRIED FROM 07-27: MAP REFRESH ON SOURCE CHANGE (do first, stop-the-bleeding)
DO FIRST not a root-cause fix
The REPLACE/refresh function on the map-source select screen spawned 3287 downloads, lat/long spanning the continental US; downloads then stopped entirely.
⚠ Cancel All does NOT persist. Cancel appeared to clear the queue; all 3287 jobs resurfaced on restart — the clear happens in memory and is never written to disk, so loadQueue re-reads the stale file every launch. This is the boot-loop mechanism, demonstrated — just without a crash.
⛔ No recovery path on a release build. adb run-as = denied; X-plore cannot reach Android/data/&lt;pkg&gt;/ — Android 13+ removed third-party file-manager access entirely, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE excludes it, the document-tree picker refuses it. Only root, adb-on-debuggable, or the app itself can read there. The only escape is Clear-App-Data.
Decision (Fred 07-23): turn off the JSON write / auto-refresh on source change. Refresh becomes manually requested as an Area download, riding the hardened submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells path. DISABLE, don't delete — gate behind a marked constant; the bug is still undiagnosed and the path will be wanted.
⚠ This does NOT fix Cancel All — separate defect, still open.
⛔ DO NOT run replace-map-source again until this ships — recovery costs an hour and possibly all app-internal data.
Root cause still open: leading hypothesis is that the bbox handed to enqueueRefresh is not the viewport — a zero-initialised value, or swapped bounds arguments. Note 3287 ≈ ceil(enormous/50K), so segmentation worked correctly on garbage input → the bug is upstream of segmentCells. Compare ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt:255-290 against ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:218-250 for argument order; also read ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:440-490 (:473 declares a quarantine file, and it is likely the same function where cancel's persistence fails).

THE GOAL (Fred 08-06, verbatim intent)
⭐⭐⭐ "I do not care about route. I am trying to create a method where a PRE-RIDE
ROUTE CAN BE DISTRIBUTED AND IMPORTED WITH MAPS, allowing a rider to download accurate maps with
efficient space utilisation BEFORE TRAILS ARE CAPTURED."
⭐ CORRIDOR, NOT AREA. Fred 08-09: "we know 90% of area are air." Confirmed by the
08-08 measurement — 30 tracks swept as areas cost 2M+ tiles on ONE source; 89 as corridors cost
1.5M across THREE. A route bbox is mostly air, so route downloads run as corridors from the WKT.
⚠ Half a mile either side is the padding (~1 mile band). Fred 08-09: "we should be fine
with maps downloaded and trail being on it." ⚠ Holds for a SNAPPED route, whose geometry IS
trail geometry via snap-2. A DRAWN route cuts across country — its corridor covers ground the rider
will not travel and misses the trail where it bends. Open: does a drawn route download at all,
or must it be snapped first?
⭐ WHAT FRED TESTED 08-09 — TWO THINGS DO NOT WORK TODAY
SAVE MAPS does not render for routes. ArtifactDetailPanel:111 gates on
artifactType == "Tracks" &amp;&amp; onDownloadCorridor != null.
⭐ The panel is otherwise ALREADY generic — line 27 documents "Routes" as valid, and
rename/delete work for them (only Trails is excluded). SAVE MAPS is the one place someone
narrowed it.
Import did not process maps for routes. Routes may have imported as artifacts —
unconfirmed which half failed. ConvoyMapViewerScreen:230 calls
ConvoyTrackOps.importGpxAllArtifacts.
⭐⭐ THE ARTIFACT-SPECIFIC SURFACE IS THREE LINES. EVERYTHING ELSE IS ALREADY GENERIC.
ComponentArtifact-specific?
enqueueCorridor:667 getTrackPoints(context, geomHash)
YES — geometry resolve
enqueueCorridor:~702 allTrackGeomHashes() label lookup
YES — a route would show a hex fragment as its queue label
ConvoyCorridorWorker:49 re-resolves from inputData
YES — the job may run in a fresh process
corridorTiles(segments)✅ takes points, no opinion
slot/layer multiplier · bbox loop · QueueEntry✅ all derive from segments
worker dispatch · download · progress · tile write · ORPHAN block · markFailed✅ untouched
⭐ So there is NO second worker, NO parallel enqueue, NO duplicated job-building. Fred
08-09: "two new callable functions, return geometry for tracks and return geometry for artifacts,
and all the work comes out of here and does not complicate this job."
⭐⭐ THE BUILD — TWO PASSES (Fred 08-09)
"Separate the existing working function into a new route/track solution but only
implement the existing track in the new method. We will test and certify and then introduce the
route bits."
⭐ WHY: this is the 08-08 lesson applied. Every component of the migration was already
working; the REASSEMBLY introduced the defects and cost a device rebuild. Proving the refactor
behaviour-neutral first means any failure in pass 2 is unambiguously the route code.
PASS 1 — structure only, ZERO behaviour change:
resolveGeometry(context, type, key)   -> wraps getTrackPoints; "Tracks" only
resolveLabel(context, type, key)      -> wraps allTrackGeomHashes; "Tracks" only
enqueueCorridor(..., artifactType)    -> explicit at EVERY call site
QueueEntry.artifactType               -> new field, persisted
inputData "artifact_type"             -> worker reads it, calls resolveGeometry
CERTIFY PASS 1: corridor downloads behave EXACTLY as before — same tile counts, same queue
rows, same labels, same completions. Nothing new in the UI, so any difference is a regression.
PASS 2 — routes: the route branch in both resolvers · the routes SAVE MAPS button ·
import offers downloads at the END of the batch (Fred: "current import process creates db tables
and submits imports at the end. I prefer that approach.") · route-create on final save.
⭐ Fred's entry-point order: prove it from Work-With-Artifacts FIRST — a stable bench where
any number of SAVE MAPS requests can be submitted — then attach to import and route-create by
artifact key.
⚠ DECISIONS AND TRAPS — carry these into the build
⛔ NO DEFAULT ON artifactType. ~7 call sites edited explicitly. A default
silently sends a route to the tracks table — CODE RULE 1.
⚠ replaceExisting: Boolean = false is an existing default at a function we are
touching — CODE RULE 2 says evaluate it at point of contact.
⛔ THE SILENT SKIP AT :670. No geometry returns 0 with a log warning, and
enqueueCorridorBatch counts it as SKIPPED, not failed. A route that cannot
resolve would report as skipped and download nothing — worse than an error, because it looks like
it worked. ⭐ Make it a real failure during PASS 1, before routes can hit it.
⚠ QueueEntry.geomHash becomes a KEY whose meaning depends on type (routes
would put a route id there). Name it honestly in pass 1 rather than leaving a field called
geomHash holding a route id in pass 2.
⚠ SERIALISATION MUST BE BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE — startedAt/tilesPerSec
were added 08-08 with optLong/optDouble so old queue files still load.
The new field needs the same, or Droid 2's persisted queue breaks on read.
⚠ The worker error text at :55 ("Corridor job missing track or source")
becomes wrong for routes.
⭐ ADD THE ENTRY ID TO THE COMPLETION LOG LINE. The start line carries
id= and hash=; Corridor complete carries NEITHER, so per-job
durations cannot be matched from logcat — proven on 08-09 when the analysis had to fall back to
completion sums. One field makes every future run exactly measurable.
⚠ A BATCH SUBMIT IS WHERE 08-08 BIT. The migration queued 172 jobs and became
unexitable. Route import producing several corridors must show the count BEFORE submitting and
leave a way out after.
⚠ Dedup: a route drawn along an existing track produces an IDENTICAL geom hash.
resolveByGeom(type, name, geomHash) is type-aware so probably fine — verify, or
planning a route over known trail could fail to save.
⚠ insertRoute returns a FABRICATED id on duplicates — newId(),
then INSERT OR IGNORE, then returns the fabricated id rather than the surviving row's.
Fix while in there (carried from 07-27).
⭐ A mixed route is the best test artifact (Fred 08-09): snap-2 segments and straight-line
draws within ONE route exercise the whole range at once. Snapped portions should hug the trail;
drawn portions produce a straight band across country. If they look identical, something is
re-deriving geometry instead of using what was stored.
⭐ The blocker dissolved on inspection: the routes table already carries geom_hash. ⚠ Defects to fix while in there: insertRoute returns a fabricated id on duplicates — newId(), then INSERT OR IGNORE, then returns the fabricated id rather than the surviving row's.

🟠 19 — FIX 6 — PLANNER PADDING DRIFT (Fred priority)
FRED PRIORITY
"Annoying continually entering a shrinking panel." Trail shrinks / map grows on every reopen: the FIT function is reused for persistence, so restore re-pads an already-padded saved bbox → cumulative zoom-out.
Chosen fix: explicit padding argument — fitToBounds(bbox, padding:Int); restore passes 0, content-fit passes ~60. If the function is SHARED with convoy, default the argument to the content-fit value so convoy's call site is untouched (respects the freeze).
Scope first: grep -rn "fitBounds\|fitToBounds" --include='*.kt' app/src/main/java/ and grep -n "fitBounds" app/src/main/assets/*.html — the planner fit may go through the HTML.
THE PERSIST CHAIN (confirmed 07-29, three hops): the fit call → (…, 400) (MVS:284-285) → savePlanningState() (MVS:259) writes planning_panel.json. ⚠ savePlanningState() reads lastViewport* and ONLY onViewportChanged sets them, so a redraw racing a map move can persist a stale viewport.
⛔ CORRECTION: "convoy has cumulative zoom-out" is misleading as written — the convoy map is frozen and its call site is untouched; the drift is the planner's restore path.
THE PLANNER HAS TWO FIT IDIOMS AND THEY DISAGREE — site idiom vs content idiom. Reconcile before patching.

THE DISCARD BUG — root cause found + fixed + device-verified. The toolbar
Discard button (ConvoyRouteToolbar:196) branches
if (routeLifecycleState == ROUTE_LS_RESUMED) onDiscardRequested() else onExit(). For a
NEW route it called onExit(), which cleared the screen + memory but had no

onExit (ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt ~1651). Device-verified on Droid 2: create
route, 5 pts, Discard → route_drafts/ empty. Committed f9652276c.

branches we had bolted on during the earlier DISCARDWINS attempts (they fought the flow). Net
7 insertions, 22 deletions.

▶ TOMORROW — TWO TASKS, IN ORDER. Full detail so a fresh conversation can execute.
TASK 1 — Standardize all discard functions to the same 6-call teardown
Why: the discard/teardown logic is duplicated across sites, each doing a different
subset of the steps — classic copy-paste drift, and exactly what let the onExit bug hide.
Fred: "standardize all discard functions to the same 6 calls … there is no reason for the
differences." Consistency pass FIRST (safe — only adds missing steps), refactor to a shared
function SECOND (separate, later step). Rationale: refactoring identical code is safe;
consolidating divergent code forces picking a winner per difference and can propagate a bug to every
call site at once.
The canonical 6-step teardown (active-session discard):
1. RouteManager.clearRoute()
2. RouteDraftStore.deleteDraft(&lt;name&gt;)
3. webViewRef?.evaluateJavascript("setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine();", null)
4. addPointMode = false
5. routeMode = false
6. draftListTick++
Sites in app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt
(⚠ RE-GREP line numbers first — they drift every edit):

🗣 00-2.7-DISCUSSION — planning substrate for 2.7 (accumulated design findings, 08-14). NOT a spec — a roadmap to plan from.
⭐⭐ FEATURE VISION (Fred 08-15) — THE "MOST INTERESTING ROUTE" PLANNER. Differentiated; future (2.7+ / own tier). NOT 2.6f.
The feature: user drops vertices/waypoints all over a map → app auto-designs 3-4 DISTINCT rideable routes, each 45-60 miles / 5-9 hours of riding (at OHV speeds), that collectively connect all the dropped points. Multi-day trip planning over the trail network.
⭐ THE DIFFERENTIATOR: existing routing (Google/onX/standard nav) optimizes SHORTEST/FASTEST. OURS optimizes the MOST INTERESTING route — the best RIDE, not the quickest path. For OHV riders "shortest" is the WRONG answer; nobody off-roads to get somewhere fast. We BORROW the routing machinery (graph traversal / pathfinding — solved, take from existing algos) but CHANGE THE OBJECTIVE FUNCTION from minimize-distance to MAXIMIZE-INTERESTINGNESS. Plumbing is standard; the optimization TARGET is ours = the innovation.
The real work isn't the algorithm (borrow it) — it's DEFINING "interesting" (a product problem = where we win). Scoring inputs: trail quality/difficulty (technical sections, the good stuff — Thunderforest Outdoors trail data + trail classifications), scenery (overlooks, vistas, terrain variety), loop-ness (good rides loop, not out-and-back), variety (mix trail types, avoid 40mi of the same fire road), hitting the user's dropped waypoints, all within the 45-60mi/5-9hr envelope as the FRAME. Leans on the spatial DB (89K trails, routing graph) + RideCalc (10-15 mph → the constraint that makes it multi-DAY trip planning, not point-to-point). Big nav apps CAN'T easily do this — built around shortest-path, no OHV-trail-quality data, no rider's-day framing. ⚠ constrained-optimization / vehicle-routing-family problem (distance + time + coverage constraints) — real algorithm needed (nearest-neighbor+constraints or a proper solver). Fits the 2.7 MapLibre/spatial-routing direction. NOT 2.6f (compliance only), likely 2.7+ or its own premium-tier feature.
Raw findings recovered from the design docs + past conversations on 08-14, parked here so 2.7 planning starts from what's already been analyzed rather than re-recovering it. Each item tagged DECIDED / OPEN. Sources: SCOPING_v2.7_vector_rendering_2026-07-26.html, memory grouptrack-vector-rendering / grouptrack-map-sources, and conversations "Track map downloading in 2.6c corridor" (07-26), "Release 2.6e route and convoy handling improvements" (08-02).
Rendering engine — the core decision
DECIDED 08-14 MapLibre, rendering satellite imagery, to leverage the spatial DB + improve functionality + tighter integration with existing JS functions. INTEGRATE not rip-and-replace: JS functions kept and integrated more tightly; MapLibre upgrades the rendering surface beneath them; spatial DB drives sat-image rendering.
DECIDED 08-02 ⭐⭐ THE (A)/(B) SPLIT — carry this into planning, every prior version bundled them:
(A) MapLibre as RENDERER, raster/satellite sources UNCHANGED — gets rotation, 3D tilt, Terrain-RGB slope shading, data-driven artifact styling, and the iPad/PC cross-platform multiplier, while satellite stays exactly as it is. (B) VECTOR BASEMAPS — the storage-savings argument. ⭐ (A) does NOT require (B). The 08-14 direction (sat imagery in MapLibre) is essentially (A).
DECIDED Fred 08-02: "If I could rotate sats we would not be having this discussion." → He CAN — MapLibre rotates RASTER tiles, the camera is source-agnostic. Rotation/tilt/pitch all work on plain satellite with no vector tiles. Leaflet cannot rotate at all (a Leaflet limitation, not a raster one).
What (A) buys — judge each on load-bearing vs. pleasant (Fred's framing)
WEIGH Rotation (heading-up) — arguably NAVIGATION, not decoration: a rider following a trail reads a rotated map faster than north-up (every handheld GPS offers it). Judge SEPARATELY from 3D — it was not previously on the list.
WEIGH Terrain-RGB slope shading — for OHV arguably more useful than the imagery itself.
WEIGH Cross-platform reuse — MapLibre GL is both native iOS/macOS SDK and JS lib; map layer is already HTML/JS in a WebView → one renderer all three surfaces (Android/iPad/PC) inherit. Ties to 2.8.
WEIGH 3D tilt / styling polish — closer to genuinely nice-to-have.
The real cost of (A) — known and large
Renderer swap on FROZEN code — the dominant cost is operating on the frozen convoy tangle. ⭐ SEQUENCING ARGUMENT: a convoy rewrite opens that tangle anyway → rewrite the layer ONCE with MapLibre as target, or TWICE. (This is why 2.7 = convoy rewrite is the right home.)
spatial_artifacts.js rewritten from L.polyline to GeoJSON sources + layer specs (MapLibre gives no DOM per feature — queryRenderedFeatures instead).
MapStateStore + self-saving setView extended for BEARING and PITCH.
Tile interception moves from shouldInterceptRequest to MapLibre's addProtocol. ⭐ ties to the 2.6e shared-tile-module work — build that module with this migration in mind.
⚠ Snap is UNAFFECTED — it's Kotlin, renderer-independent, resolves by DB ID.
⚠⚠ 08-02 — "THE WHOLE APP CHANGES, MAP SOURCES ETC HAVE TO BE RE-THOUGHT." A MapLibre move re-opens the whole source model: the catalog is RASTER-SHAPED (url_template {z}/{x}/{y}, cache_dir, max_zoom per source); vector needs a style spec, glyph/sprite URLs, source-layers. And the SLOT concept assumes 4 mutually-exclusive raster basemaps while MapLibre composites raster+vector+terrain simultaneously — slots may not survive as a concept.
If (B) vector is ever pursued — the storage arithmetic + gotchas (parked, not decided)
≈80% tile reduction finding: two of SAT's three stores are LABELS not photography (place + transportation labels delivered as photographs of words). Bar 10: ~107,000 raster → ~21,700 with vector labels. Vector is small because it STOPS at ~z14 and renders deeper by scaling geometry — z15-18 is ~98% of downloads; vector removes those levels rather than shrinking them.
⛔ GLYPH BUNDLING for offline labels — the requirement most likely to be missed if (B) is done.
⚠ The storage argument is the part that FAILS in the woods (tagged-data coverage question) — which is why (A) may be all that's wanted.

The move — Mac Air/Pro replaces the PC for ALL development
DECIDED Confirmed "release 2.8 in your numbering." Goals: performance (builds hit 33–53 min under PC disk pressure), storage, and positioning for the Mac/iPad version discussion.
⛔ The irreplaceable item — handle first
The release keystore (grouptrack-release-key.jks). Everything else re-downloads or re-clones; the keystore cannot — lose it and you can never update the Play listing again. HANDLED already in 4 locations under /GroupTrack Application Keys/ (local, Google Drive, iCloud, Desktop) — the two cloud copies reach the Mac immediately. Whatever holds its passwords (keystore.properties/gradle.properties/password manager) travels with it.
Traps specific to this setup
PLAN Line endings. Every commit prints "LF will be replaced by CRLF" — working tree is CRLF, repo stores LF, macOS checks out LF natively. Done carelessly, the first git status on the Mac shows EVERY file modified. Plan .gitattributes/config so it doesn't churn the tree.
PORT Machine-specific tooling — patch scripts hardcode C:\Users\kixaz\...; build output → /d/; commands use MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 (Git Bash only); local.properties points at a Windows SDK path. A rewrite pass, not a copy.
MOVE The generation machinery, not just outputs — the xref generators, AllDocs assembly, the doc history used to gen AllDocs, any Google Drive activity/stores. Not in git, can't be reconstructed. (Inventory these before the move.)
VERIFY Devices need re-authorizing — ADB's RSA key is per-machine, both Droids re-prompt.
What must move
Irreplaceable: keystore + passwords · uncommitted work · unpushed branches/stashes · AllDocs · Downloads/ fallback sets. Credentials: Play Console, AWS RDS, PHP API, Thunderforest key, Crashlytics/Firebase. Reinstallable: JDK, Android SDK, Gradle, platform-tools. SQLite tooling is a non-issue — macOS ships sqlite3 built in (more than the PC had); DB Browser runs native on Apple silicon; workflow (adb pull → inspect locally) is identical minus MSYS_NO_PATHCONV (commands get SIMPLER).
⚠ AWS access from New Hampshire (blocking sub-item)
Console access is NOT IP-restricted (sign in from anywhere). The RDS security group IS — add current IP as an inbound rule (VPC → Security Groups → RDS one). ⚠ Home IP is dynamic (can re-lock). ⛔ EC2 blocked since March on a support case (PRE-01/02/03) — so RDS may be only half of what's needed if the PHP API is unreachable. Tie in with the 2.6e credential rotation.
Cross-platform / iPad — what the move positions for
OBJECTIVE Fred: "two platforms sharing as much of the code base and implementation as possible."
First step (Fred's plan): Apple browser supporting Bluetooth updates → deploy the app in-browser on iPad. ⚠ Web Bluetooth is NOT in Safari — it's Bluefy (a WebKit browser implementing Web Bluetooth). Changes the distribution story (users install a 3rd-party browser first; small vendor).
⭐ What it buys: map layer is already HTML/JS in a WebView → a browser-hosted version reaches iPad with no App Store review, no second signing identity, no Swift. Proves the shared-code thesis cheaply.
⚠ What it CAN'T do: background track recording (a tab can't record with screen off), storage at scale (browser storage capped/evictable — nothing like a 14GB MBTiles file), filesystem access. So it PROVES the architecture split, it's not a shipping product. (Gaia/onX store GBs because they're NATIVE apps — that's the difference.)
⭐ MapLibre is well-suited: exists as both native iOS/macOS SDK and JS — the 2.7 renderer rewrite could run on both without a fork. Doing 2.7 on the Mac = the point the architecture starts being written for two targets.
DECIDE EARLY How far the shared layer extends (SpatialDbManager/tile store/queue are Kotlin → KMP candidate; the service-layer split decides how much survives), and whether 2.7 targets iPad or just develops on Mac (building ON vs building FOR Apple — the second means a 2nd signing identity, store, test device). ⚠ A rewrite carrying a second platform as a constraint is slower — be explicit: Android-only with a portable interior, or genuinely dual-target. Memory: grouptrack-crossplatform (service layer + logic-free panels, Mac-first sequencing).
✅ 00-2.6e-OPEN — FINALIZED 08-14. The definitive 2.6e open-items list (discovery complete; supersedes the scattered pre-2.6 backlog).
Result of the 08-14 discovery pass over the 07-13/07-22 pre-2.6 backlog + accumulated operational items, with Fred's 08-14 scope decisions applied. Killed/closed items recorded at the bottom so nothing is silently dropped. This is the list that gates 2.6e.
⭐ BUILD ORDER (Fred 08-14) — MODULE/COMPONENT WORK FIRST, INSTALL REDESIGN LAST.The feature/module tasks (Task A route display+fit, Task B calc, discard consolidation, tile-intercept module, rename/delete triggers) all fit the methodology below and share momentum + a clear plan — do them while that's true. The install/authority blocker tier (items 7–9) is scheduled LAST: it's a different kind of work — a high-stakes data-safety fix needing its own focused session and verification on a GENUINE fresh install — so it doesn't interleave well with the module cadence. It remains a hard gate on shipping 2.6e; last in build order, not last in priority.
⛔ OVERRIDING RULE — EVERY SEGMENT (Fred 08-14). IDENTIFY DUPLICATE CODE IMPLEMENTATIONS AND FACTOR THEM INTO CALLABLE MODULES WHENEVER THEY ARE DISCOVERED.This is a continuous operating rule, not a per-task technique. During ALL work — any segment, any release — actively watch for the same logic implemented in more than one place, and when found, extract it into ONE callable module and wire the call sites. Duplicate implementations are the root disease behind this project's worst bugs (the discard bug = six divergent teardowns; the two tile intercepts; the scattered distance calcs) — each copy drifts and one silently misses a step. De-duplication is therefore a reflex during every segment, whether or not the task is nominally about consolidation. HOW (the supporting discipline below): shared modules not parallel implementations · build components then string them · stub-first (mark all call sites, build once, grep every stub wired) · consistency-first then consolidate (never extract from divergent copies — make them consistent first, or you propagate a bug to all sites at once).
⭐ STANDING ARCHITECTURE DIRECTION (Fred 08-14) — SHARED MODULES, NOT PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATIONS.The same disease behind the discard bug (scattered duplicated logic, each copy drifting and missing a different step) applies across the app. The cure is the same everywhere: a capability lives in ONE reusable module, called from multiple places — never reimplemented per surface. Applies to: local-tile retrieval (one module, both maps' shouldInterceptRequest call it — item 6), distance + ride-time calc (called functions any surface uses — artifact panels, route planning, trail display — Task B), and going forward any capability that would otherwise be copied per screen/per artifact type. ⚠ When fixing a "missing on surface B" gap, EXTRACT the shared module and wire both — do NOT copy surface A's implementation to B (that creates the second copy that drifts).
⭐ BUILD METHOD — STUB-FIRST (Fred 08-14). For any new shared module: (1) IDENTIFY the module — fix its name/signature/return even before implementing; (2) PLACE PLACEHOLDER STUBS at every call site that needs it, with a grep-able marker (e.g. // STUB:RIDECALC) so every consumer is identified up front; (3) BUILD OUT the module once; (4) VERIFY every stub was converted to the real call — grep -c the marker (= all sites before, = 0 after), no stub left unwired. ⭐ Step 4 makes the stubs a completeness CHECKLIST — you cannot forget a call site because they were all marked first. This is exactly the discipline that would have caught the discard bug (a missing call at one exit would show as an unconverted stub). Pairs with the existing marker-count patch verification.

Data-recovery — the REBUILD function (recovery side of the install story; designed in §00-RECOVERYFILE)
Fred's last known 2.6e item. The recovery/healing side of the data-safety story: an install error means a protected-data reinstall, and this is how you rebuild afterward — unattended, from a recipe, instead of manual reconstruction. Full design already in §00-RECOVERYFILE — do NOT redesign; this is the wiring + display item. ⭐ BUILD ORDER: QUEUED AFTER the install revisions (which are themselves last) — DR follows the install fix.
Rebuild function + Recovery display. A rebuild function that consumes the map-configuration recipe (the .gtmaps file the recipe writer produces — a few-KB JSON of slots + boxes, the same quadtree enqueueRecreateSource computes), linked to a Recovery display that shows: (a) the current 60-day window of restore points (the recipe writer keeps one file/day, deletes >60 days; the date in the filename IS the index), listed by date with tile counts; (b) any recipe available in Downloads (import via the picker/content-URI path — needs no All-Files authority). Select a restore point or recipe → REBUILD (or EMAIL). ⭐ CLEAR-vs-ADD CHOICE (Fred 08-14): the user chooses at rebuild/import time between clear + rebuild (replace — start fresh from the recipe) and add to existing (MERGE — add only the tiles you don't already have to My Maps, existing tiles untouched). ⭐ MERGE IS STRICTLY ADDITIVE — it ONLY adds new tiles (gap-fill, INSERT OR IGNORE-style), never overwrites and never duplicates. So multiple recipes UNION into one consolidated collection ("adds maps to my maps → one consolidated data collection"), running a merge twice is free, and a partial recipe just contributes its subset. ⚠ This clear-vs-add choice is DIFFERENT from — and does not reopen — the "NO per-slot selection at rebuild" rule in §00-RECOVERYFILE (that was about picking which slots, a failure point). Replace-vs-merge is a legitimate top-level user choice; per-slot picking stays out. ⛔⛔ THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE RIGHT: the replay job must be downloadType = DownloadType.AREA (NOT MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH) with priority = REFRESH — because ConvoyDownloadWorker:97 filters refresh-typed jobs to hasTile, so a refresh-typed replay downloads NOTHING and LOOKS successful (silent-failure, only found during a real recovery). Put a comment at that line. ⚠ NO slot selection at rebuild (another failure point — INSERT OR REPLACE fills gaps, running twice is free); no health guards (60-day history kills the partial-snapshot problem — if today's file is mid-rebuild garbage, yesterday's is intact). ⚠ TILES ONLY — tracks/trails/routes/waypoints are captured data needing real backup, not reproducible from this recipe. ⚠ VERIFY ONCE: does a file the app writes to Downloads survive an uninstall? (MediaStore tracks the owning app — DR must not rest on an untested assumption.) (§00-RECOVERYFILE; on the 2.6e list per Fred 08-14)
Data-loss / install blocker tier — designed, NOT built
The must-fix tier. Root cause of both data-loss events (08-01 ~89k trails, 08-08 whole spatial DB). Full design already in this living master — see §00-INSTALL + its 08-09 code-located update, and grouptrack_allfiles_fix_strategy_2026-08-09_v1.html. Referenced by the release index; do NOT re-derive.
Reinstall shows the app as already having all-authority → grant prompt bypassed → app launches and clears/creates the DB BEFORE authority is granted. ⭐ THE BOTTOM LINE: on reinstall, the authority value is not read properly — the app looks like it already has all-files access, so the "grant all authority" screen is skipped, and the program launches and writes over / creates the DB while it does NOT actually have authority. That is the whole data-loss defect: an ordering failure driven by a lying value. ⚠⚠ AND YOU GET NO SIGNAL UNTIL THE DAMAGE IS DONE — the app looks healthy, the checkbox says yes, the prompt is correctly skipped as far as the app can tell, and the first evidence anything was wrong is the DB already overwritten (no error, no failed check, no warning). You cannot detect your way out of it because the thing you'd query (the API) is the thing lying, and you cannot recover after because the overwrite is the one permanent loss. → the fix must be REFUSE-BEFORE-PROCEED (a real read, treat can't-see as refuse), never check-and-warn. MECHANISM: isExternalStorageManager() reads the AppOps record, which says granted while the filesystem refuses; the per-process mount view only updates on a permission TRANSITION, so the broken yes→yes state fires no event and the prompt never shows. TRIGGERS: cleardata-parameter installs, and reinstall-after-delete where the files still exist — the program opens the MBTiles/spatial DB, can't see the old data, and creates a new empty version over it. FIX in build order (per §00-INSTALL): (1) replace the API test with a real read (hasRealStorageAccess() — plain File I/O, treat "can't see" as UNKNOWN and refuse); (2) manufacture the transition (Panel A → settings OFF → verify → Panel B → settings ON → re-read); (2b) gate EVERY SpatialDbManager/MBTilesStore/import/download entry on the read passing, not on settings-return. ⚠⚠ SCOPE CONSTRAINT (Fred): do NOT rest/re-check authority on every update — a normal -r update keeps authority intact and must stay seamless; forcing the grant dance every update is wrong. The dangerous path is specifically the inherited Meshtastic clear-values / reinstall setup that runs on a clear-values reinstall and triggers the all-files conflict. DISCRIMINATOR (per §00-INSTALL): the filesDir marker — wiped by uninstall/clear, survives a normal update. Marker PRESENT = normal update, skip the dance. Marker ABSENT + data present in Documents/ = the clear-values/reinstall-over-data path → run the real-read gate + refuse-to-create + grant transition. So the authority handling fires ONLY where the conflict actually is.
Refuse-to-create floor (00-REFUSE) — stop the app writing a blank over a real DB when it can't see its files. The floor under everything. Highest-value unbuilt item.
Self-uninstall flow (00-INSTALL) — ACTION_DELETE while the app is alive and holds authority; rename Documents/GroupTrack→.bak → uninstall → reinstall → grant-first → real-read → restore. ⚠ First action: verify on Droid 2 that an uninstall leaves Documents/GroupTrack/ intact (whole flow rests on it).

⭐ API CORRECTION (research 08-15) — there is NO separate "new API 36 method." The correct all-files-access API is STILL: declare MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE in manifest → check Environment.isExternalStorageManager() → if not granted, fire Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION with a package: URI (opens THIS app's toggle directly). So the April greyed-toggle was likely NOT "wrong method" but one of: (1) ⭐ INTENT VARIANT — using ACTION_MANAGE_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION (opens a LIST of all apps) instead of ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION (opens OUR app directly), or firing the app-specific one WITHOUT the correct package: URI → system doesn't associate the request with our app → toggle greys; (2) the isExternalStorageManager() verification lie (item 7). ⚠ MUST SEE CURRENT CODE FIRST (Fred's point): grep -rn "isExternalStorageManager\|MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE\|ACTION_MANAGE\|ALL_FILES_ACCESS" app/src/main/java/ → reveals which intent variant, whether the package: URI is passed, how the grant is checked, and where the code lives. Fix is likely: switch to the _APP_ intent variant + correct URI, AND add item-7 real-read verification. Determine BEFORE building.

Rationale: (1) authority handling has no business inside the frozen map composable — extract it OUT so convoy can ASSUME authority is granted; (2) a pre-launch gate is the natural home for the item-7 proper flow (real-read hasRealStorageAccess(), correct app-specific intent, manufactured grant transition, refuse-to-proceed floor); (3) removes authority code from the frozen file (no more surgery on ConvoyScreen.kt); (4) structurally enforces "authority before any DB/MBTiles/import/download" — the exact ordering requirement. ⭐ THIS ONE SCREEN = the API-36 fix + item-7 redesign + clean separation, all at once. It's the convergence made concrete. Build on a throwaway branch with TARGET_SDK=36, test toggle-works + reinstall-survives.
⭐⭐ BROADER ARCHITECTURE DECISION (Fred 08-15): BOTH the GPS-SOURCE and the ALL-FILES AUTHORITY are bolted-on ADD-ONS embedded in ConvoyScreen.kt, and they BEHAVE like add-ons — fragile, order-dependent, failing illogically (GPS source not following the device-name swap = the radio-GPS bug; authority toggle greying out on A16). They were slapped in where convenient, not where they belong. → Extract BOTH into their own unique processes/screens that run BEFORE and INDEPENDENT of convoy. Convoy should ASSUME both are already established (authority granted, GPS source correctly selected from connection state) and never handle them inline. ⭐ SAME DISEASE as the discard bug / tile intercept / distance calc — foundational logic embedded in the big screen where it drifts and breaks; the OVERRIDING RULE (factor embedded logic into proper modules) applies. The GPS-source fix (derive from connection state, STATUS-IS-DERIVED — see §00-BUG-RADIOGPS) and the authority gate (see above) are BOTH pre-convoy foundational processes. Design them as such: a launch sequence that establishes authority → establishes GPS source → THEN loads convoy, each a clean separate module, none embedded in the map composable.
⭐⭐⭐ THE PRE-CONVOY GATE — architectural decision (Fred 08-15). Build a SYNCHRONOUS, ORDERED, BLOCKING gate that runs before convoy and is THE sanctioned home for anything that must execute before convoy — NO FREE-FOR-ALL. Today's bugs (greyed authority toggle, GPS-reporting flakiness, order-dependent failures) share ONE root: things that should precede convoy got scattered INSIDE convoy, racing each other as async add-ons. The gate makes the rule structural: if it must precede convoy, it goes in the gate — in order, synchronously — or it doesn't run. Two things at once: (1) the GATE MECHANISM — a synchronous ordered blocking pre-convoy sequence; (2) the gate as CONTRACT — the single place pre-convoy requirements live; a new requirement is ADDED to the gate's ordered list, never bolted into convoy. Gate establishes, IN ORDER, each verified before proceeding: (a) ALL-FILES access (real-read verified, correct _APP_ intent + package: URI, refuse-to-proceed floor); (b) BACKGROUND LOCATION "all the time" (ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION — note Android's 2-step rule: foreground location FIRST, then escalate to background, often via settings); (c) [SCOPE TBD] Bluetooth/Nearby-Devices for the radio?; (d) [PLACEHOLDER] anything new. → THEN convoy loads, ASSUMING all gate requirements are met (never re-checks inline). ⭐ This is the durable fix for the whole class of "add-on that behaves like an add-on." Synchronous = no race conditions like today. Build: dedicated pre-convoy Composable/Activity upstream of the convoy entry point; throwaway branch test/launch-authority, TARGET_SDK=36; test each permission + reinstall-survival on Android 16.
⭐⭐ BROADENED (Fred 08-15) — THE GATE IS A FULL STARTUP SEQUENCE, not just permissions. It's the home for ANYTHING that must complete before convoy: (1) AUTHORITY/PERMISSIONS (all-files, background location, bluetooth) — blocking; (2) STARTUP WORK — file conversions, data migrations, integrity checks, DB prep — anything that must finish before convoy touches its data. ⭐ "can live somewhere besides in the app" (Fred): this work doesn't belong inside convoy's process OR silently in Application.onCreate() — it belongs in a dedicated startup STAGE that runs, does its job, shows progress, reports done, and hands off. Convoy stays clean: it assumes permissions granted AND data prepped/converted, never does this inline. ⭐ ENFORCES the existing "NO SILENT PROCESSES" rule — a conversion buried in convoy's load path runs silently, blocks the UI, fails invisibly; a conversion step IN the startup gate shows progress on a visible surface, exactly as required. So the pre-convoy gate = ordered startup sequence: [permissions gates] → [startup work w/ visible progress] → convoy. Each step a clean module; the sequence is the sanctioned, extensible home (the placeholder) for all pre-convoy requirements.
⭐⭐ NEW CAPABILITY (Fred 08-15) — RUN-ONCE-PER-RELEASE CODE. The startup gate finally gives a home for one-time, run-once-per-release work that never had a clean place before (previously hacked into convoy badly, or just couldn't be done safely). Pattern: new release installs → gate checks a version-stamp/flag "has this release's one-time work run?" → if not, RUN IT (back up the DB, copy files, migrate schema, convert a format, fix up data), mark done → if already done, skip → proceed to convoy. Convoy never sees it. ⭐ HIGH-VALUE USES: (a) FILE/DB BACKUPS before a risky release touches data — a release that might modify the spatial DB backs it up FIRST, in the gate, before anything can corrupt it (directly mitigates the data-loss history); (b) ONE-TIME DATA MIGRATIONS for the 2.6f DB work — route-dedup-by-hash rebuild, shared extension-DB restructuring, rename/delete schema changes ALL need a "migrate existing user data to the new structure, once" step, with a backup taken first and visible progress. This is the structural enabler for safely shipping the 2.6f DB-trigger cluster to existing users. The gate = permissions + startup work + run-once-per-release migrations, all before convoy, all visible, none inline.
⛔⛔⛔ THE GATE'S FIRST PRINCIPLE (Fred 08-15) — SAFE HALT, NEVER DESTRUCTIVE PROCEED. The whole reason the gate exists: TODAY, the way the app tests authority to the MBTiles files can STOP the app from proceeding IN A WAY THAT DESTROYS THE DBs. The current check's failure mode is DESTRUCTIVE — when authority is uncertain/absent, the app stumbles forward into create-if-missing / DB-touching code and overwrites good data (the item-7 data-loss). THE GATE INVERTS THIS: authority-uncertain must mean STOP, never "proceed and hope." Rules: (a) authority CONFIRMED REAL (real filesystem read of the MBTiles/spatial DB path succeeds) → proceed; (b) authority uncertain / absent / check errored → HALT IN THE GATE, show grant screen, TOUCH NOTHING — do NOT open the DB, do NOT create-if-missing, do NOT load convoy, do NOT run any migration/conversion/backup. Freeze until authority is real. ⭐ NO PATH exists from the gate forward to any DB/MBTiles/import/download unless authority is PROVEN real by a real read (not the lying isExternalStorageManager). This IS the 00-REFUSE floor made the gate's foundational law. "Uncertain = stop" is the safety inversion that is the entire point of the gate — every other capability (permissions, migrations, conversions) sits BEHIND this halt.
⭐ SCOPE DISCIPLINE (Fred 08-15) — DON'T GET AHEAD OF THE SKIS. The above captures the full vision, but the ACTUAL immediate scope is tight and only two things: (1) GRANT AUTHORITY PROPERLY — the current grant is JUVENILE (a naive method that does NOT survive an accurate test for authority); replace it with a grant that survives a real authority test (real read, not the lying isExternalStorageManager, correct _APP_ intent). (2) A PLACEHOLDER to launch code before convoy on an application upgrade — the pre-convoy spot to run upgrade code. That's it. Migrations, conversions, backups, the full startup sequence = DOWNSTREAM, enabled by the placeholder but NOT to be designed/built now. Build the proper grant + the pre-convoy launch spot first; everything else lives behind it later.

⭐⭐ DESIGN CORRECTION (Fred 08-15) — POINT-OF-USE GUARDS ARE NOT CRUFT. The location prompt at ConvoyScreen.kt ~1299 fires right where a track is RECORDED (inside the recording flow / "hornet's nest") — deliberately placed so authority is verified AT THE MOMENT OF THE WRITE, not assumed from an earlier moment. That's GOOD defensive design = the opposite of the juvenile launch-grant that assumed-and-failed. The whole lesson of the data-loss bug is DON'T HOPE YOU GOT IT RIGHT EARLIER — VERIFY AT POINT OF USE. So the gate and the point-of-use checks are NOT redundant — they're LAYERED DEFENSE: the gate is the front door (establish authority up front so the app doesn't boot destructive); the point-of-use check is the guard at the vault (authority can be revoked mid-session; verify it STILL HOLDS at the consequential action). ⭐ CORRECTION to the removal plan: do NOT blindly neuter/remove point-of-use authority checks "because the gate handles it" — that IS the "hope you got it right" mistake. Instead, point-of-use checks should STAY and ideally be STRENGTHENED to use the real-read test (hasRealStorageAccess / real bg-location check) like the gate does. Only the pure LAUNCH-TIME duplicate (the all-files launch dialog at 145/152, which just re-implements what the gate now does at boot) is safe to neuter. The recording-time guard STAYS.

⭐⭐⭐ REAL DIAGNOSIS (Fred 08-15) — AUTHORITY IS CHANGING WHILE THE APP RUNS. The flash-past (no pause) says authority PRESENT at the moment the gate evaluates; the all-files prompt appearing at the END of install says authority ABSENT — BOTH true at different moments in the SAME run → the authority state is FLIPPING during startup. Not merely stale — TRANSITIONING. Something in startup changes the authority state (or the app races the OS establishing it). This is the exact async/order-dependent/racing failure mode the gate was meant to kill, now seen in the authority state itself moving under us. ⭐ DECISION (Fred): STOP trying to DETECT authority at startup (it's a moving target — any check reads a transient value). INSTEAD: ALWAYS DISPLAY THE SYSTEM GRANT-ALL-FILES SCREEN ON INSTALL, unconditionally. Don't gamble on a check; route the user to the REAL system all-files toggle every fresh install, let them grant/confirm explicitly, THEN proceed. Sidesteps the race entirely: don't trust any startup check, always show the system grant, proceed only after explicit user action. ⚠ IMPLEMENTATION: gate's NeedStorage should fire the system intent unconditionally on install (not gated behind the flaky real-read); "already granted" detection is the unreliable part. Consider: on install, show system all-files grant; only skip if a durable install-stamp says we already completed it (not a live authority check).
⭐⭐⭐ THE FIX REFINEMENT (Fred 08-15) — PAUSE/SETTLE BEFORE DB OPEN. Since authority is CHANGING during startup (two-record split settling asynchronously), the gate must WAIT for authority to SETTLE before the app tries to open the DB — not check-once-and-proceed instantly (the flash-past). The current gate evaluates instantly = races the transition. FIX: after the user grants all-files, don't immediately trust it — POLL the real write-canary (retry over a short window) until it CONSISTENTLY succeeds = authority "settled" = real + stable. Only then proceed to convoy → DB opens against SETTLED authority. This is the true synchronous barrier the gate was meant to be: wait out the authority change rather than reading a transient value mid-transition. Implementation: gate holds on a "verifying/settling" state, polls hasRealStorageAccess() (write-canary) on an interval until N consecutive passes (or a timeout), THEN onProceed. Combined with "always show system grant on install" — show grant, user acts, poll until settled, proceed. The DB open must never happen before the write-canary reliably passes. ⚠ ALSO TEST (answers "why doesn't granting work"): the appops split — appops set --uid ... allow AND appops set ... allow (both records), relaunch, does data read? If yes = toggle was setting only one record; enforcement read the other.
