The move — Mac Air/Pro replaces the PC for ALL development
DECIDED Confirmed "release 2.8 in your numbering." Goals: performance (builds hit 33–53 min under PC disk pressure), storage, and positioning for the Mac/iPad version discussion.
⛔ The irreplaceable item — handle first
The release keystore (grouptrack-release-key.jks). Everything else re-downloads or re-clones; the keystore cannot — lose it and you can never update the Play listing again. HANDLED already in 4 locations under /GroupTrack Application Keys/ (local, Google Drive, iCloud, Desktop) — the two cloud copies reach the Mac immediately. Whatever holds its passwords (keystore.properties/gradle.properties/password manager) travels with it.
Traps specific to this setup
PLAN Line endings. Every commit prints "LF will be replaced by CRLF" — working tree is CRLF, repo stores LF, macOS checks out LF natively. Done carelessly, the first git status on the Mac shows EVERY file modified. Plan .gitattributes/config so it doesn't churn the tree.
PORT Machine-specific tooling — patch scripts hardcode C:\Users\kixaz\...; build output → /d/; commands use MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 (Git Bash only); local.properties points at a Windows SDK path. A rewrite pass, not a copy.
MOVE The generation machinery, not just outputs — the xref generators, AllDocs assembly, the doc history used to gen AllDocs, any Google Drive activity/stores. Not in git, can't be reconstructed. (Inventory these before the move.)
VERIFY Devices need re-authorizing — ADB's RSA key is per-machine, both Droids re-prompt.
What must move
Irreplaceable: keystore + passwords · uncommitted work · unpushed branches/stashes · AllDocs · Downloads/ fallback sets. Credentials: Play Console, AWS RDS, PHP API, Thunderforest key, Crashlytics/Firebase. Reinstallable: JDK, Android SDK, Gradle, platform-tools. SQLite tooling is a non-issue — macOS ships sqlite3 built in (more than the PC had); DB Browser runs native on Apple silicon; workflow (adb pull → inspect locally) is identical minus MSYS_NO_PATHCONV (commands get SIMPLER).
⚠ AWS access from New Hampshire (blocking sub-item)
Console access is NOT IP-restricted (sign in from anywhere). The RDS security group IS — add current IP as an inbound rule (VPC → Security Groups → RDS one). ⚠ Home IP is dynamic (can re-lock). ⛔ EC2 blocked since March on a support case (PRE-01/02/03) — so RDS may be only half of what's needed if the PHP API is unreachable. Tie in with the 2.6e credential rotation.
Cross-platform / iPad — what the move positions for
OBJECTIVE Fred: "two platforms sharing as much of the code base and implementation as possible."
First step (Fred's plan): Apple browser supporting Bluetooth updates → deploy the app in-browser on iPad. ⚠ Web Bluetooth is NOT in Safari — it's Bluefy (a WebKit browser implementing Web Bluetooth). Changes the distribution story (users install a 3rd-party browser first; small vendor).
⭐ What it buys: map layer is already HTML/JS in a WebView → a browser-hosted version reaches iPad with no App Store review, no second signing identity, no Swift. Proves the shared-code thesis cheaply.
⚠ What it CAN'T do: background track recording (a tab can't record with screen off), storage at scale (browser storage capped/evictable — nothing like a 14GB MBTiles file), filesystem access. So it PROVES the architecture split, it's not a shipping product. (Gaia/onX store GBs because they're NATIVE apps — that's the difference.)
⭐ MapLibre is well-suited: exists as both native iOS/macOS SDK and JS — the 2.7 renderer rewrite could run on both without a fork. Doing 2.7 on the Mac = the point the architecture starts being written for two targets.
DECIDE EARLY How far the shared layer extends (SpatialDbManager/tile store/queue are Kotlin → KMP candidate; the service-layer split decides how much survives), and whether 2.7 targets iPad or just develops on Mac (building ON vs building FOR Apple — the second means a 2nd signing identity, store, test device). ⚠ A rewrite carrying a second platform as a constraint is slower — be explicit: Android-only with a portable interior, or genuinely dual-target. ✅ 00-2.6e-OPEN — FINALIZED 08-14. The definitive 2.6e open-items list (discovery complete; supersedes the scattered pre-2.6 backlog).
Result of the 08-14 discovery pass over the 07-13/07-22 pre-2.6 backlog + accumulated operational items, with Fred's 08-14 scope decisions applied. Killed/closed items recorded at the bottom so nothing is silently dropped. This is the list that gates 2.6e.
⭐ BUILD ORDER (Fred 08-14) — MODULE/COMPONENT WORK FIRST, INSTALL REDESIGN LAST.The feature/module tasks (Task A route display+fit, Task B calc, discard consolidation, tile-intercept module, rename/delete triggers) all fit the methodology below and share momentum + a clear plan — do them while that's true. The install/authority blocker tier (items 7–9) is scheduled LAST: it's a different kind of work — a high-stakes data-safety fix needing its own focused session and verification on a GENUINE fresh install — so it doesn't interleave well with the module cadence. It remains a hard gate on shipping 2.6e; last in build order, not last in priority.
⛔ OVERRIDING RULE — EVERY SEGMENT (Fred 08-14). IDENTIFY DUPLICATE CODE IMPLEMENTATIONS AND FACTOR THEM INTO CALLABLE MODULES WHENEVER THEY ARE DISCOVERED.This is a continuous operating rule, not a per-task technique. During ALL work — any segment, any release — actively watch for the same logic implemented in more than one place, and when found, extract it into ONE callable module and wire the call sites. Duplicate implementations are the root disease behind this project's worst bugs (the discard bug = six divergent teardowns; the two tile intercepts; the scattered distance calcs) — each copy drifts and one silently misses a step. De-duplication is therefore a reflex during every segment, whether or not the task is nominally about consolidation. HOW (the supporting discipline below): shared modules not parallel implementations · build components then string them · stub-first (mark all call sites, build once, grep every stub wired) · consistency-first then consolidate (never extract from divergent copies — make them consistent first, or you propagate a bug to all sites at once).
⭐ STANDING ARCHITECTURE DIRECTION (Fred 08-14) — SHARED MODULES, NOT PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATIONS.The same disease behind the discard bug (scattered duplicated logic, each copy drifting and missing a different step) applies across the app. The cure is the same everywhere: a capability lives in ONE reusable module, called from multiple places — never reimplemented per surface. Applies to: local-tile retrieval (one module, both maps' shouldInterceptRequest call it — item 6), distance + ride-time calc (called functions any surface uses — artifact panels, route planning, trail display — Task B), and going forward any capability that would otherwise be copied per screen/per artifact type. ⚠ When fixing a "missing on surface B" gap, EXTRACT the shared module and wire both — do NOT copy surface A's implementation to B (that creates the second copy that drifts).
⭐ BUILD METHOD — STUB-FIRST (Fred 08-14). For any new shared module: (1) IDENTIFY the module — fix its name/signature/return even before implementing; (2) PLACE PLACEHOLDER STUBS at every call site that needs it, with a grep-able marker (e.g. // STUB:RIDECALC) so every consumer is identified up front; (3) BUILD OUT the module once; (4) VERIFY every stub was converted to the real call — grep -c the marker (= all sites before, = 0 after), no stub left unwired. ⭐ Step 4 makes the stubs a completeness CHECKLIST — you cannot forget a call site because they were all marked first. This is exactly the discipline that would have caught the discard bug (a missing call at one exit would show as an unconverted stub). Pairs with the existing marker-count patch verification.

Data-recovery — the REBUILD function (recovery side of the install story; designed in §00-RECOVERYFILE)
Fred's last known 2.6e item. The recovery/healing side of the data-safety story: an install error means a protected-data reinstall, and this is how you rebuild afterward — unattended, from a recipe, instead of manual reconstruction. Full design already in §00-RECOVERYFILE — do NOT redesign; this is the wiring + display item. ⭐ BUILD ORDER: QUEUED AFTER the install revisions (which are themselves last) — DR follows the install fix.
Rebuild function + Recovery display. A rebuild function that consumes the map-configuration recipe (the .gtmaps file the recipe writer produces — a few-KB JSON of slots + boxes, the same quadtree enqueueRecreateSource computes), linked to a Recovery display that shows: (a) the current 60-day window of restore points (the recipe writer keeps one file/day, deletes >60 days; the date in the filename IS the index), listed by date with tile counts; (b) any recipe available in Downloads (import via the picker/content-URI path — needs no All-Files authority). Select a restore point or recipe → REBUILD (or EMAIL). ⭐ CLEAR-vs-ADD CHOICE (Fred 08-14): the user chooses at rebuild/import time between clear + rebuild (replace — start fresh from the recipe) and add to existing (MERGE — add only the tiles you don't already have to My Maps, existing tiles untouched). ⭐ MERGE IS STRICTLY ADDITIVE — it ONLY adds new tiles (gap-fill, INSERT OR IGNORE-style), never overwrites and never duplicates. So multiple recipes UNION into one consolidated collection ("adds maps to my maps → one consolidated data collection"), running a merge twice is free, and a partial recipe just contributes its subset. ⚠ This clear-vs-add choice is DIFFERENT from — and does not reopen — the "NO per-slot selection at rebuild" rule in §00-RECOVERYFILE (that was about picking which slots, a failure point). Replace-vs-merge is a legitimate top-level user choice; per-slot picking stays out. ⛔⛔ THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE RIGHT: the replay job must be downloadType = DownloadType.AREA (NOT MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH) with priority = REFRESH — because ConvoyDownloadWorker:97 filters refresh-typed jobs to hasTile, so a refresh-typed replay downloads NOTHING and LOOKS successful (silent-failure, only found during a real recovery). Put a comment at that line. ⚠ NO slot selection at rebuild (another failure point — INSERT OR REPLACE fills gaps, running twice is free); no health guards (60-day history kills the partial-snapshot problem — if today's file is mid-rebuild garbage, yesterday's is intact). ⚠ TILES ONLY — tracks/trails/routes/waypoints are captured data needing real backup, not reproducible from this recipe. ⚠ VERIFY ONCE: does a file the app writes to Downloads survive an uninstall? (MediaStore tracks the owning app — DR must not rest on an untested assumption.) (§00-RECOVERYFILE; on the 2.6e list per Fred 08-14)
Data-loss / install blocker tier — designed, NOT built
The must-fix tier. Root cause of both data-loss events (08-01 ~89k trails, 08-08 whole spatial DB). Full design already in this living master — see §00-INSTALL + its 08-09 code-located update, and grouptrack_allfiles_fix_strategy_2026-08-09_v1.html. Referenced by the release index; do NOT re-derive.
Reinstall shows the app as already having all-authority → grant prompt bypassed → app launches and clears/creates the DB BEFORE authority is granted. ⭐ THE BOTTOM LINE: on reinstall, the authority value is not read properly — the app looks like it already has all-files access, so the "grant all authority" screen is skipped, and the program launches and writes over / creates the DB while it does NOT actually have authority. That is the whole data-loss defect: an ordering failure driven by a lying value. ⚠⚠ AND YOU GET NO SIGNAL UNTIL THE DAMAGE IS DONE — the app looks healthy, the checkbox says yes, the prompt is correctly skipped as far as the app can tell, and the first evidence anything was wrong is the DB already overwritten (no error, no failed check, no warning). You cannot detect your way out of it because the thing you'd query (the API) is the thing lying, and you cannot recover after because the overwrite is the one permanent loss. → the fix must be REFUSE-BEFORE-PROCEED (a real read, treat can't-see as refuse), never check-and-warn. MECHANISM: isExternalStorageManager() reads the AppOps record, which says granted while the filesystem refuses; the per-process mount view only updates on a permission TRANSITION, so the broken yes→yes state fires no event and the prompt never shows. TRIGGERS: cleardata-parameter installs, and reinstall-after-delete where the files still exist — the program opens the MBTiles/spatial DB, can't see the old data, and creates a new empty version over it. FIX in build order (per §00-INSTALL): (1) replace the API test with a real read (hasRealStorageAccess() — plain File I/O, treat "can't see" as UNKNOWN and refuse); (2) manufacture the transition (Panel A → settings OFF → verify → Panel B → settings ON → re-read); (2b) gate EVERY SpatialDbManager/MBTilesStore/import/download entry on the read passing, not on settings-return. ⚠⚠ SCOPE CONSTRAINT (Fred): do NOT rest/re-check authority on every update — a normal -r update keeps authority intact and must stay seamless; forcing the grant dance every update is wrong. The dangerous path is specifically the inherited Meshtastic clear-values / reinstall setup that runs on a clear-values reinstall and triggers the all-files conflict. DISCRIMINATOR (per §00-INSTALL): the filesDir marker — wiped by uninstall/clear, survives a normal update. Marker PRESENT = normal update, skip the dance. Marker ABSENT + data present in Documents/ = the clear-values/reinstall-over-data path → run the real-read gate + refuse-to-create + grant transition. So the authority handling fires ONLY where the conflict actually is.
Refuse-to-create floor (00-REFUSE) — stop the app writing a blank over a real DB when it can't see its files. The floor under everything. Highest-value unbuilt item.
Self-uninstall flow (00-INSTALL) — ACTION_DELETE while the app is alive and holds authority; rename Documents/GroupTrack→.bak → uninstall → reinstall → grant-first → real-read → restore. ⚠ First action: verify on Droid 2 that an uninstall leaves Documents/GroupTrack/ intact (whole flow rests on it).

⛔⛔⛔ CRITICAL — WHY WE DROPPED TO 35, AND WHY THE BUMP IS NOT TRIVIAL (found 08-15 in past-chat a2329bc4, 04-29): current state is TARGET_SDK=35, COMPILE_SDK=36 (compile already 36, only target retreated). The retreat from 36 happened because TARGET_SDK=36 GREYED OUT / broke the ALL-FILES-ACCESS toggle on Android 16 — the app could not enable MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, which is the CORE of the entire 50-60GB map-persistence model (the exact feature just justified to Google). Fred at the time: "testers cannot afford to lose their tracks again." So the API-36 deadline and GroupTrack's core data-persistence feature are IN DIRECT CONFLICT — bumping target→36 re-triggers the storage-permission break. ⭐ This is NOT a one-line bump; it's real work: Android 16 changed how all-files access is granted (the old settings-toggle path greys out), so target=36 requires requesting MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE the Android-16-correct way (likely a specific intent/flow, not the legacy toggle). ⭐ TIES DIRECTLY TO ITEM 7 (install-authority redesign) — same permission, same subsystem; the API-36 all-files fix and the item-7 authority fix are the same body of work and should be done together. STRATEGY: (a) strongly consider the Nov 1 EXTENSION to buy time — the closed test can run on the current 35/36 build (35 keeps existing-user discoverability; only NEW update SUBMISSIONS after Aug 31 need 36); (b) do the target=36 + Android-16 all-files-request fix deliberately with item 7, on a throwaway branch, tested against the greyed-toggle symptom, NOT rushed in the 2-week window. ⚠ verify: does the current live closed build (35) let testers enable all-files access? If yes, the closed test is fine on 35 for now.
⭐⭐ REFRAME (Fred 08-15) — THE API-36 BUILD MAY SOLVE THE AUTHORITY CONFLICT AT ITS ROOT. Hypothesis: the greyed-toggle (API 36 broke all-files access) and the item-7 authority defect (lying isExternalStorageManager, reinstall clears DB before authority granted) are likely the SAME underlying problem — both are the app failing to properly obtain/recognize MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. The April greyed-toggle happened because we used the LEGACY request path, which Android 16 tightened. Doing the API-36 build PROPERLY = implementing the Android-16-correct all-files-access request = rewriting exactly the fragile inherited permission code that item 7 says is broken. So API 36 isn't just the deadline — it may be the FORCING FUNCTION that fixes the authority handling at its root, solving BOTH the deadline AND item 7 (and the data-loss events) in ONE body of work. ⚠ CAUTION — test as a hypothesis, not an assumption: Android 16 could also make MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE HARDER to obtain (that's why it greyed out). Best case: correct modern flow fixes deadline + item 7. Worst case: A16 restricts the permission so hard the whole app's model is squeezed. Likely in-between: the correct A16 implementation is MORE ROBUST than the current lying/fragile inherited code, i.e. closer to item-7's goal regardless. PLAN: do API-36 + item-7 as ONE deliberate project (throwaway branch, with the Nov 1 extension for time), and verify BOTH (1) toggle works on A16, (2) authority is real + survives reinstall. If both hold, two of the hardest problems die in one build.
⭐ THE TASK, STATED CLEANLY (Fred 08-15): "we used the OLD method to grant all-files because it was easier — didn't know much in April. ⭐ API CORRECTION (research 08-15) — there is NO separate "new API 36 method." The correct all-files-access API is STILL: declare MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE in manifest → check Environment.isExternalStorageManager() → if not granted, fire Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION with a package: URI (opens THIS app's toggle directly). So the April greyed-toggle was likely NOT "wrong method" but one of: (1) ⭐ INTENT VARIANT — using ACTION_MANAGE_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION (opens a LIST of all apps) instead of ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION (opens OUR app directly), or firing the app-specific one WITHOUT the correct package: URI → system doesn't associate the request with our app → toggle greys; (2) the isExternalStorageManager() verification lie (item 7). ⚠ MUST SEE CURRENT CODE FIRST (Fred's point): grep -rn "isExternalStorageManager\|MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE\|ACTION_MANAGE\|ALL_FILES_ACCESS" app/src/main/java/ → reveals which intent variant, whether the package: URI is passed, how the grant is checked, and where the code lives. Fix is likely: switch to the _APP_ intent variant + correct URI, AND add item-7 real-read verification. Determine BEFORE building.

⭐⭐ BROADER ARCHITECTURE DECISION (Fred 08-15): BOTH the GPS-SOURCE and the ALL-FILES AUTHORITY are bolted-on ADD-ONS embedded in ConvoyScreen.kt, and they BEHAVE like add-ons — fragile, order-dependent, failing illogically (GPS source not following the device-name swap = the radio-GPS bug; authority toggle greying out on A16). They were slapped in where convenient, not where they belong. → Extract BOTH into their own unique processes/screens that run BEFORE and INDEPENDENT of convoy. Convoy should ASSUME both are already established (authority granted, GPS source correctly selected from connection state) and never handle them inline. ⭐ SAME DISEASE as the discard bug / tile intercept / distance calc — foundational logic embedded in the big screen where it drifts and breaks; the OVERRIDING RULE (factor embedded logic into proper modules) applies. The GPS-source fix (derive from connection state, STATUS-IS-DERIVED — see §00-BUG-RADIOGPS) and the authority gate (see above) are BOTH pre-convoy foundational processes. Design them as such: a launch sequence that establishes authority → establishes GPS source → THEN loads convoy, each a clean separate module, none embedded in the map composable.
⭐⭐⭐ THE PRE-CONVOY GATE — architectural decision (Fred 08-15). Build a SYNCHRONOUS, ORDERED, BLOCKING gate that runs before convoy and is THE sanctioned home for anything that must execute before convoy — NO FREE-FOR-ALL. Today's bugs (greyed authority toggle, GPS-reporting flakiness, order-dependent failures) share ONE root: things that should precede convoy got scattered INSIDE convoy, racing each other as async add-ons. The gate makes the rule structural: if it must precede convoy, it goes in the gate — in order, synchronously — or it doesn't run. Two things at once: (1) the GATE MECHANISM — a synchronous ordered blocking pre-convoy sequence; (2) the gate as CONTRACT — the single place pre-convoy requirements live; a new requirement is ADDED to the gate's ordered list, never bolted into convoy. Gate establishes, IN ORDER, each verified before proceeding: (a) ALL-FILES access (real-read verified, correct _APP_ intent + package: URI, refuse-to-proceed floor); (b) BACKGROUND LOCATION "all the time" (ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION — note Android's 2-step rule: foreground location FIRST, then escalate to background, often via settings); (c) [SCOPE TBD] Bluetooth/Nearby-Devices for the radio?; (d) [PLACEHOLDER] anything new. → THEN convoy loads, ASSUMING all gate requirements are met (never re-checks inline). ⭐ This is the durable fix for the whole class of "add-on that behaves like an add-on." Synchronous = no race conditions like today. Build: dedicated pre-convoy Composable/Activity upstream of the convoy entry point; throwaway branch test/launch-authority, TARGET_SDK=36; test each permission + reinstall-survival on Android 16.
⭐⭐ BROADENED (Fred 08-15) — THE GATE IS A FULL STARTUP SEQUENCE, not just permissions. It's the home for ANYTHING that must complete before convoy: (1) AUTHORITY/PERMISSIONS (all-files, background location, bluetooth) — blocking; (2) STARTUP WORK — file conversions, data migrations, integrity checks, DB prep — anything that must finish before convoy touches its data. ⭐ "can live somewhere besides in the app" (Fred): this work doesn't belong inside convoy's process OR silently in Application.onCreate() — it belongs in a dedicated startup STAGE that runs, does its job, shows progress, reports done, and hands off. Convoy stays clean: it assumes permissions granted AND data prepped/converted, never does this inline. ⭐ ENFORCES the existing "NO SILENT PROCESSES" rule — a conversion buried in convoy's load path runs silently, blocks the UI, fails invisibly; a conversion step IN the startup gate shows progress on a visible surface, exactly as required. So the pre-convoy gate = ordered startup sequence: [permissions gates] → [startup work w/ visible progress] → convoy. Each step a clean module; the sequence is the sanctioned, extensible home (the placeholder) for all pre-convoy requirements.
⭐⭐ NEW CAPABILITY (Fred 08-15) — RUN-ONCE-PER-RELEASE CODE. The startup gate finally gives a home for one-time, run-once-per-release work that never had a clean place before (previously hacked into convoy badly, or just couldn't be done safely). Pattern: new release installs → gate checks a version-stamp/flag "has this release's one-time work run?" → if not, RUN IT (back up the DB, copy files, migrate schema, convert a format, fix up data), mark done → if already done, skip → proceed to convoy. Convoy never sees it. ⭐ HIGH-VALUE USES: (a) FILE/DB BACKUPS before a risky release touches data — a release that might modify the spatial DB backs it up FIRST, in the gate, before anything can corrupt it (directly mitigates the data-loss history); (b) ONE-TIME DATA MIGRATIONS for the 2.6f DB work — route-dedup-by-hash rebuild, shared extension-DB restructuring, rename/delete schema changes ALL need a "migrate existing user data to the new structure, once" step, with a backup taken first and visible progress. This is the structural enabler for safely shipping the 2.6f DB-trigger cluster to existing users. The gate = permissions + startup work + run-once-per-release migrations, all before convoy, all visible, none inline.
⛔⛔⛔ THE GATE'S FIRST PRINCIPLE (Fred 08-15) — SAFE HALT, NEVER DESTRUCTIVE PROCEED. The whole reason the gate exists: TODAY, the way the app tests authority to the MBTiles files can STOP the app from proceeding IN A WAY THAT DESTROYS THE DBs. The current check's failure mode is DESTRUCTIVE — when authority is uncertain/absent, the app stumbles forward into create-if-missing / DB-touching code and overwrites good data (the item-7 data-loss). THE GATE INVERTS THIS: authority-uncertain must mean STOP, never "proceed and hope." Rules: (a) authority CONFIRMED REAL (real filesystem read of the MBTiles/spatial DB path succeeds) → proceed; (b) authority uncertain / absent / check errored → HALT IN THE GATE, show grant screen, TOUCH NOTHING — do NOT open the DB, do NOT create-if-missing, do NOT load convoy, do NOT run any migration/conversion/backup. Freeze until authority is real. ⭐ NO PATH exists from the gate forward to any DB/MBTiles/import/download unless authority is PROVEN real by a real read (not the lying isExternalStorageManager). This IS the 00-REFUSE floor made the gate's foundational law. "Uncertain = stop" is the safety inversion that is the entire point of the gate — every other capability (permissions, migrations, conversions) sits BEHIND this halt.
⭐ SCOPE DISCIPLINE (Fred 08-15) — DON'T GET AHEAD OF THE SKIS. The above captures the full vision, but the ACTUAL immediate scope is tight and only two things: (1) GRANT AUTHORITY PROPERLY — the current grant is JUVENILE (a naive method that does NOT survive an accurate test for authority); replace it with a grant that survives a real authority test (real read, not the lying isExternalStorageManager, correct _APP_ intent). (2) A PLACEHOLDER to launch code before convoy on an application upgrade — the pre-convoy spot to run upgrade code. That's it. Migrations, conversions, backups, the full startup sequence = DOWNSTREAM, enabled by the placeholder but NOT to be designed/built now. Build the proper grant + the pre-convoy launch spot first; everything else lives behind it later.

⭐⭐⭐ REAL DIAGNOSIS (Fred 08-15) — AUTHORITY IS CHANGING WHILE THE APP RUNS. The flash-past (no pause) says authority PRESENT at the moment the gate evaluates; the all-files prompt appearing at the END of install says authority ABSENT — BOTH true at different moments in the SAME run → the authority state is FLIPPING during startup. Not merely stale — TRANSITIONING. Something in startup changes the authority state (or the app races the OS establishing it). This is the exact async/order-dependent/racing failure mode the gate was meant to kill, now seen in the authority state itself moving under us. ⭐ DECISION (Fred): STOP trying to DETECT authority at startup (it's a moving target — any check reads a transient value). INSTEAD: ALWAYS DISPLAY THE SYSTEM GRANT-ALL-FILES SCREEN ON INSTALL, unconditionally. ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIX REFINEMENT (Fred 08-15) — PAUSE/SETTLE BEFORE DB OPEN. Since authority is CHANGING during startup (two-record split settling asynchronously), the gate must WAIT for authority to SETTLE before the app tries to open the DB — not check-once-and-proceed instantly (the flash-past). The current gate evaluates instantly = races the transition. FIX: after the user grants all-files, don't immediately trust it — POLL the real write-canary (retry over a short window) until it CONSISTENTLY succeeds = authority "settled" = real + stable. Only then proceed to convoy → DB opens against SETTLED authority. This is the true synchronous barrier the gate was meant to be: wait out the authority change rather than reading a transient value mid-transition. Implementation: gate holds on a "verifying/settling" state, polls hasRealStorageAccess() (write-canary) on an interval until N consecutive passes (or a timeout), THEN onProceed. Combined with "always show system grant on install" — show grant, user acts, poll until settled, proceed. The DB open must never happen before the write-canary reliably passes. ⚠ ALSO TEST (answers "why doesn't granting work"): the appops split — appops set --uid ... allow AND appops set ... allow (both records), relaunch, does data read? If yes = toggle was setting only one record; enforcement read the other.

⭐⭐ CLEANER DIAGNOSIS (Fred 08-15) — EXISTENCE PASSES, READS FAIL (two separate mechanisms, was conflated). Observed on the current (pre-V2) release build: the DB-tracking / EXISTENCE test PASSES → app does NOT create a new database → destructive-proceed is NOT happening → DATA IS SAFE (not overwritten). BUT the app FAILS ON AUTHORITY FOR APPLICATION READS → it can SEE the DB exists but can't READ its contents. So two distinct layers: (1) existence/create-guard = "DB exists? yes → don't create" = WORKING (data safe); (2) authority-for-reads = actually opening/reading the DB needs real MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE = FAILING. This is the two-record appops split showing exactly where expected: existence works (weaker/stat access), reads fail (needs the real all-files authority stuck in the split state). GOOD: destructive create-empty-over-real-data is NOT occurring in this build. PRECISE PROBLEM: authority isolated to the READ layer. The V2 gate targets exactly this — establish REAL read authority (write-canary passes) BEFORE the DB is accessed; settle barrier + write-canary hold the app at the gate until reads would actually work. NOTE: the DB-tracking code wasn't changed this release; authority is the isolated failure.
⭐⭐⭐ UID HYPOTHESIS (Fred 08-15) — possibly THE root: file I/O authority is UID-DEPENDENT, and the UID changed under the grant. appops showed a UID-mode separate from the package op; the search + Android docs confirm all-files ENFORCEMENT is keyed to the UID. Mechanism: uninstall+reinstall of the SAME package can assign a NEW UID; the all-files appops "allow" record can be stranded on the OLD UID. Tonight's churn (release installed+granted → uninstall → debug install → debug uninstall → release reinstall) likely gave release a NEW UID, leaving the grant on a stale UID → release can't do file I/O → "data there, can't read." (Debug is a different package/UID entirely, so its grant never applied to release regardless.) ⭐ TEST — grant to the CURRENT uid explicitly (the --uid form from web search): adb -s 24039703201775 shell appops set --uid com.grouptrack.android MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE allow, then relaunch → does the DB read? If YES = confirmed, grant was keyed to a stale UID; forcing it onto the current UID fixes it. Also check current UID: dumpsys package com.grouptrack.android | grep -i "userId\|appId". ⭐ IMPLICATION FOR V2: the settle-barrier + forced fresh re-grant helps — it makes the user grant under the CURRENT UID rather than trusting a stale record. Also found (web): Android 12+ "Remove permissions if unused" auto-revoke + "major updates require re-grant" — disable "Remove permissions if app is unused" in app settings. No specific "A16 broke all-files" bug found — it's the UID/record split + auto-revoke, both addressable.
⭐⭐⭐ THE CLEAREST FRAMING (Fred 08-15) — SAME IDENTITY, DIFFERENT AUTHORITY. Android has TWO notions of "who the app is": (1) PACKAGE NAME (com.grouptrack.android) = the IDENTITY the user + app see, stable across reinstalls; (2) UID = the actual SECURITY PRINCIPAL the OS uses for file-I/O enforcement, which CAN CHANGE on reinstall. The bug: the running app IS GroupTrack by every identity measure (same package, icon, name, code) but is a DIFFERENT UID than the one that was granted all-files → it presents as "the app that has authority" but is NOT the same principal that was granted it. The grant is attached to the OLD principal; the running app is a NEW principal wearing the same identity. That's why: isExternalStorageManager()/the toggle can look "granted" (package-level / stale identity-tied record) BUT file I/O FAILS (checks the UID principal, never granted); data is there (existence doesn't care about UID) but unreadable (I/O checks the ungranted UID). ⭐ AUTHORITY ATTACHES TO THE UID (PRINCIPAL), NOT THE PACKAGE (IDENTITY) — and they can diverge. A robust gate cannot trust "am I GroupTrack?" (identity); it must verify "can THIS UID actually do the I/O?" (principal) = EXACTLY what the write-canary does (tests the UID's real I/O capability, not the identity's claimed grant). The fix already built is precisely aimed at this.

Confirmed by web research: applicationIdSuffix ".debug" makes debug a fully ISOLATED app on purpose; a grant to debug never applies to release; authority is UID-keyed. ⭐ THIS IS WHY FRED'S RULE IS RELEASE-ONLY — he learned this lesson before and made the rule to prevent exactly this. Tonight Claude violated the rule (used assembleGoogleDebug for fast compile checks), which reintroduced the very problem the rule exists to avoid. ⭐⭐⭐ REAL ARCHITECTURAL BUG FOUND (Fred 08-15) — IMPORT-TRACKS JOB RUNS BEFORE THE AUTHORITY GATE AND OPENS THE DBs. Sequence: app launch → import-tracks job executes (opens DBs) → THEN the authority gate → convoy. The DB is opened BEFORE authority is established. This VIOLATES the gate's core principle ("no free-for-all — everything pre-convoy goes through the gate first"). We gated the NAVIGATION entry (gate = nav start destination) but a NON-navigation job (import-tracks) fires at PROCESS startup, upstream of the whole nav graph — the gate guards the UI path but not the background-job path. That's why "no data" on the clean test: the import job hit the DB without authority before the gate could run. FIX DIRECTION: the import-tracks job (and anything that opens a DB at startup) must NOT run until the gate establishes authority — either (a) GATE IT: the job checks the same real-read authority and defers/refuses until authority is real, or (b) SEQUENCE IT: the job doesn't fire at process start; it's triggered AFTER the gate proceeds (moved downstream). This is the "no free-for-all" principle applied to background jobs, not just navigation. NEXT: locate the import-tracks job (grep importTracks/TrackImport + Application onCreate/WorkManager) and see where it fires + what opens the DB.

⭐⭐ ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (Fred 08-15) — THE GREY IS AN AUTHORITY MISMATCH: "can't grant if you already have." Theory: the toggle greyed because the OS side thought authority was ALREADY present (grant control disabled — granting an already-granted permission is a no-op → greyed), WHILE the app's isExternalStorageManager() check said NOT granted (so it kept prompting). The two disagree = a LINGERING/STALE authority record (AppOps grant survived a prior install, or an inconsistent state) → OS-settings and app-runtime-check out of sync, and NEITHER can resolve it because the toggle is disabled precisely because the OS thinks it's done. This IS the item-7 "lying authority" defect WITH A MECHANISM: not random lying, but a stale/mismatched grant record. ⭐ VALIDATES THE REAL-READ DESIGN: the real read asks the FILESYSTEM "can I actually read?" (ground truth) instead of the OS "do I have authority?" (stale/lying answer) — cutting through the mismatch entirely. ⚠ POSSIBLE ADDED NEED: explicitly handle the mismatch state (OS says granted but real read fails) — may need a clean clear-and-re-request rather than assuming the toggle works. "Fixing a lingering issue" — the stale grant record is the lingering thing.
⭐⭐⭐ OBSERVED / CONFIRMED (Fred 08-15) — THE MISMATCH IS REAL, seen directly. On clear-data: the app's authority was REMOVED (app-side lost real access) BUT the system setting still showed "all files: YES" (OS-side stale record) → so the app NEVER GOT PROMPTED. The app checked isExternalStorageManager() → OS returned the stale "yes" → prompt suppressed → app proceeded AS IF it had authority it didn't actually have → destructive-proceed → orphaned/overwrote the real data. THE ENTIRE BUG IN ONE SENTENCE: clear-data wipes the app's real access but leaves the OS record saying "yes," the app trusts the record (the lie), skips the prompt, and destroys data. ⭐ THIS IS EXACTLY WHY THE REAL-READ GATE IS THE CURE: OS says "yes" (stale) and isExternalStorageManager() returns true (trusts it), but a REAL READ would FAIL (actual access was removed on clear-data). Old code trusts "yes" → no prompt → destroys. New gate ignores "yes," does the real read → read FAILS → mismatch DETECTED → halt + force proper re-grant → real read passes → THEN proceed, data intact. The real read is the ONLY check that reflects actual access vs the stale record — it catches the exact case (stale-yes + no-prompt + gone-access) that the old code is blind to.
⭐ MECHANISM THEORY (Fred 08-15, plausible — exact internals NOT confirmed): the grant RECORD and the actual ACCESS live in DIFFERENT places; clear-data updated one but not the other, because the version that SET the grant predated/was-unaware-of the clear-out behavior. Maps to Android's real model: MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is tracked in AppOps (system special-op record), separate from app data and separate from filesystem enforcement. Clear-data clears app data but the AppOps grant can persist / go inconsistent — especially across the target-SDK churn (36→34→35), since different targets interpret MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE differently, so a grant RECORDED under one target's rules is ENFORCED differently under another → "record says yes, real access gone." ⚠ EXACT term/location ("manifest attached to the object") NOT verified — could be AppOps, a package-manager flag, or MediaProvider state; the precise internals are version-specific and unconfirmed. ⭐ KEY POINT — THE FIX DOESN'T DEPEND ON KNOWING: the real-read test consults NONE of these records; it asks the filesystem "can I actually read?" (ground truth). So the fix is CORRECT whether or not the exact mechanism theory is right — it bypasses the stale record entirely rather than reverse-engineering where it lives. Diagnosis precision matters less than fix robustness here.
⭐ POSSIBLE ADDED REQUIREMENT (Fred 08-15) — FORCE-OFF-THEN-GRANT for the mismatch state. If the mismatch persists (OS record "yes" + real access gone → toggle greyed = "can't grant what you already have"), then granting properly may require first getting authority into a clean OFF state so it CAN be granted. Reset the stale "yes" before re-requesting. ⚠ ENGINEERING REALITY: an app CANNOT revoke its own MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE in code (no self-revoke API) — so the gate can't force-off itself. Options: (1) guide the USER to settings to toggle OFF then back ON (two-step, clunky, but resets the stale record); (2) the app's all-files settings page may itself clear stale state on off→on; (3) for TESTING only (not users): adb shell appops set com.grouptrack.android MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE default resets the AppOps record — useful to reproduce clean-slate on Droid 2. So mismatch handling = detect (real-read fails + OS says yes) AND drive-the-reset (user-guided force-off-then-grant, since app can't self-revoke). ⚠ SCOPE: this is DESIGN-IF-THE-TEST-SHOWS-IT-NEEDED, not built speculatively. Current gate does real-read detection. IF the Droid 2 test shows "real read fails + OS yes + plain re-grant doesn't fix (toggle greyed)" → THEN add force-off-then-grant. The test tells us whether this branch is required (and whether the mismatch even persists on API 36).
⚠ UX CONSTRAINT on force-off (Fred 08-15): since the app can't self-revoke, force-off-then-grant means prompting the user TWICE (off, then on). CONTROLLED PANELS = manageable — wrap the 2-step reset in OUR OWN gate screens as one guided/explained flow ("Step 1 toggle off, Step 2 toggle on"), double-prompt hidden inside a coherent experience. UNCONTROLLED (raw Android settings twice) = HARD TO EXPLAIN — "revoke then re-grant" reads like a bug, not a fix, especially for backcountry OHV users who aren't power users. So IF the double-prompt is unavoidable, it MUST be behind controlled panels. ⭐ PRIORITY ORDER (avoid the awkward thing): (1) hope the test shows API 36 clear-data leaves a CLEAN state (no stale yes → no mismatch → no reset → no double-prompt); (2) if mismatch exists, hope a PLAIN re-grant clears it (single prompt); (3) ONLY if neither → build the controlled-panel double-prompt flow. Don't build it unless the test proves it's unavoidable.
⭐ WORST-CASE FALLBACK DESIGN (Fred 08-15) — GATED EXPLAINER SCREEN. IF the test fails (mismatch persists) AND we can't control the OS panels → build a gated explainer screen that BRACKETS the two uncontrolled OS trips and makes them comprehensible. Flow: [OUR explainer screen: explains the OS error in plain terms ("Android has your permission in an inconsistent state") + explains the TWO screens coming ("you'll see system settings twice — first turn access OFF, then we bring you back to turn it ON; this clears the stuck state")] → [OS settings: turn OFF — uncontrolled but now EXPECTED] → [OUR bridge screen: "now turn it back on"] → [OS settings: turn ON — uncontrolled but expected] → [real read passes → proceed]. KEY: our screens bracket the raw OS trips so we control the NARRATIVE even without controlling the panels — the user is never dropped into raw settings without our explanation first, so "revoke then re-grant" reads as a guided repair, not a bug. This is the worst-case path only (priority order above still applies: prefer no-mismatch, then plain-regrant, THEN this).

🐛 00-BUG-RADIOGPS — surfaced 08-14, INTERMITTENT (currently working 08-15, root cause NOT confirmed). Watch for recurrence.
⚠ STATUS 08-15: started working again on its own during testing — root cause was NOT identified/fixed, so this may be QUIET rather than FIXED. If it recurs, the diagnosis below still applies. The isolation test was solid (same radio, two phones, different behavior) so something real was happening — an intermittent handoff/timing issue is the likely character. On recurrence, capture the exact on-screen state of BOTH devices (has-Android-GPS vs no-Android-GPS) immediately, and note what changed right before it started working (reconnect? app restart? moved outside for sky view? nothing?).
Symptom (as diagnosed 08-14): Expected — radio connects → device name centered on map → GPS sourced FROM the radio. Actual — radio connects, device name shows in My Cart (BLE transport OK), but radio GPS not driving the map on a device that ALSO has internal Android GPS. Exact on-screen states of the two devices were never fully pinned before it self-resolved — capture them if it recurs.
What the symptom narrows it to: BLE is fine (My Cart shows the node). The break is in the POSITION-packet path: Meshtastic sends POSITION packets → app must receive → decode → feed position to map as active source → switch map source from Android-GPS to radio-GPS. Break is in one of: (1) the node itself has no GPS fix (no GPS hardware, or no sky view indoors — MOST LIKELY given it was tested indoors for the Play demo); (2) position packets arrive but app isn't parsing/subscribing; (3) packets parse but app never switches the map's location source from Android to radio.
⭐ FIRST DIAGNOSTIC (cheapest, do before touching code): confirm the Meshtastic NODE has an actual GPS fix — open the official Meshtastic app / node status, check for satellite lock. If the board has no GPS or no sky view, there's no position to send and this is NOT a code bug. Rule this out first. THEN if the node has a fix but the app still doesn't show it → logcat for POSITION packet receipt + the location-source switch (onRadioPosition / the source-selection logic).
⭐⭐ SHARPER DIAGNOSIS (Fred 08-14): device ID correctly shows the RADIO NAME (not Android name) — so the IDENTITY/device switch DID fire; the app knows a radio is connected. But GPS is still not processed from the radio. So there are TWO switches that should move together on radio-connect: (1) identity/device-name → WORKING, (2) GPS-source → NOT following. They're OUT OF SYNC — identity flipped to radio, but the position pipeline didn't switch from Android-GPS to the radio's position stream. Bug = "GPS source selection didn't follow device identity selection."
Two leads (Fred): (1) ⭐ STRONGEST — recent changes to "recognizing the Android default" GPS may have broken the HANDOFF: when a radio connects, the code that switches AWAY from Android GPS TO radio GPS was likely affected, severing "radio connected → use radio position" while leaving the identity switch intact. Look at what changed in Android-default recognition + whether it touched the source-selection branch. (2) SEED GPS SOURCE AT STARTUP — more robust pattern: DERIVE the GPS source from connection state ("is a radio connected?") rather than relying on an event-driven flag that can fail to fire / drift out of sync with identity. Echoes STATUS-IS-DERIVED: source should be derived from connection state, not a held flag.
⭐⭐⭐ CONFIRMED 08-14 by isolation test: a SECOND Android with NO internal GPS, connected to the radio → RADIO GPS WORKS. So the radio-GPS ingestion path is fully functional; the app CAN receive/process Meshtastic GPS. ⭐ PRECISE BUG (Fred): on connection the app REPLACES THE DEVICE NAME (identity) with the radio but does NOT replace the GPS SOURCE. Two separate actions at connect; only the name one fires. Identity flips to radio, position pipeline stays on Android GPS. Device WITH Android GPS → name shows radio but position stays Android (source never replaced) → looks like "radio GPS not working." Device WITHOUT Android GPS → no Android source to stay on → radio GPS used → works. FIX: at the connection handler, replace the GPS SOURCE at the same point the device NAME is replaced (they must move together) — or better, DERIVE the source from connection state ("radio connected? → radio is the source") so it can't be forgotten (STATUS-IS-DERIVED). Find the connect handler that swaps the name and add/repair the source swap beside it.
⭐ ISOLATION COMPLETE (Fred 08-14): SAME radio used on BOTH devices → rules out ALL radio config/firmware/GPS-settings issues (the node is proven good — Device B receives its position fine). The ONLY variable is the phone, specifically whether it has an internal GPS to compete. Fault is 100% app-side in the source-selection/replacement logic, and only manifests when an Android GPS source EXISTS to not-be-replaced. Radio exonerated, ingestion path exonerated. Bug fully located: connect handler replaces NAME but leaves existing Android GPS source in place instead of swapping to radio.

⛔ ALL-FILES-ACCESS (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) — Play review justification. HIGHEST rejection risk.
TRIPWIRE RULES: NEVER write on the form — "performance/faster/slow/speed/mph", "convenience/easier", or "forked Meshtastic/inherited/don't control install" (all read as "you don't really need it" or hit the explicit "performance is not acceptable" rejection). FIELD 1 (feature, ≤500): "GroupTrack is an offline navigation app for backcountry areas with no cellular service. Users download 50–60 GB of satellite and topographic map tiles into a shared-storage map database for offline use. All files access lets the app read and manage this large user-owned map database in shared storage so it persists across app reinstalls and data-clears, ensuring downloaded maps are not lost when connectivity to re-download them is unavailable."
FIELD 2 (usage checkboxes): Core functionality ONLY.
FIELD 3 (technical reason, ≤500): "The map-rendering engine opens map tiles directly by file path from a shared tile database as the user navigates. MediaStore manages only gallery media (images, audio, video), not a path-addressed tile database, and cannot provide the coordinate-based file access the renderer requires. SAF returns document URIs, not file paths, and cannot provide the direct file-path access the rendering and database layer depends on. The scoped alternatives are structurally incompatible with a path-based tile database."
FIELD 4 (video, https:// unlisted YouTube): airplane mode ON → open map → pan/zoom to z18 showing offline tiles loading from local storage. 20–30s. Caption: "Offline map tiles loading by file path from shared storage — no network."
⭐ THE REAL (internal-only) REASON, NOT for the form: at 30–60 mph the map renders hundreds of thousands of large PNG tiles at z18 by direct file path; MediaStore/SAF cannot serve that access model (this is feasibility, but stated as "performance" it auto-rejects — so the FORM says access-model incompatibility). FORK ORIGIN (also internal-only): the app is a Meshtastic fork; the inherited install/permission process has no provision for shared-storage map data — this is the architectural root of the install-authority defect (item 7). item 7's fix guarantees exactly the "survives reinstall" behavior this Play justification promises Google.
Observability — DECISION 08-14: SURVEY, not telemetry. (telemetry rejected)
The gap: Play Console shows only AGGREGATE install/version data, never per-person ("which of my testers, on what version, active when"). Fred wants that visibility.
⛔ REJECTED — launch telemetry (app phones home {userID, versionCode, timestamp} to RDS). Reason (Fred): it would require TRACKING USERS — dragging in Data-Safety declarations, privacy-policy coverage, deletion-request handling, data security, and Google privacy scrutiny. Too much compliance overhead for a free app just to satisfy curiosity about usage.
✅ CHOSEN — SURVEY the testers directly (a quick form: what version are you on? using it? issues?). Gives the observability with ZERO data-collection burden, zero Google privacy exposure, zero backend work — testers volunteer the info, nobody is silently tracked. Cleaner ethically, legally, operationally. Play's aggregate Statistics (active devices by version) covers the rest once the closed test goes live.
2.7 architecture question (raised 08-14 by the Play review): can we DROP all-files access?
Google steers hard toward scoped storage; all-files is the most-rejected permission and a single point of failure for the whole Play presence. Evaluate in 2.7: can the spatial DB + tile store migrate to a scoped shared directory (SAF tree / app-owned shared location) to eliminate MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE? ⚠ Blocker = the data layer opens tiles/DB by ABSOLUTE FILE PATH (SQLite/MBTiles), and SAF gives document URIs not paths — so this is a data-layer rewrite, not a config change. Middle path: request all-files but FALL BACK to a SAF-scoped folder if denied. Ties to the 2.7 rewrite + the install-authority redesign.

▶▶ 00-DISPLAYRULES — MY CART / MY GROUP / PLANNER. Build-ready spec.
The promise the whole design serves (Fred): "while you're riding you never
lose your spot on the map. The cart and MY GROUP always snap you back to proper zoom for that view,
but your cart never leaves the screen."
Everything follows from that sentence: auto-centering keeps you on the map · auto-zoom
keeps the group framed · the taper guarantees there is imagery at whatever zoom that lands
on. Three rules, one promise.
The three modes
ModeCentreZoomManual pan
MY CARTyour own GPSSTICKY — rider sets it, it staysdisabled
MY GROUPfit to all cartsDERIVED — the fit sets it, snaps backdisabled
PLANNERfreefreeenabled — different job
Both convoy modes: manual pan DISABLED · auto-centre ALWAYS ON · zoom NEVER cancels
auto-centre. ⚠ This reverses the old behaviour, where panning or zooming turned auto-centering
off.
⚠ 08-12 item 0 gates the PLANNER behind a connection until its offline tiles are fixed.
⛔ Problem 1 — jitter
Fitting on every GPS tick flickers the zoom continuously as carts drift back and forth
across a threshold. It needs asymmetric hysteresis:
Zoom OUT immediately when a cart leaves the frame — a safety response, no delay.
Zoom IN lazily, only after the group has stayed inside a tighter inner margin for several
seconds.
⭐ Deliberately asymmetric: losing sight of someone is worse than a slightly-too-wide
view.
⛔ Problem 2 — the stale cart
One rider drives home and the fit drags everyone else's map out to include them. At forty
miles apart the auto-zoom lands near z10 and nobody can see the trail.
⭐ The fit must EXCLUDE carts with no position update in N minutes — and SAY SO.
"2 carts not reporting" on the panel, rather than silently dropping them from the frame.
⭐ How the taper ties in
Whatever zoom the fit lands on, tiles exist. That is precisely what H=4 across z9-z18
guarantees — and it is why H must cover the worst-case screen rather than a typical one.
The fit chooses the zoom; the taper makes sure the choice is always covered.
⭐ Full design, math and device verification: living master 00-STARTHERE item 3.

⭐ That table is why z16 is the last good level. A tight group sits at z16, where the
half-mile band still fills the screen. The moment the group strings out, the app&rsquo;s own
auto-fit walks off the edge of the coverage.
⭐⭐ AND THE ANSWER IS THE SAME AT EVERY ZOOM: H &asymp; 2.1 TILES. That is not
tuning — it falls out of the arithmetic. Filling the screen needs half a screen-width either side,
and a screen is always ~4.2 tiles. So the formula is self-calibrating.
buffer(z) = H &times; tileWidth(z)
tiles(z)  = (trackLength / tileWidth(z) + 1) &times; (2H + 1)
⭐⭐⭐ AND THE TAPER MUST CONTINUE UPWARD PAST z16 TOO — THIS INVERTS THE
COST. Fred: "less time at z17 and z18 because the view is tighter — worth doing, not always a
minimum of half a mile without regard to zoom."
Applying the same rule at z17/z18 makes the whole thing CHEAPER than today:
RuleTotalvs today (10,791)
H=2 at every zoom5,560&minus;48%
H=3 at every zoom7,784&minus;28%
H=4 at every zoom10,008&minus;7%
H=3 with a 0.25 mi floor8,096&minus;25%
⭐ The saving is nearly all z18: 7,807 &rarr; 3,868 tiles, because 0.23 miles
either side is ALREADY three tiles of map at that zoom. Every level below z16 added together costs
546. The z18 saving pays for the entire taper five times over.
⭐ Fred: "drops size of tiles sent AND increases coverage to full panels at each zoom."
A filled screen at every level from z9 to z18, and a 28% smaller download.
⚠ USE THE 0.25 mi FLOOR — at z18 H=3 is only 0.23 mi either side, which is tight if a
recorded track wanders or GPS was loose. The floor costs almost nothing and keeps it at &minus;25%.
⚠ corridorTiles already loops per zoom with bufferDeg as a parameter,
so this changes WHAT THE BUFFER IS, not the structure. ⚠ Existing stores keep their shape — only new
downloads taper, which is why refreshing all corridors is the test.
⚠ Size the taper per track from getTrackBbox, not from a constant — the
figures above assume a 25&times;25 mile ride; a 60-mile-wide one is roughly 5&times; at z14.

🔴 ISSUE 2 — THE HORIZON. Not a bug; a design gap with a 4% fix.
At z16 the screen fills. At z15 and z14 the corners go white.
⚠ EACH ZOOM IS AN INDEPENDENT TILE SET. Having z18 gives you nothing at z13 —
they are separate downloads of the same ground at different resolutions, and the corridor fetches
all of them, but only for the band. "Less detail" does not mean "less data": it means MORE GROUND
PER TILE, so a wider view, so more of it outside your coverage.
THE FIX FRED ARRIVED AT — a horizon measured in TILES, not miles:
buffer(z) = H &times; tileWidth(z)
tiles(z)  = (trackLength / tileWidth(z) + 1) &times; (2H + 1)
H = 2  ->  always two tiles of map beyond the track, at every zoom

⭐ Why it is nearly free: the count is dominated by
trackLength / tileWidth, which grows 4&times; per level; the buffer is only a constant
multiplier (2H+1). So widening the horizon multiplies the CHEAP levels and leaves z18
untouched. z9 at seventy-eight miles of buffer costs TEN TILES because one z9 tile is 156 km
wide.
⚠ corridorTiles already loops per zoom with bufferDeg as a parameter —
the buffer just becomes a function of z. ⚠ Existing stores keep their shape; only new downloads get
the horizon, so Bar 10 would need re-downloading to fill in (444 tiles, seconds).

The first Recreate job killed the app: 512 MB, OutOfMemory.
⛔ I recorded "the worker was never the problem" because it filters to
hasTile. It does — but only AFTER calculateTiles materialises the WHOLE
RECTANGLE. A Recreate box holds at most 50,000 STORED tiles but can span degrees: at z18 a
three-degree box is roughly 4.8 million TileKey objects allocated before one is filtered.
⭐ Fixed e128cfc65 — MBTilesStore.tilesInBounds() asks the store
what it holds. Bounded by what is stored rather than by the size of the box, and faster: one indexed
range scan per level instead of millions of allocations plus a per-tile existence check.
Fred&rsquo;s original sentence, finally built: stream real tiles in existence by zoom for x
lon and lat.
⚠ The old code even LOGGED the ratio — "N in bounds, M exist on disk". The waste was
visible all along and only mattered once a box got big enough to exhaust the heap.

🔵 00-RECOVERYFILE — the .gtmaps recipe. QUEUED AFTER THE INSTALL REVISIONS.
⚠ This started as Recreate and sprawled into DR + reseeding a next device +
sharing with a friend before Fred pulled it back — his scope-creep rule firing:
"we can complicate everything ... gotta decide what we want to be."
⭐ DECISION: DR is the purpose. Seeding and sharing fall out FREE because it is
a plain file in Downloads. They are not designed for, and nothing in the build is shaped around
them.
⚠ Why it is needed at all: 08-11 established that a fresh install destroys map data in a
way that cannot be prevented or recovered from. The recipe does not save the tiles — it makes losing
them a download instead of a disaster.
The file
JSON, extension .gtmaps, written to Downloads. All slots in one file — a DR
file capturing only SAT would be a bad recipe on the day it is needed.
grouptrack_maps_2026-08-11.gtmaps
{ "version":1, "created":"2026-08-11T19:30Z",
  "slots":[ { "slot":"SAT", "source":"google-hybrid",
              "zMin":4, "zMax":18, "tiles":625386,
              "boxes":[ {"n":37.9,"s":37.6,"e":-112.1,"w":-112.4,"tiles":48213} ] } ] }
A few KB. The boxes are exactly what enqueueRecreateSource already computes — the
export is that same quadtree with a different sink.
Cadence — and why history removes a problem rather than adding one
Written on startup, once per day (same date overwrites), on a background thread.
Delete anything older than 60 days.
⭐ KEEPING HISTORY IS WHAT KILLS THE PARTIAL-SNAPSHOT PROBLEM. If today&rsquo;s
run happens mid-rebuild and captures half the coverage, yesterday&rsquo;s file is still there.
So there is no queue-state check, no migration check, no "is the store healthy" guard, and no
skip logic. Just write it.
⚠ The date in the filename IS the index. No prefs, no manifest-of-manifests, nothing to
keep in sync — and prefs are wiped by exactly the events this protects against.
⭐ Cost is nothing: ~40 boxes across three slots is a few KB, so 60 days is under 250 KB. The
scan is a few hundred indexed COUNTs with no blobs touched — a second or two.
The Recovery section — downloads panel, map settings
Lists the .gtmaps files by date, with tile counts. Select one →
REBUILD or EMAIL.
⭐ The tile count is the only judgement left, and it is a human glance rather than logic:
a file reading 180,000 next to yesterday&rsquo;s 625,386 is visibly a mid-rebuild capture, so you
pick the other one.
⚠ NO slot selection at rebuild. Fred: "the selection is just another failure
point. treat as update in place." INSERT OR REPLACE means a rebuild over a partly
intact store simply fills the gaps — nothing to half-apply, and running it twice costs nothing.
⛔⛔ THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE RIGHT — the replay job type
downloadType = DownloadType.AREA          // so the worker actually fetches
priority     = DownloadPriority.REFRESH   // lowest, yields to everything
These are SEPARATE FIELDS on QueueEntry, and DownloadPriority.forType() is
only a default helper — nothing forces them to match.
⛔ Type must be AREA because ConvoyDownloadWorker:97 filters
MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH jobs to hasTile. Replay a refresh-typed job onto a
rebuilt store and it downloads NOTHING — every job completes at zero tiles and looks
successful. That is the silent-failure class, and it would only be discovered during an actual
recovery.
⭐ Refresh means replace what I have; replay means fetch what I had. Same boxes,
opposite intent.
⚠ Put a comment at that line explaining why they differ, or someone will later "fix" the
mismatch and reintroduce it.
Import, email, and one thing to verify
⭐ Import is the PICKER / content-URI path — the same mechanism .convoy ride
files already use. The URI grants read access, so it needs no All-Files authority: the one
path that has never failed all week.
⚠ A file arriving by email is owned by the mail app, so it must be LAUNCHED, not scanned
for. The app can only scan for files it wrote itself.
⚠ Email out is ACTION_SEND with the file attached. May need a
FileProvider entry — check whether the existing ride transfer already declares one
before adding manifest work.
⚠ VERIFY ONCE, DO NOT ASSUME: does a file the app writes to Downloads survive an
uninstall? Shared storage generally does, but MediaStore tracks the owning app — and DR must not
rest on an untested assumption. Write one, uninstall, look.
⚠ TILES ONLY. Tracks, trails, routes and waypoints are captured data and need real backup.
This recipe cannot reproduce them.
🔴🔴 00-ROOTCAUSE (08-11) — THE THREE ROOT CAUSES. FIX THESE, NOT THE SYMPTOMS.
Fred named these after the 08-11 Droid 1 collapse. Everything else that day was
downstream of one of them.
1 — AREA DOWNLOAD REQUESTS GROUND THAT HAS NO TILES
Fred: "download area must stream real tiles in existence by zoom for x lon and
lat."
The area path derives a bbox and calculates the whole rectangle. The existence check
happens later, per tile, inside the worker — so the QUEUE fills with a continent of work,
most of which is then skipped one tile at a time. Droid 1: 3,287 jobs, ETA 194 days.
⚠ Why it went continental: the scope comes from the store&rsquo;s EXTENT. With Utah
coverage and any stray tile near New Hampshire, that extent spans coast to coast and the refresh
covers all of it. ⛔ And it is not just a Fred problem — any rider who travels between
download regions gets the same result.
⭐ THE FIX: scan what actually EXISTS and refresh only that. Query the store for
stored tiles, group them into jobs, download those. A cell with no tiles never enters a job,
so disjoint regions stay disjoint and corridors stay corridors — by construction, not by
inference.
⚠ z16 is the vetting level (Fred): ~490 m, roughly a third of corridor width, so a skinny
track is traced rather than smeared. z12 (~7.7 km) would drag in ground never downloaded.
⚠ PAYLOAD: a job cannot carry hundreds of thousands of tile keys in
inputData. It must carry a re-queryable range and let the worker re-derive at
run time — the same constraint that shaped corridor jobs.
⭐⭐ THIS RETIRES THE MANDATORY DELETE IN OPTION 2. The delete existed because
the area pass inferred scope from a bbox and boxed corridor ground. Tile-for-tile refresh has no
area pass — nothing infers shape, so corridor geometry cannot be lost. Coverage never drops
either, because INSERT OR REPLACE overwrites in place. Fred: "we do not need a
delete ... this function should be refresh a map source, all tiles."
⚠ Option 1 (clear and start over) stays for people who want it.
2 — CANCELLING 3,287 QUEUED JOBS ANR&rsquo;d THE APP
The cancel walks every entry — removing it from the list, cancelling its WorkManager id,
and saving the queue file — on the main thread. Thousands of writes, UI blocked, ANR.
⭐ CANCEL WORKERS may be gentler than CANCEL ALL, since it stops workers rather than
walking entries. ⚠ The real fix is moving the walk off the main thread and batching the saves.
⭐ Related, already queued: HIDE completed and cancelled entries on hold-and-cancel — the
tester&rsquo;s panel was too congested to find live activity. Hide, NOT remove: the estimator
and the yardstick both compute from completed rows.
3 — INSTALL IS STILL HAMMERING EXISTING FILES
This is 00-REFUSE — refuse-to-create — still unbuilt after TWO
data-loss events.
A fresh install runs setup, believes it has All-Files authority when it does not, cannot see
Documents/GroupTrack/, reads that as a new device, and writes empty schemas over
real data.
⚠ It blocked a safe recovery action THREE TIMES on 08-11 alone. Every time an uninstall
and reinstall was the obvious move, this was the reason not to. ⭐ Highest-value unbuilt
item in the project.
⚠ AND THE 08-11 DROID 1 SYMPTOM WAS NEVER DIAGNOSED
White basemap at every zoom, every source, ONLINE AND OFFLINE, while tracks and trails
drew normally.

🔵 00-DEADCODE (2.7 PREREQUISITE) — DISCOVER AND REMOVE UNREFERENCED CODE
Fred 08-11: this is the FIRST 2.7 task, before the convoy rewrite. The sweep is
not housekeeping — you cannot cleanly rewrite what you cannot tell is in use, and every dead
path carried into the rewrite is a path that gets ported.
THE METHOD, in Fred&rsquo;s order:
Remove unused functionality from the PANELS first, and kill their launch points. A
function reachable only from a menu row you have just deleted becomes detectable — before that it
looks live.
Clean the GroupTrack menu, submenus and the settings panel. That is what surfaces the
next layer of orphans.
Then use the xrefs to nominate unreferenced functions and remove them ONE AT A TIME,
with a build between each, so the model always compiles and runs.
⭐ Use the cheap gate, not a full build: ./gradlew compileGoogleReleaseKotlin
is ~2 minutes against ~12-30 for an assemble. That is what makes one-at-a-time affordable.

▶ WHY THIS IS A 2.7 PREREQUISITE, NOT A CHORE
Fred 08-11: 2.7 is "the rewrite and taming of the convoy app, the removal of dead code

⭐⭐⭐ WHY IT COLLAPSED FROM A REFACTOR TO THREE SMALL COMMITS
CREATE TABLE routes (... geom_hash TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(geom_hash))
geom_hash is CONTENT-ADDRESSED and UNIQUE in BOTH tables, and
insertRoute already computes it. The same hash therefore means the same geometry
wherever it is stored, so a corridor derived from either table is identical.
⭐ That removed all of it: no artifact-type parameter, no new
QueueEntry field, no inputData change, no worker change, and no
serialisation risk to a queue already persisted on devices.
⚠ The 07-27 note in section 17 had this right all along — "the blocker dissolved on
inspection: the routes table already carries geom_hash." The 08-06 note claiming otherwise was
WRONG and drove a far larger design. ⭐⭐ CHECK THE SCHEMA BEFORE DESIGNING AROUND A DATA
MODEL. One query would have saved the detour.
⚠ A FOURTH track-only lookup surfaced only on inspection: the SAVE MAPS lambda calls
getTrackBbox BEFORE the pipeline is reached, so a route would have failed at the very
first step and been told it had no geometry. ⚠ Two call sites, and each file ALSO has an
onDownloadMaps (AREA) lambda with an identical bbox line that must stay tracks-only —
a bare-line anchor would have patched the wrong one.
⛔ insertRoute DEFECT, real now that UNIQUE is confirmed:
newId() → INSERT OR IGNORE → return id. On duplicate
geometry nothing inserts and a fabricated id is returned. Blocks reliable GPX route
import; the panel path does not need it. Fix: read back the surviving route_id by
geom_hash.
⭐ ZOOM CAP — SAT z18, RENDERED z16, DOWNLOAD AND DISPLAY
490096e49 (ZOOMSLOT-2026-08-10D, corridor downloads) +
151febe07 (both HTML maps).
⭐ KEYED ON THE SLOT, NOT THE SOURCE. Every download path already carries the
slot — enqueueCorridor takes slotName, the worker reads
refresh_slot, the area path carries selectedSlots. None carry the source:
corridorTiles had no source parameter at all. So the slot needs no new plumbing,
and it publishes as one sentence a rider can understand instead of a table of vendor ceilings.
Fred&rsquo;s economics: each level quadruples the tile count. Satellite is upscaled rather
than sharper above z18 in open country; a topo map has said everything it has by z16. "most data
in the least space."
⛔⛔ THE CAP IS OPT-IN AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. ConvoyCorridorDelete calls the
same corridorTiles. A capped delete computes a SMALLER set than an older build stored,
leaving z17-z18 tiles that nothing can ever find or remove on a multi-gigabyte store. Empty
slot = no cap; only the two DOWNLOAD paths pass one, and the patch VERIFIES the delete path did not
gain one.
⚠ STILL UNCAPPED: the AREA path — calculateTiles has a
sourceName parameter that NOTHING passes, so its cap never fires; nine call
sites would need the slot. And quickEstimate has no slot either, so the live preview
overstates against a capped download.
⭐ Display uses maxNativeZoom, so zoom CONTINUES past the cap and upscales
rather than stopping. That is the better behaviour: artifact overlays stay sharp at any zoom, so a
rider can still place a waypoint precisely over a soft basemap. ⚠ Cost: pre-cap z17-18 topo tiles
stop being drawn. They are not deleted and cost nothing; they age out at the next source change.
⚠ setMaxOfflineZoom/maxOfflineZoom is an INDICATOR, not a
ceiling — its body writes a text element and never touches currentMaxNative. It is
fed by a scan for z-named DIRECTORIES, a layout MBTiles replaced, so it likely reports nothing now.
Separate cleanup.
⛔⛔ THE ROTATION BUG — A TESTER LOST A RUNNING MIGRATION
MainActivity declared NO configChanges, so Android destroyed and recreated it
on rotation — taking the composable, its state, and the coroutine scope the corridor delete runs
on. A tester rotated their phone mid-delete and the panel vanished with no way to tell whether
the work was still running.
FIXED 15e1acebf (ROTATE-2026-08-10F):
configChanges="orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|keyboardHidden".
Fred: "just leave the screen open unless an action is taken to end it. period."
⭐ Chosen over rememberSaveable deliberately: saving state would rebuild the
panel with the right numbers, but the coroutine would still have been cancelled — it would look
alive while doing nothing, which is worse than a blank screen. Keeping the activity is what
keeps the WORK.
⚠ NOT a full fix — a swipe-away or a kill still ends it. Moving the delete off the UI
scope remains the real answer. ⚠ Watch for orientation-qualified resources no longer reloading.
⛔ WHAT THE TESTER'S RUN EXPOSED — TWO DEFECTS BEYOND THE ROTATION
1 — STRANDED: the delete completed, the submit never ran. Corridors removed,
queue EMPTY, coverage gone, and no indication anything was wrong. The code already warns
about this shape: "killing the process mid-run strands the user with removed coverage and
nothing scheduled to rebuild it."
⭐ Recovery is a re-run — already-deleted corridors skip at ~0.4 s each, so it moves through and
reaches the submit. ⚠ But the app cannot DETECT this state. A check on launch for "coverage
removed, nothing scheduled" would turn a confusing hour into a prompt.
⛔ 2 — A SUCCESSFUL DELETE WAS RECORDED AS FAILED. The first pass logged
failures; the second pass popped through in seconds, which is the signature of nothing left to
delete. The tiles came off and the record said otherwise. The delete and
recordCompletedDelete are not atomic, so a failure in the RECORD is indistinguishable
from a failure to DELETE.
⚠ This is what made an hour of diagnosis necessary — and on a destructive operation it is
worse than cosmetic: a user either re-runs needlessly, or believes their data survived when it did
not.
⭐⭐ THE DELETE IS DEVICE-BOUND, NOT CODE-BOUND — SETTLED FOR GOOD
Samsung tablet: 99 tracks in 15 SECONDS. Droid 2: ~1.8 hours. Same build.
⛔ Every hypothesis chased on 08-09 was looking for a defect in code that runs hundreds of
times faster on ordinary hardware. Seven died; the answer was that Droid 2 has slow storage.
⛔ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DOCS: the panel copy saying "a few hours" is calibrated to the slowest
device owned and will alarm everyone else. Say it depends on the device and how much is held,
and let the progress meter carry the rest. No duration claim.

⭐⭐ THE ETA WAS TWO CALCULATIONS THAT DISAGREED BY 6x
The panel displayed 37.2 tiles/sec and "3 hours" for 69,000 tiles. 69,000 ÷ 37.2 is
31 minutes; a 3-hour ETA implies ~6.4 tiles/sec — a sixth of the number on the same screen.
estimateRemaining() ignored the displayed rate and computed its own from all tiles
ever completed over elapsed-since-the-earliest-job. ⛔ Its firstStart block fell back to
createdAt — QUEUE TIME — for completed entries, so hours of waiting before the
first tile downloaded counted as elapsed. Its own comment says createdAt is queue time and that
this is what made the estimates unusable. The code then used it.
⚠ It was asymmetric too: the denominator reached back to the first job QUEUED while the numerator
only counted entries still present — so clearing completed rows shrank one side and not the
other.
⭐ FIX (Fred): one rate. liveRate() extracted as the single
definition; the display and the estimate divide by the same value. 22 lines deleted.
If the panel says 37 tiles/sec and 69,000 remain, the estimate is 31 minutes — the arithmetic the
user can do in their head.

THE CORRIDOR DELETE — SETTLED. NOT A DEFECT.
~95-100 tiles/sec, linear with tile count. 88 of 88 completed.
⛔⛔ SEVEN HYPOTHESES, ALL DEAD: missing transaction (already one, 500
rows/statement) · missing index (already exists) · O(n²) re-derivation (the preview did 88 tracks in
40 s) · concurrent deletes (one SQLite writer per file) · delete the union (re-deleting absent rows
costs 0.4 s) · drop/rebuild the index (it is the only way to find rows) ·
the pragmas (applied and confirmed on device, NO EFFECT).
⭐⭐ THE ANSWER: IT IS NOT SLOW. Deletes run ~100 tiles/sec; downloads run
20-62. The delete is faster per tile than the download. And before MBTiles there was no
removal option at all — testers factory-reset their devices. Two hours unattended replaced
days of manual work or a wipe.
⚠ THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON, by accident: tracks deleted in the morning were re-visited at
night and returned tiles=0 in 0.4 s. Bar 10 overnighter: 189 s with rows, 0.4 s
without. Same corridor, same statements. The cost is the physical row removal, nothing
else.

⛔⛔ 00-INCIDENT (08-08) — THE UNRECOVERABLE QUEUE. SPATIAL DB LOST ON DROID 2.
WHAT HAPPENED, IN ORDER
Option 2 was run with corridors selected. The delete never executed —
optTracks was false at the confirm handler although the box appeared ticked.
Corridor tiles therefore stayed on disk. The area pass read them as area coverage and
queued 172 jobs to re-download that ground as rectangles.
The panel stayed up: refreshEnqueued was only set at the END of the coroutine, so
nothing dismissed it.
Queue entries were cleared while WorkManager still held the jobs. Workers take every parameter
from inputData and never consult the queue, so they kept starting — running
20 minutes at 0 tiles, with no failure.
The panel returns early when the queue is empty, so RELEASE and CANCEL were not on
screen. Force-stop did not help: WorkManager exists to survive process death and rescheduled
them.
The only exit was clearing app data. The spatial DB went with it.
⭐ THE COST OF NOT DELETING, MEASURED: 30 tracks swept up as areas cost
2M+ tiles on ONE source. 89 tracks as proper corridors cost 1.5M across THREE.
Corridors were designed for a ~90% reduction and that holds. The delete is not space
reclamation — it is what stops corridor ground being re-covered as boxes.
WHAT WAS FIXED (all in c5fc7985b and d92e472fb)
Orphan block. Both workers look their entry up immediately after init. No
entry, no work. ⚠ Returns failure, not success — an orphan reporting success writes a lie
into the log, and failure() is terminal where retry() would resurrect it
on backoff. ⚠ Deliberately does NOT call markFailed: there is no entry to mark, and
writing one would trade a running ghost for a permanent row.
Held-queue escape. The panel now computes qoHeld from
isQueuePaused() and both early returns respect it. A held queue renders even with zero
entries, showing QUEUE HELD — nothing will start with RELEASE, and
CANCEL WORKERS whenever held or empty.
Always exitable. The migration run sets its terminal state in a finally, so
a throw cannot strand the panel.
Step 0 records what the handler received — tracks=$optTracks areas=$optAreas
to the log AND the first on-screen line. ⚠ THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO READ ON THE NEXT RUN.
If it disagrees with what was ticked, the original defect is still live and it is visible in one
second rather than twenty minutes.

🔴 00-ESTIMATOR (08-08) — WAS 8-10x LONG. REWRITTEN.
MEASURED: the panel said Aug 12 5 AM (~86 hours) for 1.5M remaining tiles. The real
rate was ~140,000/hour — about 10 hours.
Two defects compounded:
The rate came from ONE entry's elapsed time, which is a per-slot rate, while 3-4 slots
run concurrently.
Averaging the last two entries does not fix it — if those two ran concurrently their
windows overlap, so the average is still a slot rate.
⚠ And createdAt is queue time, not start time. A job that waited behind 87
others carried hours of waiting in its elapsed. That alone was worth an order of magnitude.
⭐ REPLACED WITH FRED'S FORMULATION (08-08): total tiles completed since the run
began, divided by elapsed wall-clock since the earliest job started. That IS the aggregate rate
by construction. Concurrency cannot fool it, it absorbs stalls, holds and slot changes, and it
needs no MAX_CONCURRENT multiplier — every failure mode above disappears rather than
being corrected for. It is also the same arithmetic the yardstick ledger does across sessions, so
the two finally agree.
Supporting work: startedAt stamped at dispatch, tilesPerSec computed at
completion and stored on the entry (Fred: "the job knows duration and tiles — that is where the
calc belongs"), both persisted and backward-compatible on read.

summed to 3 and happened to match what one Esri download wrote, so it looked correct. Under Google
Hybrid one layer is written and the estimate stayed at 3x.
MEASURED 08-08: a job estimated 19,000 and finished at 6,463 — 2.94x.
⭐ Every other enqueue path (:257, :279, :612) already
filtered by slot. Only the unsegmented one was missed. ⚠ Fixed by filtering to the SAT slot, NOT by
removing the multiplier — a slot back on Esri must still count its 3 layers.
