⛔⛔⛔ 00-MARKER-LIFETIME (08-16) — A PLAIN REINSTALL WAS DELETING BOTH DATABASES. FOUND, FIXED, CERTIFIED.
The defect
SpatialDbManager.init() carries a one-time "regenerate-not-migrate" delete gate. Its own
comment stated the assumption that broke it: "DBs live in PUBLIC storage and survive uninstall/clear-data,
so this in-app delete is the SOLE clearing mechanism." True — but the marker gating it was
db_schema_marker in SharedPreferences, which is app-private and does not
survive an uninstall. The gate and the thing it gated had different lifetimes. "Fires exactly once
per upgrade" was really "fires once per install."
08:15:02.463  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: delete grouptrack_spatial.db = true
08:15:02.503  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: delete grouptrack_data.db = true
08:15:02.514  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: spatial-clean=true extension-clean=true (marker was 0)
08:15:02.515  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: marker set to 3; DBs will rebuild from v3 assets
08:15:02.978  SpatialDbMgr: Spatial DB: 0 trails, 0 tracks, 0 waypoints, 0 routes
⭐ marker was 0 is the whole story. Not a failed open, not an authority problem —
the app deliberately deleted the data because it could not tell "never migrated" from "migrated, then
reinstalled." The authority canary ran at 08:15:02.123, 340 ms BEFORE the deletion, and passed.
The gate worked. This was never an authority bug.
⚠ This is the inverted form of the guard specced after 08-01: marker absent + external DB
present = fresh install over existing data → STOP. The marker was designed as a stop condition and
implemented as a delete trigger.
The fix — two commits, two independent halves
233e61e50 — marker moves to a FILE, .db_schema_version, beside the
databases so its lifetime matches theirs. Read order is file → legacy prefs → 0; the prefs
fallback carries existing installs across the changeover, without which this fix would itself have wiped
every current install exactly once. Plus a row-count guard: populated databases mean the install has
already been through the migration whatever the marker says, so it stamps and skips. A count that cannot be
taken (the SELinux ioctl denial on the FUSE-mounted .db is routine) returns −1 and is treated
as populated — refuse to delete on uncertainty.
c503b3247 — stamp-if-missing. Caught on device, not in review: an install whose
marker came from the legacy prefs value reached neither of the two branches that write the file, so
the file was never laid down at all and the install stayed protected by app-private state — the exact
mismatch the whole fix exists to remove. Now: marker resolved and current but file absent → write it.
Certification (Droid 2, 08-16)
Install over live data → marker file appears containing 3; sizes unchanged.
Uninstall → marker file survives in Documents/; prefs gone with the package.
Reinstall → log shows no migration block at all, and
Spatial DB: 152200 trails, 88 tracks, 559 waypoints. Sizes byte-identical.
⭐ Note what that proves: not the row guard catching a miss, but the marker being read straight
from public storage so the gate never armed. Belt and braces both verified independently.
Consequences to carry
THE 08-12 CLEAR-CACHE PROHIBITION IS RETIRED. Clear-cache on live data left both DBs
byte-identical and mesh setup values intact; no state restore fired, no install questionnaire.
⚠ Scope of the proof: that run had no UID change and no named-track import in flight.
⭐ Consequence: "clear the WebView cache to fix a stale bundled asset" is an available remedy again.
REFUSE-TO-CREATE (00-REFUSE) is now load-bearing, not aspirational. Today's fix closes
this trigger. A DB open that refuses to CREATE where a file should already exist is what turns the NEXT
unknown trigger into a loud error instead of silent loss. There is no backup and the map DBs are 50–60 GB.
On today's evidence it is arguably promotable into 2.6f.
Signature worth reading instantly: maps survive + artifacts vanish = a create-if-missing DB
overwrite, NOT an authority failure. .mbtiles never go through this path, so their survival
proves nothing about correctness — and a UID that could not read the DBs could not read the tiles either.
Empty-schema fingerprint: grouptrack_data.db ≈ 208,896 B, grouptrack_spatial.db
≈ 118,784 B.
Recovery profile, measured: trails re-import from OSM, tracks resync from the track directory,
waypoints likewise — full rebuild ≈ 1 hour. Graduated routes are the only unrecoverable class
(see 00-DISCARD-DESIGN). Maps are never lost.
✅ 00-GATE-FINAL (08-16) — THE AUTHORITY GATE: SETTLED BEHAVIOUR, AND THE LATCH CORRECTION
Behaviour as shipped — all three paths device-verified
SituationWhat happens
Authority already real on the FIRST evaluation of the sessionNo gate at all — straight to Convoy. Nothing was just granted, so there is nothing to settle.
State changed to Granted DURING the session (returned from settings)Continue barrier retained — the tap lets the grant land before the DB opens. This is the flash-past race and it is still real.
Went to settings, came back WITHOUT granting all-filesStorageDeclined. States the app will not open without it, and that exiting is safe. Buttons: Try again / Exit. No proceed door.
Background location not grantedAdvisory. Skip for now proceeds. Deliberately NOT remembered — the prompt recurs every launch.
Why no proceed door on storage (Fred, 08-16): "the app is unusable without that authority,
period" and "cancel is the option that should be taken — they can choose not to use the app."
Claude had proposed a proceed-at-your-own-risk path and then argued against it: without refuse-to-create,
proceeding means silently destroying data, described to the user as a risk they cannot evaluate, because
the failure looks like "no trails" rather than "your data was overwritten." Settled: no third door. The
screen also states that exiting changes nothing — which is accurate, because the gate halts before
any database is opened or created.
Why background location IS skippable and IS repeated (Fred): "background authority is not
destructive — it reduces functionality and can be quickly changed." And the repetition is deliberate:
"the reminder is fine, it warns of degradation when recording a track with an app that goes to
sleep." A rider who skipped three weeks ago will not remember before a ride that their track dies when
the screen sleeps.
⚠⚠ THE DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION — record this, not the first story
Symptom: grant all-files, return, and the screen stayed on StorageDeclined; a
force-close and relaunch then passed immediately.
Claude's theory: a settle race — the probe taken the instant the user returns reads "not granted"
because the grant has not landed yet. A five-attempt / 400 ms retry loop was built on that theory.
The logs disproved it the moment they existed. Every retry read
realStorage=false all the way through attempt 4, and the successful grant passed on
attempt 0. The retries never once rescued a grant.
The real defect: LifecycleResumeEffect(Unit) evaluated once on resume and
latched the result. With settingsVisited set, a negative read became
StorageDeclined and nothing re-evaluated — the user who had just granted access was
stranded on a screen saying the app would not open. Latched state, not a timing race. The fix that
mattered was re-evaluating on each resume; the retry loop is harmless insurance.
⭐ The general lesson: a fix built on an unverified theory can pass its test for a reason
unrelated to the theory. The instrumentation that made this visible was added in the same patch — without
it this would have gone into the release recorded as a race condition that never existed.
Also fixed: Exit was a dead button
onExit was bound to navController?.popBackStack() in
ConvoyNavigation.kt — but the gate is the nav START destination, so there is nothing
beneath it, the call returns false and no-ops. A dead button on the one screen that tells the user the app
will not open. Now finishes the hosting activity: exiting from the start destination means leaving the app,
which is the stated intent.
Gate logging (new): tag ConvoyGate, one line per evaluation —
realStorage=, background=, chosen state, attempt index.
adb -s &lt;serial&gt; logcat -s ConvoyGate. ⚠ StorageManager /
MediaProvider "Failed to update quota type for .authority_probe" is noise —
platform bookkeeping reacting to a file created and deleted within milliseconds. It appears on launches
that pass cleanly and open 152,200 trails.

🗣 00-DISCARD-DESIGN (08-16) — THE FIVE-PLUS-ONE BOUNDARY. DESIGN SETTLED, NOT BUILT. (2.6g)
⛔ THE DIAGNOSIS (Fred): "that tangle is what caused unpredictable results — 6
versions of discard all mixing and matching the 6 functions."
Six sites, six independently-assembled combinations of the same operations. Each looked reasonable
alone, so every fix was site-local and the next path exhibited a different variant. The bug was the
ABSENCE of the module; site-local fixes kept producing new variants. The tell: each fix works and the
next report describes different behaviour. This is worse than literal copy-paste — literal copies at
least fail identically.
⛔⛔ And some sites are genuinely WRONG, not merely different (Fred): they did not
remove the in-memory data or the JSON, and "those items are all joined." The JSON on disk, the
in-memory route and the drawn canvas are three representations of one thing. A site that updates a
subset leaves them disagreeing, and the next operation reads whichever it happens to consult — state
divergence. That is why the "phantom draft" looked recreated: it never left memory.
⭐ VISIBLE SYMPTOM, now a signature: the route reappears when the next vertex is dropped. Memory
was never cleared, so the append redraws it with the new vertex attached. The divergence is created at
discard and revealed later — which is why it resisted attribution. It points straight at the site; no
bisecting needed.
The boundary, as Fred specified it — FIVE in the module, ONE owned by the caller
MODULE (unconditional, every path):
  1. clearRoute()
  2. deleteDraft(name)
  3. JS clearBuildLine()
  4. addPointMode = false
  5. draftListTick++
CALLER:
  6. setRouteMode(...)
Fred: "route mode is a function of the process discard is in — does it stay in the app, in which case
draw mode stays active, or does it end the route draw session." Only the caller knows the destination.
⭐ This makes the module take no flags and no exit-vs-stay parameter, and it makes the
audit mechanical: any site doing fewer than all five is a bug, full stop. A missing
setRouteMode is not automatically a bug — it depends on where the user is going.
Previously those two questions were tangled, which is why the 08-13 survey could only mark the resolver
site "missing clearRoute + JS + arm flags" without knowing which absences mattered.
⭐⭐ It is TWO operations, not one: discard and save
Both END a route session; they differ only in what happens to the draft first (delete vs persist).
Consequence: the two SAVE sites (~1539 SAVE-as-completed, ~1717 SAVE-as-WIP) were filed in the 08-13
survey as "not discards" and were therefore never audited for teardown completeness. Under this
factoring they are the same shape and must be checked with the rest. If any save path leaves arm flags set
or the build line drawn, that is the same class of bug — just filed under a different word.
The six sites to classify by destination (ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt, ⚠ re-grep line
numbers, they drift): ~1646 onExit (fixed 08-13, the archetype) · ~1775 "Delete in-progress"
dialog · ~1834 resolver Discard · ~1923 picker Delete · ~1539 SAVE-completed · ~1717 SAVE-WIP.
⚠ No STUB: markers were ever placed — Phase 1 of the 08-13 stub plan never ran
(08-15 went to the authority gate instead). The extraction source is f9652276c.
Route recovery — the only unrecoverable data class
Trails re-import, tracks resync, waypoints likewise. Graduated (permanent) routes have nothing behind
them, because graduation is exactly the step that stops maintaining a file on disk. WIP drafts survive
everything (Fred: "they have survived since day 1") because they are files outside the DB-open path.
That asymmetry is the defect, not the incident.
Fred's fix (08-16): archive the WIP into a completed/ subfolder we can recreate from.
⭐ Cheapest useful version: COPY at save time, DB row stays authoritative — a few lines, no new read path,
no format decision, and it closes the class on its own. ⚠ OPEN: copy-and-keep-DB-authoritative, or does the
archived file become the recovery format with its own re-import path? The second is real work and overlaps
the route-distribution feature already wanted.
🔎 00-STARTUP-SURVEY (08-16) — THE DECLARED STARTUP PHASE, AND THE HUNT FOR OTHER ONE-SHOTS. (2.6g)
⭐⭐⭐ THE ARGUMENT IS OBSERVABILITY, NOT SEQUENCING (Fred): "the issue was the
unobservability of a one-shot process that deleted and recreated DBs."
It announced itself as three I/ log lines inside a 353,608-line buffer. No UI, no
user-facing consequence, no record that survives the session. We caught it only because the ring buffer had
not rolled yet. A one-shot destructive operation should be the loudest thing the app does. Same
principle already banked for the queue: the record is the artifact — filtering hides reversibly, deletion
destroys evidence.
⚠ ORDERING CORRECTION. "Ahead of the authority grants" does not work mechanically: the
08-16 log shows the canary at 08:15:02.123 and the deletes at .463 — the migration
already ran AFTER authority. Running it earlier means operating without a verified grant, and a delete that
fails on scoped storage takes the retry branch (marker NOT advanced, will retry next launch) = a loop
where each attempt is another chance to half-delete. ⭐ Correct slot: AFTER the authority gate, BEFORE
Convoy — a slot the gate already owns as the nav start destination, so it needs no edit to
ConvoyScreen at all.
Fred on why this outranks the individual fix: "a big ball of yarn twisted into a circle — it
rolls, but you are still afraid to untangle the strings." Least-invasive is how a tangle keeps rolling.
The deliverable is the RULE about where work belongs, not the relocation. A rule tells a future
migration where to go without anyone having to remember today.
⚠ Recorded honestly: a pre-convoy job would have run the SAME logic against the SAME marker
and produced the SAME wipe, just from a tidier place. The structural work buys observability and ordering;
refuse-to-create buys protection. Keep the two credits separate.
The survey — not started, and it is the input the phase needs
Fred: "who knows how many other start-up tasks are embedded in convoy using the hunt-seek-find method
of locating it within the startup stack so it runs today and produces the right results but maybe not
tomorrow." Two instances already found — the v3 migration gate and AutoResyncHost.
No reason to assume they are the last two.
Hunt shape: markers and version gates (getSharedPreferences,
getInt(.*marker, version &lt;) · one-shot latches (firstRun,
hasMigrated, if (!.*initialized) · destructive calls in startup paths
(.delete(), deleteDatabase, mkdirs near an open) · everything hanging
off MainActivity.onCreate, Application.onCreate and Convoy's entry composables.
Use --include='*.kt' to skip the .bak_* files.
⭐ Start with field_crossref_raw.txt — one-shot state lives in FIELDS
(markers, flags, hasRun), so a field index surfaces them directly; then grep the call sites.
⚠ The xrefs are DEFINITION/symbol indexes, not a call graph — grep stays authoritative for call
sites. Regenerated in f7be2e056, current as of 08-16.
Cost: about an hour of grep and reading. No builds, no device risk. Fits a window while something else

▶ TOMORROW — TWO TASKS, IN ORDER. Full detail so a fresh conversation can execute.
TASK 1 — Standardize all discard functions to the same 6-call teardown
Why: the discard/teardown logic is duplicated across sites, each doing a different
subset of the steps — classic copy-paste drift, and exactly what let the onExit bug hide.
Fred: "standardize all discard functions to the same 6 calls … there is no reason for the
differences." Consistency pass FIRST (safe — only adds missing steps), refactor to a shared
function SECOND (separate, later step). Rationale: refactoring identical code is safe;
consolidating divergent code forces picking a winner per difference and can propagate a bug to every
call site at once.
The canonical 6-step teardown (active-session discard):
1. RouteManager.clearRoute()
2. RouteDraftStore.deleteDraft(&lt;name&gt;)
3. webViewRef?.evaluateJavascript("setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine();", null)
4. addPointMode = false
5. routeMode = false
6. draftListTick++
Sites in app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt
(⚠ RE-GREP line numbers first — they drift every edit):

~1834 resolver "Discard"UNNAMED remnant discard❌ MISSING clearRoute + JS setRouteMode(false)/clearBuildLine + addPointMode=false + routeMode=false. Has only deleteDraft(UNNAMED)+draftListTick++. → bring to full 6.

independent mechanisms. Consistency-first, then consolidate — never extract from divergent copies
(that forces picking a winner per difference and can propagate a bug to all six). VERIFY via the

to confirm ZERO sites still carry their own inline teardown. This is the exact discipline that would
have prevented the original discard bug (the missing deleteDraft at onExit would have

TASK 2 — Run recommit_docs_v16.sh and verify no issues
What v16 fixes: the recommit bug where a bare git commit committed the ENTIRE
index — so anything already staged before a run got folded into the "docs:" commit (this is how the
08-11 bisect revert and asset edits got swept into docs history, shifting the ground under later
edits). v16's fix: the commit is scoped to docs only via
git commit -m "docs: …" -- "$DOCS" (pathspec), so nothing outside docs/ is
ever swept, regardless of index state. v16 is the uploaded/placed file; it is currently
untracked in git (was at docs/recommit_docs_v16.sh).
Pre-run guards (Fred's standing rules — DO NOT skip):
git status FIRST. If anything unexpected is staged, unstage it. (v16 is safe
regardless, but the glance is free.)
ONE tree-touching job at a time. No Gradle build running; not inside any patch's
generate→certify window. Recommit runs AFTER an AAB publish, never during a build.
Steps:
git status — confirm clean/expected.
Commit the v16 script itself deliberately BY NAME first (don't let a recommit be what commits
it): git add docs/recommit_docs_v16.sh &amp;&amp; git commit -m "docs: recommit v16 (scope commit to docs pathspec)".
Run bash docs/recommit_docs_v16.sh.
Verify no sweep: git show --stat HEAD on the resulting docs commit — confirm
it touched only docs/, no .kt/.html assets folded in.
Confirm the xref / AllDocs regenerated (not stale). Freshness assertions / completion marker
should report DONE.
⚠ If it swept anything outside docs/ → the pathspec fix didn't take; inspect
the commit line in the script (must be git commit -m "…" -- "$DOCS", not a bare
git commit).

🗣 00-2.7-DISCUSSION — planning substrate for 2.7 (accumulated design findings, 08-14). NOT a spec — a roadmap to plan from.
⭐⭐ FEATURE VISION (Fred 08-15) — THE "MOST INTERESTING ROUTE" PLANNER. Differentiated; future (2.7+ / own tier). NOT 2.6f.
The feature: user drops vertices/waypoints all over a map → app auto-designs 3-4 DISTINCT rideable routes, each 45-60 miles / 5-9 hours of riding (at OHV speeds), that collectively connect all the dropped points. Multi-day trip planning over the trail network.
⭐ THE DIFFERENTIATOR: existing routing (Google/onX/standard nav) optimizes SHORTEST/FASTEST. OURS optimizes the MOST INTERESTING route — the best RIDE, not the quickest path. For OHV riders "shortest" is the WRONG answer; nobody off-roads to get somewhere fast. We BORROW the routing machinery (graph traversal / pathfinding — solved, take from existing algos) but CHANGE THE OBJECTIVE FUNCTION from minimize-distance to MAXIMIZE-INTERESTINGNESS. Plumbing is standard; the optimization TARGET is ours = the innovation.
The real work isn't the algorithm (borrow it) — it's DEFINING "interesting" (a product problem = where we win). Scoring inputs: trail quality/difficulty (technical sections, the good stuff — Thunderforest Outdoors trail data + trail classifications), scenery (overlooks, vistas, terrain variety), loop-ness (good rides loop, not out-and-back), variety (mix trail types, avoid 40mi of the same fire road), hitting the user's dropped waypoints, all within the 45-60mi/5-9hr envelope as the FRAME. Leans on the spatial DB (89K trails, routing graph) + RideCalc (10-15 mph → the constraint that makes it multi-DAY trip planning, not point-to-point). Big nav apps CAN'T easily do this — built around shortest-path, no OHV-trail-quality data, no rider's-day framing. ⚠ constrained-optimization / vehicle-routing-family problem (distance + time + coverage constraints) — real algorithm needed (nearest-neighbor+constraints or a proper solver). Fits the 2.7 MapLibre/spatial-routing direction. NOT 2.6f (compliance only), likely 2.7+ or its own premium-tier feature.
Raw findings recovered from the design docs + past conversations on 08-14, parked here so 2.7 planning starts from what's already been analyzed rather than re-recovering it. Each item tagged DECIDED / OPEN. Sources: SCOPING_v2.7_vector_rendering_2026-07-26.html, memory grouptrack-vector-rendering / grouptrack-map-sources, and conversations "Track map downloading in 2.6c corridor" (07-26), "Release 2.6e route and convoy handling improvements" (08-02).
Rendering engine — the core decision
DECIDED 08-14 MapLibre, rendering satellite imagery, to leverage the spatial DB + improve functionality + tighter integration with existing JS functions. INTEGRATE not rip-and-replace: JS functions kept and integrated more tightly; MapLibre upgrades the rendering surface beneath them; spatial DB drives sat-image rendering.
DECIDED 08-02 ⭐⭐ THE (A)/(B) SPLIT — carry this into planning, every prior version bundled them:
(A) MapLibre as RENDERER, raster/satellite sources UNCHANGED — gets rotation, 3D tilt, Terrain-RGB slope shading, data-driven artifact styling, and the iPad/PC cross-platform multiplier, while satellite stays exactly as it is. (B) VECTOR BASEMAPS — the storage-savings argument. ⭐ (A) does NOT require (B). The 08-14 direction (sat imagery in MapLibre) is essentially (A).
DECIDED Fred 08-02: "If I could rotate sats we would not be having this discussion." → He CAN — MapLibre rotates RASTER tiles, the camera is source-agnostic. Rotation/tilt/pitch all work on plain satellite with no vector tiles. Leaflet cannot rotate at all (a Leaflet limitation, not a raster one).
What (A) buys — judge each on load-bearing vs. pleasant (Fred's framing)
WEIGH Rotation (heading-up) — arguably NAVIGATION, not decoration: a rider following a trail reads a rotated map faster than north-up (every handheld GPS offers it). Judge SEPARATELY from 3D — it was not previously on the list.
WEIGH Terrain-RGB slope shading — for OHV arguably more useful than the imagery itself.
WEIGH Cross-platform reuse — MapLibre GL is both native iOS/macOS SDK and JS lib; map layer is already HTML/JS in a WebView → one renderer all three surfaces (Android/iPad/PC) inherit. Ties to 2.8.
WEIGH 3D tilt / styling polish — closer to genuinely nice-to-have.
The real cost of (A) — known and large
Renderer swap on FROZEN code — the dominant cost is operating on the frozen convoy tangle. ⭐ SEQUENCING ARGUMENT: a convoy rewrite opens that tangle anyway → rewrite the layer ONCE with MapLibre as target, or TWICE. (This is why 2.7 = convoy rewrite is the right home.)
spatial_artifacts.js rewritten from L.polyline to GeoJSON sources + layer specs (MapLibre gives no DOM per feature — queryRenderedFeatures instead).
MapStateStore + self-saving setView extended for BEARING and PITCH.
Tile interception moves from shouldInterceptRequest to MapLibre's addProtocol. ⭐ ties to the 2.6e shared-tile-module work — build that module with this migration in mind.
⚠ Snap is UNAFFECTED — it's Kotlin, renderer-independent, resolves by DB ID.
⚠⚠ 08-02 — "THE WHOLE APP CHANGES, MAP SOURCES ETC HAVE TO BE RE-THOUGHT." A MapLibre move re-opens the whole source model: the catalog is RASTER-SHAPED (url_template {z}/{x}/{y}, cache_dir, max_zoom per source); vector needs a style spec, glyph/sprite URLs, source-layers. And the SLOT concept assumes 4 mutually-exclusive raster basemaps while MapLibre composites raster+vector+terrain simultaneously — slots may not survive as a concept.
If (B) vector is ever pursued — the storage arithmetic + gotchas (parked, not decided)
≈80% tile reduction finding: two of SAT's three stores are LABELS not photography (place + transportation labels delivered as photographs of words). Bar 10: ~107,000 raster → ~21,700 with vector labels. Vector is small because it STOPS at ~z14 and renders deeper by scaling geometry — z15-18 is ~98% of downloads; vector removes those levels rather than shrinking them.
⛔ GLYPH BUNDLING for offline labels — the requirement most likely to be missed if (B) is done.
⚠ The storage argument is the part that FAILS in the woods (tagged-data coverage question) — which is why (A) may be all that's wanted.
Tooling if ever built: Protomaps/PMTiles (single-file, pmtiles extract --bbox), Planetiler / Tilemaker, OpenMapTiles schema. Local artifacts exist: vector_label_prototype.html.

🗣 00-2.8-DISCUSSION — planning substrate for 2.8 (Mac migration, 08-14). NOT a spec — a roadmap to plan from.
Raw findings from the 08-13 "Grouptrack 2.6e playstore release" migration discussion + memory grouptrack-environment-locked / grouptrack-crossplatform / grouptrack-v3. Tagged DECIDED / OPEN / VERIFY. A migration document with a verification checklist was being written in that session — locate/finish it and file in AllDocs.
The move — Mac Air/Pro replaces the PC for ALL development
DECIDED Confirmed "release 2.8 in your numbering." Goals: performance (builds hit 33–53 min under PC disk pressure), storage, and positioning for the Mac/iPad version discussion.
⛔ The irreplaceable item — handle first
The release keystore (grouptrack-release-key.jks). Everything else re-downloads or re-clones; the keystore cannot — lose it and you can never update the Play listing again. HANDLED already in 4 locations under /GroupTrack Application Keys/ (local, Google Drive, iCloud, Desktop) — the two cloud copies reach the Mac immediately. Whatever holds its passwords (keystore.properties/gradle.properties/password manager) travels with it.
Traps specific to this setup
PLAN Line endings. Every commit prints "LF will be replaced by CRLF" — working tree is CRLF, repo stores LF, macOS checks out LF natively. Done carelessly, the first git status on the Mac shows EVERY file modified. Plan .gitattributes/config so it doesn't churn the tree.
PORT Machine-specific tooling — patch scripts hardcode C:\Users\kixaz\...; build output → /d/; commands use MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 (Git Bash only); local.properties points at a Windows SDK path. A rewrite pass, not a copy.
MOVE The generation machinery, not just outputs — the xref generators, AllDocs assembly, the doc history used to gen AllDocs, any Google Drive activity/stores. Not in git, can't be reconstructed. (Inventory these before the move.)
VERIFY Devices need re-authorizing — ADB's RSA key is per-machine, both Droids re-prompt.
What must move
Irreplaceable: keystore + passwords · uncommitted work · unpushed branches/stashes · AllDocs · Downloads/ fallback sets. Credentials: Play Console, AWS RDS, PHP API, Thunderforest key, Crashlytics/Firebase. Reinstallable: JDK, Android SDK, Gradle, platform-tools. SQLite tooling is a non-issue — macOS ships sqlite3 built in (more than the PC had); DB Browser runs native on Apple silicon; workflow (adb pull → inspect locally) is identical minus MSYS_NO_PATHCONV (commands get SIMPLER).
⚠ AWS access from New Hampshire (blocking sub-item)
Console access is NOT IP-restricted (sign in from anywhere). The RDS security group IS — add current IP as an inbound rule (VPC → Security Groups → RDS one). ⚠ Home IP is dynamic (can re-lock). ⛔ EC2 blocked since March on a support case (PRE-01/02/03) — so RDS may be only half of what's needed if the PHP API is unreachable. Tie in with the 2.6e credential rotation.
Cross-platform / iPad — what the move positions for
OBJECTIVE Fred: "two platforms sharing as much of the code base and implementation as possible."
First step (Fred's plan): Apple browser supporting Bluetooth updates → deploy the app in-browser on iPad. ⚠ Web Bluetooth is NOT in Safari — it's Bluefy (a WebKit browser implementing Web Bluetooth). Changes the distribution story (users install a 3rd-party browser first; small vendor).
⭐ What it buys: map layer is already HTML/JS in a WebView → a browser-hosted version reaches iPad with no App Store review, no second signing identity, no Swift. Proves the shared-code thesis cheaply.
⚠ What it CAN'T do: background track recording (a tab can't record with screen off), storage at scale (browser storage capped/evictable — nothing like a 14GB MBTiles file), filesystem access. So it PROVES the architecture split, it's not a shipping product. (Gaia/onX store GBs because they're NATIVE apps — that's the difference.)
⭐ MapLibre is well-suited: exists as both native iOS/macOS SDK and JS — the 2.7 renderer rewrite could run on both without a fork. Doing 2.7 on the Mac = the point the architecture starts being written for two targets.
DECIDE EARLY How far the shared layer extends (SpatialDbManager/tile store/queue are Kotlin → KMP candidate; the service-layer split decides how much survives), and whether 2.7 targets iPad or just develops on Mac (building ON vs building FOR Apple — the second means a 2nd signing identity, store, test device). ⚠ A rewrite carrying a second platform as a constraint is slower — be explicit: Android-only with a portable interior, or genuinely dual-target. Memory: grouptrack-crossplatform (service layer + logic-free panels, Mac-first sequencing).
✅ 00-2.6e-OPEN — FINALIZED 08-14. The definitive 2.6e open-items list (discovery complete; supersedes the scattered pre-2.6 backlog).
Result of the 08-14 discovery pass over the 07-13/07-22 pre-2.6 backlog + accumulated operational items, with Fred's 08-14 scope decisions applied. Killed/closed items recorded at the bottom so nothing is silently dropped. This is the list that gates 2.6e.
⭐ BUILD ORDER (Fred 08-14) — MODULE/COMPONENT WORK FIRST, INSTALL REDESIGN LAST.The feature/module tasks (Task A route display+fit, Task B calc, discard consolidation, tile-intercept module, rename/delete triggers) all fit the methodology below and share momentum + a clear plan — do them while that's true. The install/authority blocker tier (items 7–9) is scheduled LAST: it's a different kind of work — a high-stakes data-safety fix needing its own focused session and verification on a GENUINE fresh install — so it doesn't interleave well with the module cadence. It remains a hard gate on shipping 2.6e; last in build order, not last in priority.
⛔ OVERRIDING RULE — EVERY SEGMENT (Fred 08-14). IDENTIFY DUPLICATE CODE IMPLEMENTATIONS AND FACTOR THEM INTO CALLABLE MODULES WHENEVER THEY ARE DISCOVERED.This is a continuous operating rule, not a per-task technique. During ALL work — any segment, any release — actively watch for the same logic implemented in more than one place, and when found, extract it into ONE callable module and wire the call sites. Duplicate implementations are the root disease behind this project's worst bugs (the discard bug = six divergent teardowns; the two tile intercepts; the scattered distance calcs) — each copy drifts and one silently misses a step. De-duplication is therefore a reflex during every segment, whether or not the task is nominally about consolidation. HOW (the supporting discipline below): shared modules not parallel implementations · build components then string them · stub-first (mark all call sites, build once, grep every stub wired) · consistency-first then consolidate (never extract from divergent copies — make them consistent first, or you propagate a bug to all sites at once).
⭐ STANDING ARCHITECTURE DIRECTION (Fred 08-14) — SHARED MODULES, NOT PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATIONS.The same disease behind the discard bug (scattered duplicated logic, each copy drifting and missing a different step) applies across the app. The cure is the same everywhere: a capability lives in ONE reusable module, called from multiple places — never reimplemented per surface. Applies to: local-tile retrieval (one module, both maps' shouldInterceptRequest call it — item 6), distance + ride-time calc (called functions any surface uses — artifact panels, route planning, trail display — Task B), and going forward any capability that would otherwise be copied per screen/per artifact type. ⚠ When fixing a "missing on surface B" gap, EXTRACT the shared module and wire both — do NOT copy surface A's implementation to B (that creates the second copy that drifts).
⭐ BUILD METHOD — STUB-FIRST (Fred 08-14). For any new shared module: (1) IDENTIFY the module — fix its name/signature/return even before implementing; (2) PLACE PLACEHOLDER STUBS at every call site that needs it, with a grep-able marker (e.g. // STUB:RIDECALC) so every consumer is identified up front; (3) BUILD OUT the module once; (4) VERIFY every stub was converted to the real call — grep -c the marker (= all sites before, = 0 after), no stub left unwired. ⭐ Step 4 makes the stubs a completeness CHECKLIST — you cannot forget a call site because they were all marked first. This is exactly the discipline that would have caught the discard bug (a missing call at one exit would show as an unconverted stub). Pairs with the existing marker-count patch verification.

Data-recovery — the REBUILD function (recovery side of the install story; designed in §00-RECOVERYFILE)
Fred's last known 2.6e item. The recovery/healing side of the data-safety story: an install error means a protected-data reinstall, and this is how you rebuild afterward — unattended, from a recipe, instead of manual reconstruction. Full design already in §00-RECOVERYFILE — do NOT redesign; this is the wiring + display item. ⭐ BUILD ORDER: QUEUED AFTER the install revisions (which are themselves last) — DR follows the install fix.
Rebuild function + Recovery display. A rebuild function that consumes the map-configuration recipe (the .gtmaps file the recipe writer produces — a few-KB JSON of slots + boxes, the same quadtree enqueueRecreateSource computes), linked to a Recovery display that shows: (a) the current 60-day window of restore points (the recipe writer keeps one file/day, deletes >60 days; the date in the filename IS the index), listed by date with tile counts; (b) any recipe available in Downloads (import via the picker/content-URI path — needs no All-Files authority). Select a restore point or recipe → REBUILD (or EMAIL). ⭐ CLEAR-vs-ADD CHOICE (Fred 08-14): the user chooses at rebuild/import time between clear + rebuild (replace — start fresh from the recipe) and add to existing (MERGE — add only the tiles you don't already have to My Maps, existing tiles untouched). ⭐ MERGE IS STRICTLY ADDITIVE — it ONLY adds new tiles (gap-fill, INSERT OR IGNORE-style), never overwrites and never duplicates. So multiple recipes UNION into one consolidated collection ("adds maps to my maps → one consolidated data collection"), running a merge twice is free, and a partial recipe just contributes its subset. ⚠ This clear-vs-add choice is DIFFERENT from — and does not reopen — the "NO per-slot selection at rebuild" rule in §00-RECOVERYFILE (that was about picking which slots, a failure point). Replace-vs-merge is a legitimate top-level user choice; per-slot picking stays out. ⛔⛔ THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE RIGHT: the replay job must be downloadType = DownloadType.AREA (NOT MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH) with priority = REFRESH — because ConvoyDownloadWorker:97 filters refresh-typed jobs to hasTile, so a refresh-typed replay downloads NOTHING and LOOKS successful (silent-failure, only found during a real recovery). Put a comment at that line. ⚠ NO slot selection at rebuild (another failure point — INSERT OR REPLACE fills gaps, running twice is free); no health guards (60-day history kills the partial-snapshot problem — if today's file is mid-rebuild garbage, yesterday's is intact). ⚠ TILES ONLY — tracks/trails/routes/waypoints are captured data needing real backup, not reproducible from this recipe. ⚠ VERIFY ONCE: does a file the app writes to Downloads survive an uninstall? (MediaStore tracks the owning app — DR must not rest on an untested assumption.) (§00-RECOVERYFILE; on the 2.6e list per Fred 08-14)
Data-loss / install blocker tier — designed, NOT built
The must-fix tier. Root cause of both data-loss events (08-01 ~89k trails, 08-08 whole spatial DB). Full design already in this living master — see §00-INSTALL + its 08-09 code-located update, and grouptrack_allfiles_fix_strategy_2026-08-09_v1.html. Referenced by the release index; do NOT re-derive.
Reinstall shows the app as already having all-authority → grant prompt bypassed → app launches and clears/creates the DB BEFORE authority is granted. ⭐ THE BOTTOM LINE: on reinstall, the authority value is not read properly — the app looks like it already has all-files access, so the "grant all authority" screen is skipped, and the program launches and writes over / creates the DB while it does NOT actually have authority. That is the whole data-loss defect: an ordering failure driven by a lying value. ⚠⚠ AND YOU GET NO SIGNAL UNTIL THE DAMAGE IS DONE — the app looks healthy, the checkbox says yes, the prompt is correctly skipped as far as the app can tell, and the first evidence anything was wrong is the DB already overwritten (no error, no failed check, no warning). You cannot detect your way out of it because the thing you'd query (the API) is the thing lying, and you cannot recover after because the overwrite is the one permanent loss. → the fix must be REFUSE-BEFORE-PROCEED (a real read, treat can't-see as refuse), never check-and-warn. MECHANISM: isExternalStorageManager() reads the AppOps record, which says granted while the filesystem refuses; the per-process mount view only updates on a permission TRANSITION, so the broken yes→yes state fires no event and the prompt never shows. TRIGGERS: cleardata-parameter installs, and reinstall-after-delete where the files still exist — the program opens the MBTiles/spatial DB, can't see the old data, and creates a new empty version over it. FIX in build order (per §00-INSTALL): (1) replace the API test with a real read (hasRealStorageAccess() — plain File I/O, treat "can't see" as UNKNOWN and refuse); (2) manufacture the transition (Panel A → settings OFF → verify → Panel B → settings ON → re-read); (2b) gate EVERY SpatialDbManager/MBTilesStore/import/download entry on the read passing, not on settings-return. ⚠⚠ SCOPE CONSTRAINT (Fred): do NOT rest/re-check authority on every update — a normal -r update keeps authority intact and must stay seamless; forcing the grant dance every update is wrong. The dangerous path is specifically the inherited Meshtastic clear-values / reinstall setup that runs on a clear-values reinstall and triggers the all-files conflict. DISCRIMINATOR (per §00-INSTALL): the filesDir marker — wiped by uninstall/clear, survives a normal update. Marker PRESENT = normal update, skip the dance. Marker ABSENT + data present in Documents/ = the clear-values/reinstall-over-data path → run the real-read gate + refuse-to-create + grant transition. So the authority handling fires ONLY where the conflict actually is.
Refuse-to-create floor (00-REFUSE) — stop the app writing a blank over a real DB when it can't see its files. The floor under everything. Highest-value unbuilt item.
Self-uninstall flow (00-INSTALL) — ACTION_DELETE while the app is alive and holds authority; rename Documents/GroupTrack→.bak → uninstall → reinstall → grant-first → real-read → restore. ⚠ First action: verify on Droid 2 that an uninstall leaves Documents/GroupTrack/ intact (whole flow rests on it).

⭐ API CORRECTION (research 08-15) — there is NO separate "new API 36 method." The correct all-files-access API is STILL: declare MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE in manifest → check Environment.isExternalStorageManager() → if not granted, fire Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION with a package: URI (opens THIS app's toggle directly). So the April greyed-toggle was likely NOT "wrong method" but one of: (1) ⭐ INTENT VARIANT — using ACTION_MANAGE_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION (opens a LIST of all apps) instead of ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION (opens OUR app directly), or firing the app-specific one WITHOUT the correct package: URI → system doesn't associate the request with our app → toggle greys; (2) the isExternalStorageManager() verification lie (item 7). ⚠ MUST SEE CURRENT CODE FIRST (Fred's point): grep -rn "isExternalStorageManager\|MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE\|ACTION_MANAGE\|ALL_FILES_ACCESS" app/src/main/java/ → reveals which intent variant, whether the package: URI is passed, how the grant is checked, and where the code lives. Fix is likely: switch to the _APP_ intent variant + correct URI, AND add item-7 real-read verification. Determine BEFORE building.
⭐⭐⭐ CODE FOUND + ARCHITECTURE DECISION (08-15). The all-files logic lives in ConvoyScreen.kt (the frozen convoy composable, 28 backups) and OsmImportStage.kt. Rationale: (1) authority handling has no business inside the frozen map composable — extract it OUT so convoy can ASSUME authority is granted; (2) a pre-launch gate is the natural home for the item-7 proper flow (real-read hasRealStorageAccess(), correct app-specific intent, manufactured grant transition, refuse-to-proceed floor); (3) removes authority code from the frozen file (no more surgery on ConvoyScreen.kt); (4) structurally enforces "authority before any DB/MBTiles/import/download" — the exact ordering requirement. ⭐ THIS ONE SCREEN = the API-36 fix + item-7 redesign + clean separation, all at once. It's the convergence made concrete. Build on a throwaway branch with TARGET_SDK=36, test toggle-works + reinstall-survives.
⭐⭐ BROADER ARCHITECTURE DECISION (Fred 08-15): BOTH the GPS-SOURCE and the ALL-FILES AUTHORITY are bolted-on ADD-ONS embedded in ConvoyScreen.kt, and they BEHAVE like add-ons — fragile, order-dependent, failing illogically (GPS source not following the device-name swap = the radio-GPS bug; authority toggle greying out on A16). They were slapped in where convenient, not where they belong. → Extract BOTH into their own unique processes/screens that run BEFORE and INDEPENDENT of convoy. Convoy should ASSUME both are already established (authority granted, GPS source correctly selected from connection state) and never handle them inline. ⭐ SAME DISEASE as the discard bug / tile intercept / distance calc — foundational logic embedded in the big screen where it drifts and breaks; the OVERRIDING RULE (factor embedded logic into proper modules) applies. The GPS-source fix (derive from connection state, STATUS-IS-DERIVED — see §00-BUG-RADIOGPS) and the authority gate (see above) are BOTH pre-convoy foundational processes. Design them as such: a launch sequence that establishes authority → establishes GPS source → THEN loads convoy, each a clean separate module, none embedded in the map composable.
⭐⭐⭐ THE PRE-CONVOY GATE — architectural decision (Fred 08-15). Build a SYNCHRONOUS, ORDERED, BLOCKING gate that runs before convoy and is THE sanctioned home for anything that must execute before convoy — NO FREE-FOR-ALL. Today's bugs (greyed authority toggle, GPS-reporting flakiness, order-dependent failures) share ONE root: things that should precede convoy got scattered INSIDE convoy, racing each other as async add-ons. The gate makes the rule structural: if it must precede convoy, it goes in the gate — in order, synchronously — or it doesn't run. Two things at once: (1) the GATE MECHANISM — a synchronous ordered blocking pre-convoy sequence; (2) the gate as CONTRACT — the single place pre-convoy requirements live; a new requirement is ADDED to the gate's ordered list, never bolted into convoy. Gate establishes, IN ORDER, each verified before proceeding: (a) ALL-FILES access (real-read verified, correct _APP_ intent + package: URI, refuse-to-proceed floor); (b) BACKGROUND LOCATION "all the time" (ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION — note Android's 2-step rule: foreground location FIRST, then escalate to background, often via settings); (c) [SCOPE TBD] Bluetooth/Nearby-Devices for the radio?; (d) [PLACEHOLDER] anything new. → THEN convoy loads, ASSUMING all gate requirements are met (never re-checks inline). ⭐ This is the durable fix for the whole class of "add-on that behaves like an add-on." Synchronous = no race conditions like today. Build: dedicated pre-convoy Composable/Activity upstream of the convoy entry point; throwaway branch test/launch-authority, TARGET_SDK=36; test each permission + reinstall-survival on Android 16.
⭐⭐ BROADENED (Fred 08-15) — THE GATE IS A FULL STARTUP SEQUENCE, not just permissions. It's the home for ANYTHING that must complete before convoy: (1) AUTHORITY/PERMISSIONS (all-files, background location, bluetooth) — blocking; (2) STARTUP WORK — file conversions, data migrations, integrity checks, DB prep — anything that must finish before convoy touches its data. ⭐ "can live somewhere besides in the app" (Fred): this work doesn't belong inside convoy's process OR silently in Application.onCreate() — it belongs in a dedicated startup STAGE that runs, does its job, shows progress, reports done, and hands off. Convoy stays clean: it assumes permissions granted AND data prepped/converted, never does this inline. ⭐ ENFORCES the existing "NO SILENT PROCESSES" rule — a conversion buried in convoy's load path runs silently, blocks the UI, fails invisibly; a conversion step IN the startup gate shows progress on a visible surface, exactly as required. So the pre-convoy gate = ordered startup sequence: [permissions gates] → [startup work w/ visible progress] → convoy. Each step a clean module; the sequence is the sanctioned, extensible home (the placeholder) for all pre-convoy requirements.
⭐⭐ NEW CAPABILITY (Fred 08-15) — RUN-ONCE-PER-RELEASE CODE. The startup gate finally gives a home for one-time, run-once-per-release work that never had a clean place before (previously hacked into convoy badly, or just couldn't be done safely). Pattern: new release installs → gate checks a version-stamp/flag "has this release's one-time work run?" → if not, RUN IT (back up the DB, copy files, migrate schema, convert a format, fix up data), mark done → if already done, skip → proceed to convoy. Convoy never sees it. ⭐ HIGH-VALUE USES: (a) FILE/DB BACKUPS before a risky release touches data — a release that might modify the spatial DB backs it up FIRST, in the gate, before anything can corrupt it (directly mitigates the data-loss history); (b) ONE-TIME DATA MIGRATIONS for the 2.6f DB work — route-dedup-by-hash rebuild, shared extension-DB restructuring, rename/delete schema changes ALL need a "migrate existing user data to the new structure, once" step, with a backup taken first and visible progress. This is the structural enabler for safely shipping the 2.6f DB-trigger cluster to existing users. The gate = permissions + startup work + run-once-per-release migrations, all before convoy, all visible, none inline.
⛔⛔⛔ THE GATE'S FIRST PRINCIPLE (Fred 08-15) — SAFE HALT, NEVER DESTRUCTIVE PROCEED. The whole reason the gate exists: TODAY, the way the app tests authority to the MBTiles files can STOP the app from proceeding IN A WAY THAT DESTROYS THE DBs. The current check's failure mode is DESTRUCTIVE — when authority is uncertain/absent, the app stumbles forward into create-if-missing / DB-touching code and overwrites good data (the item-7 data-loss). THE GATE INVERTS THIS: authority-uncertain must mean STOP, never "proceed and hope." Rules: (a) authority CONFIRMED REAL (real filesystem read of the MBTiles/spatial DB path succeeds) → proceed; (b) authority uncertain / absent / check errored → HALT IN THE GATE, show grant screen, TOUCH NOTHING — do NOT open the DB, do NOT create-if-missing, do NOT load convoy, do NOT run any migration/conversion/backup. Freeze until authority is real. ⭐ NO PATH exists from the gate forward to any DB/MBTiles/import/download unless authority is PROVEN real by a real read (not the lying isExternalStorageManager). This IS the 00-REFUSE floor made the gate's foundational law. "Uncertain = stop" is the safety inversion that is the entire point of the gate — every other capability (permissions, migrations, conversions) sits BEHIND this halt.
⭐ SCOPE DISCIPLINE (Fred 08-15) — DON'T GET AHEAD OF THE SKIS. The above captures the full vision, but the ACTUAL immediate scope is tight and only two things: (1) GRANT AUTHORITY PROPERLY — the current grant is JUVENILE (a naive method that does NOT survive an accurate test for authority); replace it with a grant that survives a real authority test (real read, not the lying isExternalStorageManager, correct _APP_ intent). (2) A PLACEHOLDER to launch code before convoy on an application upgrade — the pre-convoy spot to run upgrade code. That's it. Migrations, conversions, backups, the full startup sequence = DOWNSTREAM, enabled by the placeholder but NOT to be designed/built now. Build the proper grant + the pre-convoy launch spot first; everything else lives behind it later.

⭐⭐ DESIGN CORRECTION (Fred 08-15) — POINT-OF-USE GUARDS ARE NOT CRUFT. The location prompt at ConvoyScreen.kt ~1299 fires right where a track is RECORDED (inside the recording flow / "hornet's nest") — deliberately placed so authority is verified AT THE MOMENT OF THE WRITE, not assumed from an earlier moment. That's GOOD defensive design = the opposite of the juvenile launch-grant that assumed-and-failed. The whole lesson of the data-loss bug is DON'T HOPE YOU GOT IT RIGHT EARLIER — VERIFY AT POINT OF USE. So the gate and the point-of-use checks are NOT redundant — they're LAYERED DEFENSE: the gate is the front door (establish authority up front so the app doesn't boot destructive); the point-of-use check is the guard at the vault (authority can be revoked mid-session; verify it STILL HOLDS at the consequential action). ⭐ CORRECTION to the removal plan: do NOT blindly neuter/remove point-of-use authority checks "because the gate handles it" — that IS the "hope you got it right" mistake. Instead, point-of-use checks should STAY and ideally be STRENGTHENED to use the real-read test (hasRealStorageAccess / real bg-location check) like the gate does. Only the pure LAUNCH-TIME duplicate (the all-files launch dialog at 145/152, which just re-implements what the gate now does at boot) is safe to neuter. The recording-time guard STAYS.

Implies the FORCE-OFF-THEN-GRANT path may be required on this install: turn all-files OFF first (clear the stale record), THEN ON (real grant). ⚠ BUT FIRST — determine which build Droid 2 is running: if it's the PRE-FIX release (before the write-canary), then the "amateur panel says granted, no toggle" IS the false-positive bug already fixed — the write-canary would catch this (isExternalStorageManager stale-TRUE, but .authority_probe write FAILS → gate returns false → NeedStorage, not Granted). ⭐⭐⭐ REAL DIAGNOSIS (Fred 08-15) — AUTHORITY IS CHANGING WHILE THE APP RUNS. The flash-past (no pause) says authority PRESENT at the moment the gate evaluates; the all-files prompt appearing at the END of install says authority ABSENT — BOTH true at different moments in the SAME run → the authority state is FLIPPING during startup. Not merely stale — TRANSITIONING. Something in startup changes the authority state (or the app races the OS establishing it). This is the exact async/order-dependent/racing failure mode the gate was meant to kill, now seen in the authority state itself moving under us. ⭐ DECISION (Fred): STOP trying to DETECT authority at startup (it's a moving target — any check reads a transient value). INSTEAD: ALWAYS DISPLAY THE SYSTEM GRANT-ALL-FILES SCREEN ON INSTALL, unconditionally. Don't gamble on a check; route the user to the REAL system all-files toggle every fresh install, let them grant/confirm explicitly, THEN proceed. Sidesteps the race entirely: don't trust any startup check, always show the system grant, proceed only after explicit user action. ⚠ IMPLEMENTATION: gate's NeedStorage should fire the system intent unconditionally on install (not gated behind the flaky real-read); "already granted" detection is the unreliable part. Consider: on install, show system all-files grant; only skip if a durable install-stamp says we already completed it (not a live authority check).
⭐⭐⭐ THE FIX REFINEMENT (Fred 08-15) — PAUSE/SETTLE BEFORE DB OPEN. Since authority is CHANGING during startup (two-record split settling asynchronously), the gate must WAIT for authority to SETTLE before the app tries to open the DB — not check-once-and-proceed instantly (the flash-past). The current gate evaluates instantly = races the transition. FIX: after the user grants all-files, don't immediately trust it — POLL the real write-canary (retry over a short window) until it CONSISTENTLY succeeds = authority "settled" = real + stable. Only then proceed to convoy → DB opens against SETTLED authority. This is the true synchronous barrier the gate was meant to be: wait out the authority change rather than reading a transient value mid-transition. Implementation: gate holds on a "verifying/settling" state, polls hasRealStorageAccess() (write-canary) on an interval until N consecutive passes (or a timeout), THEN onProceed. Combined with "always show system grant on install" — show grant, user acts, poll until settled, proceed. The DB open must never happen before the write-canary reliably passes. ⚠ ALSO TEST (answers "why doesn't granting work"): the appops split — appops set --uid ... allow AND appops set ... allow (both records), relaunch, does data read? If yes = toggle was setting only one record; enforcement read the other.
✅ SETTLE-BARRIER IMPLEMENTED (08-15) in ConvoyAuthorityGateScreen.kt — the "Continue" button. Root problem: the resume effect AUTO-PROCEEDED the instant it saw Granted → authority-grant crashed into DB-open (the flash-past). FIX: (1) resume effect now re-evaluates but NEVER auto-proceeds; (2) the Granted state shows a "Continue" button — user must tap to proceed; (3) the tap re-verifies authority is STILL real (hasRealStorageAccess + hasBackgroundLocation) before onProceed, else re-gates. onProceed now fires from ONE place only (the Continue tap). The user's tap IS the settle barrier: gives the grant time to land before convoy/DB opens, makes the grant screen unmissable (fixes flash-past), and structurally separates authority-grant from DB-open with an explicit human action. ⭐⭐ CLEANER DIAGNOSIS (Fred 08-15) — EXISTENCE PASSES, READS FAIL (two separate mechanisms, was conflated). BUT the app FAILS ON AUTHORITY FOR APPLICATION READS → it can SEE the DB exists but can't READ its contents. This is the two-record appops split showing exactly where expected: existence works (weaker/stat access), reads fail (needs the real all-files authority stuck in the split state). ⭐⭐⭐ THE CLEAREST FRAMING (Fred 08-15) — SAME IDENTITY, DIFFERENT AUTHORITY. Android has TWO notions of "who the app is": (1) PACKAGE NAME (com.grouptrack.android) = the IDENTITY the user + app see, stable across reinstalls; (2) UID = the actual SECURITY PRINCIPAL the OS uses for file-I/O enforcement, which CAN CHANGE on reinstall. The bug: the running app IS GroupTrack by every identity measure (same package, icon, name, code) but is a DIFFERENT UID than the one that was granted all-files → it presents as "the app that has authority" but is NOT the same principal that was granted it. The grant is attached to the OLD principal; the running app is a NEW principal wearing the same identity. That's why: isExternalStorageManager()/the toggle can look "granted" (package-level / stale identity-tied record) BUT file I/O FAILS (checks the UID principal, never granted); data is there (existence doesn't care about UID) but unreadable (I/O checks the ungranted UID). ⭐ AUTHORITY ATTACHES TO THE UID (PRINCIPAL), NOT THE PACKAGE (IDENTITY) — and they can diverge. A robust gate cannot trust "am I GroupTrack?" (identity); it must verify "can THIS UID actually do the I/O?" (principal) = EXACTLY what the write-canary does (tests the UID's real I/O capability, not the identity's claimed grant). The fix already built is precisely aimed at this.

⭐⭐ ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (Fred 08-15) — THE GREY IS AN AUTHORITY MISMATCH: "can't grant if you already have." Theory: the toggle greyed because the OS side thought authority was ALREADY present (grant control disabled — granting an already-granted permission is a no-op → greyed), WHILE the app's isExternalStorageManager() check said NOT granted (so it kept prompting). The two disagree = a LINGERING/STALE authority record (AppOps grant survived a prior install, or an inconsistent state) → OS-settings and app-runtime-check out of sync, and NEITHER can resolve it because the toggle is disabled precisely because the OS thinks it's done. This IS the item-7 "lying authority" defect WITH A MECHANISM: not random lying, but a stale/mismatched grant record. ⭐ VALIDATES THE REAL-READ DESIGN: the real read asks the FILESYSTEM "can I actually read?" (ground truth) instead of the OS "do I have authority?" (stale/lying answer) — cutting through the mismatch entirely. ⚠ POSSIBLE ADDED NEED: explicitly handle the mismatch state (OS says granted but real read fails) — may need a clean clear-and-re-request rather than assuming the toggle works. "Fixing a lingering issue" — the stale grant record is the lingering thing.
⭐⭐⭐ OBSERVED / CONFIRMED (Fred 08-15) — THE MISMATCH IS REAL, seen directly. On clear-data: the app's authority was REMOVED (app-side lost real access) BUT the system setting still showed "all files: YES" (OS-side stale record) → so the app NEVER GOT PROMPTED. The app checked isExternalStorageManager() → OS returned the stale "yes" → prompt suppressed → app proceeded AS IF it had authority it didn't actually have → destructive-proceed → orphaned/overwrote the real data. THE ENTIRE BUG IN ONE SENTENCE: clear-data wipes the app's real access but leaves the OS record saying "yes," the app trusts the record (the lie), skips the prompt, and destroys data. ⭐ THIS IS EXACTLY WHY THE REAL-READ GATE IS THE CURE: OS says "yes" (stale) and isExternalStorageManager() returns true (trusts it), but a REAL READ would FAIL (actual access was removed on clear-data). Old code trusts "yes" → no prompt → destroys. New gate ignores "yes," does the real read → read FAILS → mismatch DETECTED → halt + force proper re-grant → real read passes → THEN proceed, data intact. The real read is the ONLY check that reflects actual access vs the stale record — it catches the exact case (stale-yes + no-prompt + gone-access) that the old code is blind to.
⭐ MECHANISM THEORY (Fred 08-15, plausible — exact internals NOT confirmed): the grant RECORD and the actual ACCESS live in DIFFERENT places; clear-data updated one but not the other, because the version that SET the grant predated/was-unaware-of the clear-out behavior. Maps to Android's real model: MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is tracked in AppOps (system special-op record), separate from app data and separate from filesystem enforcement. Clear-data clears app data but the AppOps grant can persist / go inconsistent — especially across the target-SDK churn (36→34→35), since different targets interpret MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE differently, so a grant RECORDED under one target's rules is ENFORCED differently under another → "record says yes, real access gone." ⚠ EXACT term/location ("manifest attached to the object") NOT verified — could be AppOps, a package-manager flag, or MediaProvider state; the precise internals are version-specific and unconfirmed. ⭐ KEY POINT — THE FIX DOESN'T DEPEND ON KNOWING: the real-read test consults NONE of these records; it asks the filesystem "can I actually read?" (ground truth). So the fix is CORRECT whether or not the exact mechanism theory is right — it bypasses the stale record entirely rather than reverse-engineering where it lives. Diagnosis precision matters less than fix robustness here.
⭐ POSSIBLE ADDED REQUIREMENT (Fred 08-15) — FORCE-OFF-THEN-GRANT for the mismatch state. If the mismatch persists (OS record "yes" + real access gone → toggle greyed = "can't grant what you already have"), then granting properly may require first getting authority into a clean OFF state so it CAN be granted. Reset the stale "yes" before re-requesting. ⚠ ENGINEERING REALITY: an app CANNOT revoke its own MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE in code (no self-revoke API) — so the gate can't force-off itself. ⚠ UX CONSTRAINT on force-off (Fred 08-15): since the app can't self-revoke, force-off-then-grant means prompting the user TWICE (off, then on). UNCONTROLLED (raw Android settings twice) = HARD TO EXPLAIN — "revoke then re-grant" reads like a bug, not a fix, especially for backcountry OHV users who aren't power users. The break is in the POSITION-packet path: Meshtastic sends POSITION packets → app must receive → decode → feed position to map as active source → switch map source from Android-GPS to radio-GPS. Break is in one of: (1) the node itself has no GPS fix (no GPS hardware, or no sky view indoors — MOST LIKELY given it was tested indoors for the Play demo); (2) position packets arrive but app isn't parsing/subscribing; (3) packets parse but app never switches the map's location source from Android to radio.

⭐⭐ SHARPER DIAGNOSIS (Fred 08-14): device ID correctly shows the RADIO NAME (not Android name) — so the IDENTITY/device switch DID fire; the app knows a radio is connected. But GPS is still not processed from the radio. So there are TWO switches that should move together on radio-connect: (1) identity/device-name → WORKING, (2) GPS-source → NOT following. They're OUT OF SYNC — identity flipped to radio, but the position pipeline didn't switch from Android-GPS to the radio's position stream. Bug = "GPS source selection didn't follow device identity selection."
Two leads (Fred): (1) ⭐ STRONGEST — recent changes to "recognizing the Android default" GPS may have broken the HANDOFF: when a radio connects, the code that switches AWAY from Android GPS TO radio GPS was likely affected, severing "radio connected → use radio position" while leaving the identity switch intact. Look at what changed in Android-default recognition + whether it touched the source-selection branch. (2) SEED GPS SOURCE AT STARTUP — more robust pattern: DERIVE the GPS source from connection state ("is a radio connected?") rather than relying on an event-driven flag that can fail to fire / drift out of sync with identity. Echoes STATUS-IS-DERIVED: source should be derived from connection state, not a held flag.
⭐⭐⭐ CONFIRMED 08-14 by isolation test: a SECOND Android with NO internal GPS, connected to the radio → RADIO GPS WORKS. So the radio-GPS ingestion path is fully functional; the app CAN receive/process Meshtastic GPS. ⭐ PRECISE BUG (Fred): on connection the app REPLACES THE DEVICE NAME (identity) with the radio but does NOT replace the GPS SOURCE. Two separate actions at connect; only the name one fires. Identity flips to radio, position pipeline stays on Android GPS. Device WITH Android GPS → name shows radio but position stays Android (source never replaced) → looks like "radio GPS not working." Device WITHOUT Android GPS → no Android source to stay on → radio GPS used → works. FIX: at the connection handler, replace the GPS SOURCE at the same point the device NAME is replaced (they must move together) — or better, DERIVE the source from connection state ("radio connected? → radio is the source") so it can't be forgotten (STATUS-IS-DERIVED). Find the connect handler that swaps the name and add/repair the source swap beside it.
⭐ ISOLATION COMPLETE (Fred 08-14): SAME radio used on BOTH devices → rules out ALL radio config/firmware/GPS-settings issues (the node is proven good — Device B receives its position fine). The ONLY variable is the phone, specifically whether it has an internal GPS to compete. ⛔ ALL-FILES-ACCESS (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) — Play review justification. HIGHEST rejection risk.
TRIPWIRE RULES: NEVER write on the form — "performance/faster/slow/speed/mph", "convenience/easier", or "forked Meshtastic/inherited/don't control install" (all read as "you don't really need it" or hit the explicit "performance is not acceptable" rejection). ALWAYS frame as: structural/technical INCOMPATIBILITY of the access model (the alternative CANNOT do it) + user-data protection (maps survive uninstall/data-clear) + "accesses only its own map/trail data."
FIELD 1 (feature, ≤500): "GroupTrack is an offline navigation app for backcountry areas with no cellular service. Users download 50–60 GB of satellite and topographic map tiles into a shared-storage map database for offline use. All files access lets the app read and manage this large user-owned map database in shared storage so it persists across app reinstalls and data-clears, ensuring downloaded maps are not lost when connectivity to re-download them is unavailable."
FIELD 2 (usage checkboxes): Core functionality ONLY.
FIELD 3 (technical reason, ≤500): "The map-rendering engine opens map tiles directly by file path from a shared tile database as the user navigates. MediaStore manages only gallery media (images, audio, video), not a path-addressed tile database, and cannot provide the coordinate-based file access the renderer requires. SAF returns document URIs, not file paths, and cannot provide the direct file-path access the rendering and database layer depends on. The scoped alternatives are structurally incompatible with a path-based tile database."
FIELD 4 (video, https:// unlisted YouTube): airplane mode ON → open map → pan/zoom to z18 showing offline tiles loading from local storage. 20–30s. Caption: "Offline map tiles loading by file path from shared storage — no network."
⭐ THE REAL (internal-only) REASON, NOT for the form: at 30–60 mph the map renders hundreds of thousands of large PNG tiles at z18 by direct file path; MediaStore/SAF cannot serve that access model (this is feasibility, but stated as "performance" it auto-rejects — so the FORM says access-model incompatibility). FORK ORIGIN (also internal-only): the app is a Meshtastic fork; the inherited install/permission process has no provision for shared-storage map data — this is the architectural root of the install-authority defect (item 7). item 7's fix guarantees exactly the "survives reinstall" behavior this Play justification promises Google.
Observability — DECISION 08-14: SURVEY, not telemetry. (telemetry rejected)
The gap: Play Console shows only AGGREGATE install/version data, never per-person ("which of my testers, on what version, active when"). Fred wants that visibility.
⛔ REJECTED — launch telemetry (app phones home {userID, versionCode, timestamp} to RDS). Reason (Fred): it would require TRACKING USERS — dragging in Data-Safety declarations, privacy-policy coverage, deletion-request handling, data security, and Google privacy scrutiny. Too much compliance overhead for a free app just to satisfy curiosity about usage.
✅ CHOSEN — SURVEY the testers directly (a quick form: what version are you on? using it? issues?). Gives the observability with ZERO data-collection burden, zero Google privacy exposure, zero backend work — testers volunteer the info, nobody is silently tracked. Cleaner ethically, legally, operationally. Play's aggregate Statistics (active devices by version) covers the rest once the closed test goes live.
2.7 architecture question (raised 08-14 by the Play review): can we DROP all-files access?
Google steers hard toward scoped storage; all-files is the most-rejected permission and a single point of failure for the whole Play presence. Evaluate in 2.7: can the spatial DB + tile store migrate to a scoped shared directory (SAF tree / app-owned shared location) to eliminate MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE? ⚠ Blocker = the data layer opens tiles/DB by ABSOLUTE FILE PATH (SQLite/MBTiles), and SAF gives document URIs not paths — so this is a data-layer rewrite, not a config change. Middle path: request all-files but FALL BACK to a SAF-scoped folder if denied. Ties to the 2.7 rewrite + the install-authority redesign.

⛔ Two defects found by reading the code, not by guessing
THE ZOOMSLOT CAP HAD NEVER FIRED. corridorTiles computed zTop
from the slot cap and LOGGED it, then passed zMax to both stampPoint
calls. Only stepDeg used the capped value — so topo corridor downloads had been
stamping z17/z18 all along while the log claimed z16. ⚠ That made download and delete agree by
accident; they now disagree deliberately, which is the safe direction.
THE FUNNEL ASKED FOR TILES THAT CANNOT EXIST.

is ninety degrees of longitude, so lon - buffer ran off the west edge.

buffer dominates the track, so every Utah track produced the same impossible URLs. Identical counts
across unrelated tracks was the tell. No coverage was ever missing.
▶▶ 00-DISPLAYRULES — MY CART / MY GROUP / PLANNER. Build-ready spec.
The promise the whole design serves (Fred): "while you're riding you never
lose your spot on the map. The cart and MY GROUP always snap you back to proper zoom for that view,
but your cart never leaves the screen."
Everything follows from that sentence: auto-centering keeps you on the map · auto-zoom
keeps the group framed · the taper guarantees there is imagery at whatever zoom that lands
on. Three rules, one promise.
The three modes
ModeCentreZoomManual pan
MY CARTyour own GPSSTICKY — rider sets it, it staysdisabled
MY GROUPfit to all cartsDERIVED — the fit sets it, snaps backdisabled
PLANNERfreefreeenabled — different job
Both convoy modes: manual pan DISABLED · auto-centre ALWAYS ON · zoom NEVER cancels
auto-centre. ⚠ This reverses the old behaviour, where panning or zooming turned auto-centering
off.
⚠ 08-12 item 0 gates the PLANNER behind a connection until its offline tiles are fixed.
⛔ Problem 1 — jitter
Fitting on every GPS tick flickers the zoom continuously as carts drift back and forth
across a threshold. It needs asymmetric hysteresis:
Zoom OUT immediately when a cart leaves the frame — a safety response, no delay.
Zoom IN lazily, only after the group has stayed inside a tighter inner margin for several
seconds.
⭐ Deliberately asymmetric: losing sight of someone is worse than a slightly-too-wide
view.
⛔ Problem 2 — the stale cart
One rider drives home and the fit drags everyone else's map out to include them. At forty
miles apart the auto-zoom lands near z10 and nobody can see the trail.
⭐ The fit must EXCLUDE carts with no position update in N minutes — and SAY SO.
"2 carts not reporting" on the panel, rather than silently dropping them from the frame.
⭐ How the taper ties in
Whatever zoom the fit lands on, tiles exist. That is precisely what H=4 across z9-z18
guarantees — and it is why H must cover the worst-case screen rather than a typical one.
The fit chooses the zoom; the taper makes sure the choice is always covered.
⭐ Full design, math and device verification: living master 00-STARTHERE item 3.

3 — TAPER THE CORRIDOR, then refresh all corridors as the test
⭐⭐ THE REQUIREMENT IS GROUP TRACKING, NOT "LOOKING AHEAD." Fred:
"when you are tracking the whole group in GroupTrack the first to the last cart may be 3 miles
apart. The app auto-zooms to keep the group in frame but the tiles disappear. That is the behaviour

Group spreadAuto-zoom lands onView widthScreen white today
1 milez161.3 mi22%

3 milesz145.1 mi80%
5 milesz1310.2 mi90%
⭐ That table is why z16 is the last good level. A tight group sits at z16, where the
half-mile band still fills the screen. The moment the group strings out, the app&rsquo;s own
auto-fit walks off the edge of the coverage.
⭐⭐ AND THE ANSWER IS THE SAME AT EVERY ZOOM: H &asymp; 2.1 TILES. That is not
tuning — it falls out of the arithmetic. Filling the screen needs half a screen-width either side,
and a screen is always ~4.2 tiles. So the formula is self-calibrating.
buffer(z) = H &times; tileWidth(z)
tiles(z)  = (trackLength / tileWidth(z) + 1) &times; (2H + 1)
⭐⭐⭐ AND THE TAPER MUST CONTINUE UPWARD PAST z16 TOO — THIS INVERTS THE
COST. Fred: "less time at z17 and z18 because the view is tighter — worth doing, not always a
minimum of half a mile without regard to zoom."
Applying the same rule at z17/z18 makes the whole thing CHEAPER than today:
RuleTotalvs today (10,791)
H=2 at every zoom5,560&minus;48%
H=3 at every zoom7,784&minus;28%
H=4 at every zoom10,008&minus;7%
H=3 with a 0.25 mi floor8,096&minus;25%
⭐ The saving is nearly all z18: 7,807 &rarr; 3,868 tiles, because 0.23 miles
either side is ALREADY three tiles of map at that zoom. Every level below z16 added together costs
546. The z18 saving pays for the entire taper five times over.
⭐ Fred: "drops size of tiles sent AND increases coverage to full panels at each zoom."
A filled screen at every level from z9 to z18, and a 28% smaller download.
⚠ USE THE 0.25 mi FLOOR — at z18 H=3 is only 0.23 mi either side, which is tight if a
recorded track wanders or GPS was loose. The floor costs almost nothing and keeps it at &minus;25%.
⚠ corridorTiles already loops per zoom with bufferDeg as a parameter,
so this changes WHAT THE BUFFER IS, not the structure. ⚠ Existing stores keep their shape — only new
downloads taper, which is why refreshing all corridors is the test.
⚠ Size the taper per track from getTrackBbox, not from a constant — the
figures above assume a 25&times;25 mile ride; a 60-mile-wide one is roughly 5&times; at z14.

🔴 ISSUE 2 — THE HORIZON. Not a bug; a design gap with a 4% fix.
At z16 the screen fills. At z15 and z14 the corners go white.
⚠ EACH ZOOM IS AN INDEPENDENT TILE SET. Having z18 gives you nothing at z13 —
they are separate downloads of the same ground at different resolutions, and the corridor fetches
all of them, but only for the band. "Less detail" does not mean "less data": it means MORE GROUND
PER TILE, so a wider view, so more of it outside your coverage.
THE FIX FRED ARRIVED AT — a horizon measured in TILES, not miles:
buffer(z) = H &times; tileWidth(z)
tiles(z)  = (trackLength / tileWidth(z) + 1) &times; (2H + 1)
H = 2  ->  always two tiles of map beyond the track, at every zoom

⭐ Why it is nearly free: the count is dominated by
trackLength / tileWidth, which grows 4&times; per level; the buffer is only a constant
multiplier (2H+1). So widening the horizon multiplies the CHEAP levels and leaves z18
untouched. z9 at seventy-eight miles of buffer costs TEN TILES because one z9 tile is 156 km
wide.
⚠ corridorTiles already loops per zoom with bufferDeg as a parameter —
the buffer just becomes a function of z. ⚠ Existing stores keep their shape; only new downloads get
the horizon, so Bar 10 would need re-downloading to fill in (444 tiles, seconds).
⛔ THE OOM — and the last link in root cause 1 was mine
The first Recreate job killed the app: 512 MB, OutOfMemory.
⛔ I recorded "the worker was never the problem" because it filters to
hasTile. It does — but only AFTER calculateTiles materialises the WHOLE
RECTANGLE. A Recreate box holds at most 50,000 STORED tiles but can span degrees: at z18 a
three-degree box is roughly 4.8 million TileKey objects allocated before one is filtered.
⭐ Fixed e128cfc65 — MBTilesStore.tilesInBounds() asks the store
what it holds. Bounded by what is stored rather than by the size of the box, and faster: one indexed
range scan per level instead of millions of allocations plus a per-tile existence check.
Fred&rsquo;s original sentence, finally built: stream real tiles in existence by zoom for x
lon and lat.
⚠ The old code even LOGGED the ratio — "N in bounds, M exist on disk". The waste was
visible all along and only mattered once a box got big enough to exhaust the heap.
