Import Artifacts1 screenImport Artifacts (from Gaia / onX GPX)
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › Import Artifacts
Import Artifacts migrates your historical data from Gaia, onX, or similar apps into GroupTrack. The workflow:
First (outside GroupTrack): in your current app, export/download the artifacts you want as GPX files, and move them into your device’s Downloads directory.
Run Import Artifacts — GroupTrack scans Downloads and lists the GPX/KML files it finds.
Check the file(s) you want (or Select All), then tap Select files to import.
The import runs, bringing those artifacts into GroupTrack. On completion the GPX files are removed from Downloads.
The screen header shows how many files were found; each entry lists its name, size, date, and format. A RESYNC TRACKS button is also here — the same one referenced in the upgrade notes for bringing recorded tracks back after an update.

Reconnect Check
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review › Proceed to Update
After you proceed, the config is written and the radio reboots. This screen runs a 60-second countdown while the update is applied and the radio reconnects — the radio reboots, Bluetooth auto-disconnects, then auto-reconnects (shown in the log: “waiting for binary install reboot,” “auto BT disconnect,” “auto BT reconnect”). Let it run; Cancel stops the wait if needed.
When the countdown finishes, an update-apply recap is shown summarizing what was applied. Check the recap: if any settings did not apply correctly, simply reapply the update (return to Apply Master Config and proceed again).
Verify Config (apply recap)
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › … › Reconnect Check › Verify
After the reconnect, the app reads the radio back and compares every field against what it tried to write — only errors are shown. The header reports the result, e.g. “5 of 40 fields failed.” A group summary at the bottom shows pass/fail per category (Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module).
In this example all five failures are in the Position group (Position 1/6) — the table lists each failed field with its Expected vs Actual value (e.g. Broadcast Interval expected 5, actual 0).
If any fields failed, reapply the update — go back to Apply Master Config and proceed again. Radios sometimes need a second pass for a group (often Position) to take. Re-verify until the recap shows all fields passed.
Restore Radio3 screensArchive Restore
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride
A key GroupTrack safety feature: before it writes any configuration to a radio, it first saves that radio’s current config to a timestamped archive. Nothing you apply is ever destructive — the prior state is always recoverable. This screen lists the saved archives for the connected radio so you can restore any of them at any time.
The header shows the radio node and how many archives were found. Each entry is a saved config with its date and time and filename — note the pre_master suffix here, which is the config that was auto-saved just before the master config was applied. The size (e.g. 391b) is shown at right.
Tap an archive to restore it to the radio. Restore writes the saved config back and runs the same reconnect + verify sequence as Apply, so the radio reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified.
Restore — confirm (gated)
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › select archive
Selecting an archive highlights it (blue, with a check) and reveals a confirmation gate before anything is written. The warning makes the consequences explicit:
⚠ Restore will overwrite current radio config — the selected archive replaces whatever is on the radio now.
Selected: the archive’s date/time, so you confirm you picked the right one.
Radio will reboot after restore.
Tap ↻ Restore This Archive to proceed. The radio then reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified — the same reconnect + verify sequence shown for Apply (above).
Restore — write &amp; reconnect
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › Restore This Archive
After you confirm, Restore writes the archived config to the radio and runs the same write · reconnect · verify process documented under Apply (the 60-second Reconnect Check, then the Verify recap). When the recap shows all fields passed, the radio is back on the chosen prior configuration.

// Focus: opening one sibling section at the same level collapses the others.
function wireSiblings(container, selector){
  var items=container.querySelectorAll(selector);
  items.forEach(function(it){
    it.addEventListener('toggle',function(){
      if(it.open){ items.forEach(function(o){ if(o!==it && o.parentNode===it.parentNode) o.open=false; }); }
    });
  });
}
document.querySelectorAll('details.map').forEach(function(mp){
  wireSiblings(mp.querySelector(':scope > .mapbody'), ':scope > details.lp');
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.lp').forEach(function(lp){
  var b=lp.querySelector(':scope > .lpbody'); if(b){ wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.sf'); wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.screen'); }
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.sf').forEach(function(sf){
  var b=sf.querySelector(':scope > .sfbody'); if(b){ wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.screen'); }
});
// Filter: match against data-search across all levels; reveal & open the path to hits.
var Q=document.getElementById('q');
function flt(){
  var t=Q.value.trim().toLowerCase();
  // reset
  if(t===''){
    document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(function(d){
      d.classList.remove('nohit');
      d.open = d.classList.contains('map');   // only maps open at rest
    });
    return;
  }
  // hide everything first
  document.querySelectorAll('details.lp, details.sf, details.screen').forEach(function(d){ d.classList.add('nohit'); d.open=false; });
  // any details whose own text matches => show it and its ancestors+descendants
  document.querySelectorAll('details.screen, details.sf, details.lp').forEach(function(d){
    var hay=((d.getAttribute('data-search')||'')+' '+d.textContent).toLowerCase();
    if(hay.indexOf(t)>=0){
      d.classList.remove('nohit');
      // open & reveal ancestors
      var p=d.parentNode;
      while(p && p!==document){
        if(p.tagName && p.tagName.toLowerCase()==='details'){ p.classList.remove('nohit'); p.open=true; }
        p=p.parentNode;
      }
      d.open=true;
    }
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('details.map').forEach(function(mp){ mp.open=true; });
}

GroupTrack V2.5 — User Manual
Screen-by-screen cookbook · Off-road convoy tracking &amp; trail navigation · grouptrack.org
How this manual works. This is a cookbook, not a reference list — it follows what you actually do. Each screen lists where it’s reached from, what you do there, and what it leads to. Chapters 4–6 cover the V2.5 heart of the app (maps, trails, tracks, routes, downloads, radio). Chapters 1–3 describe account, dashboard, and ride-management screens that are being rebuilt for Release 3.0 — they’re included for orientation and marked accordingly. Screenshots are added per screen in a following revision (live device capture).
Contents
1. Getting In — Account &amp; Enrollment
2. Home Base — Dashboard
3. Planning &amp; Managing Rides
4. Maps, Trails &amp; Tracks (the heart of V2.5)
5. Offline Maps &amp; Downloads
6. Radio Setup (Organizer)

4. Maps, Trails &amp; Tracks (the heart of V2.5)
The two maps and everything that feeds them. This is where V2.5’s big changes live — the Work with Artifacts panel, trail import, and the map source catalog.
Work with Artifacts — the V2.5 centerpiece.V2.5 replaces the simple Display Panel with the Work with Artifacts panel — a single interface to toggle, select, edit, and import all four artifact types. On the Planning Map it has full editing and import functions; on the Convoy Map the same panel is display-only (editing and import are not available during live convoy operations).
Convoy (Live Map)
Reached from: Dashboard / active ride
The live ride view — your group’s vehicles in real time. Work with Artifacts panel (accordion) controls display of Trails/Tracks/Waypoints/Routes. Header: tile source, QUEUES, zoom readout (N · Z##).
Leads to: Map Viewer · Track Export · Track Import · Settings
[ screenshot to be added ]
Map Viewer (Planning Map)
Reached from: Convoy map / Dashboard → Explore
Plan a ride: search, download tiles, and manage artifacts. Work with Artifacts here has full import + edit. IMPORT TRAILS → Trail Sources. QUEUES for downloads.
Leads to: Trail Sources (IMPORT TRAILS) · Track Import · Track Export
Work with Artifacts — the V2.5 centerpiece:
[ screenshot to be added ]
Artifact types
TrailsToggle ON to display trail overlays from the spatial database, loaded dynamically for your current viewport. Trails appear as solid cyan lines (weight 4); color varies by CartoCode classification — blue (#00AAFF) OHV/road-concurrent, orange (#FF8800) hiking &amp; biking, yellow (#FFCC00) hiking-only, purple (#AA44FF) biking-only, cyan (#00FFFF) default. Trails display at zoom 8+; zoom in to see them.
TracksToggle ON to display your recorded GPS tracks from the spatial database, loaded by viewport like trails. Tracks appear as neon green (#39FF14) dashed lines (weight 3). Tapping a track shows its name (from the GPX filename).
WaypointsToggle to display user-created waypoints. 10+ standard types: trailhead, fuel, gate, hazard, scenic viewpoint, water source, camp, parking, junction, rally, and others. Drop one by long-pressing the map on empty ground (not on a vehicle marker) — a type picker opens.
RoutesToggle to display saved routes from the spatial database, the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Build a route with “+ ROUTE” (see “Creating a Route”). Routes display as magenta lines. (Importing routes from GPX, and the Draw/Suggest methods, are coming in upcoming updates.)
SELECT / Edit and the three-state controlSELECT/Edit opens the artifact list for a type, scoped to the current view: a checkbox per item, Select All / Deselect All, and per-item actions. Each type also has a three-state display control — ON (show all in view), OFF (hide), and SELECTED (show only the items you checked). Each map remembers its own display selections independently: what you pick on the Convoy map no longer carries over to the Planning map.
Creating a Route (early access)
Open the map (Convoy or Planning) and open Work with Artifacts, then tap “+ ROUTE”. The Route+ toolbar appears.
Tap “New”. A “Name this route” box appears with a suggested name — accept it or type your own — then tap “Start”.
Tap “Add” (it turns green), then tap the map to drop each point. Each point snaps to the nearest trail or track if one is close by, so your route follows established paths; tap away from any trail to place a free point exactly where you tapped. A magenta line connects your points in order.
Use “Undo” to remove the most recent point. Pan and zoom freely between taps to reposition the map.
Tap “Save” to store the route. It is saved on your device, redraws on the map in magenta, and appears in Work with Artifacts → Routes under the name you gave it. Tap “Discard” to leave without saving.
To move the Route+ toolbar around the map, the panel must be expanded (accordion open). Drag the grip handle in the header to reposition; when collapsed, tapping the header expands it rather than moving it.
Routes display in magenta. Saved routes load from the spatial database the same viewport-aware way as trails and tracks. Saving a half-finished route to resume later (“In Progress”), editing a saved route’s geometry, and the Draw and Suggest methods are coming in upcoming updates.
Import Artifacts &amp; RESYNC TRACKS
Open Work with Artifacts and choose Import; pick your GPX file (the picker opens your device storage). Large files are processed one track at a time, so even big exports import without crashing.
When it finishes, a recap shows “X new / Y already in library.” New tracks draw on the map immediately. (If the artifact list looks empty, leave the screen and return — known refresh gap; the data is saved.)
Duplicates are identified by shape (geometry), not name: re-importing the same file is safe and shows “0 new / N already in library.”
RESYNC TRACKS recovers device track files that aren’t in the database (e.g. after an update): it scans my_tracks/ and adds any track not already saved. Run it again to confirm — a second run should add 0.
Tracks only, this build: importing a GPX brings in its tracks; waypoints and routes inside the file are skipped for now (separate import coming). The list caps at 200 shown — larger libraries are paged in a later build.
Trail &amp; track displayWhen you open the Planning Map, GroupTrack scans your my_tracks/ directory and syncs any new GPX files into the spatial database in the background (it doesn’t block the map). Files already in the database are skipped. As you pan and zoom, the track query updates automatically (400 ms debounce) so only visible tracks load — instant response even with large libraries.The current release includes trail data for southern Utah and northern Arizona (the St. George to Grand Canyon corridor). Additional regional datasets will be downloadable in future updates through the Trail Source Manager. Trails load by viewport using bounding-box indexing; below zoom 8 they are hidden for readability.
Trail Sources
Reached from: Map Viewer → Work with Artifacts → IMPORT TRAILS
Browse trail sources and import. Select UGRC Utah Trails → Validate/Confirm → ~49,000 trails + 591 trailheads download. Close &amp; reopen the app, then zoom in to see them.
Leads to: Back to Map Viewer with trails imported

function filterDoc(q){
  q=q.trim().toLowerCase();
  var blocks=document.querySelectorAll('main .screen, main .box, main h1, main h2, main .coming, main .intro, main .toc, main .row');
  if(!q){blocks.forEach(b=>b.classList.remove('hidden'));return;}
  blocks.forEach(function(b){
    if(b.classList.contains('toc')){b.classList.add('hidden');return;}
    b.classList.toggle('hidden', b.textContent.toLowerCase().indexOf(q)===-1);
  });
}

function flt(){
 var t=document.getElementById('q').value.toLowerCase().trim();
 // show/hide flows
 document.querySelectorAll('.flow').forEach(function(f){
   var hit=!t||f.getAttribute('data-fn').indexOf(t)>=0||f.textContent.toLowerCase().indexOf(t)>=0;
   f.classList.toggle('hidden',!hit);
 });
 // hide section h1/h2 with no visible flow under them
 var blocks=Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('main h1, main h2, main .flow, main .intro'));
 // simple pass: hide an h2 if the next flows until next header are all hidden
 document.querySelectorAll('main h2').forEach(function(h){
   var n=h.nextElementSibling, anyVis=false;
   while(n && n.tagName!=='H1' && n.tagName!=='H2'){
     if(n.classList.contains('flow') && !n.classList.contains('hidden')) anyVis=true;
     n=n.nextElementSibling;
   }
   h.classList.toggle('hidden', t && !anyVis);
 });
}

GroupTrack V2.5 User Manual
Drill-down edition · device screenshots · 2026-06-23
Organized the way you navigate the app. Open a map to see its launch points; open a launch point to see its options; drill into an option to reach a single screen. Opening one branch collapses the others, so you always see just where you are.
Convoy MapEvery lettered control on the Convoy map toolbar. Open a launch point below to drill into it.
A — GroupTrack → Radio SetupGroupTrack menu
Convoy Map › GroupTrack icon (Meshtastic left sidebar)
Tap the GroupTrack icon in the Meshtastic left-hand sidebar (the last icon) to open the GroupTrack menu — a slide-up panel. This is the entry to radio setup, the prerequisite for using GroupTrack with your Meshtastic radios.
The menu has two sections:
Event / Ride — the ride and radio options (expand to see them). covered below
Map Settings — an older submenu of map instructions, now built into the map panel itself. no longer used
Tap Event / Ride to expand it (next screen).
Setup Radio5 screensEvent / Ride menu
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride
Expanding Event / Ride reveals five options. In V2.5 only the two radio functions are used — ride creation and sharing are moving to the Release 3.0 cloud app.
Create a Ride coming in 3.0
Transfer Event/Ride Details via Email — “select a ride and send via email attachment” coming in 3.0
Import Ride from Downloads — “scan Downloads for .convoy files and import” coming in 3.0
Apply Ride Info to Radio — “apply master config or ride to connected radio.” used — see below
Restore Prior Config Post Ride — “select and restore from saved archive.” used — see below
Tap Apply Ride Info to Radio to begin applying config to a connected radio (next screen).
Apply Radio Config
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio
This screen applies a configuration to the connected radio so it reports each cart’s location to the Convoy map. The bar at the top shows the connection state — here ● CONNECTED, with the radio model (tracker-t1000-e) and firmware version. A radio must be connected before a config can be applied.
Apply Master Config — applies your saved master template to the connected radio. This is the function used in V2.5 to set a radio up for a ride. used
Apply Ride — applies a specific ride’s config. coming in 3.0
Review Changes → — shows what will change on the radio before you commit.
Tap Apply Master Config, then Review Changes to proceed (next screen).
Review — Changes to be Applied
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review
The review panel shows exactly what will be written to the radio before you commit. At the top, Long Name lets you set a name for the radio (here “Mike McKinney”) — edit it if you want this radio to carry a specific rider/cart name. Below, the New Channel (here Convoy, AES-256 encrypted) is the channel the radio will join.
The change table (Field · Current · New Value · Rule) is grouped into accordions you can expand to inspect each setting and see where its value is derived from:
LoRa — radio/region + modem settings
Channel — channel name, key, encryption
Device — device role and behavior
Position — GPS / position reporting
Display — on-radio display settings
Modules — module settings (telemetry, etc.)
Scrolling to the bottom of the panel shows the full accordion list and the action bar:
The action bar has two buttons: Cancel (red) backs out without changing the radio, and Proceed to Update (green) writes the config. Tap Proceed to Update to apply (next screen).
Reconnect Check
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review › Proceed to Update
After you proceed, the config is written and the radio reboots. This screen runs a 60-second countdown while the update is applied and the radio reconnects — the radio reboots, Bluetooth auto-disconnects, then auto-reconnects (shown in the log: “waiting for binary install reboot,” “auto BT disconnect,” “auto BT reconnect”). Let it run; Cancel stops the wait if needed.
When the countdown finishes, an update-apply recap is shown summarizing what was applied. Check the recap: if any settings did not apply correctly, simply reapply the update (return to Apply Master Config and proceed again).
Verify Config (apply recap)
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › … › Reconnect Check › Verify
After the reconnect, the app reads the radio back and compares every field against what it tried to write — only errors are shown. The header reports the result, e.g. “5 of 40 fields failed.” A group summary at the bottom shows pass/fail per category (Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module).
In this example all five failures are in the Position group (Position 1/6) — the table lists each failed field with its Expected vs Actual value (e.g. Broadcast Interval expected 5, actual 0).
If any fields failed, reapply the update — go back to Apply Master Config and proceed again. Radios sometimes need a second pass for a group (often Position) to take. Re-verify until the recap shows all fields passed.
Restore Radio3 screensArchive Restore
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride
A key GroupTrack safety feature: before it writes any configuration to a radio, it first saves that radio’s current config to a timestamped archive. Nothing you apply is ever destructive — the prior state is always recoverable. This screen lists the saved archives for the connected radio so you can restore any of them at any time.
The header shows the radio node and how many archives were found. Each entry is a saved config with its date and time and filename — note the pre_master suffix here, which is the config that was auto-saved just before the master config was applied. The size (e.g. 391b) is shown at right.
Tap an archive to restore it to the radio. Restore writes the saved config back and runs the same reconnect + verify sequence as Apply, so the radio reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified.
Restore — confirm (gated)
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › select archive
Selecting an archive highlights it (blue, with a check) and reveals a confirmation gate before anything is written. The warning makes the consequences explicit:
⚠ Restore will overwrite current radio config — the selected archive replaces whatever is on the radio now.
Selected: the archive’s date/time, so you confirm you picked the right one.
Radio will reboot after restore.
Tap ↻ Restore This Archive to proceed. The radio then reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified — the same reconnect + verify sequence shown for Apply (above).
Restore — write &amp; reconnect
Convoy Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride › Restore This Archive
After you confirm, Restore writes the archived config to the radio and runs the same write · reconnect · verify process documented under Apply (the 60-second Reconnect Check, then the Verify recap). When the recap shows all fields passed, the radio is back on the chosen prior configuration.
✓ This completes Convoy launch point A — GroupTrack / Radio Setup.
B — REC (record ride track)Recording in progress
Convoy Map › REC
The REC button starts track recording for the ride. It works two ways depending on your setup: with no radios it records a track for just this cart (this device’s GPS path); with radio-equipped carts it activates group tracking for the whole convoy. Either way it creates and saves a track for the ride.
Tap REC and recording begins immediately — no prompt. The button changes to ❚❚ PAUSE, and a live Distance readout appears at the bottom-right and counts up as you move.
Tap Pause to interrupt recording (next screen).
Pause3 screensPaused — End or continue
Convoy Map › REC › Pause
When you pause, recording holds and an End button appears below the Pause button. From here you choose:
Pause (top) — hold here; the button changes to Resume so you can continue when ready (see below).
End (below) — finish the recording and save the track.
Tap End to finish — you’ll be prompted to name the track (Save Track, below). Or, to continue the ride, the button shows Resume.
Resume
Convoy Map › REC › Pause › (continue)
If you don’t end, the recording stays paused and the button shows ▶ RESUME. Tap it to continue recording the same track from where you left off — the Distance readout picks back up. This lets you pause during stops and resume without starting a new track.
Save Track (name prompt)
Convoy Map › REC › Pause › End
Tapping End stops recording and opens the Save Track prompt. Type a Track name and tap Save to store the recorded track under that name. Skip discards the track (it is not saved). After saving, the REC button returns to its idle state.
The saved track becomes an artifact you can view, select, and export later from Work with Artifacts and from search.
C — Zoom (+/−)Zoom
Convoy Map › Zoom (+/−)
The + and − buttons at the top-left zoom the map in and out. You can also pinch-to-zoom directly on the map. The current zoom level is shown in the header readout (e.g. N · Z13).
D — PLAN (launch Planning Map)PLAN
Convoy Map › PLAN
The PLAN button switches from the Convoy (live) map to the Planning Map, where you search, download tiles, build routes, and manage artifacts. See Planning Map for everything you can do there. Use BACK on the Planning map to return to the Convoy map.
E — GROUP (whole group + group HUD)GROUP display + HUD
Convoy Map › GROUP
GROUP shows the entire ride group on the map and displays the group heads-up display (HUD) at the bottom-left. It’s one of the bottom-bar view modes (GROUP · MY CART · SELECT CART · HIDE).
The group HUD reports the whole convoy at a glance:
Span — the distance from the lead cart to the tail cart (how spread out the group is).
Carts — total carts in the group.
Active — carts currently reporting.
Lost — carts not heard from within the set time window. (The active threshold and the “lost” minutes are both set in setup.)
△ Lead / ▽ Tail — the front and rear carts, with distance.
CH% — mesh channel utilization. Radios broadcast position every 5 seconds; if CH% turns red the channel is too busy — slow the broadcast frequency (slide the broadcast interval up) to reduce congestion.
F — MY CART (my cart + my HUD)MY CART display + HUD
Convoy Map › MY CART
MY CART centers the map on your own cart (the starred marker, labeled with your cart name) and shows your cart’s heads-up display — your telemetry plus where you sit within the convoy.
The my-cart HUD shows:
Cart name — your cart’s name (e.g. “Fred &amp; June”).
Heading — your direction of travel.
Battery — your device/radio battery level.
Altitude — your elevation.
Speed — your current speed.
To Lead / To Tail — your distance to the lead cart and to the tail cart.
Gap Ahead / Gap Behind — the gap to the cart immediately ahead of and behind you.
G — SELECT CART (detail on selected cart)SELECT CART
Convoy Map › SELECT CART
SELECT CART opens a list of the carts in the group at the top of the screen. Tap the cart you want to view — the map centers on that cart and its heads-up display appears at the bottom-left. The cart currently being viewed is marked CURRENT in the list.
The selected-cart HUD shows the same details as MY CART, but for the chosen cart: Heading, Battery, Altitude, Speed, To Lead / To Tail, and Gap Ahead / Gap Behind. This lets you check any cart in the convoy, not just your own.
(pick a cart)1 screenSelected cart — detail &amp; actions
Convoy Map › SELECT CART › (pick a cart)
With a cart selected, its detail panel shows its live status and two action buttons. The detail fields include Status (Active), Spd (speed), Bat (battery), Pos # (its position/order in the convoy), Hdg (heading), Alt (altitude), and Seen (time since its last report).
Set as Lead — designate this cart as the lead cart for the ride.
Remove from Ride — remove this cart from the group. Use this when a cart is no longer part of the ride (breakdown, left early, etc.). Removing a cart stops “lost” messages for it and keeps the group span and stats accurate to the active riders only — so the GROUP view’s span no longer stretches out to a cart that has dropped off.
H — HIDE (clear the HUD)HIDE
Convoy Map › HIDE
HIDE clears the heads-up display from the map for a clean, unobstructed view. The cart markers stay on the map and the Distance readout remains, but the detailed HUD block is removed. Tap any of the other modes (GROUP, MY CART, or SELECT CART) to bring the HUD back.
I — Settings gear (Convoy Settings)Convoy Settings (panel 1)
Convoy Map › Settings gear
The gear opens Convoy Settings — a list of options that control the app’s behavior. This is where the thresholds referenced elsewhere in the manual are set.
Map Sources → Change Map Sources — assign tile sources to the SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ slots. (This is the one setting that opens its own screen — see below.)
Alert Thresholds → Signal Drop — minutes before the radio-disconnect warning fires (e.g. 2 min).
Signal Lost — minutes without a packet before a node is considered lost (e.g. 10 min). This is the “lost” window reflected in the group HUD’s Lost count.
Off Track — miles from the convoy track before the off-route alert fires (e.g. 0.5 mi).
Node Filter — admission settings for which nodes join the group (continues on panel 2).
(scroll down)1 screenConvoy Settings (panel 2)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › (scroll down)
Scrolling down reveals the rest of Convoy Settings:
Node Filter → Admission Window — a node must have been heard within this window today to appear on the map (e.g. 1 hr).
Track Display → Multicolor Track — when on, the track is colored by node position.
Track Recording → Lead Cart Only — record the lead cart’s track only.
Track Recording Format — KML / GPX — the saved track format (GPX works with Garmin, Strava, AllTrails).
Removed Carts — lists carts you removed from the ride today (via SELECT CART → Remove from Ride); shows “No carts removed today” when none.
The app version and build are shown at the bottom of this screen.
Change Map Sources3 screensMap Sources (drill-down)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources
This is the one Convoy Settings option that opens its own screen. Map Sources assigns a tile source to each of the three fixed map slots used by the SAT / TOPO / TOPO+ buttons on the map toolbar.
SAT — the satellite slot (e.g. Esri Imagery + Roads + Labels).
TOPO — the topo slot (e.g. Esri World Topo).
TOPO+ — the detailed-topo slot (e.g. Esri USA Topo Maps).
Each slot has a Change button to pick a different source.
API Keys — some sources (e.g. Thunderforest Outdoors) require an API key; tap to enter the key to unlock them.
Tap Change on a slot to pick a new source (next screen).
Change source (picker)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources › Change
Tapping Change opens a list of available tile sources, grouped by category. Tap a source to assign it to that slot; the currently-assigned source is checked.
Hybrid — imagery with roads/labels (Google Hybrid, Esri Imagery + Roads + Labels, USGS Imagery + Topo).
Satellite — plain imagery (Google Satellite, Esri World Imagery).
Topographic — topo maps (Esri USA Topo, Esri World Topo, OpenTopoMap, USGS Topo).
Street — road maps (Google Roads, OpenStreetMap, CartoDB Voyager).
Terrain — terrain maps (Google Terrain, and more).
Select a source and you return to the Map Sources screen with the slot updated (next screen).
Refresh Tiles (after a source change)
Convoy Map › Settings gear › Change Map Sources › Change › (select source)
After you assign a new source to a slot, the app offers to refresh the cached map tiles from the new source. It reports how many existing tiles it found and explains that the refresh downloads them at low priority, with progress visible in Work with Queues, and that it restarts automatically if interrupted.
Refresh Now — start re-downloading the tiles from the new source right away (low priority).
Later — keep the new source assignment but don’t refresh the cached tiles now.
✓ This completes Convoy launch point I — Settings (Convoy Settings → Map Sources → Change → Refresh).
J / K / L — SAT, TOPO, TOPO+ (map source buttons)SAT · TOPO · TOPO+
Convoy Map › SAT / TOPO / TOPO+
These three toolbar buttons switch the displayed map source immediately. Each shows the source assigned to that slot in Convoy Settings → Map Sources (e.g. SAT = Esri Imagery, TOPO = Esri World Topo, TOPO+ = Esri USA Topo).
They work in either NET or LOCAL mode (see the NET/Local toggle). In local mode they display from tiles downloaded in advance — so you can switch sources and ride with no connection, as long as those map tiles were downloaded ahead of time.
M — NET / Local (network vs downloaded tiles)NET / Local toggle
Convoy Map › NET / Local
This toggle switches between NET (network) and Local map modes:
NET — fetches map tiles live over the network (online).
Local — displays only from maps you have downloaded prior to your ride. If you haven’t downloaded the area in advance, local mode will have no maps to show — so download your ride area ahead of time to use it offline.
N — QUEUES (download queues)Download Queues
Convoy Map › QUEUES
Queues opens the Download Queues panel, which manages map-tile downloads. The header shows the current state (e.g. “2 active, 1 queued”), and entries are grouped by status:
Active — downloads in progress, each showing tiles downloaded and percent, with an X to cancel that entry.
Queued — downloads waiting to start (numbered #1, #2…), each with a timestamp and an X to remove it.
Completed — finished downloads, each listing the source (SAT / TOPO / TOPO+) and tile count.
Global controls: Hold pauses the queue, Cancel All stops everything, and Clear Done removes completed entries from the list. Close dismisses the panel.
O — Search (universal search)Universal Search
Convoy Map › Search
The magnifying glass opens Universal Search — one search across five modes, shown as tabs: Area · Track · Route · Trail · Waypoint. Pick a tab, type in the field (the prompt changes per mode), and press Enter. There are two kinds of search:
Area — a place search. Type a place name (a town or a feature such as a park, e.g. “Bryce”) and the map repositions there. For common names, include the state to disambiguate — e.g. “Kanab, UT” — so it lands on the right place.
Track / Route / Trail / Waypoint — artifact searches. These search your saved and imported artifacts by name. The search presents a list of matching hits; select one and its artifact detail panel opens. From the detail panel, use FIT to center the map on it.
Example — Area search for “Panguitch, UT”: the map repositions to Panguitch and the trails and tracks for that area draw immediately.
Example — artifact search: searching a name returns a list of matching hits (here two results for “Panguitch”), each with its name and ID.
Selecting a hit opens that artifact’s detail panel:
The detail panel shows the artifact’s name and type, an Aliases field, and a Details section — including the Carto Type band, its ID and bounding box, and an expandable technical section. Down the left is the action column: Rename, Delete, Share, Export, and FIT. Tap FIT to center and frame the map on that one artifact. Close dismisses the panel.
For a track, the Details section also shows the track’s recorded metrics laid out in two columns — Distance, Max Spd, Elev, and Points — alongside its Source, Track Id, Bbox, and Filename. The action column adds a green SAVE MAPS button that downloads the map tiles covering that track’s area, so the track can be used with offline maps — the map for that track’s area is available even with no signal. (Maps can also be pulled at import time via the per-file MAPS checkbox; see Import Artifacts.)
After FIT the panel closes and the map zooms to frame that artifact — here the selected track centered and fit to the view:
In short: Area moves the map to a place; the artifact modes find a saved item by name and open its details (then FIT centers the map on it).
P — Work with ArtifactsWork with Artifacts panel
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts (hamburger)
The hamburger opens the Work with Artifacts panel, which controls the four artifact types — Tracks, Trails, Waypoints, Routes — on the map. Important: all of these controls operate on the bounding box of the current display — i.e. the artifacts within the area you’re currently viewing, not the whole database.
Each type row has three buttons (the highlighted one is the current state):
OFF — hide that artifact type on the map.
ALL — show all artifacts of that type within the current view.
SEL/EDIT — opens a list of that type’s artifacts in the current view for per-artifact control: Select All, Deselect All, or check a custom combination to choose exactly which are shown. (OFF and ALL are in-panel toggles; only SEL/EDIT opens a screen.)
A + Route button at the top starts building a new route.
SEL/EDIT1 screenSEL/EDIT list (per-artifact)
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › SEL/EDIT
Tapping SEL/EDIT on a type opens its list — here Trails (23), all the trails in the current view. Each has a checkbox, with Select All and Deselect All at the top, so you can show every one, hide every one, or pick a custom mix.
You can also tap an artifact’s name in this list to open its detail info panel (the same panel shown under Search — name, type, Carto Type, IDs, with Rename / Delete / Share / Export / FIT). Tap FIT there to center that one artifact on screen.
+ Route4 screens+ Route — start a route
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route
Before you start: zoom into the area where you want to build the route. It helps to display Trails and Tracks (turn them on in Work with Artifacts) as a visual guide — the snap-to function works over both tracks and trails, so your route follows a known track or trail wherever one is available, keeping it on established paths.
Tapping + Route opens the Start a route dialog:
New Route — create and name a new route to build.
In Progress — resume an unfinished route you started earlier.
The only difference is whether you create a new named route or select an existing in-progress one. Choose New Route to begin building (next screen).
Building the route
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › New Route
The Route panel opens for building. Tap the map to place points — the route draws as a pink line, and each new point adds length and snaps to a nearby trail/track when one is available, keeping the route on known paths.
The panel controls:
Method — Point (live; tap to place points). Draw and Suggest are marked “soon.”
Build (n pts) — shows how many points the route has so far.
Add ON — toggles point-adding on/off as you tap.
Undo — removes the last point.
Save — saves the finished route.
Discard — abandons the route without saving.
Keep tapping to extend the route; each point snaps to the underlying track/trail.
Extending &amp; saving the route
Convoy Map › Work with Artifacts › + Route › (building)
As you keep tapping, the route grows and the Build point count climbs (here 26 points). The pink route traces the chosen path, snapped to the underlying tracks/trails.

F — Search (universal search)Universal Search
Planning Map › Search
The magnifying glass opens Universal Search — one search across five modes, shown as tabs: Area · Track · Route · Trail · Waypoint. Pick a tab, type in the field (the prompt changes per mode), and press Enter. There are two kinds of search:
Area — a place search. Type a place name (a town or a feature such as a park, e.g. “Bryce”) and the map repositions there. For common names, include the state to disambiguate — e.g. “Kanab, UT” — so it lands on the right place.
Track / Route / Trail / Waypoint — artifact searches. These search your saved and imported artifacts by name. The search presents a list of matching hits; select one and its artifact detail panel opens. From the detail panel, use FIT to center the map on it.
Example — Area search for “Panguitch, UT”: the map repositions to Panguitch and the trails and tracks for that area draw immediately.
Example — artifact search: searching a name returns a list of matching hits (here two results for “Panguitch”), each with its name and ID.

Down the left is the action column: Rename, Delete, Share, Export, and FIT. Tap FIT to center and frame the map on that one artifact. Close dismisses the panel.
For a track, the Details section also shows the track’s recorded metrics laid out in two columns — Distance, Max Spd, Elev, and Points — alongside its Source, Track Id, Bbox, and Filename. The action column adds a green SAVE MAPS button that downloads the map tiles covering that track’s area, so the track can be used with offline maps — the map for that track’s area is available even with no signal. (Maps can also be pulled at import time via the per-file MAPS checkbox; see Import Artifacts.)

Import Trails1 screenImport Trails → Select Source
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › Import Trails
Import Trails opens a Select Source list of approved external trail sources. Each entry shows its type, scope, and trail count (e.g. UGRC Utah Trails, Arizona State Parks &amp; Trails, Colorado COTREX, BLM, USFS, USGS National Trails, NPS Public Trails). Import Artifacts1 screenImport Artifacts (from Gaia / onX GPX)
Planning Map › Work with Artifacts › Import Artifacts
Import Artifacts migrates your historical data from Gaia, onX, or similar apps into GroupTrack. The workflow:
First (outside GroupTrack): in your current app, export/download the artifacts you want as GPX files, and move them into your device’s Downloads directory.
Run Import Artifacts — GroupTrack scans Downloads and lists the GPX/KML files it finds.
Check the file(s) you want (or Select All), then tap Select files to import.
The import runs, bringing those artifacts into GroupTrack. On completion the GPX files are removed from Downloads.
The screen is titled Import Tracks from Downloads and shows how many GPX/KML files were found. Each file has two checkboxes under the IMPORT and MAPS column headers, followed by the FILE (its name, size, date, and format).
Download maps as you import (optional). Tick a file’s MAPS checkbox to also download the map tiles covering that imported track’s area, so the track can be used with offline maps. It is off by default, and it is per file — a single track’s area can be tens of thousands of tiles, so turn it on only for the files you want map coverage for. (You can always add coverage later from a track’s detail panel with SAVE MAPS.)
When you run the import, it finishes with an Import Complete summary that reports how many items fell into each bucket: new, aliased, duplicate, and skipped. From there, KEEP FILES &amp; CLOSE leaves the source GPX files in Downloads; DELETE FILES &amp; CLOSE removes them.
A RESYNC TRACKS button is also here — the same one referenced in the upgrade notes for bringing recorded tracks back after an update. Resync has its own panel, the SYNC TRACKS panel, separate from import. Tapping RESYNC TRACKS opens it with a START / CLOSE choice; tap START to begin.
The panel then shows the total tracks to be synced and a live, rolling feed of each track as it is processed, with a running… indicator until it finishes. Each line reports what happened to that track — for example IGNORE no-geometry for a file with no usable track points, or DUPE … already known, source removed for a track already in your library. Nothing happens silently — every file is accounted for on screen.
When the feed finishes, the panel shows a final summary. It leads with any &#9888; FAILED tracks called out for follow-up (each listed by name and reason — e.g. file missing), then the tallies: processed, renamed, and properties written (shown as a ratio, e.g. 80/81). A full detail section lists every track with its distance and point count. Buttons are CLOSE and RE-RUN — use RE-RUN if failures need another pass after you resolve them.

Reconnect Check
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › Apply Master Config › Review › Proceed to Update
After you proceed, the config is written and the radio reboots. This screen runs a 60-second countdown while the update is applied and the radio reconnects — the radio reboots, Bluetooth auto-disconnects, then auto-reconnects (shown in the log: “waiting for binary install reboot,” “auto BT disconnect,” “auto BT reconnect”). Verify Config (apply recap)
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Apply Ride Info to Radio › … › Reconnect Check › Verify
After the reconnect, the app reads the radio back and compares every field against what it tried to write — only errors are shown. The header reports the result, e.g. “5 of 40 fields failed.” A group summary at the bottom shows pass/fail per category (Device, LoRa, Channel, Position, Display, Module).
In this example all five failures are in the Position group (Position 1/6) — the table lists each failed field with its Expected vs Actual value (e.g. Broadcast Interval expected 5, actual 0).
If any fields failed, reapply the update — go back to Apply Master Config and proceed again. Radios sometimes need a second pass for a group (often Position) to take. Re-verify until the recap shows all fields passed.
Restore Radio3 screensArchive Restore
Planning Map › GroupTrack › Event / Ride › Restore Prior Config Post Ride
A key GroupTrack safety feature: before it writes any configuration to a radio, it first saves that radio’s current config to a timestamped archive. Nothing you apply is ever destructive — the prior state is always recoverable. This screen lists the saved archives for the connected radio so you can restore any of them at any time.
The header shows the radio node and how many archives were found. Each entry is a saved config with its date and time and filename — note the pre_master suffix here, which is the config that was auto-saved just before the master config was applied. The size (e.g. 391b) is shown at right.
Tap an archive to restore it to the radio. Restore writes the saved config back and runs the same reconnect + verify sequence as Apply, so the radio reboots, reconnects, and the result is verified.

// Focus: opening one sibling section at the same level collapses the others.
function wireSiblings(container, selector){
  var items=container.querySelectorAll(selector);
  items.forEach(function(it){
    it.addEventListener('toggle',function(){
      if(it.open){ items.forEach(function(o){ if(o!==it && o.parentNode===it.parentNode) o.open=false; }); }
    });
  });
}
document.querySelectorAll('details.map').forEach(function(mp){
  wireSiblings(mp.querySelector(':scope > .mapbody'), ':scope > details.lp');
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.lp').forEach(function(lp){
  var b=lp.querySelector(':scope > .lpbody'); if(b){ wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.sf'); wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.screen'); }
});
document.querySelectorAll('details.sf').forEach(function(sf){
  var b=sf.querySelector(':scope > .sfbody'); if(b){ wireSiblings(b, ':scope > details.screen'); }
});
// Filter: match against data-search across all levels; reveal & open the path to hits.
var Q=document.getElementById('q');
function flt(){
  var t=Q.value.trim().toLowerCase();
  // reset
  if(t===''){
    document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(function(d){
      d.classList.remove('nohit');
      d.open = d.classList.contains('map');   // only maps open at rest
    });
    return;
  }
  // hide everything first
  document.querySelectorAll('details.lp, details.sf, details.screen').forEach(function(d){ d.classList.add('nohit'); d.open=false; });
  // any details whose own text matches => show it and its ancestors+descendants
  document.querySelectorAll('details.screen, details.sf, details.lp').forEach(function(d){
    var hay=((d.getAttribute('data-search')||'')+' '+d.textContent).toLowerCase();
    if(hay.indexOf(t)>=0){
      d.classList.remove('nohit');
      // open & reveal ancestors
      var p=d.parentNode;
      while(p && p!==document){
        if(p.tagName && p.tagName.toLowerCase()==='details'){ p.classList.remove('nohit'); p.open=true; }
        p=p.parentNode;
      }
      d.open=true;
    }
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('details.map').forEach(function(mp){ mp.open=true; });
}

2026-08-06 · INTERNAL · exactly what patch_source_scaffold_2026-08-06d.py will produce
Strings copied verbatim from the patch. Numbers shown are Droid 2's real values.
The three phases
    PHASE 1 — after the source is picked
      Map Source Changed
        SAT is now using the new source.
        142880 stored tiles came from the previous source.
        Stored tiles cannot be converted. The next step explains your options and
          what each one costs.
      NEXT STEP
    Non-dismissible. Back-button and
      outside-tap do nothing — NEXT STEP is the only way on.
    PHASE 2 — the migration panel
      Source Map Migration - SAT
        Google Hybrid carries roads and place names inside the satellite imagery, so
          it needs one map store instead of three and shows street names even with no signal.
        Your stored Esri tiles cannot be converted as they are. Road labels, place
          names and feature names will no longer show on them.
        The separate name files those come from are removed either way, whichever
          option you choose.
        DELETE AND START OVER - smallest and fastest
        Clear these maps and rebuild around your tracks. Downloading along your tracks
          uses about two thirds less storage than boxed areas - you get the ground you actually
          ride and little else, and every future track brings its own maps. Frees 3 store(s),
          about 5507 MB.
        This cannot be undone. There is no backup. Your download history for this slot
          is cleared too, so note any areas you want to redraw.
        MOVE EVERYTHING TO THE NEW SOURCE - automatic
        We convert your existing maps to Google Hybrid in the background, so road and
          place names come back across all of your coverage as quickly as possible - track maps
          first, then your areas underneath. Your maps stay usable the whole time.
        All of the downloads are submitted at once and run as background tasks. Every
          image is slowly replaced from the new source until your whole map has moved over.
        I'LL MOVE TRACKS AND AREAS ON MY SCHEDULE
        Nothing is downloaded or removed. Your existing maps stay exactly as they are,
          so you always have something to fall back on. Refresh ground as you need it from the
          downloads panel - by track, or by drawing an area, with Replace tiles ticked. Downloading
          by track is the lighter option.
        Not the best choice if you depend on road and place names - ground you have
          not refreshed stays without them.
        DELETE AND START OVER
        MOVE EVERYTHING AUTOMATICALLY
        MOVE ON MY SCHEDULE
    ▲ the body scrolls — it does not fit on one screen ▼
    PHASE 3 — the outcome
      Done
        Cleared 3 store(s), about 5507 MB freed. Draw areas or import tracks when
          ready.
      OK
    Dismissible — the work is done and
      OK does the same thing. OK also resets the panel state so the next source change starts at
      phase 1.
⚠ What the render exposes
⛔ 1 — Phase 2 is far too long for an AlertDialog
Roughly 320 words in a Material3 dialog body. It will render as a tall scrolling block on
a phone, with the three buttons below the fold on first view — so a user sees a wall of text and
no visible actions.
⭐ This is the strongest argument yet for making it a full screen rather than a dialog.
The content is a decision page, not a confirmation.
⚠ Short of that: cut each option to one sentence and move the detail behind the button, or drop
the two "not the best choice / removed either way" lines, which are qualifiers rather than
information.
⛔ 2 — Three stacked buttons in confirmButton will look wrong
Material3 expects one or two actions laid out horizontally. Three TextButtons in a
Column render right-aligned and stacked, which reads as an accidental layout
rather than a choice list.
⭐ The options are already described in the body, so the buttons are repeating text the user just
read. Making them selectable rows in the body with a single CONTINUE action would fix both
this and the length problem.
⚠ 3 — The greyed middle option is the informative one
You said nobody should make a delete decision without knowing the other options. As rendered,
the user can only pick delete everything or do nothing — the option that makes the
delete decision informed is the one they cannot choose.
⭐ It reads better once delete-by-track exists and all three are live. That is one function,
copied from enqueueDelete.
⚠ 4 — Smaller things
"142880" has no thousands separator — it is interpolated raw.
"3 store(s)" — the (s) construction appears twice.
"about 5507 MB" — 5.5 GB would read better at this size.
The option headings are plain body text, same weight as everything else, so they do not
stand out as headings on device.
⭐ What is right
Title is now honest — Source Map Migration, matching ConvoySourceMigration
and maps/source_changes/.
The advisory leads — label loss is stated before any option is presented.
"Removed either way" heads off the obvious follow-up.
Each option names its action, and each has a distinct reason to be chosen.
Phase 1 is non-dismissible, phase 3 is — the decision cannot be escaped, the receipt
can.

Option 2 — Automated Tile Data Refresh
2026-08-07 &middot; INTERNAL &middot; process flow from option select to queue release
Base commit 733164e12 &middot; stage 1 committed and inert &middot; stages 2–5 NOT BUILT
Companion to grouptrack_living_master_2026-08-06_v4.html §00-MIGRATION
1 &middot; What option 2 is
From the Source Map Migration panel, three options. This document covers option 2 only.
#OptionProtectsBehaviour
1Delete and start overnothing
Clear the column, rebuild around tracks, draw new areas. Already built —
ConvoySourceClear.kt, commit 27dfb433d, proven on Droid 2.
2Move everything (automatic)the AREA
Delete track tiles, refresh the area, re-import tracks. All submitted at once;
every image slowly replaced from the new source. This document.
3Move on my scheduleeverything
Nothing touched. Convert manually, ground by ground, with Replace tiles ticked.
Already built — existing download paths.
⭐ The governing constraint (Fred): these screens process ALL or delete ALL. No partial
conversion. That single rule removed the detection logic, the decision matrices and the pickers.
Why the delete is not a loss
Track corridors are deleted and requeued in the same operation. The store ends with the same
coverage shape it started with, sourced from the new provider. Corridors outrank area work in the
queue, so the re-imports drain before the slow area rebuild even starts.
⚠ The slot IS the store. Column 1 writes to SAT regardless of which source is assigned —
which is why Replace tiles exists: old tiles keep rendering until new ones overwrite them in the
same store. A source change therefore needs a deliberate migration, not just a repointed URL.
2 &middot; The flow
0 · User selects option 2 on the migration panel and confirms.
BUILT Panel rewritten 08-06 (54a62e4f6): three selectable rows,
CONTINUE disabled until one is chosen.
1 · holdQueue() — ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:637. Sets
queuePaused = true. Nothing new dispatches.
EXISTS
2 · cancelAll() — :647. Cancels the WorkManager job for every entry in
DOWNLOADING state, then keeps COMPLETE entries and removes the rest:
_queue.value = completed  // keep completed for history, remove rest
✅ Confirmed: download history survives the migration. Only pending and in-flight work is discarded.
EXISTS
⏸ GATE A — after hold, before anything is read
Queue is now empty and quiet. This is the only point where the store is guaranteed still.
Counting before the hold would give a number already stale by the time it is read.
3 · previewAllTracks(context, slotName) —
ConvoyCorridorDelete.kt. Counts only, deletes nothing.
BUILT 08-07 commits 0a40ec07e + 733164e12
allTrackGeomHashes()        every track with geom_hash, plus name
  per track:
    getTrackPoints(ctx, geomHash)      SpatialDbManager:1980
    corridorTiles(segments)            ConvoyTileCalculator:94
  distinct via HashSet&lt;TileKey&gt;        TileKey is a data class -> value equality
  countTiles(store, distinct)          MBTilesStore, exact on-disk count
⏸ GATE B — the destructive confirm. PERMANENT.
Checkbox launches a full-text confirm. PROCEED / CANCEL.
Shows: tracks with geometry &middot; tiles on disk, per store &middot; geometry total &middot;
tracks skipped for no geometry &middot; tracks skipped for empty corridor.
CANCEL must call resumeQueue() — backing out should not leave the queue held.
4 · Delete track corridor tiles — deleteTiles(type, tiles),
MBTilesStore.kt:265. Runs inline, not through the queue.
NOT BUILT

NOT BUILT
⏸ GATE C — after delete, before rebuild
Deleted count vs GATE B's on-disk prediction. These should match. A mismatch is the signal to stop.
6 · Requeue track corridors — enqueueCorridorBatch :503 /
enqueueCorridor :543. Existing path, all tracks.
WIRING ONLY

After step 4 the only tiles left are the ones area downloads created, so the remainder is the

Queue populated, nothing running. Last look before anything drains.

calls startNextIfAvailable(). Drain begins.
EXISTS
3 &middot; Why the sequence holds
The order is structural, not enforced by priority
Deletes never enter the queue. They run inline while the queue is held, so they cannot race
anything — you cannot lose a race you are not in.
⭐ This is what removes the atomic patch. No new DownloadType, no priority
mapping, no dispatch branch — so the exhaustive when at
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:797 never fires, and there is no window where the tree will not build.
The earlier 1b/1c plan required exactly that window.
Drain order after release — already correct, no change needed
DownloadPriority        (ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:36-41)
  DELETE    = 0
  PROMOTED  = 1
  CORRIDOR  = 2     <-- track re-imports drain first
  AREA      = 3
  REFRESH   = 4
Corridors outrank area work, so track coverage returns before the slow area rebuild starts. Area
imagery is never absent because the refresh replaces in place.
⚠ The concurrency seam
MAX_CONCURRENT = 2 (:139). Priority governs which job is picked next; it does
not stop a running job continuing alongside a higher-priority one. With hundreds queued in order, both
slots stay inside the same phase almost the whole time — the exception is the boundary, where the
last corridor and the first area job can occupy the two slots together.
⭐ Fred's assessment: acceptable — they are different tracks, so the two jobs at a seam do not
touch the same tiles. Recorded so that if a track later shows holes after a migration, this is the first
place to look rather than a fact to re-derive.
Considered and not needed: dropping concurrency to 1 while deletes are pending. The
inline-delete design makes it moot — nothing is queued to race.

5 &middot; The panel rows
Both destructive rows already exist in ConvoyDownloadPanel.kt as greyed V2.7
placeholders. Neither is a new row — both are activations, and the code comment beside them already
describes this work:
ArtifactCheckRow("Remove Tiles by Track", dimText, false, false, "V2.7") {}
ArtifactCheckRow("Clear Tile Source",     dimText, false, false, "V2.7") {}
&ldquo;by-track needs corridor-shaped deletion (the same derivation enqueueCorridor
already does), and Clear Tile Source drops the whole SAT column (base + both label stores) and is
destructive enough to need its own confirm.&rdquo;
RowWires toState
Remove Tiles by Trackthis document, stages 4–8being built
Clear Tile Sourceoption 1's clear — ConvoySourceClear.kt
code exists, proven on device
⚠ The interaction mismatch
Every row in this section is a checkbox that arms an area operation — tick "Remove Tiles by
Area", then tap Draw Area, and the delete runs against the drawn bbox. Draw Area's
enabled tests tilesChecked || trailsChecked || removeTilesChecked || osmChecked.
Corridor delete takes no area and no selection. It is all tracks, immediately. So it does not
fit the tick-then-draw idiom.
⭐ Settled: checkbox launches a full-text confirm. Precedent exists in this very section —
"Download Tiles by Corridor" routes from its own checkbox (onSelectCorridorTracks()), and
the comment states "Routing lives in the checkbox." The tick reverts on dismiss: this is an
action, not a state.
⚠ Clear Tile Source needs its warning carried with it
Inside the migration flow the user has chosen an option and been told they lose labels until tiles
are replaced. Exposed as a bare panel row, it is the same destructive operation with none of that
framing — a one-tap way to drop 5+ GB. The confirm must carry the warning, not just ask PROCEED.
6 &middot; The two numbers at GATE B
FigureMeans
totalTilesDistinct corridor tiles by geometry. An upper bound.
onDiskTotalTiles actually present in the store(s). What the delete
will remove, and what GATE C verifies against.
overlapSavingsNaive per-track sum minus distinct — tiles shared by two or
more corridors.
onDiskTotal &le; totalTiles always. The gap is corridor crossing ground that was never
downloaded.
⛔ Why this distinction exists — DELETE-BANDING-2026-07-25,
MBTilesStore.kt:345-349: a geometry count produced &ldquo;1,500,000 tiles&rdquo; for an area
holding a fraction of that, leaving a progress denominator the job could never reach. A finished job
looked permanently stuck. Showing the geometry number at a confirm would reproduce that as a
verification failure.
⭐ countTiles deliberately mirrors deleteTiles line for line — same
groupBy { z to x }, same 500-bind chunking, same WHERE shape. A pre-count selecting on
different criteria than the delete would read as authoritative while disagreeing with what happens.
7 &middot; Open questions
Does enqueueRefresh freeze the bbox onto each entry, or does the worker re-derive
it? The &ldquo;execution order does not matter&rdquo; property rests on this. It is a reading of the
code, not confirmed in the worker.
Completion rows before or after the delete? Before means a row survives an app death but
claims a completion that has not happened. After means the row is truthful but a crash leaves no trace.
Leaning: after, carrying the actual removed count.
countTiles performance on a large store. A COUNT per (z,x) group across a full
corridor set on Droid 2's 5.3 GB SAT.mbtiles is the one thing in this design that cannot be
predicted. First run answers it.
Threading. Preview is a DB read plus tile computation per track plus a COUNT per store —
background thread only. ⛔ Anything touching the WebView or a Toast from that thread must post back
via Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()). Three convoy rendering failures in this arc were
instrumentation aborting a method before its real work.
Track name on corridor queue rows. Write the name at enqueue; re-resolve at completion and
refresh it if the hash still resolves, otherwise leave what is there. Never overwrite a real name
with nothing — a completed row is the record that it happened, and a deleted track must not erase it.
8 &middot; What this design removed
DroppedWhy
ConvoyCorridorDeleteWorker.kt (step 1b)
Deletes run inline. corridorTiles is a standalone calculator, not worker-bound.
Queue wiring 1c — enum, priority, dispatch, enqueue
Nothing is queued, so nothing needs a type. Removes the build-breaking atomic window entirely.
Concurrency gating to 1 during deletesMoot once deletes leave the queue.
Track picker for the deleteAll tracks, always. No selection UI.
⭐ Final shape: one function, two callers, four existing calls in the right order —
against a plan that was a new worker file plus an atomic four-part queue patch.

GroupTrack — Session Recap2026-07-23 · INTERNAL · git purge + pushed · corridor design settled
Headline
The repo is unblocked and pushed — six large .db blobs purged from history, .git ~1GB → 82MB, and ~130 commits finally off the laptop and onto GitHub. Then the 62,000-tile mystery closed: segmentation was never broken — every split was mathematically correct. The real finding is that a bbox is the wrong model for a line feature, measured concretely: one ~100-mile figure-7 track was 22% of an entire 10-track import, its bounding rectangle ~95% empty desert. That produced a settled design for corridor downloads and a two-phase build plan.
What happened
Git purge. Backed up with git bundle after cp -r failed twice — critically, cp -r silently didn't copy .git, which would have been a worthless backup. Found SIX large blobs where memory said three; the sixth only surfaced after the first purge pass. Cleared a stale refs/original/ from a prior abandoned rewrite, purged, verified nothing above 40MB remained, re-added the remote filter-repo strips, force-pushed, and added a *.db guard.
62K investigation closed. Captured a logcat trace of the tester's import. The pre-existing SEGMENT logs carried the answer: 72 segments per source × 3 sources = 216 ≈ the 215 queued, every split obeying the 50K ceiling. Four of my theories died on inspection — the bypass had zero callers, satLayers self-initialises, the old 12-mile calc isn't reachable, and the tracks aren't oversized. The model was wrong, not the math.
Corridor design settled. Track-based and route-based downloads use a corridor; user-drawn areas keep the bbox. Two self-contained functions sharing one isolated prompt. Option B for the entry — store a geometry reference, let the worker re-derive tiles — after Fred ruled out run-boxes on the 5-10s-per-bbox startup cost.
Queue work scoped as Phase 1. DownloadType field, real ordering (there is none today), filter-scoped deletes with confirmation, and the scrolling fix — built and certified before corridor.
A live incident. Replace-map-source spawned 3287 continental-US entries that resurrected after Cancel All, and we confirmed there is no recovery path on a release build — Android 13+ blocks all third-party access to Android/data.
Decisions locked
Track/route → corridor; drawn area → bbox.
Two self-contained functions, shared isolated prompt, no branching — the caller knows which it is, so each passes its own onProceed.
Option B — entry stores geometry reference + type; worker re-derives. Run-boxes rejected on startup cost; tile-list-in-entry rejected on JSON size.
A real downloadType field, not a label prefix — "we cannot bastardize the name for expediency."
The filter scopes deletes, with scope+count labels and a gated confirmation.
Queue first, certified, then corridor.
git bundle is the backup method, never cp -r.
Lessons
Isolate with data, not theory. Four of my hypotheses died on inspection in one day. The trace settled in minutes what argument couldn't.
Fred's pushback was right repeatedly — that "no other Kotlin usage" didn't rule out JS callers; that the numbers didn't add up; that run-boxes would be unusable at 5-10s each. When the person who runs the app says it doesn't match, re-derive.
Verify generated code produces VALUES, not just that it parses. My logging patch balanced its braces perfectly and printed literal $sizeTiles.
A backup that doesn't verify isn't a backup — cp -r reported errors but still looked like it had run.

GroupTrack — Session Recap2026-07-24 · INTERNAL · queue rebuild + corridor shipped · 2.6d assets in · three defects found on device
Headline
The corridor works, and the number is not close. Tester track bar 10 — the ~100-mile figure-7 that started this whole line of investigation — went from over 1,000,000 bbox tiles to about 107,000 across three sources. A ≈90% reduction, built, queued and downloaded end to end on the planning map. On the strength of that measurement the area button was removed from the artifact panel and track import was cut over, so corridor is now the only path a track takes. Two complete tasks shipped today — the download-queue rebuild that had to come first, and the corridor feature itself.
What happened
Phase 0 + 0b — the queue rebuild. Six patches, one working build: job type and priority as real persisted fields, the first actual ordering the queue has ever had, filter chips that scope destructive actions, gated confirms carrying scope and count, per-row promote, and a real ETA. Scroll took six approaches, five wrong — the answer was that Column + verticalScroll at a fixed height only lays out the rows that fit, so there was genuinely nothing below row 8 to scroll to. LazyColumn was the right shape from the start.
Phase 2 — corridor built, F through G4. Worker dispatch on job type, geometry-to-points derivation, tile-set derivation from points plus buffer, a dedicated ConvoyCorridorWorker, and the wiring. All four compiled first try (14m03s).
Measured on real geography. 65,000 + 21,000 + 21,000 ≈ 107,000 against a bbox needing over a million for the same track. The per-source split is uneven because of layer counts, not different geometry — same corridor, SAT carrying three layers.
Cut over (patch H). Area button deleted from the artifact panel — deleted, not disabled — and track import swapped from bbox to corridor. The import swap turned out to be a loop, not a substitution: the old call covered all slots at once, corridor is one entry per source.
Patch I failed, patch J fixed it. The convoy download-confirm dialog overflows the bottom of the screen. It looked exactly like the 07-22 queues-width drift, so patch I copied planning's .align(Alignment.Center) across. It would not compile — Modifier.align() is a BoxScope extension, and convoy's dialog sits in a Column, not a Box. Patch J wrapped it in its own Box with contentAlignment instead.
Decisions locked
The area path is gone from the artifact panel, not hidden. This codebase has already been misled twice by dead functions that outlived their replacements (gridCells, downloadMapsForTrackHash). The composable parameter stays because two screens still pass it; nothing renders it.
Corridor stays unsplit for now — one entry per track per source. Splitting is a decision for after real numbers exist across differently-shaped tracks.
Route corridors and delete-area deferred, both cheap because launchWorker dispatches on type: each is a new worker that changes nothing existing.
What is pending
Install the cutover build on Droid 1 and Droid 2.
Corridor downloads still running — waiting on them to confirm the time estimate renders.
New bug: refresh jobs never log as completed.
⚠ Three things worth being careful about
1. Bar 10 is the best case, and the number will be quoted. It is the longest, thinnest track available, which is exactly why it shows corridor at its most favourable. A compact track's bounding box is already close to its corridor and will gain far less. When ≈90% gets repeated to testers, that caveat should travel with it — otherwise the first person to run a short loop track reports the feature as broken.
2. The ETA test may not be able to succeed yet. Waiting on corridor downloads to finish assumes the corridor worker stamps completion. But the refresh bug found today is precisely a job that never registers as complete, and the corridor worker deliberately duplicates the completion plumbing rather than sharing it — that was an accepted trade at design time, and this is that trade coming due. A five-minute read of whether ConvoyCorridorWorker calls markComplete is worth more than an evening of watching a progress bar.
3. The refresh bug might not be cosmetic. The obvious reading is "the status label is wrong." The one to rule out first is whether a never-completing job holds a concurrency slot forever — because that is a queue-stall mechanism, and "system just sits" is exactly what 07-23 reported when 3287 entries went in.
The afternoon — assets in, and the screen disagreed with the code
The build went on device, the 2.6d manual and release notes were written and copied into assets byte-exact, and the settings label moved to 2.6d. Then the queue panel was photographed while actually working, and three things fell out that no amount of reading the source had produced.
The ETA's finish date is three days out while its duration is exactly right — so the duration-to-clock maths works and only the date component is wrong.
Corridor jobs marked Done keep counting tiles. Three captures minutes apart show TOPO and TOPO+ climbing by hundreds while sitting under COMPLETED. Completion is being stamped before the work stops, which also means the ETA is computing its rate from a duration shorter than the real one.
SAT is frozen at exactly 15 tiles while its siblings climb. It should be the largest of the three, carrying three layers where the others carry fewer.
The good news arrived in the same capture: corridor jobs do register as completed, which closes the morning's worry and narrows the refresh bug to the refresh branch alone. Row detail, promote arrows, HOLD, concurrency, segmentation and — best of all — the scoped counts all render correctly: CANCEL ALL (6) beside CLEAR ALL (3), six cancellable against three clearable. That is the answer to the 07-23 incident working exactly as designed.
⚠ Where I was wrong today, twice, the same way
I removed "Hold" from the manual because it wasn't in the screenshot. It was simply hidden — there was nothing in the queue to hold. Minutes earlier I had explained away SAT's 15 tiles with a benign theory that the next two captures killed. Both were the same error: treating one screenshot in one state as a complete inventory. An idle panel shows what is actionable, not what exists.
Worth holding onto because the project keeps rewarding the opposite instinct. The segmentation investigation died on four theories before a log line settled it; the scroll bug survived four reasoned fixes before one printed number explained it; and today the screen contradicted the code twice in an hour.
Lessons
A matching symptom is not a matching cause. Patch I failed because the previous bug's fix was scope-illegal in a different container. Recognising a familiar shape is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis.
When several variations of one mechanism keep failing, change the mechanism. Four scroll fixes tuned parameters on a Column; the fix was a different composable.
Instrument first. One printed scroll max=0 settled in a glance what four rounds of reasoning could not.
Measure one variable at a time. The corridor number was taken before the z-cap deliberately, so the model change is attributable on its own and the cap can be measured on top.
One state is not an inventory. Absence from a screenshot is not absence from the app, and a single plausible explanation is not a diagnosis.
Look at the thing. Three defects surfaced in one photograph of a working panel that hours of reading the source had not produced.
