Map Source Change — Panel Flow
2026-08-06 v1 &middot; INTERNAL &middot; design confirmation, not a spec
Built and compiling today: ConvoySourceMigration.kt,
ConvoySourceClear.kt, and the ConvoyMapSourceScreen wiring
(patch 3 not yet applied)
  BUILT compiles today
  NEXT designed, next session
  LATER deferred deliberately
The whole flow at a glance
Map Sources ──► pick a new source ──► [RECORD OPENED] ──► DECISION PANEL ──► outcome ──► History
                                        before the                │
                                        slot changes              ├─ CLEAR TILES      BUILT
                                                                  ├─ KEEP TILES       BUILT
                                                                  └─ REPLACE IN PLACE NEXT
                                                                        │
                                                                        └─ then RELOAD: all tracks
                                                                           / selected / none  NEXT
⭐ Clear and reload are separate actions. Today's execution is the clear.
Reload is never automatic — the user chooses it deliberately, and the download panel is
always there afterwards regardless.
Step by step
    1Map Sources BUILT
      Map Sources
        Three fixed map slots. Tap to change source.
        SAT
          Esri Imagery + Overlays
          Esri &middot; HYB &middot; 3 stores &middot; 4.70 GB
        TOPO
          Esri TopographicEsri &middot; 367 MB
        TOPO+
          Esri USA TopoEsri &middot; 49 MB
    ⚠ Live sizes, not constants. The SAT column owns
    three stores — showing only SAT.mbtiles understates a clear by ~461&nbsp;MB.
  ▶
    2Pick a source BUILT
      Select Source for SAT
        HYBRID
        Google Hybrid ✓
          Google &middot; 1 store &middot; labels baked in
        Esri Imagery + Overlays
          Esri &middot; 3 stores &middot; current
        SATELLITE
        Esri World Imagery
          Esri &middot; imagery only
    ⭐ The record opens HERE, inside
    applySource, before updateSlotSource. After that call the
    outgoing source's cache dirs are unreachable and the label stores become orphans.
3The decision panel — where the whole conversation landed
      Map Source Changed
          SAT is now using Google Hybrid
          142,880 existing tiles are from the OLD source.
          Clearing removes 3 stores — SAT, SAT_LABELS_PLACES,
            SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT — freeing about 4,812 MB.
          THIS CANNOT BE UNDONE. There is no backup. Your download history
            for this column is cleared too, so note any areas you want to redraw.
          Nothing is downloaded now. When you are ready, draw areas or import
            tracks with map downloads — corridors around your tracks use about two thirds
            less storage.
            REPLACE IN PLACE
            KEEP TILES
            CLEAR TILES
      CLEAR TILES BUILT
      Runs the guarded sequence. Ends with an empty column and a completed record.
      KEEP TILES BUILT
      A stated decision, not a dismissal. ⚠ Must stamp the record
      kept_existing_tiles + complete, or it dangles as a permanently
      "interrupted" migration.
      REPLACE IN PLACE NEXT
      Area→area, corridor→corridor — swaps the source under existing coverage,
      preserving the storage method. Needs the area/corridor enqueue with
      replace=true + MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH, and
      enqueueRefresh retired.
      ⛔ No silent exit. onDismissRequest = { } — back-button and
      outside-tap do nothing. Every source change ends in a choice the record can describe.
      "Later" is gone; it was a deferral with no owner.
4What CLEAR TILES actually does BUILT
1  begin()            record written — ABORT if it cannot be written
2  holdQueue()        no new jobs start
3  cancelAll()        cancels DOWNLOADING workers (keeps COMPLETE)
4  awaitIdle()        poll ≤15s — cancelWorkById is ASYNC and returns early.
                      timeout ⇒ FAIL, do not delete under a live worker
5  clearCompleted()   drains the history cancelAll deliberately kept
6  deleteSource(dir)  per OLD-source cache dir, noteDeleted() after each
7  complete()         + resumeQueue()
⭐ Step 4 is the one that earns its place. deleteSource closes the
cached handle; doing that under a running worker risks a half-written store.
⭐ Resume is free. Already-deleted dirs are skipped, so running
clearColumn on an interrupted record finishes the job rather than repeating it.
⚠ resumeQueue() on every exit path including failure — a failed migration
that also leaves the queue paused is a worse bug than the one being avoided.
5Reload — a separate action NEXT
      Reload maps
        Pick any combination. Nothing is required.
         All tracks — corridors
         Pine Valley
         Bald Mountain (1)
         Bald Mountain (2)
         Areas — redraw
          these yourself; history was cleared
        NOTHING NOW
          QUEUE 24 JOBS
      ⭐ "All tracks" and "selected" are the same picker — one is a preselection.
      Same enqueue, same estimate, one code path. Mirrors the corridor picker where
      ALL is an ordinary checkbox.
      ⚠ Areas cannot be listed. Queue history is cleared with the tiles, so there is
      nothing to enumerate — and that is deliberate: recreating the same nine boxes on a new
      source rebuilds the problem the migration exists to fix. Users redraw and
      rethink their coverage.
      ⭐ "Nothing now" is a real answer. The download panel is always there. Draw an
      area or import tracks whenever you like.
6History on Map Sources NEXT
      Map Sources — Source history
          2026-08-06 · SAT
          Esri Imagery + Overlays → Google Hybrid
          3 stores removed · 4,812 MB freed · reload: all tracks
          2026-07-30 · TOPO
          USGS Topo → Esri Topographic
          tiles kept · no clear
          2026-07-12 · SAT — INTERRUPTED
          Esri → Google Hybrid
          1 of 3 stores removed · RESUME
      ⭐⭐ This is the answer to "where did my tiles go?"
      The migration deliberately destroys the queue history — the one record that would
      otherwise say what had been downloaded. So the record lives in
      maps/source_changes/, a sibling of maps/tiles/,
      deliberately outside everything a clear touches.
      ⚠ Interrupted records prompt, never auto-resume. Finishing means deleting GB of
      tiles, and the launch that discovers it may be at a trailhead.
Decisions this flow encodes
DecisionWhy
Refresh is not a menu itemThe transition only makes sense at the moment the
source changes — that is when "Esri → Google Hybrid" is a known fact rather than something
the app must infer.
Clear and reload are separateSeparates the action from interrelated decisions;
you pick based on your needs, nothing is automated.
Existing users are never movedwriteColumnFile:253 —
the saved column wins over the asset default. Google Hybrid is a
new-install default only.
Clear ⇒ replace = falseOn an empty store there is nothing to replace, and
hasTile then deduplicates across the whole batch — overlapping corridors download
shared tiles once.
Clear is its own job at priority 0Queue order is not guaranteed at
MAX_CONCURRENT = 2; a per-entry flag means whichever job runs first wipes what the
others wrote.
Beta recommendation: clear and start over15 testers, one path, one
configuration to reason about. ⚠ The strength of the recommendation is text that softens
later — the mechanism does not change.
Open before this is finished
KEEP TILES must complete its record — otherwise it dangles as a permanently
interrupted migration and pollutes the next source change on that column.
Segmentation threshold — 60,000 or 50,000? One number is stale, and the reload
estimate rests on it.
Startup prompt for unfinished migrations — hasUnfinished() exists;
nothing calls it yet.
Union of old and new cache dirs — the clear deletes the OLD source's stores. If the
NEW source's store already exists with stale tiles, it survives. Deliberate for now (a shared
cache dir could belong to another column) but worth a decision.
Prove on Droid 2 before Droid 1. This deletes GB with no backup.

2026-08-06 v2 &middot; INTERNAL &middot; design confirmation
v2 CORRECTION: ONE PANEL CONTROLS EVERY DECISION. v1 showed tile handling and
reload as separate cascading panels — wrong. Both live on the same surface, with one action.
  BUILT compiles today
  NEXT designed, next session
Shape

                                        slot changes           ├ reload:         tracks, any combination

⭐ Not cascading. The panel is the single control surface for the whole
process — every decision visible at once, priced, and committed together.

      Map Sources

    ⭐ The record opens HERE — inside
      applySource, before updateSlotSource. After that call the
      outgoing source's cache dirs are unreachable and the label stores become orphans.
2THE PANEL — every decision, one surface
      SAT — source changed to Google Hybrid
        142,880 stored tiles came from
          Esri Imagery + Overlays. Decide what happens to them and what to download next.
          EXISTING TILES
            Clear them — removes 3 stores, frees 4,812 MB
              Recommended. Single source, smallest footprint, nothing stale left behind.
              Cannot be undone. No backup. Download history is cleared too.
            Keep them — nothing removed, nothing downloaded
              Old tiles keep working as they are. New downloads use Google Hybrid.
              You will have two sources in this column.
            Replace in place — re-download existing coverage on the new source
              NEXT
              Keeps your storage method (area→area, corridor→corridor). Maps keep
              working throughout. No space reclaimed.
          RELOAD — PICK ANY COMBINATION NEXT
            All tracks — corridors around every track
              8 tracks · ~161,000 tiles · about 4 hours
           Pine Valley ~19,400 tiles
           Bald Mountain (1) ~22,100 tiles
           Bald Mountain (2) ~17,800 tiles
            Areas — nothing to list
              Download history is cleared with the tiles. Redraw the areas you
              actually want, in the download panel, whenever you like.
            Nothing now
              Clear only. Draw areas or import tracks later — the download panel
              is always there.
          MAP SOURCES TO DOWNLOAD NEXT
           SAT — Google Hybrid
           TOPO — Esri Topographic
           TOPO+ — Esri USA Topo
            Each source you add multiplies the download.
          Clear 3 stores · 4,812 MB freed
          Then download 8 corridors × 1 source = 8 jobs · ~161,000 tiles · about 4 hours
          Runs in the background and survives restarts.
          CANCEL — LEAVE EVERYTHING
          PROCEED
      ⭐ One panel, one commitment.
      Tile handling and reload are separate decisions but a single action.
      You see what you lose, what you get back, and what it costs — before anything runs.
      ⭐ Sections disable rather than disappear. Choosing Keep or
      Replace in place greys the reload section — there is nothing to reload. Same
      pattern as the greyed import rows: state stays visible, control goes away.
      ⭐ The numbers are the recommendation. No decision engine. 4,812 MB freed against
      4 hours to rebuild — the choice makes itself, and it stays honest for the tester with
      60 GB as well as the one with 300 MB.
      ⚠ Source count is the biggest lever and it has never been visible at the point of
      decision. Two sources instead of three is a third off the time.
      ⛔ No silent exit. Back-button and outside-tap do nothing. CANCEL is an explicit
      choice and is recorded as one — otherwise the record dangles as a permanently
      "interrupted" migration and pollutes the next source change on this column.
3What PROCEED runs BUILT (clear half)
1  begin()            record written — ABORT if it cannot be written
2  holdQueue()        no new jobs start
3  cancelAll()        cancels DOWNLOADING workers (keeps COMPLETE)
4  awaitIdle()        poll ≤15s — cancelWorkById is ASYNC and returns early.
                      timeout ⇒ FAIL, do not delete under a live worker
5  clearCompleted()   drains the history cancelAll deliberately kept
6  deleteSource(dir)  per OLD-source cache dir, noteDeleted() after each
7  complete()         + resumeQueue()
                      ── then the reload selection is enqueued ──  NEXT
⭐ Clear is its own job at priority 0, ahead of the batch — not a flag on the
first entry. Queue order is not guaranteed at MAX_CONCURRENT = 2, so a per-entry
flag means whichever job runs first wipes what the others wrote.
⭐ Clear ⇒ replace = false, forced and locked. On an empty store there is nothing to
replace, and hasTile then deduplicates across the whole batch — overlapping
corridors fetch shared tiles once instead of repeatedly.
⭐ Resume is free. Already-deleted dirs are skipped, so running on an interrupted
record finishes rather than repeats.
4History on Map Sources NEXT
      Map Sources — Source history
        2026-08-06 · SAT
          Esri Imagery + Overlays → Google Hybrid
          3 stores removed · 4,812 MB freed · reload: all tracks
        2026-07-30 · TOPO
          USGS Topo → Esri Topographic
          tiles kept · no clear
          2026-07-12 · SAT — INTERRUPTED
          Esri → Google Hybrid
          1 of 3 stores removed · RESUME
      ⭐⭐ The answer to "where did my tiles go?"
      The migration deliberately destroys the queue history — the one record that would
      otherwise say what had been downloaded. So the record lives in
      maps/source_changes/, a sibling of maps/tiles/, outside
      everything a clear touches.
      ⚠ Interrupted records prompt, never auto-resume. Finishing means deleting GB of
      tiles, and the launch that finds it may be at a trailhead.

2THE PANEL — explanation, then three options
      SAT — set up your maps for Google Hybrid
          Your stored tiles came from Esri and cannot be converted. Esri satellite needs
          two extra label stores for place and road names; Google Hybrid has those names baked
          into the imagery and does not use them.
          Either way you lose labels on your existing Esri tiles — the new
          source does not fetch label overlays, so those tiles will draw as plain satellite from
          now on. Clearing at least reclaims the 461 MB the label stores are using.
          We recommend clearing for a move from Esri to Google Hybrid — unless you are
          already running corridor-based tiles, in which case your storage is already efficient
          and replacing in place keeps your maps working throughout.
          If you clear, any reload choice is comfortable. If you are not sure, choose
          Nothing now: your Esri tiles stay exactly as they are and you can refresh on
          demand later with Download Tiles by Area or by Track.
          1 — EXISTING TILES
            Clear themRECOMMENDED
              Removes 3 stores, frees 4,812 MB. Single source, nothing stale left.
              Cannot be undone. No backup. Download history is cleared too.
            Replace in place NEXT
              Re-downloads your existing coverage on the new source, keeping your
              storage method — area stays area, corridor stays corridor. Maps keep working
              throughout. No space reclaimed. Best if you are already on corridors.
            Keep them as they are
              Nothing removed, nothing downloaded. Your Esri tiles keep working
              without labels; anything new comes from Google Hybrid.
          2 — RELOAD NEXT
            All tracks — corridorsIF YOU HAVE TRACKS
              Corridors around every imported track. Recommended when you have
              track histories — coverage follows where you actually ride, using about two thirds
              less storage. 8 tracks · ~161,000 tiles · about 4 hours.
            All areasIF YOU DO NOT
              Rebuilds your area coverage on the new source. Recommended if you
              downloaded areas and do not intend to import tracks.
            Nothing now
              Nothing is queued. Draw an area or import tracks whenever you
              like — Download Tiles by Area and by Track are always available.
          Clear 3 stores · 4,812 MB freed
          Then download 8 corridor jobs · ~161,000 tiles · about 4 hours
          Runs in the background and survives restarts.
          CANCEL
          PROCEED
      ⭐ No picker. All tracks or all areas — whole options, no per-item
      selection. The explanation does the work a selection UI would have done, and there is far
      less to build.
      ⭐ The recommendation is conditional and stated, not computed. Clear unless you
      are already on corridors · all-tracks if you have tracks · all-areas if you do not ·
      nothing-now if unsure. Four sentences, no decision engine.
      ⚠ "All areas" needs the area list to survive the clear. Queue entries carry
      north/south/east/west, but a clear wipes queue history — so clear + all
      areas cannot both be honoured unless the bboxes are copied into the migration record
      first. ⭐ Cheap fix: snapshot them into the record at begin().
      ⛔ CANCEL must complete the record, not just close the panel — otherwise it
      dangles as a permanently interrupted migration and pollutes the next source change on this
      column.
3What PROCEED runs
CLEAR HALF  ── BUILT, compiles ───────────────────────────────
1  begin()            record written — ABORT if it cannot be written
2  holdQueue()        no new jobs start
3  cancelAll()        cancels DOWNLOADING workers (keeps COMPLETE)
4  awaitIdle()        poll ≤15s — cancelWorkById is ASYNC and returns early.
                      timeout ⇒ FAIL, do not delete under a live worker
5  clearCompleted()   drains the history cancelAll deliberately kept
6  deleteSource(dir)  per OLD-source cache dir, noteDeleted() after each
7  complete()         + resumeQueue()
RELOAD HALF ── NEXT ──────────────────────────────────────────
8  all tracks  → enqueueCorridorBatch(all hashes, [new slot], replace=false)
   all areas   → area enqueue over snapshotted bboxes, replace=false
   nothing now → no-op, recorded as the choice
⭐ replace=false after a clear, forced and locked: on an empty store there is nothing
to replace, and hasTile then deduplicates across the whole batch so overlapping
corridors fetch shared tiles once.

MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 adb -s 24039703201775 shell ls -la /sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/*.db
Record the sizes before you start and after each destructive test. ⚠ Any test that clears,
deletes or uninstalls goes LAST, after everything non-destructive has passed.
⚠ THROUGHPUT NOTE — the overnight slowdown, and what it is NOT
7 PM → 7 AM produced 90 jobs, ~7.5/hour. Daytime was ~24/hour, and the rate roughly
doubled again when daytime resumed on 08-09. Overnight ran at about a third of daytime
speed.
⭐⭐ DOZE IS THE LEADING EXPLANATION AFTER ALL — AND THE REASON IS THE POWER SOURCE.
Droid 2 was charging from the laptop's USB port, and the laptop sleeps. A sleeping host
commonly cuts or throttles USB power, so Android may well have seen the device as UNPLUGGED for
much of the night — which satisfies all three Doze conditions (unplugged, screen off,
stationary). ⚠ "Plugged into a PC" is NOT the same as "on power." Use a wall charger for any
overnight run that is being measured.
⚠ RECORD OF THE REASONING, so it is not re-litigated: Doze was proposed → withdrawn when
Fred said the device was plugged in → reinstated when he identified the source as a sleeping
PC. Neither the first nor the second call was safe on the evidence available at the time.
STILL POSSIBLE ALONGSIDE IT — none ruled out, and all would hit real users:
Thermal throttling — leading candidate. Four concurrent slots for twelve hours on charge
heats both radio and battery. Check: adb shell dumpsys thermalservice | head -30
WiFi power save with the screen off — many devices drop the radio to low power even
while charging.
OEM background management — vendor-specific, independent of Doze AND of charging.
Tile server behaviour — least likely overnight in the US, not impossible.
⚠ THE 08-09 EVENING RUN IS CONFOUNDED — THREE VARIABLES CHANGED AT ONCE: Doze disabled
via ADB, battery optimization + all auto-optimization turned off for GroupTrack, and the power
situation understood. ⭐ RESULT: 36 tiles/sec — a NEW HIGH, above the 33.2 aggregate measured at
4 slots on 08-08, which had been the ceiling. So the changes did more than recover the daytime
rate. ⚠ Which single change delivered it is NOT established.
⭐⭐ PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE, not just a test note: users cannot run ADB. Large corridor
downloads left running overnight will hit whatever this is. The app should request a battery
optimization exemption (REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS), and the manual and
quickstart should say plug in AND set the app to Unrestricted before a large download.
⚠ Do not quote overnight completion times from daytime rates until this is settled.

GroupTrack — Tooling &amp; Troubleshooting Reference
Created 2026-08-05 · additive section for the Living Master · branch feature/convoy-event-ride
WHY THIS EXISTS
Four separate defects this week shared one shape: a method aborted before its real work, silently, and no structural tool could have found it. The existing xrefs answer where is this touched. Every one of these bugs lived on a different axis — on what thread, in what lifecycle phase, against which page. This section documents what each tool can and cannot answer, the execution-context contracts that have no tool at all, and step-by-step recipes aimed at specific results.
1 · The xref tools — what each one actually indexes
All three live in the repo root and are regenerated on demand (recommit rebuilds them). They are DEFINITION / SYMBOL INDEXES, NOT A CALL GRAPH.
ToolIndexesUse it to answer
  field_crossref_raw.txt
  Field and property declarations with [R] / [W] markers and line numbers
  Who reads and who writes a field. The 08-02 source-persistence root cause came straight out of this: MapSourceManager had exactly two writes, both the API-keys file, so nothing persisted a slot. A field with many [R] and no [W] is a value nobody maintains.
  where_used_raw.txt
  Symbol occurrences by file and line
  Blast radius of a rename or signature change. First stop before touching a shared symbol.
  function_universe_raw.txt
  Function declarations with signatures and locations
  Does this function exist, where, and with what signature. Also the starting list for a dead-code sweep — but see §4 before deleting anything on its say-so.
  grep
  Raw text
  CALL SITES. Source of truth, always. Use --include='*.kt' to skip .bak_* files.
THE STANDING RULE
xref for candidates, grep for call sites. The xrefs give signatures and locations; they do not tell you who calls what. Every time that rule has been skipped it has cost a session.
Known blind spots — each one cost real time
Invisible to the xrefsEvidence
Lambda parametersonDownloadMaps is a lambda parameter on a composable and appears in no xref. Looked dead; was live in two screens.
var X by remember { } localsaddPointMode is in no xref, which is why "find where it is declared" took a whole session.
Annotated bridge methods@JavascriptInterface methods were missed in an earlier sweep for the same reason.
Tags held in constants08-05: grep "Log\.[a-z](\"TAG\"" returned nothing across four well-instrumented files — the tags are TAG constants, not literals at the call site. The scan reported silence that did not exist.
Anything inside a non-executing block08-03: a def-scan of a deleted range found only checkLayer and reported it clean — the range was inside a &lt;script src="…"&gt; tag whose inline body never executes by spec. The scan could not have seen what was wrong.
⛔ THE PATTERN BEHIND ALL FIVE
Scanning for one shape of evidence and reporting "clean" when the scan could not have seen what was there. A negative result from a grep is only as good as the pattern. Before trusting an empty result, prove the pattern can match a known-present case.
2 · Layer contracts — the axis with no tooling
These are execution-context rules. Violating one produces valid, compiling code that silently does nothing. Every row here was discovered by a production failure, not by review.
BoundaryRuns onRuleLearned
  @JavascriptInterface methods
  JavaBridge thread
  Any WebView or UI call MUST go through Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { }. evaluateJavascript and Toast throw off-main, and the throw aborts the rest of the method silently.
  08-01 convoy · 08-05 planner (:717)
  Argument positions
  —
  Never ?: return inside an argument. It reads as a null-safe accessor and is an early exit from the entire enclosing function.
  08-01 onPageFinished
  onPageFinished
  main
  Page is not ready until the postDelayed completes. Kotlin→JS calls before it fail with &lt;fn&gt; is not defined — visible only in a console log.
  07-30, still live
  evaluateJavascript(fn)
  main only
  The named function must exist in both map HTMLs. SpatialDisplayManager is map-agnostic; its jsUpdate/jsShow/jsHide contract assumes parity that is hand-maintained.
  standing
  WorkManager workers
  fresh process
  Jobs survive app death. ensureInit() re-reads config from scratch — never trust in-memory state across the process boundary. A slot resolved at execution time may differ from the one queued against.
  08-02 / 08-03
  shouldInterceptRequest
  network thread
  No UI, no WebView calls.
  standing
  Composable declaration order
  —
  A local fun defined before a val cannot forward-reference it.
  08-01
⭐ AUTOMATABLE — the one check worth scripting
Row 1 is mechanical: scan for WebView/UI calls inside @JavascriptInterface method bodies (brace-depth walk over the two screen files) and report them. Seconds to run, and it would have caught ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:717 the day it was written.
It also answers the divergence question for free: run it against both screens and diff. Convoy clean, planner flagged is the output that would have ended 08-05 at 9am instead of 4pm.
3 · Divergence is a defect until proven intentional
Convoy is the reference implementation. Four times this week convoy had a fix the planner did not, and nobody knew until it broke:
  [Fix2] fresh re-read of MapStateStore — convoy :728. Planner still read a first-compose remember. (fixed 08-05, PLANNERSEED)
  Seeding lastViewport* before draw — convoy :730-733. Planner had no equivalent. (fixed 08-05)
  Posting evaluateJavascript to main — convoy does it via SpatialDisplayManager. Planner called direct. (fixed 08-05, VIEWPORTMAIN)
  Reseed gate — convoy dropped it 07-01; planner retains it. This one IS intentional (convoy is persistent and owns one map identity; the planner is entered and left, and the gate prevents cross-map bleed).
⚠ THE LIMIT
The maps are not symmetric by nature and should not be forced to be. Convoy has no entry event; the planner does. Making the lifecycles identical would reintroduce the contamination MapStateStore exists to prevent. The target is SHARED CODE, not MATCHED CODE — two hand-maintained copies drift again no matter how carefully aligned today. SpatialDisplayManager has been the reliable layer all week precisely because there is one copy. This is the same argument that makes the 2.7 service-layer work worth doing.
4 · Recipe — dead-code prune (2.7)
⛔ READ FIRST — THE TRAP UNIQUE TO THIS CODEBASE
Kotlin calls JavaScript functions BY NAME, from inside a string. ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:578 calls showProximityPopup that way. No JS tool sees that call. No Kotlin tool sees it either. A JS function with zero references in the HTML can be fully live; a Kotlin function whose only caller is a nav registration can be fully dead. Neither toolchain crosses the boundary — you are the only thing that does.
The sequence — do not skip a step
  Candidate list from function_universe_raw.txt.
  Grep the Kotlin for the bare name: grep -rn "name" --include='*.kt' app/src/
  Grep the ASSETS — both map HTMLs and any .js: grep -rn "name" app/src/main/assets/
  Grep for the name inside STRINGS — this is the cross-boundary step and the one that gets skipped: grep -rn '"[^"]*name[^"]*"' --include='*.kt' app/src/
  Check nav registration. A destination can be registered with no navigate() caller — e.g. ConvoyRouteCreateScreen.kt, a 27-line stub registered at ConvoyNavigation.kt:87 and reachable from nowhere.
  Confirm at runtime before deleting. Add one log line, build, exercise the app, confirm silence. Cheaper than a wrong deletion.
  Delete WITH its caller, in the same commit. Never leave a dead pair for later.
⚠ CURRENT DEAD-OR-DYING INVENTORY
  showProximityPopup + Kotlin onProximityTap + its ROUTETAP-2026-08-02 guard — planner proximity was removed 08-03; these are now uncalled. When this path retires, must-fix #3 stays closed but closed BY REMOVAL, not by the guard. Record it that way or a future session reads the guard as load-bearing.
  ConvoyRouteCreateScreen.kt — stub, registered, no caller.
  spatial_artifacts.js — orphan, nothing loads it; both HTMLs carry divergent inlined copies.
  Convoy dead __routeMode scaffolding — permanently dead given TAPRESET; the // BUG A comment at convoy_map.html:552 is a proven false lead.
  gridCells (ConvoyTileDownloader:297) · downloadMapsForTrackHash (SpatialDbManager:1945).
  Duplicate var tracksVisible in convoy_map.html — :27 declares true, :443 declares false. Same variable, two vars, opposite values.
  TRACK-DBG: TICK (twice per 5s — actively destroys logcat evidence) · WAYPOINT-TRACE · smoothFactor on trails.
5 · Recipe — "it should draw and it doesn't"
The 08-05 sequence, generalised. Each step is a measurement, not a theory.
  Prove the channel before believing silence. Console tags: planner MapJS · convoy ConvoyJS · sources MapSourceMgr · workers CorridorWorker/DownloadQueue/TileDownloader/Corridor. Filter the FILE, never the stream — a bad pattern on a live stream is indistinguishable from a silent app.
    adb -s &lt;serial&gt; logcat -d &gt; /d/cap.txt &amp;&amp; wc -l /d/cap.txt
    Use -d (dump and exit). Streaming with a pipe does not respond to Ctrl-C in Git-Bash and truncates silently.
  READ THE HEAD OF ANY STACK TRACE. The 08-05 root cause was at frame 99 of a trace present in every capture from 9am; the exception type was one line above it. Nobody read up.
  Partition with gestures, not code: cold start → direct entry (no other map first) → pan → fit. Which gesture fails localises the defect faster than any read.
  Compare against convoy at every step. A hypothesis that cannot answer "then why does convoy work?" is dead before it costs a build.
  Separate stale from absent. Wrong-region artifacts = a bad bbox. No artifacts, prior content persisting = the draw never ran. Conflating these cost most of 08-05.
  Watch for residue on the shared WebView. Convoy is persistent; its drawn layers survive. Artifacts on the planner may be convoy's pixels, not the planner's output. Any test that visits convoy first is contaminated.
6 · Standing hazards worth re-reading before a build
HazardCheck
APK older than the source you patchedls -la --time-style=+%H:%M:%S &lt;apk&gt; &lt;changed sources&gt; — 20 seconds vs a wasted test session
Asset copied but not the one you editedVerify by content grep for a marker unique to today's edit, never by "cp succeeded"
Cheap compile gate skipped./gradlew compileGoogleReleaseKotlin — 1–4 min vs 12–40. Patch scripts prove the anchor matched; only the compiler proves the code is valid
Diagnostic work bundled with fixesNever. Settled and exploratory work carry different risk, and bundling entangles verification
Instrumentation left inIt comes out in the commit that closes the task, not on a cleanup list. All of this week's rendering failures happened in the window between "found it" and "we'll clean that up"
Device clock confusionDroid 2 is on Utah time; the laptop is Eastern. logcat timestamps are DEVICE time
Install downgradePlain -r, never -d. Cancel immediately on first-install prompts for an already-installed app
TOOLING OWED
  Bridge-thread scanner (§2) — highest value, smallest effort.
  Cross-boundary name checker — every evaluateJavascript("fn(...)") in Kotlin has a matching function fn in both HTMLs. Would have caught setRouteMode is not defined and its two siblings.
  Screen-parity diff — the two screen files' handling of the same shared-manager calls, side by side.

GroupTrack — Troubleshooting Tools and Uses
Created 2026-08-05 · additive section for the Living Master · branch feature/convoy-event-ride
WHY THIS EXISTS
Four separate defects this week shared one shape: a method aborted before its real work, silently, and no structural tool could have found it. The existing xrefs answer where is this touched. Every one of these bugs lived on a different axis — on what thread, in what lifecycle phase, against which page. This section documents what each tool can and cannot answer, the execution-context contracts that have no tool at all, and step-by-step recipes aimed at specific results.
1 · The xref tools — what each one actually indexes
All three live in the repo root and are regenerated on demand (recommit rebuilds them). They are DEFINITION / SYMBOL INDEXES, NOT A CALL GRAPH.
ToolIndexesUse it to answer
  field_crossref_raw.txt
  Field and property declarations with [R] / [W] markers and line numbers
  Who reads and who writes a field. The 08-02 source-persistence root cause came straight out of this: MapSourceManager had exactly two writes, both the API-keys file, so nothing persisted a slot. A field with many [R] and no [W] is a value nobody maintains.
  where_used_raw.txt
  Symbol occurrences by file and line
  Blast radius of a rename or signature change. First stop before touching a shared symbol.
  function_universe_raw.txt
  Function declarations with signatures and locations
  Does this function exist, where, and with what signature. Also the starting list for a dead-code sweep — but see §4 before deleting anything on its say-so.
  navigation_xref.txt
  Four sections: A nav-host routes (every registered destination) · C navigation triggers — navigate() calls and onNavigate* params with the line where each is invoked · D screen composables + exit callbacks · E user-visible labels
  WHERE A SCREEN IS CALLED FROM — real call sites, not declarations. This is the one xref that crosses into call-site territory, for navigation only. ⭐ Section A vs C makes the dead-destination check mechanical: a route registered in A with no navigate() in C is unreachable. Proven: ConvoyRouteCreate is in A and D, absent from C. Section E is the manual-writing tool — it is what the user actually taps.
  grep
  Raw text
  CALL SITES. Source of truth, always. Use --include='*.kt' to skip .bak_* files.
THE STANDING RULE
xref for candidates, grep for call sites — with ONE exception. field_crossref, where_used and function_universe give signatures and locations and do not tell you who calls what. Every time that has been forgotten it has cost a session.
⭐ navigation_xref.txt IS the exception — its section C carries real invocation sites. So for anything about screen routing, reachability or what a user can actually get to, read the navigation xref FIRST rather than grepping. Check its Generated: timestamp against your last commit; a call-site index that lags the code produces confident wrong answers.
Known blind spots — each one cost real time
Invisible to the xrefsEvidence
Lambda parametersonDownloadMaps is a lambda parameter on a composable and appears in no xref. Looked dead; was live in two screens.
var X by remember { } localsaddPointMode is in no xref, which is why "find where it is declared" took a whole session.
Annotated bridge methods@JavascriptInterface methods were missed in an earlier sweep for the same reason.
Tags held in constants08-05: grep "Log\.[a-z](\"TAG\"" returned nothing across four well-instrumented files — the tags are TAG constants, not literals at the call site. The scan reported silence that did not exist.
Anything inside a non-executing block08-03: a def-scan of a deleted range found only checkLayer and reported it clean — the range was inside a &lt;script src="…"&gt; tag whose inline body never executes by spec. The scan could not have seen what was wrong.
⛔ THE PATTERN BEHIND ALL FIVE
Scanning for one shape of evidence and reporting "clean" when the scan could not have seen what was there. A negative result from a grep is only as good as the pattern. Before trusting an empty result, prove the pattern can match a known-present case.
2 · Layer contracts — the axis with no tooling
These are execution-context rules. Violating one produces valid, compiling code that silently does nothing. Every row here was discovered by a production failure, not by review.
BoundaryRuns onRuleLearned
  @JavascriptInterface methods
  JavaBridge thread
  Any WebView or UI call MUST go through Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { }. evaluateJavascript and Toast throw off-main, and the throw aborts the rest of the method silently.
  08-01 convoy · 08-05 planner (:717)
  Argument positions
  —
  Never ?: return inside an argument. It reads as a null-safe accessor and is an early exit from the entire enclosing function.
  08-01 onPageFinished
  onPageFinished
  main
  Page is not ready until the postDelayed completes. Kotlin→JS calls before it fail with &lt;fn&gt; is not defined — visible only in a console log.
  07-30, still live
  evaluateJavascript(fn)
  main only
  The named function must exist in both map HTMLs. SpatialDisplayManager is map-agnostic; its jsUpdate/jsShow/jsHide contract assumes parity that is hand-maintained.
  standing
  WorkManager workers
  fresh process
  Jobs survive app death. ensureInit() re-reads config from scratch — never trust in-memory state across the process boundary. A slot resolved at execution time may differ from the one queued against.
  08-02 / 08-03
  shouldInterceptRequest
  network thread
  No UI, no WebView calls.
  standing
  Composable declaration order
  —
  A local fun defined before a val cannot forward-reference it.
  08-01
⭐ AUTOMATABLE — the one check worth scripting
Row 1 is mechanical: scan for WebView/UI calls inside @JavascriptInterface method bodies (brace-depth walk over the two screen files) and report them. Seconds to run, and it would have caught ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:717 the day it was written.
It also answers the divergence question for free: run it against both screens and diff. Convoy clean, planner flagged is the output that would have ended 08-05 at 9am instead of 4pm.
3 · Divergence is a defect until proven intentional
Convoy is the reference implementation. Four times this week convoy had a fix the planner did not, and nobody knew until it broke:
  [Fix2] fresh re-read of MapStateStore — convoy :728. Planner still read a first-compose remember. (fixed 08-05, PLANNERSEED)
  Seeding lastViewport* before draw — convoy :730-733. Planner had no equivalent. (fixed 08-05)
  Posting evaluateJavascript to main — convoy does it via SpatialDisplayManager. Planner called direct. (fixed 08-05, VIEWPORTMAIN)
  Reseed gate — convoy dropped it 07-01; planner retains it. This one IS intentional (convoy is persistent and owns one map identity; the planner is entered and left, and the gate prevents cross-map bleed).
⚠ THE LIMIT
The maps are not symmetric by nature and should not be forced to be. Convoy has no entry event; the planner does. Making the lifecycles identical would reintroduce the contamination MapStateStore exists to prevent. The target is SHARED CODE, not MATCHED CODE — two hand-maintained copies drift again no matter how carefully aligned today. SpatialDisplayManager has been the reliable layer all week precisely because there is one copy. This is the same argument that makes the 2.7 service-layer work worth doing.
4 · Recipe — dead-code prune (2.7)
⛔ READ FIRST — THE TRAP UNIQUE TO THIS CODEBASE
Kotlin calls JavaScript functions BY NAME, from inside a string. ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt:578 calls showProximityPopup that way. No JS tool sees that call. No Kotlin tool sees it either. A JS function with zero references in the HTML can be fully live; a Kotlin function whose only caller is a nav registration can be fully dead. Neither toolchain crosses the boundary — you are the only thing that does.
The sequence — do not skip a step
  Candidate list from function_universe_raw.txt.
  Grep the Kotlin for the bare name: grep -rn "name" --include='*.kt' app/src/
  Grep the ASSETS — both map HTMLs and any .js: grep -rn "name" app/src/main/assets/
  Grep for the name inside STRINGS — this is the cross-boundary step and the one that gets skipped: grep -rn '"[^"]*name[^"]*"' --include='*.kt' app/src/
  Check reachability with navigation_xref.txt — section A against section C. A destination registered in A with no navigate() in C is unreachable, whatever else references it. Worked example: ConvoyRouteCreate is registered at ConvoyNavigation.kt:87 (A) and its composable is declared at ConvoyRouteCreateScreen.kt:18 (D) — and it appears nowhere in C. A 27-line stub reachable from nothing. ⭐ This is mechanical — do it before any manual grepping.
  Confirm at runtime before deleting. Add one log line, build, exercise the app, confirm silence. Cheaper than a wrong deletion.
  Delete WITH its caller, in the same commit. Never leave a dead pair for later.
⚠ CURRENT DEAD-OR-DYING INVENTORY
  showProximityPopup + Kotlin onProximityTap + its ROUTETAP-2026-08-02 guard — planner proximity was removed 08-03; these are now uncalled. When this path retires, must-fix #3 stays closed but closed BY REMOVAL, not by the guard. Record it that way or a future session reads the guard as load-bearing.
  ConvoyRouteCreateScreen.kt — stub, registered, no caller.
  spatial_artifacts.js — orphan, nothing loads it; both HTMLs carry divergent inlined copies.
  Convoy dead __routeMode scaffolding — permanently dead given TAPRESET; the // BUG A comment at convoy_map.html:552 is a proven false lead.
  gridCells (ConvoyTileDownloader:297) · downloadMapsForTrackHash (SpatialDbManager:1945).
  Duplicate var tracksVisible in convoy_map.html — :27 declares true, :443 declares false. Same variable, two vars, opposite values.
  TRACK-DBG: TICK (twice per 5s — actively destroys logcat evidence) · WAYPOINT-TRACE · smoothFactor on trails.
5 · Recipe — "it should draw and it doesn't"
The 08-05 sequence, generalised. Each step is a measurement, not a theory.
  Prove the channel before believing silence. Console tags: planner MapJS · convoy ConvoyJS · sources MapSourceMgr · workers CorridorWorker/DownloadQueue/TileDownloader/Corridor. Filter the FILE, never the stream — a bad pattern on a live stream is indistinguishable from a silent app.
    adb -s &lt;serial&gt; logcat -d &gt; /d/cap.txt &amp;&amp; wc -l /d/cap.txt
    Use -d (dump and exit). Streaming with a pipe does not respond to Ctrl-C in Git-Bash and truncates silently.
  READ THE HEAD OF ANY STACK TRACE. The 08-05 root cause was at frame 99 of a trace present in every capture from 9am; the exception type was one line above it. Nobody read up.
  Partition with gestures, not code: cold start → direct entry (no other map first) → pan → fit. Which gesture fails localises the defect faster than any read.
  Compare against convoy at every step. A hypothesis that cannot answer "then why does convoy work?" is dead before it costs a build.
  Separate stale from absent. Wrong-region artifacts = a bad bbox. No artifacts, prior content persisting = the draw never ran. Conflating these cost most of 08-05.
  Watch for residue on the shared WebView. Convoy is persistent; its drawn layers survive. Artifacts on the planner may be convoy's pixels, not the planner's output. Any test that visits convoy first is contaminated.
6 · Standing hazards worth re-reading before a build
HazardCheck
APK older than the source you patchedls -la --time-style=+%H:%M:%S &lt;apk&gt; &lt;changed sources&gt; — 20 seconds vs a wasted test session
Asset copied but not the one you editedVerify by content grep for a marker unique to today's edit, never by "cp succeeded"
Cheap compile gate skipped./gradlew compileGoogleReleaseKotlin — 1–4 min vs 12–40. Patch scripts prove the anchor matched; only the compiler proves the code is valid
Diagnostic work bundled with fixesNever. Settled and exploratory work carry different risk, and bundling entangles verification
Instrumentation left inIt comes out in the commit that closes the task, not on a cleanup list. All of this week's rendering failures happened in the window between "found it" and "we'll clean that up"
Device clock confusionDroid 2 is on Utah time; the laptop is Eastern. logcat timestamps are DEVICE time
Install downgradePlain -r, never -d. Cancel immediately on first-install prompts for an already-installed app
TOOLING OWED
  Bridge-thread scanner (§2) — highest value, smallest effort.
  Cross-boundary name checker — every evaluateJavascript("fn(...)") in Kotlin has a matching function fn in both HTMLs. Would have caught setRouteMode is not defined and its two siblings.
  Screen-parity diff — the two screen files' handling of the same shared-manager calls, side by side.

Device clock confusionDroid 2 is on Utah time; the laptop is Eastern. logcat timestamps are DEVICE time
Install downgradePlain -r, never -d. Cancel immediately on first-install prompts for an already-installed app
TOOLING OWED
  Bridge-thread scanner (§2) — highest value, smallest effort.
  Cross-boundary name checker — every evaluateJavascript("fn(...)") in Kotlin has a matching function fn in both HTMLs. Would have caught setRouteMode is not defined and its two siblings.
  Screen-parity diff — the two screen files' handling of the same shared-manager calls, side by side.

  V3.0 MAP FUNCTIONS DEFINITION · APRIL 10, 2026 · CONFIDENTIAL
    01 Map Architecture
      V3.0 separates map functionality into two distinct maps. The Convoy Map remains operational and focused. The Planning Map is a new greenfield screen in the Maps section of the bottom nav.
          MapPurposeFunctions
              CONVOY MAP
              Operational — launched from main nav during a ride
              Live node tracking, HUD, track recording, layer switch, NET/LOCAL toggle, show downloaded areas, KML/GPX overlay (read-only, from library)
              PLANNING MAP
              Planning — dedicated Maps section in bottom nav
              Waypoint creation, track/route overlays, area search, tile download management, layer preferences, storage management, AWS coverage display, route planner, download region draw
      Rule: Planning Map functions never bleed into Convoy Map. During a ride the screen stays clean and operationally focused. All asset management lives in the Maps section.
      Map Bar — Two-Row Layout (V2.4 Current)
          T
          TRAILHEAD
            ▼
            MAP &nbsp;SAT
              NET
            SAT
            HYB
            TOPO
            RD
        CURRENT VIEWPORT — ASSETS SHOWN WITHIN THIS AREA ONLY
    02 Asset Types
        ⬛ TRACK
        Recorded path — already ridden. GPX or KML. Solid line display. Color from assigned palette or default #6B4EFF.
        -- ROUTE
        Planned path — not yet ridden. GPX or KML. Dashed line display. Orange #F5A623. Types: LOOP, OUT &amp; BACK, POINT TO POINT.
        ⊙ TRAILHEAD
        Named meeting/start point. Waypoint subtype with icon_type=TRAILHEAD. Always visible on map regardless of toggle state.
        ⬡ WAYPOINT
        Single named point. Types: HAZARD, LANDMARK, MEETING POINT. Standard pins, OFF by default in layer panel.
    03 Track Storage Rules
        FolderContents
          mytracks/recorded/GPS recordings from GroupTrack
          mytracks/imported/Files brought in via file picker from Downloads
          mytracks/rides/{ride_id}/Auto-created when track associated with a ride. Copy of track — original in imported/ remains.
    Hard rule: All tracks stored in mytracks/ folder or subfolders — no exceptions. File picker scans Downloads only, GPX and KML files only. Import copies file — original remains in Downloads.
    04 Vignette Display Rules
    A vignette is a small map thumbnail shown on any card that references spatial data. Used consistently everywhere — import list, ride cards, track library, dashboard invite cards, route list. Tile source: HYB tiles (satellite + labels gives best context).
        PriorityConditionDisplay
          1Track existsTrack line (solid, 2.5px, purple #6B4EFF) over HYB tile background
          2Route existsRoute line (dashed, 2px, orange #F5A623) over HYB tile background
          3Trailhead onlyOrange pin marker centered on trailhead location
          4Bounding box onlyArea rectangle with no line
          5No spatial dataGeneric map grid placeholder
        ContextHeight
          Import list card / Ride card (Dashboard, My Rides)Full card width × 80px
          Track Detail / Route DetailFull card width × 165px
          Ride DetailFull card width × 120px
    05 Layer Panel — Accordion Display
        Accordion pattern — one section open at a time. Type-level toggles only — no individual asset visibility control. No preferences stored — always opens with all types ON, all sections collapsed.
            ToggleDefaultControls
              ⊙ TRAILHEADSONAll trailhead pins in viewport
              ⬛ TRACKSONAll recorded tracks in viewport
              -- ROUTESONAll planned routes in viewport
              ↯ GPX / KMLONAll imported files in viewport
              ⬡ WAYPOINTSOFFAll standard waypoints in viewport
        LAYERS
            ⊙
            TRAILHEADS
            (3)
            ▶
            TRACKS
            (12)
            ▼
            ROUTES
            (4)
              Gooseberry Mesa Loop
              14.2 mi · MODERATE · LOOP
              Hurricane Cliffs
              22.1 mi · HARD · OUT &amp; BACK
            ▶
            GPX / KML
            (2)
            ▶
            WAYPOINTS
            (8 hidden)
    06 Viewport-Driven Display
    Hard rule: Only assets whose geometry intersects the current map viewport are shown — no exceptions. List and map display are always in sync. No asset appears in the list that is not visible in the current viewport.
        Zoom LevelDisplay Rule
          Below z10No assets rendered — layer panel shows "Zoom in to see assets"
          z10 – z13Trailheads only, clustered
          z14 – z16Trailheads + track/route lines simplified, waypoints clustered
          z17 – z18Full detail, all types, all points, labels visible
    07 Layer Z-Order
        1
        Tile base layer (SAT / HYB / TOPO / RD)
        2
        Downloaded area overlay (blue fill)
        3
        AWS available overlay (second color — V3 addition)
        4
        Tracks (solid lines, oldest to newest)
        5
        Routes (dashed lines)
        6
        Waypoints (standard pins)
        7
        Trailheads (always visible, above standard waypoints)
        8
        Active ride route (always on top of asset layers)
        9
        UI overlays (node markers, HUD)
    08 Bounding Box Auto-Calculation
        SourceRule
          Track attached to rideMin bounding box of all track points + 1 mile buffer on each edge
          Route attached to rideMin bounding box of all route points + 1 mile buffer on each edge
          Trailhead only (no track/route)Manual draw — map flies to trailhead, organizer draws rectangle
          No spatial dataManual draw only — same as V2.4 download flow
    Rule: 1 mile buffer on each edge is the recommended default. Organizer can adjust the suggested bounding box before confirming download. Buffer measured from outermost track/route points.
    09 Ride Creation — Hard Gate
    A ride CANNOT be saved without a map boundary. SAVE button is disabled and shows "MAP AREA REQUIRED" until a bounding area exists.
        PrioritySourceResult
          1Attach a trackBounding box auto-calculated from track points + 1 mile buffer
          2Attach a routeBounding box auto-calculated from route points + 1 mile buffer
          3Draw manuallyDraw tool activated — organizer draws rectangle on Planning Map
    10 Download Layer Preferences
    User selects which layers to download. No preferences are mandated — user decides. Default recommendation: HYB only.
        LayerDefaultStorage (relative)Notes
          SATOFFBaseline (1×)Satellite imagery only — no labels
          HYBON~1× (same as SAT)Recommended — satellite + trail/road labels
          TOPOOFF~0.6×Terrain contours — useful for elevation planning
          RDOFF~0.3×Lightest layer — road/POI only
    SAT + HYB together = ~2× storage for same satellite imagery. Users who want both should understand the duplication. At least one layer must remain checked.
    11 RDS Schema
-- tracks
track_id, user_id, ride_id (nullable), name,
difficulty ENUM('EASY','MODERATE','HARD'),
distance_mi FLOAT, file_path VARCHAR(500),
bounds_n DOUBLE, bounds_s DOUBLE, bounds_e DOUBLE, bounds_w DOUBLE,
trailhead_lat DOUBLE, trailhead_lon DOUBLE, created_at
-- routes
route_id, user_id, name,
type ENUM('LOOP','OUT_AND_BACK','POINT_TO_POINT'),
difficulty ENUM('EASY','MODERATE','HARD'),
distance_mi FLOAT, file_path VARCHAR(500),
bounds_n DOUBLE, bounds_s DOUBLE, bounds_e DOUBLE, bounds_w DOUBLE,
trailhead_lat DOUBLE, trailhead_lon DOUBLE, created_at
-- waypoints (includes trailheads via icon_type)
waypoint_id, user_id, ride_id (nullable), name, description,
icon_type ENUM('TRAILHEAD','HAZARD','LANDMARK','MEETING_POINT'),
lat DOUBLE, lon DOUBLE,
parking_available BOOLEAN, facilities TEXT, access_notes TEXT,
created_at
-- rides (additions)
trailhead_lat DOUBLE, trailhead_lon DOUBLE,
route_id INT REFERENCES routes(route_id),
track_id INT REFERENCES tracks(track_id),
bounds_n DOUBLE, bounds_s DOUBLE, bounds_e DOUBLE, bounds_w DOUBLE
    12 Key SQL Queries
    Assets in Viewport
-- Tracks in viewport
SELECT track_id, name, difficulty, distance_mi, file_path,
       trailhead_lat, trailhead_lon
FROM tracks
WHERE bounds_w &lt; :east AND bounds_e &gt; :west
  AND bounds_s &lt; :north AND bounds_n &gt; :south
ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20;
-- Routes in viewport
SELECT route_id, name, type, difficulty, distance_mi, file_path,
       trailhead_lat, trailhead_lon
FROM routes
WHERE bounds_w &lt; :east AND bounds_e &gt; :west
  AND bounds_s &lt; :north AND bounds_n &gt; :south
ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20;
-- Trailheads in viewport
SELECT waypoint_id, name, lat, lon, parking_available, facilities
FROM waypoints
WHERE icon_type = 'TRAILHEAD'
  AND lat BETWEEN :south AND :north
  AND lon BETWEEN :west AND :east;
    Unified Asset Search
SELECT 'track' AS type, track_id AS id, name, distance_mi,
       difficulty, bounds_n, bounds_s, bounds_e, bounds_w,
       trailhead_lat AS lat, trailhead_lon AS lon
FROM tracks WHERE name LIKE :query
UNION
SELECT 'route', route_id, name, distance_mi,
       difficulty, bounds_n, bounds_s, bounds_e, bounds_w,
       trailhead_lat, trailhead_lon
FROM routes WHERE name LIKE :query
UNION
SELECT 'trailhead', waypoint_id, name, 0,
       NULL, lat, lat, lon, lon, lat, lon
FROM waypoints WHERE icon_type = 'TRAILHEAD' AND name LIKE :query
UNION
SELECT 'waypoint', waypoint_id, name, 0,
       NULL, lat, lat, lon, lon, lat, lon
FROM waypoints WHERE icon_type != 'TRAILHEAD' AND name LIKE :query
ORDER BY name;
    Rides Departing from Trailhead
-- 0.004 degrees ≈ 0.25 miles proximity threshold
SELECT r.ride_id, r.name, r.ride_date, r.is_public,
       u.first_name, u.last_name
FROM rides r
JOIN users u ON r.organizer_id = u.user_id
WHERE r.trailhead_lat BETWEEN :lat - 0.004 AND :lat + 0.004
  AND r.trailhead_lon BETWEEN :lon - 0.004 AND :lon + 0.004
  AND r.ride_date >= CURDATE()
ORDER BY r.ride_date ASC;

function toggleLayer(el) {
  const assets = el.parentElement.querySelector('.layer-assets');
  if (assets) assets.classList.toggle('open');
}
// Smooth scroll for nav links
document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(item => {
  item.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
    document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(i => i.classList.remove('active'));
    this.classList.add('active');
  });
});

var ALL_IDS = ["mapmenu_on", "mapmenu_off", "s01", "s01b", "s02", "s03", "s04", "s05", "s06", "s07", "s08", "s09", "s10", "s10b", "s11", "s12", "s13", "s14", "s15", "s16", "s17", "s18", "s19", "s20", "s20b", "s20c", "s21", "s22", "s23", "s24", "s25", "s26", "s27", "s28", "s29", "s30", "s31", "s32", "s33"];
var currentScreen = null;
function toggleFlow(id) {
    var list = document.getElementById(id);
    var isOpen = list.style.display === "block";
    document.querySelectorAll(".fb").forEach(function(b) { b.classList.remove("open"); });
    document.querySelectorAll(".sl").forEach(function(s) { s.style.display = "none"; });
    if (!isOpen) {
        list.previousElementSibling.classList.add("open");
        list.style.display = "block";
    }
}
function gotoScreen(id, flow, title) {
    currentScreen = id;
    document.querySelectorAll(".si").forEach(function(s) { s.classList.remove("active"); });
    document.querySelectorAll(".si").forEach(function(s) {
        var oc = s.getAttribute("onclick") || "";
        if (oc.indexOf("'" + id + "'") >= 0) s.classList.add("active");
    });
    var main = document.getElementById("main");
    main.innerHTML =
        "" + flow + "" + title + "" +
        "";
    buildScreen(id);
    renderNotes(id);
}
function buildScreen(id) {
    var slot = document.getElementById("phone-slot");
    if (!slot) return;
    var fn = SCREENS[id];
    if (fn) slot.innerHTML = "9:41&#9608;&#9608;&#9608; 100%" + fn() + "";
    else slot.innerHTML = "Screen " + id + " — content coming in next pass";
}
function renderNotes(id) {
    var slot = document.getElementById("notes-slot");
    if (!slot) return;
    var d = SD[id] || {a:[], r:[]};
    var ca = []; try { ca = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("ca_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
    var cr = []; try { cr = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cr_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
    var note = ""; try { note = localStorage.getItem("note_" + id) || ""; } catch(e) {}
    var atags = d.a.map(function(f) {
        var sel = ca.indexOf(f) >= 0 ? " sel" : "";
        return "" + f + "";
    }).join("");
    var rtags = d.r.map(function(f) {
        var sel = cr.indexOf(f) >= 0 ? " sel" : "";
        return "" + f + "";
    }).join("");
    slot.innerHTML =
        "" +
        "&#10003; FUNCTIONS ACTIVE &mdash; click to confirm / mark changed" + atags + "" +
        "&#9675; RELATED NOT USED &mdash; click to select for this screen" + rtags + "" +
        "&#9998; SCREEN NOTES &amp; ADJUSTMENT REQUESTS" +
        "" + note + "" +
        "";
}
function toggleTag(id, type, fn) {
    var key = (type === "a" ? "ca_" : "cr_") + id;
    var arr = []; try { arr = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
    var idx = arr.indexOf(fn);
    if (idx >= 0) arr.splice(idx, 1); else arr.push(fn);
    try { localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(arr)); } catch(e) {}
    renderNotes(id);
}
function saveNote(id) {
    try { var el = document.getElementById("note_" + id); if (el) localStorage.setItem("note_" + id, el.value); } catch(e) {}
}
function copyEmail(email) {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(email).catch(function() {});
    var els = document.querySelectorAll(".email-copy");
    els.forEach(function(el) { if (el.textContent.indexOf(email) >= 0) { el.style.background = "rgba(0,170,68,0.3)"; setTimeout(function() { el.style.background = ""; }, 1200); } });
}
function openExport() {
    var lines = ["GROUPTRACK V3.0 PROTOTYPE REVIEW — " + new Date().toLocaleString(), "=".repeat(55), ""];
    var hasData = false;
    ALL_IDS.forEach(function(id) {
        var note = ""; try { note = localStorage.getItem("note_" + id) || ""; } catch(e) {}
        var ca = []; try { ca = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("ca_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
        var cr = []; try { cr = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cr_" + id) || "[]"); } catch(e) {}
        if (note || ca.length || cr.length) {
            hasData = true;
            lines.push("SCREEN: " + id.toUpperCase());
            if (ca.length) lines.push("  CONFIRMED ACTIVE: " + ca.join(", "));
            if (cr.length) lines.push("  SELECTED FROM RELATED: " + cr.join(", "));
            if (note) lines.push("  NOTES: " + note.trim());
            lines.push("");
        }
    });
    if (!hasData) lines.push("No selections or notes yet.\n\nClick GREEN tags to confirm functions.\nClick GREY tags to add related functions.\nType in notes field.\nThen export and paste to Claude.");
    document.getElementById("export-out").textContent = lines.join("\n");
    document.getElementById("export-modal").classList.add("open");
}
function closeExport() { document.getElementById("export-modal").classList.remove("open"); }
function copyExport() {
    var txt = document.getElementById("export-out").textContent;
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(txt).then(function() {
        var b = document.getElementById("copy-btn");
        b.textContent = "COPIED!"; setTimeout(function() { b.textContent = "COPY ALL"; }, 2000);
    }).catch(function() { document.execCommand("copy"); });
}
function tA(h) {
    var b = h.nextElementSibling, a = h.querySelector("span:last-child");
    if (b.classList.contains("open")) { b.classList.remove("open"); b.style.display = "none"; a.textContent = "▶"; }
    else { b.classList.add("open"); b.style.display = "block"; a.textContent = "▼"; }
}
function bnav(active) {
    var items = [["HOME","&#x1F3E0;","s04","Dashboard"],["RIDES","&#x1F690;","s09","My Rides"],["MAP","&#x1F5FA;","s16","Map - SOLO"],["PROFILE","&#x1F464;","s05","Profile"]];
    return "" + items.map(function(x) {
        return "" +
               "" + x[1] + "" + x[0] + "";
    }).join("") + "";
}
function emailBlock(name, email, phone) {
    var ph = phone ? "&#128222; " + phone + "" : "";
    return "" +
        "" + name + "" +
        "" +
        "&#128203;" + email + "" + ph + "";
}

const SCREENS = 29;
const TITLES = {
  1:'SIGN IN',2:'RIDER TERMS',3:'PRIVACY POLICY',
  4:'DASHBOARD',
  5:'PROFILE',6:'BECOME ORGANIZER',7:'FIELD RADIO',
  8:'MAP SOLO',9:'MAP SETTINGS',10:'MAP CONVOY',11:'MAP ORGANIZED',12:'STOP SURVEY',
  13:'MY RIDES',14:'EXPLORE',15:'CREATE RIDE',16:'RIDE DETAIL',17:'SEND INVITE',18:'BROADCAST',19:'FOLLOWING',20:'INVITE ACCEPT',
  21:'MAP MANAGER',22:'FIND AREA',23:'SET TRAILHEAD',24:'SET MAP AREA',25:'TILE DOWNLOAD',26:'IMPORT ROUTE',27:'OVERLAY SELECTOR',28:'WAYPOINTS',29:'CREATE WAYPOINT'
};
const SECTIONS = {
  1:'A',2:'A',3:'A',
  4:'B',
  5:'C',6:'C',7:'C',
  8:'D',9:'D',10:'D',11:'D',12:'D',
  13:'E',14:'E',15:'E',16:'E',17:'E',18:'E',19:'E',20:'E',
  21:'F',22:'F',23:'F',24:'F',25:'F',26:'F',27:'F',28:'F',29:'F'
};
const SECTION_NAMES = {A:'ONBOARDING',B:'DASHBOARD',C:'ACCOUNT',D:'RIDE MAP',E:'RIDES',F:'MAP MANAGER'};
let current = 1;
function buildSidebar() {
  const sb = document.getElementById('sidebar');
  let lastSec = '';
  for(let i=1;i<=SCREENS;i++){
    const sec = SECTIONS[i];
    if(sec !== lastSec){
      const div = document.createElement('div');
      div.style.cssText='width:36px;font-family:Share Tech Mono,monospace;font-size:8px;color:#F5A623;text-align:center;padding:2px 0;border-top:1px solid rgba(245,166,35,0.3);margin-top:4px;';
      div.textContent=sec;
      sb.appendChild(div);
      lastSec=sec;
    }
    const d = document.createElement('div');
    d.className='sdot'+(i===1?' active':'');
    d.textContent=i;
    d.title=TITLES[i];
    d.onclick=()=>goTo(i);
    sb.appendChild(d);
  }
}
function goTo(n) {
  if(typeof n === 'string') n = parseInt(n);
  if(nSCREENS) return;
  document.getElementById('screen-'+current)?.classList.remove('active');
  document.querySelectorAll('.sdot')[current-1]?.classList.remove('active');
  current=n;
  document.getElementById('screen-'+current)?.classList.add('active');
  document.querySelectorAll('.sdot')[current-1]?.classList.add('active');
  const sec = SECTIONS[current];
  document.getElementById('screenInfo').textContent=
    'SCREEN '+current+' OF '+SCREENS+' — '+SECTION_NAMES[sec]+' — '+TITLES[current];
  window.scrollTo(0,0);
}
function nextScreen(){goTo(current+1);}
function prevScreen(){goTo(current-1);}
function toggleAcc(header){
  const body=header.nextElementSibling;
  const arrow=header.querySelector('.acc-arrow');
  if(body.classList.contains('open')){
    body.classList.remove('open');
    body.style.display='none';
    arrow.textContent='▶';
  } else {
    body.classList.add('open');
    body.style.display='block';
    arrow.textContent='▼';
  }
}
document.addEventListener('keydown',e=>{
  if(e.key==='ArrowRight')nextScreen();
  if(e.key==='ArrowLeft')prevScreen();
});
buildSidebar();

    GroupTrack
    Do You Know WhereYour Riders Are?
    OFF-GRID &nbsp;|&nbsp; MESH RADIO &nbsp;|&nbsp; NO CELL REQUIRED
      Learn More
      Join Beta
    Our Mission
    Convoy Coordination.Without the Network.
    GroupTrack keeps your group connected when cell service disappears. Built on Meshtastic&#8217;s low-power LoRa mesh radio technology, every rider in your convoy can see every other rider&#8217;s position in real time &#8212; no towers, no data plan, no excuses.
        Whether you&#8217;re leading a UTV convoy through the canyon country of southern Utah, coordinating a group trail ride in the backcountry, or managing search and rescue operations in a dead zone &#8212; GroupTrack gives your group the situational awareness it needs to stay safe, stay together, and stay on track.
        Pre-download your maps. Configure your radios. Head out. GroupTrack does the rest.
          &#128247;
            Real-Time Position
            See every rider on a live map. Updated every few seconds over the mesh.
          &#128225;
            No Cell Required
            Runs entirely on LoRa mesh radio. Works 10+ miles from the nearest tower.
          &#127757;
            Offline Maps
            Pre-download your riding area before you leave. Full map tiles stored on device.
          &#128274;
            Encrypted Mesh
            Private channel with PSK encryption. Only your group sees your group.
    What It Does
    Built for the Trail.
    Every feature in GroupTrack was designed for real-world off-grid use &#8212; by riders, for riders.
        &#128205;
        Live Convoy Map
        See your entire group on an interactive map in real time. Color-coded by rider position in the convoy. Never lose track of who&#8217;s ahead or behind.
        &#127760;
        Offline Map Downloads
        Search for your trail area, draw your download zone, and cache map tiles before you leave. Satellite, topo, hybrid, and road layers all work offline.
        &#128267;
        Mesh Radio Network
        Powered by Meshtastic LoRa radio. Each device acts as a relay, extending range across the entire convoy automatically.
        &#128196;
        Ride Management
        Organizers create rides, set radio configs, and invite riders with a single link. Riders tap the link, download the ride, and go. Zero technical setup required.
        &#127981;
        GPS Track Recording
        Record your ride track with one tap. Pause, resume, and save. Export as KML for Google Earth or share with the group after the ride.
        &#9889;
        One-Boot Radio Config
        Set channel, frequency, PSK, and device settings from the app. Apply with one tap. Radio reboots configured and ready to mesh in under 60 seconds.
    Development Status
    Where We Are Right Now.
        V2.4 — Beta
        GroupTrack V2.4 is live and in the hands of authorized beta testers. The core feature set is proven &#8212; offline maps, live convoy tracking, one-boot radio configuration, and GPS track recording all working on Android in the field.V3.0 brings the full ride management platform including Google Sign-In, cloud-based ride creation, and invite link distribution.
        Coming in V3.0

          Cloud Ride LibrarySave and share favorite routes and configs

          Organization AccountsClub and outfitter management tools

Workplan &mdash; 2026-07-27Order of work &middot; read with grouptrack_living_master_2026-07-26.html and grouptrack_handoff_2026-07-26.html
Sequenced so each step is independently verifiable and nothing blocks on a decision that has not been made. Steps 0&ndash;2 are cheap and unblock everything else; step 3 is the day's build.
0 &middot; Post fresh xrefs (first thing)
15 min Today added ConvoyDeleteWorker, deleteTileRange/countTileRange/storeExists/reclaimableBytes, enqueueDelete/submitDelete, and changed launchWorker. Yesterday's xref index cannot know about any of it, and tomorrow's work is squarely in trail ingestion &mdash; blast-radius analysis against a stale index would miss exactly the new code.
&#9888; Standing caveat: the xrefs index DECLARATIONS, not call sites. Lambda parameters (e.g. onDownloadCorridor) appear in none of them &mdash; same class as the earlier @JavascriptInterface miss. xref for candidates, grep for call sites.
1 &middot; The markComplete refreshMode collision &mdash; ONE LINE, highest value
DO THIS BEFORE THE ETA WORK ConvoyDownloadQueue:549 branches on entry.refreshMode and silently removes the entry from the queue. But enqueueArea and enqueueCorridor both set refreshMode = replaceExisting.
So any download submitted with REPLACE ticked is deleted on completion instead of marked COMPLETE &mdash; no completion row, no completedAt stamp, no ETA sample. Fix: branch on downloadType == MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH.
Why first: it is one line, it plausibly explains BOTH the refresh-never-completes report AND a large share of the ETA being 50&times; long, and any ETA measurement taken before this fix is untrustworthy. Give it its own patch so its verification is not tangled with anything else.
2 &middot; Settle SAT-frozen-at-15 &mdash; one download, no code
GATES PROMOTION PAST THE INTERNAL TRACK Run the same track's corridor with REPLACE TICKED. Replace bypasses the hasTile pre-fetch filter, so SAT must derive and fetch its full corridor.
SAT returns in the thousands &rarr; the filter was working, 15 was honest remaining work, nothing is broken.
SAT returns 15 again &rarr; SAT corridor derivation/fetch is broken, and the &asymp;90% headline measures what was QUEUED, not what LANDED. Testers would be getting corridor downloads with no satellite imagery.
Costs one download and no code. It is the only open defect that changes what a tester actually receives.
3 &middot; OSM trail import &mdash; the day's build
Full design is in the Living Master. Do it in this order &mdash; each step is verifiable before the next.
Validate the field mapping off-device first. osm_trails_extract_2026-07-26.py --bbox -113.70,37.00,-113.40,37.25 (add --insecure if the cert bundle is still stale, or pip install --upgrade certifi). Read the ATTRIBUTE COVERAGE table &mdash; the MotorizedAllowed percentage decides whether OSM is a genuine second attribute source or just geometry that extends snap reach. Both are useful; they are different arguments. ⚠ This script is a VALIDATION TOOL, never the user path.
Load the output into grouptrack_display_model.html alongside the UGRC subset (geojson_subset_2026-07-26.py cuts the 22MB file to something the browser can hold). Confirm at z15+ that coexistence looks the way it did today.
Then write the patch: (a) source_type in trail_sources.json; (b) buildUrl branches on it; (c) response transform branches on it &mdash; elements[] &rarr; FeatureCollection with mapped property names, OSM semantics live HERE so insertFeature stays untouched; (d) catalog entry #9.
Verify on device: Method B &rarr; pick a small area &rarr; import. Check source_ingestions for the run, and that OSM trails render cyan "Unspecified" (blank carto_code) distinct from UGRC.
&#9888; Traps, both fatal if missed: PAGING &mdash; Overpass does not page; a response of &ge; max_records loops forever re-fetching the same page. Treat Overpass as single-page or chunk the bbox. file:// &mdash; httpGet casts to HttpURLConnection and will throw; a local-file source is impossible without touching that method.
&#9888; Do not guess motorized access. highway=track with no access tag &rarr; leave motorized_allowed BLANK. A track is wide enough for a vehicle by definition, but that is physical capability, not legal access &mdash; and legal access is the whole purpose of that column.
4 &middot; If time remains
ETA startedAt &mdash; only meaningful AFTER step 1. Three timestamps per entry: submit (createdAt, exists), start-execution (startedAt, MISSING), finish (completedAt, exists). Stamp in DownloadQueueManager where status goes active, not in each worker &mdash; three workers now, and per-worker duplication is what produced the refresh bug. Re-stamp on resume, and stamp tilesAtStart alongside or the rate comes out too fast. Sampling policy still needs Fred's call.
Rotation clears selections &mdash; remember &rarr; rememberSaveable in ConvoyDownloadConfirm. Small, and it removes the last reason to rotate.
COTREX misconfiguration &mdash; "type": "feature_id", "use": "place_id" are filling carto_code with record IDs. Catalog-only fix.
Identify the three "Find closest point on line" sites in grouptrack_map.html (:39, :89, :827). Authoritative snap is Kotlin, so these are probably display helpers &mdash; but confirm before any renderer work.
&#9940; NOT tomorrow
V2.7 vector rendering &mdash; scoped, parked. It earns its place only inside the convoy tracking rewrite, and only after the open defects are closed.
VACUUM / space reclamation &mdash; blocked until the "0 MB reclaimable" reading is explained.
Manual updates &mdash; the queue sections are current; SAVE MAPS remains deliberately undocumented (Fred: it is one button).

    Do You Know WhereYour Riders Are?
    OFF-GRID &nbsp;|&nbsp; MESH RADIO &nbsp;|&nbsp; NO CELL REQUIRED
      Learn More
      Join Beta
    Our Mission
    Convoy Coordination.Without the Network.
    GroupTrack keeps your group connected when cell service disappears. Built on Meshtastic&#8217;s low-power LoRa mesh radio technology, every rider in your convoy can see every other rider&#8217;s position in real time &#8212; no towers, no data plan, no excuses.
        Whether you&#8217;re leading a UTV convoy through the canyon country of southern Utah, coordinating a group trail ride in the backcountry, or managing search and rescue operations in a dead zone &#8212; GroupTrack gives your group the situational awareness it needs to stay safe, stay together, and stay on track.
        Pre-download your maps. Configure your radios. Head out. GroupTrack does the rest.
        &#128247;Real-Time PositionSee every rider on a live map. Updated every few seconds over the mesh.
        &#128225;No Cell RequiredRadio-to-radio transmission up to 10 miles per hop. Each device automatically relays for others &#8212; the more riders in your convoy, the greater your range.
        &#127757;Offline MapsPre-download your riding area before you leave. Full map tiles stored on device. Works with zero connectivity in the field.
        &#128274;Encrypted MeshPrivate channel with PSK encryption. Only your group sees your group.
    What It Does
    Built for the Trail.
    Every feature in GroupTrack was designed for real-world off-grid use &#8212; by riders, for riders.
      &#128205;Live Convoy MapSee your entire group on an interactive map in real time. Color-coded by rider position in the convoy. Never lose track of who&#8217;s ahead or behind.
      &#127760;Offline Map DownloadsSearch for your trail area, draw your download zone, and cache map tiles before you leave. Satellite, topo, hybrid, and road layers all work offline.
      &#128267;Self-Extending MeshPowered by Meshtastic LoRa radio. Each device transmits up to 10 miles and automatically relays for other nodes. The more riders you have, the farther your network reaches.
      &#128196;Ride ManagementOrganizers create rides, set radio configs, and invite riders with a single link. Riders tap the link, download the ride, and go. Zero technical setup required.
      &#127981;GPS Track RecordingRecord your ride track with one tap. Pause, resume, and save. Export as KML for Google Earth or share with the group after the ride.
      &#9889;One-Boot Radio ConfigSet channel, frequency, PSK, and device settings from the app. Apply with one tap. Radio reboots configured and ready to mesh in under 60 seconds.
