    Frequently Asked Questions
    Got Questions?
    Everything you need to know about GroupTrack before heading out on the trail.
        Do I need a cell signal to use GroupTrack? &#9660;
        No &#8212; GroupTrack works entirely over LoRa mesh radio. There is no cellular or internet requirement in the field. Each rider&#8217;s Meshtastic radio communicates directly with nearby radios, and each radio automatically relays signals for others in the mesh. You do need an internet connection to initially download the app and pre-download your offline map tiles before the ride.
        What hardware do I need? &#9660;
        Each rider needs an Android device (tablet recommended for map visibility) and a Meshtastic-compatible LoRa radio. The SenseCAP T1000-E is our recommended radio &#8212; compact, weatherproof, and long battery life. Any Meshtastic device running firmware 2.6 or later will work. The radio pairs to the Android device via Bluetooth.
        How far does the radio signal reach? &#9660;
        Each radio transmits up to 10 miles per hop in open terrain. Because every device in the mesh automatically relays signals for others, the effective range of your convoy network grows with every rider you add. A 10-vehicle convoy can maintain connectivity across distances far greater than any single radio hop.
        How do offline maps work? &#9660;
        Before your ride, search for your trail area in the app, draw a rectangle over the zone you want to cache, and tap Download. The app downloads map tiles for that area at all zoom levels and stores them on your device. Once downloaded, the map works with WiFi and cell completely off. Satellite, topographic, hybrid, and road map layers are all supported.
        How do I get GroupTrack? &#9660;
        GroupTrack V2.4 is currently in authorized beta testing on Android. Contact us at [email&#160;protected] to request access. The organizer will send you the APK file and installation instructions. A Google Play Store release and iOS version are planned for V3.0.
        Is my location data private? &#9660;
        Yes. GroupTrack uses encrypted LoRa channels with a private pre-shared key (PSK). Only devices configured with the same channel name and PSK can see your position. No data is sent to any server during a ride &#8212; everything stays on the local mesh network between your group&#8217;s radios.
    Development Status
    Where We Are Right Now.
        V2.4 &#8212; Beta
        GroupTrack V2.4 is live and in the hands of authorized beta testers. The core feature set is proven &#8212; offline maps, live convoy tracking, one-boot radio configuration, and GPS track recording all working on Android in the field.V3.0 brings the full ride management platform including Google Sign-In, cloud-based ride creation, and invite link distribution.
        Coming in V3.0
          Automated Map DownloadsEnroll in a ride and the app automatically downloads the map tiles for your trail area. No manual selection &#8212; just accept the invite and go.

Because every device in the mesh automatically relays signals for others, the effective range of your convoy network grows with every rider you add. A 10-vehicle convoy can maintain connectivity across distances far greater than any single radio hop.
        How do offline maps work? &#9660;
        Before your ride, search for your trail area in the app, draw a rectangle over the zone you want to cache, and tap Download. The app downloads map tiles for that area at all zoom levels and stores them on your device. Once downloaded, the map works with WiFi and cell completely off. Satellite, topographic, hybrid, and road map layers are all supported.
        How do I get GroupTrack? &#9660;
        GroupTrack V2.4 is currently in authorized beta testing on Android. Contact us at kixazz25@gmail.com to request access. The organizer will send you the APK file and installation instructions. A Google Play Store release and iOS version are planned for V3.0.
        Is my location data private? &#9660;
        Yes. GroupTrack uses encrypted LoRa channels with a private pre-shared key (PSK). Only devices configured with the same channel name and PSK can see your position. No data is sent to any server during a ride &#8212; everything stays on the local mesh network between your group&#8217;s radios.
    Development Status
    Where We Are Right Now.

The core feature set is proven &#8212; offline maps, live convoy tracking, one-boot radio configuration, and GPS track recording all working on Android in the field.V3.0 brings the full ride management platform including Google Sign-In, cloud-based ride creation, and invite link distribution.

function toggleFaq(btn) {
  var item = btn.parentElement;
  var isOpen = item.classList.contains('open');
  document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(function(el){ el.classList.remove('open'); });
  if (!isOpen) item.classList.add('open');
}

];

const me = NODES.find(n => n.mine);
const map = L.map('map', {
  center: [me.lat, me.lng],
  zoom: 14,
  zoomControl: true,
  attributionControl: false,
}).on('click', () => {}); // prevent any click bubbling issues
// OSM tiles — will swap for MapLibre offline tiles in production
L.tileLayer('https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
  maxZoom: 19,
}).addTo(map);
// ─── CONVOY TRACK polyline ──────────────────────────────
// Multi-colored segments: each segment = color of rear node of that segment
const trackCoords = NODES.map(n => [n.lat, n.lng]);
// Draw as individual colored segments
for (let i = 0; i < NODES.length - 1; i++) {
  L.polyline(
    [[NODES[i].lat, NODES[i].lng], [NODES[i+1].lat, NODES[i+1].lng]],
    { color: NODES[i+1].color, weight: 5, opacity: 0.85, lineCap: 'round' }
  ).addTo(map);
}
// ─── NODE MARKERS ───────────────────────────────────────
NODES.forEach(node => {
  const size  = node.mine ? 18 : 12;
  const pulse = node.mine ? 'marker-mine' : '';
  const opacity = node.lost ? 0.35 : 1;
  const icon = L.divIcon({
    className: '',
    html: `<div class="${pulse}" style="
      width:${size}px; height:${size}px;
      border-radius:50%;
      background:${node.color};
      border:2px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.6);
      opacity:${opacity};
    ">`,
    iconSize: [size, size],
    iconAnchor: [size/2, size/2],
  });
  const marker = L.marker([node.lat, node.lng], { icon }).addTo(map);
  marker.bindTooltip(node.id, {
    permanent: false,
    direction: 'top',
    className: 'leaflet-tooltip',
    offset: [0, -8],
  });
});

function toggleHide() {
  hudHidden = !hudHidden;
  document.getElementById('hudOverlay').classList.toggle('hidden', hudHidden);
  document.getElementById('btnHide').classList.toggle('hud-off', hudHidden);
  document.getElementById('hideLabel').textContent = hudHidden ? 'Show' : 'Hide';
  document.getElementById('eyePath').setAttribute('d', hudHidden ? EYE_OFF : EYE_OPEN);
}
function flashGear() {
  const b = document.getElementById('btnGear');
  b.classList.add('active');
  setTimeout(() => b.classList.remove('active'), 250);
}

function showPanel(id){['panelGroup','panelMyCart','panelSelected'].forEach(p=>{document.getElementById(p).style.display=p===id?'block':'none';});}
function selectCart(node){
  document.getElementById('selName').textContent=node.id;
  document.getElementById('selName').style.color=node.color;
  document.getElementById('selHdg').textContent=node.hdg||'—';
  document.getElementById('selBat').textContent=node.bat||'—';
  document.getElementById('selAlt').textContent=node.alt||'—';
  document.getElementById('selSpd').firstChild.textContent=node.lost?'—':(node.spd||'—');
  document.getElementById('selToLead').textContent=node.toLead||'—';
  document.getElementById('selToTail').textContent=node.toTail||'—';
  document.getElementById('selGapAhead').textContent=node.gapAhead||'—';
  document.getElementById('selGapBehind').textContent=node.gapBehind||'—';
  showPanel('panelSelected');
  document.getElementById('btnGroup').classList.remove('active');
  document.getElementById('btnMyCart').classList.add('active');
  map.setView([node.lat,node.lng],15,{animate:true});
}
function setView(v){
  document.getElementById('btnGroup').classList.toggle('active',v==='group');
  document.getElementById('btnMyCart').classList.toggle('active',v==='mycart');
  showPanel(v==='group'?'panelGroup':'panelMyCart');
  if(v==='group')map.fitBounds(L.latLngBounds(NODES.map(n=>[n.lat,n.lng])),{paddingTopLeft:[20,60],paddingBottomRight:[20,80]});
  else if(v==='mycart'){if(navigator.geolocation)navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(p=>map.setView([p.coords.latitude,p.coords.longitude],15,{animate:true}),()=>map.setView([me.lat,me.lng],15,{animate:true}));else map.setView([me.lat,me.lng],15,{animate:true});}
}

  GroupTrack Privacy Policy
  Off-Grid Group Awareness Platform
  Effective Date: April 29, 2026
  1. Who We Are
  GroupTrack is a mobile application for off-grid group coordination. It enables real-time position awareness over LoRa mesh radio, organized ride management, and offline map navigation for outdoor activities including off-road driving, hiking, mountain biking, overlanding, and search and rescue.
  This privacy policy explains what information GroupTrack collects, how it is used, and how it is shared. It applies to the GroupTrack Android application and the GroupTrack website at grouptrack.org.
  2. Information We Collect
  Account Information. When you sign in with Google, we receive your name, email address, and Google account identifier. This information is stored on our servers to create and manage your GroupTrack account.
  Location Data. GroupTrack uses your device's GPS to display your position on the map, record tracks, and share your location with other riders in your convoy via mesh radio. GPS data is processed on your device and transmitted directly between radios — it does not pass through our servers during a ride. Recorded GPS tracks are stored locally on your device. If you choose to donate a track after an organized ride, that track file is uploaded to our servers.
  Ride and Enrollment Data. When you create a ride, enroll in a ride, accept an invite, or follow an organizer, those actions are recorded on our servers to coordinate ride logistics between participants.
  Device Information. We collect basic device information for app functionality and crash reporting, including device model, Android version, and app version. This is handled through Google Firebase Crashlytics.
  Map Tile Downloads. When you download offline map tiles, requests are sent to third-party tile providers (such as Esri). These requests include the geographic coordinates of the area you are downloading. GroupTrack does not control the privacy practices of these tile providers.
  3. How We Use Your Information
  We use the information we collect to:
    Create and manage your account
    Coordinate ride logistics — invitations, enrollments, and ride details between organizers and riders
    Display your position on the convoy map during group activities
    Record and store GPS tracks on your device
    Diagnose crashes and improve app stability
    Send ride-related notifications and organizer broadcasts (if you have opted in)
  We do not use your information for advertising. We do not sell your information to third parties.
  4. How We Share Your Information
  With Ride Organizers. When you follow an organizer or enroll in a ride, your name and email address are visible to the ride organizer. This enables the organizer to communicate with participants about ride logistics.
  With Other Riders. During an active ride, your GPS position is shared with other riders in your convoy via mesh radio. This sharing happens directly between devices over radio — it does not pass through our servers.
  With Service Providers. We use Amazon Web Services (AWS) to host our backend infrastructure and Google Firebase for crash reporting. These providers process data on our behalf under their respective privacy policies.
  Track Donations. If you choose to donate a GPS track after an organized ride, that track becomes available in the community track library for other users to download. Track donations are always optional and require your explicit consent.
  We do not share your information with advertisers or data brokers.
  5. Data Storage and Security
  Account and ride data are stored on servers hosted by Amazon Web Services in the United States (us-east-1 region). GPS tracks and offline map tiles are stored locally on your device.
  We use industry-standard security practices including encrypted connections (HTTPS/SSL), database access controls, and secure authentication via Google Sign-In. However, no method of electronic storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.
  6. Your Choices
  Offline Use. You can use GroupTrack's offline features — map tile download, radio configuration, GPS track recording, and GPX/KML file import — without signing in or creating an account. No personal information is collected in offline-only mode.
  Track Donations. Sharing your GPS track with the community is always optional. You choose whether to donate a track at the end of each organized ride.
  Account Deletion. You may request deletion of your account and associated data by contacting us at support@grouptrack.org.
  Email Communications. You can opt out of organizer broadcast emails through your profile settings.
  7. Children's Privacy
  GroupTrack is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child under 13 has provided us with personal information, please contact us and we will delete that information.
  8. Changes to This Policy
  We may update this privacy policy from time to time. The app will prompt you to review and accept the updated policy on your next launch after any changes. The effective date at the top of this page indicates the most recent revision.
  9. Contact
  If you have questions about this privacy policy or your data, contact us at:
  support@grouptrack.org
  GroupTrack
  grouptrack.org
  &copy; 2026 GroupTrack. All rights reserved.

GroupTrack
Version 2.5 Release Notes — What&rsquo;s New
Field Test Release &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; Map Feature Update &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; updated 2026-06-02
About this release
V2.5 completes the free map product: trail and trailhead data you can download straight onto your maps, plus a single, consistent way to show and hide Trails, Tracks, Waypoints, and Routes on both the Convoy Map and the Planning Map. This is a FIELD TEST build — known rough edges are listed at the end.
New in this build (2026-06-02): Track import fixed for large files
  Big GPX files import without crashing. Large onX &ldquo;markups&rdquo; exports (25MB+, dozens of tracks) used to crash the app during import — that&rsquo;s fixed. You can import your full track collection in one pass.
  Much faster. Large tracks that took minutes each now take seconds.
  Import summary. After an import you see &ldquo;X new / Y already in library&rdquo; — how many tracks were actually added versus already on your device.
  Safe to re-import. Tracks already saved are recognized by their shape and skipped — re-importing the same file does not create duplicates.
  Limitation this build: importing a GPX brings in its tracks only. Any waypoints or routes in the file are skipped for now (a separate import feature is coming). Dropping waypoints on the map yourself still works.
Headline: Import Utah Trails onto your map
The trail source catalog lets you pull a full set of Utah trails and trailhead waypoints directly onto your maps as artifacts — no files to copy, and no internet needed once they&rsquo;re down.
How to import UGRC Utah Trails:
  Open Work with Artifacts (accordion button).
  Select Import Trails. The trail source list displays.
  Select UGRC Utah Trails.
  Tap Validate/Confirm. Trails and trailhead waypoints download as artifacts.
  Fully close the app, force close, then reopen. Imported trails and trailheads now appear.
If imported trails don&rsquo;t show: (1) Fully close and reopen (or Force Stop) so trail data loads. (2) Zoom in — about 49,000 trails only draw at close zoom (see Known Issues).
What else is new
  Trail source catalog — browse and import. UGRC Utah Trails first (~49,000 trails + 591 trailheads). BLM/USFS planned.
  One consistent artifact display — Trails/Tracks/Waypoints/Routes show and hide the same way on both maps.
  Independent map selections — the Convoy and Planning maps each keep their own selections, saved across restarts.
  SELECTED shows exactly what you pick — draws only the items you checked, consistent on both maps.
  Drop waypoints on the map — long-press empty ground for a 12-type picker plus an optional name. (Works on the Planning Map; Convoy Map waypoint drop is in progress — see Known Issues.)
  Work with Artifacts panel — accordion; per-type OFF / ON / SELECTED plus an item list.
  Default on launch — Trails ON, others OFF.
  RESYNC TRACKS — rebuilds the track list from your saved GPX files, and adds any track on the device that isn&rsquo;t yet in the database.
  Zoom readout — the compass shows the zoom level (N &middot; Z##).
  Standalone GPS / offline maps — carried from V2.4.
Requirements
Android 8.0+ (tablet recommended). Auto-update via the Play Store internal track. 500MB+ free for tiles (trail data ~15–30MB per state). Meshtastic SenseCAP T1000-E or LoRa firmware 2.6+ (for convoy only, not maps). Internet needed once to import/download.
Known issues — please read
  Trails not visible zoomed far out — expected; zoom in.
  Item list sometimes shows no names — known; being addressed.
  Item list shows up to 200 entries — paging is coming in a later build.
  After a track import, the artifact list may not refresh until you leave the screen and return. (Tracks appear on the map right away.)
  Convoy Map: QUEUES button and waypoint long-press are not working yet — both work on the Planning Map; convoy parity is in progress.
  Tracks missing after an update — RESYNC TRACKS rebuilds.
Resolved since last build
  Track re-import no longer duplicates. The earlier &ldquo;don&rsquo;t import the same tracks repeatedly&rdquo; warning is fixed for tracks — they&rsquo;re de-duplicated by shape, so re-importing skips ones already present. (Trail-source re-import dedupe is still rolling out — import UGRC once.)
  Large track files no longer crash the import.
  Map selections are independent per map and saved.
Troubleshooting
  Imported trails don&rsquo;t appear &rarr; zoom in; confirm the import finished.
  Imported tracks don&rsquo;t appear in the list &rarr; leave the screen and return; they&rsquo;re already on the map.
  A big track file used to crash &rarr; fixed in this build; if any import still stalls, note the file size and track count and report it.
  No vehicles (convoy) &rarr; is the radio connected (green)? Same channel and PSK?
  Tiles blank offline &rarr; download tiles while online first.
  Tiles not loading online &rarr; check your internet.
  A track is missing &rarr; RESYNC TRACKS.
  Anything else &rarr; report it (note what you tapped and what you expected).

  ESRI RASTER + OSM VECTOR LABELS
  Toggle Esri's raster labels against OSM vector labels over the same imagery. Compare coverage before committing.
    BASE IMAGERY
    Esri World Imagery (raster)
    ESRI LABELS — RASTER, WHAT YOU DOWNLOAD NOW
    Boundaries &amp; Places
    Transportation
    3D TERRAIN — LEAFLET CANNOT DO THIS AT ALL
    elevation (drape imagery on terrain)
    hillshade
    exaggeration
      Tilt with ctrl + drag (or two fingers). Elevation is a separate
      DEM source — it does not come from the imagery.
    YOUR DATA — GEOJSON FROM THE SPATIAL DB
    tracks / routes / trails
    their names
      Export GeoJSON from grouptrack.gpkg and drop it here.
    OSM LABELS — VECTOR, THE ALTERNATIVE
    place — settlements
    transportation_name — roads
    mountain_peak
    water_name
    poi
    tracks &amp; paths (geometry)
move the map — zoom/centre shown here
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Esri raster tiles use {z}/{y}/{x} order (row before column) — NOT the usual
// {z}/{x}/{y}. Getting this backwards yields a map that looks plausible but is
// transposed. Same raw z/x/y convention MBTilesStore uses; no TMS flip.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
const ESRI = 'https://services.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services';
const r = (p) => [`${ESRI}/${p}/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}`];
// OpenFreeMap serves the OpenMapTiles schema with no key required — same layer
// names you would get from a self-hosted Planetiler build, so a style written
// here carries over to your own tiles unchanged.
const OMT = 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet';
const style = {
  version: 8,
  glyphs: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf',
  sources: {
    sat:       { type:'raster', tiles:r('World_Imagery'), tileSize:256, maxzoom:19,
                 attribution:'Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics' },
    esriRef:   { type:'raster', tiles:r('Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places'), tileSize:256, maxzoom:19 },
    esriTrans: { type:'raster', tiles:r('Reference/World_Transportation'), tileSize:256, maxzoom:19 },
    omt:       { type:'vector', url:`${OMT}/tiles.json`, attribution:'© OpenStreetMap contributors' },
    // YOUR SPATIAL DB. Identical to what spatial_artifacts.js already builds -
    // wktToGeoJsonCoords output, unchanged. MapLibre takes GeoJSON natively,
    // exactly as Leaflet does, so the data path from SpatialDbManager does not
    // change at all. Only the RENDERING call differs.
    mine:      { type:'geojson', data:{ type:'FeatureCollection', features:[] } },
    // ELEVATION. Public AWS terrain tiles, terrarium encoding, no key needed.
    // These encode metres-above-sea-level in the RGB channels rather than a
    // pre-rendered grey hillshade - so the CLIENT computes relief, and the same
    // tiles can drive elevation lookup, slope shading or a viewshed. Capped at
    // z13: terrain shape does not need the zoom depth imagery does, which is
    // why a DEM for a whole state is small.
    dem:       { type:'raster-dem',
                 tiles:['https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png'],
                 encoding:'terrarium', tileSize:256, maxzoom:13,
                 attribution:'Terrain: Mapzen / AWS Open Data' }
  },
  layers: [
    { id:'bg', type:'background', paint:{ 'background-color':'#0a0e14' } },
    // NOTE: no 'sky' layer. type:'sky' is MapLibre v5+; on v4 it is an unknown
    // layer type and the WHOLE style is rejected -> blank canvas.
    { id:'sat', type:'raster', source:'sat' },
    { id:'shade', type:'hillshade', source:'dem', layout:{visibility:'none'},
      paint:{ 'hillshade-exaggeration':0.5, 'hillshade-shadow-color':'#000000' } },
    { id:'esriTrans', type:'raster', source:'esriTrans', layout:{visibility:'none'} },
    { id:'esriRef',   type:'raster', source:'esriRef',   layout:{visibility:'none'} },
    // --- OSM track/path geometry: what OHV-relevant ways exist at all -------
    { id:'vTrack', source:'omt', 'source-layer':'transportation', type:'line',
      filter:['in','class','track','path'],
      layout:{visibility:'none','line-cap':'round'},
      paint:{ 'line-color':'#f0883e', 'line-width':['interpolate',['linear'],['zoom'],10,0.6,16,2.5],
              'line-opacity':0.9 } },
    // --- YOUR ARTIFACTS ----------------------------------------------------
    // Casing + line, drawn from the geojson source. Note the colour is a
    // DATA-DRIVEN EXPRESSION over feature properties: MapLibre reads `rating`
    // straight off the feature, so the 1-5 star field being added to
    // track_properties can drive rendering with no extra layers and no
    // per-feature style callbacks. Leaflet cannot do this natively.
    { id:'mineCase', source:'mine', type:'line',
      layout:{ 'line-cap':'round','line-join':'round' },
      paint:{ 'line-color':'#000000','line-opacity':0.55,
              'line-width':['interpolate',['linear'],['zoom'],8,3,16,9] } },
    { id:'mineLine', source:'mine', type:'line',
      layout:{ 'line-cap':'round','line-join':'round' },
      paint:{ 'line-color':[
                'case',
                ['has','rating'],
                  ['interpolate',['linear'],['to-number',['get','rating']],
                    1,'#8b949e', 3,'#3fb950', 5,'#f0883e'],
                '#3fb950'
              ],
              'line-width':['interpolate',['linear'],['zoom'],8,1.5,16,5] } },
    { id:'mineLabel', source:'mine', type:'symbol',
      layout:{ 'symbol-placement':'line','text-field':['get','name'],
               'text-font':['Noto Sans Bold'],'text-size':11 },
      paint:{ 'text-color':'#3fb950','text-halo-color':'#000000','text-halo-width':1.8 } },
    // --- Labels: the layers that would replace Esri's raster label tiles ----
    { id:'vRoad', source:'omt', 'source-layer':'transportation_name', type:'symbol',
      layout:{ 'symbol-placement':'line', 'text-field':['coalesce',['get','name'],['get','ref']],
               'text-font':['Noto Sans Regular'], 'text-size':11 },
      paint:{ 'text-color':'#ffffff','text-halo-color':'#000000','text-halo-width':1.6 } },
    { id:'vWater', source:'omt', 'source-layer':'water_name', type:'symbol',
      layout:{ 'text-field':['get','name'], 'text-font':['Noto Sans Italic'], 'text-size':11 },
      paint:{ 'text-color':'#9ecbff','text-halo-color':'#000000','text-halo-width':1.4 } },
    { id:'vPeak', source:'omt', 'source-layer':'mountain_peak', type:'symbol',
      layout:{ 'text-field':['concat',['get','name'],'  ',['get','ele'],'m'],
               'text-font':['Noto Sans Regular'], 'text-size':10, 'text-offset':[0,0.6] },
      paint:{ 'text-color':'#ffd7a8','text-halo-color':'#000000','text-halo-width':1.4 } },
    { id:'vPoi', source:'omt', 'source-layer':'poi', type:'symbol',
      layout:{ visibility:'none', 'text-field':['get','name'],
               'text-font':['Noto Sans Regular'], 'text-size':10 },
      paint:{ 'text-color':'#c9d1d9','text-halo-color':'#000000','text-halo-width':1.4 } },
    { id:'vPlace', source:'omt', 'source-layer':'place', type:'symbol',
      layout:{ 'text-field':['get','name'], 'text-font':['Noto Sans Bold'],
               'text-size':['interpolate',['linear'],['zoom'],6,11,12,17] },
      paint:{ 'text-color':'#ffffff','text-halo-color':'#000000','text-halo-width':2 } }
  ]
};
function boot() {
const map = new maplibregl.Map({
  container:'map', style,
  center:[-109.5498, 38.5733],   // Moab — swap for your own riding areas
  zoom:11, maxZoom:19, hash:true
});
map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl(), 'bottom-right');
map.addControl(new maplibregl.ScaleControl({unit:'imperial'}), 'bottom-right');
const bind = (id, layer) => {
  const el = document.getElementById(id);
  el.addEventListener('change', () => {
    map.setLayoutProperty(layer, 'visibility', el.checked ? 'visible' : 'none');
  });
};
map.on('load', () => {
  [['sat','sat'],['esriRef','esriRef'],['esriTrans','esriTrans'],
   ['vPlace','vPlace'],['vRoad','vRoad'],['vPeak','vPeak'],
   ['vWater','vWater'],['vPoi','vPoi'],['vTrack','vTrack']].forEach(([i,l]) => bind(i,l));
  // your-data toggles cover casing + line together
  document.getElementById('gjOn').addEventListener('change', (e) => {
    const v = e.target.checked ? 'visible' : 'none';
    map.setLayoutProperty('mineCase','visibility',v);
    map.setLayoutProperty('mineLine','visibility',v);
  });
  bind('gjLbl','mineLabel');
  bind('shade','shade');
  // 3D terrain is not a layer - it displaces the whole scene, so imagery and
  // your track lines drape over the landform rather than sitting flat.
  const exag = document.getElementById('exag');
  const applyTerrain = () => {
    if (document.getElementById('terr').checked) {
      map.setTerrain({ source:'dem', exaggeration: parseFloat(exag.value) });
      if (map.getPitch() < 20) map.easeTo({ pitch:62, duration:900 });
    } else {
      map.setTerrain(null);
      map.easeTo({ pitch:0, bearing:0, duration:700 });
    }
  };
  document.getElementById('terr').addEventListener('change', applyTerrain);
  exag.addEventListener('input', () => {
    if (document.getElementById('terr').checked) {
      map.setTerrain({ source:'dem', exaggeration: parseFloat(exag.value) });
    }
  });
});
// --- load a GeoJSON export from the spatial DB ---------------------------
document.getElementById('gjFile').addEventListener('change', (ev) => {
  const f = ev.target.files && ev.target.files[0];
  if (!f) return;
  const info = document.getElementById('gjInfo');
  const rdr = new FileReader();
  rdr.onload = () => {
    try {
      const gj = JSON.parse(rdr.result);
      const feats = gj.type === 'FeatureCollection' ? gj.features
                  : gj.type === 'Feature' ? [gj] : [];
      if (!feats.length) { info.textContent = 'No features found in that file.'; return; }
      map.getSource('mine').setData({ type:'FeatureCollection', features:feats });
      // report which properties came through - these are what styling can key on
      const props = new Set();
      feats.slice(0,200).forEach(ft => Object.keys(ft.properties||{}).forEach(k => props.add(k)));
      info.innerHTML = feats.length + ' feature(s) loaded.props: ' +
                       (props.size ? [...props].slice(0,12).join(', ') : '(none)');
      // fit to the data
      let n=-90,s=90,e=-180,w=180;
      const walk = (c) => {
        if (typeof c[0] === 'number') {
          if (c[1]>n)n=c[1]; if (c[1]<s)s=c[1];
          if (c[0]>e)e=c[0]; if (c[0]<w)w=c[0];
        } else c.forEach(walk);
      };
      feats.forEach(ft => ft.geometry && ft.geometry.coordinates && walk(ft.geometry.coordinates));
      if (w<=e && s<=n) map.fitBounds([[w,s],[e,n]], { padding:60, maxZoom:16 });
    } catch (err) {
      info.textContent = 'Could not parse: ' + err.message;
    }
  };
  rdr.readAsText(f);
});
const readout = document.getElementById('readout');
const upd = () => {
  const c = map.getCenter();
  readout.textContent = `z${map.getZoom().toFixed(1)}  ${c.lat.toFixed(4)}, ${c.lng.toFixed(4)}`;
};
map.on('move', upd); map.on('load', upd);
map.on('error', (e) => {
  const box = document.getElementById('err');
  box.style.display = 'block';
  box.textContent = 'Tile/style error: ' + (e.error && e.error.message ? e.error.message : 'see console');
});
}  // end boot()
/* MapLibre is CDN-loaded. If one CDN is blocked the library never defines
   maplibregl and every line above throws. Try three, then say so plainly. */
(function () {
  const V = '4.7.1';
  const J = ['https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/maplibre-gl@'+V+'/dist/maplibre-gl.js',
             'https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@'+V+'/dist/maplibre-gl.js',
             'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/maplibre-gl/'+V+'/maplibre-gl.js'];
  const C = ['https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/maplibre-gl@'+V+'/dist/maplibre-gl.css',
             'https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@'+V+'/dist/maplibre-gl.css',
             'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/maplibre-gl/'+V+'/maplibre-gl.css'];
  const css = (i) => { if (i>=C.length) return;
    const l=document.createElement('link'); l.rel='stylesheet'; l.href=C[i];
    l.onerror=()=>css(i+1); document.head.appendChild(l); };
  const js = (i) => {
    if (i>=J.length) {
      const b=document.getElementById('err'); b.style.display='block';
      b.textContent='Could not load MapLibre from any CDN (jsdelivr, unpkg, cdnjs). '+
                    'Something on this network is blocking them, or there is no internet '+
                    '- note the satellite tiles need internet too.';
      return; }
    const sc=document.createElement('script'); sc.src=J[i];
    sc.onload=()=>{ if (window.maplibregl) { css(0); boot(); } else js(i+1); };
    sc.onerror=()=>js(i+1);
    document.head.appendChild(sc); };
  js(0);
})();
